title: D4: Resolve cost method (open question Q4)
description:
Decision: Phase 0 implements 'standard' cost method only. Schema includes a cost_method enum + column on skus (added in L1/R1) so future methods are additive, not a rewrite.

Rationale (per user, 2026-04-27):
- Phase 0 priorities: schema correctness + perf exploration. Standard cost has the smallest implementation surface (deterministic function of master data + event qty; no read-then-write of accumulator balances), making conformance fixtures and invariant tests deterministic and easy to author.
- WAC was tempting because it's simpler to OPERATE (no variance accounts), but it requires the read-then-write-under-FOR UPDATE pattern, which expands Phase 0's correctness surface and adds order-dependence to T5 conformance fixtures.
- 'Support any cost method eventually' is a real goal — addressed by the dispatch hook (cost_method enum) so WAC / FIFO / lot are additive in later phases without disturbing the existing 'standard' path or any existing table.

Implementation:
- L1 adds cost_method enum: 'standard', 'wac', 'fifo', 'lot'.
- R1 adds cost_method column to skus, NOT NULL DEFAULT 'standard'.
- W2 dispatches on skus.cost_method; only 'standard' branch implemented; others raise P0006 ('cost_method_not_implemented').
- Future cost methods tracked in a follow-up issue.
close_reason: Standard cost only in Phase 0; cost_method enum + column on skus serves as dispatch hook for future methods. WAC/FIFO/lot tracked as acct-8gg. Per user directive: prioritize ease of testing while preserving future-method optionality.

title: D2: Confirm Postgres major version + extension list
description:
Decision: Postgres 18 with io_uring async I/O backend (io_method=io_uring), pg_stat_statements, and pg_cron. Deployed as a Docker container for dev/test (production deployment deferred).

Rationale:
- PG 18 introduces native async I/O via the io_method GUC. io_uring is the highest-throughput option on Linux (kernel >= 5.1) and is a meaningful win for ledger workloads where we expect many small concurrent reads under FOR UPDATE locks.
- pg_stat_statements: query-level perf observability, baseline for §14.1 exploratory testing.
- pg_cron: reservation expiry job (O1) and daily reconciliation job (O2).

Verification needed during S1:
- Confirm the official postgres:18 image is built with liburing support (--with-liburing). If not, build a custom Dockerfile FROM postgres:18 that adds liburing.
- shared_preload_libraries must include 'pg_stat_statements' and 'pg_cron'.
- io_method=io_uring set in postgresql.conf.
- Validate at startup: 'SHOW io_method' returns 'io_uring'; 'SELECT * FROM pg_extension' shows both extensions.

Document the configuration in db/README.md when this issue closes.
close_reason: PG 18 + io_method=io_uring + pg_stat_statements + pg_cron, in Docker for dev. Decision per user directive.

title: Close the period-coverage-gap backdate side door; constrain period overlap
description:
Why: accounting_period (0002) has only UNIQUE(start_date,end_date) — no overlap exclusion, no contiguity. 0017's period_guard_trx_line loops only over periods COVERING the new row's posted_at, so an event backdated into a date range no period covers (before the first period, or a gap) is admitted; the feed then lowers a recost floor below a closed period's end, the full replay recomputes closed-period costs, and the 0017 cost_settlement guard rejects every subsequent pass — the exact permanent-wedge class reject_out_of_order (close.rs:336-360) exists to prevent, reachable through the uncovered-dates side door. gate_pools explicitly supports pre-period activity, so the hole is realistic.

What: treat the latest closed period's end as a monotonic backdate floor in period_guard_trx_line (reject physical inserts with posted_at at/below it regardless of coverage), and add EXCLUDE USING gist (daterange(start_date,end_date,'[]') WITH &&) on accounting_period plus a contiguity/ordering check at period creation.

Acceptance: pin with a test that backdates into a pre-first-period date after a close and into an inter-period gap — both must reject loud at insert time, not wedge the engine later.

PROVENANCE: recalc-close (P2), parity (overlap item); 0002_reference.up.sql:30-39, 0017, close.rs:336-360

title: Slot-loss detection, recovery/reseed routine, and first-startup dirty-set bootstrap
description:
Why: max_slot_wal_keep_size=4GB deliberately permits slot invalidation; ensure_slot (ledger-feed/src/consumer.rs:112-121) then recreates the slot past the gap, so backdated events lost with the slot never lower a recost floor — a truly silent mis-valuation that defeats the loud-alarm mitigation (which only fires if the event is eventually delivered). The live cluster was observed with NO ledger_feed slot at all while poc_v3_2 held data. Nothing monitors pg_replication_slots.invalidation_reason or slot absence (the feed_lag view returns zero rows when the slot is missing). Additionally, events committed before the FIRST feed startup are never marked dirty — ensure_slot creates at current WAL and seeds nothing.

What: (a) slot-health gauge that emits a row even when the slot is absent/invalidated (expose invalidation_reason; also fix 0014's hardcoded slot_name='ledger_feed' vs the FEED_SLOT env override — either drop the env overrides or enumerate slots on the publication). (b) A ledger_feed_reseed()/recovery routine: when ensure_slot creates a slot while pool_settlement is non-empty (or on demand), enqueue every fifo/lifo pool whose trx_line tail extends past its settled frontier and set conservative recost floors (e.g. last-closed-period boundary or earliest event lacking a current-generation cost_settlement) forcing full re-fold. (c) wal_status='lost' detection in the feed loop with a loud abort instead of infinite peek-error retries. (d) Script the cluster prereqs (wal_level=logical, max_slot_wal_keep_size) with a verify step per the parent dev-up.sh convention — today they were applied via manual ALTER SYSTEM and a container rebuild silently drops them. (e) Document feed-before-load ordering in run-feed.sh.

Acceptance: test that drops/invalidates the slot mid-run, runs recovery, and proves convergence (R1 oracle equivalence) afterward.

PROVENANCE: feed (2 items), design-core, bench-ops, parity (consumer.rs:112-121, 0014, README phase 3)

title: Gate ledger_close_period on feed/slot currency, not just report it
description:
Why: gate_pools (close.rs:367-409) counts unsettled events above settled_through and reads feed-maintained recost floors, so a BACKDATED event committed pre-close but not yet delivered by the slot sits below the frontier, sets no floor, and is invisible — the close stamps an immutably wrong valuation and the pool later wedges permanently on the 0017 cost_settlement guard. feed_lag_bytes is carried in the close report only (close.rs:148,157,226) and NULL (slot missing) is indistinguishable from healthy. The headline soak showed nonzero lag (39,728 bytes) during a realistic close probe.

What: under the existing 32022 advisory fence, capture pg_current_wal_lsn() and require the ledger_feed slot's confirmed_flush_lsn to reach it (or a small bound) before the gate re-check and stamp; fail loud when the slot is absent/inactive/invalidated. Keep feed_lag_bytes in the report as the diagnostic. Decide whether force bypasses this leg (recommend: force still requires a live slot, mirroring the drain-not-skip posture).

Acceptance: an acceptance case that submits a backdated in-period event, does NOT ingest, and calls ledger_close_period — close must fail loud (not stamp); after ingest+drain it closes clean. A slot-absent close must also fail loud. Update the close.rs module doc premise paragraph (lines 60-69) to describe the enforcement.

PROVENANCE: design-core, recalc-close, feed, archaeology, parity, bench-ops (6/9 auditors; close.rs:60-69, 0017 guard, soak-results §1)

title: v3.2 recalc engine: stale EPQ claim + non-monotonic settle() regresses recalc_generation — permanent cost_layer_consumption_pkey wedge
description:
FOUND BY the acct-qm7o.6 soak (trend profile, 10% backdate, 4 concurrent workers): ERROR duplicate key value violates unique constraint "cost_layer_consumption_pkey", DETAIL Key (depletion_trx_line_id, layer_trx_line_id, recalc_generation)=(9024, 5767, 33) already exists — the SAME key failing identically across every worker that claimed the pool (permanent wedge; a second key (2623, 1522, 13) failed once transiently). Full evidence + writeup: poc/ledger-v3.2/bench/soak-results.md section 5.

ROOT CAUSE (two independent adversarially-verified code walks; BOTH defects required):
(1) STALE CLAIM VIA EvalPlanQual — claim_next (recalc.rs:353-368, FOR UPDATE OF rq SKIP LOCKED) and claim_pool (recalc.rs:286-298, blocking) read pool_settlement.recalc_generation / settled_through_* / recost_floor_* through an UNLOCKED LEFT JOIN inside the locking statement. Under READ COMMITTED, when a sibling pass commits (generation bump + requeue re-stamp UPDATE of the queue row, recalc.rs:920-936) between the claim statement snapshot and its lock acquisition, the EPQ recheck locks the NEW queue tuple but re-evaluates the join against the ORIGINAL-snapshot pool_settlement tuple: the claim carries the pre-commit generation AND a stale still-set recost floor, while all post-claim statements see fresh state.
(2) NON-MONOTONIC SETTLE — settle() writes recalc_generation = EXCLUDED.recalc_generation unconditionally (recalc.rs:815-816) with generation = claim.generation + i64::from(wrote) (recalc.rs:210-211). The stale-claimed pass full-replays (stale floor, recalc.rs:162), deterministically re-derives costs identical to the committed gen-33 rows (load_priors sees them fresh), so pending is empty, wrote=false — and settle() COMMITS the regression 33 to 32. Committed gen-33 consumption rows now sit ABOVE the recorded generation; the next genuine re-cost computes 32+1=33 and collides; the abort rolls back the pass so generation stays 32, floor stays set, queue row survives — every worker repeats the identical replay and collision forever.

VERIFIED MINIMAL FIX (preserves D6 no-op-passes-free exactly; no schema change, no fold change, R1-R7 untouched):
(a) Split lock-then-read in BOTH claim paths: stmt 1 locks ONLY the queue row (SELECT pool_id FROM recalc_queue ... FOR UPDATE [SKIP LOCKED]); stmt 2 reads pool + pool_settlement post-lock on a fresh snapshot (every writer of recalc_generation commits under this same queue-row lock, so the second read is guaranteed current; the feed lock-free floor writes only ever LOWER the floor, which the settle floor-clear CASE recalc.rs:819-826 already preserves). claim_pool: if EPQ finds the row deleted after blocking (zero rows), loop back to the ensure-INSERT and retry.
(b) Defense-in-depth (NOT a substitute — stops only the parked regression, not the direct stale-pass collision): settle() recalc_generation = GREATEST(pool_settlement.recalc_generation, EXCLUDED.recalc_generation).

REGRESSION TEST (deterministic — the blocking claim_pool path IS the rendezvous, no sleeps): two-connection tokio+sqlx test: settle a fifo pool at gen G with the queue row surviving (tail); session 1 BEGIN + ledger_recalc_step() writing gen G+1 + requeue, HOLD open; session 2 ledger_settle_pool(pool) blocks on the queue-row lock (poll pg_locks until provably waiting); COMMIT session 1; session 2 wakes through EPQ with the stale join — pre-fix its no-op pass commits recalc_generation = G over G+1. Assert generation == G+1 after session 2 returns, then deliver a backdated receipt and drain: pre-fix wedges on the duplicate key, post-fix re-costs cleanly. ALSO: add a generation-monotonicity invariant to property_recalc_engine.rs, and RE-RUN the trend-profile soak (scripts/soak.sh SOAK_PROFILE=trend SOAK_BACKDATE_PCT=10) to fill the missing trend drift row in bench/soak-results.md section 3.

NOTE the wedge also means ledger_close_period forced-drain would spin on a poisoned pool (drain_pool_to_head hits the same duplicate) — the fix unwedges close too. Workers hitting the wedge spin at claim rate; the bench abort trips after 20 consecutive errors, production run-recalc.sh has no such trip yet.
notes:
RESUME PLAN (written pre-compaction 2026-07-11; phase 6 SHIPPED as cda1dbe and CLOSED — phases 1-6 all closed with decision records; HEAD cda1dbe on branch ledger-v3.2).

READ ORDER before coding: (1) bd show acct-qm7o (epic onboarding block) + THIS issue IN FULL — the DESCRIPTION already carries the complete adversarially-verified root cause (two defects: stale-EPQ claim + non-monotonic settle), the verified minimal fix, and the deterministic regression-test recipe; (2) the acct-qm7o.6 close reason (how the bug was found + the other soak findings + verify-side lessons); (3) poc/ledger-v3.2/bench/soak-results.md section 5 (the published writeup of this bug) + section 3 (the trend drift row this fix unblocks); (4) the code: ledger-direct/src/recalc.rs — claim_pool (~286-298), claim_next (~353-368, incl. the deliberate-unlocked-join comment at 348-352), generation computation (~210-214), settle (~808-844, the non-monotonic write at 815-816 and the floor-clear CASE at 819-826), decide_queue (~895-936); ledger-direct/src/close.rs sweep_pool/drain_pool_to_head (they call claim_pool — the blocking path shares the defect and the fix unwedges forced close); (5) tests/property_recalc_engine.rs header (R1-R7 conventions; add generation monotonicity) + tests/common/mod.rs helpers.

title: ledger-v3.2 recalc engine (c): cadence-vs-load control + quiet-backlog / throughput-inequality mitigation
description:
Design the control layer that keeps recalc from silently falling behind — the load-bearing §19 risk under the surviving architecture (§18).

THE THROUGHPUT INEQUALITY (design-v3.1 §19, retained + centralized): recalc must process the SAME event volume as the hot path while doing strictly MORE work per line (walk layers, assign cost, post GL, materialize position). Sole-engine posture (§16) RAISES the stakes — a backlog gates whenever ANY authoritative cost/GL is needed, not merely when a correction lands; ahead of recalc the value plane simply does not exist yet.

QUIET-BACKLOG FAILURE CHAIN (§19): consumer falls behind → logical-slot confirmed_flush_lsn lags (pins WAL → disk-exhaustion risk, §17) AND no authoritative cost/GL for the tail → mid-period drift (biased under a trend, §19 table) persists and compounds → period close blocks until recalc drains (SAP CKMLCP precedent: multi-hour closes, plant-wide locking) → forced close emits the whole valuation move at once, large + one-signed.

Design scope (the three §19 levers — framed, not yet chosen):
- CADENCE: the §16 configurable recalc-period knob. Does NOT change total work; trades peak backlog depth + drift latency against per-run fixed-cost overhead. Continuous (shallow backlog, steady load, more fixed-cost repetition) vs at-close (deep backlog, big batch move). "Real-time FIFO" = the small-period limit, not a second strict plane.
- PER-POOL PARALLELISM interaction (child b): Pareto-hot pools set the close-drain floor even fully parallelized.
- BACKPRESSURE: throttle the insert-only hot path when slot-lag exceeds a bound. Alt-C absorbs it gracefully (just INSERTs) but it reintroduces a hot-path→recalc coupling alt C otherwise severs — a deliberate tradeoff.

DETECTION SIGNAL (unify per §17): slot-lag IS recalc-backlog — one gauge (confirmed_flush_lsn lag) is the single backlog depth. Complementary bounds: count/value of un-costed trx_line behind the cursor; conservation-invariant sweep (acct-0at4.5, gate-kept) over flagged negative aggregates caps how far the physical signal has run ahead of authoritative cost.

Depends on children (a) + (b). Design-only.

LEVER 1 cadence: default CONTINUOUS drain (claim-driven workers, b), force full sweep+settle at close boundaries as backstop (child e). §16 "period" maps to a close gate, not to gating forward passes. Residual knob = worker count/poll eagerness (not a strict period). Per-pool cadence unnecessary (claim-driven self-adjusts).

LEVER 2 per-pool ceiling (from b §3): parallelism ACROSS pools only; a depth-50k pool folds ~25 events/s (strict curve) and no cadence/worker fixes it. Forces PER-POOL detection: global gauge hides a hot pool's settled_through lag. Close-drain floor = max over pools of (unsettled events / fold rate).

LEVER 3 backpressure: throttle hot path when backlog exceeds bound. Alt-C insert-only absorbs it but re-couples hot-path->recalc (§16 severed it) = last resort. title: ledger-v3.2 recalc engine (a): layer-walk + chronological re-sort (R-1) — correctness vs strict-FIFO replay oracle
description:
Design the core recalc algorithm: for a single layer-tracked pool, walk its trx_line stream and assign authoritative FIFO/LIFO cost, posting the value leg to the GL.

THE HARD CORE per design-v3.1 §19. This is the serial-fold at the center of the surviving architecture (§18): recalc is the SOLE costing engine under alt C (§16) — the hot path posts no cost leg, so this walk produces the only authoritative valuation.

Design scope:
- Layer-walk algorithm proper: strict FIFO/LIFO layer consumption, receipt layer creation, depletion-against-layers, variance vs the provisional running-avg the hot path recorded.
- Chronological re-sort (R-1, §19 / bench/replay-oracle-results.md §1): recalc must order each pool by (pool_id, posted_at, id) = business chronology, NOT trx_line.id identity/commit order. The logical-decoding feed (§17) delivers COMMIT order; the within-pool cost-correctness re-sort is recalc's job (§17 is explicit the feed does not solve this).
- Backdated receipt (R-2): a receipt that commits after events it should chronologically precede forces RE-COSTING of already-costed depletions in its pool — so recalc is not a naive forward scan and incremental streaming does not bound per-event work. Design how re-costing is scoped/bounded.
- The real strict fifo.rs / lifo.rs implementations that §8 left as MethodMismatch stubs are built here (or here-adjacent).

Correctness oracle: validate against acct-0at4.7 offline strict-FIFO replay oracle (bench/replay-oracle-results.md) — architecture-agnostic, kept+elevated at the gate (§18 re-triage). The variance magnitudes there (biased-under-trend, §19 table) are the acceptance target.

Foundational: children (b) scheduler / (c) cadence / (d) schema / (e) close-time all build on this. Design-only under this issue (algorithm + data-access shape); implementation is a follow-up once the v3.2 spec §5 lands.
design:
DESIGN SHIPPED: poc/design_research/design-v3.2-recalc-a.md (referenced from design-v3.2.md §5).

Algorithm = the acct-0at4.7 replay oracle's strict StrictPool (VecDeque front=FIFO/back=LIFO, banker_div weighted-average of consumed layers, i128 accum, 1e-6 precision) lifted to persistent pool_state.layer_id>0 rows (layer_id = receipt trx_line.id per §2.2). Recalc writes the layers the hot path never materializes; per depletion it produces authoritative unit_cost + variance(=authoritative-provisional, the GL cost-adjustment leg, directional under trend per oracle §2b) + per-consumed-layer linkage tuples.

R-1: re-sort each pool by (pool_id, posted_at, id) — posted_at business-effective primary, id the faithful within-date tiebreak (oracle §1a). Two obligations: write-path must supply REAL business posted_at (harness stamps a constant today, oracle §1c — recalc can't repair it after); data-access needs a (pool_id, posted_at, id) ordered path (D1: recommend denormalize trx_line.posted_at + index → child d).

R-2: backdated receipt (posted_at precedes already-costed depletions) forces re-cost → recalc is a per-pool REPLAY anchored at a re-cost floor, NOT a forward scan (feed delivers backdated events in commit/late order). D2: full-pool-replay-from-opening as the correct-first baseline (IS the oracle, idempotent by construction, zero reproduction risk); checkpoint+replay-from-floor deferred to child b/c as the optimization once full-replay is shown binding. Fan-out bounded by feed-advanced pool_ids (cross-pool parallelism = child b); within-pool work unbounded (the shape child c models).

Real fifo.rs/lifo.rs replace the §8 MethodMismatch stubs (recalc-only; hot path stays provisional §3.5).

Acceptance (reuse oracle as golden): reproduce TRUE arm line-for-line; variance == recorded-true incl. the trend directional bias; R-2 vignette A returns authoritative 100 not id-order 300; idempotent re-run posts zero net new; conservation sweep (acct-0at4.5). Test-bed gap: needs a receipt-cost-volatility knob (oracle §2a).

Open decisions D1-D4 handed to siblings (none gate (a)'s correctness): D1 posted_at denorm→(d); D2 full-replay-first→(b); D3 per-layer linkage form→(d); D4 re-cost-floor granularity→(b).

title: ledger-v3.1 ARCH-POSTURE: resolve cost-provisional/qty-strict/order-unordered incoherence + interrogate the FIFO requirement (C/G)
description:
Source: FEEDBACK-ARCH.md problem #2 (incoherent posture) + problem #5 (intrinsic per-pool ceiling) + alternative C (cost-less hot path) + alternative G (interrogate the FIFO requirement). **A requirements decision, not an engineering one — needs the accounting-requirement owner.**

## The incoherence
The design holds three positions at once:
- **cost is provisional** (record now, reconcile at recalc/close),
- **quantity is strict** (reject oversell synchronously, under `pool_lock`),
- **execution order across chunks is unordered** (spurious drops accepted, acct-0at4.1).

These don't compose. The strict-qty check is the **only** reason the hot path reads state under `pool_lock` at all — and it is enforced against a number the design elsewhere admits can be wrong-ordered across chunks. So we pay full per-pool serialization to enforce an invariant we don't deliver deterministically, in service of a "record now, reconcile later" philosophy that argues against enforcing it synchronously at all. The half-measure gets the costs of both postures and the guarantees of neither.

## The per-pool ceiling (why this matters for throughput)
Every variant that maintains synchronous per-pool state — direct, batched, routed — has a hard ceiling per hot pool: one serialized fold. Routed raises the ceiling to ~`batch_size_max / commit_time` but the ceiling **remains** (three committers idle behind the hot pool). The ONLY architecture that removes it is one where the hot path does not read-modify per-pool state at all. Routed is a constant-factor improvement on a fundamentally serial design, framed in the doc as *the* answer to "1000 callers, one pool."

## Pick a posture
- **Everything strict** → honestly back to Path A/B and per-pool ordering. Costs acknowledged, ceiling acknowledged.
- **Everything provisional (alt C)** → qty is also just a running signal (negative allowed, oversell becomes a recalc finding). Then the hot path needs **no read** — append-only, scales with heap-insert throughput, ceiling removed, no provisional-vs-authoritative dual bookkeeping. Mid-period GL is qty-only or standard-valued (SAP material-ledger shape: real-time perpetual quantity, periodic valuation). The business may or may not accept that — **that is the question to ask before building two costing planes.**

## Sub-question G — interrogate the FIFO requirement
The costliest requirement in the system is per-depletion FIFO fidelity. Most regimes that "require FIFO" actually require **periodic** FIFO (month-end layer consumption), and many FIFO businesses would pass an audit on WAC. If the real requirement is periodic → alt C is the design and strict per-depletion layer math never needs to exist. If some pools genuinely need real-time layer cost (specific-id already does) → **scope strict mode to those pools only**. The cheapest architecture is the one where the hard requirement turns out not to exist.

## Output
A recorded posture decision in design-v3.1 (everything-strict / everything-provisional-alt-C / hybrid-scope-strict-to-named-pools), with the FIFO-granularity requirement (per-depletion vs periodic) settled by the requirement owner. This decision determines whether recalc is a corrective sidecar (hard, risky, dual-bookkeeping — acct-0at4.14) or the sole costing engine (simpler, single-plane). Flagged for human decision.

## Acceptance
Posture + FIFO-granularity decision recorded in design-v3.1 with the requirement owner's sign-off; the acct-0at4.1 cross-chunk disposition and acct-0at4.14 recalc framing both re-derived from the chosen posture.

title: ledger-v3.1 SPIKE-B: single-statement commutative aggregate UPDATE vs RMW-across-SPI (pool_lock-deletable test)
description:
Source: FEEDBACK-ARCH.md problem #4 + alternative B. **Spike #2 — days, not weeks.**

## Thesis
Even for the "constant-time" aggregate update, the current flow is: acquire `pool_lock` row → SELECT aggregate → round-trip into ledger-core (Rust) → plan → UPSERT back. The lock is held across multiple SPI calls and a Rust round-trip **because the arithmetic lives outside SQL**. But the aggregate mutation is almost commutative — `qty += ΔQ, value_sum += ΔV` — and PostgreSQL will serialize a single-row

    UPDATE pool_state
       SET qty = qty + $1, value_sum = value_sum + $2
     WHERE pool_id = $3 AND layer_id = 0 AND qty + $1 >= 0

on its own tuple lock, hold time = one tuple update: no `pool_lock` table, no sorted-acquisition protocol, no lazy-create dance, no deadlock-ordering discipline. The running-average read a depletion needs (applied_unit_cost = banker_div(value_sum, qty) at read time) fits in the same statement via a CTE. The `qty + $1 >= 0` predicate enforces the strict-qty gate in-statement, and a `RETURNING` reports whether the row moved (→ InsufficientInventory when the predicate fails).

The design never asks whether ledger-core-in-Rust actually beats one SQL statement for the aggregate path. The entire `pool_lock` edifice (and its WAL churn, and the deadlock-ordering discipline) may be solving a problem the RMW-across-SPI shape created.

## Build
Fold hydrate/plan/write for the aggregate-only paths (running_avg receipt, running_avg + standard-basis depletion) into one SQL statement under PG's own row lock. Keep ledger-core for the genuinely stateful methods (specific-id, future strict layer math) only.

## Decision gate
Benchmark lock-hold + throughput vs the current direct RMW on the same box. If within noise → drop `pool_lock`, the sorted-acquisition protocol, and most of the single-pool deadlock surface. **Subsumes acct-0at4.3 #7** (advisory-lock vs row-lock) — if the whole `pool_lock` table disappears, the advisory-vs-row micro-question is moot.

## Acceptance
Single-statement commutative aggregate variant built (throwaway); lock-hold + throughput measured head-to-head vs current direct with CIs; a recorded verdict in design-v3.1 (drop pool_lock for aggregate paths / keep, with the measured delta); acct-0at4.3 #7 dispositioned as subsumed.
acceptance_criteria: Single-statement commutative variant built; lock-hold + throughput vs current direct with CIs; recorded verdict (drop pool_lock for aggregate paths / keep); acct-0at4.3 #7 dispositioned as subsumed.
notes:
SPIKE-B DONE (verdict: pool_lock deletable for aggregate paths). Built ledger_submit_trx_single_c (single-pool/single-line, B-full one-CTE) + banker_div-in-SQL (bench/spike-b-setup.sql, 17 cases match Rust) + PG18 RETURNING old.unit_cost. Correctness byte-identical to RMW baseline: 6 differential cases agree (receipts, depletions, banker half-even both directions, empty-pool value_sum reset, account swap) + insufficient-inv raises atomically writing nothing (bench/spike-b-verify.sql). 0 errors / 0 neg-qty across all runs.

Throughput single/RMW: S1 cap10 uncontended receipts 1.00x (2301 vs 2300); S5 cap8 moderate 1-pool deplete 1.37x (460 vs 335); S5 cap400 saturated 0.98x (332 vs 340). Single is >= RMW everywhere on throughput, p50 20-35pct lower under contention, ~4-6pct less WAL (no pool_lock tuple). ONE regression: p99 tail ~1.9x worse under single-hot-pool contention (cap8 33.5->63.8ms; cap400 2.5->5.1s) -- structural, unchased; that pathological regime is what SPIKE-A routed/staging coalescing owns anyway.

Finding: RMW-across-SPI does NOT materially inflate throughput (in-process SPI + kept plans are cheap; commit fsync dominates) -- pool_lock is not costing much, it is simply not BUYING anything; one commutative UPDATE matches behavior+perf without it. acct-0at4.3 #7 (advisory-vs-row-lock) SUBSUMED: no pool_lock row left to make advisory. Writeup bench/spike-b-results.md. design-v3.1 verdict + downstream re-triage deferred to acct-0at4.11.5 per gate structure. Left in_progress (feeds gate verdict) like SPIKE-A.
close_reason: GATE dispositioned — verdict recorded in design-v3.1 §16/§17/§18 (acct-0at4.11.5). Machinery not justified: staging-table + single-statement + alt-C + logical-decoding-feed is the surviving architecture. Downstream re-triaged (§18 table).

title: ledger-v3.1 SPIKE-A: staging-table outbox + SKIP LOCKED committers vs shmem routed (routed-crate-deletable test)
description:
Source: FEEDBACK-ARCH.md problem #3 + alternative A. **Spike #1 — the boring design the shmem stack should have been benchmarked against before being built.**

## Thesis
§6.2–§6.5 rebuilds inside postmaster shared memory exactly the machinery a durable queue already provides — state machines, claims, generations, pid liveness, boot sweeps, eject/backpressure, xid triage against clog — and ends up with **weaker** semantics: volatile on crash, non-transactional with the caller (the savepoint hole), invisible to SQL tooling, and requiring the caller to run an outbox anyway. The database underneath already *is* a durable, transactional, ordered, crash-recoverable queue: a table. The entire `pg_xact_status`/eject apparatus exists **solely** because the enqueue escaped the caller's transaction. Put the enqueue *in* the transaction and the whole problem class evaporates.

## Build
- `INSERT INTO ledger_inbox (...)` inside the caller's tx (rides on the fsync the caller already pays for its business writes).
- Committer loop: `SELECT ... FROM ledger_inbox FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED ORDER BY id LIMIT N`, group by pool, process, mark done (UPDATE, not a shmem flag).

## What it buys (for free, vs the shmem stack)
- **Atomicity with the caller** → kills xid triage, eject, savepoint, and syncoff problems in one move (dissolves acct-0at4.2).
- **Per-pool FIFO by construction** (`ORDER BY id`) → dissolves the cross-chunk spurious-drop problem (acct-0at4.1) — no predecessor-wait machinery needed.
- **Free observability** — the row *is* the status; poison is an `UPDATE`, not a shmem flag that a postmaster restart erases (dissolves acct-0at4.3 #18).
- **Recovery = nothing** (WAL is the protocol).
- No flag-day upgrades / gdb-against-postgres / replica-invisibility lifecycle tax that shmem carries.

Costs: one heap insert + drain reads + vacuum on the inbox.

## The measurement (this is the deliverable)
Benchmark staging-table routed vs shmem routed on the hot-pool scenarios (S5/S7/S8) on the same box. Strong prior: the delta is small because committer-side PG work dominates, not the enqueue. Report the delta with CIs (use the confound/soak discipline from acct-0at4.10).

## Decision gate
If staging-table routed lands within ~20% of shmem routed on the hot-pool scenarios → **the routed crate is deletable**, and that is the finding. Record keep/delete in design-v3.1.

## Acceptance
`ledger_inbox` + SKIP-LOCKED committer prototype (throwaway quality); head-to-head vs shmem routed on S5/S7/S8 with CIs; a recorded keep-routed / delete-routed verdict in design-v3.1 with the measured delta.
acceptance_criteria: ledger_inbox + SKIP-LOCKED committer prototype; head-to-head vs shmem routed on S5/S7/S8 with CIs; recorded keep/delete-routed verdict in design-v3.1 with the measured delta.
notes: SPIKE-A DONE. Staging-table (INSERT-in-tx + FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED drain, K=4 looping conns) vs shmem routed on S5/S7/S8, 400 callers, 3 reps interleaved. Staging/routed throughput ratio (median): S5 4.4x (9969 vs 2280), S7 5.3x (10624 vs 2001), S8 ~17x (8880 vs 523). Routed shed ~57% of offered load (bounded-ring backpressure, ~1000 enqueue_errors/run); staging 0 errors, 0 unseen, exact conservation. Caller ack p99: staging 130-165ms vs routed 5-68s. S8 routed spends 78pct of committer time on pool_lock. Gate (within 20pct -> deletable) far exceeded: table alternative dominates several-fold while deleting CQ ring/arena/router-unionfind/identity-gen/xid-triage-eject, and is WAL-durable. Client-driven committer handicaps staging (per-batch round-trip) so this is a conservative lower bound; BGWorker option B would only widen the gap. VERDICT: routed crate deletable on throughput grounds. Writeup: bench/spike-a-results.md. design-v3.1 paragraph + acct-0at4.1/.2 re-triage deferred to GATE-VERDICT acct-0at4.11.5 per gate structure.
close_reason: GATE dispositioned — verdict recorded in design-v3.1 §16/§17/§18 (acct-0at4.11.5). Machinery not justified: staging-table + single-statement + alt-C + logical-decoding-feed is the surviving architecture. Downstream re-triaged (§18 table).

title: ledger-v3.1 ARCHITECTURE DECISION GATE (FEEDBACK-ARCH) — is the shmem/routed machinery buying anything?
description: Gate epic for FEEDBACK-ARCH.md (poc/ledger-v3.1). Unlike FEEDBACK/FEEDBACK-TESTING (point-fixes to a design assumed to be a keeper), FEEDBACK-ARCH is a structural go/no-go: it argues ~5 load-bearing choices (deferred-recalc risk inversion; incoherent cost-provisional/qty-strict/order-unordered posture; shmem queue as wrong-layer engineering; RMW-across-SPI inflating the critical section; the intrinsic per-pool ceiling) may be complexity without yield, and prescribes cheap spikes to run BEFORE hardening v3.1. title: ledger-v3.1 testing: open-loop load generator + latency-SLO / saturation methodology
description:
Source: FEEDBACK-TESTING.md #8, #13; FEEDBACK.md #13.

The harness is closed-loop (N callers each submit-then-wait). Closed-loop load suffers **coordinated omission**: when the system stalls, callers stop generating, so the stall never appears in the latency distribution — the latency numbers are fiction at the margins, and the routed-vs-direct crossover *is* a latency claim there.

- **Open-loop generator:** drive a Poisson arrival process at fixed target rates; record per-submission latency from the *intended* send-time, not from when a free caller happened to issue it. Report full HDR distributions (p50/p99/p999), never means. Keep closed-loop only for peak-throughput measurement.

- **Saturation methodology:** ramp offered load until goodput plateaus/degrades; headline = **throughput at a latency SLO** (e.g. max sustainable rate with p99 < 10 ms), with peak throughput secondary. Peak-only comparisons systematically flatter routed (it trades latency for batching) — the current framing bakes that bias in.

- **Routed latency floor (FEEDBACK #13):** 50 ms latch + 500 µs dwell ⇒ a ~25 ms mean floor from tick alignment alone, against direct's microsecond critical section. Add a `SetLatch`-on-enqueue immediate-wake path (dwell gate still applies) so crossover latency measures the architecture, not the tick constant. (The SetLatch variant is also an ablation axis in the baselines issue.)

## Acceptance
Open-loop mode in the harness with intended-send-time latency capture + HDR output; crossover reported as throughput-at-SLO with full distributions; the `SetLatch`-on-enqueue variant measured against the 50 ms tick.
notes: RE-SCOPE (2026-07-09, empty-notes judgment call surfaced to user): SetLatch-on-enqueue (bullet 3) DEFERRED to acct-0at4.9 — it targets the shmem-routed committer 50ms latch, the flavor the gate verdict acct-0at4.11.5 displaced, and the issue text itself flags it as an ablation axis of .9. .8 ships the architecture-agnostic core: open-loop generator (Poisson arrivals) + coordinated-omission fix (latency from INTENDED send-time) + p999/HDR output + throughput-at-SLO saturation methodology. Flavor scope: pace direct-single (SPIKE-B) + staging (SPIKE-A) + routed, so the crossover-at-SLO is a genuine 3-way comparison. Starting state: --target-rate pacing + HDR already exist but ROUTED-ONLY and measure latency from ACTUAL issue instant (driver_routed.rs:377/385 started.elapsed()) with debt-shedding (:365 *nf=now) = live coordinated omission; LatencyPercentiles has no p999; no ramp/SLO runner.
close_reason: Delivered the architecture-agnostic open-loop core (commits 5605b8f + 3bd338d): pacing::Pacer drives a fixed offered rate on an absolute, never-rebased schedule and measures latency from the INTENDED send-time (wrk2/Gil-Tene) — replacing the routed-only debt-shedding + actual-issue-instant pacer that was live coordinated omission. Poisson (default) + uniform arrivals via --arrival, generalized from routed to all modes (direct-*, staging, routed). LatencyPercentiles gains p999; committed latency is CO-free too (intended origin in submission_log); every report self-documents offered_rate + arrival_process. scripts/saturation-sweep.sh produces the throughput-at-SLO headline (max sustainable rate with p99 < SLO and achieved >= keep_up x offered) and a per-rung JSON array for .9/.10. Validated: 8000 trx/s offered to a ~1900-ceiling run drives p99 to 3.0s (honest backlog vs the sub-10ms a CO-broken clock reports); ramp finds crossover; 43 harness unit tests + 4 new pacing tests green; clippy-clean. Acceptance bullet 3 (SetLatch-on-enqueue vs the routed 50ms tick) DEFERRED to acct-0at4.9 per the surfaced scope decision — it targets the shmem-routed committer displaced by gate verdict acct-0at4.11.5 and the issue text itself flags it as a .9 ablation axis; the CO-free clock already surfaces routed p99 ~118ms tick floor for .9 to attack. Notes recorded on both .8 and .9.

title: ledger-v3.1 testing: offline strict-FIFO replay oracle -> Path C premise + variance magnitude
description:
Source: FEEDBACK-TESTING.md #6 + FEEDBACK.md #11. **Highest business value of the testing set.**

Path C's entire premise is that the trx_line stream is *sufficient* to reconstruct authoritative FIFO/LIFO state later (recalc/close, §7). That premise is currently **untested**, and the variance the *business case* hangs on is **unmeasured** (the §10.6 Phase-3 note explicitly defers it to the recalc/close phase).

A throwaway offline strict-FIFO/LIFO replay over a trx_line dump (Python or a scratch Rust binary — does **not** need production `fifo.rs`/`lifo.rs` quality) closes both loops cheaply:

1. **Premise check:** does replay produce a well-defined authoritative answer from what the hot path recorded? If backdated receipts (§14.5) or chunk reordering (§14.2) make it ill-defined, the architecture is falsified — cheaply, now, instead of after building recalc/close.
2. **Variance distribution:** provisional-vs-true-FIFO unit_cost variance per basis (`running_avg` vs `standard`) and per volatility profile, over the harness's own runs. That is the number Path C's production go/no-go decision consumes.

Distinct from building recalc/close — this is a read-only replay for *characterization*, not a settlement mechanism. Benefits from the `trx_line (pool_id, id)` index (ARCH roll-up #17).

## Acceptance
Replay script runs against a harness run's trx_line dump; emits per-basis / per-volatility-profile variance distributions; a short writeup states whether the stream is reconstruction-sufficient and, if not, exactly which inputs break it.
close_reason: Shipped offline strict-FIFO/LIFO replay oracle (bench/replay-oracle/, bench/replay-oracle-run.sh) + writeup (bench/replay-oracle-results.md), commit 26fb536. Premise CONFIRMED with sharpened contract: real dump (149,392 concurrent depletions) reproduces recorded provisional 100.0000% via id-order, but authoritative FIFO reconstruction requires posted_at business-chronology + chronological recalc sort — backdated events (business-order != commit-order, 14.5) are the exact breaking input; recorded (qty,unit_cost,id) alone cannot recover them. Variance measured & material: running_avg FIFO 0.7% (low) -> 32% (high) rel, and BIASED under a cost trend (FIFO +58k / LIFO -121k). Native harness seed is constant-cost -> zero variance (tooling finding for acct-0at4.12: needs a cost-volatility knob). Feeds acct-0at4.12 as recalc requirements R-1/R-2.

title: ledger-v3.1 testing: concurrency verification (proptest + loom + stateright + fault injection)
description:
Source: FEEDBACK-TESTING.md #3, #4, #5.

Control the schedule; don't pray for it. "Run 1000 callers and check the end state" finds races at whatever rate the OS scheduler feels like. Four layers:

- **proptest at the ledger-core boundary:** arbitrary interleavings of receipts/depletions with adversarial values — qty=1, qty near i64 bounds, unit_cost=0, costs straddling the rounding cliff, value_sum near i64 on the accumulation path. Properties: model equivalence (reference-oracle issue), monotone value_sum for running_avg receipts, receipts-only permutation invariance (already tested), and **negative-value_sum reachability for standard basis** — now the correct, expected behavior post-0009; the property *pins* it (the old CHECK is gone).

- **loom for the shmem core:** staging/committer queue CAS transitions, arena alloc/free, identity-registry generation protocol. 2–3 threads, exhaustive interleavings including the weak-memory reorderings the `Ordering::` choices permit. This actually *verifies* the AUDIT "memory ordering is sound" claim rather than asserting it.

- **stateright (or TLA+) for the cross-process protocols** loom can't reach: router/committer/recovery, claim–die–reclaim, generation-vs-pid-recycling, eject/backpressure interlock. Check liveness (every committed-caller submission eventually terminal) and safety (no submission processed twice, none orphaned forever). The pid-recycling liveness hole (FEEDBACK #15) and the backpressure livelock (FEEDBACK #5) are exactly the shape a model checker finds in minutes.

- **Deterministic fault injection via the existing `test_hooks` feature:** pause a committer between pre-flight dedup and INSERT (forces the 23505 re-drive path); kill between COMMIT and cleanup CAS (reclaim-of-completed-work); kill router mid-`processing`; a `kill -9` postmaster loop ×N with an invariant sweep after each restart. Force every §6.5/§6.8 branch rather than hoping to hit it.

## Acceptance
loom suite green on the shmem state machines; a stateright/TLA+ model with liveness + safety properties checked; each §6.5/§6.8 branch has a forcing test; a kill-9 postmaster loop runs clean under the conservation-invariant sweep.
notes: RE-SCOPED by GATE VERDICT (acct-0at4.11.5, design-v3.1 §18). DROP the shmem targets (machinery deleted): loom for the shmem core, stateright/TLA+ for the router/committer/recovery/eject cross-process protocol, and the shmem-specific test_hooks fault injection. KEEP: ledger-core proptest (model equivalence, value_sum monotonicity, permutation invariance, negative-value_sum reachability) and the kill-9-postmaster loop + conservation-invariant sweep, now run against the staging table. A light stateright model of the SKIP LOCKED drain is optional.
close_reason:
Delivered the two mandatory layers of the re-scoped issue (gate verdict acct-0at4.11.5 dropped the shmem targets — loom / stateright-for-shmem / shmem fault injection — since that machinery was deleted).

Part 1 (commit 0cc348f): ledger-oracle/tests/proptest_model_equivalence.rs — a pure-Rust property-based differential at the ledger-core boundary driving plan_apply_provisional and the independent ModelLedger on the same proptest-generated interleavings with adversarial values (qty=1, near i64 bounds, unit_cost=0, banker-rounding cliff, value_sum near i64). Four properties: model equivalence, monotone value_sum for running_avg receipts, receipts-only permutation invariance, negative-value_sum reachability for the standard basis (pins post-0009). 20k cases/property green in ~1.5s. Surfaced (and correctly normalized) a benign oracle None-vs-(0,0,0) representation quirk the .4 DB differential never hit.

Part 2 (commit 3175c05): scripts/kill9-staging-recovery.sh — SIGKILLs the postmaster mid-drain over the SPIKE-A staging table, restarts (WAL crash recovery), drains the backlog, and asserts the acct-0at4.5 conservation sweep is clean. 3/3 iterations clean with ~50k in-flight rows recovered per crash. Invariant: claim+apply+mark-done is one tx so a crash is all-or-nothing, and trx UNIQUE (trx_type, source_id) forbids double-apply.

The optional light stateright model of the SKIP LOCKED drain was scoped out per user decision and captured as follow-up acct-0at4.14 (P3).

title: ledger-v3.1 testing: conservation-invariant SQL sweep as a post-run post-condition
description:
Source: FEEDBACK-TESTING.md #2.

A cheap SQL sweep run after every test and every bench run, catching whole bug classes no unit test targets:

- per pool: `pool_state.qty` (layer_id=0) == `Σ trx_line.qty` for that pool.
- `value_sum` == net posted amounts (the §3.1 GL-reconcilable claim — *tested*, not asserted).
- every trx has ≥1 trx_line; every trx_line has its expected posting_lines.
- `Σ debits == Σ credits` per posting_event across the run.
- no `(trx_type, source_id)` duplicates; every completed harness submission has exactly one trx **XOR** a recorded drop reason.

The last invariant requires the harness to keep its own durable log of what it submitted (the caller-side outbox from the ARCH roll-up, #6). "trx exists iff submission completed" is currently unverifiable because nothing records intent.

**Post-0009 correction:** the value_sum invariant is `value_sum == net posted amounts` (which *can be negative* for standard-basis pools), NOT `value_sum ≥ 0`. See design §14.1 / §15 as reconciled — a sweep that asserts non-negativity would now be wrong.

## Acceptance
Sweep is a reusable test helper + a harness `--verify` post-pass; wired into CI test teardown and the bench harness; a deliberately-injected imbalance is caught.
close_reason: Shipped conservation-invariant sweep: new ledger-verify crate (run_conservation_sweep), method-aware value reconciliation (C1 qty, C2a accumulator tail-since-empty, C2b std/specific recompute, C2c banker_div well-formedness, C3 orphans w/ deep-seed exemption, C4 posting integrity, C5 idempotency dups) in one READ ONLY REPEATABLE READ snapshot; harness verify subcommand + run --verify + equivalence folding; opt-in run-tests.sh SWEEP teardown; 7 direct + 3 routed acceptance tests (positive incl empty-refill + negative value_sum, plus 4/2 injected imbalances caught); harness PASS->0 / FAIL->1 validated. Intent-XOR-drop invariant deferred: needs caller-side intent log (acct-0at4.3 #6). Commit 247f66c.

title: ledger-v3.1 testing: sequential reference oracle (exact + envelope mode)
description:
Source: FEEDBACK-TESTING.md #1, #5.

The single highest-leverage test artifact — everything else checks against it. A pure-Rust in-memory oracle (~300 lines): `HashMap<PoolId, ModelPool>` implementing design-v3.1 §3 semantics directly, using `num-rational` for exact arithmetic alongside the BIGINT path. Two comparison modes:

- **Exact mode** (direct flavor, single-threaded): drive the same operation sequence through the model and through `ledger_submit_trx_c`; every field matches byte-for-byte — aggregate qty, value_sum, unit_cost, trx_line contents, posting amounts, and **error-for-error (including *which* error)**.

- **Envelope mode** (routed / concurrent): exact equality is undefined per §14.2, so the model computes the *set of legal outcomes*. Given the multiset of submissions, check the actual result is explainable by *some* serialization: final qty ∈ {reachable qtys under any drop-and-continue ordering}; receipts-only pools byte-equal to `banker_div(ΣQC, ΣQ)`; every recorded trx present in the input exactly once. Enumerate orderings for small N; for large N, check the conservation invariants (see the invariant-sweep issue) + per-pool serializability of the fold.

Why this and not what exists: today's cross-flavor equivalence test (§9.4) is a *differential* oracle (direct vs routed) — it cannot catch a bug both flavors share. This adds the independent reference model.

## Acceptance
Oracle crate committed; exact-mode differential passes on the §9.2 direct scenarios; envelope-mode check runs on the §9.3 routed integration scenarios and on harness runs.
close_reason: Independent sequential reference oracle shipped (commit 6778b72). New pure-Rust crate ledger-oracle: ModelLedger re-derives §3 (WAC/provisional FIFO+LIFO/STD/specific) with independent half-to-even rounding (BigRational, cross-checked vs banker_div on ~14k inputs), transactional + error-for-error; envelope module (receipts-only exactness, reachable-qty enumeration small-N, bounds+subset-sum large-N); 22 unit tests. Exact-mode differential (ledger-direct-c) byte-for-byte vs real ledger_submit_trx_c on all §9.2 scenarios + 300-op randomized sequence — 11 tests green. Envelope-mode (ledger-routed-c) on §9.3 routed scenarios — 3 tests green — plus wired into `ledger-harness equivalence` (envelope-checks routed final qty per pool every run), validated s18 mixed PASS. All DB-validated against poc_v3_1.

title: Experiment with batch sizes + router batch-formation on a multi-SKU workload (research then implementation)
description:
Why: sustained-load benchmarking surfaced that on a multi-SKU / multi-pool (spread) workload the routed committer is starved of large commit_groups, defeating the committer-side write batching shipped in acct-sczx / acct-e95d / acct-q6sx.

Evidence (5-min sustained runs, committed at 73467f2):
- Baseline (single pool, single-push, cc=1): commit_group_size_avg ~180 DOCUMENTS, ~14,765 trx/s median, apply 49.7 us/trx, fsync 12.3 us/trx (18 pct), committer CPU-bound (on-CPU 83 pct, lock ~0).
- Slight step-up (cc=4, 16 callers, 64 pools, same workload shape): commit_group_size_avg collapsed to ~8 documents, ~5,314 trx/s median (about 2.8x SLOWER), fsync 328.8 us/trx (52 pct of committer time), staging-ring shmem-LWLock 52.7 pct of busy.

Root cause is router batch-FORMATION, not the committer: the router groups by pool affinity (union-find by pool overlap, design-v3.1 section 6.3, router.rs affinity_group) and emits one commit_group per pool-component by default. On a hot-pool workload (the case Path C was built to win, sections 6.1 / 6.5 / 6.6) that fuses many callers on one pool into a big group. On a spread there is no hot pool, so each component is tiny and groups fragment -- per-group fixed costs (fsync, decode, hydrate, the batched-INSERT setup) amortize over ~8 documents instead of ~180. router_pack_disjoint (acct-xdwk, default OFF) is an existing half-measure that bin-packs disjoint components up to batch_size_max.

INVARIANT to preserve: a document (submission) is atomic. batch_size_max caps the number of DOCUMENTS per commit_group, never lines; one submission carries all its lines in one staging entry (payload.rs encode_submission, line_count is u32) and is never split. Any batch-formation change MUST keep document atomicity.

PHASE 1 -- RESEARCH (characterize):
Use the parameterized runner ledger-harness/bench/run-sustained-5min.sh on a MULTI-SKU / multi-pool workload. Sweep:
- batch_size_max in {50, 100, 200, 400, 800}
- router batch-formation policy: affinity-first (current default) vs router_pack_disjoint=on vs (if warranted) a prototype queue-fill-first policy (take N documents off the queue regardless of pool, affinity as a secondary preference)
- caller / committer counts (e.g. cc in {1,4}, callers in {16,64})
Measure per cell: commit_group_size_avg in DOCUMENTS, throughput (trx/s + trx_line/s + posting_line/s quartiles), fsync pct and us/trx, staging-LWLock pct of busy, apply us/trx, caller ack + committed latency.
Answer: does pack_disjoint=on restore cg toward batch_size_max and recover throughput on the spread? Is queue-fill-first batch-formation warranted as the default? What batch_size_max default best trades throughput vs caller latency? Does any change regress the hot-pool aggregation case (s5 / s7)?
Deliverable: a committed results/ writeup with the sweep table + a recommendation.

PHASE 2 -- IMPLEMENTATION (based on the research recommendation):
Implement the chosen router batch-formation change. Candidates: make queue-fill-first the default batch-formation (affinity demoted to a routing preference), flip router_pack_disjoint default on, and/or retune the batch_size_max default. Preserve document atomicity and the hot-pool cross-caller aggregation win (one pool_lock + one aggregate UPSERT per pool per group). Ship property / acceptance tests (affinity grouping, document-atomicity / no-split-of-a-submission) and a re-measurement confirming multi-SKU amortization is restored without regressing hot-pool (s5/s7).
design: Document atomicity invariant: a submission is one staging entry carrying all its lines (payload.rs encode_submission, line_count u32); the router chunks SETS of submissions at batch_size_max, never a single submission (router.rs chunker, chunk_cap = batch_size_max documents). Lever space: router batch-formation in router_tick (affinity_group + optional pack_disjoint_components, router.rs) and GUCs batch_size_max / batch_window_us / router_pack_disjoint. Keep the hot-pool cross-caller aggregation win (design-v3.1 section 6.5).
acceptance_criteria: Phase 1: a committed results/ writeup sweeping batch_size_max x router batch-formation policy on a multi-SKU workload, reporting commit_group_size_avg in documents, throughput quartiles, and a fsync/LWLock breakdown per cell, plus a recommendation. Phase 2: the recommended router batch-formation change implemented with tests preserving document atomicity, and a re-measurement showing multi-SKU commit_group size and throughput recover toward the batch_size_max-filled regime without regressing the hot-pool (s5/s7) aggregation case.
notes: Phase 1 DONE — results/p1al_batch_formation_sweep.md. Finding: router_pack_disjoint=ON is strictly win-or-neutral across all regimes. Spread s2 (64-pool): cg 8.1->148 at bsm200, throughput 2.06x, committed-p99 58.8s->4.0s (14.6x), fsync 52%->7.5%. Deep s7: cg 3.8->163, +170% (WALWrite->row-lock). s5 single hot pool: inert (cg unchanged 164->166, pack has no disjoint components to fuse) — fresh current-build OFF vs ON, +1-7% noise. s19 mixed: neutral +1% (already row-lock-bound). Structural reason it never regresses: pack fuses only pool-DISJOINT components -> still one pool_lock+one UPSERT per pool, no new same-pool contention; pure commit/fsync amortization. Recommendation for Phase 2: flip router_pack_disjoint default ON + raise batch_size_max default 50->200 (the knee; 800 adds only +15% at rising pool_lock/row-lock). Queue-fill-first prototype NOT warranted. NOT run: finer bsm 100/400 on spread (knee bracketed at 200). Harness: added PACK_DISJOINT knob to run-sustained-5min.sh; new sweep-p1al-{decisive,nonregress}.sh.
close_reason: Phase 1+2 complete. Research: router_pack_disjoint=ON strictly win-or-neutral across all regimes (spread 2.06x + committed-p99 14.6x better, deep-zipf s7 +170%, mixed s19 neutral, single-hot-pool s5 inert) — writeup results/p1al_batch_formation_sweep.md (commit 2ec4872). Implementation (commit 83b51a5): lib.rs ROUTER_PACK_DISJOINT default ON + BATCH_SIZE_MAX 50->200; two document-atomicity unit tests on pack_disjoint_components (11/11 green); run-sustained restore aligned. Verified: pg_settings boot_val on/200, default-path routed run cg 83 vs 8.1 OFF baseline, 0 dropped. Queue-fill-first prototype NOT warranted. Follow-ups filed: cross-stream restore-trap alignment.

title: Committer apply hot path: batch SPI writes across the commit group + prepared plans
description:
Motivation (acct-q6sx flamegraph + span counters): the committer apply ceiling (~4900 trx/s, ~160us/trx at cc=1) is per-statement SQL execution via SPI. Self-time DSO rollup: 89.4% postgres binary (executor), 2.5% our Rust, 0.6% pg_stat_statements self (~33% in-path). >=37.7% of samples through SPI_execute_with_args. NOT WAL (5%), NOT Rust (the per-trx snapshot.clone is a non-issue at 2.5%).

Root cause in ledger-spi-common/src/bulk_write.rs driven by committer.rs plan_and_write (lines 663-716): apply runs PER SUBMISSION inside the group loop and issues many one-shot (re-planned) SPI statements:
- insert_trx (8.1): SINGLE-ROW Spi::get_one_with_args per submission -> 171 single-row INSERTs for a 171-trx group.
- insert_trx_lines (8.2): bulk UNNEST but one-shot, once per submission (~171 calls).
- apply_pool_state_mutations (8.3): up to 3 one-shot UNNEST stmts per submission (~hundreds/group; the aggregate is already collapsed once at end).
- insert_posting_lines (8.4): bulk one-shot per submission (~171 calls).
=> ~700+ parse+plan+execute cycles per group of 171, ALL one-shot (Spi::*_with_args / client.select with inline args) so Postgres re-parses+re-plans every call.

Two levers:
1) CROSS-SUBMISSION BATCHING. Separate PLAN (sequential, must stay ordered for WAC running-average; cheap in Rust at 2.5%) from WRITE (batchable). Accumulate all planned rows, then issue ONE multi-row INSERT per table per group: trx, trx_line, posting_line, pool_state. insert_trx single-row -> multi-row is the easiest big win (171 -> 1). Complication: the trx.id -> trx_line.id -> posting_line.trx_line_id FK chain and RETURNING-id alignment across submissions (the UNNEST WITH ORDINALITY + ORDER BY ord pattern already in insert_trx_lines generalizes).
2) PREPARED/CACHED PLANS. Replace one-shot Spi::*_with_args with backend-lifetime prepared statements (SPI_prepare + SPI_keepplan, or a pgrx PreparedStatement cached in a thread_local). The committer is a long-lived BGWorker so a plan cache amortizes across all groups.

Also evaluate pg_stat_statements: it sits in ~33% of sample call paths (instruments every statement); measure its hot-path cost and decide if it belongs on the committer path in production.

Acceptance: re-run ledger-harness/bench/{measure-apply-spans,setup-cc1-for-perf}.sh and show apply-ns/trx down + throughput up + SPI_execute_with_args share reduced. Optional first step: install postgresql-18-dbgsym and re-fold /tmp/committer.perf.data to split the 89% (parse/plan vs heap/index/WAL) and target the dominant lever.

Discovered-from acct-q6sx (measurement); not blocked by it.
design: Lever B first (prepared/cached plans). Per acct-q6sx STEP 0 (commit 5a63266), ~47% of committer CPU is parse+analyze+plan (per-statement, identical every call, eliminable); execute is ~17%. Cache the SPI plans in the long-lived committer BGWorker (SPI_keepplan, or pgrx PreparedStatement in a thread_local) so each apply statement is parsed+planned once and re-executed thereafter. Statements are already parameterized (Spi::*_with_args), so a saved generic plan reuses across commit groups. Low risk: no FK id-chain / WAC-ordering restructure. Lever A (cross-submission batching) layered after, measured.
notes: Lever B (prepared/cached plans) shipped + verified: commit bf03add (code), 598432a (STEP 3 measurement). cc=1 measured: apply CPU/trx 217.8us->85.1us (2.56x less), apply% 89.3->74.6, throughput ~4900->~9950 trx/s (~2.0x). Correctness: run-tests.sh --path both 8/8 binaries green. STEP 0 finding/flamegraph in commit 5a63266. Proceeding to Lever A (cross-submission batching) for the residual per-statement SPI/executor framing (~5x ceiling target).
close_reason: Both levers shipped + correctness-verified + measured. Lever B (prepared/cached SPI plans) bf03add, measured 598432a. Lever A (cross-submission batched commit-group write) a88d2ed, measured 7a9cf14. Cumulative cc=1: apply CPU/trx 217.8->45.8us (4.76x less), apply% 89.3->62.4, throughput ~4900->~15550 trx/s (~3.2x). Correctness: run-tests.sh --path both 8/8 binaries / 38 tests green for each lever. Motivated by acct-q6sx STEP 0 (5a63266). Residual prep+fsync floor exposed by this work tracked as acct-e95d.

title: Proper committer benchmarking: use pgrx #[pg_bench] for apply-path microbench + flamegraph for CPU breakdown
description:
Why: all committer perf data so far is coarse and black-box. We have THREE instruments: end-to-end throughput (black box), a pg_stat_activity wait-event sampler (CPU-vs-IO only, not which code), and in-process ns counters (apply-vs-commit split only). We have NEVER profiled the committer — no flamegraph, no per-function CPU breakdown. The end-to-end harness (callers -> staging ring -> router -> committer) CANNOT isolate the apply-CPU ceiling because the staging-ring LWLock starves committers as caller count rises (busy_frac 0.92 at cc=1 -> 0.14 at cc=4; see acct-ruex results/affinity_1sku_batched.csv).

Robust facts established: commit/fsync = 4.0 pct of committer time (ns counters AND wait-sampler io_of_busy independently agree); apply pipeline = 96 pct, internal breakdown UNKNOWN. Anomaly: committer pipeline_count implies 0.63 trx/group vs harness cg_avg ~115 — disagree ~180x, so the coarse counters are NOT trustworthy for fine conclusions.

Tooling verified present (2026-06-01): pgrx 0.18.0 — our exact pinned version — ships cargo pgrx bench + the #[pg_bench] macro: Criterion-style benchmarks that run IN-PROCESS inside a live Postgres backend with full SPI access, with a persistent pgrx_bench schema (git metadata + pg_settings snapshots + history). We are NOT using it. perf 7.0.0 + cargo-flamegraph + flamegraph are installed on the host (perf_event_paranoid currently 4 — must be lowered to <=1 for unprivileged attach; sudo needed).

What to do:
1. #[pg_bench] microbench of the committer apply path (build a Prepared batch, call plan_and_write/attempt_commit_phase) with NO ingress (no staging lock, no router) -> the committer single-core apply ceiling with criterion stats + regression history. This is the ceiling the end-to-end harness cannot reach.
2. Pure-commit floor: trivial BEGIN/INSERT/COMMIT at 1 backend (#[pg_bench] or pgbench) -> bounds what is even possible on this host.
3. Flamegraph the committer at cc=1 (perf record -F 999 -g --call-graph dwarf -p <committer_pid> for ~20s during steady load) -> WHERE the 96 pct apply CPU goes (candidates: SPI parse/plan, pool_lock FOR UPDATE, hydration SELECT, bulk_write INSERTs, aggregate UPDATE, line decode). #[pg_bench] gives time-per-op; flamegraph gives time-per-function — complementary.

Prereqs/risks: confirm the release .so carries frame pointers/debuginfo (profile.release debug=true) or the flamegraph is a wall of [unknown]; apply path fns may be private / assume committer shmem context and need a thin test harness to drive; lower perf_event_paranoid for the perf run (user runs sudo).

Acceptance: a reproducible #[pg_bench] apply-path number + a committer flamegraph SVG naming the top apply-CPU consumers; the trx/group counter anomaly resolved or documented as untrustworthy.
notes: STEP 0 done (commit 5a63266): committer apply 89% split via symbol-resolved perf. Inclusive: raw parse 8.5% + analyze/rewrite 21.9% + plan 16.9% = ~47% per-statement planning (eliminable); execute (ExecModifyTable heap/index/WAL) ~16.7%. GetCachedPlan 17.6% is NOT caching (one-shot SPI re-plans every call). pg_stat_statements ~1% (jumble), not the coarse ~33%. Resolved flamegraph results/committer_resolved.svg + results/committer_apply_phase_split.md. Flamegraph half of acceptance met; optional remaining item is the pgrx pg_bench apply-path microbench. Decided Lever B (prepared plans) first on acct-sczx.
close_reason: Acceptance met across all three items. (a) In-process apply-path microbench shipped (commit 0648a7f): ledger_routed_c_bench_apply, a bench_hooks-gated pg_extern timing plan_and_write in a rolled-back subtx with NO ingress; 39.7 us/trx at batch 183 vs the span-measured ~44 us/trx (two independent instruments agree within ~10%), irreducible floor ~36 us/trx, fixed per-call INSERT/UPSERT overhead amortizing from 103 us/trx at batch 1; committed==batch on every row. Chose the Docker-native in-process bench over literal cargo pgrx bench: the latter cannot target the running Docker acct-postgres (installs to local pkglibdir + owns its own pgrx-managed postmaster, no attach-to-running-server mode) and would need a separate cluster + hand-injected sqlx base schema + shared_preload, not worth it for a number already had from the span counter. (b) Flamegraph done (5a63266): named the ~47 pct per-statement planning since removed by sczx prepared plans. (c) trx/group anomaly documented: a cc=4 staging-starvation artifact (pipeline_count counts empty drains); at cc=1 counters are trustworthy (trx_per_group ~183 = cg_avg), independently corroborated by the bench-vs-span agreement at cc=1. Writeup results/apply_inproc_microbench.md. Production .so restored clean (bench fn absent, to_regproc IS NULL; GUCs at defaults).

title: Path C routed: raise hot-pool throughput via batching then committer→pool affinity
description: Measured bottleneck (acct-235v): on hot/Pareto workloads the committers serialize on the per-pool row lock. SELECT FROM pool_lock WHERE pool_id=$1 FOR UPDATE is 78.4% of all DB time (29ms mean on hot pools); a live committer-bgworker wait sample shows 92% of committer wait-time in Lock/transactionid. Not WAL/fsync (WALInsert ~1 sample), not IO, not the router (router scans ~9 entries/tick, defers <2%, keeps up). Root cause: the committer claim queue has NO pool affinity (committer.rs:210 first-come CAS), and affinity_group (router.rs:358) dedupes a pool only WITHIN one tick, so the same hot pool's groups across consecutive ticks land on different committers and block on each other's FOR UPDATE. s6 (disjoint) scales 958->1791 with committers; s10/s11 (Pareto) flat ~1390; s5 (single pool, coalesced to cg=27-32) is the FASTEST cell (2705 trx/s) because one big group => one committer => no cross-committer handoff. Two levers, explore in order: (1) BATCHING -- wider coalescing window / higher batch_size_max so a hot pool drains in one larger group per tick, amortizing the ~29ms lock handoff over more trx (throughput on a contended pool ~= trx-per-group / (lock-hold + handoff)). Caveat: cg is arrival-bound -- the window can only coalesce submissions that have arrived, so at low offered concurrency (50c Pareto) cg stays ~9-12 regardless; batching bites where same-pool concurrency exists. (2) AFFINITY -- pin a pool to a single committer (route by pool hash) so its lock is taken sequentially by one worker with zero cross-committer wait; the lock becomes uncontended. Deliverable: characterize batching gains + latency cost (this issue starts the batch-size sweeps), then design/prototype committer->pool affinity. Bench-only; no production-path change required to characterize. Cross-ref acct-235v POC-REPORT.md section (g).
design:
RESUME PLAN — begin acct-xdwk.

STEP 0: bd update acct-xdwk --claim.

STEP 1 — Lever 1b: router disjoint-component PACKING (production-path change to ledger-routed-c/src/router.rs).
  WHY: measured (see notes) — batch_size_max only helps when a pool's submissions cluster (s5 4.7x). On spread/Pareto workloads cg plateaus at ~10 because affinity_group (router.rs:358, union-find on pool overlap) emits ONE commit_group per connected component (emit loop router.rs:182) and never packs disjoint components, so commit/fsync is not amortized (s19 single-drain stuck ~1000 trx/s, cg~10).
  CHANGE: in router_tick, after affinity_group() returns components, greedily BIN-PACK disjoint components into commit_groups of size <= batch_size_max, then emit; a single component > cap still chunks (existing behavior).
  SAFE BY CONSTRUCTION: affinity_group already unions ALL same-pool submissions into one component, so each pool appears in exactly one component per tick -> packing disjoint components preserves the "one pool -> one group per tick" invariant; no new cross-group pool overlap, no new FOR UPDATE contention. Keep members sorted by request_seq within each source component; order emitted groups by min request_seq.
  SURFACE DESIGN CHOICES FIRST (AskUserQuestion, per user pattern, before editing): (a) GUC-gate it (e.g. router_pack_disjoint bool default off) vs change default; (b) pack policy greedy first-fit vs sort-components-by-size desc; (c) whether to also bump default batch_window_us so a tick accumulates more components to pack.
  BUILD/INSTALL: scripts/install-routed-c.sh (rebuilds .so + regenerates SQL + restart; keeps minimal preload since ledger_routed_c already in list).
  TEST: rebuild WITH_TEST_HOOKS=1; run ledger-routed-c tests — tests/acceptance_routed_affinity_grouping.rs, tests/acceptance_routed_enqueue.rs, tests/property_ledger_enqueue_trx_c.rs (affinity-grouping correctness + idempotency MUST hold). Cluster-per-binary if cross-test flake.
  MEASURE: ledger-harness/bench/run-batch-size-sweep.sh on s19 at cc=1 AND cc=4, before/after; expect cg to break past ~10 and throughput to rise on spread workloads. Re-check s10/s11. Load-gated.

STEP 2 — Lever 2: committer->pool AFFINITY (bigger change; after 1b lands).
  Route by pool-hash -> fixed committer so a hot pool's FOR UPDATE is taken sequentially by ONE worker (kills the 29ms cross-committer handoff = 78% of DB time). Touches the committer claim model (committer.rs:210, currently first-come CAS, no affinity). Measure s10/s11 committer-count scaling — expect them to scale like s6 (disjoint) once affinity removes the shared-lock handoff.

ENVIRONMENT (carry forward):
  - Cluster acct-postgres (docker), DB poc_v3_1, MINIMAL preload pg_stat_statements,pg_cron,ledger_routed_c. pgbouncer:6432 for s5-s9 only.
  - Host is a DAILY-DRIVER WORKSTATION; Chrome swings throughput ~2x. ALWAYS load-gate (common.sh::wait_for_quiet_host, LOAD_GATE=1.5); check /proc/loadavg + ps -eo pcpu,comm|grep chrome before trusting absolutes. Correctness counters are load-robust.
  - committer_count read once at _PG_init -> RESTART to change. batch_size_max / batch_window_us are GucContext::Sighup (live via ALTER SYSTEM + pg_reload_conf).
  - DROP DATABASE wedges the committer (orphans cluster-lifetime arena) -> clean MUST docker-restart (restart_db already in the scripts).
  - results/*.json gitignored; CSVs committed. Branch worktree-poc-31. User policy: commit when bench is clean.
  - Tooling caution: do NOT over-batch dependent Bash calls (one error cancels the batch); avoid heredocs in the Bash tool (shell-snapshot input buffer got garbled this session) — prefer Write-to-file then read.
notes:
LEVER 2 (committer->pool affinity) — REVERTED + CHARACTERIZED as a dead-end. Negative-result writeup committed e9a77d8 (POC-REPORT §g lever-2 subsection + AFFINITY bench knob + results/committer_count_sweep_s1{0,1}_aff{off,on}.csv). Production claim-path code git-checked-out — refuted optimization kept out of the committer hot path.

MEASURED (load-gated committer_count sweep 2/4/8, affinity off vs on):
  s10 (Pareto receipts 50c):  off 1280/1374/1376  on 1221/1352/1407  (neutral)
  s11 (Pareto receipts 200c): off 1080/1194/1258  on  967/1069/1194  (~10% WORSE)
Affinity throughput-neutral-to-negative; does NOT make the flat committer-count curve scale.

WHY: acct-235v 78%-FOR-UPDATE was a single-hot-pool profile; real Pareto receipts touch ~13.5 pools/trx. Min-pool
affinity leaves the other ~12 pools contended across groups and just fragments commit_groups (cg 12->7). A pool-set
affinity cannot help (a 13-pool group cannot be one-committer-owned without re-serializing). Only s5 single-pool would
benefit, and it is already the fastest cell.

BOTH LEVERS NOW EXPLORED: lever 1b (disjoint-component packing) SHIPPED 9de2a50 = the real win; lever 2 REFUTED+characterized e9a77d8.
Cluster clean (reverted .so reinstalled; committer_affinity GUC gone, router_pack_disjoint stays off, committer_count=4).
close_reason: Both levers resolved. Lever 1 + 1b: batch-size sweep + router disjoint-component packing (router_pack_disjoint GUC) is the shipped throughput win (03f0f46, 9de2a50) — breaks the spread-workload cg plateau (12->66 at cap=200), ~5.5x fewer commits/fsyncs, correctness green off and on. Lever 2: committer->pool affinity (hash(min pool_id) % committer_count + age-gated steal) measured throughput-neutral on s10 and ~10% worse on s11, never converts the flat committer-count curve to a scaling one; root cause is Pareto receipts touch ~13.5 pools/trx so min-pool keying cannot isolate hot-pool contention. Production claim-path code reverted; kept the AFFINITY bench knob, the four sweep CSVs, and the POC-REPORT (g) characterization (e9a77d8). Rigorous redo of affinity tracked as acct-0usf.

title: P4: ledger-harness (3 submission modes + deep-pool seeding + lock-hold metric)
description: Adapt ledger-v3/ledger-harness: cli.rs subcommands (seed-pools, run, equivalence); drivers driver_direct (per-call), new driver_direct_batched (section 5.5/10.0), driver_routed (enqueue + poll completion); seed.rs deep-pool seeding via direct SQL into pool_state plus matching trx_line receipts (section 10.5); metrics.rs (throughput, per-trx lock-hold time, fsync rate, WAL volume, deadlock-retry/poison counts, HDR histograms, JSON); scenarios S1-S8 (section 10.6); bench/run-*.sh + results/.
design: The hot path never creates FIFO/LIFO layer rows, so deep pools are seeded by direct SQL (pool_state + consistent trx_line receipts), not by driving ingestion.
acceptance_criteria: pools are seedable to depths 10/100/1000; all three modes drive S1-S8 and emit JSON reports; equivalence --scenario s7 runs both flavors; the per-trx lock-hold metric is captured per depth.
notes:
RESUME / P4 START HERE (ledger-harness; P3.4 done & closed, P4 ready — NOT yet claimed).

WHERE THINGS STAND:
- Epic acct-2ttr. Closed: P1.1 5e077ad, P1.2 e574ee8, P2/acct-2ttr.3 8ea7b3c, P3.1/acct-2ttr.4 f36d741, P3.2/acct-2ttr.5 5c6e8cf, P3.3/acct-2ttr.6 e7cb6b4, P3.4/acct-2ttr.7 42b44ab. PAUSE gate acct-1wyk closed. Only P4 (acct-2ttr.8) + P5 (acct-2ttr.9) remain.
- Workspace poc/ledger-v3.1/ builds clean. DB poc_v3_1 on localhost:5111 (postgres://acct:acct_dev@localhost:5111/poc_v3_1), container acct-postgres, max_worker_processes=32 (ALTER SYSTEM). Both extensions installed: ledger_direct_c (CREATEd), ledger_routed_c (PRELOADED+CREATEd). Reinstall: bash scripts/install-direct-c.sh / install-routed-c.sh (routed always restarts the container; WITH_TEST_HOOKS=1 for tests). Integration runner: bash scripts/run-tests.sh --path direct|routed|both (cluster-per-binary). pgrx pg18=/usr/bin/pg_config; cargo-pgrx skill. BD worktree gotcha: if bd shows 0 issues, recreate .beads/redirect=../../../.beads; never bd init.
- ledger-harness is currently a 13-line stub (src/main.rs only). Cargo.toml exists.

P4 SCOPE (design-v3.1 Phase 4, spec lines 972-985; §10 / §10.0 / §10.5 / §10.6 / §11). Adapt poc/ledger-v3/ledger-harness/ (4359 lines: cli 120, driver_direct 296, driver_routed 635, equivalence 1619, main 166, measure 261, pool_universe 194, report 329, sampler 244, scenarios 230, workload 265 + tests/smoke_*). It is a SEPARATE binary (sqlx + tokio multi-session PG client, NOT pgrx). Deliverables:
(1) cli.rs — subcommands seed-pools / run / equivalence (v3 shape, clap-derived). DSN default MUST be poc_v3_1 (v3 uses poc_v3). run takes --scenario s1..s8, --mode (THREE modes, see 2), --concurrency, --overlap, --method-mix, --depth, --batch-size, --duration, --output. Keep v3's --max-callers cap.
(2) THREE submission modes (§10.0, spec 826-828): direct-per-call (ledger_submit_trx_c once per user-tx); NEW direct-batched-per-caller (one user-tx, ledger_submit_trx_c N times, default batch 50, §5.5 spec 535-557 — NO new SPI, plain PG txn batching); routed (ledger_enqueue_trx_c + poll for trx completion). v3 has driver_direct + driver_routed; ADD driver_direct_batched. SPI NAMES are the v3.1 _c names (ledger_submit_trx_c / ledger_enqueue_trx_c) — v3 uses un-suffixed names.
(3) NEW seed.rs deep-pool seeding (§10.5, spec 866-870): Path C hot path NEVER creates FIFO/LIFO layer rows, so deep pools CANNOT be made by driving ingestion. Seed via direct SQL: bulk INSERT INTO pool_state (pool_id, layer_id, qty, unit_cost) for layer_id 1..depth PLUS matching trx_line receipt rows (so the trx_line stream stays consistent for future recalc/close replay). Depths 10/100/1000. pool_state v3.1 shape is (pool_id, layer_id, qty, unit_cost, created_at) — layer_id not layer_seq, no value_sum/last_trx_line_id. pool carries provisional_basis (running_avg|standard); standard_cost table is (sku_id, location_id, unit_cost, updated_at).
(4) metrics (measure.rs/report.rs): throughput (trx/s), PER-TRX LOCK-HOLD TIME as fn of pool depth (THE headline measurement — §11.2 spec 1003-1011; constant w.r.t. depth = the premise; if it grows, premise failed), fsync rate, WAL volume, committed trx/s, HDR histograms, JSON report. ADD deadlock-retry + poison counters (new in P3.4): read ledger_routed_c_committer_deadlock_retries_total() / _poisoned_total(). (6) equivalence.rs (§11.1, spec 950-954): cross-flavor — direct-c vs routed-c given identical input produce IDENTICAL pool_state aggregate.qty; provisional unit_costs MAY DIFFER (within-batch order, by design, not a bug — assert qty equality, allow unit_cost divergence). v3 equivalence.rs is 1619 lines (largest module) — adapt carefully to the qty-only equality + 3-mode matrix.
(7) bench/run-*.sh runners + results/ dir.

PROPERTY-TEST CONVENTION (acct-1cer): the harness is a binary, not an entry-point fn, so property_*.rs per-fn does not apply; v3 ships tests/smoke_measure.rs + smoke_sampler.rs — port equivalents.

ACCEPTANCE (bd): pools seedable to depths 10/100/1000; all 3 modes drive S1-S8 + emit JSON; equivalence --scenario s7 runs both flavors; per-trx lock-hold metric captured per depth.

GOTCHAS — READ BEFORE RUNNING:
- HARD TIMEOUT every harness/load run (timeout 600 ...) and background it (run_in_background, no timeout arg). P3.4 lesson: a bug wedged a backend in an LWLock-holding CPU spin for 68 min ignoring SIGTERM. The arena now has a bounded-walk guard, but always cap wall-time so nothing can wedge the session again.
- pgbouncer for >~100 concurrent callers (memory project_pocv3_pgbouncer / acct-8cn2): S5/S7/S8 use 1000 callers — PG max_connections cannot hold 1000 direct sessions. Either front poc_v3_1 with pgbouncer/pgcat (production posture) OR use v3's --max-callers cap and document the cap. Surface this choice when claiming; do NOT silently cap-and-pretend-1000.
