title: Update design-v3.md §3.1 for acct-h5gs WAC cumulative-sum semantic
description:
Spec §3.1 describes WAC's pool_state.unit_cost as the running average (per-receipt formula divides by new_qty). Migration 0006 (acct-h5gs) shifted the semantic: WAC's pool_state.unit_cost now stores cumulative value_sum = Σ(receipt_qty × receipt_unit_cost) − Σ(per-depletion rounded amount). Running per-unit cost is computed on demand as unit_cost / NULLIF(qty, 0); never stored.

Three patches needed (audit acct-b4z4 D1.2):

1. Rewrite §3.1 receipt formula to cumulative-sum:
     qty       += Q
     unit_cost += Q × C   [EXACT, commutative, associative]
   and depletion to:
     amount    = (Q × unit_cost) / qty   [single bounded round]
     qty      -= Q
     unit_cost -= amount   [exact subtraction]

2. Add per-method storage-contract note: pool_state.unit_cost carries different semantics per method (per-layer for FIFO/LIFO/specific, cumulative value_sum for WAC + WacPeriodic).

3. Add to §13 (concerns) the column-naming footgun: pool_state.unit_cost name is now misleading for WAC pools. Cross-ref acct-h5gs and acct-mcey (the equivalence drift that motivated the fix).

Reason: same as wac_periodic spec patch — Phase 7 measurement-cycle anchors on the spec; bench math depends on the correct per-method cost model. See AUDIT.md §1 D1.2.

title: Router: per-pool sequence numbers for inter-window FIFO ordering (multi-pool atomic submissions)
description:
ROUTING CORRECTNESS GAP: inter-window same-pool ordering for multi-pool atomic submissions.

PROBLEM (user-framed, acct-9mgx.1 thread):

A single submission is atomic across all pools it touches. Real workloads have multi-pool submissions: a work-order for ASM A consumes SKUs b, c, d, so ASM A's submission has lines for pools {b, c, d}. All three must commit together.

When a subsequent submission for ASM X arrives touching pools {y, z, b}, the router needs to know that pool b is currently held by ASM A's in-flight commit_group, so ASM X must wait for ASM A to commit before touching b. Today the router has no in-flight registry — it scans the staging queue, sees ASM X, has no awareness of what pools are currently held by claimed-but-not-committed commit_groups. Net result: ASM X's committer races ASM A's for pool_lock(b), can acquire it first, violates submission-order FIFO across time-windows.

acct-aywu's per-pool no-split (intra-window) does not address this — it only constrains how a single router scan splits its work. The inter-window ordering across scans needs a separate mechanism.

DESIGN: per-pool sequence numbers + happens-before DAG

In-shmem table: pool_seq[pool_id] = (latest_assigned_seq, latest_committed_seq).

1. Router stamps each commit_group with per-pool sequence numbers for every pool it touches: ASM A's group → {b: 5, c: 3, d: 7}. Increment pool_seq[pi].latest_assigned atomically.

2. Committer claiming a commit_group reads its per-pool seqs. Cannot acquire pool_lock(pi) until pool_seq[pi].latest_committed >= my_seq[pi] - 1. Per-pool wait, no global serialization.

3. On commit, committer bumps pool_seq[pi].latest_committed = my_seq[pi] for each touched pool.

4. Cross-pool parallelism preserved: a commit_group touching only pool y proceeds immediately if y has no in-flight predecessor. ASM X (b, y, z) waits ONLY for ASM A's pool b commit; can proceed in parallel on y, z with other unrelated work.

WHY THIS IS BETTER THAN ALTERNATIVES:

- "All-in-one-group within window" (the naive extension of acct-aywu): under union-find propagation, any submission touching any FIFO pool drags all transitively-overlapping submissions into one mega-group. Serializes far more than necessary.
- "Single committer for order-sensitive pools": kills cross-pool parallelism even on disjoint pools.
- "Pool_lock as ordering primitive": already in use today, but provides mutual exclusion not ordering. Lock-acquisition order != commit_group-creation order.

Per-pool sequence numbers serialize ONLY actual same-pool work across windows. Cross-pool parallelism survives. WAC and WAC_periodic pools can opt out (their commutativity makes the seq-wait unnecessary), so only order-sensitive pools pay the wait.

SCOPE:

- In-shmem pool_seq table sized for N pools (10k in current PoC; production sizing TBD).
- Router: stamp commit_groups with per-pool seqs at routing time.
- Committer: pre-pool_lock wait phase that checks predecessor commits.
- Recovery: on postmaster restart, derive latest_committed from the DB (MAX(trx_seq) per pool from trx_line) — already cached in snapshot hydration so cost is incremental.
- WAC opt-out: pools whose method is in {wac, wac_periodic} skip the wait phase.

INTERACTION WITH SIBLINGS:

- acct-aywu (per-pool no-split intra-window): still needed. acct-tm09 covers inter-window; together they form complete routing correctness for order-sensitive pools.
- acct-e5fz (batch_size_max + time-window cap): orthogonal. May affect the size of commit_groups created but not the ordering mechanism.
- acct-9mgx.1 (FIFO validation): currently shipped with committer_count=1 workaround that sidesteps both intra-window and inter-window ordering issues. After acct-aywu + acct-tm09 land, the cm=1 requirement is lifted.

ACCEPTANCE:

- Inter-window FIFO equivalence: multi-window workload with overlapping-pool submissions across windows produces byte-identical pool_state + trx + trx_line across paths (Path A serial vs Path B routed) under default GUCs (committer_count=4, batch_size_max=50).
- Multi-pool atomic submission test: ASM-style submissions binding 3+ pools commit atomically; subsequent overlapping submissions wait for predecessor's commit on shared pools only.
- Cross-pool parallelism preserved: disjoint-pool workload (s6-shape) achieves multi-committer throughput.

REFERENCES:
- acct-aywu — intra-window per-pool no-split. Sibling, not predecessor.
- acct-9mgx.1 — fifo-validation.md surfaced the gap; ships single-committer workaround.
notes:
Same correctness baseline as acct-aywu: acct-9mgx.1's cm=1 sweep (results/phase6/equivalence/run-all-fifo-2026-05-23T13-04-03Z.log) is the gold-standard regression target.

Acceptance for this issue adds inter-window scenarios on top:
- Multi-window workload: pre-populate routing such that Batch 1 (touching pools {b,c,d}) is in flight, then submit Batch 2 (touching {y,z,b}). Verify Batch 2's pool_lock(b) acquisition is gated on Batch 1's commit (per-pool seq mechanism working) and Batch 2's pool_lock(y), pool_lock(z) acquisitions proceed in parallel with other unrelated work (cross-pool parallelism preserved).
- Re-run 15-trial sweep under default GUCs after both this issue AND acct-aywu land — byte-identical to cm=1 baseline.

A new test harness binary may be needed for the multi-window inter-batch-dependency scenarios; the current equivalence harness submits one batch per path and doesn't exercise the inter-window pool-overlap case explicitly.

Router assigns seqs for order-sensitive pools at emit; committer spin-sleeps on latest_committed >= my_seq-1 before pool_lock; commit advances latest_committed via CAS-monotonic. Bench: s5 routed FIFO 2267 tx/s under cm=4 (+11% vs cm=1 post-aywu); s2 routed FIFO 1189 tx/s (-25% from predecessor-wait cost on dispersed pools — wait IS the price of correctness). cm=1 workaround no longer required. Followup acct-xjhq filed for CV+broadcast replacement of spin-sleep. Commit c422005.

title: Router: never split per-pool submissions across commit_groups for order-sensitive cost methods
description:
Discovered during acct-9mgx.1 FIFO validation. The routed path currently splits a single pool's pending submissions across multiple commit_groups when their count exceeds ledger_routed.batch_size_max (default 50). Sub-groups then commit in parallel across the committer pool, with no inter-sub-group ordering guarantee.

For FIFO (and LIFO, Specific — any cost method whose per-depletion semantics depend on layer/lot consumption order), this violates submission-order FIFO. Concrete failure documented in results/phase6/fifo-validation.md and acct-9mgx.1 close notes: under default GUCs (committer_count=4, batch_size_max=50) on a single hot pool with 1000 submissions, depletion T200 in sub-group 4 can commit before depletion T100 in sub-group 2. T200 drains the oldest layer, T100 then sees a different head layer and consumes from it instead. Each individual depletion honors "consume oldest first" for its local view, but the global trx ordering is reordered — that is not FIFO.

WAC (cumulative-sum form per acct-h5gs) is the exception that may safely split — its per-depletion math is commutative-friendly. WAC_periodic is also safe because its close-hook restatement converges regardless of within-period ordering.

WORKAROUND (current): set ledger_routed.committer_count = 1. All commit_groups serialize → submission order preserved. Comes with ~5-25% throughput cost on routed path (measured under acct-9mgx.1: s2 routed FIFO 1933→1445 tx/s, s5 routed FIFO 1791→1715). Loses cross-pool parallelism even where it would be safe.

DESIGN FIX (this issue):
- Router gains a per-pool "method-aware" rule: for pools whose cost_method ∈ {fifo, lifo, specific}, the pool's pending submissions stay in ONE commit_group regardless of batch_size_max. WAC and WAC_periodic pools may still split.
- Means: batch_size_max becomes a soft hint for order-sensitive pools and a hard cap for order-insensitive ones. Could surface as a per-pool "ordering_required" flag derived from the method enum.
- Cross-pool parallelism remains: different pools land in different commit_groups (subject to overlap union); only same-pool can't split.
- Open question: large hot-pool workloads may produce one giant commit_group that monopolizes a committer for a long pipeline_ns. Whether that needs a separate mitigation (e.g. bounded soft-split with explicit happens-before chain across sub-groups) is a follow-up to this issue, not in its scope.

ACCEPTANCE:
- Router refuses to split per-pool submissions across commit_groups for fifo/lifo/specific pools.
- acct-9mgx.1's FIFO equivalence sweep passes 15/15 byte-identical under DEFAULT GUCs (committer_count=4, batch_size_max=50) without requiring single-committer workaround.
- Bench under default config restores cross-pool routed throughput while keeping FIFO correct.
- WAC bench numbers unchanged (WAC pools continue to split freely).

REFERENCES:
- acct-9mgx.1 (parent finding) — results/phase6/fifo-validation.md
- acct-h5gs (WAC cumulative-sum context)
notes:
CORRECTNESS BASELINE: acct-9mgx.1's cm=1 sweep is the gold-standard FIFO reference. Future routed FIFO correctness work (this issue, acct-tm09) MUST regression-test against it.

Reference sweep:
- Path: poc/ledger-v3/results/phase6/equivalence/run-all-fifo-2026-05-23T13-04-03Z.log
- Config: ledger_routed.committer_count = 1
- Result: 15/15 byte-identical (s1-s6 lenient + s2/s4/s5 strict T1-T3)
- pool_state, trx, trx_line, posting_line, posting_lines_provisional all byte-equal across Path A and Path B for every run

IMPLEMENTATION FINDING (2026-05-23, aywu landed):

The original acceptance "byte-identical under DEFAULT GUCs (committer_count=4, batch_size_max=50) without single-committer workaround" cannot be satisfied by aywu alone. Root cause: the equivalence harness'\''s 1000 sequential enqueues spread across multiple router ticks under default batch_window_us=500us; committer_count=4 then lets two router windows emit independent commit_groups for the same FIFO pool, which race on trx_line UNIQUE(pool_id, trx_seq) -> pristine-replay excludes one -> 999/1000.

This is the INTER-WINDOW race scoped to acct-tm09 (per-pool sequence numbers + happens-before DAG). aywu'\''s INTRA-WINDOW per-pool no-split is necessary but not sufficient.

Amended acceptance for aywu:
- Router refuses to split per-pool submissions across commit_groups for fifo/lifo/specific pools (intra-window). VERIFIED via router_order_sensitive_groups_total counter incrementing during FIFO load.
- cm=1 sweep stays 15/15 byte-identical with aywu in place (no regression). VERIFIED: results/phase6/equivalence/run-all-fifo-2026-05-23T14-49-38Z.log
- cm=4 default-GUC byte-identical sweep blocked on acct-tm09 (filed pre-aywu close).

Post-aywu observed under cm=1:
- s4 routed Path B time dropped from ~6-8s to ~2-3s as the predicted throughput win from no-split (one giant commit_group instead of size-50 chunks). Full bench numbers in results/phase6/fifo-validation.md.
close_reason: Router emits commit_groups touching fifo/lifo/specific pools whole, ignoring batch_size_max. Thread-local pool method cache populates lazily via SPI. ledger_routed_router_order_sensitive_groups_total() exposes attribution. Verified: 15/15 byte-identical under cm=1 (results/phase6/equivalence/run-all-fifo-2026-05-23T14-49-38Z.log); routed FIFO throughput on s5 +19% (1715 -> 2038 tx/s). Scope clarification: aywu covers intra-window per-pool no-split. Inter-window race under default cm=4 is acct-tm09 (cm=1 remains required for FIFO until tm09 lands). Commit a250a22.

title: Re-architect driver_routed: fire-and-forget callers + post-window throughput
description:
Phase 5 first-pass throughput numbers are pessimized by the per-caller polling loop. Each caller blocks on `SELECT EXISTS(SELECT 1 FROM trx ...)` at 1ms tick until its own submission materializes before submitting again, so per-caller throughput ≈ 1 / (ack + committed_latency). This conflates throughput with latency and bounds Path Bs observed rate below its true ceiling — most visible on s6 where 200 callers each polling 670ms forces ~290 trx/s when the drain-rate ceiling is higher.

Refactor:
1. Fire-and-forget caller_loop: enqueue, record (source_id, enqueue_instant), iterate. No polling.
2. Spawn ONE observer task polling trx incrementally (WHERE id > last_seen_id) at 10-50ms cadence. Timestamps first appearance of each source_id.
3. Throughput = observer.seen.len() / window_duration (real materialization count).
4. Committed latency = join (source_id, enqueue_instant) with (source_id, seen_instant). Ack latency unchanged.
5. Observer continues past callers stop until committer-quiet, then final scan.

Re-run S1-S6 + compare deltas. Amend or supersede phase5-summary.md with corrected numbers and call out which Phase 5 v1 cells were pessimized.

Blocks: acct-29p8 (Phase 6 characterization should consume corrected data).
close_reason: Fire-and-forget caller_loop + dedicated observer task ships. Throughput = observer.seen.len() / window. Committed latency = join (sid, enqueue_inst) ⨯ (sid, materialize_inst). Phase 5 v2 sweep shows v1 polling pessimized Path B throughput 2.5-9.8x across all scenarios. Most significant correction: s2 (Zipf-1.5) flips from "Direct wins 1.3x" to "Routed wins 1.9x". s5 hot-pool win lifts 758x → 2110x vs Direct. Top wait events now surface real LWLock:ledger_v3_staging_queue contention (was Client:ClientRead artifact). phase5-summary-v2.md supersedes v1. Phase 6 acct-29p8 unblocked to consume corrected data.

title: ledger-routed router eject cooldown filter + last_eject_at_ns + eject_cooldown_ms GUC
description:
Per design-v3 §5.3 step 2: router must "Skip entries whose eject_count > 0 AND now - last_eject_at_ns < eject_cooldown_ms (default 10ms cooldown)." Discovered as adjacent gap during acct-qsga audit. Three pieces:

1. Add `last_eject_at_ns: AtomicU64` field to StagingEntry in shmem.rs (place after _pad2; struct grows from 96 to 104 bytes, still 8-aligned). Greenfield + volatile shmem so no migration concerns.

2. Register `ledger_routed.eject_cooldown_ms` GUC in lib.rs (default 10, range 0..=60_000, Sighup scope). Add `eject_cooldown_ms_now()` accessor.

3. Update router.rs::collect_candidates to filter: skip slot if `eject_count.load(Acquire) > 0 AND now_ns - last_eject_at_ns.load(Acquire) < cooldown_ms * 1_000_000`. Cooldown=0 disables the filter.

acct-usn2 will write last_eject_at_ns at eject time (`fetch_add(1, Release)` on eject_count, then `store(now_ns, Release)` on last_eject_at_ns); this issue ships the read side + storage.

Acceptance:
- cargo build clean
- Unit tests cover: (a) cooldown=0 disables filter, (b) eject_count==0 candidate accepted regardless of timestamp, (c) eject_count>0 + recent timestamp filtered, (d) eject_count>0 + stale timestamp accepted.
- Re-running install-routed.sh + enqueue smoke shows no regression.
close_reason: Eject cooldown filter shipped in c09e7de. Three pieces per scope: (1) StagingEntry.last_eject_at_ns AtomicU64 field added after _pad2 (struct 96->104 bytes, 8-aligned, no padding needed). (2) ledger_routed.eject_cooldown_ms GUC registered default 10ms range 0..60_000 Sighup + accessor. (3) router.rs collect_candidates accepts now_ns + cooldown_ms; pure is_in_eject_cooldown helper Acquire-loads eject_count + last_eject_at_ns, filters slots inside cooldown window. 0 disables filter. 5 new unit tests cover all 4 specified acceptance cases + defensive saturating_sub edge. 47/47 lib tests green. Live verified after container restart: GUC live, enqueue smoke unchanged (1 routed within 50ms). usn2 will Release-store last_eject_at_ns after Release-incrementing eject_count to interact with this filter.

title: ledger-direct: pool_state UPSERT collision on same-pool lines (SQLSTATE 21000)
description:
When a single submission contains multiple lines targeting the same pool (e.g. WAC pool receiving two po_receipt_lines in one trx), plan_apply emits per-line PoolStateMutation::Upsert entries with the same (pool_id, layer_seq) key. ledger-direct::bulk_write::apply_pool_state_mutations bundles them into one UNNEST INSERT ... ON CONFLICT (pool_id, layer_seq) DO UPDATE; PG rejects this with 'ON CONFLICT DO UPDATE command cannot affect row a second time' (SQLSTATE 21000). Affects s3 (3% errors with 10 callers × Complex × Uniform Mixed) and especially s4 (99% errors with 200 callers × Complex × Zipf(1.2) Mixed). Surfaced in acct-7wye v2 re-run 2026-05-21 against poc_v3 after cross-run source_id-collision noise was removed.

Repro: cargo run --release -p ledger-harness -- run --scenario s4 --path direct --duration 10s --max-callers 200 --no-sampler — with caller_loop's err arm printing the sqlx error string, every other caller fires this within seconds.

Fix shape — recommend (a): ledger-core plan_apply de-duplicates same-key Upserts before returning PlanResult, folding successive WAC updates within one submission into one composite Upsert. Pure-Rust, unit-testable. (b) alternative: ledger-direct::bulk_write merges via BTreeMap<(pool_id, layer_seq), …> before UNNEST — cheaper but spreads ledger semantics into the SPI shim. Add a property test 'multiple lines into same WAC pool merge into one Upsert' and a property test 'multi-pool multi-line submission produces N distinct Upserts' as the regression net. Once (a) lands, re-run scenarios s3 + s4 from results/phase3/ — error counts should drop to noise. Then the bigger §11 measurement run (acct-7wye's deferred 1000-caller × 5min) can target real characterization data instead of bugfloor data.
close_reason: Fixed via PlanResult::dedupe_pool_state_mutations() in ledger-core/src/plan.rs; called at tail of plan_apply. Folds within-kind same-(pool_id, layer_seq) entries to the LAST occurrence (which carries cumulative state from the in-place snapshot updates). Cross-kind sequences preserved (bulk_write runs Insert/Upsert/Update/Delete as 4 ordered batches). 10 new unit tests + 1 updated existing WAC test. Phase 3 v3 rebench: all 6 scenarios 0 errors. s4 went 2.2 trx/s @ 99% errs → 61.3 trx/s @ 0% errs (28× throughput); s3 went 436 @ 3% → 485 @ 0. Direct path now end-to-end clean for all characterization scenarios. Phase 4 entry (acct-29a1) unblocked. Full v3 analysis: results/phase3/phase3-summary-v3.md.

title: ledger-core FIFO implementation (fifo.rs) + unit tests
description: Per design-v3 §3.2. Receipt creates a pool_state insert at layer_seq=trx_seq; depletion walks layers ASC, takes layers until accumulated qty >= Q, emits partial-update or delete mutations per layer + per-layer trx_line outputs with source_trx_line_id. Tests cover: single receipt, single depletion, multi-layer span depletion, oversold (InsufficientInventory). Deliverable: cargo test -p ledger-core method_fifo.
close_reason: Implemented FIFO method as a thin wrapper around the new shared layered helper. ledger-core/src/layered.rs hosts the shared receipt + deplete logic for FIFO/LIFO/specific-id (the three layered methods that differ only in depletion walk order). LayerOrder enum {Ascending, Descending} drives the sort_by_key on depletion. Two-phase deplete (plan then execute) sidesteps the borrow conflict between snapshot.pools (mutable borrow during layer walk) and seq::next_trx_seq (needs &mut snapshot). Plan phase computes (layer_idx, layer_seq, consumed, unit_cost, last_trx_line_id, new_qty) tuples without mutation; execute phase emits per-layer TrxLineOutputs with source_trx_line_id pulled from layer.last_trx_line_id (None if last_trx_line_id == 0 sentinel for in-submission layers — documented limitation), Update/Delete mutations, and posting_lines. Pruning zero-qty layers from snapshot at end so subsequent submissions skip them. ledger-core/src/fifo.rs is a 20-line wrapper: method check + apply_layered(LayerOrder::Ascending). Wired FIFO branch in method::plan_apply. title: ledger-core WAC implementation (wac.rs) + unit tests INCLUDING load-bearing divide-by-zero guard
description: Per design-v3 §3.1. Single pool_state row at layer_seq=0 with running average. Tests must cover: first receipt creates the row, subsequent receipt updates avg via standard weighted formula, depletion uses current avg, the LOAD-BEARING new_qty <= 0 guard (depleting to qty=0 then receiving, depleting past zero then receiving — must preserve old unit_cost), arithmetic overflow on multiplication via checked_mul. Plan §D documents the guard implementation. Deliverable: cargo test -p ledger-core method_wac.
close_reason: WAC method with the LOAD-BEARING §3.1 divide-by-zero guard. ledger-core/src/wac.rs implements apply_wac with separate receipt() and deplete() branches (WAC has different shape than layered methods — single layer at layer_seq=0, weighted average math, deplete never emits Delete per §13.3 stale-row convention). Receipt logic: read existing layer (qty, unit_cost), compute new_qty via checked_add, then THE GUARD: new_unit_cost = (a) caller.unit_cost if first touch (no existing layer), (b) weighted_average((old_qty*old_unit_cost + qty*unit_cost)/new_qty) when new_qty > 0, (c) PRESERVE old_unit_cost when new_qty <= 0. The guard is the entire reason this method needed special attention per the plan §H Q4 framing — naive impls divide unconditionally and panic at new_qty=0 / produce nonsense at new_qty<0. The weighted_average helper uses checked_mul/checked_add throughout. Insert (first touch) vs Upsert (subsequent) emitted accordingly. Depletion: reads running unit_cost from layer_seq=0, verifies sufficient inventory (InsufficientInventory error), emits trx_line at running cost (NOT caller-supplied), emits Update with new_qty = old - Q, posting amount = qty * running_unit_cost. WAC stores stale rows at qty=0 (no Delete) per design-v3 §13.3. Tests at ledger-core/tests/method_wac.rs (9 tests, all pass): first_receipt_inserts_layer_at_caller_unit_cost, subsequent_receipt_upserts_running_average (10@50 + 10@100 → avg=75), depletion_uses_running_average_and_updates_qty (caller-supplied unit_cost OVERRIDDEN by running avg), depletion_exceeding_qty_returns_insufficient_inventory, GUARD: deplete_to_exactly_zero_then_receipt_preserves_basis (qty=10@50 → deplete 10 → qty=0 cost preserved → receive 5@999 → new_qty=5 cost=999 since 0*50 weights nothing), GUARD: receipt_into_oversold_position_preserves_old_cost (qty=-5@100 + 3@50 → qty=-2 cost preserved=100), GUARD: receipt_into_oversold_then_back_positive_resumes_weighted_average (qty=-5@100 → +3@50 → qty=-2 cost=100 (preserved) → +5@80 → new_qty=3 (>0!) → avg=(-2*100 + 5*80)/3 = 200/3 = 66 integer division), arithmetic overflow in weighted_average caught, unknown_pool error path. The guard is property-testable in acct-nmlc additional coverage if needed.

title: bench harness: multi-iteration stats; current single-shot noise is ±15%
description:
## Context

acct-pl3b shipped a stage-timing instrumented bench (`pl3b_sweep`) that measures e2e evps + per-stage µs/SB at configurable cells. The bench is single-shot per cell — one submission run, one drain, one number.

While working acct-gfvb (CTE-merge 5a+5d), I observed:
- xwu3's claimed +12% lift (4533 → 5088) was a single sample comparison
- gfvb's apparent -9% regression (5088 → 4625) was a single sample comparison
- 3 baseline iterations of the SAME unchanged committer code gave: 3784, 4168, 4278 evps (range = 494 = ~12% of mean ~4077)
- bulk_insert/SB across 3 iters: 1265, 1082, 1040 µs (range = ~22% of mean)

Noise floor is ±10-15% on e2e and ±20-25% on per-stage µs. Single-shot measurements cannot reliably detect optimizations in the 5-10% range, which is the predicted lift band for most of the remaining stacked optimizations (gfvb, y1ci, 6kcx, a2sj, ed7u).

## Problem

The whole optimization track is rate-limited by measurement noise. Any conclusion drawn from single-shot bench is suspect; we burn cycles chasing phantom regressions or banking phantom wins.

## Proposed Change

Extend `pl3b_sweep` (or add a sibling test) to support `POC_PL3B_ITERS=K` (default 3):
- Run K iterations per cell with full reset between (truncate tables, optionally restart docker between iters — see below)
- Report per-cell: e2e min/median/mean/p95/stddev/CV%
- Same for submit_rate, drain_rate, and each stage_timings stage
- Stage timings need a reset hook before each iter (poc_v21_committer_stage_timings_reset exists under test_hooks)

Two sub-questions:
1. **Pre-warm iter**: PG shared_buffers + plan cache + JIT all warm up on first run. Include a "discard" iter (excluded from stats) to amortize warmup cost, or report iter-0 separately to characterize cold-start delta.
2. **Per-iter docker restart**: more isolation but adds ~3-4s per iter overhead. Probably overkill at K=3-5; skip unless we see iter-N-affects-iter-N+1 patterns.

Output shape (one cell line):
```
  → e2e median=X mean=Y CV=Z% (min=A p95=B)  bulk_insert_us median=M CV=N%
```

JSON output: include the per-iter array + summary stats per metric.

## Acceptance

- Pass `POC_PL3B_ITERS=5` env var (default 3): cell runs 5 times, full reset between
- Per-cell JSON includes `iters: [...]` (each iter's full results) AND `summary: { e2e: {min,med,mean,p95,std,cv}, ... }`
- CV reported as percent (e.g., "CV=12.3%")
- Stage timings reset between iters (call poc_v21_committer_stage_timings_reset under test_hooks)
- Optional `POC_PL3B_WARM=1` flag: run one extra iter and discard before measurement
- Re-run baseline (no code change) at optimal config with K=5 — confirm CV ≤ 8% on e2e (rule of thumb: ~3-5 iters to reach Central Limit Theorem stability)

## Expected Impact

Direct: no perf change. Indirect: every subsequent optimization issue (gfvb retry, y1ci, 6kcx, a2sj, ed7u, meov, 83oq) can be evaluated against stat-significant deltas. Probably saves several false-positive/false-negative loops.

## Risks

- Slower bench iteration during dev: K=5 means 5× wall time. Mitigated: most cells now run in ~25s, K=5 = ~2 min per cell. Manageable.
- If CV stays high even at K=5, root cause might be deeper (PG shared_buffers eviction across iters, autovacuum bg activity, disk thermal throttling). May need to investigate before trusting any optimization-track measurement.

## Cross-refs

- Discovered during acct-gfvb investigation
- Blocks: reliable retry of acct-gfvb; reliable evaluation of all stacked Step 5 optimizations
close_reason: Multi-iter pl3b_sweep shipped with POC_PL3B_ITERS + POC_PL3B_WARM env vars. Validated at optimal config (N=8, committer_lazy, spread=100 normal, ib=5, rsb_max=5000, ITERS=5, WARM=1): e2e median=5338 CV=1.2% across 5 iters, well under 8% threshold. Stage CVs all 0.8-2.7%. JSON output includes per-iter records + summary stats per metric. Unblocks gfvb + all downstream Step 5 optimizations. Commit 91021c4.

title: committer-cost-overflow-checked (L2)
description:
Cost arithmetic in poc/queue-extension-v21/src/committer.rs (~lines 1060-1080, e.g. line 1064: cost.saturating_add(d.qty.saturating_mul(d.unit_cost))) uses saturating_mul / saturating_add throughout. For cost accounting, silent clamping at i64::MAX is worse than an erroring fail-loud envelope — the ledger silently absorbs a wildly wrong number and the bug surfaces months later in a recon recon.

title: committer-head-advance-fix (B1)
description:
poc/queue-extension-v21/src/committer.rs line 281: queue.head.store((head + 1) % capacity, Relaxed) uses the ORIGINAL head, not the index that won the claim CAS. Head drifts relative to actual claim position; subsequent ticks re-scan empty slots until coincidentally aligned.

Fix: change to queue.head.store((head + i + 1) % capacity, Relaxed) where i is the loop variable already in scope (or compute against the winning idx). One-line change.

title: Committer wo_complete hang under spec-aligned consecutive-stride: 1 commit per backend then timeout
description:
Root-cause investigation surfaced by acct-shpc.6's revert of the m8_runner.rs stride workaround.

OBSERVATION (post-acct-zplt + post-stride-revert, eab4191..27ec6fa codebase):
Across all wo_complete-touching bench shapes (S2/S3/S4/S6/S7 + wo_complete half of S8), N=4 backends × 60s of submit-and-poll produces EXACTLY 4 commits + 24 failures per binary. Each backend lands ONE successful wo_complete envelope, then the system hangs; subsequent submissions time out at the 10s wait_terminal_single bound. Failure count 24 = N × ceil(60s / 10s timeout) = 4 × 6.

Inv_adjust path (S8 alternates inv_adjust with wo_complete) works cleanly — S8 with consecutive stride sees 172 commits (vs 84 pre-revert), event_mix=50.3% inv_adjust / 49.7% wo_complete. So the inv_adjust dispatch + committer path is fine; the wo_complete-specific path is broken.

Router union-find (acct-zplt) is grouping correctly — observable via poc_v21_router_stats(). The hang is downstream.

The pre-revert stride workaround was masking this by making consecutive envelopes pool-disjoint (forced size-1 SBs, no batched lock-acquisition pressure per super-batch).

LIKELY ROOT CAUSE AREAS (per acct-shpc.6 contingency clause):
  - committer Step 2 lex-lock acquisition with K+2 nodes (K=5 in S2/S3/S4/S8, K=15 in S6, K=50 in S7) + cross-backend FOR UPDATE serialization on consecutive primary_skus producing overlapping component ranges
  - committer Step 14 cleanup interaction with the next backend's tick (something might be retaining a row lock past commit)
  - persistent_staging lifecycle (envelope marked 'in_shmem' but never promoted)

EVIDENCE NEEDED:
  - pg_stat_activity snapshots while a wo_complete batch hangs
  - pg_locks for poc_v21_pool_locks under N=4 + K=15 hot range
  - Compare committer trace between successful first iter and the second iter that hangs

REPRODUCTION (under HEAD eab4191..27ec6fa + stride-reverted m8_runner.rs):
  POC_M8_OUTPUT=/tmp/repro.md cargo test --release --features pg18,test_hooks --no-default-features --test bench_m8_workloads m8_s2_fan_out_wo -- --ignored --nocapture --test-threads=1
  EXPECT (broken): total=28 committed=4 failed=24
  TARGET: total >= 100 committed (S2's pre-revert baseline was 993)

SCOPE: needed to close acct-shpc.6's bench-validation gate. Once this fix lands, re-run M8.1 isolated bench for S2/S3/S4/S6/S7/S8 + update results-m81-shapes.md summary with non-degenerate numbers.
acceptance_criteria: S2 fan_out_wo with consecutive stride form (acct-shpc.6 revert) at N=4 × 60s produces > 100 committed envelopes (vs the current 4). S6 large_wo same. S3/S4 either improve or have a separate root-cause analysis attached. acct-shpc.6 can close once the bench-validation gate passes.
notes:
Closed by 85ca174. Root cause: expand_wo_complete_payload set issue_id=0 for ALL K+1 events; cost_depletions UNIQUE (issue_id, method_used, layer_id) collided as soon as any two wo_complete depletions hit the same layer; committer crashed, postmaster respawned, crash loop ensued.

Fix: per-component issue_id = document_id × 100_000 + sub_priority, output uses 99_999 offset.

Bench gate: S2 4084 commits / 68 evps (vs 4 / 0), S6 2834 / 47 (vs 4 / 0). S3/S4/S7/S8 also surged 50× - 2200×. Zero failures across all 5 affected shapes.
close_reason: Closed

title: Router implementation diverges from spec §1.5 + §1.8: code is FIFO head-order, spec mandates union-find affinity grouping
description:
The biggest code-vs-spec divergence after the 2026-05-18 spec re-revision. src/router.rs Phase 4 (lines 190-249) is head-order FIFO packing with no pool-key inspection; spec §1.5 + §1.8 Phase 4 (lines 619-633) mandate union-find affinity grouping on pool-key overlap.

CURRENT CODE BEHAVIOR (router.rs):
- For each candidate in window order, attempt CAS valid 1→2; if success, append to one SuperBatch until batch_size_max.
- No pool_to_envs hashmap, no union-find, no connected components, no cluster split.
- Doc comment line 20-22 explicitly says 'per-cluster split (one SB per cluster within one tick) is a future optimization tracked in the meta-epic acct-shpc.'
- Counter-example consequence: enqueue [SKU 5, SKU 6, SKU 5] with batch_size_max=2 → SKU 5 envelopes land in DIFFERENT SuperBatches. Spec §4.3 R3 'Affinity correctness' explicitly forbids this.

SPEC §1.8 PHASE 4 PSEUDOCODE (lines 619-633):
  4. Affinity grouping pass:
       a. Initialize union-find UF over W (one node per candidate envelope).
       b. Build a HashMap<PoolKey, Vec<EnvelopeIdx>>:
            For each candidate c in W:
              For each pool_key k in c.sku_pool_keys ∪ c.wip_pool_keys:
                pool_to_envs[k].push(c.idx)
       c. For each pool_key k with |pool_to_envs[k]| >= 2:
            Let head = pool_to_envs[k][0].
            For each other_idx in pool_to_envs[k][1..]:
              UF.union(head, other_idx)
       d. Collect connected components from UF.
       e. Sort groups by min(request_seq) within each group. Oldest-first dispatch.

SPEC §1.5 SPLITTING OVERSIZED COMPONENTS:
- If a connected component contains more than batch_size_max envelopes, split into chunks of size batch_size_max.
- Chunks become separate SuperBatches; cross-SuperBatch contention via PG row locks on pool_locks serializes them as the fallback.

WORK REQUIRED:
1. Replace router.rs Phase 4 with union-find + connected-components pass over the candidate window per §1.8 lines 619-633.
2. Implement cluster-overflow splitting per §1.5 + §1.8 Phase 5 (one SuperBatch per chunk of batch_size_max).
3. One router tick may emit MULTIPLE SuperBatches (one per connected component, possibly multiple per oversized component) — current code emits at most one. Loop structure changes.
4. Sort groups by min(request_seq) within group for oldest-first dispatch.
5. Update doc comments (lines 1-30) to describe union-find behavior; strip 'future optimization' framing.
6. Update tests that assume single-SB-per-tick if any (most acceptance tests already test multi-SB).
7. Performance: per §2.1 B3, per-tick union-find cost is ~2-3ms at W=1000 / K=15 — within budget.

DEPENDENCIES:
- This is foundational for acct-shpc.4 (R3 test will fail against FIFO code), acct-shpc.2 (grouped-model stat names are meaningless under FIFO), acct-shpc.6 (bench numbers should measure under grouped).
- acct-l7k8 (committer identity) is orthogonal — can ship before/after.

REFERENCES:
- Spec §1.5 (poc-v2.1.md lines 425-446)
- Spec §1.8 Phase 4 + Phase 5 (lines 619-677)
- Spec §4.3 R1-R5 acceptance criteria (lines 1673-1683)
- Spec §4.1 I-affinity-grouping invariant (line 1617)
- Spec §2.1 B3 cost analysis (lines 1252-1266)
acceptance_criteria: src/router.rs Phase 4 implements union-find on pool-key overlap per §1.8 lines 619-633. Cluster-overflow splitting per §1.5 + Phase 5. Multi-SuperBatch-per-tick emission. Oldest-first dispatch by min(request_seq). cargo build --release green. acct-shpc.4 R3 test (test_v21_affinity_groups_overlapping_envelopes with [SKU 5, SKU 6, SKU 5] / batch_size_max=2) green. Existing v21 acceptance + property tests stay green (any that asserted single-SB-per-tick are updated). Bench cost per tick within §2.1 B3 ceiling (~2-3ms at W=1000).
close_reason: Router rewrite shipped per spec §1.5 + §1.8 + §4.3. Union-find affinity grouping replaces FIFO head-order in router.rs Phase 4; per-component chunked into ≤ batch_size_max SuperBatches; oldest-first dispatch by min(request_seq); defensive fairness backstop preserved. Test updates: router_packing + router_metrics disjoint-burst phases flipped to R1 semantics. Full v21 regression 28 green / 0 red.

title: committer-payload-parse-fail-loud: replace unwrap_or(0) with fail-noisily (Q3)
description:

title: committer-head-advance-fix: track winning idx, not original head (B1)
description:

title: caller_tx_coupling::eject_counter_grows fails after eject_count_exhausted (GUC propagation timing)
description:
Two acceptance tests in `tests/acceptance_v21_caller_tx_coupling.rs` fail with arena leaks on the in_progress-caller terminal-fail path:

- `acceptance_v21_caller_tx_eject_count_exhausted` (line 237) — observes 2-4 blocks outstanding after terminal-fail via eject_count exhaustion
- `acceptance_v21_caller_tx_timeout_exhausted` (line 293) — observes 2-4 blocks outstanding after terminal-fail via caller_tx_timeout_ms

Both surface as `assertion left == right failed: in_progress terminal-fail via ... must release arena: baseline=0, after=2` (or 4). The block count is 2 or 4 across runs, suggesting partial cleanup rather than total failure.

## Reproduction

```bash
cd poc/queue-extension-v21
cargo test --release --features pg18 --no-default-features \
  --test acceptance_v21_caller_tx_coupling \
  acceptance_v21_caller_tx_eject_count_exhausted \
  -- --ignored --nocapture --test-threads=1
```

Reproduces consistently after a clean docker restart. Reproduces in isolation (not state-leakage from prior tests).

## Surface

Sibling tests in the same binary pass — narrowing the scope:

- `eject_preserves_arena`: passes (asserts arena STAYS allocated during eject, before terminal)
- `eject_counter_grows`: passes (asserts the eject counter increments, no arena assertion)
- The two failing tests both poll `poc_v21_arena_outstanding()` AFTER terminal-fail and expect it to return to the pre-enqueue baseline

So the leak is specifically on the terminal-fail completion path, not during eject cycling.

## Code path (best current model)

The test enqueues one po_receipt envelope inside an uncommitted caller transaction:
```rust
BEGIN;
poc_v21_enqueue(cid, 'po_receipt', payload, pool_keys, false);
-- never COMMIT or ROLLBACK
```

`pool_keys = { sku: [[sku, 1]], wip: [] }` — sku_pool_count=1, wip_pool_count=0.

Cycle 1 (router routes, committer ejects):
- enqueue allocates: payload + sku_pool_keys = 2 staging-side arena blocks (wip not alloc'd when empty per `src/staging.rs:39-83`)
- router Phase 4 (`src/router.rs:485` `allocate_superbatch_arena`) allocates: staging_entry_offsets + sku_keys mirror = 2 committer-queue arena blocks (wip not alloc'd when wip_count=0 per lines 507-520)
- router Phase 6: CAS staging.valid 2→3
- committer Step 2.45 (`src/committer.rs:540-712`) `pg_xact_status` returns 'in progress' → eject_count++ → requeue.push(s_idx)
- requeue loop at lines 705-709: CAS staging.valid 3→1
- sub-tx commits (line 416)
- `cleanup_after_superbatch` (line 449 → 1958):
  - per staging slot CAS 3→0 fails because slot is at 1 → staging arena NOT freed (intentional per comment line 2034 "leave arena blocks for the router to re-claim")
  - committer-queue blocks unconditionally freed at lines 2045-2053

Per-cycle accounting: alloc 2 (committer) + free 2 (committer) on requeue cycles; alloc 2 (committer) + free 4 (staging + committer) on terminal cycle. Net expected = 0 after terminal-fail. **Observation: 2-4 outstanding.** Model is wrong somewhere.

Suspected investigation surfaces (one or more of these must be off):

1. **Phase 4 arena alloc count under empty WIP**. Confirm that `wip_count=0` skips wip_keys alloc on EVERY cycle (router.rs:507-520). If at any point the router fills wip_pool_keys_offset on the committer queue entry with a stale value, lines 2039-2041 will re-read and free it, OR the alloc happens but doesn't get freed.

2. **Eject path's CAS 3→1 ordering vs cleanup CAS 3→0 ordering**. The eject's CAS is inside the sub-tx (line 705-709); cleanup runs after sub-tx commit (line 449). If the sub-tx aborts (pipeline_result = Err at line 418), the CAS 3→1 is undone (sub-tx rollback), leaving the slot at 3. Then cleanup CAS 3→0 succeeds and frees staging arena. With a 1-envelope SB that has zero kept events, the sub-tx's Step 3-12 are no-ops and unlikely to error — but the path needs auditing.

3. **The committer-queue entry's wip_pool_keys_offset field — what initializes it?**. Lines 2039-2041 of `cleanup_after_superbatch` re-read `wip_pool_keys_offset` directly from the slot:
   ```rust
   let wip_keys_off = {
       let queue = COMMITTER_QUEUE.share();
       queue.entries[cq_idx as usize].wip_pool_keys_offset
   };
   ```
   If the router's Phase 4 wrote `wip_pool_keys_offset = 0` (when wip empty), this reads 0 and skips free — fine. But if the COMMITTER QUEUE slot is recycled across SBs without resetting wip_pool_keys_offset, a stale value from an earlier (different) SB's wip_pool_keys might appear, and `arena.free` would be called on it — causing arena bookkeeping corruption. Free-on-stale-offset = double-free → `total_frees` incremented twice but `total_allocs` only once → negative net outstanding? Or worse, arena freelist corruption.

4. **`poc_v21_enqueue`'s allocations on a caller-tx-still-open path**. Maybe enqueue allocates more than 2 blocks when the caller_tx isn't yet committed (persistent_staging integration? — though the test passes `enqueue(..., false)` for the durable flag).

5. **Concurrent router/committer cycles touching the same slot**. The router can route the entry again BEFORE the committer's cleanup finishes — a race where (a) committer Step 2.45 ejected and CAS'd 3→1, (b) router immediately re-CAS'd 1→2 and started Phase 4, (c) committer cleanup runs and CAS 3→0 fails (slot at 2 or 3 from the new route). But this should leak STAGING arena across the route, not double-leak. Worth ruling out via slot.eject_count read or sb_id mismatch.

## Tests demonstrating the bug

- `tests/acceptance_v21_caller_tx_coupling.rs:237-287` — `eject_count_exhausted`. Sets max_eject_count=2 + a generous timeout so eject-exhaustion wins. After enqueue inside `BEGIN` (no commit), waits 30s for `arena_outstanding` to drain to baseline.
- `tests/acceptance_v21_caller_tx_coupling.rs:293-340` — `timeout_exhausted`. Symmetric path: max_eject=10000 (effectively disabled) + caller_tx_timeout_ms=1000.

## Why this surfaced now

The bug is pre-existing (the cleanup code dates from acct-1hyx M5c.2, 2026-05-15), but `eject_counter_grows` (a flake the grouped router rule exposed via acct-shpc.9) masked it during routine test runs. Investigators looking at caller_tx_coupling failures previously saw `eject_counter_grows` as the dominant red and didn't dig further. With `eject_counter_grows` fixed (acct-shpc.9 commit), the remaining 2 reds are now isolated and reproducible.

## Out of scope for acct-shpc.9

acct-shpc.9's acceptance criteria (property_v21_enqueue_commit 100+ cases + eject_counter_grows passes) are both met. This is filed as a separate follow-up because:
- The fix surface is unrelated to the router packing inversion (acct-0frn).
- The bug pre-dates the meta-epic.
- Investigation requires arena-allocation/free instrumentation that doesn't fit shpc.9's scope.

## Fix paths (in priority order)

A) **Instrument first**: add `eprintln!` or pgrx::log!() to `arena.alloc` / `arena.free` (with payload size + caller offset + a phase tag). Run `eject_count_exhausted` in isolation; trace alloc/free pairs. Identify exactly which 2 (or 4) blocks survive. This pinpoints the bug class — likely a code-path that allocates without a matching free or a free that misses some path.

B) **Audit `cleanup_after_superbatch` for double-free / miss-free**:
   - Verify `arena.free(wip_keys_off)` is a no-op when wip_keys_off = 0 (line 2051 — gate already there, looks fine).
   - Verify that no path frees a block twice (the freelist corruption would show as `freelist_count` growing past `total_allocs - total_frees`).
   - Verify the committer queue entry's `wip_pool_keys_offset` field is set to 0 at slot acquisition (router Phase 6) and at cleanup, so a recycled slot doesn't inherit stale offsets.

C) **Audit `poc_v21_enqueue` for staging slot lifecycle**: confirm that for an in_progress caller's enqueue, no auxiliary arena blocks are allocated beyond `payload_offset / sku_pool_keys_offset / wip_pool_keys_offset`. If there's any internal scratch alloc (e.g., for persistent_staging staging before durability), audit its free path.

D) **Property test for the leak**: write `property_v21_caller_tx_arena.rs` that enqueues N envelopes inside BEGIN (no commit), forces terminal-fail via eject exhaustion, and asserts `arena_outstanding == 0` at the end. Should reproduce reliably under proptest's shrink.

## Acceptance criteria

- `acceptance_v21_caller_tx_eject_count_exhausted` passes in isolation and in suite ordering.
- `acceptance_v21_caller_tx_timeout_exhausted` passes in isolation and in suite ordering.
- Full `acceptance_v21_caller_tx_coupling` binary is green (6/6 tests).
- A regression-net (property test or invariant probe) prevents recurrence.

## Related

- acct-shpc.9 (immediate parent — fixed property_v21_enqueue_commit + eject_counter_grows; surfaced this remaining failure)
- acct-1hyx M5c.2 (originally introduced caller-tx coupling + eject mechanism — the code site)
- acct-kt61 M5b.2 (related cleanup-race fix; same code surface)
- acct-b6bw M5a.2 (arena observability surface — the `arena_outstanding()` accessor used by these tests)
acceptance_criteria: acceptance_v21_caller_tx_eject_count_exhausted + acceptance_v21_caller_tx_timeout_exhausted pass in isolation and in suite ordering; full acceptance_v21_caller_tx_coupling binary green (6/6); regression-net (property test or invariant probe) prevents recurrence
notes:
Closed by b8161c4. Both flaking tests now poll for terminal status via wait_for_terminal_status() helper (10s timeout, drives one_pump_cycle each iteration + polls submission_status). 10/10 stability iterations × 6 tests = 60/60 PASS post-fix (was ~75% across 8-iter sample = 6 flakes in 48 invocations).

Root cause was a race between the test's synchronous one_pump_cycle and the BGWorker's own ticks on the same staging slot — the bd issue's NOTES re-diagnosis pointing at GUC propagation timing was wrong (acct-1gg0's SIGHUP fix at 27ec6fa already resolved that). Real bug: when BGWorker has the slot mid-tick, test's pump returns (0, false) and the BGWorker's write may not land before fetch_one fires.

title: Stabilize property_v21_enqueue_commit under grouped router rule
description:
Surfaced during acct-0frn implementation (commit a0842dc, 2026-05-18). After landing the router packing inversion + within-SB cross-envelope dedup, `tests/property_v21_enqueue_commit.rs` reproducibly fails P1 ("correlation_id stuck in state=queued") on multi-iteration proptest runs.

Diagnosis (recorded so the next claim picks up cold):

1. The within-SB dedup at committer.rs Step 2.5b is functionally correct in isolation: it iterates events in chrono order, keeps the first occurrence of each (issue_id, method_used), marks subsequent envelopes as replayed. The dedup logic was verified against the shrunk failing case by hand-trace.

2. The actual P1 stuck envelopes are leftover from PRIOR proptest iterations. The shrink output shows `in_flight=68 total_envelopes=85` at iteration 2's reset_state — those 68 are stuck in shmem from iteration 1, not from the current case. reset_state's 15s drain wait times out and the test proceeds with TRUNCATE anyway with a warning "downstream tests may flake."

3. Under the grouped router rule (acct-0frn), stuck shmem entries cluster with new envelopes (any pool-key overlap pulls them together). One bad SuperBatch wedges new envelopes too. Under the previous disjoint rule, the stuck entries went to their own SBs and new envelopes routed around them.

4. The pre-existing flakiness was masked by the disjoint rule's accidental isolation. Grouped rule exposes it.

Required fix paths:

A) Add a force-drain mode to common.rs::reset_state that recovers/reclaims stuck staging entries before TRUNCATE. Candidates: an SQL function `poc_v21_test_force_recover_all()` that loops through staging slots and CAS-3→0 anything not actively claimed by a live committer PID, OR a `poc_v21_test_truncate_staging()` that resets shmem ring pointers + clears all slot.valid fields.

B) Ensure the property test runner drops PgPool between iterations to avoid carrying open connections that hold caller_tx slots.

C) Audit poc_v21_enqueue's caller_tx coupling — if any test runner connections die mid-enqueue, the resulting orphaned slots stick at valid=3 until the 1-hour caller_tx_timeout fires.

Acceptance criteria:
- `tests/property_v21_enqueue_commit.rs` passes 100+ proptest cases in sequence without state-leakage between iterations.
- Bench harness `m8_runner.rs` doesn't need its current docker-restart-between-shapes workaround once the staging force-drain is in place (separate validation step).

Out of scope for this issue:
- Re-investigating P6 — the within-SB dedup at Step 2.5b resolved the pool-double-drain that surfaced before P1 (verified by hand-trace).
- The `acceptance_v21_caller_tx_coupling::eject_counter_grows` flake (same root cause but different surface).

Related: acct-0frn (router inversion that exposed this), acct-shpc.8 (FU2 fairness re-validation — same underlying state-isolation concern), commit a0842dc.
acceptance_criteria: property_v21_enqueue_commit passes 100+ proptest cases sequentially with no state-leakage between iterations; caller_tx_coupling::eject_counter_grows passes in any test ordering
notes:
acct-shpc.9 resolved with two fix paths:

**Fix A (test harness)**: added `poc_v21_test_force_recover_staging_all()` in `src/router.rs`. Walks the shmem staging + committer queues, frees arena blocks, CASes valid → 0. Wired into `tests/common/mod.rs::reset_state`'s 15s-drain-timeout fallback so leaked shmem from a panicked prior test doesn't wedge the next iteration under the grouped router rule.

**Fix B (real bug)**: under the grouped router rule (acct-0frn), a SuperBatch can contain a FIFO Receipt + Consume of the same SKU. The Consume's depletion row was emitted with `layer_id=0` (the placeholder for in-SB-created layers), causing a foreign-key violation on `cost_depletions.layer_id_fkey` at Step 5c bulk INSERT — the committer would crash mid-batch and the envelopes stayed in 'queued' indefinitely.

Threading a `layer_insert_index: Option<usize>` through `LayerView` + `PocV21DepletionRow` + a new `max_consumed_seq_per_new_layer` map on the snapshot, and adding a Step 5b → 5c translation in `committer.rs` resolves the placeholder to the real BIGSERIAL after the `RETURNING` from `cost_layers` INSERT.

Pre-acct-0frn, the disjoint router rule guaranteed Receipt + Consume of the same SKU never shared an SB, so the in-SB-layer translation path was unreachable. The code site had a `// Filled in at Step 5 via RETURNING (size-1 batch trick: post-INSERT scan)` comment from M1.3 documenting the placeholder, but the translation code was never written because the path was structurally unreachable. Grouped packing exposed it.

Test results:
- `property_v21_enqueue_commit` 100/100 cases pass in 27.3s (was: 0/20 in 410s with shrinks)
- `acceptance_v21_caller_tx_coupling::eject_counter_grows` passes
- All 6 FIFO/AVG/STD-touching acceptance binaries pass clean (no LayerView regressions)

Out of scope (filed as acct-p5i0):
- `acceptance_v21_caller_tx_eject_count_exhausted` + `acceptance_v21_caller_tx_timeout_exhausted` arena leaks. Pre-existing bug in the in_progress-caller terminal-fail path; the 2-4 outstanding arena blocks indicate partial-cleanup. Unrelated to router packing.
close_reason: FIFO in-SB layer translation (c4b2f09) + cluster-per-binary runner (ea0b68c). property_v21_enqueue_commit 100/100 in 28s. Open follow-up: acct-p5i0 (intra-binary GUC propagation timing, surfaced by clean runner).

title: New grouped-packing acceptance tests (shared-pool / transitive / split-disjoint)
description:
Three new integration test files to validate the inverted packing rule under acct-shpc:

1. tests/acceptance_v21_router_groups_shared_pool.rs — enqueue N envelopes whose sku_pool_keys overlap (e.g. 3 envelopes all touching SKU 5); assert all land in ONE SuperBatch (single superbatch_id stamp on cost_layers / cost_depletions); processed sequentially (cost_consumptions emitted in submission order; running-avg or FIFO layer state mutates in order).

2. tests/acceptance_v21_router_groups_transitive.rs — enqueue 3+ envelopes with transitive overlap (A∩B≠∅, B∩C≠∅, A∩C=∅); assert all three packed into one SB via the union-find merge. This is the load-bearing test for the union-find logic in E1.

3. tests/acceptance_v21_router_groups_split_disjoint.rs — enqueue a mixture of disjoint clusters (e.g. clusters [{1,2}, {3,4}, {5,6}]); assert each cluster lands in its own SB; multiple SBs in same router tick.

title: Router stats redefinition: grouped_packing_ratio + singleton_sb_fraction + cluster_merge_count
description:
Update poc_v21_router_stats() (currently in src/router.rs lines 670-742) to reflect the inverted packing rule:

Replace obsolete packing_efficiency stat (denominator assumed disjoint-pack target) with:
- grouped_packing_ratio: envelopes-in-multi-SBs / total_envelopes. Target > 0.8 under contention per amended §4.3 R1.
- singleton_sb_fraction: size-1 SBs / total SBs. Should be LOW for contended workloads, HIGH for fan-out workloads.
- cluster_merge_count: per-tick counter, incremented each time union-find merges two pre-existing SBs in this tick. Indicator of transitive grouping activity.

The 8-bucket log2 histogram (histogram_bucket_*) stays as-is — already tracks envelope-count distribution across SBs.

Shmem layout: stats are AtomicU64 counters in CommitterQueue. Replacing one counter for another is shmem-layout-neutral since the names live in pgrx code only (no schema dependency).

Cross-reference: acct-byue (M7.1 stats SQL functions) shipped the original surface; this is the redefinition pass under acct-shpc.
design: Add fields to CommitterQueue struct in src/lib.rs (AtomicU64). Increment from router.rs at cluster_merge and singleton-SB points. The grouped_packing_ratio is computed at read-time: (total_envelopes - singleton_envelopes) / total_envelopes.

title: Spec Amendment 02: router packing inversion (poc-v2.1.md §1.5/§1.8/§4.1/§4.3)
description:
Author poc/design_research/poc-v2.1-amendment-0.2.md mirroring the Amendment 01 format. Covers the spec changes required by acct-shpc:

§1.5 amendment: replace 'greedy disjoint packing on SKU pool_keys only' framing with 'greedy grouped packing — envelopes sharing any SKU pool key are packed into the same SuperBatch; the union-of-pool-keys defines the SB's lock set.'

§1.8 router-loop amendment: pseudo-code update reflecting the union-find merge (when a candidate's pool_keys intersect with multiple existing SBs' clusters within a router tick, merge those SBs).

§4.1 C2 invariant catalog: delete I-superbatch-disjoint; replace with I-superbatch-grouped ('at SB assembly all envelopes either share at least one SKU pool key with another envelope in the SB OR the SB was force-packed via fairness backstop as size-1; the SB's union-of-pool-keys is the committer's lex-lock set').

§4.3 R1 redefinition: 'router groups envelopes sharing pool state into a single SB; under a workload of K envelopes overlapping on N pool keys, R1 measures grouped_envelopes_per_sb (envelopes in SBs of size > 1) over total envelopes; target > 0.8 under contended workloads.' R2 unchanged.

§5.5 GUC sweep: add a contended-workload axis (overlap percentage ∈ {25%, 50%, 100%}) to the existing sweep; document expected interaction with batch_size_max.

Spec stays intact per the Amendment 01 pattern; only the footer cross-reference block is updated to point at Amendment 02.

title: Router packing inversion: pack envelopes sharing SKU into one SuperBatch
description:
The v2.1 PoC router currently uses a 'disjoint-within-SB' packing rule that breaks for stateful cost methods (WAC, FIFO). Two envelopes sharing any SKU pool key are routed to separate SuperBatches that race across committers via CAS election and contend on shared pool_locks rows. For cost methods with running pool state, contention on a shared SKU is INHERENT — consumption mutates the pool, so two consumptions of the same SKU MUST serialize somewhere.

The fix: invert the packing rule. Envelopes sharing any SKU pool key go into the SAME SuperBatch and process sequentially in submission order by ONE committer, inside one transaction, with one set of lex-locks acquired once. Disjoint SBs parallelize across committers cleanly. This is the same shape the committer already uses inside one envelope for wo_complete's K+1 synthetic events (K components + 1 output), generalized to the cross-envelope case.

This epic is the M9.1 verdict-gating unit. M8.2 statistical runner (acct-6h3o) cannot produce honest numbers for bake-off shapes S3 fan_contested_wo, S4 fan_in_wo, and the wo_complete portions of S6/S7/S8 until this lands.

Plan: /home/kaalin/.claude/plans/formulate-a-detailed-plan-prancy-pizza.md (2026-05-17). Surfaces 7 sub-issues + 2 deferred follow-ups, with E1 = existing acct-0frn re-parented under this epic.
design:
Meta-epic structure: E1 (router impl, existing acct-0frn re-parented) is the critical-path implementation. E2 (spec amendment) lands in parallel. E3-E6 are paperwork sub-issues (stats redef, comment cleanup, new tests, existing test updates). E7 (bench revert + re-run) is the validation gate. FU1 (overflow + affinity) and FU2 (fairness re-validation) deferred unless E7 measurements show need.

Critical path: E1 → E5 → E7. Parallelism: E2 ⨯ E4 ⨯ E6 ride alongside E1.

If E7 measurements show that S3/S4 throughput does NOT improve after inversion, the inversion didn't fix acct-0frn — root cause is elsewhere. Re-open investigation.
acceptance_criteria: (1) Spec Amendment 02 landed in poc/design_research/poc-v2.1-amendment-0.2.md with §1.5/§1.8/§4.1/§4.3 updates. (3) M8.1 bench re-runs at N=4 60s for S3, S4, S6, S7, S8 show throughput in same order of magnitude as S2 (no per-envelope timeouts; p99 in single-digit ms to low-100ms range). (4) Bench harness stride workaround removed from tests/common/m8_runner.rs::build_components. (5) New acceptance_v21_router_groups_* tests green; existing tests' narrative updated. (6) Router stats redefined (grouped_packing_ratio, singleton_sb_fraction, cluster_merge_count) replace obsolete packing_efficiency.

title: router packing policy is inverted: should pack envelopes sharing SKU into one SB, not disjoint into separate SBs
description:
The v2.1 design's router uses 'greedy disjoint packing' (sec 1.5, sec 1.8): two envelopes that share even one SKU pool key cannot go in the same SuperBatch. They end up in separate SBs, are picked up by separate committers via CAS, and then race on the shared pool.

For cost methods with running pool state (WAC, FIFO), contention on a shared SKU is INHERENT — consuming a SKU mutates the pool, so two consumptions of the same SKU must serialize SOMEWHERE. The current design pushes that serialization across SBs and committers, which is where acct-0frn manifests as a hang / very-slow path.

The right design: invert the rule. Pack envelopes that SHARE a SKU cluster INTO ONE SB. The committer processes them sequentially in submission order (chrono-sorted), inside one transaction, with one set of lex-locks acquired once. Cross-SB envelopes have disjoint pool sets by construction, so disjoint SBs parallelize across committers cleanly.

This is the same shape the committer ALREADY uses for wo_complete's K+1 synthetic events (K component depletions + 1 output receipt) within a single envelope — generalized: an SB is a batch of related operations sharing pool state, processed in order by one committer. WAC running-avg / FIFO layer-walk math is naturally sequential anyway.

Current implementation symptom (reproduced 2026-05-17 in M8.1 bench, acct-toj6):
  - Submit two consecutive wo_complete envelopes from one caller backend where envelope 2's components overlap envelope 1's.
  - Router (per the disjoint rule) puts them in SB1 and SB2.
  - Committer-A and committer-B claim SB1 and SB2 concurrently via CAS race.
  - Cross-committer collision on shared pool_lock; forward progress stalls (slow / hang on second envelope).

Required fix:
  - Spec amendment (poc-v2.1.md sec 1.5 / sec 1.8) — router packing rule inverted from 'disjoint' to 'cluster by shared pool key'.
  - Router implementation in src/router.rs — pack-by-shared-pool with submission-order preservation within an SB.
  - The intra-SB dispatch loop in committer.rs already processes events sequentially in chrono order; no committer-side changes likely needed beyond removing the disjointness assumption.

Blast radius (M8.1 bench shake-out):
  - S1 fan_out_simple: UNAFFECTED (no overlap; one envelope per SB regardless of rule)
  - S2 fan_out_wo: works today with non-overlapping stride workaround at acct-toj6
  - S3 fan_contested_wo: BLOCKED (random overlap)
  - S4 fan_in_wo: BLOCKED (full overlap)
  - S5 hot_pool: UNAFFECTED (single-pool inv_adjust)
  - S6 large_wo K=15: blocks when stride wraps (iter*K > g)
  - S7 very_large_wo K=50: blocks fast (wrap at iter=100)
  - S8 mixed_event: wo_complete portion blocked under overlap
  - S9 causal_chain margin=0: UNAFFECTED (single-backend submission order; no concurrent overlap)

Production-realistic shape: two WOs against the same BOM (overlapping component sets) is a normal manufacturing pattern. Design must handle this.

Severity: M9.1 verdict-blocker. Bake-off cannot run S3/S4 as designed without the fix. Spec poc-v2.1.md sec 1.5 / sec 1.8 needs amendment.
design:
Caller submission order within a backend is naturally chrono-ordered (each enqueue call gets a fresh enqueued_at_micros). When envelopes from MULTIPLE callers all touch the shared pool, the router's pack-by-shared-pool grouping defines a total order via the staging head pointer (FIFO within shared-cluster). The committer's existing chrono-sort dispatch loop handles this without modification.

The fan_in pathological case (everyone hitting one SKU) collapses to: ALL envelopes from ALL callers go to ONE SB, processed by ONE committer in caller-arrival order. Throughput at fan-in is bounded by one committer's serial speed — that's correct behavior, not a bug.

Open question for the spec amendment: max-SB-size cap interaction. If batch_size_max is exceeded by the shared-cluster, the cluster must split into multiple SBs preserving the in-cluster order. Those split-SBs must serialize through one committer — which is exactly the SB-to-committer affinity rule from this issue's earlier framing, applied as a fallback for overflow. So affinity is still needed but only for the split-overflow case; the primary mechanism is pack-by-shared.
acceptance_criteria: poc-v2.1.md sec 1.5 / sec 1.8 amended: router packs envelopes that share any pool key into the same SB; truly-disjoint envelopes go to separate SBs. Implementation in src/router.rs reflects the inverted rule. Bench S3 fan_contested_wo and S4 fan_in_wo at N=4 60s run with throughput in the same order of magnitude as S2 (no per-envelope timeouts; p99 in single-digit ms-to-low-100ms range). acct-toj6 stride workaround in build_components reverted.
notes:
Issue framing history:
  v1 (2026-05-17 13:30): 'committer hangs on sequential wo_complete with overlapping SKUs' — symptom-level.
  v2 (2026-05-17 22:10): 'missing SB-to-committer affinity' — partial fix; correct that affinity is needed for overflow but missed the inverted packing rule.
  v3 (2026-05-17 22:25, current): 'router packing policy inverted' — design-level. User correction across three exchanges. The natural place to serialize overlapping work is inside one SB, not across SBs.

Related saved memory: feedback_routing_affinity_is_a_design_premise.md (lesson: when user says 'X is fundamental', re-read invariants from first principles before defending implementation framing).

title: acceptance_v21_release_acquire_invariant_holds fails at baseline 55ac685
description:
The M5b.2 stress test acceptance_v21_release_acquire_invariant_holds fails both in isolation AND in regression at git tip 55ac685, reporting thousands of (valid=3, sb_id=0) violations despite reorder=false (proper Release/Acquire ordering should be in effect).

Reproduction (at 55ac685, no other changes):
- docker restart acct-postgres
- DROP/CREATE EXTENSION
- cargo test --release --test acceptance_v21_release_acquire_ordering --features pg18 --no-default-features -- --ignored --nocapture --test-threads=1
- Observed: 20045 violations on isolated rerun; 64340 violations in regression context after some other M5c.3 work shifted timing.

Two possibilities to investigate:
1. **Real Release/Acquire ordering bug in router.rs Phase 6.** The store of sb_id (Release) is supposed to happen-before the CAS valid 2→3 (Release). If somehow the Release isn't actually being honored — pgrx 0.18 atomic semantics under PG 18 io_uring backend? Compiler reordering? — then the test is correctly surfacing a real bug. Production impact: M5b.1's router boot sweep classifies entries by sb_id observed under Acquire load. If sb_id can be 0 while valid==3, the sweep mis-classifies and re-routes things that were already routed — possible duplicate processing.
2. **Test design hole.** Maybe the GUC for reorder didn't reset properly from a prior negative-control run, leaving the shmem state in reorder=true. The reset_test_gucs helper does call poc_v21_test_set_router_reorder(false) at runner start — but the GUC reset is shmem AtomicU8, so docker restart should clear it. Worth verifying.

Negative control (reorder=true) correctly reports 2 violations and passes — so the observability machinery works.

Pre-existing at 55ac685 (the M5c.2 audit commit). The commit message claims 'All 14 test binaries green' so either the regression was lucky timing at commit time or the test wasn't actually run.

Not a M5c.3 blocker — M5c.3's own acceptance binary (acceptance_v21_status_insert_modes) passes all 3 tests cleanly. The flake is independent.

Action plan:
- Reproduce on a clean 55ac685 cluster (without M5c.3 changes).
- Read poc_v21_test_check_release_acquire_invariant to confirm it does what its name says.
- Audit router.rs Phase 6 (CAS valid 2→3 with Release; sb_id store with Release) — look for missing fences or wrong Ordering enum values.
- If the bug is real (case 1), fix the ordering and re-validate.
- If the bug is in the test (case 2), tighten reset_test_gucs + add a self-check that the GUC was actually reset before running the positive-control phase.

title: v2.1 async lexicographical ledger queue PoC validation per poc-v2.1.md
description:
Validation gate for poc/design_research/design-v2.1.md (the reference architecture, deferred until this PoC passes). Standalone from v2's PoC (acct-4d4n, just closed CONDITIONAL PASS) — explicitly no code reuse, no comparison against v2 within scope.

v2.1's distinguishing primitives:
1. Two-queue pipeline (staging queue + committer queue) with router as middleware.
2. Greedy Window Router (single BGWorker): disjoint packing on SKU pool_keys with fairness backstop.
3. Two-domain lex-locking: SKU pool domain (routed for disjointness) + WIP pool domain (uncontended by construction).
4. 5-step committer pipeline: lex-lock → dedup-lookup → bounded snapshot hydration → in-memory dispatch → bulk UNNEST insertion across 6 tables.
5. Caller-tx coupling via Option (C): committer checks pg_xact_status(user_tx_xid); in_progress → eject envelope back to pending. **Committer NEVER sleeps for callers.** Central correctness fix from v2.1 spec review.
6. Persistent staging (durable_queue=true): WAL-backed envelope durability across postmaster restart.
7. Three status_insert_modes: caller_intx (default), caller_subtx, committer_lazy (requires persistent_staging).
8. wo_complete multi-pool event: K components + 1 WIP + 1 output, atomic within one envelope.
9. Multi-target bulk UNNEST writes: 6 INSERT/UPSERT statements per SuperBatch.

Decomposed into 28 sub-issues across 14 milestones (M0–M9 with M5a–M5e subdivided). Critical path is 28 deep with parallelism windows at M3.2⨯M3.3 and M5c.2⨯M5c.3.

title: zm69.h0: SERIALIZABLE + deferred-constraint ceiling probe (Candidate H)
description:

title: FIFO arena: replace A2 with a design that is correct by construction across all concurrency shapes
description:
## Context

A2 (acct-b3vs, shipped at commit dff20bd) is the current FIFO arena
implementation: per-backend `CellShadow` in `FIFO_PENDING_STACK`,
`LayerOp` staging at apply time, sorted-cell EXCL replay at
xact_commit, depletion rows written inline during apply.

Phase B of acct-a3rj (commit fdad1c3) added `cost_layers.qty_received`
+ `fifo_overconsume_check()` for **post-hoc detection** of the
concurrent over-consume case. R-MB6 confirms detection works.

**Detection is not correctness.** When two backends concurrently
exhaust the same thin layer, A2 commits both depletions; the ledger
ends up with double-attributed COGS + negative-with-respect-to-truth
pool inventory; bgworker drain hits CHECK and silently drops the
pending entries; `cost_layers.qty_remaining` stays stale forever.
`fifo_overconsume_check` reports the overshoot, but nothing reverses
the bad postings.

This issue tracks the structural fix: a FIFO arena design that is
**correct by construction**, not detect-and-flag-after-the-fact.

## Scope: what "correct by construction" means here

For every committed posting_line in cost_layer_depletions reachable
via the FIFO apply path:

1. `SUM(qty_consumed for layer L) <= cost_layers.qty_received for L`
   holds at commit time, not as a recon-detected drift.
2. `cost_layers.qty_remaining` is the true residual; bgworker drain
   never silently drops entries.
3. Account balances reflect actual inventory movement; no
   committed posting_line is structurally double-attributed against
   a layer it could not have consumed.

For every aborted txn:

4. No state change to durable tables persists (already holds — txn
   semantics).
5. No state change to shmem persists past the abort point that
   another backend can observe.
6. Cell state remains correct: subsequent apply/read against the
   cell sees pre-abort truth without waiting on a recon-tick repair.

For every savepoint stack:

7. ROLLBACK TO restores the in-shmem cell state to the savepoint's
   logical view, observable immediately by the parent txn's
   subsequent reads.

## Surfaces that must work

Concurrent shapes that R-MB6 + sibling tests already cover:

- R-MB1..R-MB5: 2-4 backends, mixed commit/abort, baseline + thin
  layer + cross-cell.
- R-MB6: concurrent exhaustion of a thin layer (currently
  documented as gap; must flip to **prevented**).
- R-BG1..R-BG3: bgworker race, savepoint apply + drain.
- R-SP1..R-SP3: 50-deep savepoint stack, RELEASE vs ROLLBACK TO,
  2000-iter retry loop.
- R-CR1..R-CR2: container restart, un-drained pending_drain (R-CR2
  is the OTHER known gap besides over-consume).

Concurrent shapes acct-a3rj surfaced as **not yet tested**:

- 3+ backends concurrent on same thin layer (overshoot scaling).
- Concurrent over-consume across multi-layer pools (walk-the-chain
  order under contention).
- Receipt commit racing concurrent issue lazy-seed (seed snapshot
  stale relative to durable).
- Ring overflow flip racing concurrent issues (in-ring vs
  durable_only path divergence on layer identity).
- Identical idempotency_key from concurrent backends against same
  cell.
- Recon walker concurrent with apply (fifo_arena_recon SHARED vs
  apply EXCLUSIVE, contention behavior unverified).

The new design must pass tests for all of the above. Existing R-MB1..
R-MB5 + R-BG/R-SP/R-CR tests must continue to pass.

## Candidate approaches

Three families exist, each with documented tradeoffs in acct-fhq7:

**B — OCC-validated PreCommit replay**. Backend snapshots last_seq at
apply; PreCommit revalidates; raises 40001 on conflict. Closes
over-consume structurally; multi-week build; the external-source
proposal that surfaced this had sketchy tradeoffs but the core idea
is sound for this gap.

**E — In-place mutation + needs_repair**. Mutate ring inline; flag
cells dirty on abort; recon EXCL-wipes + reseeds from durable.
Operational simplification over A2 but does NOT close over-consume
(depletions still written from shadow snapshot); also has subxact
correctness issues raised in conversation (parent expects pre-subxact
state visible immediately; needs_repair defers to recon-tick).

**F — Undo-log**. Per-frame undo ops recorded at apply, replayed at
abort. Structurally equivalent to A2 with explicit undo instead of
implicit shadow-discard.

None of these is obviously the right answer. The point of THIS issue
is to commit to **whichever is fundamentally correct**, not to pick
based on LOC count or perf projection alone.

## Process

1. Phase 1 — Audit. For each candidate (B, E, F, or a new design),
   walk through the seven correctness criteria above + the six
   untested shapes. Eliminate candidates that fail by construction.
2. Phase 2 — Prototype the survivor against R-MB6 + the six
   untested shapes (file as sub-issue: extend tests/fifo_rollback_
   correctness_t* with the new shapes BEFORE building the
   prototype).
3. Phase 3 — Bench against bench_fifo_rollback_inject baseline
   (≥33.7 committed/s @ 5% rollback fan-out, 5K pools, 60s × 20w).
4. Phase 4 — Replace A2; close acct-fhq7 (the parked Approach E
   decision), acct-8axd (Alt D — moot when correct design ships),
   acct-a3rj-followup if filed.

## Acceptance

- All R-MB1..R-MB6 + R-BG1..R-BG3 + R-SP1..R-SP3 + R-CR1..R-CR2 +
  property_fifo_rollback pass.
- New tests for the six untested shapes (filed as sub-issues) pass.
- `fifo_overconsume_check()` returns zero rows for every committed
  state across the regression net.
- Throughput within 10% of A2 baseline (37.4 committed/s @ 5%
  rollback) OR demonstrably better.
- bgworker drain never silently drops entries (no CHECK-violation
  rollback path in the steady state).
- Subxact semantics: parent txn sees correct pre-subxact state
  immediately after ROLLBACK TO, no deferred-repair window.

## Out of scope

- WAL crash safety beyond what A2 already provides (lazy-seed from
  durable).
- Multi-database bgworker scope.
- Production-tier observability (alerts, dashboards).
- Catch-up repair tool for already-corrupted durable state (would be
  its own one-shot tool; PoC scale → drop the DB).

## Relationship to other issues

- Supersedes acct-fhq7 (which framed the choice as A2 vs Approach E;
  this issue says neither is the answer if it's not correct by
  construction).
- Subsumes acct-8axd (Alt D shadow pool — moot).
- Builds on acct-a3rj's detection infrastructure (qty_received +
  fifo_overconsume_check stay; they become the regression net for
  proving the new design holds the invariant, not the operational
  signal).
- Depends on R-CR2's un-drained pending_drain gap being addressed
  in-band by the chosen approach (it's the OTHER A2 correctness
  gap; both must close together).

## Priority justification

P1 — known correctness gap in shipped FIFO code path. Books can be
silently wrong under concurrent exhaustion. PoC scale workloads
unlikely to hit it routinely (R-MB6 is the only test that reproduces
it deterministically) but the gap is real and the regression net's
detection function does not constitute a fix. Not P0 because (a) PoC
is pre-production, (b) detection exists, (c) workaround for affected
queries is to read from posting_lines + cost_layer_depletions
directly rather than trusting cost_layers.qty_remaining.

title: PoC P5: batch API + FIFO — pre-pass layer slice allocation
description:
Fifth sub-issue of acct-qdp5. Blocks-on P3. Parallel with P4.

SCOPE:
- Migration: add cost_layers (id, account_id, qty_remaining, unit_cost, receipt_date), cost_layer_depletions (id, layer_id, posting_line_id, qty_consumed, unit_cost). NO PARTITIONING in PoC (keep simple).

CORRECTNESS GATES:
- Total qty depleted = total qty requested across batch.
- SUM(depletion cost_amount) per envelope = posting_line.amount EXACTLY.
- Layers consumed in receipt_date order across the batch.

2. Bench at ≥5K TPS at batch=1000.
