close_reason: Superseded by acct-wb75 (convergence meta-epic). The Path A vs B framing was narrower than the actual decision. The convergence adopts subledger separation as part of broader GL-first convergence per research/posting-lines-convergence-plan.md.

title: AP1: post_inventory_adjustment wac_perpetual uses stock_available cross-class qty divisor (acct-fii sibling)
description:
Surfaced by Phase 2 of acct-du2 audit. mig 0027 (latest version) post_inventory_adjustment wac_perpetual branch has the SAME bug shape as the original acct-fii (P1) which was fixed only in post_cost_adjustment (mig 0069). post_inventory_adjustment was overlooked.

Lines 345-348:
  SELECT debits_total - credits_total INTO v_qty_balance FROM accounts WHERE id = v_qty_acct;  -- stock_available(sku, location): CROSS-CLASS
  SELECT debits_total - credits_total INTO v_val_balance FROM accounts WHERE id = v_val_acct;  -- inv_value_<class>(sku, location, currency): PER-CLASS

Lines 360 / 381: v_effective_uc := v_val_balance / v_qty_balance — per-class value divided by cross-class qty. When SKU has both raw and fg pools at same location, divisor is too large → unit cost under-priced → value-leg amount under-posted → per-class running avg drifts wrong.

Undetected because tests/inventory_adjust.rs uses single-class fixtures.

Fix: replace the v_qty_balance read with the per-class signed SUM on transfers.qty filtered to v_val_acct (mirrors mig 0069 lines 198-206 in post_cost_adjustment).

Test: extend the planned A18_same_loc_raw_and_fg conformance case to also exercise post_inventory_adjustment, not just post_cost_adjustment.
close_reason: False alarm. Phase 2 audit read the older mig 0027 body of post_inventory_adjustment which had the cross-class qty divisor bug. The LATEST version is in mig 0031 (lines 562-564 + 594-596) which uses per-class signed SUM on transfers.qty filtered to v_val_acct — same pattern as the acct-fii fix in mig 0069 for post_cost_adjustment. The fix actually landed in mig 0030 (acct-1vr 'transfers.qty migration') BEFORE acct-fii surfaced the same shape in post_cost_adjustment. No code change needed; verified by re-reading mig 0031 wac_perpetual + wac_periodic branches.

title: EPIC: codebase audit for class-confusion / pool-divisor / dispatch-resolution bugs + correctness invariant test regime
description:
META-EPIC for systematic detection and prevention of the bug-class exposed by acct-rgb, acct-fii, and acct-69e: 'function presents class-/cost-method-/document-specific semantics but reads cross-class / cross-method / cross-document state'.

# Bug class characterization

Three closed bugs share the same DNA:

* acct-rgb (P1): rm_issue_to_wo silently substituted component_std for component cost_method dispatch. wac_perpetual / wac_periodic components were tracked at running avg on the inventory side but consumed at standard cost on the WO side.
* acct-fii (P1): post_cost_adjustment used stock_available qty (cross-class) as divisor while applying delta against inv_value_<class>. Same-location raw+fg over-adjusted by the other class's qty share.
* acct-69e (P3): post_wo_complete pre-balance + residual sweep absorbed OTHER WOs' WIP balance into THIS WO's variance_wo_close when multiple WOs shared parent_sku × routing_op.

Common DNA:
1. State reads aggregate across an axis (class, cost_method, document) the function is conceptually scoped to a single slice of.
2. The bug surfaces only in 'realistic' multi-tenant pool layouts (mixed raw+fg, mixed components, interleaved WOs). Tests built with isolated pools mask it.
3. The fix is always 'narrow the read to the function's true scope' (per-class signed SUM, dispatch-on-this-SKU, solo-at-pool gate).

# Audit strategy

## Phase 1: Pattern-grep audit (~1 day)

Search every plpgsql function for these anti-patterns:

* **AP1: stock_available as divisor.** Any 'SELECT (debits_total - credits_total) ... WHERE kind = stock_available' followed by division — flag for review. Correct pattern: per-class signed SUM on the value pool's transfers.
* **AP2: debit-first SKU resolution in flagging/dispatch.** Any 'COALESCE(d_acct.sku_id, c_acct.sku_id)' on a path that flags into transfers_provisional or dispatches cost_method. Should be credit-first (depletion source).
* **AP3: pool reads outside FOR UPDATE.** Any 'SELECT debits-credits' on accounts that subsequently get balance-mutating writes in the same function without an intervening FOR UPDATE on those accounts.
* **AP4: cost_method assumed not dispatched.** Any value computation 'qty * resolve_standard_cost_at(...)' without a CASE on the SKU's cost_method. Tier 1 of acct-rgb fixed _wo_emit_bom_lines; sweep for siblings (post_so_ship for sold SKU? post_inventory_adjustment for asserted unit cost vs running avg? post_scrap for parent value?).
* **AP5: parent/document scope mixing.** Any pool read that doesn't gate on 'this is the only document touching this pool right now' before mutating. acct-69e gate pattern: stock_wip qty == p_qty before drain (== 0 after).
* **AP6: variance routing on drained debit-normal pools.** Any close-hook style posting that DR/CR a debit-normal pool that the WO/document path drained to 0 in-period — risk of pushing negative on signed-mixed multi-doc drift.
* **AP7: cross-currency pool reads.** Any inv_value_* read that doesn't filter by currency when the SKU might have multi-currency partitions.
* **AP8: idempotency-replay race.** Any function reading wo_events / similar idempotency tables BEFORE the FOR UPDATE on its primary lock target. acct-69p caught one; sweep for siblings.

Deliverable: REVIEW.md listing every function + match + verdict (clean / suspicious / bug / fix-needed).

## Phase 2: Structural per-function audit (~3 days)

For every entry-point document function (post_*) AND every helper (_*_compute_amount, _wo_emit_bom_lines, _post_transfers_apply_event, _wac_close_pool_qty_in, etc.):

1. **Enumerate inputs + outputs**: what's the function's conceptual scope? (Single class? Single SKU? Single WO? Single period?)
2. **Enumerate value-pool reads**: each pool read — is it scoped to the function's intended domain, or does it aggregate across?
3. **Enumerate qty-divisor reads**: same exercise; flag any cross-class.
4. **Enumerate cost_method dispatches**: resolve which SKU drives each branch; verify it's the depletion-source SKU.
5. **Enumerate document/WO-sharing assumptions**: does the function assume sole-occupancy of any pool? If so, is that gated?
6. **Enumerate currency/period boundaries**: where does the function cross either, and is the cross handled?
7. **Enumerate post-write invariants**: what should hold after the function returns?

Output: per-function review notes + fix-needed flags.

## Phase 3: Property-based / fuzz testing (~2 days)

Add tests/property/ with proptest-style generators that exercise each entry point with random inputs:

* Random number of SKUs (1–5), random cost_methods per SKU
* Random number of locations (1–3), random shared/distinct layouts
* Random per-class qty/value seedings
* Random sequence of operations (po_receive, ap_bill, inventory_adjustment, cost_adjustment, wo_start/op_move/scrap/wo_complete)
* Random period boundaries with close_period interspersed
* Random idempotency replay attempts

Post-run invariants asserted on EVERY scenario:
* I1 No debit-normal account has negative balance.
* I2 No credit-normal account has positive balance.
* I3 For every (sku, loc, class, currency): per-class signed qty SUM on inv_value_<class> >= 0.
* I4 For every parent_sku × routing_op: stock_wip qty >= 0.
* I5 Class avg = inv_value_<class>.balance / per-class qty SUM (within ±1 truncation tolerance).
* I6 Per-(ledger_kind, currency) double-entry: SUM(debits) == SUM(credits) always.
* I7 No transfers_provisional row with finalized_at NOT NULL AND variance_amount IS NULL (CHECK already enforces).

Test framework: extend tests/common/mod.rs with assert_invariants_hold(pool, label). Call it at the end of every scenario (and optionally between operations for deeper coverage).

## Phase 4: Conformance fixture extensions (~1 day)

Extend tests/data/conformance.json with A18 cases:

* A18_same_loc_raw_and_fg (acct-fii regression lock)
* A18_mixed_component_cost_methods (acct-rgb regression lock; mixed std + wac_perpetual + wac_periodic in one BOM)
* A18_interleaved_multi_wo (acct-69e regression lock)
* A18_credit_first_sku_resolution (multi-output co-product wo_complete_v with output_sku ≠ parent_sku)
* A18_currency_partition (multi-currency same-location)

## Phase 5: Static lint tooling (~2 days, optional)

Build a lightweight SQL-aware grep tool (Rust binary or shell script with sqlfluff if available) that flags anti-patterns AP1–AP8 in db/migrations/ on every CI run. Output: lint warnings, no build break (optional break on AP1 / AP4 / AP5 specifically — those are the high-confidence bugs).

## Phase 6: Documentation (~half day)

Add to CLAUDE.md a 'Class-confusion checklist' load-bearing decision block enumerating:

* RULE: Per-class qty divisors MUST come from per-class signed SUM on the value pool's transfers, NEVER from stock_available (which is cross-class).
* RULE: cost_method dispatch resolves SKU from the CREDIT side (depletion source) of the transfer.
* RULE: Functions that mutate a shared pool MUST gate state-affecting operations on solo-occupancy (qty before == this_doc's_contribution).
* RULE: Pool reads MUST be under FOR UPDATE on the same account before subsequent writes — even if the writes are routed via post_transfers later.
* RULE: variance routing on debit-normal pools that are drained in-period must use single-leg (orig_debit ↔ variance_acct) not 2-leg through the pool.
* RULE: Idempotency replay checks happen BOTH before FOR UPDATE (fast path) AND after (race-safe).

Each rule cites the bug that motivated it (acct-rgb, acct-fii, acct-69e, acct-smn, acct-69p) so future readers see why.

# Testing regime (ongoing)

After this epic ships:

1. **Pre-commit / CI step**: pattern-grep AP1–AP8 over modified migration files; fail on AP1 / AP4 / AP5 matches without explicit allowlist comment.
2. **PR template addition**: 'Does this function read pool_qty? If yes, confirm it uses per-class signed SUM (not stock_available). Does it dispatch on cost_method? Confirm credit-first SKU resolution. Does it operate on pools other documents may share? Confirm solo-occupancy gate.'
3. **New-function checklist in CLAUDE.md**: every new post_* function gets the property-based test treatment from Phase 3.
4. **Quarterly re-audit**: re-run Phase 1 grep; sample 3–5 random functions for Phase 2 walk; refresh property-test seeds.

# Acceptance

* REVIEW.md committed listing every function + AP scan results + verdict.
* Every flagged bug filed as a sub-issue (or fixed in scope if straightforward).
* tests/property/ harness with all 7 invariants enforced + at least 100 random scenarios per entry-point function.
* tests/data/conformance.json A18 cases.
* CLAUDE.md 'Class-confusion checklist' added.
* Optional: scripts/sql-lint.sh for AP1–AP8.

# Sub-issues (file as discovered during audit)

Phase 1 + 2 will surface concrete fix-needed flags. Each gets its own bd issue (P1 if real correctness bug, P2 if code-smell-but-not-broken, P3 if Phase 2-deferrable).

# Estimate

7–10 days of focused work, half audit, half tooling/tests/docs. Best done as a focused sprint after Slice C / acct-rso ship to avoid re-auditing churned code.

# Why P1

Correctness violations of this class were silent until specifically tested. Each bug surfaced only when the user pushed back on a specific test scenario. Without systematic detection, the codebase will accumulate more. The epic is meta-correctness infrastructure, not a feature.
close_reason: All 16 sub-issues closed (12 fixes via migrations 0071-0076 + 1 false alarm + 3 Phase 3 property-test binaries). REVIEW.md captures the audit trail; CLAUDE.md 'Class-confusion checklist (R1-R6)' codifies the rules; tests/property_*.rs provide ongoing regression coverage.

title: post_cost_adjustment uses cross-class stock_available qty — over-adjusts when raw+fg share a location
description:
post_cost_adjustment (mig 0024) reads v_pool_qty from stock_available(sku, loc), which is NOT class-segmented (one row per (sku, loc) regardless of inventory_class). When a SKU has both raw and fg pools at the same location (a common ERP layout — contract manufacturers, small shops, etc.), the function uses the COMBINED qty as the divisor in v_new_value = target_unit_cost × v_pool_qty, but applies the resulting delta against the class-specific inv_value_raw or inv_value_fg pool. The class-specific pool ends up over- or under-adjusted by the OTHER class's qty share.

Concrete failure: SKU X at loc L has 100 raw @ $10 ($1000 inv_value_raw) and 50 fg @ $20 ($1000 inv_value_fg). stock_available(X, L) = 150. post_cost_adjustment(X, L, USD, 'raw', target=$12): v_pool_qty=150 (bug, should be 100), v_new_value=150×$12=$1800, v_delta=$1800-$1000=$800. Posts dr inv_value_raw / cr variance_cost_adjustment $800. Result: inv_value_raw=$1800 over raw_qty=100 → avg=$18/unit, NOT $12.

Same family of bug as acct-rgb (silent cost-method substitution): function presents class-specific semantics but reads cross-class state. Tests in tests/cost_adjust_interleaved.rs currently work around by using distinct locations per class — that masked the bug.

FIX: Replace the stock_available qty read with the per-class qty SUM signed by direction on the value pool — same pattern as acct-1vr / mig 0030, used in tier 1/2 of acct-rgb (_wo_emit_bom_lines wac_perpetual / wac_periodic branches):

  SELECT COALESCE(SUM(
    CASE WHEN t.debit_account_id  = v_val_acct THEN  t.qty
         WHEN t.credit_account_id = v_val_acct THEN -t.qty END
  ), 0) INTO v_pool_qty
    FROM transfers t
   WHERE v_val_acct IN (t.debit_account_id, t.credit_account_id)
     AND t.qty IS NOT NULL;

LOCK ORDER: v_val_acct already locked FOR UPDATE prior to the read; pattern is consistent with existing post_cost_adjustment lock sequence. The stock_available account no longer needs FOR UPDATE for this divisor (the per-class SUM is over the historical transfer log against v_val_acct, which is held under exclusive lock); but keep it locked anyway to maintain the broader lock-order invariant with concurrent inventory_adjustment.

ACCEPTANCE: tests/cost_adjust_interleaved.rs::wac_perpetual_class_isolation_under_interleaved_adjust extended (or new test) to use SAME location for raw+fg; verify cost_adjust on raw doesn't poison fg pool's avg and vice versa.
close_reason:
Migration 0069 swaps post_cost_adjustment's qty divisor from stock_available(sku, loc) — which is cross-class (one row per (sku, loc) regardless of inventory_class) — to per-class signed SUM on the class-specific value pool's transfer log: SUM(t.qty signed by direction on v_val_acct). Same pattern as acct-1vr / mig 0030 used by post_inventory_adjustment, _wo_emit_bom_lines tier 1/2 wac branches, and tier 1/2 wac_periodic on WIP. Class-isolated; works correctly when raw + fg share a location (common ERP layout for contract manufacturers and small shops).

Pre-fix concrete: 100 raw @ $10 + 50 fg @ $20 at same loc → stock_available=150. cost_adjust(raw, target=$12): pre-fix posted $800 over-shoot → raw avg=$18 not $12. Post-fix: $200 delta → raw avg=$12 (correct).

16 new tests in tests/cost_adjustment_per_class_qty.rs cover same-location raw+fg both classes, sequential adjustments, multi-currency same-location class isolation, empty class P0010 (when other class populated), idempotency replay, delta=0 audit-only path, post-consumption adjustment, write-up + write-down on different classes, audit pool_qty per-class invariant, cross-class activity isolation, and many-flux fluctuations. 368/0/9 tests pass; ci-check digest ea2000c5...

title: Tier 1: wac_perpetual components issue at running avg (rm_issue_to_wo)
description:
Sub-issue of acct-rgb. Lift the standard-only cost path on rm_issue_to_wo for wac_perpetual components.

**Change.** _wo_emit_bom_lines computes item value-leg amount using the COMPONENT's cost_method:
- standard → resolve_standard_cost_at(component, business_date) × adj_qty (today's behavior; unchanged).
- wac_perpetual → SELECT (debits_total - credits_total) FROM the component's inv_value_<class>(sku, location, currency) account FOR UPDATE; SELECT pool qty via per-class transfers.qty SUM (acct-1vr pattern); unit = pool_value / pool_qty; amount = adj_qty × unit.
- wac_periodic / wac_retroactive → P0026 deferred to acct-rgb-tier2 / acct-rso.

Lock order: lock the component's inv_value pool BEFORE post_transfers's lock pre-scan acquires its own locks (the pre-scan re-acquires the same lock idempotently). Same pattern as acct-wig (mig 0063) for wac_perpetual on parent WIP.

**Edge cases.**
- Empty pool at issue time → P0010 (cannot deplete empty pool). Component must have inventory before WO consumes it. Today we'd succeed-with-wrong-cost; tier 1 fails-fast.
- wac_perpetual component with no standard_cost row → no longer required; resolve_standard_cost_at not called for this branch.
- Yield gross-up (bom_lines.scrap_pct) still applies on adj_qty; only the per-unit cost source changes.

**Tests.**
- wac_perpetual component + WO consumption drains at running avg (after PO receipt at one cost, second PO receipt at another, the issue uses blended avg).
- post_cost_adjustment on the component pool propagates into the next rm_issue (pool revalued → next issue uses new avg).
- Multi-component WO with mixed cost methods (one standard, one wac_perpetual): each issued correctly.
- Pool running avg stays consistent (no drift) across multiple rm_issue events on the same component.
- Empty pool raises P0010.

**Files.** db/migrations/0066_rm_issue_actual_cost_tier1.{up,down}.sql + tests/wac_perpetual_component_issue.rs (or extension to existing tests/wac_perpetual_wip.rs).
close_reason: Closed

title: rm_issue_to_wo dispatch on component.cost_method — actual costing across component → WIP boundary
description:
**Bug.** rm_issue_to_wo always values the consumption at component_std (resolve_standard_cost_at), regardless of the component SKU's cost_method. Components declared wac_perpetual / wac_periodic / wac_retroactive are tracked at average on the inventory side but consumed at standard on the WO side. The arithmetic gap silently absorbs into the source pool's running avg as drift. This violates the contract cost_method is supposed to enforce: 'wac_perpetual means the SKU's value is its running weighted average, period.'

**Manifestation.**
- Pool: 100 units at $12 avg ($1200 total).
- Component standard: $10 (set days/weeks ago via post_standard_cost_roll).
- WO issues 40 units. BOM2 drains 40 × $10 = $400 instead of 40 × $12 = $480.
- Pool: 60 units at $13.33 avg ($800). The $80 mismatch was eaten silently by pool drift; never surfaced as a transfer.
- post_cost_adjustment on the raw pool revalues the carrying value but the next rm_issue still drains at $std, so the cost_adjust delta never propagates into WIP either.

**Fix.** rm_issue_to_wo dispatches on component.cost_method, mirroring how op_move / wo_complete / scrap dispatch on parent.cost_method (acct-wig / acct-bol / acct-smn).

**Scope by tier.**

**Tier 1 (wac_perpetual components):** _wo_emit_bom_lines (or _post_transfers_compute_amount via reason-list extension) reads source pool running avg under FOR UPDATE at issue time. Lock order: source pool value account → existing locks. Standard branch unchanged. Tests cover: cost_adjust on wac_perpetual component now propagates into next WO's WIP fill; pool running avg stays consistent across rm_issue events.

**Tier 2 (wac_periodic components):** Same running-avg read mid-period; the resulting rm_issue_to_wo value-leg flags into transfers_provisional with cost_method='wac_periodic'. Close hook (wac_periodic_close_hook) extends the topological pool-walk DAG to include raw → WIP edges (rm_issue_to_wo from a wac_periodic raw pool feeds a downstream WIP pool). The existing acct-smn topological walk handles op_move chains; extending it to rm_issue is mechanical — same LEFT-JOIN-on-variance_amount cache trick, same single-leg posting on inv_value_wip destination. wac_retroactive parents on WIP (acct-rso) will need similar treatment but is gated separately.

**Tier 3 (wac_retroactive components):** chronological replay across all in-period rm_issue events for the component pool. Composes with acct-rso's broader retroactive replay redesign — likely fold into that epic rather than a standalone tier.

**Out of scope.**
- BOM rollup tool's parent_std calculation. parent_std stays as a forward-looking planning snapshot computed from component_std at rollup time. The variance between parent_std and actual-WAC-per-WO is what wo_close_v captures at WO close. (If a future requirement is 'live actual rollup', that's a separate epic.)
- FIFO / lot components. Tracked under acct-8gg.

**Implication for parent SKU cost methods.** Once components issue at actual, parent SKUs declared wac_perpetual (acct-wig) will see their WIP pool's running avg become a meaningful function of actual material cost rather than a near-deterministic mirror of parent_std. acct-wig's existing tests assume std-fill into WIP; they may need extension or revision once tier 1 lands.

**Acceptance.**
- Tier 1: wac_perpetual component issued via rm_issue_to_wo drains at pool running avg; pool's running avg unchanged by WO consumption (no drift); cost_adjust on the raw pool propagates into next WO's WIP fill; tests for these in tests/wac_perpetual_component_actual_cost.rs (or extension to existing wac_perpetual_wip.rs).
- Tier 2: wac_periodic component flagged on rm_issue; close hook re-amounts at raw pool's final_avg; downstream WIP final_avg picks up the cost shift via topological cache; tests for 2-WO drift through raw → WIP chain.
- Tier 3: aligned with acct-rso.
acceptance_criteria: See description.
close_reason: Tier 1 (acct-24b, mig 0066) + Tier 2 (acct-7py, mig 0067) shipped. Tier 3 (wac_retroactive components) folds into acct-rso per the umbrella's design: wac_retroactive's per-event chronological replay reads transfers.qty from value-pool events; for inv_value_wip pools rm_issue_to_wo carries component qty (qty_per_parent × p_qty), breaking final_avg. Surgery is the same refactor that lifts wac_retroactive parents on WIP. Tracked as acct-rso. Mixed parent/component cost methods are filed as acct-7eo. Core correctness violation (component cost_method silently substituted by component_std on rm_issue_to_wo) is closed for standard / wac_perpetual / wac_periodic components.

title: T5: Conformance fixture (input → expected output triples)
description:
Per Appendix B suggested next steps. tests/data/conformance.toml (or .json): 30-50 input batches with their expected per-event result codes and resulting account-balance deltas. Driven by a Rust harness (cargo test) that resets state between cases. Catches semantic regressions in post_transfers.

Path convention: tests/data/ is the Rust-idiomatic location for cargo-test-consumed fixture data. db/ stays reserved for SQL-side artifacts (migrations, init scripts, SQL seed fixtures under db/fixtures/).

Format choice (TOML vs JSON) deferred to implementation. JSON via serde_json comes free as a sqlx transitive; TOML needs an added dep (toml crate). User to confirm at implementation time.

Verify: all triples pass; adding a new triple round-trips through the harness.

title: T4: Deadlock-freedom load test (Rust)
description:
Per Part IV §13's 'Done when invariant tests pass' requirement. Rust integration test using tokio + sqlx: 100 concurrent writers, each picking a random subset of 5–20 accounts from the fixture and posting a valid batch via post_transfers. Sustain for 30 minutes. Snapshot pg_stat_database.deadlocks at start and end; assert delta is zero. Also assert per-ledger double-entry holds at the end.

Trigger: manual, opt-in. Long-running test gated behind #[ignore] (run via 'cargo test -- --ignored deadlock_freedom') or a dedicated bin under tests/. Not part of the default 'cargo test' run, and not part of scripts/ci-check.sh — there is no scheduled CI in this project.

Verify: 30-minute run completes with zero deadlocks delta; per-ledger double-entry GROUP BY ledger_kind, currency returns zero rows.
notes:
Scenario carried over from T3 (acct-93b.17 was its predecessor; folded
into T3, then deferred here because it is fundamentally a post_transfers
concurrency test, not a reservation test):

  Concurrent op_moves on the same WIP account serialize without
  divergence (W2 path). Multiple writers post op_move events touching
  the same stock_wip (sku, routing_op) account. Assert: no deadlocks,
  final balances equal sum of submitted amounts, no torn writes.

Naturally fits the 100-writer harness already specified — pick a
fixture (sku, routing_op) WIP account, route a fraction of the random
batches through it, assert balance integrity at the end alongside the
deadlock-delta and per-ledger double-entry checks.
close_reason: Closed

title: T3: Reservation atomicity tests
description:
Per Part IV §3.3 and the M7-resolved expiry path, in tests/ as Rust integration tests (flat .rs binaries — Rust integration tests cannot live in subdirectories):

- reserve_concurrency.rs: Concurrent reserves against the same (sku, location) — qty_promisable CTE under FOR UPDATE prevents over-reservation when total > on-hand.
- reserve_insufficient.rs: Reservation insert when qty_promisable < requested fails (RETURNING 0 rows; no row inserted).
- reservation_state_transitions.rs: Allocate, cancel, expire transitions only from 'active'. Attempts from other states no-op (UPDATE returns 0 affected rows).
- reservation_expiry.rs: Expiry single-statement UPDATE handles 1K simultaneously expired rows in one statement (correctness only).

Deferred from this issue:
- Concurrent op_moves on the same WIP account → folded into T4 (acct-93b.19); see notes there. This is post_transfers concurrency, not a reservation test.
- "1K rows < 100ms" wall-clock budget on the expire UPDATE → deferred to O1 (acct-93b.21) once Part IV §14.1 perf baseline exists; see notes there. Wall-clock budgets in unit tests are flaky and there is no Phase 0 perf baseline yet.

Run via cargo test. Verify: under contention, no double-reservation; expire UPDATE flips all 1K rows in one statement (RETURNING/affected count = 1000); state-transition UPDATEs from non-'active' states return 0 affected rows.

Originally written from a pre-D1 plan that referenced "tests/reservations/" — Rust treats `tests/<dir>/` as an internal module of a single test binary, not a directory of independent test binaries, so this suite uses flat tests/*.rs filenames matching T2's convention.
close_reason: Closed

title: W2: post_transfers — cost-computation dispatch (standard only)
description:
Per Part IV §3.4 / §3.5 and D4 (standard cost only in Phase 0; dispatch hook for future methods).

Add cost-computation logic for op_move / scrap / wo_complete / so_ship under the existing FOR UPDATE lock from W1. The function looks up skus.cost_method and dispatches:

- 'standard' branch (IMPLEMENTED in Phase 0):
  - op_move: amount = qty * std_unit_cost (sourced from skus.standard_cost; routings.std_cost when routings exist in Phase 1).
  - scrap: amount = qty * std_cost_to_current_op.
  - wo_complete: move qty_completed * sku.standard_cost from WIP to FG; residual WIP_value (if any) posts as a variance event to variance_wo_close.
  - so_ship: amount = qty_shipped * sku.standard_cost.
  - All amounts are deterministic functions of master data + event quantity. NO read-then-write of accumulator balances on this path.

- 'wac', 'fifo', 'lot' branches (NOT IMPLEMENTED in Phase 0):
  - RAISE EXCEPTION 'cost_method_not_implemented' (SQLSTATE 'P0006') with the method name and event reason in the message.
  - Future phases fill these in additively without changing the dispatch shape or any existing table.

Document the P0006 error code in W1's header comment.

Verify:
- 3-event WO sequence (start → op_move → wo_complete) on a 'standard' sku produces expected per-event balances and zero residual when std rates match.
- A sku with cost_method='wac' raises P0006 on any consumption event.
close_reason: Migration 0013_post_transfers_cost_dispatch added per Part IV §3.4/§3.5 and D4. Phase 0 implementation chose Option A (pure gate) over Option B (function-computed amount): caller still pre-computes 'amount' from W1 base path; function adds a check that for reason in {op_move, scrap, wo_complete, so_ship} the resolved sku's cost_method must be 'standard', else raise P0006. Sku resolution: COALESCE(debit.sku_id, credit.sku_id); if both NULL also raises P0006. Option B (required before non-standard methods can be implemented) tracked as acct-0ig; acct-8gg (WAC/FIFO/lot) depends on acct-0ig. Down migration restores W1 body verbatim. db/README.md 'Write path' section updated with P0006 row + Option A explanation. Verified with 4-case suite (TC1: 3-event WO sequence — wo_start, op_move, wo_complete — on standard sku, all 'ok' with correct balance deltas / TC2: op_move on wac sku -> P0006 / TC3: so_ship on fifo sku -> P0006 / TC4: ar_invoice on wac sku bypasses dispatch and posts 'ok') plus migrate run/revert/run round-trip across 0001..0013 (revert restores W1 body — verified by absence of 'cost_method_not_implemented' string in pg_proc.prosrc; redeploy restores W2 body).

title: W1: post_transfers — base path
description:
Implement non-cost-computation portion of post_transfers per Part IV §2.1.

Behavior:
1. Lock all referenced accounts in ascending ID order (deadlock prevention).
2. Loop per event in input JSONB array.
3. Idempotency: short-circuit on idempotency_key match → return 'exists' for that event index.
4. Validate: account_closed (P0001), ledger_mismatch (P0002), currency_mismatch (P0003), period_missing (P0004), period_closed (P0005) unless p_override_closed_period.
5. UPDATE accounts.debits_total / credits_total. CHECK constraints from L2 raise on violation, rolling back the surrounding txn (linked-batch semantics for free).
6. INSERT into transfers.
7. Return JSONB array of {index, result} per event.

Signature: post_transfers(p_events JSONB, p_override_closed_period BOOLEAN DEFAULT FALSE) RETURNS JSONB.

Document each error code (P0001..P0005) in a header comment block.

Length target: under 100 lines.

Verify: golden inputs produce expected state; each error code fires for its scenario; multi-event batch with one failing event rolls back the whole batch.
close_reason: Migration 0012_post_transfers added per Part IV §2.1 verbatim. Function post_transfers(p_events JSONB, p_override_closed_period BOOLEAN DEFAULT FALSE) RETURNS JSONB. Algorithm: lock all referenced accounts in ascending id order via FOR UPDATE (deadlock-free); per event — idempotency check on transfers.idempotency_key (skip with result='exists'), validate (P0001 account_closed, P0002 ledger_mismatch, P0003 currency_mismatch), period lookup (P0004 period_missing, P0005 period_closed unless override), UPDATE accounts.debits_total/credits_total, INSERT transfer; return JSONB array of {index (1-based), result}. Multi-event batch rolls back entirely on any validation failure (linked-batch semantics for free); idempotent duplicates skip without rollback. db/README.md updated with 'Write path' section: full event shape + error code table. Verified with 11-case suite (T1 valid event / T2 idempotency / T3-T4 P0001 closed debit+credit / T5 P0002 / T6 P0003 / T7 P0004 / T8 P0005 / T9 override bypasses P0005 / T10 multi-event batch with one P0001 fails atomically (no rows committed, balance unchanged) / T11 empty array returns []) plus migrate run/revert/run round-trip across 0001..0012.

title: L3: transfers table + append-only trigger
description:
Create transfers.sql per Part IV §1.2 — non-partitioned in Phase 0 (decision documented below). Columns:
- id BIGSERIAL PRIMARY KEY
- reason transfer_reason NOT NULL
- document_kind TEXT NOT NULL, document_id UUID NOT NULL, document_line_id UUID
- debit_account_id BIGINT NOT NULL REFERENCES accounts(id)
- credit_account_id BIGINT NOT NULL REFERENCES accounts(id)
- amount BIGINT NOT NULL CHECK (amount > 0)
- routing_op INT, counterparty_id UUID
- period_id BIGINT NOT NULL REFERENCES periods(id), business_date DATE NOT NULL
- idempotency_key UUID NOT NULL UNIQUE
- posted_at TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL DEFAULT clock_timestamp()
- posted_by UUID NOT NULL
- CHECK (debit_account_id <> credit_account_id)

Indexes (per §1.2, all 6):
- transfers_document  ON (document_kind, document_id, posted_at)
- transfers_debit_ts  ON (debit_account_id, posted_at DESC)
- transfers_credit_ts ON (credit_account_id, posted_at DESC)
- transfers_reason_ts ON (reason, posted_at)
- transfers_counterparty ON (counterparty_id) WHERE counterparty_id IS NOT NULL
- transfers_routing_op ON (routing_op) WHERE routing_op IS NOT NULL

Partitioning decision (Phase 0): NOT partitioned. Doc §1.2 spec is internally inconsistent — PARTITION BY RANGE (posted_at) + UNIQUE (idempotency_key) cannot coexist in Postgres (unique constraints on partitioned tables must include every partition-key column). Phase 0 ships non-partitioned + idempotency_key UNIQUE directly. Conversion to partitioning + a separate idempotency_keys side table is tracked as a future task gated on Part IV §14.1 exploratory baseline.

Then transfers_append_only.sql per Part IV §1.9 verbatim: fn_block_transfer_modifications() RAISE EXCEPTION 'transfers are append-only; UPDATE/DELETE rejected' USING ERRCODE = 'P9999'; trigger BEFORE UPDATE OR DELETE FOR EACH ROW.

Verify (deliberate-violation suite):
- INSERT valid transfer succeeds.
- UPDATE on transfers raises P9999.
- DELETE on transfers raises P9999.
- amount = 0 raises CHECK 23514.
- debit_account_id = credit_account_id raises CHECK 23514.
- Duplicate idempotency_key raises 23505.
- Non-existent account_id (debit or credit) raises FK 23503.
- Non-existent period_id raises FK 23503.
Plus migrate run/revert/run round-trip across 0001..00NN.
close_reason: Migrations 0007_transfers + 0008_transfers_append_only added per Part IV §1.2 / §1.9. Phase 0 path: NOT partitioned. Doc §1.2 internal inconsistency (PARTITION BY RANGE + UNIQUE idempotency_key incompatible) resolved by deferring partitioning to acct-e8g, gated on §14.1 baseline. PRIMARY KEY (id), idempotency_key UUID NOT NULL UNIQUE, all 6 indexes per spec, 3 FKs (debit/credit account, period), CHECK (amount > 0), CHECK (debit_account_id <> credit_account_id), append-only trigger fn_block_transfer_modifications raising P9999 on UPDATE/DELETE. Verified with 8-case suite (T1 valid insert / T2 UPDATE -> P9999 / T3 DELETE -> P9999 / T4 amount=0 -> 23514 / T5 same debit=credit -> 23514 / T6 duplicate idempotency_key -> 23505 / T7 non-existent debit account -> 23503 / T8 non-existent period -> 23503) + migrate run/revert/run round-trip across 0001..0008.

title: S3: Local clean-DB migration round-trip check (no remote CI)
description:
Local-only pre-push check. No remote CI host, no YAML workflows — a single shell entry-point developers run before pushing schema changes, verifying every migration applies cleanly and reverts cleanly against a clean Postgres.

Deliverables:
- scripts/ci-check.sh (host-agnostic shell):
  1. Ensure the dev Postgres container is up (call dev-up.sh idempotently, or fail with a clear message).
  2. Provision an ephemeral throwaway database (e.g. 'acct_ci') in the running instance — does NOT touch the dev DB or its data.
  3. 'sqlx migrate run --source db/migrations' against the clean DB.
  4. 'sqlx migrate info' — assert every migration shows installed.
  5. 'sqlx migrate revert' until empty, then 'sqlx migrate run' again — assert green.
  6. 'pg_dump -s' on the clean DB | sha256sum — print the schema digest for visibility.
  7. Drop the throwaway DB on exit (success OR failure; trap EXIT).
- db/README.md note pointing devs at scripts/ci-check.sh and what it guarantees.

Verify:
- scripts/ci-check.sh on a clean repo -> exit 0; schema SHA printed.
- Introduce a deliberately broken migration -> exit non-zero with a useful error.
- Re-run after fix -> exit 0 again.

Out of scope:
- Remote CI workflow (GitHub Actions / GitLab / Forgejo / etc.) — deferred until a git remote is configured. The script is the substance; any future host is a thin wrapper that calls it.
- pgTAP, SQL linting, 'cargo test' — added later as separate steps when those layers exist.

Open implementation question:
- Clean DB strategy: ephemeral database in the existing instance (CREATE DATABASE acct_ci ... DROP DATABASE) vs ephemeral parallel container. DB-in-instance is simpler/faster and reuses the loaded shared_preload_libraries (pg_cron). Parallel container is more isolated. Lean DB-in-instance unless pg_cron global state makes it messy.
close_reason: scripts/ci-check.sh added. 5-step pre-push guard against ephemeral acct_ci DB inside the existing dev Postgres instance: (1) sqlx migrate run on fresh DB, (2) info asserts every migration installed (greps for 'pending'), (3) revert loop until empty, (4) re-run migrate, (5) pg_dump -s | sha256sum prints schema digest. Drops acct_ci on EXIT via trap. db/README.md gains a 'Schema integrity check' section. Verified end-to-end on the current chain: 13 migrations forward, 13 reverts, 13 redeploys, schema SHA256 ec7c5cbe288d83e3413676552047829a2f0f8c88a07a7469b42006b1edfab8e6. Committed as ae37f2e.

title: S1: Provision Postgres dev environment
description:
Stand up a Postgres 18 dev environment in Docker per D2.

docker-compose.yml:
- service: postgres, image: postgres:18 (verify liburing support; if absent, build a custom Dockerfile FROM postgres:18 that installs liburing-dev and rebuilds — flag during implementation if the upstream image is sufficient).
- named volume for /var/lib/postgresql/data.
- mount a postgresql.conf with: io_method=io_uring, shared_preload_libraries='pg_stat_statements,pg_cron', cron.database_name set appropriately.
- expose 5432 to host for dev tooling.

scripts/dev-up.sh: docker compose up -d, wait for healthcheck, run 'CREATE EXTENSION IF NOT EXISTS pg_stat_statements; CREATE EXTENSION IF NOT EXISTS pg_cron;' on first boot.
scripts/dev-down.sh: docker compose down (preserves volume by default; -v flag to wipe).

Document in db/README.md.

Verify:
- psql connects from host
- 'SHOW io_method' returns 'io_uring' (not 'sync' or 'worker')
- '\dx' shows pg_stat_statements and pg_cron
- container restart preserves data
- liburing presence: confirm postgres binary is linked against liburing (ldd in the container)

title: posted_at write contract: R-1 correctness rests on true business dates
description:
Why: the recalc engine replays each pool in (pool_id, posted_at, id) order (design-v3.2-recalc-a R-1). Correctness therefore rests on trx.posted_at carrying the TRUE business/effective date at write time — a semantic contract no CHECK constraint can enforce (the DB cannot know the real business date). The v3.1 harness precedent shows the failure mode: it stamped a compile-time-constant posted_at on every run, which silently degrades R-1 replay to id-order. Backdated events are admitted BY DESIGN (that is R-2), so posted_at-close-to-now is not a valid guard either — the contract is about truthfulness, not recency.

What: (a) specify the write contract explicitly in the spec-of-record (rides acct-476a.1): who stamps posted_at, what it means, what writers MUST NOT do (wall-clock defaults, constant stamps); (b) add the mechanical guards that ARE possible: NOT NULL, staging-write validation, optional sanity bounds vs the open-period window (the 0017 closed-prefix rejection already bounds the past side at admission); (c) decide recalc-a D1: denormalize posted_at onto trx_line + (pool_id, posted_at, id) index vs join-at-recalc — measure or argue, record the decision; (d) audit in-tree writers (ledger-bench drivers, harness, SPI entry points) for constant/wall-clock stamping and fix.

Acceptance: contract text in the spec-of-record; guard set implemented or explicitly declined with reasons; D1 decided and recorded; writer audit clean.

title: Backport design: document-cost read model under two-phase costing (R7 under alt-C)
description:
Why: acct's convention persists document-line cost snapshots that must equal posting amount/qty (rule R7, motivated by acct-5prc/acct-quca). Under alt C the observed provisional cost on trx_line is 22-36% wrong per depletion until recalc trues it up (soak §3 drift table), and the authoritative value lives in max-generation cost_settlement rows that keep moving until close. No read model or contract exists for 'the document's cost': which generation, when it is displayable, how invoicing/COGS consumers should read it.

What: a design note specifying a document-cost read model — max-generation cost_settlement view joined to the depletion line, plus a settled-vs-provisional status flag — and R7 restated for a two-phase costing plane (the document audit field points at the settlement view, never snapshots the provisional observed cost). This is the parity item that decides whether alt-C can coexist with acct's document-line conventions at all.

PROVENANCE: parity (parent R7/acct-5prc, soak-results §3, 0009 generation model)

title: Backport design: currency dimension and the non-inventory posting plane
description:
Why (two schema-shape decisions that multiply through every recalc structure): (a) CHARTER-EXCLUDED single currency — trx_line.unit_cost/posting_line.amount are bare BIGINT with no currency column; pools, layers, settlements, and the close sweep are currency-less. Parent acct's double-entry invariant is per (ledger_kind, currency) (B3) and pools are keyed per currency. Every recalc structure (cost_layer_consumption, pool_settlement, sweep residue) grows a currency dimension at backport — a key-shape decision, not an add-a-column patch. (b) trx_line requires pool_id NOT NULL and qty <> 0, so cash/AR/AP/FX/tax/revenue legs — which acct posts as qty-NULL SKU-less posting_lines (Slice C relaxed the gate for exactly this) — cannot exist in this ledger; backport must define how the non-inventory posting plane (needs no recalc) shares period close, immutability guards, and the posting_account_map convention with the recalc plane.

What: one sizing/design note covering both, written before any acct integration epic fixes schema. Include the effective-dated standard-cost delta (v3.2's mutable standard_cost row is replaced outright by the parent's acct-hlr shape — append-only standard_costs + _resolve_standard_cost_at — not merged) and the actor/provenance posture (defer with parent Part VII Q6; when RBAC resolves, add posted_by to trx and the inbox in one change).

title: Backport design: reservations under alt-C's no-gate posture
description:
Why: no reservation table or lifecycle exists in v3.2 (not charter-promised), but parent acct treats inventory_reservations as first-class rows (blocker-B1 lineage; post_so_ship flips reservations atomically), and reservation enforcement is exactly the synchronous per-pool qty-adjacent gate that alt C deliberately removed for FIFO/LIFO (design-v3.1 §16: qty is a flagged signal, not a gate). Graduation cannot bolt reservations on without deciding where the gate lives — this is the sharpest posture conflict with the parent system.

What: a design note (not implementation) resolving reservation semantics under alt-C. Candidate shape: reject-at-admission consult like the recalc_backpressure probe, which already proved the read-free-common-case pattern (one probe against a normally-empty PK); alternatives: aggregate-signal soft reservations. Must cover the interaction with flagged-negative pools and the P0006-vs-flag mapping decision for the parent's no-negative-inventory posture (Epic H acct-9ij). Prerequisite for any acct integration epic.

title: Close interaction coverage: close × backpressure, close under live load, premise-violation wedge shape
description:
Why (three untested interaction surfaces on one function): (a) No test closes a period containing a throttled pool — unpinned: the close drain's exact-tail counter reset + release per swept pool, sweep-line exclusion from the counter, feed blocking behind the close's counter-row hold, and post-close admission on a pool throttled at stamp time (a stuck throttle would 53400-reject next-period traffic). (b) The fence (advisory 32022) and the gate re-check loop have never fired: every soak close happens after quiesce, the headline run reports recheck_rounds 0, and no test submits concurrently across the gate→fence→stamp window. (c) The documented 'loud post-close alarm' for an undelivered backdated straggler is entirely unverified — nothing pins what the wedge actually looks like (floor set, queue row present, generation unchanged, stable across retries).

What: (a) acceptance case engaging a fifo pool (low bound), running forced and unforced ledger_close_period, asserting counter reset, throttle release, next-period submit flows, sweep line not counted; plus a parked-feed-bump-vs-close-sweep interleaving using the existing pg_stat_activity rendezvous pattern. (b) deterministic interleaving parking a submit across the fence, asserting the straggler is swept in a re-check round or lands pre-stamp, and that recheck_rounds >= 1 is reachable; optionally a soak variant with a REAL (non-rolled-back) mid-load close, forced, asserting the emitted variance move reconciles against the pre-close G2b bound. (c) the premise-violation case — settle, submit backdated, close WITHOUT ingesting, then ingest and drive recalc_step — asserting the 55000 wedge shape and gauge visibility (this test then evolves with the gate-fix and quarantine issues in the other epics).

PROVENANCE: tests (3 P2/P3 items merged), bench-ops (forced-close-at-scale item); close.rs, soak-results §1/§8, README Phase 5

title: Restart/crash recovery coverage: real process kills and a mid-workload Postgres restart
description:
Why: every crash simulation in the suite is in-transaction (BEGIN/step/ROLLBACK crash-steps; apply-without-advance at the consumer API level). Nothing kills a recalc worker backend mid-pass (pg_terminate_backend), kills the standalone feed process, or docker-restarts acct-postgres mid-workload. The crash-safety story (claims are xact row locks released on backend death; dirty-set is the crash-recovery boundary; slot cursor survives restart) is argued in README/recalc-c §6 but never exercised — notable because recalc is the SOLE costing plane for FL, and the claim protocol already had one defect (acct-qm7o.8) only live sessions could reach.

What: a restart-recovery acceptance/chaos harness: bounded workload with feed + 2 workers as real child processes; SIGKILL a worker mid-pass and the feed between apply and advance; docker-restart acct-postgres mid-workload; re-attach and assert quiesce converges, R1 oracle equivalence holds, the slot resumes from confirmed_flush_lsn, and no queue row/floor/backpressure row is wedged. Add --kill-feed-at/--kill-worker-at/restart-pg knobs to the soak so the shapes are repeatable. Also cover the documented feed-redelivery backpressure over-count: assert the doubled recalc_backlog value after crash-redelivery, the spurious engage below the true bound, and the settle-heals-and-releases tail (currently a stated contract with zero pins).

Memory note: pgrep self-matches in sentinel loops — exclude self in any wait primitive.

PROVENANCE: tests (P2), bench-ops (chaos shape), design-core (§18 kill-9 residual), feed (redelivery contract untested)

title: Fix: footprint watchdog does not stop the load generators
description:
Why: budget.rs's module doc claims every long-running loop checks AbortSignal and bails, but only the feed task, worker tasks, and quiesce loop do (soak.rs:147-151,198,361). driver.rs run_load/LoadCfg has no AbortSignal field — caller and drainer loops run to the duration deadline regardless of a 20 GB trip, continuing appends at the offered rate (~2.6 KB WAL/commit) for the entire remaining run. On a long/hot rung that overshoots the cap by GBs on the shared dev cluster — the same ENOSPC class soak §4 documents taking the cluster down once already.

What: thread AbortSignal into LoadCfg; check abort.is_tripped() in the caller and drainer loops each iteration; unit test that a tripped abort halts submission within one pacing interval; fix the budget.rs docstring if any loop is deliberately excluded.

PROVENANCE: bench-ops (budget.rs docstring vs driver.rs:49-65/175-254; soak-results §4)

title: v3.2 audit: Test and bench coverage
description: The suite is strong on sequential/deterministic coverage but the tests auditor mapped systematic holes exactly where history says bugs live (acct-qm7o.8 needed live sessions; acct-qm7o.10 lived in an unseeded basis cell). Restart recovery, close×backpressure, and the harness watchdog gap are the load-bearing ones; the bench epic items establish the baselines the parent's 'baseline before complexity' posture requires.
notes: DESIGN INPUT transferred from acct-hh7b (closed 2026-08-07, superseded machinery): the acct-235v/hh7b batching physics apply directly to the v3.2 staging-drain SKIP LOCKED committers. (1) Committers parallelize on DISJOINT pool work only — on pareto-hot/intertwined workloads they serialize on per-pool FOR UPDATE locks and sit idle (235v s10: flat ~1390 trx/s across committer_count 2/4/8); the bind is per-pool lock serialization, inherent to a correct ledger. (2) Batching leverage lives in same-pool coalescing (235v s5 single hot pool: cg=32 gave 0.03 locks/trx, host-max throughput, at ack-latency cost). (3) UNVERIFIED user hypothesis (2026-06-03): on small-pool/intertwined workloads, invert the spread tuning — FEWER committers + LARGER batches; committer_count is a pool-distribution-dependent balance axis. The 63qs perf work (esp. the gated 63qs.6 baseline) should include a drain-batch-size x committer-count x pool-distribution sweep cell to verify. Artifacts: poc/ledger-v3.1/ledger-harness results CSVs named in acct-hh7b notes; full finding text preserved there.

title: Wedged-pool quarantine + fail-fast operator loops
description:
Why: a permanently-aborting recalc pass (0017 PeriodClosed reject from a post-close straggler, MissingPostingAccounts, etc.) rolls back, so the recalc_queue row survives with its ORIGINAL enqueued_at — oldest-first claim ordering (recalc.rs:360-363) makes the poisoned pool the FIRST claim of every worker tick forever, degrading claim throughput for the whole dirty set. scripts/run-recalc.sh retries every 1s unconditionally with no consecutive-error trip; soak §5 explicitly credits the bench harness's fail-fast (10-20 consecutive errors) with surfacing the acct-qm7o.8 wedge 'in seconds; without it the run would have hung to timeout'. A stuck backpressure row has no documented release override (engine owns release; a wedged engine never releases).

What: (a) recalc_queue.parked_at set after K consecutive PeriodClosed-class failures, excluded from claim ORDER BY, surfaced in recalc_queue_depth (the future reopen workflow consumes the parked state — D14 attach point); (b) consecutive-error trip + loud non-zero exit in run-recalc.sh (and an escalation/backoff classification in the feed loop's retry policy: Parse/Protocol = fatal exit, sqlx transient = capped backoff — today a poison batch re-delivers every 250ms while retained WAL climbs to slot invalidation); (c) a documented manual-release/diagnosis procedure for a throttled wedged pool.

Acceptance: deterministic test that wedges a pool (backdate-after-close shape), asserts it parks after K failures, other pools keep settling, and the parked state is visible in the gauge.

PROVENANCE: recalc-notes, recalc-close, archaeology, bench-ops, feed (recalc.rs:360-363, run-recalc.sh:16-31, main.rs:47-59, soak-results §5)

title: v3.2 audit: Operational readiness
description: The soak produced the incident catalog (ENOSPC, wedged pool, sticky throttle, gate-fail close, slot loss) but the operator surface is shell loops that retry forever, gauge views nobody polls, no thresholds, no runbook, and no escape hatches. Five auditors flagged overlapping pieces; these issues turn the documented loud-alarm posture into something an operator can actually see and act on.

title: Retention/pruning for append-only bookkeeping: superseded generations and the inbox tail
description:
Why: cost_settlement + cost_layer_consumption are append-only and generation-keyed (0009); only the max-generation row is ever read (load_priors DISTINCT ON), so after a period closes every superseded generation for in-period depletions is dead weight that nothing prunes — and the amplification axis makes this the dominant growth surface. ledger_inbox done/failed rows accumulate with pruning explicitly deferred in the 0011 header ('an operational follow-up, out of scope here') but no follow-up was ever filed. Parent repo has the acct-sbr2 partition-lifecycle convention these tables would need at graduation.

What: (a) post-close pruning/compaction of superseded generations for finalized periods (keep max-generation rows + their adjustment linkage + anything a future reopen needs); (b) a drained-tail sweep or partition policy for ledger_inbox; (c) evaluate acct-sbr2-style monthly partitioning for trx_line/posting_line/cost_settlement as the graduation posture. Acceptance: prune runs against a closed period leave verify/close-report invariants intact and authoritative valuation unchanged.

PROVENANCE: recalc-close, parity, design-core, archaeology (0009, 0011 header, parent acct-sbr2 convention)

title: Bound the backdate/re-cost write-amplification axis (throttle + gauge)
description:
Why: every backdated event forces an R-2 full-opening replay and appends a new generation of cost_settlement + cost_layer_consumption rows per affected depletion. soak-results §4 measured a 3600s backdate window at 400 trx/s filling ~70 GB → ENOSPC in minutes, wedging feed and workers; even the passing headline run shows ~2.2 settlement writes per FL depletion. The shipped backpressure lever (acct-qm7o.7, migration 0018) deliberately bounds only the un-costed tail — backdates settle promptly while invalidating history, so they never accumulate in that counter (soak §8 scope note names this 'future work'). Only harness-side mitigations exist (20 GB watchdog, 120s backdate knob); production-shaped deployments have nothing.

What: (a) expose settlement-rows-per-physical-event (the §8-named natural input) as a gauge; (b) a second throttle keyed on that rate, or an admission rule on below-frontier posted_at beyond a configured depth/age, or floor debouncing (coalesce multiple backdates into one replay per pool per pass) to cut the amplification constant; (c) a disk/WAL headroom check in the operator scripts equivalent to the bench watchdog. Also fold in: materialize_layers currently DELETEs and re-INSERTs the full open-layer set on every pass (recalc.rs:768-795) — recalc-b §6 promised O(new events) churn; switch forward passes to differential materialization (insert new-receipt layers, touch only fold-drawn layers), keeping wholesale rewrite for full replays.

Red-green: re-run the soak §4 configuration (3600s window) under the throttle and show bounded growth.

PROVENANCE: design-core, recalc-notes, recalc-close, bench-ops, archaeology, parity (6/9; soak-results §4/§8, 0018 header, recalc.rs:768-795)

title: v3.2 audit: Write-amplification and recalc scalability
description: The one measured catastrophic failure mode of the architecture: soak §4's 3600s backdate window filled ~70 GB to ENOSPC in minutes, and 6 of 9 auditors independently flagged that the shipped backpressure lever deliberately does not bound this axis, nothing prunes the append-only generation tables, and full replay is O(entire pool history) forever. All deferred-by-design pieces are currently untracked in bd.

title: Enable overflow-checks in the release profile
description:
FOUND BY the audit completeness critic. Workspace Cargo.toml [profile.release] sets lto/codegen-units but NOT overflow-checks = true, so the installed extension wraps silently on any unchecked i64 arithmetic — contrary to the fail-loud charter. ledger-core is disciplined at multiply sites (i128 + try_into) but additive paths (fold_qty accumulation, counter bumps, qty sums) are plain i64 ops. WORK: add overflow-checks = true to [profile.release], rebuild, full suite, and grep for any hot-path additive site that deserves an explicit checked_add with a domain error instead of a panic.

PROVENANCE: critique wf_81df5b8c-3ec; Cargo.toml [profile.release]

title: Idempotency: payload-hash replay instead of duplicate-key backstop
description:
Why: UNIQUE (trx_type, source_id) raises a raw 23505 on the direct path and marks a staging duplicate terminally 'failed'. An at-least-once caller retrying after a lost ack cannot distinguish 'already applied' from 'genuine source-id collision with different payload' — the caller must treat 23505 as maybe-success. design-v3.1 §18's gate re-triage explicitly kept the idempotency payload-hash item (acct-0at4.3 row) as an architecture-agnostic survivor for this build, and the parent's R6 bar is replay-returns-original-result.

What: add payload_hash to trx; on unique-violation compare hashes — equal returns the existing trx.id (true replay), different fails loud with a distinct error; mirror in the staging drain (mark 'done' carrying the existing id). Tests: retry-after-commit returns the same id; conflicting reuse fails loud on both paths.

PROVENANCE: hot-path, parity (both flag it; design-v3.1 §18 survivor row; 0003/0011 comments)

title: Decide and pin the staging-inbox ordering contract for strict methods
description:
Why: drain.rs:19-23 and the 0011 header justify unguaranteed cross-committer same-pool apply order via the alt-C argument (recalc re-sorts, observed cost is provisional) — which covers FIFO/LIFO only. For WAC pools the depletion's running-average cost is order-sensitive AND authoritative (WAC has no recalc plane), so multi-committer reordering changes posted GL nondeterministically. Worse, for any strict method a receipt→deplete pair split across two committers can invert: the depletion is claimed first, fails the qty gate, and lands terminally 'failed' even though its receipt commits milliseconds later — no retry exists. Coverage matches the gap: the concurrent-committer acceptance case is FIFO receipts-only; the equivalence property is explicitly single-committer.

What: choose one — (a) document single-committer (or pool-affine claiming) as a hard requirement when strict-method lines ride the inbox, or (b) scope the inbox to fifo/lifo lines, or (c) implement pool-affine claim grouping (also the direction the drain-batch convoy finding points at; cf. memory: routing affinity — pack shared-state work into one batch). Add a strict-method multi-committer interleaving test pinning whichever contract is chosen.

PROVENANCE: hot-path (drain.rs:19-28, 0011 header, acceptance_staging_drain.rs:100-133); archaeology (convoy finding, same-pool batching direction)

title: Enforce the specific-method qty=1 contract — partial deplete of an oversized layer strands inventory
description:
Why: specific.rs deplete accepts qty_to_deplete < layer.qty (guard is l.qty >= qty, specific.rs:140-150) then unconditionally DeleteLayer. Receipt qty=5 + deplete 2 → layer deleted, aggregate qty=3 with value retained, GL posts only 2×uc, and every subsequent depletion raises InsufficientInventory(available=0) forever; the 3 units are permanently unreachable with no error on the corrupting operation itself. design-v3.1 §3.4 documents this as the deliberately-unenforced 'qty=1 half' of the caller contract, but a one-line guard closes the whole class and the project discipline is that defensive guards in ERP code are load-bearing.

What: enforce qty == 1 at specific receipt (or full-layer equality at deplete) as a new LedgerError variant + SQLSTATE mapping in ledger_error_map.rs + acceptance case. Then extend property coverage (see the property-net issue) with partial-deplete probes that must reject.

PROVENANCE: hot-path (specific.rs:116-187, design-v3.1 §3.4); tests auditor confirms specific is absent from every property net

title: Wire up PlanResult::coalesce_aggregates — multi-line same-pool STD/specific submissions abort with raw 21000
description:
Why: ledger-core/src/plan.rs:182 coalesce_aggregates exists precisely because the bulk INSERT..ON CONFLICT DO UPDATE apply step rejects touching one row twice, and its doc comment says SPI callers call it first — but grep shows zero call sites. apply_submission (submit.rs:206-218) passes the plan straight to bulk_write::apply_plan_result, which batches all UpsertAggregate rows into ONE ON CONFLICT statement (bulk_write.rs:234-249). Two lines on the same STD pool in one submission (e.g. +5/-3 inv_adjustment), or a specific receipt+deplete on one pool, emit two UpsertAggregate mutations for (pool_id,0) → PG 21000 'ON CONFLICT DO UPDATE command cannot affect row a second time', aborting the whole submission (direct) or marking the inbox row terminally failed with that cryptic message (staging). WAC handles the identical shape correctly, so parity is silently method-dependent.

What: call plan.coalesce_aggregates() in apply_submission (or inside apply_plan_result). Add same-pool multi-line STD and specific receipt+deplete cases to acceptance_direct_methods and the property net.

Failure is currently loud and atomic (no corruption), but a legitimate shape fails with an unclassified SQLSTATE.

PROVENANCE: hot-path (plan.rs:169-213, submit.rs:206-218, bulk_write.rs:234-249)

title: v3.2 audit: Hot-path correctness
description: The hot-path auditor found one reachable defect (a legitimate submission shape aborts with a raw 21000), one silently-corrupting caller-contract hole, and a cluster of missing decode/dispatch guards. All are small, isolated fixes in ledger-direct/ledger-core with clear acceptance shapes.

title: Audit + pin session-timezone independence of period boundary casts
description:
FOUND BY the audit completeness critic (wf_81df5b8c-3ec). Every period-coverage predicate casts DATE to timestamptz using the SESSION TimeZone: 0017 period_guard_trx_line (NEW.posted_at >= start_date::timestamptz), period_guard_cost_settlement, close.rs gate_pools (($1::date + 1)::timestamptz), and the sweep scoping. A connection with a non-UTC TimeZone GUC evaluates different period membership than the UTC-session writers did — silent mis-valuation class, same family as the close-gate P1 items. WORK: characterize the exposure (which casts run in whose session), then pin: either AT TIME ZONE 'UTC' on every boundary cast or store period bounds as timestamptz; add a regression test that runs a close and a guarded insert under SET TIME ZONE 'America/New_York' and asserts identical membership to UTC.

PROVENANCE: critique wf_81df5b8c-3ec; db/migrations/0017; close.rs gate_pools

title: Trigger-block UPDATE/DELETE on trx_line, posting_line, cost_settlement, cost_layer_consumption
description:
Why: 0017 ships BEFORE INSERT guards only. The engine's closed-period correctness argument is literally 'an unchanged physical prefix means the engine can never recompute a different authoritative cost' (0017 header) — a single stray UPDATE to a historical trx_line silently breaks replay determinism and closed-period valuation with no fail-loud. Parent doctrine: append-only is a schema invariant, not API discipline (Part IV §1.9); v3.2 has it half-implemented (inserts yes, mutations no).

What: BEFORE UPDATE/DELETE triggers raising loud on trx_line, posting_line, cost_settlement, cost_layer_consumption (engine writes are INSERT-only already; the pool_settlement upsert stays exempt). One acceptance case per table.

Memory note: defensive guards in ERP scope are load-bearing even when no current code path mutates these tables.

AMENDED from the completeness critique: include accounting_period in the guard set — 0017's period_guard_trx_line re-reads accounting_period.state LIVE per insert, so a stray UPDATE accounting_period SET state='open' after close silently unfreezes the closed prefix (inserts flow again, replay input mutates, no fail-loud anywhere). A BEFORE UPDATE trigger must confine legal transitions (open->closing->closed, no closed->open outside a future D14 reopen workflow).

PROVENANCE: parity (0017 header rationale; parent CLAUDE.md posting_lines append-only invariant)

title: v3.2 recalc: aggregate value_sum diverges from fold−deltas identity on backdated uncovered-depletion replay (pre-existing; ~1-in-850 property flake)
description:
FOUND BY the acct-qm7o.8 adversarial verification workflow while soaking the R8-extended property_recalc_engine binary (2 failures in ~1900 random cases, ~1-in-850). CONFIRMED PRE-EXISTING by A/B: the identical deterministic repro fails on both the fixed acct-qm7o.8 build AND the pre-fix .so (git-stash rebuild), so the claim-protocol change is not the cause — the diff only touches claim/settle, and sequential (uncontended) execution reads byte-identical state either way.

DETERMINISTIC REPRO (single fifo pool, property_recalc_engine case shape, T-grid timestamps):
Receipt(T11, qty 4, cost 279); Ingest; Ingest; Deplete(T13, 29); Ingest; Receipt(T11, 37, 39); Receipt(T11, 35, 327); Step; Deplete(T10, 47); CrashStep; Deplete(T13, 47); Ingest; Ingest; Deplete(T13, 32); quiesce (ingest+drain until clean).
RESULT: pool_state aggregate value_sum = -20019, but the R3 identity (hot-path commit-order fold with exact-empty flush, minus telescoped generation deltas sum((auth_final − observed) × qty)) = -14016 — off by -6003. The R1/R2/R4-R8 invariants all hold on the same state; only the aggregate-value identity diverges.

SUSPECTED AREA (unverified): reconcile_aggregate_value / uncovered-depletion re-cost telescoping — the shape needs deep negative inventory (uncovered depletions observed at clamp-0) plus a backdated receipt re-costing them across generations; the per-depletion delta uses (auth − prior) × qty per pass while the R3 test model telescopes (auth_final − observed) × qty once. ALTERNATIVELY the R3 test-model fold itself may mis-model a clamp/flush edge for this shape — decide which side is wrong before touching engine code (the acct-qm7o.6 flush-wipe finding, soak-results.md section 6, was a test-model bug of this kind).

IMPACT: property_recalc_engine flakes at ~1-in-850 cases (PROPTEST_CASES=100 default → roughly 1-in-8 full-suite runs hits it eventually); a red R3 in that binary is THIS bug, not the acct-qm7o.8 claim fix. The wedge-free soak + close paths are unaffected (verify V2/V4 passed all soaks; the divergence needs the specific uncovered-then-backdated shape).
notes:
Evidence trail: acct-qm7o.8 verification workflow wf_0dedfcba-c88, refute:concurrency agent — standalone replay test reproduced left:-20019 right:-14016 on the fixed .so (contains read_claim marker) and on the pre-fix .so (marker absent). R3 assertion is property_recalc_engine.rs (search "R3"; line drifted after the R9 addition).

RESUME PLAN (written pre-compaction 2026-07-12; acct-qm7o.7 SHIPPED as e3cc835 and CLOSED — every epic child except THIS one is closed; HEAD e3cc835 on branch ledger-v3.2, worktree /home/kaalin/dev/acct/.claude/worktrees/ledger-v3.2, paths under poc/ledger-v3.2/).

READ ORDER before anything: (1) THIS issue in full — the deterministic repro and the decide-which-side-is-wrong framing are in the description; (2) ledger-direct/tests/property_recalc_engine.rs — the R3 identity formulation (hot-path commit-order fold with the exact-empty flush, minus telescoped generation deltas sum((auth_final - observed) x qty)) AND its in-test fold model; (3) ledger-direct/src/recalc.rs — write_generation's per-pass delta math ((auth - prior) x qty, prior = gen-N-1 authoritative or observed for first costing), reconcile_aggregate_value (single-statement aggregate value_sum -= net_delta), and the uncovered-depletion path (strict_fold costs the uncovered remainder at the depletion's OWN observed cost; ledger-core strict module); (4) ledger-bench/src/verify.rs V2 — the same identity at scale WITH the v2_skipped_flush_wiped precedent; (5) bench/soak-results.md section 6 — the acct-qm7o.6 flush-wipe finding: the FL exact-empty flush (qty - delta = 0 => value_sum := 0) DISCARDS engine corrections folded in before it, and that time the fix was the TEST MODEL / verify formulation, not the engine; (6) ledger-direct/src/cte.rs — fl_deplete's clamp/flush arithmetic (what the hot path actually records for uncovered depletions and when the flush fires).

STEP 1 — ROOT-CAUSE, DO NOT TOUCH ENGINE CODE YET. The issue names two hypotheses: (A) engine bug in the telescoping — per-pass deltas use (auth_N - auth_{N-1}) x qty; summed across passes they SHOULD telescope to (auth_final - observed) x qty per depletion; a divergence of exactly -6003 on the repro suggests one pass's prior resolution or one depletion's observed anchor is wrong (candidate: a depletion re-costed in a pass where its gen-N-1 row was written with prior != what reconcile_aggregate_value assumed, or an uncovered depletion whose observed cost the hot path recorded differently than load_priors' fallback assumes); (B) the R3 TEST MODEL mis-models a clamp/flush edge for the deep-negative + backdated-receipt shape (the .6 precedent — the exact-empty flush makes the offline identity non-reconstructible for some shapes, and verify.rs already skips-and-counts flush-wiped pools; the property model may need the same carve-out or a corrected fold). Recommended method (ultracode is ON): reproduce deterministically first — write a standalone scratch test (or pin the repro sequence as a #[ignore] case) and dump per-step state: after EVERY op, capture pool_state aggregate (qty, value_sum), all cost_settlement rows (depletion, gen, auth, prior, adjustment_posting_line_id), posting_line amounts, and the in-test model's fold value; the FIRST step where model and DB diverge localizes the side. THEN fan out a verification workflow if the arithmetic is contested. The -6003 delta factors: check whether it equals (some auth - some observed) x some qty combination from the dumped rows — that usually names the exact depletion and pass.

STEP 2 — DECISION GATE: if root cause is (B) test-model, the fix is test-only (model correction or a principled skip-and-count mirroring verify.rs v2_skipped_flush_wiped + a doc note in soak-results section 6 style); if (A) engine, the fix touches recalc.rs value math — REAL design surface. If the remedy involves choosing among alternatives with tradeoffs (e.g., change delta anchoring vs post-hoc aggregate true-up vs document-as-non-reconstructible-and-cover-at-close), AskUserQuestion BEFORE implementing (surface-design-choices rule; claiming is not authorization to pick). Note the close sweep already trues value_sum := sum(open-layer value) at close and posts the residue to variance — so mid-period aggregate drift of this kind is BOUNDED and swept; that context matters for choosing remedy weight.

STEP 3 — SHIP: either way, the repro becomes a permanent deterministic regression test (acceptance_recalc_engine case or a pinned case in the property binary — follow the .8 precedent of a dedicated acceptance test if engine code changes). Engine-code fix => rebuild/reinstall (scripts/install-direct.sh, cargo-pgrx 0.18.1 at ~/.cargo-pgrx/0.18.1/bin/cargo-pgrx — global is 0.19.1, do NOT clobber) + docker restart acct-postgres + orphan sweep BEFORE the full cycle (NEVER recreate the container) + FULL suite (13 DB binaries, SKIP_INSTALL=1 bash scripts/run-tests.sh, backgrounded sequential, ONE watcher) + consider a bounded soak (trend shape, seed 42, 20GB cap is watchdog-default; scripts/soak.sh defaults RATE 400/WINDOW 3600 are DANGEROUS — always pass bounded values; check /proc/loadavg + foreign compiles first — bench host is the noisy daily driver). Test-only fix => run the touched binaries only (tiered-testing rule). Then commit (acct-qm7o.9: ... + Co-Authored-By trailer, local only, no remote), bd close with decision record, STOP and report.

KEY FACTS / CONSTRAINTS: pgrx SpiTupleTable .first().get() ERRORS on zero-row results — use t.next() for maybe-empty reads. property_recalc_engine now carries R9 (backpressure stays-off) — unrelated to R3; reset_state also truncates recalc_backlog/recalc_backpressure and resets recalc_backpressure_config to defaults (bound 200 — the repro's ~7 events never engage backpressure; the lever is orthogonal to value math). 18 migrations now (0018 = backpressure); migrations are content-addressed — never edit applied+committed ones (0018 is now COMMITTED: new schema = 0019+). The R3 flake rate means a red R3 anywhere during THIS issue's suite runs is THE bug under work — expected until fixed. Greenfield comments (no historical/change-relative phrasing in code; bench-report docs may narrate findings). Never quote time estimates. Single-quote bd close reasons containing backticks.

close_reason: DECISION RECORD: root cause = R3 TEST MODEL (hypothesis B), engine correct per the acct-qm7o.6-ratified flush semantics. The FL exact-empty flush (post-event qty 0 => value_sum := 0) discards engine corrections folded before it; the deterministic repro reproduced both published numbers exactly (value_sum -20019 vs telescoped identity -14016; divergence -6003 = the wiped gen-1 correction (72-279)x29). (6) Publication = migration (schema); slot = consumer-created runtime state (ensure_slot). (7) Cluster prereqs applied: wal_level=logical (ALTER SYSTEM + docker restart, orphan sweep first); max_slot_wal_keep_size=4GB dev guardrail against an abandoned slot pinning WAL (slot invalidation acceptable in dev; production posture = monitor feed_lag). TESTS: parser units + 10 acceptance (dirty-set, floor R-1 tiebreaks, crash-redelivery idempotency, empty-batch advance, gauges under lag) + 100-case property (F1 dirty-set == touched-pool set exactly; F2 floor == min (posted_at,id) behind frontier regardless of batch cuts / simulated crashes; F3 drained stream is a strict no-op). Full 6-binary suite green. NOTE for phase 4: recalc workers drain recalc_queue FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED and delete on settle; G2a view reads pool_settlement which phase 4 populates; a worker settling past an event the feed later delivers just causes a free no-op pass (conservative, correct).

title: v3.2 phase 2: HOT PATH — SPIKE-B direct UPDATE + staging outbox + SKIP LOCKED committers

- Staging-table outbox + SELECT ... FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED committers (SPIKE-A)
