title: ledger-v3.2 recalc engine (e): close-time semantics — finalize provisional to authoritative valuation
description:
Design what happens at period close: the transition from mid-period provisional/standard-valued reporting to a finalized authoritative valuation, and how close interacts with recalc backlog.

Per design-v3.1 §16/§19: under alt C mid-period GL is qty-only or standard-valued (SAP material-ledger shape). Close is when recalc's authoritative valuation move lands. This is NOT an adjustment storm reversing a prior cost plane (§19 voided that framing — there is one costing plane, nothing to reverse); it is the FIRST and only authoritative valuation, sized by the acct-0at4.7 replay-oracle drift (§19 table: biased under a trend, worst for standard basis at rel 61.72% FIFO).

Design scope:
- Close gating: period close cannot complete until recalc drains for that period (§19 chain). Design the gate + the forced-close escape (emit the accumulated valuation at once — large, one-signed under a trend) and its operator signal.
- The three production worker-model shapes (§7) to choose among / support: Oracle continuous-worker, SAP on-demand (ledger_settle_pool(pool_id) SPI before a statutory query), Dynamics periodic Inventory-Close-on-schedule gating the period transition. Cadence knob (child c) parameterizes across these.
- accounting_period close hook (§7 / §13: table exists, close hooks NOT implemented in PoC) — the hook that triggers finalize.
- Finalize semantics: what makes a period's valuation authoritative + immutable; relationship to the parent acct repo's period-close invariants is NOT in scope (v3.2 PoC stays single-currency, no multi-period reopen — §13).

Depends on children (a) + (d). Design-only.
design:
DESIGN SHIPPED: poc/design_research/design-v3.2-recalc-e.md (referenced from design-v3.2.md §5). The finalize child — last of the five.

"Close" under alt-C: mid-period GL is qty-only/standard-valued (§16); close is when the FIRST-and-only authoritative valuation lands (NOT an adjustment storm — one plane, nothing to reverse, §19), sized by acct-0at4.7 drift (c's G2b, biased under trend). Since recalc runs continuous (c), close is a consistency gate + finalize, not a from-scratch batch.

accounting_period (open->closing->closed, §2.4) + the close HOOK (§7/§13: table exists, hook unimplemented) this child adds — orchestrated close_period(p_period_id, p_actor, p_force), mirroring parent-repo "close is orchestrated not a manual UPDATE": FOR UPDATE period row (serialize callers) -> closing -> gate -> sweep -> finalize.

GATE (on c's G2a): period P=[start,end] drain-complete iff every pool with event posted_at<=end_date has recost_floor none in-period AND settled_through_posted_at>=end_date. Period-scoped via R-1 chronological key (a). Pass->finalize; fail->block (wait for continuous drain) unless forced.

FINALIZE = authoritative + IMMUTABLE (adopts parent "period lock is a schema invariant"): freeze the period's max-generation cost_settlement rows; stamp closed_at/closed_by; state->closed. Backdated-into-closed-period REJECTED (PeriodClosed, analogous to parent P0021) — reopen out of scope §13. Consistent with c's D11 (no reopen => no backdate-into-closed => no historical checkpoint need).

VARIANCE-INTO-EMPTY-POOL sweep (from d §6, timing owned here): per in-period pool AT FINALIZE (not per pass), residue = Sum(auth depletion value) - Sum(consumed layer value) - remaining open-layer value, posted as ONE cost_adjustment_line vs posting_account_map.variance_acct, value_sum absorbs (neg allowed 0009). Makes value_sum EXACT at period end (conservation acct-0at4.5 reconciliation point). NULL variance_acct -> fail loud.

FORCED CLOSE = drain SYNCHRONOUSLY, NOT skip (departs from parent p_force_provisional which bypasses): under alt-C there is NO provisional cost leg to fall back on (§19), so a period closed with un-costed in-period depletions has NO valuation = incoherent. Force = burst all workers + caller through remaining in-period dirty pools then finalize = the SAP CKMLCP forced-close (pays the whole fold now, long for a deep Pareto pool = honest cost). NO SILENT FORCE: surface G2b (sized move) + G2a (lagging pools) before forcing; close report returns them.

Three §7 worker-models COEXIST as facets, not alternatives: Oracle continuous = c's default drain; Dynamics periodic = close_period gate; SAP on-demand = settle_pool(pool_id) SPI (force-drain one pool to head). Deployment picks posture by how it CALLS these, not a different engine.

SPI: close_period(period, actor, force); settle_pool(pool_id); immutability trigger (PeriodClosed).

Validation: post-close completeness (every in-period depletion finalized, conservation reconciles, value_sum exact); gate blocks-while-lagging/passes-when-settled; forced close drains+emits G2b move+finalizes (magnitude surfaced first); immutability reject; idempotent re-close; worker-model coexistence (settle_pool + continuous + close_period == same finalized valuation).

Open (all operational, none touch correctness): D12 forced-close granularity; D13 immutability mechanism (recommend trigger = schema invariant per parent); D14 PeriodClosed-reject site = where a future reopen hook attaches.
close_reason: design shipped: design-v3.2-recalc-e.md. close_period orchestrated hook: G2a recalc-drain gate (period settled through end_date) + variance-into-empty-pool sweep at finalize (d) + finalize=authoritative+immutable (period lock schema invariant; backdate-into-closed rejected, reopen out of scope §13). Forced close = drain SYNCHRONOUSLY not skip (no provisional plane, §19), operator sees G2b move first. Three §7 worker-models coexist (Oracle continuous=c drain / Dynamics periodic=close gate / SAP on-demand=settle_pool SPI). All validated == full-opening replay = the acct-0at4.7 oracle.

title: ledger-v3.2 recalc engine (d): recalc state/bookkeeping schema + idempotent re-run
design:
DESIGN SHIPPED: poc/design_research/design-v3.2-recalc-d.md (referenced from design-v3.2.md §5).

Fixed constraint (§17): durable STREAM cursor is the logical-decoding slot confirmed_flush_lsn — NO home-grown trx_line watermark. The tables below are pool-side authoritative-state (what has been costed + to which generation), distinct from stream progress.

Builds on shipped v3.1 0006-0011: pool_state.value_sum exists (0007), aggregate CHECKs scoped to layer_id=0 so layer rows (layer_id>0) already unconstrained → recalc writes/rebuilds them freely; value_sum allowed negative on aggregate (0009). source_trx_line_id single-column = the D3 gap; posted_at not denormalized = the D1 gap.

Schema deltas:
- Enums: trx_type+=cost_adjustment, line_type+=cost_adjustment_line, posting_event_type+=cost_adjustment (DISTINCT from existing 'variance' which carries STD PPV — keep recalc correction auditably separate). Sequence cost_adjustment_id_seq for adjustment trx.source_id (satisfies UNIQUE(trx_type,source_id)).
- D1 RESOLVED: denormalize trx_line.posted_at (populated from trx.posted_at at insert, off critical section) + index (pool_id, posted_at, id) → index-only R-1 walk, drops the JOIN. Hot-path write-contract add (surface to §3). Write-path must supply REAL business posted_at (schema can NOT NULL but can't enforce truthful).
- D3 RESOLVED: cost_layer_consumption(depletion_trx_line_id, layer_trx_line_id, recalc_generation, qty, unit_cost) — the marking/audit linkage (§14.4/§13); authoritative unit_cost DERIVABLE as banker_div over gen-N rows. Chosen over per-layer posting_line decomposition (bloats journal, worse query).

Idempotency = MODEL 1 generation-delta (append-only), recommended over Model 2 (settled-flag+overwrite, rejected: loses audit, bad crash boundary, fights append-only ethos):
- pool_settlement(pool_id, recalc_generation, settled_through_posted_at/id, recost_floor_posted_at/id, last_recalc_at) — recost_floor implements R-2; generation = per-pool monotonic counter.
- cost_settlement(depletion_trx_line_id, recalc_generation, authoritative_unit_cost, prior_unit_cost, adjustment_posting_line_id) append-only.
- GL adjustment posted = (authoritative_N - prior)*qty, ONE cost_adjustment_line per depletion; delta 0 => post nothing. All gen-N writes keyed by generation, ONE tx that bumps recalc_generation last.
- Idempotent: crash-retry recomputes same N (full-replay determinism, child a) => zero net GL; no-op re-cost => all deltas 0; genuine backdated re-cost => new gen N+1, posts exactly the delta; slot cursor advances only on flush so crash replay is safe.

value_sum reconciliation: no new total_value column needed (value_sum + 0009 relax suffice); variance-into-empty-pool absorption is a close-time hook → child (e). 

Open: D5 keep/drop 0010 (pool_id,id) index; D6 no-op pass bump generation? (recommend not); D7 distinct cost_adjustment event type (recommend yes). None change the idempotency contract.
close_reason: design shipped: design-v3.2-recalc-d.md. Enums/seq (cost_adjustment) + D1 posted_at denorm+(pool_id,posted_at,id) index + D3 cost_layer_consumption linkage table + Model 1 generation-delta idempotency (pool_settlement + append-only cost_settlement; repeated pass => zero net GL, backdated re-cost => inter-generation delta). §17 slot stays the stream cursor; no home-grown watermark. value_sum reconciliation, no total_value column. title: ledger-v3.2 recalc engine (b): cross-pool scheduler + parallelization / materialization strategy
description:
Design how the per-pool layer-walk (child a) scales across the whole pool population concurrently with an appending hot path.

Per design-v3.1 §19: the per-pool fold is intrinsically serial (a depletion's cost depends on every prior event in the SAME pool) but pools are INDEPENDENT, so recalc parallelizes ACROSS pools. Wall-clock is bounded by the slowest single pool's serial fold. The #5 per-pool ceiling that §18 removed from the hot path REAPPEARS inside recalc (relieved of a latency SLA but still setting the close-drain floor). Under Pareto-hot pools a handful dominate recalc latency exactly as they dominated the hot path.

Design scope:
- Cross-pool work distribution: how pools are assigned to recalc workers (feed-driven vs claim-driven), how a hot pool's long fold does not starve others.
- Recalc chases a MOVING TAIL (concurrent with appends), not a fixed backlog — design the catch-up loop and how it interacts with the logical-decoding cursor (§17).
- Materialization strategy: what recalc writes back — pool_state layer rows (layer_id > 0), running position, GL value legs, cost-adjustment trx/trx_line. §7 sketches the schema-add surface (cost_adjustment enum values, sequences, layer-row materialization); §14.1 has the per-pool id-ordered replay access path (composite index trx_line(pool_id,id), migration 0010, gate-elevated).
- Access-path/index requirements for the walk at scale.

Depends on child (a) (the per-pool algorithm) and informs child (d) (schema). Design-only.
design:
DESIGN SHIPPED: poc/design_research/design-v3.2-recalc-b.md (referenced from design-v3.2.md §5).

Grounding: recalc IS the strict layer-walk (child a) off the hot path, so its per-pool cost = the measured strict Path A curve (POC-REPORT §A): ~460us + 0.79us*depth, O(depth*log depth), throughput 2127->25 trx/s from depth 1->50000 (85x collapse). Full-pool replay pays this over the whole stream each pass = the §19 throughput inequality made concrete.

INTRINSIC per-pool serial fold (NOT the killed m4g5 lever): a depletion's cost depends on every prior event in the SAME pool -> exactly ONE worker owns a pool's replay at a time (correctness, not a throughput lever). m4g5 killed committer->pool affinity on the HOT PATH because alt-C hot path is insert-only/commutative (no serial dep; limiter was shared LWLock). Recalc is the opposite; do NOT cite m4g5 against per-pool ownership. Parallelism is ACROSS pools only; wall-clock bounded by slowest pool (Pareto #5 ceiling reappears, sets close-drain floor).

D9 RESOLVED: claim-driven SKIP LOCKED dirty-set (SPIKE-A shape) over static hash-shard — reuses gate-blessed drain, row-lock gives per-pool exclusivity free, load-balances under Pareto. Thin recalc_queue(pool_id) populated by feed consumer, drained FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED LIMIT 1. Worker loop: claim -> replay -> materialize+adjust+bump generation in ONE tx -> advance settled_through -> release. Worker count default = committer_count 4 (D10, tunable).

MATERIALIZATION = THE CHECKPOINT (resolves D2/D4): persist pool_state.layer_id>0 layer rows (persistent VecDeque; already unconstrained by 0006/0009). The persisted layer state at settled_through IS a checkpoint.
- D2 RESOLVED: incremental-from-persisted-checkpoint is the STEADY STATE (adopted now, falls out free since layers persisted for queryability) — forward pass replays only (posted_at,id)>settled_through, O(new events) not O(depth), sidesteps the depth collapse. Full-opening replay (a's baseline) retained as correctness FALLBACK for a backdated event with no checkpoint <= floor. Refines a's "full-replay first, checkpoint later."
- D4 RESOLVED: re-cost floor replays from nearest persisted checkpoint <= floor; start with ONE live checkpoint (= current persisted state at settled_through, covers forward-only + backdated-at/after-settled_through). Historical multi-checkpoint retention deferred = D11 (storage vs recost-depth; full-opening always correct just O(depth)).

D8 SURFACED, handed to (c) with §17 interaction explicit: cursor advance-on-completion (§17-literal, slot-lag=backlog one gauge, but one deep pool pins ALL cluster WAL) vs advance-on-ingestion+durable dirty-set (WAL freed at ingestion, recalc backlog a SEPARATE gauge = two coupled gauges, refines §17's single-gauge). Recommend advance-on-ingestion (alt-C hot path runs far ahead of a deep-pool fold; pinning all WAL to the slowest pool is a real outage mode). NOT reopening §17's feed decision (slot not watermark — untouched); specifying the cursor-advance policy §17 left implicit. (c) ratifies + owns any §17 op-note update.

Validation: checkpoint-equivalence (incremental == full-opening == acct-0at4.7 oracle TRUE arm); backdated-from-checkpoint == from-opening; per-pool exclusivity property test (no co-ownership, N-worker disjoint == serial); moving-tail convergence.

Open: D8/D11 -> (c); D10 worker-count default. None change (a)'s correctness contract (all optimizations validated == full-opening replay = the oracle).

Intrinsic per-pool single-ownership (NOT the killed m4g5 hot-path lever). D9 claim-driven SKIP LOCKED dirty-set; D2 incremental-from-persisted-checkpoint steady state + full-opening fallback; D4 replay from nearest checkpoint<=floor, one live checkpoint; materialization = the checkpoint. D8 (cursor advance policy, §17 interaction) + D11 (historical checkpoint depth) handed to (c) with recommendations. All optimizations validated == full-opening replay = the acct-0at4.7 oracle.

title: Plan the v3.2 implementation spec — propagate the §18 surviving architecture; recalc engine is the hard core
description:
design-v3.1 §18 (gate verdict, 2026-07-08) fixed the surviving cost-ledger architecture but explicitly left "propagating the surviving architecture into a v3.2 implementation spec" as downstream work. §19 characterized the deferred-recalc RISK but did NOT design the recalc engine; §20 records it as "the one genuinely undesigned piece ... no open issue yet ... the natural head of a v3.2 recalc/close workstream." Verified 2026-07-10: no v3.2 spec file and no v3.2 issue exist. This issue opens that workstream — produce the PLAN for a v3.2 implementation spec that turns the decided architecture into something buildable, with the recalc/close engine as its hard core.

Deliverable = a v3.2 spec plan: a skeleton poc/design_research/design-v3.2.md consolidating the decided inputs + a decomposition of the recalc-engine design into filable sub-issues. It CONSOLIDATES decided decisions by reference; it does NOT re-litigate them.

SURVIVING ARCHITECTURE to propagate (decided — cite, do not re-open):
- Hot path: single-statement DIRECT (SPIKE-B: one commutative `UPDATE ... WHERE qty - delta >= 0` with `RETURNING old.unit_cost`) for aggregate paths + staging-table OUTBOX drained by `SELECT ... FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED` committers (SPIKE-A) where batching/coalescing is wanted — replaces the §6 shmem router/committer wholesale.
- Posture: everything-provisional (alt C, §16) — no cost leg on the hot path; append the physical event + optional commutative qty aggregate; qty a flagged running signal.
- Feed: logical-decoding slot (§17) — commit-ordered, confirmed_flush_lsn-cursored.
- Wire contract (§3.7 v3.2 change): callers send inventory facts only (pool_id, line_type, qty, unit_cost); the ledger resolves debit/credit/variance accounts from posting_account_map.
- ledger-core retained for genuinely stateful methods (specific-id; future strict layer math).
- ledger-routed-c is superseded; its PHYSICAL DELETION is a SEPARATE follow-up, NOT this issue.

THE HARD CORE to design (the one undesigned piece, §19/§20): the recalc/close engine — layer-walk algorithm, cross-pool scheduler, parallelization + materialization strategy, chronological re-sort (R-1), cadence-vs-load knob, and the quiet-backlog / throughput-inequality mitigation. Size against the acct-0at4.7 replay-oracle variance (biased-under-trend => recalc is load-bearing; bench/replay-oracle-results.md).
design:
RESUME PLAN — take this issue on session resume; do the PLANNING (produce the spec plan), not the full spec.

WHERE: new poc/design_research/design-v3.2.md (mirror design-v3.1.md structure + voice). Decided inputs already live in design-v3.1 §16 (posture) / §17 (feed) / §18 (gate) / §19 (recalc risk) / §20 (alternatives) / §3.7 (wire contract) — the v3.2 spec REFERENCES these, consolidates, and adds the recalc-engine design.

PROPOSED v3.2 SPEC SECTION OUTLINE (the plan to produce as the design-v3.2.md skeleton):
1. Purpose + relationship to v3.1 (what carries over, what is superseded).
2. Schema deltas from v3.1 (alt-C: drop hot-path cost leg; qty = flagged running signal; posting_account_map; recalc state/bookkeeping tables; logical-decoding slot config).
3. Hot-path semantics (direct single-statement + staging-table outbox; per-pool FIFO by construction; failure / backpressure).
4. SPI surface v3.2 (inventory-facts-only wire contract; ledger-side account resolution).
5. Recalc/close engine — THE HARD CORE (own decomposition below).
6. Feed (logical-decoding slot consumer).
7. Testing strategy (reuse survivor oracles — acct-0at4.4 sequential reference / .5 conservation sweep / .7 strict-FIFO replay — all architecture-agnostic; add recalc-correctness vs strict-replay; cadence-vs-load soak).
8. Out of scope / deferred (E app-tier partitioned consumer = kept scale-out path, not instantiated, §20.1; F TB split rejected, §20.2; negative inventory / multi-currency / period-close per §13).
9. Open questions.

RECALC-ENGINE DECOMPOSITION (§5, to become child issues on resume):
(a) layer-walk algorithm + chronological re-sort (R-1) — correctness vs the strict-FIFO replay oracle;
(b) cross-pool scheduler + parallelization / materialization strategy;
(c) cadence-vs-load control + quiet-backlog / throughput-inequality mitigation (the §19 risk);
(d) recalc state/bookkeeping schema + idempotent re-run;
(e) close-time semantics (finalize provisional -> authoritative valuation).

DO NOT: re-litigate §16/17/18 (settled at the gate); design ledger-routed-c changes (superseded; deletion is a separate follow-up); pull in negative inventory / multi-currency / period-close (out of scope, §13). All decided inputs are CLOSED issues: acct-0at4.11.1 (SPIKE-A) / .11.2 (SPIKE-B) / .11.3 (§16 posture) / .11.4 (§17 feed) / acct-0at4.12 (§19 recalc risk) / acct-0at4.13 (§20 alternatives).

STATE AT FILING (2026-07-10): gate verdict settled; all acct-0at4 survivor children CLOSED; no v3.2 file/issue existed before this. HEAD at filing on branch worktree-poc-31 (local-only). This is the head of the v3.2 recalc/close workstream (design-v3.1 §20).
acceptance_criteria: A poc/design_research/design-v3.2.md skeleton exists with the section outline above; decided inputs (§16/17/18/19/20/§3.7) consolidated by reference (not re-litigated); the recalc/close engine design problem decomposed into filable sub-issues (a-e); ledger-routed-c physical deletion noted as a separate follow-up; open questions listed — enough that spec-writing + child design tasks can proceed.
notes:
PLANNING DELIVERABLE SHIPPED (commit 4f09271, 2026-07-10): poc/design_research/design-v3.2.md skeleton (9-section outline; decided inputs §16/17/18/19/20/§3.7 consolidated by reference; recalc engine = §5 the hard core) + recalc-engine decomposed into children acct-q1oj.1-.5 (a layer-walk+R-1 / b cross-pool scheduler / c cadence-vs-load / d state schema / e close-time; deps: a foundational, b/c/d->a, c->b, e->a+d). ledger-routed-c physical deletion filed separately as acct-uena. design-v3.1 §19 stale "no open issue yet" pointer updated to reference this workstream.

NOW THE v3.2 RECALC/CLOSE WORKSTREAM HEAD (design-v3.1 §20). Left OPEN: the plan shipped but the engine is undesigned — closes when children .1-.5 land. Ready child: acct-q1oj.1 (foundational, unblocked). Next step is per-child DESIGN work under the spec §5, one at a time, on explicit pick.
close_reason: v3.2 recalc/close engine fully designed. Planning deliverable (design-v3.2.md skeleton + decided inputs consolidated by reference) shipped 4f09271; recalc engine decomposed and all five children DESIGNED + closed: (a) q1oj.1 layer-walk+R-1/R-2 (design-v3.2-recalc-a.md), (b) q1oj.2 cross-pool scheduler+checkpoint/materialization (recalc-b), (c) q1oj.3 cadence/backlog+two-gauge (recalc-c), (d) q1oj.4 state schema+generation-delta idempotency (recalc-d), (e) q1oj.5 close-time finalize (recalc-e). Whole engine correctness reduces to (a) full-opening replay = the acct-0at4.7 oracle. D8 accepted (advance-on-ingestion). IMPLEMENTATION (migrations + Rust) is future follow-on, not this planning/design epic. ledger-routed-c physical deletion tracked separately at acct-uena.

title: ledger-v3.1 A: pgbouncer pool-size sweep of S5/S7/S8 (confound FEEDBACK #12)
description: The 1000-caller scenarios route through the pgbouncer transaction pooler, so direct-flavor contention is shaped by an unstated pool size, not 1000-way lock queuing. The confound is asymmetric (barely touches routed fast enqueue) and flatters routed. Sweep DEFAULT_POOL_SIZE {25,50,100,200}, run S5/S7/S8 x {direct,routed}, show the crossover is stable or report crossover as a function of pool size. Put the pool size next to every S5/S7/S8 number in POC-REPORT sections (b)/(c). New bench/pgbouncer-poolsize-sweep.sh; setup-pgbouncer.sh DEFAULT_POOL_SIZE env recreates the pgbouncer container only (safe, not acct-postgres). HAZARD: DROP/CREATE poc_v3_1 between cells wedges the routed committer, so docker restart acct-postgres after. Full recon with file:line anchors in acct-0at4.10 design field.
close_reason: Pool-size confound sweep shipped (bench/pgbouncer-poolsize-sweep.sh + POC-REPORT §(b) confound-check subsection). Re-measured S5/S7/S8 direct-per-call vs routed across default_pool_size {25,50,100,200}; crossover STABLE (routed wins at every pool, routed/direct in [6.4,22.9]/[3.7,8.1]/[3.6,4.4] for s5/s7/s8). Finding: direct-per-call flat across pool size (pool-row-lock-bound, not backend-bound) so pgbouncer pool size is NOT a material confound; larger pool compresses routed lead via enqueue-path contention but never flips it. Pool size now sits next to every §(b) number. Commit a0fb669.

title: ledger-v3.1 testing: advisory-lock + SetLatch-on-enqueue ablations (new-code axes split from acct-0at4.9)
description:
Split out of acct-0at4.9 (measurement-only baselines/ablations shipped there). These two ablation axes require NEW pgrx extension code + .so rebuild/reinstall into the shared acct-postgres container, so they are a distinct kind of work from the existing-knob measurement sweeps.

Two axes:

E. advisory-lock vs pool_lock row.
   Hot path currently locks pools via ledger_spi_common::pool_lock::acquire_pool_locks (ledger-direct-c/src/submit.rs:~101) = shared FOR UPDATE on pool_lock heap rows. Advisory variant = pg_advisory_xact_lock(pool_id) which touches no heap row (no xmax churn, no WAL for the lock). Add a variant fn or a GUC branch. Directly feeds the FEEDBACK #7 / ARCH roll-up disposition with data (WAL/xmax churn on the hot lock page).

F. SetLatch-on-enqueue vs 50 ms tick.
   Router BGWorker waits on BackgroundWorker::wait_latch(50ms) (ledger-routed-c/src/router.rs:~89,:118); the 50ms latch + 500us dwell => ~25ms mean materialization floor (FEEDBACK #13). SetLatch-on-enqueue = store the BGWorker latch in shmem at startup and SetLatch it from ledger_enqueue_trx_c (ledger-routed-c/src/lib.rs) for immediate wake. Measure the materialization-latency floor against the plain 50ms tick using acct-0at4.8 open-loop + throughput-at-SLO methodology. Inherited from the acct-0at4.8 re-scope.

Reuse acct-0at4.8 infra: scripts/saturation-sweep.sh, open-loop --target-rate/--arrival, p999/HDR, slo_p99_us, ledger-harness verify.

Hazards: rebuild/reinstall ledger_direct_c (E) and ledger_routed_c (F) .so via install scripts; do NOT recreate the container (wipes all stream .so). Bench on a quiet host if possible (noisy-workstation memory); report structural ratios / same-minute A/B. Full statistical rigor is acct-0at4.10.

Acceptance: advisory-vs-row-lock delta measured and reported (feeds ARCH #7); SetLatch-vs-tick materialization-latency floor measured and reported.
design:
RECON 2026-07-09 (pre-resume, read-only). Two axes; E has a SCOPE CONFLICT to resolve FIRST via AskUserQuestion before writing code.

== SCOPE CONFLICT on E (advisory-lock vs pool_lock row) ==
The advisory-vs-row ablation only applies to ledger_submit_trx_c (the RMW pool_lock path, ledger-direct-c/src/submit.rs:101) — the DISPLACED baseline. The CHOSEN direct hot path is SPIKE-B ledger_submit_trx_single_c (submit_single.rs), which has NO pool_lock row at all (folds the mutation into one INSERT...ON CONFLICT DO UPDATE CTE on the pool_state aggregate row). bench/spike-b-results.md:107-109 AND design-v3.1 §18 declare FEEDBACK #7 advisory-vs-row SUBSUMED ("Drop advisory-vs-row (subsumed, SPIKE-B)"). So E measures a displaced baseline, not the chosen architecture. RESOLVE on resume: (a) do E on submit_trx_c anyway as retrospective FEEDBACK #7 / ARCH #7 documentation (put a WAL/xmax number on it, moot for the chosen path); (b) DROP E as subsumed, keep only F, record the subsumption disposition in POC-REPORT; (c) lighter descriptive E: measure WAL bytes / xmax churn of the existing row-lock path without building an advisory variant. Recommend surfacing (a) vs (b) with a lean toward (b)+note unless the user wants the retrospective number.

== E IMPLEMENTATION (only if kept) ==
- acquire_pool_locks: ledger-spi-common/src/pool_lock.rs:28-64 (sorts asc dedup for deadlock-avoidance; 1 SPI/pool: SELECT 1 FROM pool_lock WHERE pool_id=$1 FOR UPDATE; lazy INSERT ON CONFLICT first-touch; lock held to caller tx end).
- Add acquire_pool_locks_advisory(pool_ids) in the SAME shared module: SELECT pg_advisory_xact_lock($1) per pool (i64 direct fit, void return, no lazy-create, auto-release at tx end — strictly shorter than row branch).
- GUC lives LOCAL to ledger-direct-c (shared crate can't own a GUC; name-collision risk). No GUC exists in ledger-direct-c yet (lib.rs:45 empty _PG_init). Mirror ledger-routed-c/src/lib.rs GucSetting pattern (define_bool_guc). Use GucContext::Userset (regular SPI fn, not a BGWorker -> reads live, flippable per-session with SET, NO restart needed for A/B). Branch at submit.rs:101.
- Sibling call sites (out of scope for direct-single, extend only for apples-to-apples): drain.rs:184 (staging), committer.rs:676 (routed).
- BOOT-SAFE: ledger_direct_c is NOT in shared_preload. scripts/install-direct-c.sh: cargo build --release -p ledger-direct-c --features pg18 --no-default-features; .so at target/release/libledger_direct_c.so; DROP/CREATE EXTENSION in place, NO restart. Bad build only fails CREATE, never blocks boot.
- TESTS: ledger-direct-c/tests/acceptance_direct_lock_and_concurrency.rs (PRIMARY — 50 concurrent depletions to one hot FIFO pool must still serialize with no lost updates). property_ledger_submit_trx_c.rs invariant I6 = "pool_lock row exists for touched pool" WILL FAIL under advisory (no row created) -> make mode-aware / skip when advisory.

== F IMPLEMENTATION (SetLatch-on-enqueue vs 50ms tick) ==
- Router steady loop: ledger-routed-c/src/router.rs:118 while BackgroundWorker::wait_latch(Some(50ms)); drains via while router_tick()>0 at :143. Startup-only spin wait_latch at :89 (ignore).
- Dwell/coalesce gate: router.rs:174-192 — defers if oldest candidate age < batch_window_us_now() (~500us FEEDBACK #13). For PURE wake-floor measurement set batch_window_us=0 (else floor = max(wake_latency, batch_window)); ALSO measure at default window for the realistic floor.
- Enqueue entrypoint: enqueue.rs:52 ledger_enqueue_trx_c; slot published by valid CAS 0->1 Release at enqueue.rs:546-549; loop breaks with seq at :164. Add SetLatch AFTER success (~:191-194) so publish happens-before wake. Batch entrypoint ledger_enqueue_trx_batch_c:221 (push loop :370-412) wants the same wake.
- NO NEW SHMEM FIELD NEEDED: CommitterQueue.router_pid: AtomicI32 at shmem.rs:210 already holds the router MyProcPid (stored router.rs:105-108, Release). Wake helper (net-new, few lines): read router_pid -> pg_sys::BackendPidGetProc(pid) -> if !proc.is_null() SetLatch(&mut (*proc).procLatch). Self-healing: stale/crashed router PID resolves NULL -> wake skipped. Idiom reference in-repo: poc/queue-extension/src/committer.rs:1026-1029, queue.rs:1824-1826.
- pgrx 0.18.1: router's own latch is pg_sys::MyLatch; no accessor hands another backend the router latch -> PID->PGPROC->procLatch path. SetLatch/BackendPidGetProc/procLatch are raw pg_sys FFI, available. No existing SetLatch usage in ledger-routed-c to extend.
- CAUTION: the DrainConfig.notify_channel / single-listener / drain-tx pg_notify (shape-L) plumbing is NOT in ledger-routed-c — it lives in the unrelated outbox subsystem (tests/outbox_drain.rs, db/migrations/0070). Do not expect to reuse it here.
- BOOT-BLOCKING: ledger_routed_c IS in shared_preload_libraries. scripts/install-routed-c.sh: cargo build --release -p ledger-routed-c --features pg18 --no-default-features; .so target/release/libledger_routed_c.so; docker cp + ALTER SYSTEM preload-append + unconditional docker restart. SAFE SEQUENCE: build must exit 0 BEFORE docker cp (script set -e guards); keep a known-good libledger_routed_c.so; recovery if bad .so lands = cp last-good back + restart, or edit postgresql.auto.conf in the data volume to drop ledger_routed_c from shared_preload while postmaster down. DO NOT recreate the container (wipes all stream .so).
- Gate the SetLatch call behind a GucContext::Postmaster/Sighup bool (e.g. ledger_routed_c.wake_on_enqueue) OR build two .so, for the A/B. Note from .9: routed Sighup GUCs are NOT adopted live by the BGWorker — but the ENQUEUE backend is a regular backend and CAN read a Userset/Sighup GUC live; the SetLatch call is on the enqueue side, so a Userset gate is readable live. Simplest robust A/B: one build, ledger_routed_c.wake_on_enqueue bool (Userset), flip + measure (no restart needed since the reader is the enqueue backend, not the router).
- TESTS: scripts/run-tests.sh --path routed (builds test_hooks .so). acceptance_routed_enqueue.rs (MOST affected), property_ledger_enqueue_trx_c.rs, acceptance_routed_affinity_grouping.rs (timing-sensitive: header assumes ~50ms latch). With test_bgworker_paused, an enqueue SetLatch wakes the router which re-parks at the pause continue (router.rs:131-133) — harmless.

== MEASUREMENT (F) ==
Reuse acct-0at4.8 open-loop: --target-rate/--arrival, p999, slo_p99_us, scripts/saturation-sweep.sh. The .8 work already surfaced routed's ~118ms tick-driven materialization floor; F's number is what should beat it. A/B stock 50ms-tick vs wake-on-enqueue at batch_window_us=0 (pure wake floor) and at default window (realistic). Committed/materialization latency is the metric (not just ack).

== DELIVERY ==
Resolve E scope (AskUserQuestion) -> implement kept axes -> measure -> record deltas in results/POC-REPORT.md (advisory-vs-row feeds ARCH #7; SetLatch materialization floor) -> commit (acct-0at4.15: <title> + HEREDOC + Co-Authored-By trailer, local-only) -> bd close (single-quote reason) -> STOP and report (one-issue-at-a-time STRICT; do NOT auto-claim acct-0at4.10). Bench hygiene: orphan-shell sweep + Chrome/load check + docker restart before measuring; noisy-host posture = structural ratios / same-minute A/B; full statistical rigor is acct-0at4.10.
notes: RESOLVED per user decision (2026-07-10): E (advisory-vs-row) DROPPED as subsumed — SPIKE-B direct-single holds no pool_lock row, and design-v3.1 §18 (acct-0at4.3/.9 rows) declares FEEDBACK #7 subsumed; disposition recorded in results/POC-REPORT.md, ARCH #7 moot, no code. F (SetLatch-on-enqueue) IMPLEMENTED + measured: new ledger_routed_c.wake_on_enqueue bool (default off), enqueue SetLatches the router via BackendPidGetProc(router_pid); committed-latency p50 ~62-64ms (tick floor) → ~26-34ms (~2x) across batch_window_us {0,500}; residual ~26-34ms is the router→committer tick (F wakes only the router) → follow-up acct-0at4.16. NOTE: design §18 also lists SetLatch-vs-tick among routed-lever ablations to drop (alongside router_pack_disjoint); measured anyway as CHARACTERIZATION of the retained routed alternative — same basis as acct-0at4.9 §C/§D. All 9 routed test binaries green incl. new acceptance_routed_wake_on_enqueue.rs.

title: ledger-v3.1 ARCH-RECALC-RISK: characterize the deferred-recalc throughput/backlog risk (the hard half) + size the adjustment storm
description:
Source: FEEDBACK-ARCH.md problem #1 (risk inversion). Downstream of the gate — characterizes the deferred half the PoC never touched.

## Thesis
Path C's bet is "hot path cheap now, reconciliation later." But recalc must process **the same event volume** as the hot path while doing strictly *more* work per line (layer math, adjustment posting, materialization), **sequentially per pool**, while contending with a hot path that keeps appending. If the hot path needed batching heroics to keep up, the reconciler — which cannot skip anything — is **harder, not easier**. Its only structural advantages are latency-insensitivity and per-pool parallelism.

The failure mode is **quiet**: backlog grows → provisional drift compounds → period close blocks → the close posts an adjustment storm into the GL. The PoC validated the part that was never in doubt (cheap hot path) and deferred the part that sinks real ERPs. SAP/Oracle/D365 cited as precedent cuts both ways — CKMLCP and Inventory Close are famously the **worst-behaved** components of those systems (multi-hour closes, locking entire plants).

## Deliverable
An honest risk section in design-v3.1 that:
1. States the recalc throughput inequality (recalc work/line > hot-path work/line, same volume, sequential/pool, concurrent with appends) and the quiet-backlog failure chain.
2. **Sizes the adjustment storm** using the provisional-vs-true variance distribution from acct-0at4.7 (offline replay oracle) — that variance IS the magnitude of the close-time correction.
3. Frames the mitigation space (per-pool parallel recalc; continuous vs at-close reconciliation; backpressure when backlog exceeds a bound) WITHOUT designing recalc — design waits on the posture (acct-0at4.13) and feed (acct-0at4.15) decisions.

## Dependencies
- Depends on the gate (posture .13 decides sidecar-vs-sole-engine; feed .15 decides the input substrate).
- Consumes acct-0at4.7 variance output to size the storm.

## Acceptance
Risk section in design-v3.1 quantifying (a) the recalc throughput inequality, (b) the adjustment-storm magnitude from .7's variance distribution, (c) the quiet-backlog failure chain and its detection signal (backlog depth / drift bound); mitigation space framed but recalc left undesigned pending .13/.15.
acceptance_criteria: Risk section in design-v3.1: recalc throughput inequality, adjustment-storm magnitude from acct-0at4.7 variance, quiet-backlog failure chain + detection signal; mitigation framed, recalc undesigned pending .13/.15.
notes: Recalc framing re-derived under ARCH-POSTURE (acct-0at4.11.3, design-v3.1 §16, DECIDED 2026-07-08): posture is everything-provisional (alt C), so recalc is the SOLE costing engine on a single plane, NOT a corrective sidecar. (a) DROP the dual-bookkeeping / close-time adjustment-storm framing — the hot path posts no provisional cost amounts to correct, so there is no provisional-vs-authoritative second plane. (b) RETAIN and CENTRALIZE the throughput-inequality / quiet-backlog risk (FEEDBACK-ARCH #1): recalc does strictly more work per line than the hot path, same event volume, sequential per pool, concurrent with appends — and it is now the only path that assigns cost and posts GL, so backlog gates when ANY authoritative cost/GL exists, not merely when a correction lands. (c) ADD the cadence-vs-load tradeoff: FIFO granularity is a configurable recalc-period knob (short periods emulate real-time), and shorter periods run recalc more often over the same volume, trading provisional-drift latency against recalc throughput load. Still depends on the recalc-feed decision (acct-0at4.11.4 / alt D).
close_reason: design-v3.1 §19 deferred-recalc risk section shipped (commit). Re-framed under §16 alt C: dropped adjustment-storm/dual-bookkeeping, centralized the throughput-inequality/quiet-backlog risk, sized drift from acct-0at4.7 variance (biased-under-trend = recalc load-bearing), added cadence-vs-load tradeoff. Stale .13/.15 dependency corrected — posture (§16) + feed (§17) decided; only the recalc engine remains undesigned.

title: ledger-v3.1 ARCH-RECALC-FEED: lock recalc feed to logical decoding (commit-order + confirmed_flush_lsn), not trx_line watermark scan (D)
description:
Source: FEEDBACK-ARCH.md alternative D. **A decision to lock BEFORE any recalc design starts** (so it never has to be re-litigated inside recalc).

## Thesis
Whatever recalc/close gets built, do NOT feed it by scanning `trx_line` with watermarks — §14.6 already documents why allocation-order watermarks are broken (backdated receipts, chunk reordering, no safe high-water mark from a settled-state column). A **logical replication slot** delivers `trx_line` inserts in **commit order** with a durable cursor (`confirmed_flush_lsn`) for free. That solves the safe-watermark problem in the substrate instead of hand-rolling it in settled-state columns.

## Decision
Commit to logical decoding as the recalc feed, or record why not, as a fixed input to recalc design. Concretely: a logical slot + output plugin (or `pgoutput` + a consumer) yields ordered, durable, replayable `trx_line` delivery with a resumable cursor; recalc consumes that rather than `SELECT ... WHERE id > watermark`.

## Dependencies / interactions
- This is the substrate that the recalc-risk characterization (acct-0at4.14) assumes; it must be settled before .14's design section is written.
- Interacts with the posture decision (acct-0at4.13): if the posture goes all-provisional (alt C), recalc becomes the *sole* costing engine and the feed matters even more; if hybrid, only strict pools need the ordered feed.
- Independent of the hot-path spikes (A/B) — the feed is a recalc-side concern.

## Acceptance
A recorded decision in design-v3.1: recalc feed = logical-decoding slot (commit-ordered, `confirmed_flush_lsn` cursor) vs the rejected `trx_line` watermark scan, with the §14.6 breakage cited as the driver. No recalc design proceeds until this is fixed.
acceptance_criteria: Recorded decision in design-v3.1: recalc feed = logical-decoding slot vs rejected trx_line watermark scan, §14.6 breakage cited. No recalc design proceeds until fixed.
notes: DECIDED 2026-07-08 (technical decision; not human-flagged; delegated via "proceed to .11.4"). Recalc feed = logical-decoding replication slot (trx_line in COMMIT order, durable confirmed_flush_lsn cursor). REJECTED: SELECT ... WHERE id > watermark (broken per §14.6 — id-alloc order != commit order, silent gap). DOMINATED (hand-rolled, reimplement in app what the slot gives free): snapshot-based safe-watermark + settled-state column. Key honest caveat recorded: logical decoding fixes DELIVERY ordering + durability, NOT costing chronology — commit-order != posted_at-order for backdated receipts (§14.5 within-pool re-sort stays recalc job). Operational: slot lag pins WAL; under alt-C posture the slot-lag alarm == recalc-backlog alarm (acct-0at4.12), one gauge (confirmed_flush_lsn lag); needs wal_level=logical. Deferred sub-choice (NOT locked, recalc-design-time): pgoutput+consumer vs custom output plugin — lean pgoutput first. Recorded in design-v3.1 §17 (new decision section) + forward-pointer notes at §7, §14.5, §14.6. Doc decision only, no build. Left in_progress feeding acct-0at4.11.5 (gate verdict synthesis + downstream re-triage), matching SPIKE-A/B and ARCH-POSTURE handling.

title: ledger-v3.1 testing: confound control + soak runs + statistics discipline
description:
Source: FEEDBACK-TESTING.md #10, #11, #12; FEEDBACK.md #12.

Kill the confounds, then run long enough to see temporal failures.

- **pgbouncer pool size (FEEDBACK #12):** S5/S7/S8 run 1000 "callers" through a transaction pooler because the container can't hold 1000 backends — so direct flavor's contention is shaped by an unstated pool size, not 1000-way lock queuing, and the confound is **asymmetric** (it barely touches routed's fast enqueue) → it flatters routed. Sweep pool size {25 / 50 / 100 / 200} and show the crossover is stable, or report crossover as a function of pool size. Put the pool size next to every S5/S7/S8 number.

- **Environment:** pin CPUs; isolate WAL onto its own device (or report the device's fsync latency); fix and *report* `shared_buffers` / `checkpoint_timeout`; disable autovacuum only for short runs.

- **Soak (#11):** 30 s runs never cross a checkpoint, accumulate clog, trigger autovacuum, or reveal arena fragmentation (an arena leak was already found once — by code reading, not by test). Run 1–4 h at ~70% of measured saturation; plot throughput / p99 over time vs `pg_stat_bgwriter`, `pool_lock` / `pool_state` bloat, WAL volume, and — given ARCH-2 — `age(datfrozenxid)` slope. A flat 30 s number with a sawtooth 2 h profile is a different architecture verdict.

- **Statistics (#12):** ≥5 runs/cell with fresh seeds; randomized cell execution order (thermal/cache drift); report median + bootstrap CI; compare cells with Mann-Whitney rather than eyeballing. Declare the steady-state window mechanically (discard until a rolling-CoV threshold), not by trimming N seconds by feel. Every crossover claim gets an uncertainty band — that X is the deliverable the production decision consumes.

## Acceptance
pgbouncer pool-size sweep reported for S5/S7/S8; env knobs pinned + reported; ≥1 multi-hour soak with the time-series plots; results re-reported with medians + CIs and a stated steady-state-window rule.
design:
RECON 2026-07-10 (pre-resume, read-only, two scout agents). acct-0at4.10 is the
HEAVIEST testing child: 4 distinct sub-deliverables, most of the stats/soak/
time-series machinery is GREENFIELD. Resolve scope FIRST via AskUserQuestion.

== SCOPE / SEQUENCING (resolve FIRST via AskUserQuestion) ==
4 sub-deliverables of very different weight. Mirror the .9 "split: some now,
follow-up" precedent. Options to surface:
(a) SPLIT into 4 sub-issues (pool-size sweep / env-capture / soak / statistics),
    do one at a time — RECOMMENDED (one-issue-at-a-time; each is independently
    shippable).
(b) Do the LIGHT high-value subset now (A pool-size sweep + B env-capture — both
    reuse existing infra, no multi-hour wait, no big new code), defer C soak +
    D statistics-refactor to follow-ups.
(c) Full pass in one issue (large; the multi-hour soak is the long pole).
KEY CONSTRAINT to surface regardless: the soak (1-4h) runs on this NOISY daily-
driver workstation (Chrome swings throughput 2x, memory project_pocv3_bench_host
_is_noisy_workstation). A multi-hour throughput/p99 profile would be dominated by
host load, not architecture. Ask: run soak on a quiet/overnight host, or reframe
it as DRIFT-detection (xid slope / arena bloat / WAL accumulation / checkpoint
sawtooth survive host noise; absolute throughput does not)?

== A. pgbouncer pool-size sweep (S5/S7/S8) — LIGHT, existing infra ==
- setup-pgbouncer.sh: DEFAULT_POOL_SIZE env (default 24), POOL_MODE=transaction,
  MAX_CLIENT_CONN=2000, separate container poc-v3-1-pgbouncer (edoburu/pgbouncer)
  on docker net acct_default, host port 6432 -> acct-postgres:5432. Re-run
  DEFAULT_POOL_SIZE=<n> bash bench/setup-pgbouncer.sh per value {25,50,100,200}
  (it recreates the PGBOUNCER container only — NOT acct-postgres, safe).
- common.sh:44 dsn_for_scenario() UNCONDITIONALLY returns POOLER_DSN — ALL
  scenarios route through pgbouncer now (acct-uix8), not just S5/S7/S8. DIRECT_DSN
  (5111) is admin/DDL/seed/1-caller-canary only.
- scenarios.rs: S5 (:143 1000 callers, Zipf exp=100 => single hot pool, Simple,
  deplete=100, depth 10 — pathological for direct); S7 (:161 1000, Zipf 1.2,
  Simple, deplete=100, depth 1000 DEEP — Path C home); S8 (:168 1000, Zipf 1.2,
  Complex, deplete=50, depth 1000). Caller count is ONLY thing scenarios set;
  pooler-routing is 100% shell-side. Driver caller-pool sizing driver_routed.rs
  :99 (callers+16), driver_direct.rs:86 (callers+8) => 1000 callers can't be
  direct backends (io_uring memlock ceiling, acct-8cn2) => must fan into 24.
- DELIVERABLE: new bench/pgbouncer-poolsize-sweep.sh: for pool in {25,50,100,200}
  { setup-pgbouncer DEFAULT_POOL_SIZE=$pool; run S5/S7/S8 x {direct,routed};
  tabulate crossover }. Show crossover STABLE across pool size OR report
  crossover(pool_size). Put pool size next to every S5/S7/S8 number in POC-REPORT
  §(b)/§(c). HAZARD: DROP/CREATE poc_v3_1 between cells wedges the routed
  committer -> docker restart acct-postgres after (memory
  project_routed_drop_database_wedges_committer).

== B. Environment capture + pinning — LIGHT/MEDIUM ==
- Config at acct REPO ROOT db/postgresql.conf (OUTSIDE worktree; shared container
  mount): shared_buffers=8GB, effective_cache_size=24GB, max_connections=200,
  checkpoint_timeout=15min, checkpoint_completion_target=0.9, max_wal_size=8GB,
  wal_compression=lz4, commit_delay=20/commit_siblings=5, io_method=io_uring,
  effective_io_concurrency=256, autovacuum=on (naptime 30s), synchronous_commit
  unset => on. NO env-capture into results exists anywhere (agents confirmed).
- DELIVERABLE: bench/capture-env.sh writing results/env-<ts>.json = pg_settings
  subset (the knobs above) + host (nproc, /proc/loadavg, docker inspect cpus) +
  fsync latency. fsync: check `pg_test_fsync` present in container; if not,
  REPORT checkpoint/commit_delay + the shipped commit-span-ns fsync PROXY
  (report.rs:98 txn-pipeline). Prefer shell helper (no Rust rebuild) over
  embedding in report.rs.
- CPU pinning: NONE exists (no taskset/cpuset/numactl; compose has no cpus/cpuset).
  Pinning the container needs a docker-compose cpuset edit at acct ROOT (shared,
  outside worktree) — do NOT silently change shared infra; surface. Default:
  REPORT env, note daily-driver caveat, only pin if user asks.
- autovacuum "off for short runs": ALTER SYSTEM SET autovacuum=off + restart for
  short cells, re-enable after (shared container — report it).

== C. Multi-hour soak + time-series — HEAVY, net-new ==
- Existing (all INADEQUATE): run-sustained-5min.sh (5min DUR=300, samples ONE
  counter committer_trx_committed_total at 1Hz via a bash loop -> quartile
  summary, NO plot); run-routed-longdur.sh (1m vs 10m single-value compare, no
  series); analyze-routed-longdur.py (threshold classifier, no stats/plot). NONE
  sample bgwriter/WAL-over-time/xid-age/pool-bloat; NONE plot.
- sampler.rs is an AGGREGATOR (10Hz, sums pg_locks + wait_event into HashMaps,
  emits ONE SamplerReport at shutdown) — NOT a time-series emitter.
- NET-NEW: a periodic (1-5s) DB sampler emitting timestamped CSV rows:
  {ts, throughput_delta (committer_trx_committed_total delta), committed_p99 (from
  harness or a probe), pg_stat_bgwriter cols, pg_current_wal_insert_lsn delta,
  age(datfrozenxid) of poc_v3_1, pool_state & pool_lock row counts, arena
  outstanding}. Simplest: extend run-sustained-5min.sh sample_loop to psql these
  each tick into a CSV; parametrize DUR to hours; run at ~70% of measured
  saturation. Then plot (matplotlib -> svg) throughput/p99/bgwriter/WAL/xid-slope/
  bloat over time.
- ARCH-2 angle (issue + acct-0at4.2 which this BLOCKS): enqueue forces xid
  allocation (GetCurrentFullTransactionId), so routed throughput burns xids fast;
  soak must show age(datfrozenxid) SLOPE + whether anti-wraparound autovacuum
  triggers. Query: SELECT age(datfrozenxid) FROM pg_database WHERE datname=
  'poc_v3_1'.
- Plotting: matplotlib may be absent — CHECK; fallback = commit CSV + a computed
  drift-slope table (linear fit per metric), no plot. results/.gitignore ignores
  *.json/*.log/*.samples but TRACKS .md/.csv/.svg (deliverables).
- HAZARD (surface, see SCOPE): multi-hour on noisy host = load-dominated absolute
  numbers; frame as drift-detection.

== D. Statistics discipline — HEAVY, net-new Rust + python ==
- NET-NEW Rust: a --seed <u64> CLI flag (cli.rs has only --seed-count/-skus/
  -locations/-depth = DB seeding, NOT RNG). Driver RNG is HARD-CODED
  StdRng::seed_from_u64(0xDEAD_BEEF + caller_id) at driver_routed.rs:353 /
  driver_direct.rs:229 / driver_staging.rs:322 — every rep replays the SAME
  stream. Add --seed, thread to drivers, use (seed + caller_id). Boot-safe
  (harness rebuild only, no .so; ledger-harness is a plain binary).
- NET-NEW python: hand-rolled stats (NO numpy/scipy in-tree; project avoids heavy
  deps — match the existing hand-rolled q() quantile in profile-aggregate.py:34 /
  batch-aggregate.py:32). Need: bootstrap CI (resample-with-replacement median,
  use fixed PRNG seed for reproducibility), Mann-Whitney U (rank-sum, hand-
  implementable), rolling-CoV steady-state-window detection (discard until
  rolling std/mean < threshold — replaces the crude fixed 3-sample trim in
  run-sustained-5min.sh:187).
- Orchestration: randomized cell order (shuf the cell list; none exists — only
  ABAB interleave in run-affinity-sweep.sh:127), >=5 reps/cell each a DIFFERENT
  --seed. Reuse REPS + common.sh:78 wait_for_quiet_host load-gate pattern
  (existing sweeps already REPS=5).
- Re-report the crossover claims (POC-REPORT §(b) crossover map + S5/S7/S8) with
  median + bootstrap CI + MWU p-value + a STATED steady-state-window rule. That X
  +/- band is the deliverable the production decision consumes.
- Reusable substrate: per-run scalar JSON schema report.rs:144-175 (throughput,
  ack/committed LatencyPercentiles incl p999, routed sub-object counters) — good
  for cross-run aggregation; the compact stdout JSON line adds trx_materialized/
  ack_p99 (analyze-routed-longdur.py depends on those).

== HAZARDS / MEMORY ==
- Noisy host (Chrome 2x); frame soak as drift-detection; report structural ratios.
- DROP/CREATE poc_v3_1 wedges routed committer -> docker restart acct-postgres
  after (memory project_routed_drop_database_wedges_committer). Harness --output
  is pretty JSON (grep with whitespace).
- Do NOT recreate acct-postgres (wipes all stream .so). setup-pgbouncer recreates
  only the pgbouncer container (safe).
- Env config db/postgresql.conf + docker-compose are at acct ROOT (shared, OUTSIDE
  worktree). autovacuum/cpuset/shared_buffers changes affect ALL streams —
  report/coordinate, don't silently change shared infra.
- pgbouncer must be UP for pooler runs; run-routed-longdur auto-provisions, others
  assume up (bench/setup-pgbouncer.sh).
- --seed harness change is boot-safe (no preloaded .so). Full stats rerun of the
  crossover cells is many runs x >=5 reps — size it to host time.

== DELIVERY ==
Bench hygiene (orphan sweep + loadavg/Chrome + docker restart acct-postgres) ->
bd update acct-0at4.10 --claim -> re-read this design field -> resolve SCOPE via
AskUserQuestion (split vs light-subset-now vs full; + soak-on-noisy-host framing)
-> implement kept sub-deliverables (A/B light + existing infra; C/D net-new,
harness rebuild boot-safe) -> measure -> re-report in results/POC-REPORT.md with
CIs + steady-state rule + pool-size next to every S5/S7/S8 number -> commit
(acct-0at4.10: <title> + HEREDOC + Co-Authored-By trailer, local-only) -> bd close
(single-quote reason) -> STOP and report (one-issue-at-a-time STRICT; do NOT auto-
claim acct-0at4.16 or acct-0at4.2). Noisy-host posture throughout; full absolute
rigor is exactly what THIS issue is about, so pin+report the env before trusting
absolutes.
close_reason: All four children delivered: A (.10.1 pgbouncer pool-size confound sweep), B (.10.2 environment capture + pinning), C (.10.3 soak reframed as drift-detection), D (.10.4 statistics discipline — --seed, bootstrap CI, Mann-Whitney, steady-state rule). Confound control + soak + statistics discipline complete for ledger-v3.1 testing.

title: ledger-v3.1 testing: real baselines + ablations (strict Path A, raw ceiling, lever ablations)
description:
Source: FEEDBACK-TESTING.md #9 (also answers FEEDBACK #7 with data).

Without baselines every number is self-referential. §11.2's direct-flavor flat-vs-depth result is near-tautological (the hot path never reads layer rows), so it de-risks the *cheap* half of Path C and proves nothing about the *decision* on its own.

- **Strict-mode Path A on the same box** — the linear-in-depth curve is the entire motivation; measuring Path C flat without measuring strict linear proves nothing about the decision. This is one build of the `ledger-v3` workspace.
- **Raw ceiling** — plain `INSERT INTO trx_line` batch throughput on the same hardware; bounds how much of Path C's cost is the ledger vs the substrate.
- **Ablations:**
  - `batch_size_max ∈ {1, 50, 200, 1000, ∞}` — maps the batching curve (and grounds the reconciled "1000 → ⌈1000/batch_size_max⌉ commit_groups" claim empirically).
  - `router_pack_disjoint` on/off.
  - **advisory-lock vs `pool_lock` row** — directly answers FEEDBACK #7 / the ARCH roll-up with data (WAL/xmax churn on the hot lock page).
  - `SetLatch`-on-enqueue vs 50 ms tick — ties to the open-loop/latency issue.

## Acceptance
Results table adds the strict Path A depth curve + raw-INSERT ceiling on the same box; the four ablation axes measured and reported; the advisory-vs-row-lock ablation feeds the ARCH #7 disposition.

title: ledger-v3.1: forced xid allocation on enqueue -> anti-wraparound vacuum pressure at routed throughput
description:
Source: FEEDBACK.md finding #3 (third bullet); design-v3.1 §6.1; code `ledger-routed-c/src/enqueue.rs` (`GetCurrentFullTransactionId`).

## Problem
`ledger_enqueue_trx_c` captures `GetCurrentFullTransactionId()` so the committer eject loop can probe `pg_xact_status` to detect caller in_progress / aborted / committed. That **forces xid assignment** on an otherwise read-only tx. For the standalone-enqueue pattern (the harness's 1000-caller shape, and the likely production shape for a pure event feed), every submission burns a permanent xid with **zero WAL written**. At routed's target throughput that is cluster-wide anti-wraparound autovacuum pressure — a cost §6.1's "no DB write at submission" framing elides.

## Constraint (why the obvious fix is wrong)
Switching to `pg_current_xact_id_if_assigned()` (no xid → triage as always-keep) would break the eject mechanism's ability to detect an *aborted* standalone caller. The forced xid is load-bearing, not accidental. A real fix needs an alternative liveness signal — virtual-xid tracking, a caller heartbeat, or scoping forced-xid to genuinely transactional callers only — or an explicit decision to accept the cost.

## Do
1. Document the xid-burn cost honestly in §6.1 (it is currently elided).
2. Add a soak measurement of `age(datfrozenxid)` slope under sustained routed load (ties to the soak issue).
3. Evaluate whether standalone-enqueue callers can avoid forcing an xid without losing abort detection.

Related (savepoint-rollback, bullet 1 of FEEDBACK #3): already handled — `enqueue.rs` captures the *current subtransaction's* full xid via `GetCurrentFullTransactionId()`, which is exactly the reviewer's prescribed fix, so a rolled-back subtransaction's enqueue triages as aborted. No action there beyond a one-line spec note that the sub-xid (not top-level) is captured.

## Acceptance
§6.1 states the xid-burn cost and the sub-xid capture; a soak run quantifies `datfrozenxid` slope at target throughput; a decision recorded on mitigate-vs-accept.
close_reason: Close-moot per GATE VERDICT (acct-0at4.11.5, design-v3.1 §18). Staging-table enqueue is an ordinary heap INSERT in the caller tx (SPIKE-A) — no xid escapes the tx, so forced-xid / anti-wraparound pressure evaporates with the shmem eject/xid-triage apparatus (FEEDBACK-ARCH #3). --force because moot regardless of its (kept) prerequisite .10.

title: ledger-v3.1: routed cross-chunk can silently drop a correctly-ordered depletion
description:
Source: FEEDBACK.md finding #2 (poc/ledger-v3.1); design-v3.1 §14.2 split-chunk note, §15.

## Problem
When a single hot pool's connected component exceeds `batch_size_max` (default 200), the router splits it into independent commit_groups claimed concurrently by different committers with **no predecessor-wait**. `pool_lock FOR UPDATE` serializes same-pool writes but does not order them by enqueue position. Consequence: a depletion a caller enqueued *after* its replenishing receipt can execute *before* it if they land in different chunks — a spurious `InsufficientInventory` for a caller who ordered everything correctly. §14.2's "preserves strict-time-order semantics" holds only *within* a chunk.

## Amplifier
Routed caller observability is out of scope, so the failure is **silent**: no trx row appears and no error is raised. The business event is lost, detectable only by absence-polling + resubmit — and the resubmit races the same way. This bites hardest exactly where routed is meant to win (hot pool → large component → guaranteed chunking).

## Proposed mitigation (cheap for the dominant case)
Chunks split from a single hot pool are already fully serialized by `pool_lock`; add a **per-pool predecessor-wait** (chunk N+1 claimable only after chunk N commits). Costs zero parallelism there — it only constrains claim order. The general multi-pool-component case is harder (that is why predecessor-wait was dropped), but a per-pool chain covers the S5/S7/S8 shapes.

## Decision needed
(a) implement per-pool predecessor-wait, (b) add a routed error/observability channel so drops surface, or (c) accept-and-document as a load-characterization limit. This is a routed *behavioral* gap, not a hot-path correctness bug within a commit_group.

## Acceptance
A test forces a receipt→depletion pair across a chunk boundary and asserts the chosen behavior (no spurious drop, or a surfaced error). §14.2's "strict-time-order" wording updated to match whichever option is chosen.
notes: Re-derived under ARCH-POSTURE (acct-0at4.11.3, design-v3.1 §16, DECIDED 2026-07-08): posture is everything-provisional (alt C). With no synchronous qty gate on the hot path, the spurious-InsufficientInventory failure mode is MOOT — the depletion is appended unconditionally and a transient negative aggregate is a recalc finding, so there is no synchronous failure to be spurious. Per-pool predecessor-wait is NOT needed for quantity. Residual cross-chunk COST-order-sensitivity (which provisional running-avg a depletion records) survives but is already provisional and trued up by recalc regardless of order (§14.2/§14.3). Disposition: supersede/close as moot at the gate verdict acct-0at4.11.5 (formal re-triage lives there, not here).
close_reason: Close-moot per GATE VERDICT (acct-0at4.11.5, design-v3.1 §18 + §16). Double-dissolved: staging-table drain gives per-pool FIFO by construction (SPIKE-A) AND everything-provisional posture (alt C) removes the synchronous qty gate entirely — no spurious InsufficientInventory exists to be dropped. --force because the bug is moot regardless of its (kept) oracle prerequisites .4/.5/.6; there is nothing left to fix.

title: Pass-3 C4 (P2): routed acceptance suite RED at production defaults — 2 affinity-grouping tests encode the pre-p1al pack-off contract
description: AUDIT-PASS3.md C-ii finding C4, from the one-time Pass-3 suite run (acct-mvq4.6). bash scripts/run-tests.sh --path routed is RED at shipped defaults: acceptance_routed_affinity_grouping fails 2/4 — disjoint_submissions_group_independently (asserts 3 independent commit groups; observes 1 group holding all 3 submissions) and transitive_overlap_merges_into_one_component (asserts merged-component + singleton = 2 groups; observes 1 group holding all 4 submissions). title: Pass-3 Q10: committer ERROR-exit orphans its in-flight commit_group — Phase-2 reclaim only triggers at router restart
description: Found by acct-mvq4.4 (AUDIT-PASS3.md section B-ii.6 Q10, P2, recovery trigger gap). The only trigger for §6.5 Phase-2 dead-committer reclaim is try_recover_router_orphan at ROUTER startup (router.rs:105); committers run no sweep at their own (re)start. A committer that exits via ERROR->FATAL->exit(1) - an uncaught tick error outside the write subtx (e.g. the trx_type label-cache query failing: the documented abort-the-tick path at committer.rs:104-106) or operator pg_terminate_backend mid-pipeline - is respawned in 5s, takes over its old identity slot (generation bumps), and its orphaned CQ entry sits at valid==2 with a dead identity INDEFINITELY: claim only takes valid==1, no periodic sweep exists, the router has no reason to restart. The group staging slots stay at valid==3 (callers poll forever). A genuine crash (signal) is fine - postmaster reinitializes and shmem evaporates; the gap is the clean-FATAL class. The acceptance suite exercises the reclaim mechanism via synthetic injection + manually-invoked sweep, so the missing trigger is invisible to it. Fix shape: run the (already idempotent, CAS-elected) Phase-2 sweep at committer startup too, or sweep periodically from the router tick.
close_reason: Q10 fixed with both triggers (belt-and-suspenders per user). (1) Router periodic sweep: re-run idempotent try_recover_router_orphan every RECLAIM_SWEEP_INTERVAL_NS=2s from the router wake loop, at loop top before the tick drain (no self-emit race) and behind the test-pause gate. (2) Committer-startup reclaim: new Phase-2-only reclaim_dead_committers() called in committer_main after claim_committer_identity; touches only the committer queue (never staging) so it is safe under a live router emit. Both share try_reclaim_dead_committer_entry extracted from sweep_queue_phase (behavior-preserving), CAS-elected. Closes the gap where a clean-FATAL committer exit orphaned its CQ entry at valid==2 until router restart. Tests: added acceptance (e) Phase-2 entry point recovers injected orphan + (f) router periodic sweep reclaims autonomously (no manual sweep/restart) — the triggers the prior manual-sweep tests could not see; new test_hook ledger_routed_c_test_reclaim_dead_committers. title: Pass-3 Q9: xid-triage SPI-error swallow keeps everything — fail-open inversion of the caller-tx contract
description: Found by acct-mvq4.4 (AUDIT-PASS3.md section B-ii.6 Q9, P2, latent fail-open). classify_and_eject runs the batched pg_xact_status probe inside an Spi::connect closure that early-returns None on any error (.ok()? three times) and the caller does .unwrap_or_default() (committer.rs:1097-1114) -> empty status map -> every per-submission lookup misses -> unwrap_or(CallerTxStatus::Unknown) (:1141) -> Unknown is KEPT (:1143). One SPI failure commits work for callers that may be in-progress or aborted - precisely the atomicity the eject loop exists to enforce. Contradicts the fail-closed posture yojk.10 established for status-wording drift (Unrecognized -> WARNING + never kept); the query-error path fails open. Reachability low (SPI failure in a healthy BGWorker: OOM, interrupt) but the failure direction is wrong. Both-ways trap: propagating Err instead -> TxError -> cleanup releases slots -> submissions silently lost (also wrong). Correct shape: treat triage failure as eject-all so slots return to pending and the next tick retries.
close_reason: Q9 fixed — xid-triage SPI-probe failure now fails CLOSED. Split the probe into probe_xid_statuses(); on SPI error it returns None and classify_and_eject ejects EVERY submission back to pending (staging valid 3->1, cg_id cleared, last_eject_at_ns set for 10ms cooldown) and returns Ok(empty) -> AllEjected -> router re-packs -> next tick re-triages. Replaces the pre-fix fail-open (empty status map -> Unknown -> KEPT, committing possibly-open/aborted callers work). Not Err->TxError (that drops/loses the group). Probe failure is ours not the callers, so no eject_count bump (never terminal-drops legitimately-committed work). AllEjected cleanup already skips ejected slots so existing InProgress-eject safety carries over. Added production getter ledger_routed_c_committer_eject_total_count + one-shot test_inject_xact_probe_fail hook. Test: acceptance (g) xact_probe_failure_ejects_all_then_retries asserts ejected (eject_total_count++), not dropped (dropped/tx_failures unchanged), commits exactly once after re-triage (no double-apply). Verified: full routed suite 5/5 green (27 tests). Commit ea9f616.

title: Pass-3 Q7: eject-vs-stamp race — unconditional eject mutations vs publish-before-stamp window lose or leak staging slots
description: Found by acct-mvq4.4 (AUDIT-PASS3.md section B-ii.6 Q7, P2, latent race). emit_commit_group publishes the CQ entry (claimable) BEFORE the per-entry data-before-flag stamps (router.rs:269-310 vs :321-363), so a committer can claim, decode, and reach pg_xact_status triage while staging entries are still at valid==2. classify_and_eject (committer.rs:1166-1180) bumps eject_count, zeroes cg_id, and CASes valid 3->1 with NO state gate - against a slot at 2 the CAS fails but the mutations stand. Interleaving (a): eject completes before the router stamp -> router stores cg + CAS 2->3 succeeds -> cleanup sees cg-match at valid==3 -> releases the slot as if committed: the in-progress caller submission is silently discarded (no trx, no retry, no counter). Interleaving (b): router cg store, then eject cg-0 store, then router CAS 2->3 -> slot at valid==3 / cg==0 / eject>0 - cleanup skips both CAS arms, router scans only valid==1, sweeps only touch valid==2 -> stuck slot + arena held until postmaster restart. Preconditions: caller tx still open at triage (the DESIGNED §6.1 usage - enqueue inside an open user tx; harness autocommit callers almost never arm it, hence zero ejects in all shipped results) + router preempted mid-stamp-loop. Fix shape: gate the eject mutations on the 3->1 CAS succeeding (mutate-after-CAS), or stamp staging before publishing the CQ.
close_reason: Fixed (commit ef1c1bf, shape A committer-local). Both eject sites in classify_and_eject now move the staging slot to pending via eject_staging_slot_to_pending — a bounded CAS loop over {3,2}->1 — instead of a bare CAS 3->1 that no-ops against a still-at-valid==2 slot while the metadata writes stand. This closes interleaving (a) silent-loss (router late 2->3 no longer frees an ejected in-progress submission as committed) and (b) stuck-slot (no valid==3/cg==0 orphan). Chose A over shape B (stamp-before-publish) because B inverts the data-before-flag ordering that sweep_queue_phase Phase-1 recovery depends on. 4 deterministic unit tests pin both interleavings + normal valid==3 path + loop termination; full routed acceptance suite green (5 binaries / 27 tests incl. xact_probe_failure_ejects_all_then_retries which exercises the fail-closed eject loop).

title: Pass-3 Q1: provisional standard-basis partial depletion emits negative value_sum -> 0007 CHECK violation instead of typed error
description: Found by acct-mvq4.3 (AUDIT-PASS3.md section B-i.7 Q1, P2, latent code defect). wac.rs aggregate_deplete (:175) subtracts the posted depletion amount from value_sum unclamped whenever new_qty > 0. Under ProvisionalBasis::Standard (provisional.rs:78-82) the posted amount is qty x C_std, decoupled from the pool book value. Repro: receipt 10 @ 100 (value_sum=1000), standard_cost=150, deplete 7 -> mutation {qty:3, value_sum:-50} -> pool_state_aggregate_value_sum_nonneg (migration 0007) rejects with 23514 at write time. Realistic shape: any C_std above the running average plus a deep-but-partial depletion (10 pct drift breaks at >91 pct depletion). The 0007 header semantics (value_sum reconcilable to GL posting sum) legitimately goes negative here - the CHECK and the stated semantics conflict. Coverage gap: unit test plan_apply_provisional.rs:110 and integration acceptance_direct_methods.rs:224 both use C_std < avg; no test asserts the mutation value_sum in the over-book shape; every harness pool is seeded running_avg (pool_universe.rs:159) so no measured run ever drove the path - all shipped results unaffected. Twin edge on running-avg basis: banker-rounding-up of the average times a large partial deplete (qty 5 / value_sum 3 -> avg 1, deplete 4 -> value_sum -1); sub-micro-unit costs only.
acceptance_criteria: Pick one: (a) clamp value_sum at 0 on depletion like the empty-pool case (loses GL reconcilability - document), (b) return a typed LedgerError when posted amount exceeds book value, (c) relax the 0007 CHECK to match the GL-reconcilable semantics. Whichever: add the C_std > avg partial-deplete shape to plan_apply_provisional.rs AND acceptance_direct_methods.rs, asserting the mutation value_sum explicitly.
close_reason: Fixed via option (c) (user-selected): migration 0009 drops pool_state_aggregate_value_sum_nonneg — negative aggregate book value is a legitimate intermediate state under provisional standard-basis over-book depletion, matching 0007 own GL-reconcilable semantics (qty CHECK 0006 + NOT NULL stay). wac.rs depletion site documents the contract; decrement now checked_sub -> typed Overflow. Acceptance criteria met: unit repro {qty 3, unit_cost -17, value_sum -50} + running-avg rounding twin edge in plan_apply_provisional.rs; integration over-book shape asserting persisted aggregate via new aggregate_with_value helper in acceptance_direct_methods.rs. title: Time-window-only commit_group formation: drop the document cap, adaptively size batch_window_us to committers / workload / pool distribution / machine IO
description:
Why: acct-p1al found that with router_pack_disjoint on, commit_group size (cg) is co-limited by TWO entangled knobs -- batch_size_max (a hard DOCUMENT-count cap) and batch_window_us (the time coalesce gate). cg tracks the cap (42 at cap 50, 148 at cap 200, 490 at cap 800 on the s2 64-pool spread), so the document cap is actively clipping group formation, and a positive feedback loop (bigger cap -> bigger groups -> slower per-group commit -> more accumulation before the next emission) makes the two inseparable from the existing data. acct-p1al raised disentangling them as the open follow-up.

Idea to explore (user, 2026-06-03): cap commit_group formation by TIME WINDOW ONLY, not by document count. Make batch_window_us the SOLE gate and remove batch_size_max as a binding constraint (drop it, or keep it only as a high non-binding safety ceiling), so a commit_group is simply everything that accumulated during the window. Crucially the window must be MATCHED to the deployment so formation is BALANCED for: (a) the number of committer background workers, (b) the workload type, (c) the pool distribution (spread vs single-hot-pool vs deep), and (d) the machine compute + IO power. Objective is balance: committers well utilized but not backlogged, fsync/commit amortized to an appropriate degree, caller tail latency bounded, no committer starved and none overloaded -- for the actual hardware and load.

PHASE 1 RESEARCH (characterize time-window-only formation):
- Neutralize the document cap (set batch_size_max very high so the window binds) and sweep batch_window_us across workload types (spread s2, hot s5, deep s7, mixed s19) and committer_count in {1,2,4,8}.
- Measure per cell: cg, throughput quartiles, caller ack + committed latency, fsync per-trx and percent of committer time, committer busy_frac / utilization, staging-ring backpressure / queue-full events, pool_lock and row-lock fractions.
- Answer: does pure-time gating beat the cap+window combo on throughput AND latency? What is the relationship between the balanced window and committer_count x arrival rate x pool overlap x machine IO? What is the failure mode of an uncapped group (unbounded committer lock-hold, arena/memory pressure, tail-latency blowup under arrival spikes)? Does a safety ceiling on group size remain necessary?
- Deliverable: a committed results writeup with the sweep, a model relating the balanced window to committers / workload / IO, and a recommendation on whether to pursue time-only formation.

PHASE 2 (if warranted -- EXPLORATION; surface design choices, do not pre-decide):
Candidate directions to evaluate, NOT a chosen design:
- Static-but-tuned: a per-deployment batch_window_us derived from a calibration of committer_count + measured machine IO + expected workload, with batch_size_max retained only as a high safety ceiling.
- Closed-loop adaptive: a controller that adjusts batch_window_us (and possibly committer_count) from live signals (arrival rate, committer drain time, fsync fraction, staging backpressure) toward a balance objective.
Open questions to resolve during exploration: is batch_size_max removed entirely or retained as a non-binding safety ceiling? Static-tuned vs dynamically-adaptive? What is the balance objective function (committer utilization target, fsync-fraction target, p99 SLO)? How does it interact with caller backpressure (queue_full_timeout) and the LISTEN/NOTIFY pseudo-sync escape hatch?

INVARIANTS to preserve: document atomicity (a submission is one staging entry, never split -- the invariant acct-p1al pinned with tests); one pool_lock + one aggregate UPSERT per pool per group; a bound on committer lock-hold / group size so a pure time window cannot form an arbitrarily large group that starves callers or blows tail latency.

Related: acct-p1al (motivating finding; pack_disjoint now default on, batch_size_max default 200, with the window-vs-cap disentanglement left open), acct-235v (routed throughput<->latency dial via batch_window_us sweep -- IN PROGRESS, directly overlaps and should inform Phase 1), acct-czz4 (rigorous batch-size sweep), acct-jdgm (batch_size_max default + ingress). design-v3.1 sections 6.3 / 6.5 (router batch formation).
design:
PHASE 1 COMPLETE (commit 4485269; deliverable poc/ledger-v3.1/results/hh7b_window_only_sweep.md). User HELD at Phase1->Phase2 boundary ("hold - discuss first", 2026-06-03). RESUME PROTOCOL (user directive 2026-06-03: "resume hh7b exploration on resume"): on session resume, re-present the findings + exploration menu below and AWAIT USER DIRECTION. Do NOT claim a Phase 2 path, do NOT start implementation, do NOT launch cluster-touching benches without an explicit pick. This is an exploration/discussion resume, not an execution resume.

PHASE 1 OUTCOME (full detail in the committed writeup):
1. Dropping batch_size_max does NOT make the window the sole gate -- router_window_size (per-tick scan budget, 1000) is the real ceiling; max_group tracks it 1-for-1. Raising it past 1000 strictly worse (latency up, tput flat-down); 1000 = the knee, a good natural ceiling.
2. Window has near-zero throughput leverage on high-arrival workloads (backlog-bound; cg 5-10x up, tput <±10%). Window has leverage only at low arrival (s10 cc1) -- and there it is a LATENCY knob.
3. Real throughput lever = committer_count x pool-overlap: scales on disjoint (s6) + batched hot-pool (s5); FLAT-to-declining on intertwined (s10 ~1k, locks/trx 4.6). User hypothesis "fewer committers on intertwined" VERIFIED; "larger batches win" NOT a throughput lever.
4. No runaway: arena <=46MB/128, zero drops; document atomicity preserved.

CROSS-POLLINATION from acct-at8x (latency-vs-load, CLOSED, commit e1fe448, results/latency_vs_load.md -- ran between Phase 1 and this hold):
- Below saturation: admission sub-ms; commit ~60-90ms p50 / 105-160ms p99. hh7b multi-second figures = pure overload backpressure (user verdict: multi-second p50 unacceptable -> answered: it does not exist below the knee).
- Commit-latency FLOOR = 50ms BGWorker tick cadence (router.rs:107, committer.rs:138 wait_latch(50ms)). Sub-50ms = latch-kick on enqueue, cheap isolated change.
- Knees: intertwined ~850->925 trx/s; spread p99 knee 3500->4000 (zipf hot pool crossing its SERIAL drain rate; p50 holds to ~10k). A skewed workload p99 SLO is set by its hottest pool serial rate.
- UNIFYING FINDING: per-pool lock serialization is the wall for BOTH throughput AND latency, in both regimes. Formation knobs do not move it.
- New harness capability: --target-rate paced open-loop (cli.rs/main.rs/driver_routed.rs) + bench/sweep-latency-vs-load.sh -- reusable for any future SLO calibration.

EXPLORATION MENU on resume (user picks; my reads attached):
A. batch_size_max disposition: drop vs keep as high non-binding safety bound. Read: keep as documented safety bound; real ceiling knob is router_window_size ~1000.
B. Closed-loop WINDOW controller (original Phase 2 framing). Read: NO -- tunes the wrong variable.
C. committer_count-vs-pool-overlap direction: per-deployment calibration / make committer_count live-tunable (restart-only today) / document tuning rule only. Read: most valuable formation-adjacent direction; arguably a NEW issue not hh7b Phase 2.
D. (new, from at8x) Latch-kick on enqueue to cut the 50ms tick floor -> sub-50ms commit latency. Cheap, isolated, high value if latency SLO matters.
E. (new, from at8x) Attack per-pool serialization itself -- the actual wall everywhere. Correctness-sensitive ledger design question (pool_lock granularity / intra-pool pipelining); biggest potential payoff, biggest risk; needs its own issue + design discussion.
F. Close hh7b as answered (window-only characterized; safe but not a win) + file C/D/E as separate issues.
