Bench discipline: noisy host (chrome ~2x swing), drop_db_robust retry pattern in sweep-hh7b-window.sh + sweep-latency-vs-load.sh handles the DROP DATABASE committer-reconnect race. NOTES field of this issue holds the 235v fold-in + original hypothesis (do not overwrite).
notes:
FOLD-IN of acct-235v (closed 2026-06-03): 235v was the batch_window_us throughput<->latency characterization; its findings + artifacts are carried here so hh7b Phase 1 does not redo them.

Carried-forward findings from acct-235v (load-gated, quiet host, 8-core host):
- Committers parallelize on DISJOINT work: s6 (1000c disjoint, cg~1) = 958 (cc2) -> 1234 (cc4) -> 1791 trx/s (cc8). They do NOT parallelize on PARETO-HOT / intertwined work: s10 (50c Pareto, cg~12) flat ~1390 across cc 2/4/8 -- committers sit idle AND serialize on shared hot-pool FOR UPDATE locks (each complex receipt touches ~13.5 pools).
- The window can only coalesce submissions that have ARRIVED; on hot workloads the bind is per-pool lock SERIALIZATION, not lock count (inherent to a correct ledger). Batching has large leverage where same-pool overlap is high: s5 (single hot pool) cg=32 -> 0.03 locks/trx -> 2705 trx/s (host max), trading ack latency.
- Router is NOT the ceiling (entries_scanned/tick ~8.8, window_defers ~2 pct, groups_formed == groups_drained). Remaining cost is synchronous-ack latency (p99 0.3s @50c, 1-4s @1000c) -> shape-L pseudo-sync escape hatch.
- Contamination caveats: stale shared_preload BGWorkers halve throughput; Chrome swings it ~2x; all pre-load-gate absolutes are unreliable. Correctness counters (dropped/poisoned/deadlock_retries/takeover) all 0.
- Artifacts: results/committer_count_sweep_s6s10.csv, results/committer_count_sweep.csv, results/batch_window_sweep.csv, router observability getters in ledger-routed-c/src/lib.rs, wait_for_quiet_host load gate in bench/common.sh.

NEW HYPOTHESIS TO VERIFY (user, 2026-06-03): on SMALL-POOL / INTERTWINED (high pool-overlap) workloads, bias toward LARGER batches + FEWER committer bg-workers -- the INVERSE of the disjoint/spread tuning. Rationale: 235v shows extra committers cannot parallelize intertwined work (they serialize on shared pool locks / sit idle, e.g. s10 flat across cc), so MORE committers add lock contention + overhead without throughput; FEWER committers cut that overhead while LARGER batches maximize per-pool coalescing/amortization on the overlapping pools (the s5 leverage). This makes committer_count an explicit BALANCE AXIS in Phase 1: for intertwined/small-pool cells test cc in {1,2} with large windows; for disjoint/spread cells test higher cc. The balanced operating point is pool-distribution-dependent -- the core thesis of this issue. NEEDS VERIFICATION in the Phase 1 sweep (add a small-pool/high-overlap workload crossed with low committer_count + large window).

title: Committer prep/fsync floor: prepare the dedup SELECT against trx + commit-group sizing
description:
Motivation: acct-sczx Levers A+B (prepared plans + cross-submission batching) cut committer apply CPU/trx 4.76x (217.8->45.8us) and lifted cc=1 throughput ~3.2x (~4900->~15550 trx/s). That EXPOSED the fixed per-group costs as the new floor (measure-apply-spans.sh, commit 7a9cf14):
- prep: 4.9% -> 19.7% of committer time, now the LARGEST non-apply span. prep = pipeline - (pool_lock+hydrate+apply): payload decode + pg_xact_status triage + the dedup SELECT against trx + line-decode. The dedup SELECT is still ONE-SHOT SPI (re-parsed/re-planned every group) - the same fix as Lever B applies (prepare_mut + keep, thread_local). It also runs per-group, so it could batch the lookup keys.
- fsync: 5.1% -> 15.4%. One COMMIT per commit group (committer.rs wraps the group in one BackgroundWorker::transaction -> 1 fsync/group). Only LARGER commit groups amortize it further (router batch_size_max trades latency for fsync amortization). No code fix; a tuning/characterization question (and bound by group fill rate).

Scope:
1. Prepare the prep-phase dedup SELECT against trx (cached plan in the committer pipeline), mirroring acct-sczx bulk_write.rs. Measure prep% drop via measure-apply-spans.sh.
2. Characterize fsync vs commit-group size (router batch_size_max sweep) - latency/throughput tradeoff, not a code change.

Out of scope / done: the apply (write) path - that is acct-sczx, shipped. This is the residual prep+fsync floor uncovered by it.

title: Routed-c: caller-side batch enqueue + diagnostic bench (isolate ingress-lock vs downstream ceiling)
description:
Motivation: acct-0usf.1 (commit 4007738) proved LWLock/ledger_v31_staging_queue is the throughput ceiling, but did NOT disambiguate WHICH pressure dominates: producer-vs-producer lock-acquisition contention, or downstream drain capacity (router grouping + committer commit + WAL). This issue settles it by a direct causal test rather than instrumentation.

Idea (user): push LARGE batches FROM THE CALLER so N trx ride ONE STAGING_QUEUE.exclusive() acquisition. Lock HANDOFFS (where LWLock contention lives) drop ~Nx; the ring just fills with work to drain. Then whatever ceiling remains IS the true downstream capacity. If batched throughput >> the 4348 trx/s single-push cc=4 number => ingress lock-acquisition WAS the ceiling (justifies the cursor fix / sharding / lock-free ring). If batched throughput ~= 4348 => the ceiling is downstream and a lock fix will not help; the committer sampler then NAMES the real limiter (WAL/IO, tuple lock, on-CPU).

Required NEW CODE (no batch path exists today — ledger_enqueue_trx_c is single-push; the harness batch_size is DIRECT-mode only):
  1. Extension: ledger_enqueue_trx_batch_c(envelopes) that pushes N entries under ONE STAGING_QUEUE.exclusive() (loop push_entry_into_queue or a batch variant). Preserve QueueFull/backpressure CV, spillover-arena alloc/free, and recovery scan semantics.
  2. Harness: a routed-batched caller mode that builds N envelopes per push and drives the batch entry-point.

Bench: routed, FEW callers (1/2/4 — minimal handoff contention) x large batch (e.g. 100-1000 trx/push), router batch_size_max=200, s2 receipts. Record throughput + committer sampler named wait + busy_frac.

Caveat: batched-push is a SYNTHETIC ceiling probe (real callers post one trx per business event) — label results as a downstream-capacity probe, not realistic load. The bench run is a cluster touch (DROP/CREATE + restart) requiring explicit per-run go-ahead.

Separate from the cheap router-cursor fix (its own issue). Feeds the staging-LWLock reduction decision and acct-m4g5.4 keep/kill synthesis.
notes:
Caller-side batching (8192 = half the 16384 ring) vs single-push, 1 SKU per committer (pinned, steals=0), router batch 200, sweep committers=SKUs=callers=1/2/4. Result (results/affinity_1sku_batched.csv): cc=1 4836 (+60% vs single-push 3017), cc=2 5433 (+44% vs 3767), cc=4 1066 (-75% vs 4348). errs=0.
Caller batching WINS at low caller count (removes per-trx staging handoffs, commit groups fill, committer runs apply-bound) and INVERTS at cc=4: top_wait=LWLock/ledger_v31_staging_queue (NOT the spillover_arena I predicted), committers 86% idle (busy_frac 0.14) — 4 producers each pushing a half-ring batch hold the staging EXCLUSIVE lock for long durations and starve the router share() read. Crossover between 2 and 4 callers. Confirms the staging LWLock as the ingress ceiling from a 2nd angle; relates to acct-ozln (router collect_candidates cursor) and the push-side hold.
close_reason: Done. Code shipped (ledger_enqueue_trx_batch_c batch entry-point + harness routed-batched caller mode; commits 9e90a77, 5ba9b6c) and the diagnostic bench ran (results/affinity_1sku_batched.csv). Result settles the acct-0usf.1 question from a 2nd angle: caller-side batching (CBATCH=8192) removes per-trx staging handoffs and WINS at low caller count (cc=1 4836 +60% vs single-push 3017; cc=2 5433 +44%) but INVERTS at cc=4 (1066, -75%) — 4 producers each holding STAGING_QUEUE.exclusive() for a half-ring batch starve the router share() read (top_wait=LWLock/ledger_v31_staging_queue, committers 86% idle). Confirms the staging LWLock as the ingress ceiling. Crossover between 2 and 4 callers. Downstream-capacity probe (synthetic, not realistic load). Feeds acct-ozln (router cursor) + the push-side hold; lock-reduction decision is downstream of this. errs=0.

title: Routed-c: bound router collect_candidates share-lock scan (staging-side cursor; sibling of acct-m4g5.2)
description:
Motivation: the acct-0usf.1 1-SKU-per-committer result (commit 4007738) proved LWLock/ledger_v31_staging_queue is the unanimous throughput ceiling even with a perfect static committer pin and zero cross-committer contention (lock_of_busy=0.0000 every rep). One of the two pressures on that single global lock is the ROUTER side.

Mechanism: collect_candidates (router.rs:530) takes STAGING_QUEUE.share() and scans from `head` forward up to router_window_size (default 1000) valid slots, OR all 16384. `head` is the consumer low-water mark advanced ONLY by the committer (committer.rs:261); the router never advances it. When the live band near `head` is sparse/holey (routed-but-not-yet-consumed slots, or the committer lagging on head advancement), the router re-walks that prefix every tick UNDER THE SHARED LOCK, and a held share blocks every producer exclusive push (enqueue.rs:146).

This is the staging-side analog of acct-m4g5.2 (committer claim-loop O(ring) scan under shared LWLock) — same bug shape, router side.

Fix: give the router a local cursor / skip-already-routed-prefix so the scan starts at the first live un-routed slot and the share-lock hold is bounded, not O(ring) when sparse. Preserve recovery.rs scan/reclaim semantics and slot ordering.

Acceptance: router share-hold per tick bounded (not O(ring) under sparse occupancy); producer exclusive-wait on the staging lock measurably drops; no correctness regression (recovery, ordering, eject-cooldown intact). Measure before/after with the committer sampler + a router-hold metric.

Cheap, low-risk: lever identified in the staging-LWLock reduction analysis (router-hold side). Sibling: acct-m4g5.2.
notes: Pass-3 .4 re-verification (2026-06-06): confirmed at the field level — StagingQueue.head has NO store anywhere in the crate (load-only, permanently 0), so every collect_candidates scan is O(ring) from slot 0. Recorded in AUDIT-PASS3.md B-ii.3 atomic table (head row: DEAD) + B-ii.1 router verdict. Related new finding acct-mvq4.33 (Q12) names the third LWLock-hold site in the family: attempt_commit_phase holds the COMMITTER_QUEUE share guard across the entire SPI write phase, starving the router exclusive CQ claim.
close_reason: Router collect_candidates bounded to the occupied band via a router-local cursor (commit d0f1f76). StagingQueue.head is never advanced, so the old head=0 scan walked all 16384 slots under STAGING_QUEUE.share() every tick under sparse occupancy — the hold that blocks producer exclusive pushes. Fix: process-local thread_local cursor tracks the oldest OCCUPIED (`valid != 0`) slot; scan only [cursor, tail). Pure hint (the `valid` 1->2 CAS stays the routing gate); UNINIT bootstrap does one full-ring min-request_seq pass (wrap-safe on router restart). Band head is `valid != 0` not `valid == 1` because in-flight slots eject back to pending (3->1/2->1) in place — regression caught by orphan_recovery::xact_probe_failure_ejects_all_then_retries and fixed. router_entries_scanned_total now counts slots INSPECTED (name/doc were already right; impl was the outlier) — no new shmem field/pg_extern/SQL. Measured sparse s1 routed: 12.5 slots inspected/tick vs ~16384 old (~1300x shorter hold), drops=0 poison=0. Full routed acceptance suite green (10 binaries incl. orphan_recovery/backpressure/affinity/conservation). Container restored to production .so (0 test-hook fns, wake GUCs off).

title: acct-m4g5 STEP B: fix the committer claim-loop bug (per-committer cursor; no O(ring) scan under shared LWLock)
description: Only proceed if STEP A shows headroom. Two defects in ledger-routed-c/src/committer.rs that contaminate every affinity-ON measurement: (1) line ~261 queue.head.store((head+i+1)%capacity, Relaxed) — a single shared FIFO head cursor; when a committer skips non-owned entries and claims at offset i>0 it slams head PAST the skipped (other-committer-owned) entries, stranding them so they only resurface via the 5ms aging-steal (this is most of the observed ~74% steal_frac — an artifact, not 'one owner cant keep up'); (2) lines ~232-277, in ON mode each committer scans up to 2048 ring slots under the shared CommitterQueue LWLock (vs O(1) at-head in OFF), inflating lwlock + lock-hold time. FIX: replace the shared FIFO head with a per-committer claim cursor; eliminate the O(ring) scan-under-shared-LWLock (cheap per-owner indexing) so affinity-ON carries NO overhead artifact. Rebuild (cargo build --release --features pg18 --no-default-features), install via install-routed-c.sh, prove via engagement counters that owned-claims dominate + steal_frac low on a clean disjoint split. Production path stays inert at affinity_scheme=0.
acceptance_criteria: Per-committer claim cursor replaces the shared FIFO head; no O(ring) scan under shared LWLock in ON mode. Builds clean (0 err/0 warn, pg18). description: Design E of acct-0usf, the step the acct-xdwk lever-2 pass skipped. title: acct-0usf STEP 3 V2: per-pool ownership + route-to-majority
description: Design C variant V2: each pool is owned by a committer; a group routes to the committer owning the plurality of its pools, then takes the remaining cross-owner locks. Adds the V2 key to the scaffolding. Measure the residual cross-owner lock collisions, the contention majority-ownership cannot remove.
design: Expected effect: removes contention on the majority-owned pools; residual collisions on the minority pools bound the gain. On the ~13.5-pool Pareto groups the plurality is thin so residual collisions stay high. This variant is the direct H3 probe. Measure cross-owner collision count + lock_frac_of_busy + throughput.
acceptance_criteria: V2 implemented behind the GUC. ABAB N>=5 on the 13 CANDIDATE scenarios, median+IQR, load1 per rep, CSV committed. Residual cross-owner collision rate reported per scenario. Deltas vs OFF and vs V0 against the STEP 2 thresholds; explicit H3 read on the Pareto cells.

title: acct-0usf STEP 3 V1: whole-pool-set hash affinity
description: Design C variant V1: a group is owned by a hash of its full sorted pool-set (stable for identical groups; a re-formed group with a different pool-set hashes elsewhere). Adds the V1 key to the STEP 3 scaffolding (V0). Quantify how often re-formed groups change owner, the instability the whole-set hash trades for set-stability. Benched on the 13 CANDIDATE scenarios, ABAB N>=5.
design: Expected effect vs V0: identical-set groups land on one committer (better hot-pool isolation than min-pool when sets repeat); cost is owner churn when set membership drifts. Measure churn-on-reform rate + lock_frac_of_busy + throughput via the STEP 1 instruments.
acceptance_criteria: V1 key implemented behind the GUC. ABAB N>=5 sweep on the 13 CANDIDATE scenarios, median+IQR, load1 per rep, raw CSV committed. Owner-churn-on-reform rate reported per scenario. Deltas vs OFF and vs V0 evaluated against the STEP 2 thresholds.

title: acct-0usf STEP 2: pre-register affinity hypotheses H1/H2/H3 with falsification criteria
description: Design F of acct-0usf, split out per the always-separate-complex-work directive. BEFORE writing any affinity-variant code (the STEP 3 V0-V3 issues), pre-register falsifiable hypotheses with explicit numeric kill criteria, into this issue AND results/POC-REPORT.md, so STEP 3 variant results cannot be post-hoc rationalized. Numeric thresholds are derived from the STEP 1 measured IQRs (committer_profile_sweep.csv). This issue blocks all STEP 3 variant issues.
design: H1 (affinity shrinks the handoff): on a lock-bound CANDIDATE scenario, an affinity variant reduces committer lock_frac_of_busy by at least X pp vs affinity-OFF at matched load1, WITHOUT raising committer lwlock_frac_of_busy by more than it removes from lock. FALSIFIED if lock does not drop, or LWLock rises by at least the lock reduction. H2 (it converts to throughput): the lock reduction yields a throughput gain whose median clears the cell measured noise band (the STEP 1 IQR). FALSIFIED if median throughput delta is inside the IQR, or throughput moves without lock moving. H3 (many-pools kill criterion): on high-pool-count Pareto cells (~13.5 pools/trx: s11/s15/s19 and the s14-s21 builds/mixed), NO single-committer-ownership key can both keep commit_group atomicity and avoid re-serializing the multi-owner group, so affinity is structurally bounded there regardless of key. PRE-COMMIT to declaring these SKIP-for-affinity if H1 fails across V0-V3. Set X and the per-cell noise band from STEP 1 IQRs BEFORE running.
acceptance_criteria: H1/H2/H3 each written as a dated pre-registration block with concrete numeric thresholds (X pp, per-cell noise band) derived from STEP 1 IQRs; committed to results/POC-REPORT.md and mirrored into this issue notes. No STEP 3 affinity code committed before this block lands.
notes:
STEP 1 measured inputs: s5 single-hot-pool lock_of_busy 67pct (affinity best case); s8/s9 72pct; Pareto 50c (s10,s14,s16-18,s20,s21) lock 64-66pct LWLock 7-9pct; Pareto 200c (s11,s15,s19) lock 50-52pct LWLock 22-24pct; lock_of_busy IQR under 2pp across load1 1.6-2.8. SKIP a-priori: s6 (lock 0pct), s7 (lock 9pct, on-CPU bound).
STEP 2 DONE 2026-05-31 (commit 8210c20). Pre-registered H1/H2/H3 with numeric kill criteria into results/POC-REPORT.md (### acct-0usf STEP 2 block). Thresholds from STEP 1 OFF-arm IQRs: X_lock=max(2*lockIQR,5pp)=5.0pp all cells (lockIQR<=2pp); tput band=max(2*tputIQR,3% median) per cell (37-95 trx/s). H1 lock_of_busy drops >=X_lock without lwlock rising >= the drop. H2 tput median clears band where H1 holds; falsified if lock moves w/o tput or tput w/o lock. H3 PRE-COMMITTED kill: ~13.5-pool Pareto (s11/s15/s19 + s14-21) declared KILL-for-affinity if H1 (or H1-not-H2) fails across all V0-V3; refuted only if some variant clears BOTH on a high-pool cell surviving N>=5. title: Comprehensive committer→pool affinity investigation: measure the mechanism, full scenario matrix, falsifiable hypotheses
description:
Follow-up to acct-xdwk lever 2, which prototyped committer->pool affinity (hash(min pool_id) % committer_count + age-gated steal), measured it on s10/s11, found no benefit, and reverted the code. That investigation was too thin and too inference-driven to be conclusive. This issue redoes affinity rigorously.

What was inadequate in the acct-xdwk lever-2 pass (explicitly DO NOT repeat):

1. Bottleneck INFERRED, not MEASURED. The premise "cross-committer pool_lock FOR UPDATE handoff dominates" came from a single pg_stat_statements snapshot on a single-hot-pool run, then was generalized to all workloads. Per-committer lock-wait time under affinity off vs on was never directly measured. Throughput deltas were used as a proxy for a lock-contention claim.

2. Two scenarios only (s10, s11 -- both Pareto receipts), a single ~20s run per cell, with off-vs-on deltas INSIDE the host-load noise band (load1 swung 1.5-3.4 across cells). No repetitions, no variance, no confidence interval. A <=10% delta from one 20s run on a daily-driver host is not a result.

3. Affinity-ON correctness was never cleanly proven. The one cross-flavor equivalence run was contaminated by a concurrent docker restart (its failures were in the test's connect/seed helpers, not in any ledger assertion), and the code was reverted without ever obtaining a clean equivalence pass.

4. Only ONE affinity key was explored (min pool_id). The actual finding -- Pareto receipts touch ~13.5 pools/trx, so keying on min-pool cannot isolate a hot pool's contention -- points at a fundamental design tension that was never characterized: a commit_group spanning pools owned by N different committers must either be routed to one committer (re-serializing) or be split across committers (violating commit_group atomicity). That tension, not "min-pool didn't work," is the real subject.

GOAL: a rigorous, reproducible characterization of whether ANY committer-affinity scheme improves Path C throughput, measured across the FULL contention spectrum, with the bottleneck mechanism instrumented directly (not inferred from throughput), correctness proven per variant, statistical dispersion reported, and pre-registered falsifiable hypotheses -- ending in a defensible per-scenario-class keep/kill decision backed by numbers that survive host noise.
design:
METHODOLOGY (the rigor bar; each section is a deliverable).

A. MEASURE THE MECHANISM BEFORE OPTIMIZING IT.
   Decide per scenario whether affinity is even worth attempting, from direct measurement -- not from throughput deltas.
   - Per-committer wait-event sampling: high-frequency poll of pg_stat_activity wait_event / wait_event_type on backends WHERE backend_type LIKE 'ledger_routed_c_committer%'; aggregate % of committer time in Lock/transactionid vs IO/DataFileRead vs WALWrite vs CPU(null wait). The harness sampler currently samples CLIENT backends only -- it MUST be extended to committer BGWorkers (that gap is exactly why acct-235v missed the FOR UPDATE waits the first time).
   - pg_locks snapshots: count committers simultaneously blocked on the same pool_lock row (the literal cross-committer handoff).
   - Committer pipeline-time decomposition: split committer_pipeline_ns into lock-acquire-wait / hydrate / apply / bulk_write / commit-fsync via scoped timed spans (test_hooks-gated counters if they cost anything hot).
   DELIVERABLE: a per-scenario "where does committer wall-time go" table, affinity OFF. If lock-wait is a small share for a scenario, affinity is a priori pointless there -- record that and move on.

B. FULL SCENARIO MATRIX (not 2 cells). Span the contention spectrum:
   - s5  single hot pool       -- affinity's BEST case; MUST win here or the mechanism premise is false.
   - s6  disjoint              -- affinity MUST be neutral (no shared locks to serialize).
   - s7/s8/s9 deep zipf        -- mid concentration.
   - s10/s11 Pareto receipts   -- 50c / 200c.
   - s14-s21 Pareto builds/mixed -- multi-touch + deplete (the ~13.5-pools/trx regime).
   Each x committer_count {2,4,8(,16)} x affinity {variants below}.

C. AFFINITY DESIGN VARIANTS (characterize the ownership tension; don't just re-test min-pool).
   For EACH: state the expected mechanism effect, then measure it per (A).
   - V0 min-pool (the reverted baseline) -- control.
   - V1 whole-pool-set hash: group owned by a hash of its full sorted pool-set (stable for identical groups; a re-formed group with a different set hashes elsewhere -- quantify how often that happens).
   - V2 per-pool ownership + route-to-majority: each pool owned by a committer; a group is routed to the committer owning the plurality of its pools, then takes the remaining (cross-owner) locks. Measure the residual cross-owner collisions.
   - V3 router-side assignment: router assigns group->committer at emit time (full group knowledge) vs the committer-side claim filter V0-V2 use.
   (Drop variants early if (A) shows they cannot change the measured bottleneck.)

D. STATISTICAL RIGOR.
   - N >= 5 reps per cell; report median + IQR (or mean +/- 95% CI). No single-run conclusions.
   - Load-gate AND record load1 per rep; flag/discard reps above the gate.
   - Interleave arms ABAB (off,on,off,on...) so host drift doesn't alias onto one arm.
   - A delta counts only if it clears that cell's measured noise band.

E. CORRECTNESS PER VARIANT (the step skipped last time).
   - For every variant that ships even GUC-off: a CLEAN, ISOLATED affinity-ON cross-flavor equivalence run (property_ledger_enqueue_trx_c --ignored) with NOTHING else touching the cluster (no concurrent install/restart/cp), plus the committer acceptance suite. Aggregate-qty equivalence MUST hold (affinity changes which committer drains, never the ledger result).
   - Liveness: prove the steal/fallback under a deliberately stalled AND a killed owner committer (committer-death takeover still drains the queue; no starvation).

F. PRE-REGISTERED HYPOTHESES + FALSIFICATION (write these BEFORE running; do not post-hoc rationalize).
   - H1: affinity reduces committer lock-wait% on concentrated workloads (s5/s7/s8). FALSIFIED if lock-wait% is unchanged.
   - H2: a lock-wait reduction moves throughput ONLY when lock-wait was a large share of committer time. FALSIFIED if throughput moves without lock-wait moving, or vice versa.
   - H3 (the kill criterion): on many-pools-per-trx workloads (s10/s11/s14-21) NO affinity key helps, because group pool-sets overlap only partially so no single-committer ownership removes the contention. If confirmed across V0-V3, affinity is killed for those classes with evidence.
   Decide keep/kill PER scenario-class from the numbers.
acceptance_criteria:
- Mechanism breakdown (Design A) produced for the full scenario matrix (Design B), affinity OFF, committed as a CSV/markdown artifact -- committer wall-time decomposed (lock-wait / hydrate / apply / write / fsync), from DIRECT measurement (committer-backend wait sampling + pg_locks), not throughput inference.
- >= 3 affinity variants (incl. the min-pool control) measured across the matrix with N >= 5 reps per cell and reported dispersion (median + IQR or mean +/- 95% CI); raw CSVs committed.
- Every variant that lands in the tree (even GUC-off) has: (a) a clean ISOLATED affinity-ON cross-flavor equivalence pass, (b) committer acceptance green, (c) a committer-death/stall liveness test for its steal path.
- Pre-registered H1, H2, H3 each EXPLICITLY confirmed or falsified, each citing the supporting numbers.
- A written per-scenario-class keep/kill recommendation in POC-REPORT.md, superseding the acct-xdwk lever-2 (g) paragraph.
- Bench scripts reproducible and committed; load1 recorded per rep; ZERO single-run conclusions in the writeup.
- If the conclusion is "kill," it is killed with measured evidence across variants -- not from one workload.

Real STEP 1 commits: 2d531c6 (measured decomposition + POC-REPORT table + committer_profile_sweep.csv) and 80f7ce1 (profile-aggregate.py). Also: the first attempt at the POC-REPORT edit silently failed to match and I committed a false-message commit (e3271dc, report claim with only the CSV); fixed by amend so 2d531c6 contains BOTH report and CSV (verified: measured table present, old inference header gone, 15 scenario rows).

STEP 1 COMPLETE. POC-REPORT lever-2 section now carries the MEASURED per-scenario where-does-committer-wall-time-go table superseding the inference.

MEASURED (median, load-robust IQR<2pp, of-busy split lock/on-CPU/LWLock):
- s5 single-hot-pool: 67/24/6 busy74 -> CANDIDATE (best case yet only 67pct lock)
- s6 disjoint: 0/29/46 busy88 -> SKIP (LWLock-bound, cg~1)
- s7 deep-zipf-simple: 9/41/28 busy77 -> SKIP (on-CPU FIFO-bound)
- s8/s9 deep-zipf complex: 72/26/1 busy84-85 -> CANDIDATE
- s10,s14,s16,s17,s18,s20,s21 Pareto 50c: lock64-66 LWLock7-9 busy89-91 -> CANDIDATE
- s11,s15,s19 Pareto 200c: lock50-52 LWLock22-24 busy90 -> CANDIDATE but handoff only HALF of busy
13 CANDIDATE, 2 SKIP (s6,s7).

KEY: lever-2 bottleneck DIAGNOSIS right (13/15 lock-bound) but NOT universal (s6/s7 not lock-bound); NEW affinity-immune bottleneck found (shmem-ring LWLock 22-24pct on high-conc Pareto); even best case s5 only 67pct lock (caps affinity upside below the 78pct headline, which was total-DB across all backends not committer busy-time). All STEP 1 commits: c420ad6 (1a spans), 6233e77 (1b sampler), 8d4648f (sweep harness+regen SQL), 2d531c6 (table+CSV), 80f7ce1 (aggregator).

NEXT: STEP 2 = pre-register H1/H2/H3 with explicit falsification criteria (into issue + POC-REPORT before running variants). STEP 3 = affinity variants V0 min-pool / V1 whole-pool-set / V2 per-pool-ownership / V3 router-side, GUC-gated default-off, tested ONLY on the 13 CANDIDATE scenarios; s6/s7 a-priori SKIP. Reframed Q: on lock-bound cells can any committer->pool assignment shrink the handoff without re-serializing ~13.5-pool Pareto groups or trading row-lock for more LWLock wait. STEP 1a+1b instruments measure the answer per-variant.

title: Characterize routed throughput<->latency dial (batch_window_us sweep)
description: Bench characterization: routed batch_window_us is the throughput<->latency knob (GucContext::Sighup, range 0..5e6 us, read per-tick via batch_window_us_now()). The acct-0516 long-duration sweep ran at the default 500us and showed commit_group_size_avg well under the batch_size_max=50 cap (s5~28, 50/200-caller cells ~8-12) — so cg is arrival/coalesce-bound, not cap-bound. Raising batch_window_us makes the router defer a tick when the oldest candidate has waited < window, letting more pool-overlapping submissions pack into one commit_group => larger cg, fewer pool_locks/upserts per trx, higher throughput, at the cost of added ack latency. Goal: chart cg_avg / throughput / ack-p99(p50/p95/p99) vs batch_window_us on hot scenarios (s5 single-hot-pool, s7 deep-zipf) at a fixed load+duration, live-retuned via ALTER SYSTEM SET + pg_reload_conf() (no restart). Bench-only; touches no production code. Deliverable: a sweep script + a POC-REPORT.md note on the tuning curve. Cross-ref acct-0516 section (g).
notes:
FINAL clean characterization (load-gated, quiet host, minimal preload). Resolves the "batch size does not change throughput => something fundamentally incorrect" challenge: nothing is fundamentally broken; the flat-throughput observations are explained by per-pool write serialization + insufficient offered concurrency, plus earlier Chrome contamination.

EVIDENCE (cc = committer_count; all clean+restart+seed per cell; LOAD_GATE=1.5):
- committer parallelism scales on DISJOINT work: s6 (1000c, disjoint pools, cg~1.06) = 958 (cc2) -> 1234 (cc4) -> 1791 trx/s (cc8); commits/s 898->1161->1683; ack p99 4.3s->2.3s->1.2s. Committers DO parallelize.
- committer parallelism does NOT scale on PARETO-HOT work: s10 (50c, Pareto receipts, cg~12) = 1397/1379/1399 trx/s flat across cc 2/4/8; commits/s pinned ~115. Committers are idle at cc=8 (115 groups split 8 ways) AND serialize on shared hot-pool FOR UPDATE locks (each complex receipt touches ~13.5 pools; Pareto concentrates them).
- caller scaling on Pareto does NOT raise throughput: s10 (50c)=1379 vs s11 (200c)=1184; mean ack 36ms->169ms (4x callers -> 4.7x latency, throughput flat/down). Saturated on hot-pool serialization, not arrival.
- batching IS a real dial when overlap exists: s5 (1000c, single hot pool) coalesces to cg=32 => 0.03 locks/trx => 2705 trx/s (highest of all), trading latency (ack p50 450ms). This is the per-pool lock amortization working as designed.
- router is NOT the bottleneck (direct profile): entries_scanned/tick ~8.8 (not scan-bound; window=1000 unused), window_defers ~2% (gate not throttling), ticks ~34/s draining all available per tick, cumulative groups_formed==groups_drained (balanced).

SYNTHESIS:
1. batch_window_us looked flat on s5/s10 because (a) at those caller counts the workload already coalesces as much as its concurrency allows (can't batch submissions that have not arrived), and (b) the bound on hot workloads is per-pool lock SERIALIZATION, not lock COUNT - and serialization is inherent to any correct ledger. s5 shows batching has large leverage (2705 trx/s, 0.03 locks/trx) when same-pool overlap is high.
2. committer_count helps exactly to the degree the workload's pools are disjoint (s6 scales; s10 does not).
3. The router is exonerated as the ceiling (earlier "serial router" claim retracted).

title: v3.1: store cumulative value_sum on pool_state for exact, order-independent receipt running average
description:
Concern-7 follow-up (design-team round 2: TREAT AS DEFECT). The v3.1 running average is computed INCREMENTALLY with banker re-rounding off the already-rounded stored average — wac.rs aggregate_receipt: new_unit_cost = banker_div(old_qty*old_unit_cost + Q*C, new_qty), shared by WAC and provisional FIFO/LIFO receipts (provisional.rs:65). Consequence: for >=3 contributing receipts the final aggregate unit_cost (a) does NOT equal the single-division weighted average banker_div(sum(qty*cost), sum(qty)), and (b) is ORDER-DEPENDENT (rounding error from step n re-weights into step n+1). Currently documented as deliberate in §11.1 ("provisional unit_costs may differ ... order-of-processing ... not a bug") and §3.0/§3.1 ("stores the average directly, not a cumulative value_sum").

Decision: make the receipt running average exact and order-independent by storing a cumulative value_sum.

Scope:
- Schema (migration 0007): add value_sum BIGINT to pool_state aggregate row (layer_id=0).
- ledger-core wac.rs aggregate_receipt: value_sum += Q*C (i128-safe); unit_cost = banker_div(value_sum, new_qty). Then unit_cost == banker_div(sum(qty*cost), sum(qty)) EXACTLY and order-independent across receipt permutations.
- snapshot.rs read_aggregate/put_aggregate carry value_sum; both flavors hydration.rs + bulk_write.rs read/UPSERT it.
- Spec reconciliation IN THE SAME CHANGE so spec matches code at the landing commit: §3.0/§3.1 (storage is value_sum, unit_cost derived), §11.1 (drop the receipts "may differ" caveat), §14.2 (the round-2 wording becomes ACCURATE for receipts-only).
- Test: add the receipts-only assertion routed final unit_cost == banker_div(sum(qty*cost), sum(qty)) to property_ledger_enqueue_trx_c.rs; cross-flavor unit_cost equivalence becomes assertable for receipts in the equivalence harness.

LOAD-BEARING REVERSAL: this reverses the deliberate §3.0 "store the average, not value_sum" decision. Cost: one extra BIGINT column carried through hydration/bulk_write; lock-hold characterization unaffected (still aggregate-only, constant w.r.t. depth).

DEPLETION CAUTION (needs design before coding): WAC/provisional deplete at the current rounded average and leave unit_cost unchanged (wac.rs aggregate_deplete). value_sum must drop by the proportional share to keep the unit_cost == value_sum/qty invariant, but depletion-at-rounded-average is inherently lossy, so MIXED receipt+depletion sequences may remain order-sensitive in unit_cost even with value_sum. Scope the exactness+order-independence GUARANTEE to RECEIPTS-ONLY; keep mixed-sequence depletion order-sensitivity documented in §11.1/§14.2 unless a lossless depletion model is found.
acceptance_criteria: pool_state carries value_sum; receipt unit_cost == banker_div(sum(qty*cost), sum(qty)) exactly and order-independent across permutations; both flavors carry value_sum through hydrate+write; §3.0/§3.1/§11.1/§14.2 reconciled in the same change; receipts-only value-weighted assertion added to the routed property test; depletion order-sensitivity decision documented.
close_reason: Shipped value_sum storage (commit 62a43d2). pool_state carries value_sum; aggregate unit_cost is derived banker_div(value_sum, qty). Receipts add Q*C exactly -> receipts-only final unit_cost == banker_div(sum(Q*C), sum(Q)), exact and order-independent (the design-team assertion now holds). Depletions subtract the posted Q*applied_unit_cost so value_sum == net posted amounts (GL-reconcilable, the hard requirement); qty->0 forces value_sum=0. Mixed receipt+depletion stays order-sensitive in unit_cost (lossy depletion-at-rounded-average) -- documented in §11.1/§14.2, not fixed (would need per-receipt history). Migration 0007 (column + non-neg CHECK + DROP DEFAULT fail-loud). Spec §3.0/§3.1/§11.1/§14.2 reconciled in the same change. New property routed_receipts_only_unit_cost_is_value_weighted asserts the exact value-weighted average. Green: 8/8 acceptance+property binaries both flavors @40 cases, 38 ledger-core unit tests. NOTE: cross-flavor unit_cost equivalence for receipts is now assertable in the equivalence harness (equivalence.rs) but was not added there -- the property test covers the invariant; fold into the harness if a bench-level check is wanted.

title: v3.2: table-driven posting-account resolution (drop debit/credit/variance from SPI line)
description:
Post-build review concerns 1 + 2. The v3.1 SPI line carries debit_account, credit_account (required) and variance_account (optional) supplied by the caller verbatim — the ledger does no lookup (payload.rs PocV3Line, submit.rs LineJson, plan.rs TrxLineRequest; consumed straight into PostingLineRequest). This pushes GL chart-of-accounts knowledge to every caller. standard_cost is ALREADY table-hydrated (ledger-spi-common hydration.rs), so the principled fix extends that exact pattern to posting accounts.

Scope (v3.2, NOT a v3.1 patch — does not change what the v3.1 PoC measured):
- Add a posting-account config table keyed by some combination of (sku_id, trx_type, line_type, location_id) resolving debit / credit / variance accounts.
- Hydrate it at pool hydration alongside standard_cost; fail-loud (RAISE EXCEPTION) if a required account is missing.
- Drop debit_account / credit_account / variance_account from the SPI line tuple; the ledger looks them up.
- Update both flavors (ledger-direct-c, ledger-routed-c) + ledger-core TrxLineRequest.

Pushed back on doing this in v3.1 (user decision): caller-supplied accounts are a valid PoC simplification; the table-driven design is production GL-routing work for v3.2.
design: Wide-row posting_account_map keyed (sku_id, location_id): one full account set per pool with a debit/credit column pair per operation (receipt/transfer/build/scrap/adjustment) + variance_acct. line_type selects the pair; engine copies into journal. Hydrated alongside standard_cost; fail-loud (RAISE / new LedgerError) on missing config. SPI line drops debit/credit/variance. DDL change accepted when fundamental trx types change. Doc folds into design-v3.1.md (not a separate v3.2 doc).
acceptance_criteria: A v3.2 design exists for table-driven posting-account resolution; debit/credit/variance no longer caller-supplied per-line; hydration fail-loud on missing config.
close_reason: Shipped in 6d6c81c. posting_account_map (wide row per sku+location, debit/credit pair per operation stored receipt-direction + nullable variance_acct, migration 0008) resolves posting accounts ledger-side via hydration; dropped debit/credit/variance from the SPI line in both flavors + ledger-core TrxLineRequest; fail-loud MissingPostingAccounts. Both-path suite 8/8 green. Spec folded into design-v3.1.md §3.7.

title: ledger-routed-c: arena leaks ~1 block per committed submission (outstanding never returns to 0)
description:
Found during acct-yojk.3 (routed property test). After a fully-drained workload, the spillover arena does NOT return to baseline: outstanding_allocs grows by exactly 1 block per committed submission.

REPRO (fresh container, ledger_routed_c test_hooks): seed one fifo pool + aggregate, enqueue 4 single-line po_receipts, wait 3s for the committer to drain (trx=4, staging all-empty), then read the arena counters:
  allocs_total=20, frees_total=16, outstanding=4, freelist_count=6
i.e. 4 submissions -> 20 allocs / 16 frees / 4 permanently outstanding (one per submission). A 6-submission run (3 receipt + 2 deplete + 1 poison) left outstanding=6 likewise. Staging fully releases (pending/routed/processing/abandoned all 0); only the arena leaks.

PATH: committer.rs commits each group then calls cleanup::cleanup_after_commit_group, which for each staging index calls try_release_staging_slot (cleanup.rs:55) and, only when it returns Some, free_staging_arena_blocks (payload + pool_keys), then free_committer_queue_arena (staging_offsets + pool_keys arrays). ~5 allocs/submission, ~4 frees/submission -> exactly 1 unfreed. Need to identify WHICH of the per-group/per-submission arena blocks is not freed (candidate: a committer-queue metadata block, or a sentinel-offset case in free_staging_arena_blocks where payload_off/pool_keys_off==0 short-circuits a real block).

IMPACT: slow leak of the 128 MB arena over a long-running cluster (~1 block/submission). Non-blocking for the PoC (recalc/close + production hardening are out of scope per design-v3.1 §7/§13; 128 MB gives a large runway), but a genuine reclaim gap. The acct-yojk.3 property test documents this and gates drain quiescence on committed-count + staging-drained rather than arena_outstanding.
acceptance_criteria: Identify which arena block is not freed for committed (and dropped/poisoned) submissions; either free it in the cleanup path or document why it is intentionally retained. After a full drain, arena_outstanding returns to its baseline (modulo any intentional fixed overhead). A regression probe asserts outstanding does not grow monotonically with committed-submission count.
close_reason: Fixed: encode_submission allocates a lines blob + submission blob; committer cleanup freed the sub blob + pool-keys but leaked the lines blob (1 block/submission). Added line_offset to StagingEntry, populated at enqueue, captured in try_release_staging_slot, freed in free_staging_arena_blocks. Live probe: arena_outstanding 6->0 after full drain (5 commit + 1 dropped). New regression test committed_group_reclaims_all_arena_blocks; cleanup unit tests updated; full suite 8/8 green. Committed 49cc894.

title: ledger_submit_trx_c fails on multi-line single submission touching same pool twice
description: P4 (acct-2ttr.8) harness work surfaced a direct/routed asymmetry in ledger-v3.1 Path C. In ledger-direct-c bulk_write apply_pool_state_mutations pushes one aggregate UPSERT row per UpsertAggregate mutation, and ledger-core emits one UpsertAggregate per inventory line. So a single ledger_submit_trx_c submission whose lines list the same pool_id more than once produces duplicate (pool_id, layer_id=0) rows in the bulk INSERT ... ON CONFLICT (pool_id, layer_id) DO UPDATE, which Postgres rejects with: ON CONFLICT DO UPDATE command cannot affect row a second time. The routed committer is NOT affected: it processes a whole commit_group against one working snapshot and evidently coalesces to one aggregate mutation per pool (verified empirically: s7 routed ran 0-error with commit_group_avg 2.94 on a Zipf-concentrated hot-pool set, i.e. many submissions per group on the same pools). A real multi-line document for one SKU/location (same pool) would crash the direct SPI but succeed via routed. Fix options: (a) coalesce per-pool aggregate mutations in plan_apply_provisional / PlanResult so both paths emit one mutation per pool; (b) dedupe by (pool_id, layer_id) in apply_pool_state_mutations keeping the last mutation; (c) document distinct-pools-per-submission as a hard caller contract. The P4 harness already generates distinct pools per submission (matches design-v3.1 section 5.1 touched-pool dedup framing) so the harness is unblocked; this issue tracks the underlying direct/routed inconsistency.
acceptance_criteria: A single ledger_submit_trx_c submission with two lines on the same pool either succeeds (coalesced, aggregate reflects both lines) or the distinct-pools contract is documented in the SPI surface; direct and routed agree on the behavior.
close_reason: Fixed via approach (a): PlanResult::coalesce_aggregates() in ledger-core (commit d4c2c5c), called at end of plan_apply_provisional, collapses per-line UpsertAggregate to one-per-pool (keep-last = cumulative full-state). Direct two-line same-pool submission now succeeds with aggregate reflecting both lines; routed already coalesced via post-pass snapshot reconstruction and agrees. Acceptance criterion met (succeeds + coalesced + direct/routed agree). Tests: 2 ledger-core unit + 1 direct-c acceptance + 1 routed-c acceptance; full regression 7/7 binaries 34 tests green.

title: Reframe batch_window_us as primary cap, batch_size_max as soft safety bound
description:
Part B of acct-e5fz (Part A closed with measurement showing default bsm=50 is correct; see results/phase6/batch-size-tuning.md).

CONTEXT FROM PART A SWEEP:
The acct-e5fz sweep across batch_size_max ∈ {50, 200, 1000, 5000} on s2/s4/s5 routed AllWac surfaced two distinct problems with the size-cap-as-primary semantic:
1. s4 (zipf-1.2 complex) collapses 46% when raising bsm from 50 to 200, and 52% by bsm=1000. Mechanism: pipeline_ns_avg grows superlinearly with cg_size × lines_per_submission; pool lock-hold time blocks subsequent commit_groups. The cap protects this case at 50 and silently fails at higher values.
2. s5 (single hot pool) gains 25% throughput from bsm=5000 vs bsm=50 but pays 4× p99 ack latency (245ms vs 58ms). Caller-facing flows cannot afford this trade.

PROPOSAL (per parent issue's Part B framing):
Reframe the router emit decision:
- batch_window_us becomes PRIMARY cap. Router emits a commit_group when window elapses, with whatever accumulated.
- batch_size_max becomes a SOFT SAFETY CAP (e.g. 50000) to bound worst-case memory under spike load.
- Latency contract: submission queue residency ≤ batch_window_us + commit_time. Tunable per deployment.

EXPECTED OUTCOMES:
- s4 lock-hold runaway is naturally bounded by window time (not by submission count).
- s5 can grow commit_groups to whatever the window naturally produces (likely 100-200 at default 500us window based on Part A cg_avg).
- Hot-pool monopolization under aywu's per-pool no-split (the 'open question' from acct-aywu) is mitigated because the window-based emit bounds growth.

DESIGN OPEN QUESTIONS:
- GUC migration: add a new GUC switch (legacy size-primary vs new time-primary) for backwards compat, OR just flip the semantic and document? Greenfield code suggests just flip.
- batch_window_us default: currently 500us. May need re-tuning under the new semantic since the cap no longer fires.
- batch_size_max safety bound: 50000? 100000? Bounded by arena footprint.

ACCEPTANCE:
- router.rs emit decision uses window as primary, size as soft safety bound.
- Latency contract documented in design-v3.md or in the router module-doc.
- Re-run acct-e5fz sweep shape (s2/s4/s5 routed AllWac × {default, window=2ms, window=10ms}) post-change to confirm throughput parity and quantify latency contract.
- Doc: results/phase6/batch-window-tuning.md.

REFERENCES:
- acct-e5fz Part A — results/phase6/batch-size-tuning.md (closed 2026-05-24)
- acct-aywu — per-pool no-split fix; the 'hot-pool monopolization open question' is in scope here
- acct-9mgx.1 — surfaced the cm=1 throughput cost that started this thread
- ledger-routed/src/router.rs:229-280 — current emit-decision logic
close_reason: Reframe disproven by measurement. Single-session 10-cell resweep on s4 + s5 at bsm in {50, 1000, 5000, 10000, 50000} shows: s4 (complex) wins at bsm=50 with 576 tx/s, drops 46% above bsm=200 due to committer pipeline_ns runaway; s5 (hot pool simple) peaks at bsm=5000 with 2580 tx/s for +42% at 3.5x ack latency cost. No single default helps s5 without regressing s4. Shipped as partial reframe: default holds at bsm=50, GUC range max bumped 10000 -> 100000 for operator opt-in on hot-pool workloads, doc-comments updated. Doc: poc/ledger-v3/results/phase6/batch-window-reframe.md. No behavior change. Part A acct-e5fz recommendation (bsm=50 default) stands.

title: Replace spin-sleep with CV+broadcast in routed FIFO predecessor wait
description:
acct-tm09 ships per-pool sequence-number ordering with a spin-sleep wait when a committer's predecessor seq has not yet committed (100us interval, capped at committer_lease_ms). Spin-sleep is simple and correct but wastes CPU on long waits and occupies a committer slot when other committers could be doing unrelated work.

Replace with a PgLwLock + condition-variable per pool (or per N-bucket pools sharing a CV to bound shmem footprint). Committer waits via CV; committing committer broadcasts on each touched pool's CV after bumping latest_committed.

Trade-off: shmem layout grows with N CVs; committers wake from CV broadcasts only when predecessor commits.

Acceptance: routed FIFO throughput under cm=4 with high pool overlap shows reduced CPU% in committer BGWorkers (sampler observation) and equivalent or better throughput vs the spin-sleep baseline from tm09.

title: Re-evaluate batch_size_max default + reframe as time-window primary cap
description:
Default ledger_routed.batch_size_max = 50 inherited verbatim from queue-extension-v21 (lib.rs:81); never re-justified for v3. v21's own m8-ceiling bench raised it to 5000 for headline numbers (poc/queue-extension-v21/bench/results-m8-ceiling/README.md: "raised from 50 default during this issue"). At 50 the router emits many small commit_groups, each paying one fsync; throughput is capped by fsync count rather than the bulk-write efficiency the routed path is designed for.

This issue covers two related questions:

PART A — Re-tune the size cap:
After acct-aywu lands (per-pool no-split for order-sensitive methods), batch_size_max only affects WAC pools — order-sensitive pools are forced to single-group regardless. WAC is split-safe. Larger batch_size_max for WAC = more amortization = higher throughput, at the cost of larger per-commit memory + lock-hold time + arena footprint.

Sweep batch_size_max ∈ {50, 200, 1000, 5000} on s2/s4/s5 routed under AllWac, capture throughput + p99 ack latency + tail-latency. Pick the lowest value whose throughput doesn't materially trail the highest — preserves the safety margin the conservative default was protecting.

PART B — Reframe as time-window primary, size cap secondary:
batch_size_max as a HARD CAP couples throughput to a discrete count rather than to time. For latency-sensitive callers what matters is "how long does my submission sit in the queue before commit," which is naturally a TIME quantity. Reframe:

  - batch_window_us already exists as the router scan interval (default 500us). Today batch_size_max can fire BEFORE the window closes, fragmenting work into small commit_groups.
  - Proposed: batch_window_us becomes the primary cap. Router emits a commit_group when window elapses, with whatever's accumulated. batch_size_max becomes a SOFT SAFETY CAP (e.g. 50000) to bound worst-case memory under spike load — not the throughput cliff it is today.
  - Latency contract: submission queue residency ≤ batch_window_us + commit_time. Tunable per deployment.

DESIGN NOTES:
- Part A is the immediate measurement; can ship without Part B.
- Part B is a behavior change to the router's emit decision. May need a GUC switch (legacy mode = size-primary, new = time-primary) for backwards compat — or just flip the semantic and document.
- Part B interacts with acct-aywu: under per-pool no-split, time-window emit on a hot pool means one growing commit_group accumulates until the window fires, then drains as one giant group. Bounded by window time, not by submission count. May need acct-aywu's "open question" mitigation (bounded soft-split with happens-before edges).

ACCEPTANCE:
- Part A: sweep numbers + recommendation in results/phase6/batch-size-tuning.md, default updated if measurement supports.
- Part B: router emits on window-only (or window-primary with high soft cap); latency contract documented; bench shape from Part A re-run to confirm throughput parity.

REFERENCES:
- acct-9mgx.1 — surfaced the cm=1 throughput cost, motivated this followup
- acct-aywu — per-pool no-split fix; this issue follows it (acct-aywu's "open question" on hot-pool monopolization is in scope here under Part B)

title: WAC cumulative-sum: (qty_sum, value_sum) per pool
description:
Replace running-average (qty, unit_cost) storage with cumulative-sum (qty_sum, value_sum) for WAC pools. Eliminates receipt-side truncation compounding (root cause of acct-mcey drift); bounds remaining drift to single per-depletion rounding events that do not propagate into subsequent state.

MOTIVATION:
Current pool_state.unit_cost is computed as `(old_qty * old_uc + Q * C) / new_qty` on each receipt, then stored truncated. The truncated value is read back as `old_uc` on the next receipt, so error compounds linearly over receipt count on a shared pool. acct-mcey observed |Delta| <= 4 in human units across the equivalence sweep; acct-iwlq scaling reduced this to <= 0.0006 but did not eliminate the property.

APPROACH:
Store (qty_sum, value_sum) per WAC pool. Both BIGINT.
- Receipt of (Q, C): qty_sum += Q; value_sum += Q * C  [exact, no truncation]
- Depletion of Q: cost_out = round(Q * value_sum / qty_sum); qty_sum -= Q; value_sum -= cost_out
- Display unit_cost = value_sum / qty_sum on read

For receipt-only workloads (s5): zero drift forever.
For mixed workloads (s4): bounded depletion-side error, no compounding.

SCOPE:
- migration: add pool_state.value_sum BIGINT NULL (WAC-only; non-WAC methods leave NULL); back-fill is N/A (greenfield).
- ledger-core/src/wac.rs: rewrite apply_wac receipt branch; rewrite apply_depletion (still uses current avg = value_sum/qty_sum)
- ledger-core/src/snapshot.rs: PoolStateRow.value_sum: Option<i64>
- ledger-core tests/method_wac.rs: rewrite to assert (qty_sum, value_sum) invariants
- ledger-direct/src/hydration.rs + ledger-routed/src/hydration.rs: SELECT value_sum for WAC pools
- ledger-direct/src/bulk_write.rs + ledger-routed/src/bulk_write.rs: INSERT/UPSERT value_sum on WAC writes
- ledger-harness/src/equivalence.rs: compare value_sum as primary; rename wac_drifts bucket to depletion_round_drifts (now expected at single-event scale, not compounding)
- Re-validate via equivalence sweep; expect zero drift on s5 strict (receipt-only) and bounded depletion-side drift on s2/s4 strict

ALTERNATIVES:
1. i128/DECIMAL intermediate (same per-step rounding, no actual fix)
2. M=10000 multiplier (acct-iwlq, validated then discarded — band-aid)

VALIDATION ACCEPTANCE:
- equivalence --scenario s5 --strict: zero drift across 5 trials (receipt-only, must be exact)
- equivalence --scenario s2 --strict: bounded depletion drift, |Delta value_sum| < small constant per depletion (no compounding)
- All other scenarios: lenient pass; strict either passes or shows bounded non-compounding drift

CROSS-REF: acct-mcey (closed, surfaced the property), acct-iwlq (closed superseded, scaling band-aid).

title: WAC accuracy: scaled fixed-point unit_cost (multiplier)
description:
Follow-up to acct-mcey. acct-mcey tolerates WAC running-avg truncation drift in the equivalence test; this issue REDUCES the drift by carrying unit_cost in higher-precision fixed-point.

PROBLEM:
WAC stores unit_cost as integer dollars (or some base unit) in pool_state. Each per-submission update computes:
  new_uc = (old_qty * old_uc + new_qty * new_uc) / (old_qty + new_qty)
Integer division truncates the fractional remainder. Over many updates the truncation accumulates. Under Path B multi-committer reordering, the accumulation diverges from Path A by bounded but visible amounts (1-unit drift observed on s5/s2 reproducers — see acct-mcey).

APPROACH (per user direction):
Treat unit_cost as a scaled fixed-point value. Multiplier M = 10^N (e.g. 100 for cents, 10000 for microcents). Storage and arithmetic stays BIGINT — only the INTERPRETATION changes: $0.93 stored as 9300 (M=10000) instead of 93 (M=1).

Each WAC step:
  new_uc_scaled = (old_qty * old_uc_scaled + new_qty * new_uc_scaled) / (old_qty + new_qty)
Truncation still happens but at the scaled precision — drift per step is now ~1/M of the original. With M=10000, a 1-unit drift in old units becomes a 0.0001-unit drift in new units; 1000 truncations accumulate to bounded drift well within the M precision.

CHANGES:
- Schema: no column type change (BIGINT stays BIGINT); update column comments to document the scale.
- ledger-core: WAC math reads/writes scaled values; expose unscaled value as a derived view at read time.
- Bulk-write helpers: unit_cost stored scaled; debit/credit posting_line amounts likewise scaled if they derive from unit_cost × qty.
- Reports / equivalence: divide by M when comparing or displaying.
- pool_universe seeder: keep input unit_costs in current units; scale at insert.
- Workload generator: same.

GATE QUESTION (decide during impl):
- M = 100 (cents)?
- M = 10000 (basis points)?
- Higher (microcents, M=1,000,000)? — overflow risk on (old_qty * old_uc_scaled) when qty in millions and uc in thousands of dollars × 10^6: 10^6 × 10^9 = 10^15, still within BIGINT range (9.2 × 10^18) but worth checking the worst-case workload.

ALTERNATIVES CONSIDERED:
1. Cumulative sum approach: store (qty_sum, value_sum) per WAC pool instead of (qty, unit_cost). Order-independent — eliminates truncation drift entirely. Bigger schema change; affects all WAC code paths.
2. i128 / DECIMAL intermediate: keep BIGINT storage, use higher precision during computation. Same per-step truncation; just no overflow concerns.

The multiplier approach is the smallest change with meaningful precision improvement. The cumulative-sum alternative (#1) is the most rigorous if drift bound matters more than schema stability.

VALIDATION:
After landing, re-run `equivalence --scenario s5 --strict` repeatedly. Drift should be unobservable at typical workloads (M chosen so per-step drift × max_drains_per_pool < 1 in the scaled unit).
close_reason: Superseded by cumulative-sum WAC approach. M=10000 multiplier was validated (max human-unit drift 0.0006 across 15-run sweep, 4 orders of magnitude below pre-scale baseline) but is a precision band-aid: WAC running-avg truncation property still exists at finer grain, --strict still race-conditional. Cumulative-sum stores (qty_sum, value_sum) directly per pool, making receipts exact additive ops; eliminates compounding error from receipts entirely, bounds depletion-side error to single non-compounding events. Strictly better correctness for ~2x the touch points. Filing follow-up issue for cumulative-sum implementation. iwlq work was uncommitted; restored cleanly.

title: WAC running-avg truncation drift under multi-committer reordering
description:
Discovered during acct-t9lo equivalence subcommand validation.

WHAT: Path Bs multi-committer concurrent commit_group draining can reorder commit_groups touching the same WAC pool when they hit pool_lock in different order than submission arrival. Per-submission integer truncation in WAC running-average computation accumulates differently — pool_state.unit_cost drifts by plus-or-minus 1 vs Path As strict-sequential equivalent.

REPRODUCER:
- equivalence --scenario s5 (single hot pool, 1000 submissions, 2 committers)
- Diff: pool_state[pool=1] A.unit_cost=249 vs B.unit_cost=248
- Total qty exact (52101 = 52101). Total value preserved within rounding.
- Same shape on s2 (Zipf-1.5 head concentration): 1-unit unit_cost drift.

DOES NOT AFFECT:
- s1 (uniform across 100 pools — committer collision on same pool rare)
- s6 (disjoint stripes — no overlap)
- FIFO/LIFO/STD pools (no running-avg, no truncation accumulation)

BOUNDED BY: drift at most 1 per reordering boundary; cumulative bound = number of distinct commit_groups serializing on the pool.

ROOT CAUSE: WAC integer-truncation order-dependence. The per-submission formula new_uc = (old_qty * old_uc + new_qty * new_uc) / (old_qty + new_qty) uses integer division; truncation discards fractional bits. Order [A,B,C] gives different cumulative U than [B,A,C].

This is a property of WAC arithmetic, NOT a Path B implementation bug. Path A is order-deterministic because submissions serialize through one tx; Path B is order-non-deterministic across commit_groups because multiple committers race.

OPTIONS FOR acct-33b6 (cross-path equivalence run for S1-S6):
1. Force ledger_routed.committer_count = 1 for equivalence runs. Makes Path B deterministic. Requires postmaster restart (GucContext::PostmasterStart).
2. Tolerance-based diff: allow plus-or-minus N unit_cost on WAC pool_state rows.
3. Compute value equivalence — diff (qty, qty * unit_cost) instead of (qty, unit_cost).
4. Restrict equivalence runs to FIFO/LIFO/STD method mixes (acct-llt2 --method-mix already supports AllFifo).

acct-t9lo equivalence subcommand ships with trx_seq excluded and this WAC issue deferred — meets bd description acceptance gate (cargo run -- equivalence --scenario s1 exits 0). acct-33b6 picks an option above and runs S1-S6.
close_reason: Hybrid mitigation shipped per user choice. Equivalence diff classifies pool_state mismatches by pool method; WAC unit_cost diffs become wac_drifts (informational, dont fail exit code); non-WAC mismatches stay errors. New --strict flag upgrades wac_drifts to errors for single-committer byte-equivalence scenarios. Doesnt mask non-WAC bugs; tests realistic multi-committer Path B; surfaces drift for audit. Underlying WAC precision improvement filed as acct-iwlq (scaled fixed-point unit_cost via integer multiplier, per user direction). 25/25 harness unit tests green.

title: io_uring + high max_connections memlock ceiling in dev container
description:
Bumping max_connections to 1100 (target for full §11 1000-caller run) against PG18 io_method=io_uring fails container startup with 'could not setup io_uring queue: Cannot allocate memory'. Each backend pre-allocates its io_uring submission/completion queues at startup and the container's RLIMIT_MEMLOCK is exhausted at that backend count. Surfaced in acct-7wye 2026-05-21; tune-pg-for-phase3.sh now defaults to TARGET=500 (fits 200 callers + sampler + collector + headroom).

Two paths to land:
  (a) Raise RLIMIT_MEMLOCK on the acct-postgres container (docker-compose ulimits.memlock = -1 or a finite increase) so backends can each lock their io_uring queues. Keeps io_uring as the production-target IO path per CLAUDE.md.
  (b) Add a --io-method flag to scripts/run-phase3-measurements.sh that ALTER SYSTEMs io_method=worker for the run window then reverts. Lets the measurement use 1000 callers without raising memlock, but the resulting numbers won't reflect production io_uring behavior.

Recommend (a) — io_uring is the chosen DB config per the project decision; the measurement should reflect production. Verify the container's docker-compose service definition under /home/kaalin/dev/acct/docker-compose.yml (or wherever acct-postgres is declared), set ulimits.memlock: -1, recreate the container, re-run tune-pg-for-phase3.sh with TARGET=1100 and the full §11 run. NOTE: recreating the container reads from the host-mounted /home/kaalin/dev/acct/db/postgresql.conf and the postgresql.auto.conf in the data volume — settings persist.
notes:
RESUME / START HERE (take acct-8cn2 next — prepared at compaction). This is a SHARED dev-container infra change, NOT a ledger-v3.1-isolated task. Surfaced by the ledger-v3 (Path A/B) Phase 3 work (acct-7wye), not ledger-v3.1.

WHERE THINGS STAND (ledger-v3.1 stream is DONE):
- Epic acct-2ttr CLOSED. All build phases + P5 report shipped. Follow-ups acct-036x (direct/routed same-pool UPSERT, commit d4c2c5c) and acct-0z5m (harness std_cost seeding, commit 9b6e6b5) both CLOSED. P5 report at poc/ledger-v3.1/results/POC-REPORT.md (committed; results/*.json + *.log gitignored).
- acct-8cn2 is the LAST non-PAUSE ready item. Worktree clean. pgbouncer torn down. DB acct-postgres healthy.
- BD worktree gotcha: if bd shows 0 issues, recreate .beads/redirect=../../../.beads; never bd init.

THE PROBLEM (from the description): max_connections=1100 (target for a full 1000-direct-caller run) + PG18 io_method=io_uring fails container startup with "could not setup io_uring queue: Cannot allocate memory" — each backend pre-allocates io_uring submission/completion queues and the container RLIMIT_MEMLOCK is exhausted. tune-pg-for-phase3.sh defaults TARGET=500 to dodge it.

CURRENT MEASURED STATE (verified at compaction):
- acct-postgres memlock ulimit: 8192 (KB) = 8 MB. docker inspect shows NO explicit Ulimits => this is Docker's default; the compose service has no ulimits entry, so one must be ADDED.
- max_connections=500, io_method=io_uring (confirmed live).
- docker-compose.yml exists in BOTH /home/kaalin/dev/acct/docker-compose.yml AND the worktree .claude/worktrees/poc-31/docker-compose.yml (both 751 bytes). MUST determine which launched the live container before editing — check `docker inspect acct-postgres` labels (com.docker.compose.project.working_dir / config_files) or `docker compose ls`. Edit the authoritative one (likely the main repo); the worktree copy may be a stale duplicate.
- Phase3 scripts referenced by the issue live in poc/ledger-v3/scripts/ (tune-pg-for-phase3.sh, run-phase3-measurements.sh) — the OTHER stream. NOT poc/ledger-v3.1.

NOT BLOCKING ledger-v3.1: the ledger-v3.1 1000-caller scenarios (S5/S7/S8) already route through pgbouncer (host 6432, validated in P5), which multiplexes 1000 logical callers onto ~64 backends and sidesteps memlock entirely. acct-8cn2 is about enabling DIRECT 1000+ backend runs (matters mainly for ledger-v3 Phase 3, and as the production-posture infra fix).

TWO PATHS (issue enumerates; SURFACE the choice + the shared-container risk to the user BEFORE acting):
(a) RECOMMENDED by the issue + keeps io_uring (production target per CLAUDE.md): add ulimits.memlock to the acct-postgres compose service (memlock: -1, or a finite bump e.g. 8GB), recreate the container, re-run with TARGET=1100. The measurement then reflects production io_uring behavior.
(b) Add a --io-method flag to poc/ledger-v3/scripts/run-phase3-measurements.sh that ALTER SYSTEM io_method=worker for the run window then reverts — lets 1000 callers run without raising memlock, BUT numbers won't reflect production io_uring.

WHY THIS NEEDS A USER CHECK FIRST (do NOT just execute):
1. Design choice (a) vs (b) — per the surface-design-choices discipline, the issue enumerates options; confirm (a) (recommended) vs (b) with the user.
2. SHARED CONTAINER: acct-postgres is used by EVERY stream (ledger-v3, ledger-v3.1, queue-extension-v21, the main acct project) + any in-flight work. `docker compose down/up` or recreate disrupts all of them and drops connections. Confirm nothing else is mid-run and the user is OK recreating the shared container.

FIX STEPS for (a) once approved:
- Identify the authoritative docker-compose.yml (docker inspect labels). Read its postgres/acct-postgres service block.
- Add under that service:  ulimits:\n    memlock: -1   (YAML; docker-compose supports `memlock: -1` for unlimited, or `memlock: { soft: N, hard: N }`). Mirror existing seccomp:unconfined style already in the file (the container already runs seccomp:unconfined for io_uring per CLAUDE.md / acct-hbp).

Recreating reads host-mounted db/postgresql.conf + the data-volume postgresql.auto.conf — settings persist; data persists (volume mount).
- Verify: `docker exec acct-postgres sh -c 'ulimit -l'` is raised (or `unlimited`); `SHOW io_method` still io_uring; `pg_isready`.
- Test the actual fix: bump max_connections to 1100 (ALTER SYSTEM SET max_connections=1100 then restart, OR poc/ledger-v3 tune-pg-for-phase3.sh TARGET=1100) and confirm the container/PG starts with NO "could not setup io_uring queue" error. Optionally a high-direct-backend smoke. Then revert max_connections to a sane default (500) if 1100 isn't wanted as the standing value — or leave per user pref.

ACCEPTANCE (implied): container starts cleanly at max_connections=1100 with io_method=io_uring (memlock no longer the ceiling); the chosen path documented. If (b) chosen instead: the --io-method flag works and is documented as non-production-representative.

GOTCHAS: shared container (coordinate); recreate persists settings via host-mounted conf + auto.conf; restart-docker etiquette; CLAUDE.md notes production memlock hardening is acct-hbp (cross-ref); commit convention <id>: <title> + HEREDOC body + Co-Authored-By trailer, no push; single-quote bd reasons w/ backticks; NO time estimates; greenfield-no-mixed-mode (no cutover patterns). Plan file: ~/.claude/plans/formulate-a-detailed-plan-lucky-dijkstra.md.

close_reason: Added ulimits.memlock: -1 to the postgres service in /home/kaalin/dev/acct/docker-compose.yml (committed e4668a1 on main). Verified: container recreate gives ulimit -l = unlimited; PG boots healthy at max_connections=1100 with io_method=io_uring and no "could not setup io_uring queue" error. Standing max_connections restored to 500 (per-run tunable now that memlock is not the ceiling). Path (a) per user. Note: the --force-recreate wiped all 5 runtime-installed pgrx preload .so (ledger_extension, poc_ledger, poc_v21_ledger, ledger_routed, ledger_routed_c) plus the 2 direct .so; rebuilt/restored all and the shared container is back to prior working state with all 7 databases + data intact.

title: WAL: tune max_wal_size, checkpoint_timeout, wal_buffers, wal_writer settings for STD bench
description:
## Context

WAL is 72% of backend wait in the STD-receipt bench. Constraint: synchronous_commit STAYS ON (durability non-negotiable). Within that envelope, WAL infrastructure tuning is the remaining knob.

Current cluster (postgres:18, io_method=io_uring, dev defaults) likely has stock values for the WAL-related GUCs. Worth a sweep before declaring the WAL ceiling.

## Knobs to sweep

| GUC | default | rationale |
|-----|--------:|-----------|
| `max_wal_size` | 1GB | larger → less frequent checkpoint → fewer FPIs → less WAL bytes |
| `checkpoint_timeout` | 5min | longer → same as above (FPI-reduction) |
| `wal_buffers` | -1 (auto, ~16MB) | larger → fewer flushes from wal_writer; less wait_event LWLock/WALWrite |
| `wal_writer_delay` | 200ms | how often wal_writer wakes to flush completed records |
| `wal_writer_flush_after` | 1MB | flush threshold — interacts with wal_writer_delay |
| `commit_delay` | 0 | group-commit delay (small wins, niche) |
| `commit_siblings` | 5 | min concurrent xacts before commit_delay applies |
| `wal_log_hints` | off | enables FPI on hint bit updates; needed for some compression effectiveness |

## Methodology

1. Capture current values (`SHOW <guc>` for each).
2. Establish baseline: bench at current settings K=5+warm with full telemetry capture (stage timings, pg_stat_statements, sampler).
3. Sweep one knob at a time (NOT compound): change one GUC via ALTER SYSTEM, restart-or-reload, rerun. Compound effects investigated only after individual baselines.
4. Headline metric: e2e_evps median + % reduction in LWLock/WALWrite samples.
5. Stop sweeping a knob when diminishing returns are apparent (typically 2-3 values per knob).

## Acceptance

- Baseline (current settings) recorded for diff comparison.
- Each knob swept independently, K=5+warm per cell.
- Results table: GUC value vs e2e_evps median vs WAL wait % vs CV.
- v21 acceptance suite passes at the winning combination.
- Decision: persist winning combination as ALTER SYSTEM (with rationale + bench reference in the commit message), OR document that defaults are already optimal for this workload.

## Risks

- max_wal_size growth pushes recovery time up. At ~50MB WAL/100k bench run, max_wal_size=4GB is ~80x the steady-state emission rate — should still be acceptable recovery.
- wal_buffers larger than 1/32 of shared_buffers is wasteful; current shared_buffers needs checking before bumping.
- checkpoint_timeout up to 30min is documented-safe; beyond that requires testing recovery from controlled crashes.

## Cross-refs

- Related: acct-3lwo (status_insert_mode), acct-380c (wal_compression). Probably want acct-380c landed before this sweep — compression may shift the WAL byte volume and change the knob sensitivities.
- Comprehensive telemetry summary: this session's WAL emitter ranking + sampler wait-event distribution.
notes:
Pre-inventory of /etc/postgresql/postgresql.conf (modified 2026-05-17) shows the major knobs are already tuned:

| GUC                          | Current   | Default | Status   |
|------------------------------|-----------|---------|----------|
| max_wal_size                 | 8GB       | 1GB     | TUNED    |
| min_wal_size                 | 2GB       | 80MB    | TUNED    |
| checkpoint_timeout           | 15min     | 5min    | TUNED    |
| checkpoint_completion_target | 0.9       | 0.9     | (default == tuned) |
| wal_buffers                  | 64MB      | -1/16MB | TUNED    |
| wal_compression              | lz4       | off     | TUNED (verified neutral per acct-380c) |
| commit_delay                 | 20µs      | 0       | TUNED    |
| commit_siblings              | 5         | 5       | (default == tuned) |
| wal_writer_delay             | 200ms     | 200ms   | DEFAULT  |
| wal_writer_flush_after       | 1MB       | 1MB     | DEFAULT  |
| wal_log_hints                | off       | off     | DEFAULT (correct; enabling adds FPI bytes) |
| synchronous_commit           | on        | on      | locked by user mandate |

Decision: closing as already-applied.

Rationale for not sweeping the remaining defaults (wal_writer_delay, wal_writer_flush_after):
acct-380c confirmed the workload is fsync-bound (count of commits), not WAL-byte-bound (bytes per commit). wal_writer parameters govern background flush cadence of completed records — they help when WALWrite latency is the bottleneck. Per acct-380c sampler distribution, LWLock/WALWrite samples were ~280 across all three compression settings with identical e2e throughput. If compression CPU additions don't move e2e, smaller wal_writer flush windows won't either — they shift WAL write timing, not the fsync count that gates commit latency.

wal_log_hints stays OFF intentionally — turning it ON would create FPIs on hint-bit updates, INCREASING WAL volume. Inverse of the desired direction.

Reopen if: (a) commit eliminations from acct-3lwo expose new wait_event types that fs83 knobs would address, (b) workload shifts to FPI-heavy (bulk updates, page-aged buffers), (c) a structured test reveals checkpoint pressure from increased throughput.

Current ceiling: clean Docker restart + committed optimization stack ⇒ ~8200 evps median, CV ~1-2%.
close_reason: All major WAL knobs already tuned in /etc/postgresql/postgresql.conf. Remaining defaults (wal_writer_*, wal_log_hints) don't address the fsync-bound bottleneck per acct-380c finding.

title: WAL: enable wal_compression and measure throughput lift on STD bench
description:
## Context

WAL is 72% of backend wait in the STD-receipt bench (LWLock/WALWrite 62% + IO/WalSync 10% + IO/WalWrite 1% per pg_stat_activity sampling). User-stated constraint: synchronous_commit MUST stay ON — durability is not negotiable.

`wal_compression` is the cheapest knob in this constraint envelope. PG 18 supports `pglz | lz4 | zstd` (default off). It compresses full-page images (the bulk of WAL volume after checkpoint) and, with `wal_log_hints=on`, also routine record bytes via FPI piggybacking.

## Proposed change

1. ALTER SYSTEM SET wal_compression = 'lz4' (or 'zstd' — sweep both)
2. Restart postgres (this GUC is postmaster-scope)
3. Re-run the optimal-cell bench with K=5+warm + telemetry capture
4. Compare:
   - e2e_evps (median, CV)
   - pipeline_total stage timings
   - pg_stat_statements WAL emit (rows = bytes written; total_exec_time correlates with WAL wait)
   - pg_locks_sampler wait_event distribution (% reduction in WALWrite samples is the headline)

## Expected impact

Modest. Compression helps full-page images most; the bench workload has ~100k small INSERTs (~80B rows + indexes ≈ ~300B/envelope). FPIs only occur post-checkpoint and on first-touch pages. Realistic estimate: 3-8% e2e lift on this workload; potentially higher under different checkpoint cadence.

## Acceptance

- Bench at lz4 + zstd vs default off, K=5+warm at the optimal cell.
- Stage timings + pg_stat_statements + sampler report captured for each setting.
- v21 acceptance suite passes under wal_compression=lz4 (and zstd if measured).
- Decision: keep default OR switch to lz4/zstd + document the call.

## Cross-refs

- Comprehensive telemetry summary: this session's WAL emitter ranking.
- Related: acct-3lwo (status_insert_mode investigation), WAL tuning sweep (filed separately).
notes:
Bench sweep at clean Docker restart, K=5+warm, optimal cell (counts=100000 spread=100 normal ingress=5 rsb=5000, GUCs: batch_window_us=500 batch_size_max=5000 drain_batch_size=2 status_insert_mode=caller_intx, synchronous_commit=on):

| wal_compression | e2e median | CV    | LWLock/WALWrite mean | IO/WalSync mean |
|-----------------|-----------:|------:|---------------------:|----------------:|
| off             | 8242       | 1.2%  | 281.8                | 31.0            |
| lz4             | 8142       | 2.6%  | 273.8                | 35.4            |
| zstd            | 8267       | 1.4%  | 288.6                | 33.8            |

Range 8142-8267 = 1.5%, well inside per-config CV. Three settings are statistically indistinguishable for this workload.

Root cause: PG wal_compression only compresses full-page images (FPI). Small-row INSERT-heavy workloads emit very few FPIs (low buffer-touch ratio per WAL record). The compressor has nothing to bite into.

Decision: keep wal_compression=lz4 as configured in /etc/postgresql/postgresql.conf. No worse than off for this workload; would help mixed workloads with more FPI traffic.

IMPLICATION: WAL-bottleneck framing is fsync-bound, not byte-bound — count of commits matters, bytes per commit doesn't. Shifts attention to acct-3lwo (status_insert_mode caller_intx → committer_lazy collapses one caller-side commit per envelope).

Additional finding: clean Docker restart yields ~8200 evps baseline. Prior session's '7180' baseline was contaminated by host CPU load (Chrome ~50% per session memo). The committed optimization stack (a2sj/ed7u/0sc4) plus clean state is the real current ceiling pre-3lwo.
close_reason: Swept off/lz4/zstd at clean state — all within 1.5%, indistinguishable. Keeping lz4. Workload is fsync-bound not byte-bound. See notes.

title: WAL: investigate status_insert_mode=caller_intx vs committer_lazy default + measure
description:
## Context

Comprehensive telemetry capture (acct-0sc4 follow-on) found that `caller_intx` is the GUC default for `poc_v21.status_insert_mode` and is what the bench has been running with. pg_stat_statements shows:

  20,000 calls  4,908ms total  245µs mean  100k rows  INSERT submission_status (enqueue side)
  14,490 calls  4,247ms total  293µs mean  100k rows  INSERT submission_status (Step 12 UPSERT)

The enqueue-side INSERT is 4.9s of total exec time across the run plus its share of WAL emission (~50% of submission_status WAL). The committer Step 12 path does an UPSERT regardless, so the enqueue row is redundant work for the throughput-optimized hot path.

## Hypotheses to verify

1. **Default mode was meant to be `committer_lazy`** but stayed `caller_intx` for historical reasons. Decision rationale unknown without git-log archaeology.
2. **`committer_lazy` requires `persistent_staging=on`** per startup validation. Current cluster has persistent_staging=on but bench uses `durable_queue: false` at the per-envelope level — no rows land in persistent_staging at enqueue time. Step 12's `INSERT ... ON CONFLICT DO UPDATE` still creates the terminal-state row, so polling still works. Verify with a test run that polling latency stays bounded.
3. **Why the prior session claimed committer_lazy was set via ALTER SYSTEM but auto.conf only has batch_size_max=5000**. Either the memo was wrong, or the setting was lost during a session reset. Confirm by setting it explicitly and re-running the bench.

## Expected impact

WAL emitter ranks:
  posting_lines INSERT: 3,464ms total (~25% of submission_status)
  posting_line_inventory INSERT: 3,142ms
  submission_status enqueue INSERT: 4,908ms  <-- caller_intx-only
  submission_status Step 12 UPSERT: 4,247ms

Removing the enqueue-side INSERT eliminates ~50% of submission_status WAL emission and ~5% of total WAL bytes. Throughput lift depends on how WAL-bound the workload is — at current measurements, WAL waits are 72% of backend time.
