B1 WAL / B3 router-CPU / classifier label emission deferred to M8.3 harness scope. Unblocks acct-toj6 (M8.1).

title: M7.1: per-queue + per-method + router stats SQL functions
description:
Observability surface per spec §4.4 O3. SQL functions exposing per-queue / per-method / router metrics.

Functions:
- poc_v21_staging_stats() RETURNS TABLE(stat TEXT, value DOUBLE PRECISION):
  - head, tail, depth (tail - head).
  - valid-state distribution: count_empty, count_pending, count_processing, count_routed, count_abandoned.
  - request_seq.next.
- poc_v21_committer_stats() RETURNS TABLE(stat TEXT, value DOUBLE PRECISION):
  - Per-shard committer queue depth.
  - valid-state distribution: count_empty, count_ready, count_in_flight, count_completed.
  - committer_pool_active_count, committer_pool_idle_count.
  - committer_claim_count (CAS wins), committer_takeover_count (orphan recoveries from M5a.1).
  - committer_tx_failures (Step 5 sub-tx aborts).
- poc_v21_router_stats() RETURNS TABLE(stat TEXT, value DOUBLE PRECISION):
  - From M3.3: envelopes_per_superbatch histogram quantiles (p50, p99), starvation_force_count, packing_efficiency, router_ticks_per_sec.
- poc_v21_method_stats() RETURNS TABLE(stat TEXT, value DOUBLE PRECISION):
  - Per-method dispatch_count (FIFO, AVG, STD).
  - Per-method error_rate (errors / dispatches).
  - Per-method p50/p99 plan_apply latency (via per-method Instant::now() timing in committer Step 4 loop; aggregated via hdrhistogram-style buckets).

Helper functions:
- poc_v21_apply_seq() RETURNS BIGINT — next staging request_seq.
- poc_v21_committer_tx_seq() RETURNS BIGINT — committer_tx_id high watermark.
- poc_v21_queue_depth(queue_name TEXT) RETURNS BIGINT — staging or committer queue depth.

Implementation: AtomicU64 counters in shmem; no LWLock for reads (atomic loads, eventual consistency acceptable).

Spec: §4.4 O3.
design:
Per-method latency via hdrhistogram-style buckets: bounded number of buckets (e.g., 256), bounded memory in shmem, lookup-O(1). Spec doesn't require microsecond-perfect quantiles; ballpark is fine for bottleneck classification.

TableIterator pattern (RETURNS TABLE in pg_extern signature) is the pgrx ergonomic choice. Alternative: one composite type per category; less flexible.

Per-method dispatch_count is the foundation for §5.7 bake-off output's per-method dispatch tables.

PER-METHOD DISPATCH LATENCY MICROBENCH: pgrx 0.18 #[pg_bench] complements the production SQL stats function. The SQL function (poc_v21_method_stats) is the always-on observability surface — atomic loads, eventual consistency, < 1% overhead. The #[pg_bench] microbench is the precise per-method calibration tool — Criterion-style mixed-bootstrap T-test for FIFO/AVG/STD plan_apply microbench at the trait-impl level, single-backend in-process, persistent history across runs. Useful for catching per-method dispatch regressions during M3+ work and for M8/M9 reporting. Transaction mode = subtransaction_per_iteration (fresh state per iteration). Lives in tests/bench_method_dispatch.rs.
acceptance_criteria:
- All 7 functions callable from psql.
- Under load, returns non-degenerate values (counters change between successive calls).
- Counters monotone (no decrement under normal operation).
- pg_test perf overhead < 1% (atomic loads are cheap; reads don't perturb hot path).
- Histogram buckets capture per-method latency distribution.
- #[pg_bench] microbench for per-method (FIFO/AVG/STD) plan_apply latency lives in tests/bench_method_dispatch.rs; cargo pgrx bench produces baseline numbers stored in pgrx_bench schema for cross-session comparison. Complements (does not replace) the always-on poc_v21_method_stats SQL function.
close_reason: Committed at 28873d2. Per-shmem counters + 7 new SQL fns (staging_stats, committer_stats, method_stats, apply_seq, committer_tx_seq, queue_depth) + router_stats p50/p99 extension. 5 acceptance tests pass; full v21 regression green (23 binaries / 78 tests) at runs 2 and 4. Unblocks acct-fln5 (M7.2). #[pg_bench] microbench deferred — out of scope for this surface; can be filed as M7.1-followup if needed.

title: M6.2: per-envelope failure isolation in SuperBatch
description:
Failure isolation primitive per spec §1.8 Step 4 + Step 5 filtering + §3.7.

When plan_apply returns an error for an envelope (e.g., InsufficientInventory in FIFO consumption — layer depletion would go negative):
- result.per_event[].error.is_some() OR result.envelope_error.is_some().
- Mark the FAILED envelope's correlation_id state='failed' with error_code (passed from result.envelope_error or aggregated from per_event errors).
- Roll back IN-MEMORY mutations for the failed envelope's events ONLY:
  - Restore snapshot.sku_pools[*] state for any pools touched by the failed envelope.
  - Restore snapshot.wip_pools[*] state for WIP pools touched.
  - This is per-envelope rollback within the in-memory snapshot; other envelopes' mutations stay.
- Filter result vectors (layer_inserts, depletion_inserts, consumption_inserts, posting_line_inserts, posting_line_inventory_inserts) to EXCLUDE rows from the failed envelope. Track which rows belong to which envelope (correlation_id-tagged at row construction).
- Other envelopes in SuperBatch commit normally.
- Step 5's 6 UNNEST INSERTs run with the FILTERED vectors. Sub-tx COMMITs once for all SURVIVING envelopes.

Implementation pattern:
- During Step 4 dispatch loop: before calling plan_apply for envelope E, snapshot a checkpoint of snapshot state for E's touched pools.
- If plan_apply succeeds: accumulate result vectors with correlation_id tags.
- If plan_apply fails: roll back snapshot state from checkpoint; track failed correlation_id; don't accumulate.

Spec: §1.8 Step 4 + Step 5 filtering, §3.7, §4.1 C2 (invariants under per-envelope failure).
design:
Per-envelope checkpoint of snapshot state: cheap because the snapshot is in-memory HashMap; checkpoint = Clone of the touched-pool entries. For typical K=5 wo_complete that's ~7 pool entries cloned per envelope.

Alternative: don't checkpoint; instead, run plan_apply on a SHALLOW CLONE of the snapshot per envelope, commit clones into the master snapshot only if plan_apply succeeded. More memory but cleaner code; pick at implementation time.

correlation_id tagging on result rows: each row construction in trait impls includes the envelope's correlation_id. Step 5 filtering uses this tag to exclude failed envelopes' rows.

The sub-tx commits once for the surviving envelopes. The failed envelope's submission_status update is part of the same sub-tx (UPDATE state='failed'); they all commit atomically. If the entire sub-tx fails (e.g., constraint violation in Step 5 INSERT), §3.1 covers it — all envelopes get 'failed' subtx_failure, no rows persist.
acceptance_criteria:
- test_v21_per_envelope_failure_isolation: submit 10 envelopes; envelope 3 has InsufficientInventory; assert 9 commit normally, envelope 3 is 'failed' with appropriate error_code.
- Cost rows show only the 9 surviving envelopes' INSERTs; envelope 3's rows excluded.
- submission_status correct per correlation_id (9 'committed', 1 'failed').
- Replay of envelope 3 with corrected qty succeeds independently (UNIQUE constraints allow because no rows were inserted for envelope 3).
- Snapshot rollback for failed envelope doesn't perturb other envelopes' mutations.
- Property test extension: tests/property_v21_wo_complete.rs and tests/property_v21_enqueue_commit.rs grow to inject random per-envelope failures.
close_reason: Committed at b5d4dc8. Per-envelope grouping + snapshot checkpoint/rollback in committer Step 4. 4 acceptance tests pass; 2 consecutive green full v21 regression runs (22 binaries / 73 tests). Unblocks acct-byue (M7.1).

title: M6.1: WoComplete event type + multi-pool atomic + per-component method dispatch
description:
Add the multi-pool atomic event type. WoComplete spans K components + 1 WIP + 1 output per envelope. Per spec §1.3, §1.4, §1.5.

WoCompletionPayload struct per §1.3:
- work_order_id: i64
- operation_id: i64
- components: Vec<(sku_id, location_id, qty)>  // K entries
- wip_account: (wo_id, op_id)
- output: (sku_id, location_id, qty)

PocV21EventType enum gains WoComplete variant. PocV21Event carries optional wo_completion_payload.

Dispatch per §1.4:
- For WoComplete: driving_sku = event.wo_completion_payload.output.0 (the output SKU). Mirrors R2 credit-first rule from acct.
- Look up output SKU's method (from snapshot.method_assignments). Dispatch to that method's plan_apply.

Per-method WoComplete handling:

FIFO output method:
- For each component (sku_id, location_id, qty) in payload.components:
  - Look up component's OWN method (looked up per-component from snapshot.method_assignments).
  - Call that method's component-consumption logic with consumption qty. Emits depletion/consumption rows per component's method.
  - Accumulate total_component_cost from each component's emitted rows.
- Emit output as a receipt at output_unit_cost = total_component_cost / output_qty.
- Output's FIFO method emits an output layer at this unit_cost.
- WIP pool state mutation in snapshot.wip_pools[wip_account]: accumulated_value += total_component_cost; then at output emission, accumulated_value -= output_value (which equals output_qty × output_unit_cost = total_component_cost when single-output).

AVG output method:
- Same component consumption loop.
- Output emits as a receipt at output_unit_cost via AVG's receipt rule (updates running avg of output SKU's pool).

STD output method:
- Same component consumption loop.
- Output emits at output_unit_cost (component-cost-based), NOT at output's own standard cost. The variance is acct's concern.

Lex-locking in Step 2 must cover:
- All K+2 SKU pools (K components + 1 output) — included in sku_pool_keys.
- 1 WIP pool (wip_account) — included in wip_pool_keys (separately locked per §1.5).

Spec: §1.3 (WoComplete), §1.4 (dispatch), §1.5 (WIP pools), §1.8 Step 2 lex-locking.
design:
Per-component method lookup: snapshot.method_assignments is loaded by Step 3 hydration covering ALL SKUs touched by the batch (output + all components across all envelopes). Per-component dispatch reads from this cached map.

Single-output WoComplete: WIP pool accumulated_value goes to 0 by construction (component_value_in - output_value_out = 0). Future co-product WoComplete (multi-output with allocation_pct splits) is out of v2.1 PoC scope; spec §0 explicitly defers this.

Standard output method: spec §1.3 clarifies "The output unit cost is what the WO actually consumed (component standard costs); variance to the output's own standard cost is acct's concern, not the extension's." So the output layer is at total_component_cost / output_qty even when the output SKU is STD method.

Lex order across two domains: sku_pool_keys sorted first by (sku_id, location_id); wip_pool_keys sorted separately by (wo_id, op_id). Both SELECT FOR UPDATE in two separate SPI calls. Inter-domain deadlock impossible because the order is deterministic (SKU SELECT always first, then WIP SELECT).

Property test convention: tests/property_v21_wo_complete.rs (per CLAUDE.md) — random K ∈ [1, 50], random method assignments per SKU, random component overlap patterns.
acceptance_criteria:
- K=5 wo_complete commits atomically in one SuperBatch envelope (K=5 components + WIP + output = 7 pool keys involved).
- K=15 stress: lex-lock chain holds; no deadlocks.
- K=50 stress: per shape S7; lex-lock chain length doesn't break.
- Mixed-method components within one wo_complete: each component's own method's consumption logic applied; total_component_cost accurate.
- Fan_contested shape S3 with overlapping component sets correctly serialized via lex-locks; 0 deadlocks.
- Output SKU's method drives dispatch + receipt rule.
- Property test: tests/property_v21_wo_complete.rs covers random K + random method mixes + random component overlap.
- WIP pool_lock acquired in Step 2; WIP pool state snapshot mutation works correctly.
close_reason: Shipped at f35667a. M6.1: WoComplete event_type + multi-pool atomic. PocV21EventType::WoComplete + wo_id/op_id on PocV21Event. expand_wo_complete_payload at staging-read returns K+1 synthetic events (K components qty<0 sub_priority 0..K-1, 1 output qty>0 sub_priority 1_000_000). Step 4 dispatcher tracks wo_cost_accum per correlation_id; output unit_cost = total_component_cost / output_qty. Per-method WoComplete handling (FIFO + AVG + STD); STD output uses component-cost-based unit_cost (variance is acct's concern). Step 12 dedupes succeeded/failed correlation_ids to avoid 'ON CONFLICT DO UPDATE second time' on K+1 same-correlation per_event entries. Pre-sub-tx parse errors mark per-envelope failed not whole-batch. reset_state drain timeout 5s→15s for wo_complete tests' increased cleanup work. 7 acceptance tests pass (K=2/15/50 + mixed-method + STD output + insufficient inventory + empty payload). Full 21-binary / 69-test regression green twice consecutively. Unblocks acct-p0mu (M6.2: per-envelope failure isolation in SuperBatch).

title: M5e.3: postmaster restart durable recovery + mixed-mode tests
description:
Extend M5d.1's startup recovery worker to replay persistent_staging rows when persistent_staging=on. Per spec §1.9 + §3.6 Step 1.

Recovery sweep (BEFORE M5d.1's submission_status sweep):
SELECT correlation_id, user_tx_xid, event_type, payload, sku_pool_keys, wip_pool_keys, business_date
FROM poc_v21_persistent_staging
WHERE state IN ('staged', 'in_shmem')
ORDER BY request_seq;

For each row:
1. Check cost rows by correlation_id (LIMIT 1):
   - If cost rows exist: committer committed before crash.
     - UPDATE persistent_staging.state = 'completed'.
     - UPSERT submission_status: ON CONFLICT (correlation_id) DO UPDATE SET state='committed'.
     - No re-enqueue.
2. Otherwise check pg_xact_status(user_tx_xid):
   - 'committed': caller's user-tx committed durably.
     - Re-INSERT envelope into shmem staging queue (allocate StagingEntry; CAS valid 0 → 1 pending; allocate arena blocks for payload + pool_keys; write StagingEntry fields with reference to persistent_staging via correlation_id).
     - Set persistent_staging.state = 'in_shmem'.
     - Router picks it up on next tick.
   - 'aborted': caller rolled back. persistent_staging row is orphaned.
     - DELETE the row.
     - If submission_status row exists for this correlation_id (caller_subtx mode): UPDATE state='failed' with error_code='caller_tx_aborted'.
   - 'in_progress': defensive — shouldn't happen after postmaster restart (all backends killed → all txs aborted). Treat as aborted.

After sweep: M5d.1's submission_status sweep runs for non-durable envelopes (per its existing logic).

Spec: §1.9 recovery, §3.6 Step 1.
design:
Two-step ordering: persistent recovery FIRST (M5e.3 sweep), then non-durable recovery (M5d.1 sweep). The non-durable sweep excludes correlation_ids that exist in persistent_staging (per its existing WHERE NOT IN clause).

The cost-row check is the source of truth: if rows exist, committer committed, regardless of state field. Edge case: committer committed but died before transitioning state field to 'completed' (covered by re-sweep here).

Re-INSERT into shmem: allocate fresh StagingEntry, allocate fresh arena blocks for payload + pool_keys (loaded from persistent_staging.payload + sku_pool_keys + wip_pool_keys JSONB columns). Don't reuse arena blocks from before the crash — those were lost with shmem.

Sequence init still lazy per §7 hydration — first committer access per pool reads MAX(born_seq) / MAX(consumed_seq).
acceptance_criteria:
- test_v21_postmaster_restart_durable: SIGKILL postmaster mid-stream with durable_queue=true; restart; assert ALL committed-caller envelopes are recovered (either 'committed' if cost rows landed, or re-enqueued and eventually 'committed'); ZERO envelopes lost.
- test_v21_postmaster_restart_mixed: SIGKILL with durable_queue=true and =false interleaved; assert per-correlation-id classification correct (durable callers recovered, non-durable in-flight marked 'failed' with postmaster_restart_loss).
- Recovery time scales linearly with in-flight persistent_staging row count; < 60s for 10K in-flight (per §4.4 O2).
- After recovery, system resumes normal operation; new traffic processed without issue.
- committer_lazy + persistent_staging on postmaster restart: status rows created lazily during recovery for in-flight envelopes; no orphaned 'staged' persistent rows after sweep.
close_reason: Shipped at 84ade24. M5e.3 durable-path postmaster-restart recovery sweep. Persistent-staging sweep runs FIRST in poc_v21_recovery_main; for each in-flight ('staged'/'in_shmem') row: cost-rows-exist → completed (no re-enqueue); pg_xact_status committed → re-enqueue via re_enqueue_from_persistent_staging + state='in_shmem'; else → DELETE + status='failed' caller_tx_aborted. M5d.1 Pass 2 now filters out persistent_staging-covered correlation_ids so re-enqueued envelopes aren't clobbered. 6 acceptance tests cover all four classification paths + mixed-mode + Pass 2 filter regression. Full 20-binary / 62-test regression green. Closes M5e milestone (persistent_staging). Next-ready in v21 PoC chain: M6.1 (wo_complete event type, acct-emnz pending bd lookup).

title: M5e.2: committer state transitions (staged → in_shmem → completed) + GC cron
description:
Committer-side handling of persistent_staging rows per spec §1.9 + §3.4 committer_lazy mode.

Committer pulls shmem StagingEntry per M1.3 / M4.1. If the entry references a persistent_staging row (correlation_id match; query for existence at Step 4 or eagerly cached):

After confirming caller user-tx committed (via Step 4 pg_xact check):
- CAS persistent_staging.state from 'staged' to 'in_shmem' for this correlation_id.
- (Optimization: batched UPDATE WHERE correlation_id = ANY(...) for the SuperBatch.)

After Step 5 sub-tx commit (cost rows durable):
- UPDATE persistent_staging.state = 'completed' for this correlation_id (or batched).
- Status row in submission_status already transitioned to 'committed' via Step 12 updates.

Periodic GC cron (pg_cron):
- Job: poc_v21_persistent_staging_gc.
- Schedule: every hour at minute 0.
- Body: DELETE FROM poc_v21_persistent_staging WHERE state = 'completed' AND enqueued_at < NOW() - (poc_v21.persistent_staging_gc_retention_hours || ' hours')::INTERVAL.
- Default retention 24h.

committer_lazy mode (from M5c.3) interaction:
- When persistent_staging=on AND status_insert_mode=committer_lazy: enqueue path skipped the status INSERT. Committer creates the status row at terminal-state determination.
- Specifically: at Step 5 commit, INSERT INTO submission_status (correlation_id, state, enqueued_at, committed_at, committer_tx_id, superbatch_id) VALUES (...) state='committed' ON CONFLICT (correlation_id) DO UPDATE SET state='committed', ... (handles re-routing idempotently).
- For failed envelopes: INSERT ... state='failed' with error_code, ON CONFLICT DO UPDATE.

Spec: §1.9 committer flow, §3.4 committer_lazy.
design:
The 'staged → in_shmem' transition is somewhat ceremonial — the durable row exists either way; the state field tracks where the envelope is in the pipeline. It's load-bearing for the M5e.3 recovery sweep which uses state to decide re-routing logic.

GC cron via pg_cron: poc_v21_ledger requires pg_cron extension (already loaded per shared_preload_libraries). Schedule + body inline in mig 0NN_persistent_staging.up.sql.

Batched UPDATE for state transitions: instead of one UPDATE per envelope, the committer batches all correlation_ids for the SuperBatch into a single UPDATE WHERE correlation_id = ANY($1::uuid[]). Reduces SPI overhead per SuperBatch.

committer_lazy mode is the LOWEST enqueue overhead — no status row write in enqueue path. But it requires persistent staging (otherwise in-flight envelopes have no observable state after shmem loss). The startup gate from M5c.3 enforces this.
acceptance_criteria:
- Successful enqueue → committed cycle: persistent_staging row transitions staged → in_shmem → completed; submission_status row transitions queued → committed.
- Caller user-tx abort: persistent_staging row state stays 'staged'; recovery sweep (M5e.3) deletes it. Status row rolls back with caller (caller_intx mode) or transitions to 'failed' (caller_subtx mode).
- GC cron deletes completed rows older than 24h (test-only: set retention to 1s and observe deletion).
- committer_lazy mode: enqueue path doesn't write status row; committer creates 'committed'/'failed' rows via ON CONFLICT DO UPDATE idempotently.
- Re-routing under committer_lazy: two committers attempting INSERT for same correlation_id (rare); UNIQUE PK + ON CONFLICT ensures exactly one row.
close_reason: Shipped at 34d216b. M5e.2: committer state transitions for persistent_staging + GC function. After Step 2.45 caller-tx check: batched UPDATE staged→in_shmem. After Step 12 succeeded UPSERT: batched UPDATE in_shmem→completed inside Step 5 sub-tx. Mig 0007 ships poc_v21_persistent_staging_gc(retention_hours INT). committer_lazy mode end-to-end test added (already wired via M5c.3 Step 12 INSERT ON CONFLICT). 6 new acceptance tests + softened 2 M5e.1 assertions for race-safety. Full 19-binary / 56-test regression green. Unblocks acct-* (M5e.3: postmaster-restart durable recovery).

title: M5e.1: poc_v21_persistent_staging table + enqueue-path INSERT
description:
Land the persistent staging table + the durable_queue=true enqueue path. Per spec §1.9.

Schema (mig in db/migrations/):
CREATE TABLE poc_v21_persistent_staging (
    request_seq      BIGSERIAL PRIMARY KEY,
    correlation_id   UUID NOT NULL UNIQUE,
    enqueued_at      TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL DEFAULT now(),
    user_tx_xid      xid8 NOT NULL,
    event_type       TEXT NOT NULL,
    payload          JSONB NOT NULL,
    sku_pool_keys    JSONB NOT NULL,
    wip_pool_keys    JSONB,
    business_date    DATE NOT NULL,
    state            TEXT NOT NULL CHECK (state IN ('staged', 'in_shmem', 'completed')) DEFAULT 'staged'
);
CREATE INDEX poc_v21_persistent_staging_state ON poc_v21_persistent_staging (state, enqueued_at) WHERE state IN ('staged', 'in_shmem');

Enqueue path extension (extends M1.2's poc_v21_enqueue):
- After construct envelope + force user_tx_xid:
  - Validate durable_queue=true requires persistent_staging=on (already in M1.2; here verify gate still wired).
  - If durable_queue=true:
    - INSERT INTO poc_v21_persistent_staging (correlation_id, user_tx_xid, event_type, payload, sku_pool_keys, wip_pool_keys, business_date, state) VALUES (...) state='staged'.
    - Row is WAL-logged; rides with caller's normal commit; NO extra fsync.
  - Continue to shmem StagingEntry write per M1.2 (with reference to persistent_staging via correlation_id join key).

Cost of durability:
- 1 additional INSERT per durable enqueue (WAL-logged, no fsync).
- 1 additional UPDATE per durable envelope at committer's Step 5 (state transition to 'completed') — lands at M5e.2.
- Per-enqueue overhead expected 5-30% per spec §1.9.

Spec: §1.9 persistent staging.
design:
WAL-logged INSERT rides with the caller's existing commit — no separate fsync. This is the cost-minimal durability mechanism.

The correlation_id UNIQUE constraint catches duplicate enqueues at the durable boundary; the matching UNIQUE on submission_status caches at observation boundary.

State machine for persistent_staging:
- staged: INSERTed by caller's enqueue; not yet copied to shmem (caller's user-tx may or may not have committed).
- in_shmem: committer has confirmed envelope is in shmem staging queue; persistent row remains as durable backup (M5e.2's transition).
- completed: committer committed cost rows; row may be GC'd (M5e.2's transition + GC cron).

Partial index on (state, enqueued_at) WHERE state IN ('staged', 'in_shmem') keeps the active-set index small; 'completed' rows aren't indexed because they're query targets only for GC (full table scan acceptable for a periodic job).
acceptance_criteria:
- Migration creates poc_v21_persistent_staging table + index successfully.
- poc_v21_enqueue with durable_queue=true writes a WAL-logged row in caller's user-tx; rolls back with caller abort.
- poc_v21_enqueue with durable_queue=false does NOT write to persistent_staging (no overhead).
- durable_queue=true with persistent_staging=off raises ERRCODE_FEATURE_NOT_SUPPORTED with hint (already wired in M1.2; verify here).
- Throughput delta vs durable_queue=false within 5-30% per spec expectation. Measured precisely at M8.3.
close_reason: Shipped at 290366b. M5e.1: poc_v21_persistent_staging table + enqueue-path durable INSERT for durable_queue=true. Migration 0006 ships table + partial index. Enqueue extension INSERTs inside caller user-tx (rides commit; rolls back on abort) with ON CONFLICT idempotency. business_date resolved from payload.business_date_jdate. poc_v21.persistent_staging=on baked into postgresql.conf for test cycle. 7 acceptance tests cover all paths; full 17-binary regression green. Unblocks acct-jypc (M5e.2: committer state transitions staged → in_shmem → completed + GC cron).

title: M5d.2: slot leak audit (periodic 60s sweep, piggybacked on router BGWorker)
description:
Periodic audit catches slots stuck in non-terminal states due to bugs. Piggybacked on router BGWorker every 60s; avoids spawning a separate small BGWorker.

In router main loop: every N ticks (where N × batch_window_us >= 60_000_000 = 60s), run an audit pass BEFORE the next packing tick. Stash audit timestamp; skip if last audit was < 60s ago.

Audit checks per spec §3.12:
- Staging entries in processing (valid=2) for > 60s with dead backend_pid → CAS valid 2 → 1 (pending). The backend that owned the slot died before completing the enqueue write. Re-route on next tick.
- Staging entries in routed (valid=3) for > 5min with no live CommitterQueueEntry referencing them → mark submission_status state='failed' with error_code='superbatch_lost', CAS valid 3 → 0 (empty), free arena blocks. Defensive — should never happen in clean operation.
- Staging entries in routed (valid=3) for > 5min linked to a CommitterQueueEntry in state completed(3) AND the entry's committer_pid is dead → reap directly:
  - CAS staging valid 3 → 0 for each.
  - Free each staging entry's arena blocks.
  - Free CommitterQueueEntry's OWN arena blocks separately (staging_entry_offsets, sorted pool_keys arrays — queue-entry-owned, easily missed).
  - CAS CommitterQueueEntry 3 → 0 (slot reusable).
  - Cost rows are durable; this is pure cleanup of post-commit-pre-cleanup deaths. Status rows already correct.
- CommitterQueueEntry in in_flight (valid=2) for > 5min with dead committer_pid → orphan-recover per §3.2 (re-claim via M5a.1's mechanism).

Counters exposed:
- poc_v21_audit_reclaims_count (staging entries reclaimed)
- poc_v21_audit_orphans_recovered_count
- poc_v21_audit_lost_envelopes_count
- poc_v21_audit_last_run_at

Spec: §3.12, §3.3 (completed-but-committer-died convergence with router boot sweep).
design:
Piggybacking on router BGWorker: simpler than a separate audit BGWorker. The router's main loop checks a last_audit_ns timestamp at the top of each iteration; if > 60s elapsed, run audit pass. Pass is bounded (iterates fixed staging/committer queue sizes); doesn't significantly perturb router tick latency.

5-minute thresholds for routed/in_flight stale detection: spec §3.12 default. Tunable via GUC if needed (deferred).

Two-paths-converge with router boot sweep (M5b.1): both can catch the completed-but-committer-died case. Defense in depth.

Queue-entry-owned arena freeing is the load-bearing fix; M5b.1 documents the same point for the boot sweep.
acceptance_criteria:
- test_v21_slot_leak_audit_reclaims: manufactured leak (kill backend mid-enqueue allocation OR commit committer that didn't finish Step 14 cleanup); audit reclaims within 70s (60s sweep + grace).
- Audit doesn't interfere with normal router packing (it runs once per minute as a brief pass, not every tick).
- Cleanup on completed-but-committer-died: arena blocks freed correctly (both staging entries' and CommitterQueueEntry's own).
- Audit counters monotone.
- Defensive 'superbatch_lost' path: triggerable by manually CAS'ing a staging entry to valid=3 with bad superbatch_id; audit detects and recovers.
close_reason: Shipped at 5124801. Periodic 60s audit pass piggybacked on router BGWorker; 4 detection patterns (A: staging valid=2 stale, B: valid=3 lost, C: completed-but-committer-died, D: in-flight orphan backstop); 4 counters via SQL accessors; force_reset_all_shmem helper enables strong-equality test assertions immune to inter-test pollution. 6 acceptance tests green; full v21 regression green twice consecutively. Unblocks acct-m8pg (M5e.1).

title: M5d.1: startup recovery worker (non-durable path)
description:
Postmaster restart recovery per spec §3.6. Without persistent staging, in-flight envelopes are lost; recovery's job is to correctly classify which envelopes committed vs which were lost in shmem.

Registered at _PG_init via BackgroundWorker. Runs BEFORE staging/committer queues accept new traffic. Postmaster scheduling ensures this ordering.

Step 1: Sweep submission_status for non-durable envelopes.
SELECT correlation_id FROM poc_v21_submission_status
WHERE state IN ('queued', 'processing')
  AND correlation_id NOT IN (SELECT correlation_id FROM poc_v21_persistent_staging);

For each row:
- Query cost rows by correlation_id:
  SELECT 1 FROM poc_v21_cost_layers WHERE correlation_id = $1 LIMIT 1
  UNION ALL
  SELECT 1 FROM poc_v21_cost_depletions WHERE correlation_id = $1 LIMIT 1
  UNION ALL
  SELECT 1 FROM poc_v21_cost_consumptions WHERE correlation_id = $1 LIMIT 1
  UNION ALL
  SELECT 1 FROM poc_v21_posting_lines WHERE correlation_id = $1 LIMIT 1
  LIMIT 1;
- If cost rows exist: committer committed before crash. UPDATE state='committed' (or 'replayed' if appropriate based on dedup match).
- If no cost rows: envelope was lost in shmem. UPDATE state='failed' with error_code='postmaster_restart_loss'.

Step 2: Sequence initialization (lazy).
- Per-pool next_born_seq / next_consumed_seq counters are LAZY on first committer access per pool. Not initialized at startup.
- M1.3's committer code reads MAX(born_seq) from cost_layers + MAX(consumed_seq) from cost_depletions on first pool touch per snapshot hydration Step 3.

Step 3: Queues open for traffic.
- Worker exits or transitions to idle state.
- Router + committers can now claim work.

Spec: §3.6.
design:
LIMIT 1 in the cost-row check is for performance; we only need to know existence. cost_layers + cost_depletions + cost_consumptions + posting_lines all carry correlation_id stamps, so any one suffices.

The classify-then-mark pattern is the architecture per §3.6: cost rows are the source of truth, status rows are the observation layer.

Sequence init is lazy (not in this worker) per §7 hydration. M1.3's snapshot hydration reads MAX(born_seq) for each pool on first touch; this scales to billions of historical rows.

Postmaster restart scheduling: the recovery worker is registered with BgWorker_BackendsLifetime + BgWorker_None_Db_Access (TBD; verify pgrx 0.18 BackgroundWorker semantics). It runs eagerly at startup before queues open.
acceptance_criteria:
- test_v21_postmaster_restart_non_durable: SIGKILL postmaster mid-load with durable_queue=false; restart; assert committed rows intact, in-flight envelopes marked 'failed' with error_code='postmaster_restart_loss'. System resumes new traffic normally.
- test_v21_postmaster_restart_caller_intx: mixed caller commit/abort at moment of crash; rows classified correctly (committed callers get final status, aborted callers' status rows don't exist).
- Recovery completes within 60s for 10K in-flight envelopes (per §4.4 O2).
- No spurious 'failed' rows for envelopes that actually committed (cost row query is the source of truth).
- No spurious 'committed' rows for envelopes that didn't (LIMIT 1 query is correctness-preserving).
close_reason: M5d.1 shipped at b788115. Postmaster-startup recovery worker classifies in-flight submission_status rows via cost-row existence; 'committed' if cost rows exist, 'failed' with postmaster_restart_loss otherwise. Router + committer BGWorkers gated on recovery_complete shmem flag. 4 new acceptance tests pass. Persistent-staging filter deferred to M5e.x. Full regression 14/14 green twice consecutively. As a side fix: reset_state hardened against the pre-existing router-Phase-6/7 race that caused intermittent total_envelopes flakes in router_metrics + multi_committer tests.

title: M5c.3: status_insert_mode caller_subtx + committer_lazy gating
description:
Implement the other two status_insert_modes per spec §3.4 + §7 Q-A. M1.2 + M5c.2 already cover caller_intx (default + lazy fallback).

caller_subtx mode:
- In poc_v21_enqueue, after step 3 (force user_tx_xid):
  - BeginInternalSubTransaction("poc_v21_status_insert").
  - INSERT INTO poc_v21_submission_status (correlation_id, state, enqueued_at) VALUES (...) state='queued'.
  - CommitInternalSubTransaction.
- The row survives caller user-tx abort. Application observes state='queued' even if caller aborted.
- Committer later transitions to 'failed' with caller_tx_aborted (via M5c.2's path) or 'committed' (Step 5 success).
- Higher per-enqueue overhead: sub-tx commit + WAL. Stronger observability.

committer_lazy mode:
- Startup validation in _PG_init: if status_insert_mode == 'committer_lazy' AND persistent_staging == 'off' → fail to load with hint "committer_lazy requires persistent_staging=on to be safe under postmaster restart."
- When persistent_staging=on: poc_v21_enqueue SKIPS the status INSERT entirely. Committer creates rows only at terminal-state determination.
- Lowest enqueue overhead; requires persistent staging for postmaster restart correctness (in-flight envelopes have no status row but the persistent_staging table has the durable envelope copy; recovery sweep at M5e.3 creates status rows lazily from persistent_staging entries).

Lazy fallback INSERT path per M5c.2:
- When committer encounters in_progress/aborted user_tx_xid with no existing status row: INSERT ... ON CONFLICT (correlation_id) DO NOTHING for idempotency under re-routing.
- This works in all three modes; the difference is whether a 'queued' row pre-existed.

Tests per spec §3.4:
- test_v21_caller_sigkill_post_enqueue_intx (caller_intx default; lazy fallback creates 'failed' row).
- test_v21_caller_sigkill_post_enqueue_subtx (caller_subtx mode; 'queued' row survives caller abort; committer transitions to 'failed').
- test_v21_committer_lazy_blocked_without_persistent_staging (extension refuses to start with status_insert_mode=committer_lazy AND persistent_staging=off; emits expected hint).
- test_v21_committer_lazy_with_persistent_staging (committer_lazy works when paired with persistent_staging=on; postmaster restart recovery via persistent_staging table at M5e.3 creates status rows lazily).

Spec: §3.4, §7 Q-A.
design:
Sub-tx for caller_subtx is the same pgrx primitive used in M1.3 for the committer's main sub-tx. Different scope (status row only) and different lifetime (immediate commit).

committer_lazy is the cheapest enqueue path but creates a recovery semantics constraint: without a durable status row OR a durable envelope, the committer has no way to surface "this envelope was lost in shmem on postmaster restart". Persistent_staging is the durable envelope; M5e.3 recovery sweep reads it and lazily creates status rows during recovery.

Spec §3.4 explicitly defends caller_intx as the default tradeoff: cheapest, correct under postmaster restart for committed callers (durable row from inside their user-tx), and acceptable observability (lazy fallback creates a row when needed). The bake-off (M8.3) measures the alternatives.

Q-A follow-up acct-v21-fu-status-mode-prod: production deployment guidance based on M8.3 measurements (deferred follow-up).
acceptance_criteria:
- caller_subtx mode: 'queued' row written in independent sub-tx; survives caller user-tx abort.
- committer_lazy mode startup gate: psql startup with bad combo fails with descriptive error.
- committer_lazy + persistent_staging=on: enqueue path skips status INSERT; committer creates 'committed'/'failed' rows at terminal state.
- Lazy fallback ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING is idempotent under re-routing.
- Per-mode throughput delta measurable in M8.3 sweep (caller_subtx < caller_intx by sub-tx commit overhead; committer_lazy fastest).
- All four named tests pass.
close_reason: kt61: eject path no longer creates (valid=3, sb_id=0) intermediate; cleanup 2→0 fallback gated on eject_count==0. Full regression green (14/14). Commit 9ceb9aa. nidw: caller_subtx mode dropped (PG sub-tx ≠ autonomous tx); committer.rs Step 12 lifted to INSERT ON CONFLICT for committer_lazy; 3 new tests pass in acceptance_v21_status_insert_modes. Commit 084760f.

title: M5c.2: caller-tx coupling via Option (C) + ejection (central correctness piece)
description:
THE central correctness fix from v2.1's spec review. Committer NEVER sleeps for caller's user-tx. The eject-and-requeue mechanism handles in_progress callers correctly.

Committer Step 4 caller-tx check per spec §1.8 + §3.11:

For each envelope's user_tx_xid in the batch:
- pg_xact_status(user_tx_xid):
  - 'committed': keep envelope in batch. Process normally in Step 5.
  - 'aborted': mark envelope's correlation_id as 'failed' with error_code='caller_tx_aborted'; exclude from batch.
    Lazy submission_status INSERT under caller_intx mode (the original 'queued' row rolled back with caller's user-tx; create now):
      INSERT INTO poc_v21_submission_status (correlation_id, state, error_code, enqueued_at, processed_at) VALUES (...) ON CONFLICT (correlation_id) DO NOTHING.
    Under caller_subtx mode (M5c.3) the row already exists; subsequent UPDATE transitions to 'failed'.
    ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING is load-bearing under re-routing: if an envelope was ejected and re-routed, both committers might attempt the lazy INSERT. PK conflict ensures idempotency.
  - 'in_progress': **EJECT**. CRITICAL: committer NEVER sleeps for callers.
    - Increment staging.eject_count.fetch_add(1, Release).
    - If eject_count > max_eject_count (default 100) OR now_micros - enqueued_at_micros > caller_tx_timeout_ms × 1000 (default 5min): mark envelope failed with error_code='caller_tx_eject_exhausted' or 'caller_tx_timeout'; exclude from batch.
    - Else: CAS staging.valid 3 (routed) → 1 (pending). CAS staging.superbatch_id current → 0. Exclude from current batch. (Router will re-pick on a future tick.)

If all envelopes in batch were caller-tx-aborted or ejected: skip Step 5-9 entirely (no rows to insert); go straight to status updates + slot cleanup.

Step 14 cleanup must handle CAS-failure on ejected entries per spec §1.8:
- For each staging entry in the ORIGINAL SuperBatch (not the filtered-by-ejection batch):
  - CAS staging.valid: 3 → 0 (empty).
  - If CAS FAILS: this entry was ejected during Step 4 (committer found in_progress and CAS'd valid 3 → 1). The entry now belongs to the router again; its arena blocks are still in use because the router will re-pick. DO NOT free its arena blocks. Skip and continue.
  - If CAS SUCCEEDS: free this entry's spillover-arena blocks.

This is the load-bearing rule for ejection safety: CAS-failure means "someone else owns this now, hands off" — no double-free, no corruption.

Spec: §1.8 Step 4 eject path, §1.8 Step 14 CAS-failure-skip, §3.11, §4.1 C2 I-committer-non-blocking + I-eject-bounded.
design:
This is the single biggest correctness rule in v2.1. v2's PoC didn't have this problem because there was no router middleware; each shard's committer was the only thing that touched its envelopes. v2.1's router introduces a path where a committer pulls a SuperBatch containing an in_progress caller — and the spec's review fix says: NEVER sleep.

Why ejection beats committer-sleeping:
- Committer pool is small (typically 4-16 BGWorkers).
- If one committer sleeps waiting on a caller, that's one less for other SuperBatches.
- Under high concurrency where every caller is mid-commit at any moment, all committers could sleep simultaneously → pool stalls under exactly the load v2.1 is designed to absorb.

Ejection vs Step 14 cleanup: the SuperBatch's staging_entry_offsets array holds ALL original indices (router's view). Some may have been ejected by Step 4 (their valid is 1 again). Step 14's CAS 3→0 distinguishes: success means we still own the entry (proceed to free); failure means it was ejected (skip the free).

Property test convention: tests/property_v21_caller_tx_coupling.rs (per CLAUDE.md) — random sequences with random commit/abort/sleep/cancel mixes; assert invariants.
acceptance_criteria:
- test_v21_caller_eject_loop_terminates: caller holds user-tx open past caller_tx_timeout_ms+1000ms; envelope is ejected and re-routed repeatedly; eject_count grows; eventually marked 'failed' with caller_tx_eject_exhausted or caller_tx_timeout error_code.
- test_v21_eject_does_not_stall_committer_pool: inject 100 concurrent callers holding user-tx for seconds; submit 1000 disjoint envelopes; committer pool throughput remains within 10% of nominal. **THE critical correctness criterion.**
- I-committer-non-blocking property test: no committer ever observed sleeping waiting on a caller's pg_xact transition.
- I-eject-bounded property test: any envelope subject to eject cycles reaches terminal state within max_eject_count + 1 eject events OR caller_tx_timeout_ms wall time.
- Step 14 CAS-failure-skip path tested: kill caller mid-user-tx-progress so envelope ejects; verify committer's Step 14 detects the eject and skips arena-free; router re-picks; second committer processes normally.
- AtomicU16 overflow safety: max_eject_count bound 10000 prevents overflow concerns.
- Property test: tests/property_v21_caller_tx_coupling.rs covers all three pg_xact_status paths.
notes:
Implementation amendment 2026-05-17 (discovered via property test hang).

Original acceptance text in this issue said "mark envelope failed with error_code='caller_tx_eject_exhausted' or 'caller_tx_timeout'" for in_progress terminal-fail, implying a lazy INSERT into submission_status. That path violates I-committer-non-blocking under exactly the scenario the test exercises:

  pid 833 (committer)  waiting on  transactionid 189537571  ShareLock  granted=f
  pid 835 (caller)     holding     transactionid 189537571  ExclusiveLock  granted=t

The INSERT ... ON CONFLICT (correlation_id) DO UPDATE triggers _bt_check_unique → XactLockTableWait on the caller's in_progress xid → committer blocks. Direct violation of spec §3.11.

As-built contract:
  - committed caller  → process via Step 3-5 (no change).
  - aborted caller    → lazy INSERT submission_status (state='failed', error_code='caller_tx_aborted'). SAFE because aborted tx leaves dead tuple, no XactLockTableWait.
  - in_progress + budget exhausted → SILENTLY DROP. Increment staging.eject_count (observable via poc_v21_test_staging_eject_count), exclude from batch, do NOT touch submission_status, let Step 14 cleanup CAS 3→0 free the staging slot's arena normally.

Observability gap for in_progress terminal-fail: caller's eventual commit leaves an orphan 'queued' row; caller's eventual abort leaves nothing. Application-layer reconciliation handles orphans (PoC scope per user direction 2026-05-17 "we are not so worried about the application at this point").

Tests adjusted to match contract:
  - acceptance_v21_caller_tx_eject_count_exhausted: asserts eject_count reached max+1 AND staging slot returned to valid=0 (committer dropped envelope cleanly). Does NOT assert submission_status state (no row materializes from committer's drop path).
  - acceptance_v21_caller_tx_timeout_exhausted: same shape.
  - acceptance_v21_caller_tx_aborted_path: still asserts submission_status state='failed' + error_code='caller_tx_aborted' (path unchanged).
  - acceptance_v21_caller_tx_committed_path: regression check (committed path unaffected).
  - acceptance_v21_caller_tx_eject_preserves_arena: validates arena lifecycle under eject CAS-3→1 path.
  - property_v21_caller_tx_coupling: in_progress envelope assertions check "no visible row in admin's tx" (drop is the contract); P4 I-committer-non-blocking still hard-asserted (no tick > 5s).

Production-grade fix filed as acct-v5lx (P3 follow-up): adds poc_v21_committer_terminal_decisions table for committer-side terminal decisions, with trigger-driven recon merging into submission_status post-caller-commit. Out of M5c.2 scope.

Companion R6-shaped invariant for future code: any committer write that could conflict with a caller's still-open row MUST go through a path that does NOT trigger XactLockTableWait — either a separate table without overlapping unique keys, or a shmem signal, or an out-of-band recon table.
close_reason:
M5c.2 shipped at commit 1c83167. Step 2.45 caller-tx coupling check + eject mechanism inserted between Step 2 lex-locks and Step 2.4 method assignments. Three pg_xact_status branches:

  committed   → process normally
  aborted     → lazy INSERT submission_status state='failed' (safe; dead tuple, no XactLockTableWait)
  in_progress + budget exhausted → SILENTLY DROP (would XactLockTableWait on caller's xid otherwise)
  in_progress + budget remaining → CAS staging 3→1, reset superbatch_id, increment eject_count, router re-routes

5 acceptance scenarios + property test (8 cases random caller-outcome mix) green. Full regression 14 binaries / 0 failures.

Observability gap (in_progress terminal-drop leaves orphan 'queued' if caller eventually commits) deferred to acct-v5lx — adds committer_terminal_decisions table with trigger-driven recon merge.

title: M5c.1: backpressure + queue_full_timeout
description:
Handle staging queue full per spec §3.5. Caller waits on backpressure CV up to queue_full_timeout_ms.

Mechanism (extends M1.2's enqueue path):
1. Caller acquires staging queue LWLock; checks fullness (head == tail of free-list, or all slots valid != 0).
2. If full: release LWLock; wait on backpressure_cv via WaitLatchOrCV with timeout = queue_full_timeout_ms (default 5000ms).
3. Each iteration of wait: CHECK_FOR_INTERRUPTS (caller Ctrl-C propagates).
4. Router on drain (Step 5 push to committer queue) calls SetLatch on backpressure_cv tranche → wakes ALL waiting callers.
5. Caller re-acquires LWLock; retries enqueue.
6. If queue still full after waking: continue waiting up to remaining timeout.
7. If timeout exceeded: release LWLock; raise ERRCODE_INSUFFICIENT_RESOURCES with hint "staging queue full, see poc_v21.staging_queue_size GUC".

Caller's user-tx aborts on error per standard PG ERRCODE handling.

Tests per spec §3.5:
- test_v21_backpressure_blocks_then_unblocks: fill queue; observe enqueue calls blocking on CV; drain queue (router runs); observe unblock + successful enqueue.
- test_v21_backpressure_timeout: fill queue; let timeout elapse without drain; observe caller raises ERRCODE_INSUFFICIENT_RESOURCES.
- Cancel-safe: caller Ctrl-C during CV-wait propagates cleanly (CHECK_FOR_INTERRUPTS path).

Spec: §3.5.
design:
WaitLatchOrCV is the pgrx-exposed equivalent of PG's ConditionVariableWaitLatch. Bounded timeout per iteration; outer loop re-acquires LWLock and retries enqueue.

ConditionVariable in pgrx 0.18: confirm API surface at M0.1 time. If 0.18 didn't expose CV directly, use WaitLatch with explicit signal on Latch.

CHECK_FOR_INTERRUPTS must be called at every wait iteration. Without it, Ctrl-C during a backpressure wait would leave the caller blocked indefinitely.
acceptance_criteria:
- test_v21_backpressure_blocks_then_unblocks: caller blocks on CV; on drain, wakes within 100ms; enqueue succeeds.
- test_v21_backpressure_timeout: queue_full_timeout_ms=200; sleep 300ms; caller raises ERRCODE_INSUFFICIENT_RESOURCES.
- Ctrl-C during CV-wait propagates cleanly (no zombie wait state, no LWLock held).
- pg_stat_activity shows accurate wait_event during CV-wait (poc_v21.backpressure_cv tranche name).
- Backpressure recovery on drain: < 10ms p99 (per §4.4 O2).
close_reason: Closed

title: M5b.2: memory ordering invariant test
description:
Dedicated test for the Release/Acquire ordering on superbatch_id from spec §3.3 + §1.6. This is the data-before-flag invariant that M5b.1's recovery sweep depends on.

Test test_v21_router_release_acquire_ordering per spec §3.3:
- Use a test-only barrier or sleep INSIDE the router code path between superbatch_id.store(Release) and valid.compare_exchange(2, 3, Release, Relaxed).
- Gate the barrier via a #[cfg(test)] feature flag or a test-only GUC poc_v21.test_inject_delay_us (default 0).
- Spawn N writer backends (callers) producing envelopes; spawn the router; at a controlled point, kill the router (SIGKILL via libc).
- Restart the router (postmaster auto-restart).
- Run the sweep from M5b.1.
- Assert: every staging entry observed at valid == 3 (routed) has a CONSISTENT (non-zero) superbatch_id. Sweep correctly identifies SuperBatch links without false-negatives that would mis-revert entries to pending.

Stress shape:
- 8 backends pushing 100 envelopes each (800 total) at high rate.
- Router killed at a random moment with delay barrier active.
- Repeat 1000 iterations.

Failure mode being tested:
- Without Release/Acquire ordering: a reader observing valid=3 might read superbatch_id == 0 (stale value), causing sweep to mis-classify the entry as "claimed but never assigned" and CAS-revert it to pending. The envelope would be re-processed by the live SuperBatch in the committer queue, leading to duplicate cost rows.

With proper Release/Acquire: the superbatch_id store is guaranteed visible after the valid CAS to any thread that loads valid with Acquire.

Spec: §1.6 commentary on Release/Acquire, §3.3 ordering invariant, §3.3 memory ordering test name.
design:
The barrier/delay injection is the hard part. Two options:
(a) #[cfg(test)] feature flag adding sleep(test_inject_delay_us) between the two stores.
(b) Test-only GUC poc_v21.test_inject_delay_us read each iteration; production binary ignores.

Option (b) is cleaner for cargo test pgrx integration; option (a) requires building a separate test binary. Pick at implementation time.

The negative control validates the test is actually exercising the invariant. Without negative control, a test that passes "ordering correct" may also pass with weaker ordering on x86 (which has strong memory model and may not reproduce the bug). The negative control should fail on x86 too if the test is meaningful.
acceptance_criteria:
- test_v21_router_release_acquire_ordering: 1000 iterations of the ordering test pass.
- 0 race-condition false-negatives in sweep classification.
- 0 duplicate cost rows from the sweep + committer pipeline.
- Negative control: deliberately weakening ordering (e.g., using Relaxed instead of Release) reproduces a deadlock/inconsistency under the same stress shape; the regular path is clean.
close_reason: Closed

title: M5b.1: router boot sweep + 3-state-staging-entry transitions
description:
Recover from router BGWorker SIGKILL or panic per spec §3.3. Postmaster restarts router automatically; the new router runs a sweep before resuming packing.

Sweep iterates staging queue. For each entry where staging.valid.load(Acquire) == 2 (processing):
- Load superbatch_id = staging.superbatch_id.load(Acquire). (Acquire pairs with Release in M3.1 router write path.)
- If superbatch_id == 0: entry was claimed by router but never assigned to a SuperBatch (router died mid-pack). CAS valid 2 → 1 (pending). Re-routing happens on next tick.
- If superbatch_id != 0: was assigned to a SuperBatch. Look up CommitterQueueEntry by superbatch_id.
  - Queue entry doesn't exist (never pushed before router died): CAS valid 2 → 1 (pending). Re-route.
  - Queue entry is ready(1) or in_flight(2): leave staging entry alone. Committer will process and clean up via §1.8 Step 14.
  - Queue entry is completed(3): committer committed but may or may not have completed staging cleanup before any subsequent failure.
    - kill(committer_pid, 0) alive: committer is still cleaning up; leave staging entry alone. §3.12 periodic audit catches genuine leaks.
    - kill(committer_pid, 0) dead: committer committed but died before staging cleanup. Sweep takes ownership:
      - For each linked staging entry: CAS valid 2 → 0 (work is durable; no re-routing needed).
      - Free each staging entry's arena blocks (payload, pool_keys arrays).
      - Free CommitterQueueEntry's OWN arena blocks (staging_entry_offsets array, sorted sku_pool_keys + wip_pool_keys arrays). These are QUEUE-ENTRY-OWNED, not staging-entry-owned — must be freed separately. Forgetting this is a subtle arena leak source.
      - CAS CommitterQueueEntry 3 → 0 (slot reusable).
      - Update submission_status rows for the SuperBatch's correlation_ids to 'committed' (idempotent; ON CONFLICT (correlation_id) DO UPDATE SET state='committed').

Two-paths-converge: §3.12 periodic audit independently catches the completed-but-committer-died case. M5b.1 + M5d.2 are defense in depth.

Spec: §3.3.
design:
The Acquire ordering on superbatch_id load is paired with the Release in M3.1's superbatch_id.store. This is the data-before-flag invariant — Acquire ensures the post-Release write is visible.

Queue-entry-owned arena blocks are an easy-to-miss leak. Each CommitterQueueEntry owns:
- staging_entry_offsets array (u32 array of staging indices)
- sorted sku_pool_keys array
- sorted wip_pool_keys array
These live in spillover arena and must be freed separately from per-staging-entry arena blocks (payload, sku_pool_keys, wip_pool_keys per envelope).

submission_status UPSERT uses ON CONFLICT (correlation_id) DO UPDATE SET state='committed' for idempotency under repeated recovery firings.
acceptance_criteria:
- test_v21_router_sigkill_pre_push: kill router before pushing any SuperBatch; restart router; assert all pending staging entries remain valid=1 (pending) or re-pending after sweep.
- test_v21_router_sigkill_between_push_and_cas: kill router after CommitterQueueEntry write but before staging CAS 2→3; assert sweep correctly reverts staging entries with superbatch_id == 0 to pending.
- test_v21_router_sigkill_post_cas: kill router after staging CAS 2→3; assert committer pipeline processes the SuperBatch normally; no envelopes lost.
- No envelopes lost across any kill point.
- No envelopes double-processed (dedup-lookup catches the rare double-route case).
- Staging slots eventually free.
- Recovery within 5s p99 (per §4.4 O2 router-death SLA).
close_reason: Closed

title: M5a.2: concurrent recovery race + slot lifecycle correctness
description:
Stress M5a.1 under contention: multiple committers detect a stale lease simultaneously and race to claim it. Plus slot leak verification after recovery.

Test test_v21_committer_orphan_double_claim_race per spec §3.2:
- Kill a committer mid-Step-4.
- Start 4 FRESH committers simultaneously, each scanning the queue.
- Each detects the stale lease and attempts CAS-claim (committer_pid old_dead_pid → MyProcPid).
- Assert: exactly one wins the CAS; others detect the loss (CAS failure) and proceed to other entries.
- The winning committer correctly re-executes Step 1–5; cost rows are NOT duplicated (dedup-lookup catches partial writes).
- Staging slots eventually free.
- No committer pool member is stuck or spinning.

Slot lifecycle correctness verification:
- After SIGKILL recovery, verify all 3 dimensions of slot/arena state per §3.10 coupling:
  - Staging entries: valid back to 0 (empty).
  - Committer queue slot: valid back to 0 (empty) or 3 (completed pending audit).
  - Spillover arena: blocks freed (verify via shmem arena allocator's free-list size delta).
- Forgotten coupling = arena leak. M5d.2 audit catches eventual leaks but M5a.2's recovery path must not introduce them.

Spec: §3.2 race test, §3.10 lifecycle coupling.
design:
The race test is the hardest M5 correctness test. Multiple committers concurrently detecting the same stale lease is rare in real workload but must be correct because correctness can't degrade with committer pool size.

CAS-claim ordering: load committer_pid first (Acquire), check kill(pid, 0), CAS attempt (Release on success). Memory ordering matters here — using too-relaxed semantics would let one committer's kill-check result race with another's CAS.

Arena leak detection: instrument the spillover arena allocator to expose hi-water-mark and current-free-block-count via shmem stats. M5a.2 asserts these stay stable across 100 SIGKILL+recovery iterations.
acceptance_criteria:
- test_v21_committer_orphan_double_claim_race: 4 racing committers, exactly one wins; cost rows have NO duplicates; staging slots free within 5× lease.
- Slot leak audit (M5d.2 will land later but invariant check applies here): post-recovery shmem state shows 0 leaked staging entries, 0 leaked committer queue slots, 0 leaked spillover arena blocks above baseline.
- 100 iterations of the race test; no committer stuck; no duplicate cost rows.
- pgrx_locks_sampler shows no deadlocks during racing recovery.

title: M5a.1: committer death + orphan recovery via pg_xact + kill(pid, 0)
description:
Detect and recover from committer death between Step 2 lock acquisition and Step 5 commit.

Detection per spec §3.2:
- Stale lease: now_ns - committer_acquired_at_ns > committer_lease_ms × 1_000_000.
- Liveness: kill(committer_pid, 0) returns ESRCH (errno=3).
- CAS-attempt to claim: committer_pid old_dead_pid → MyProcPid. If CAS fails (another rescuer won), continue.

Recovery decision based on dead committer's committer_tx_id (stored in CommitterQueueEntry at Step 2 by M4.1):
- pg_xact_status(committer_tx_id) == 'committed': work is durable.
  - Read cost rows by superbatch_id (or by correlation_ids in the SuperBatch).
  - Mark envelopes 'committed' (idempotent — status table UPDATE on already-committed rows no-op).
  - Free staging slots; mark queue entry completed; CAS 2→3.
- pg_xact_status == 'aborted': work is gone.
  - CAS queue entry valid: 2 → 1 (ready) for re-processing.
  - Reclaim from head; re-execute Steps 1–5 normally; dedup-lookup catches any partial writes.
- pg_xact_status == 'in_progress': shouldn't happen post-death.
  - Poll with exponential backoff up to committer_lease_ms × 10 (10ms → 20ms → 40ms → ... → 1000ms).
  - After bound, treat as aborted.
  - (This is the DEAD committer's tx; the "committer never sleeps for callers" rule from §3.11 applies to CALLER tx checks in Step 4, not to orphan recovery for a dead committer.)

Step 2/2.5 re-execution on takeover: the dedup-lookup in Step 2.5 catches rows already inserted by the dead committer (if pg_xact_status was 'committed' but post-commit cleanup didn't finish). No duplicates by construction.

Spec: §3.2.
design:
The committer_tx_id stored in CommitterQueueEntry is the load-bearing recovery hook. M4.1 stores it during Step 2; M5a.1 reads it during orphan recovery.

kill(pid, 0) signal-0 check is the canonical Linux liveness check: returns 0 if process exists, ESRCH if not. Tests for permissions too (EPERM means process exists but we can't signal it — treat as alive for safety).

Exponential backoff for in_progress: 10ms initial, double each retry, cap at committer_lease_ms × 10 total. Bounded; ensures forward progress under pathological cases.

Step 2 lex-locking on takeover: committer's SELECT FOR UPDATE re-acquires the same locks; the dead committer's sub-tx aborted on its death, releasing its locks. No deadlock.
acceptance_criteria:
- Test test_v21_committer_sigkill_pre_commit: kill committer mid-Step-4 (before Step 5 INSERT); assert SuperBatch re-processed, cost rows reflect only one execution, staging slots eventually free.
- Test test_v21_committer_sigkill_post_commit: kill committer after Step 5 commit but before Step 14 cleanup; assert status correct, no row duplication via dedup-lookup, staging slots eventually free.
- Lease takeover within 2× committer_lease_ms p99 (recovery time SLA per §4.4 O2).
- pg_xact polling for in_progress dead-committer-tx terminates within lease × 10 = 1s.
- No idempotency violations under repeated kill-and-rescue cycles.
close_reason: Closed

title: M4.2: two-domain lex-locking correctness probe
description:
Dedicated correctness test verifying lex-locking is deadlock-free across the two domains (SKU + WIP) under contention.

Test scenarios:
- fan_contested shape (g=50, 16 backends, K=5 wo_complete with overlapping component sets per shape S3).
- Inject deliberate non-lex ordering attempts (test-only path): committer pulls SuperBatch but issues SELECT FOR UPDATE in REVERSE sort order. Confirms deadlock-free property holds ONLY under lex order; the test ensures M4.1's path is correct.
- 10,000 SuperBatch iterations at N=16; pg_locks_sampler at 100ms intervals.

Acceptance bars:
- 0 deadlocks over 10K SuperBatches at fan_contested N=16 (any deadlock = test failure).
- 0 SSI / serialization errors.
- pg_locks_sampler confirms wait classes on pool_locks tranche only (NOT on cost_layers / cost_depletions / cost_consumptions row locks). If sampler shows row-lock waits on cost tables, that signals the FOR UPDATE on pool_locks isn't covering correctly.
- Under contention, committers serialize through pool_locks (expected); aggregate throughput drops from N=1 to N=16 by < 3× (P2 precursor).

Spec: §4.2 P2, §1.8 Step 2 lex-locking, §1.5.
design:
This is a correctness probe; the dispatch/cost-method logic is already in place from M4.1. M4.2 is purely about validating the lex-locking property.

pg_locks_sampler reused from acct main (tests/common/pg_locks_sampler.rs in acct-8hv2 lineage). Copy into poc/queue-extension-v21/tests/common/ at M7.2 time; M4.2 may need an early copy or inline equivalent. Pick at implementation time.

The non-lex negative control is in a test-only code path gated by a #[cfg(test)] feature flag — never shipped to production binary.
acceptance_criteria:
- Test test_v21_lex_locking_deadlock_free: 10K SuperBatches at fan_contested N=16, 0 deadlocks.
- pg_locks_sampler shows pool_locks tranche only in wait classes (no row-lock waits on cost tables).
- Non-lex ordering injection (test-only): demonstrates deadlock CAN occur when ordering is violated (negative control); the regular path stays clean.
- N=1 vs N=16 throughput ratio within 3× under fan_contested (P2 precursor).
- WIP pool_locks acquisition under fan_contested with WoComplete-shape events shows no contention (M6.1 will exercise this for real).

title: M4.1: committer pool + CAS election + skip_wip_locks GUC
description:
Scale from one committer (M1.3) to a committer pool. N BGWorkers per poc_v21.committer_count GUC (default 4).

CAS election per spec §1.8 Step 1-2:
- Each committer scans CommitterQueue from head; finds valid=1 (ready) entry.
- CAS valid 1 → 2 (in_flight) AND committer_pid 0 → MyProcPid (single CAS using committer_pid as the discriminator).
- If CAS fails (another committer won): continue scanning to next entry.
- If CAS succeeds: store committer_acquired_at_ns = now_ns (load-bearing for §3.2 orphan detection).

Two-domain lex-locking per §1.8 Step 2:
- SPI INSERT ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING into poc_v21_pool_locks for each (sku_id, location_id) in sorted SKU keys.
- SPI INSERT ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING into poc_v21_wip_pool_locks for each (work_order_id, operation_id) in sorted WIP keys.
- SPI SELECT FROM poc_v21_pool_locks WHERE ... ORDER BY sku_id, location_id FOR UPDATE.
- SPI SELECT FROM poc_v21_wip_pool_locks WHERE ... ORDER BY work_order_id, operation_id FOR UPDATE.

skip_wip_locks GUC (test-only):
- New GUC poc_v21.skip_wip_locks BOOLEAN (default FALSE).
- When TRUE: skip the WIP pool_locks INSERT ON CONFLICT + SELECT FOR UPDATE (Step 2b-d for WIP only).
- Wired here at M4.1; M8.3 sweeps {false, true} to measure the WIP-locks overhead per spec §5.5 and §7 Q-G.
- If the measured throughput delta is < 5%, production deployment can drop WIP locks (per §1.5 reasoning that WIP pools are uncontended by construction).

Spec: §1.8 Step 2, §1.5 (WIP routing-less), §7 Q-G.
design:
Committer count default 4 per spec §1.7. Tunable via GUC; M8.3 doesn't sweep this (out of scope) but it can be raised for performance tuning.

CAS election uses committer_pid as the discriminator. AtomicI32::compare_exchange(0, MyProcPid). Single CAS; the valid field's 1→2 transition is implicit (only the winning CAS can be the one that moves the entry into in_flight; losing committers see committer_pid != 0 and skip).

WIP locks are defensive per §1.5: by construction WIP pools are touched by exactly one WO, so two distinct WO envelopes hit disjoint WIP pools without router-side checking. The locks are uncontended in practice; skip_wip_locks measures the cost of being defensive.

Q-G follow-up acct-v21-fu-skip-wip-locks-prod: production decision deferred to M8.3 measurement.
acceptance_criteria:
- 8 backends pushing concurrently to staging; 4 committers process in parallel.
- Aggregate throughput scales sub-linearly with active committer count (P1 precursor).
- CAS election: under contention, exactly one committer wins per CommitterQueueEntry; others continue scan.
- No deadlocks under fan_out shape (S2 g=5000) at N=8.
- No SSI errors.
- skip_wip_locks GUC: with skip_wip_locks=true the WIP SPI calls are skipped; committer still functions correctly for SKU-only events.
- Property test extension: tests/property_v21_enqueue_commit.rs grows to multi-committer multi-backend shape.
close_reason: Closed

title: M3.3: router packing metrics (R1/R2)
description:
Add per-tick router stats for validation of §4.3 R1 (packing efficiency) and R2 (router throughput).

Metrics:
- envelopes_per_superbatch histogram (per-bucket counts via hdrhistogram-style array or simple AtomicU64 buckets)
- starvation_force_count (incremented in M3.2's backstop path)
- avg_envelopes_per_sb / batch_size_max → packing efficiency ratio
- router_ticks_per_sec (denominator for throughput calc)
- committer_drain_rate_per_sec (sampled from committer pool; ratio router:drain for R2)
- per_tick_window_size_observed
- entries_scanned_per_tick / entries_packed_per_tick

SQL function `poc_v21_router_stats()`:
- Returns one row with all stats above as TIMESTAMPTZ + various counters.
- Read from shmem; no locks (atomic loads).

Used by:
- M9.1's R1 check (packing efficiency > 0.7 × batch_size_max under disjoint workload S2).
- M9.1's R2 check (router throughput > 3× committer drain rate under healthy load).
- §5.7 V21_BENCHMARK_RESULTS.md router metrics section.

Spec: §4.3 R1/R2, §5.7 router metrics, §4.4 O3 observability.
design:
Stats are AtomicU64 in shmem; no LWLock needed (eventual consistency acceptable for observability). hdrhistogram-style buckets capture distribution shape without storing all samples.

R1 efficiency is the load-bearing R-criterion: validates that greedy packing is doing meaningful work. R2 validates router is not the bottleneck. Both must pass at M9.1.

Function signature: poc_v21_router_stats() RETURNS TABLE(stat_name TEXT, stat_value DOUBLE PRECISION) — TableIterator-style for ease of use in scripts. Alternative: composite type with named fields. Pick during implementation.
acceptance_criteria:
- poc_v21_router_stats() callable from psql; returns non-degenerate row under load.
- Disjoint shape S2 (g=5000 fan-out, K=5, N=8) packing efficiency > 0.7.
- Router throughput > 3× aggregate committer drain rate under S2 (validates R2).
- Histogram captures envelopes-per-SuperBatch distribution; tail visible at batch_size_max.
- Counters monotone (no decrement under normal operation).

title: M3.2: fairness backstop + starvation tracking
description:
Add fairness backstop to M3.1's Greedy Window Router. Prevents head-of-queue envelope from starving when its pool keys overlap with every other candidate in the window.

Mechanism per spec §1.8 router loop:
- Per-entry starvation_tick_count in router-local state (HashMap<request_seq, u32>; reset on each entry packed; lost on router death — Q-B flagged).
- Per tick: increment count for each entry that was scanned but skipped (NOT CAS'd into a SuperBatch).
- Threshold = router_starvation_threshold_ticks (default 10).
- When count >= threshold AND SuperBatch is currently empty (no candidate has been packed in this tick yet): force the candidate as size-1 SuperBatch (CAS staging.valid 1→2, add to SuperBatch.lock_set, push to committer queue normally per §1.8 Step 5a-g).
- Reset starvation_tick_count on entries that get packed (including the forced one).

Tracks I-router-progress invariant from spec §4.1 C2: no envelope sits in pending state longer than router_starvation_threshold_ticks × batch_window_us × 3.

Persistence question Q-B: starvation_tick_count is router-local (HashMap in router BGWorker's process memory). On router death + restart, counters reset to 0. Spec §7 Q-B accepts ephemeral for PoC; flagged for production hardening (acct-v21-fu-router-starvation-persistent).

Spec: §1.8 router loop fairness, §4.1 C2 I-router-progress, §4.3 R3, §7 Q-B.
design:
Fairness threshold per spec §4.3 R3: bake-off (M8.3) sweeps router_starvation_threshold_ticks ∈ {1, 5, 10, 20, 50}; documents p99 latency tail vs starvation count tradeoff; pins recommended default. M3.2 ships the mechanism at default 10; M8.3 tunes it.

Q-B follow-up filed: persistent starvation_tick_count. Production hardening only — PoC accepts ephemeral.

The "SuperBatch is currently empty" gate prevents premature forcing when the router has already packed several disjoint envelopes; forcing happens only at the start of a tick where the head candidate has been starved. This balances throughput with fairness.
acceptance_criteria:
- Hot-pool workload (one SKU touched by 80% of envelopes per S5 shape) does not stall head-of-queue.
- Every envelope reaches terminal state within router_starvation_threshold_ticks × batch_window_us × 3 (I-router-progress invariant).
- starvation_tick_count resets to 0 on entries packed (including forced).
- Test test_v21_router_fairness_under_hot_pool (1000 envelopes all targeting same SKU; assert no envelope's staging time > threshold × tick_interval × 2).
- Counters lost on router death (acceptable per Q-B); flagged in design notes.
close_reason: Closed

title: M3.1: router BGWorker + greedy window router
description:
Replace M1.3's stub router with the real Greedy Window Router. Dedicated BGWorker per Q-F option (a).

Router loop per spec §1.8:
1. If staging queue head == tail → WaitLatch up to batch_window_us (default 500μs).
2. Read up to router_window_size (default 1000) pending entries from staging queue head.
3. Track per-entry starvation_tick_count in router-local state (per-PID hashmap by request_seq; deferred to M3.2 for the fairness backstop).
4. Begin SuperBatch assembly:
   a. SuperBatch lock_set = ∅ (HashSet<(i64, i64)> on SKU pool_keys).
   b. For each candidate in window (arrival order):
      If candidate.sku_pool_keys ∩ SuperBatch.lock_set == ∅:
        CAS staging.valid 1 → 2 (processing).
        If CAS success: add candidate; SuperBatch.lock_set ∪= candidate.sku_pool_keys.
      If SuperBatch.envelope_count >= batch_size_max: break.
5. If SuperBatch non-empty:
   a. Allocate next superbatch_id from CommitterQueue.next_superbatch_id.fetch_add(1).
   b. Acquire CommitterQueue LWLock; find free CommitterQueueEntry.
   c. Write fields (staging_offsets array, deduplicated sorted sku_pool_keys + wip_pool_keys in spillover arena).
   d. CAS CommitterQueueEntry.valid 0 → 1 (ready).
   e. Advance committer queue tail; release LWLock.
   f. For each staging entry in SuperBatch (in order):
      staging.superbatch_id.store(sb_id, Release)
      staging.valid.compare_exchange(2, 3, Release, Relaxed)
      CRITICAL: superbatch_id MUST be stored before valid CAS. Reversing creates a window where reader sees valid=3 with stale superbatch_id=0. Recovery sweep (§3.3) relies on data-before-flag invariant.
   g. SetLatch on idle committers (broadcast).

WIP pool_keys are carried through but NOT consulted at routing (spec §1.5 — WIP pools uncontended by construction).

Lock_set data structure: HashSet by default; sorted-Vec alternative for measurement deferred (Q-E follow-up).

Spec: §1.5, §1.6 superbatch_id Release/Acquire, §1.8 router loop, §7 Q-E, Q-F.
design:
HashSet lock_set is default per spec §2.1 B3 analysis. Sorted-Vec alternative is acct-v21-fu-router-sliding-window-adjacent (filed separately) — both data structures meet the analytical ceiling comfortably.

Q-F option (a) lean: committers and router are dedicated BGWorkers (one router, poc_v21.committer_count committers). Option (b) — callers temporarily become committers — is the v2 PoC pattern; PoC v2.1 picks (a) for clarity.

Q-E head-scan lean (current). Sliding-cursor alternative filed as acct-v21-fu-router-sliding-window for measurement.

The Release/Acquire ordering invariant is load-bearing for §3.3 router death recovery. M5b.2 ships a dedicated test for it (test_v21_router_release_acquire_ordering).
acceptance_criteria:
- Well-distributed (disjoint-pool) workload produces SuperBatches of size > 1 (validates greedy packing).
- lock_set membership check correct: no two envelopes within one SuperBatch share an SKU pool.
- Memory ordering invariant: superbatch_id store happens BEFORE valid CAS 2→3; verified by stress test under heavy concurrency.
- batch_size_max GUC respected (no SuperBatch exceeds GUC value).
- router_window_size GUC respected (per-tick scan bounded).
- Router doesn't crash under empty queue or single-entry queue.
- pgrx_locks_sampler shows zero deadlocks during router operation (router takes no DB locks except CommitterQueue LWLock briefly).
close_reason: Closed

title: M2.2: STD method + 6-target bulk UNNEST
description:
Add STD trait impl + finalize all 6 UNNEST INSERTs per SuperBatch. Establish P5 calibration baseline (multi-target vs merged-into-1 synthetic).

STD plan_apply rules per spec §1.3:
- Reads standard_cost from poc_v21_standard_costs (snapshot hydration SELECT DISTINCT ON (sku_id, location_id) ... ORDER BY effective_from DESC).
- Emits consumption row at standard_cost per consumption event.
- Does NOT track pool depth (no avg_total_qty equivalent); standard cost permits negative pool qty by accounting policy.
- For WoComplete: total component cost = Σ(qty × component_standard_cost); output layer at total / output_qty. The output unit cost is what the WO actually consumed (component standard costs); variance to output's OWN standard cost is acct's concern, not extension's. (WoComplete trait impl finishes at M6.1.)

Step 3 snapshot hydration extension:
- SPI SELECT DISTINCT ON (sku_id, location_id) sku_id, location_id, unit_cost FROM poc_v21_standard_costs WHERE (sku_id, location_id) IN UNNEST AND effective_from <= NOW() ORDER BY sku_id, location_id, effective_from DESC.

Step 5 finalize all 6 UNNEST INSERTs:
1. INSERT INTO poc_v21_posting_lines ... UNNEST(...)
2. INSERT INTO poc_v21_cost_layers ... UNNEST(...)
3. INSERT INTO poc_v21_cost_depletions ... UNNEST(...)
4. INSERT INTO poc_v21_cost_consumptions ... UNNEST(...)
5. INSERT INTO poc_v21_posting_line_inventory ... UNNEST(...)
6. INSERT INTO poc_v21_avg_pool_state ... UNNEST(...) ON CONFLICT DO UPDATE SET ... (from M2.1)

Mixed-method batches:
- Single SuperBatch where envelopes target SKUs with different methods (some FIFO, some AVG, some STD).
- Plan_apply dispatches per-event based on driving SKU's method (R2 credit-first rule from acct mirrors here for WoComplete; for simple events, dispatch on event.sku_id's method).

P5 calibration:
- Reference run: ship a synthetic "merge into 1 INSERT" path against a flat synthetic table that holds rows for all 6 destination tables.
- Compare throughput vs the real 6-UNNEST path. Document the overhead ratio in M9.1 V21_BENCHMARK_RESULTS.md.

Spec: §1.3 (STD), §1.8 Step 5 (6 UNNEST INSERTs), §4.2 P5.
design:
P5's pass criterion is "within 25% of merged-into-1 baseline" per spec §4.2 P5. M2.2 establishes the baseline; M9.1 evaluates against it.

DISTINCT ON pattern is PG-specific; equivalent: ROW_NUMBER OVER (PARTITION BY pool ORDER BY effective_from DESC) WHERE rn = 1. Use DISTINCT ON for clarity.

STD's lack of pool depth tracking is intentional. Standard cost is a configuration value, not pool state. Negative pool qty under STD is acceptable (policy choice; acct's variance accounting captures the gap when actual surfaces).

Mixed-method routing follows R2 credit-first rule (driving SKU's method dispatches; per-component method applies for WoComplete components). Document in trait dispatch fn.

P5 CALIBRATION INSTRUMENT: pgrx 0.18 #[pg_bench] is the right tool for the calibration baseline measurement. Runs in-process inside a live PG backend (no psql round-trip noise), Criterion-style statistical rigor (mixed-bootstrap T-test), persistent history with git metadata + pg_settings snapshots. Transaction mode = subtransaction_per_batch (mirrors the committer's Step 5 BeginInternalSubTransaction shape). One #[pg_bench] for the merged-into-1 synthetic path; one for the real 6-UNNEST path. Compare via cargo pgrx bench. The bake-off harness (M8.1+) stays psql-driven for the multi-backend N sweep — #[pg_bench] is single-backend in-process and can't drive concurrent contention shapes.

- STD method emits consumption row at standard cost; UNIQUE (issue_id, method_used) on cost_consumptions enforced.
- Rotating standard_costs: insert new effective row; subsequent commits use new cost; DISTINCT ON returns latest.
- Mixed-method batch with FIFO + AVG + STD envelopes commits cleanly in one SuperBatch.
- All 6 UNNEST INSERTs land per SuperBatch (verify via SPI counter or query plan inspection).
- P5 calibration baseline established via #[pg_bench] (single-backend in-process): one bench for the merged-into-1 synthetic path, one for the real 6-UNNEST path. Throughput ratio captured in poc/queue-extension-v21/bench/ for M9.1 ingestion. Use Criterion T-test verdict; expect 6-UNNEST within 25% of merged baseline.
- Property test extension: covers STD + mixed-method.

Per-row Spi loops gone. PROPTEST_CASES=100 in 13.66s green over 7 properties (P1-P7 including STD cost dispatch).
