title: FIFO arena rollback hardening — extend M10 XactCallback semantics to fifo_apply_batch_maximal
description:
The FIFO arena (`poc/ledger-extension/src/fifo.rs`) has the same structural class of rollback bug as the WAC arena had pre-M10 A1/A2 (acct-2733 / acct-4e91, both closed 2026-05-13 under acct-tpqw).

## Bug class

`fifo_apply_batch_maximal` mutates shmem state IMMEDIATELY during the apply call:

- Phase 8: `push_layer` / `consume_from_head` / `push_pending_drain` advance the ring head, push new layers, stage pending_drain entries — all under cell EXCLUSIVE LWLock.
- Phase 8 (overflow path): flips `overflow_active`, CAS-sets `overflow_first_spilled_layer_id` watermark.
- Phase 8.5 (spill walk) + Phase 8.6 (durable_only walk): SPI `UPDATE cost_layers` (durable, TX-bound — rolls back cleanly) and pushes to `accum_drain`.
- Phase 9 INSERTs: posting_lines / cost_layers / cost_layer_depletions are TX-bound (roll back cleanly).
- Phase 10 `stage_apply`: stages WAC arena balance/qty deltas.

If the surrounding PG transaction ROLLBACKs after the apply call (constraint violation, SAVEPOINT rollback, app-level ROLLBACK, backend crash mid-commit), the durable side rolls back (posting_lines / cost_layers / cost_layer_depletions disappear) but the shmem side does NOT:

- Ring head has advanced; consumed layers' qty has been decremented or whole layers evicted via head-advance.
- New receipts' layers were pushed to the ring tail.
- pending_drain has staged entries pointing at cost_layers IDs that no longer exist.
- overflow_active / watermark may have flipped permanently.
- WAC arena deltas (Phase 10 stage_apply) leak too — but those are covered by the existing acct-4e91 XactCallback path.

Net: the FIFO arena's view of pool state diverges from the durable truth post-rollback. The bgworker drain tick will then UPDATE cost_layers rows that don't exist (or worse, exist with stale values from a prior committed batch).

## Detection

The recon function `fifo_arena_recon()` would surface drift after rollback — but ONLY for the cells the rollback touched, only until the next successful apply re-syncs that cell's ring state. Latent drift is the failure mode.

## Fix shape (mirrors acct-4e91)

Extend the existing per-backend PENDING_STACK + REGISTERED flag (currently shaped around the WAC arena's balance/qty deltas) to ALSO defer FIFO mutations until commit:

1. **Phase 8 deferral.** Rather than mutating the ring under cell EXCLUSIVE during apply, stage:
   - Per-cell list of `LayerDelta::{Push(Layer), Consume(qty)}` operations.
   - Per-cell list of `PendingDrainDelta::Push(layer_id, qty)` entries.
   - `overflow_active` / `watermark` flips (idempotent, but still need ordering).

2. **PreCommit callback.** Validate capacity — MAX_LAYERS budget across queued pushes, PENDING_DRAIN_CAP across queued staging. Raise pgrx::error! on overflow so the SQL txn aborts cleanly (Commit cannot abort).

3. **Commit callback.** Acquire each touched cell EXCLUSIVE in sorted order (mirrors the apply-time discipline), replay LayerDeltas in order, replay PendingDrainDeltas, finalize overflow flags.

4. **SubXactCallback.** START_SUB pushes a fresh frame; COMMIT_SUB merges child into parent (same-cell key collapse via HashMap<cell_idx, Vec<LayerDelta>>); ABORT_SUB pops + discards.

5. **Abort callback.** Drop PENDING_STACK[0]. Shmem state untouched.

## What this means for in-batch RYW

Today's apply-time mutation gives same-cell same-batch envelopes (and same-pool same-batch envelopes through cells_to_envelopes ordering) a "read-your-writes" view of the ring. Envelope B reads the post-envelope-A ring state because Phase 8 mutates the ring envelope-by-envelope under the cell lock.

Deferring to commit breaks this. Envelope B in Phase 8 would see the pre-batch ring (or worse — partial state if some envelopes have applied and some haven't). The apply-time consume MUST work against the eventual-committed state.

Two implementation choices:

- **(a) Per-call SHADOW ring.** Build a per-cell shadow of the ring at Phase 8 entry; apply all envelopes against the shadow; queue the resulting LayerDeltas for commit. Final cost_layers INSERTs / depletions reflect the shadow's computation. At commit, replay the deltas atomically.

- **(b) Apply-then-rollback-undo.** Keep the in-place apply, but also queue an "undo" list (Push → Pop on rollback, Consume → Restore on rollback, pending_drain Push → drain-and-discard). On Abort callback, replay undos in reverse.

(a) is closer to acct-4e91's PENDING_STACK shape. (b) is closer to what databases call "compensating actions" but adds complexity (especially around interleaved pending_drain that may have already been flushed by bgworker between apply and abort).

Lean toward (a). Same architectural shape as acct-4e91, same callback infrastructure can be extended.

## Sub-decomposition (when claimed)

- **A1-equivalent (~1h).** Confirm rollback bug. Write test mirroring `tests/rollback_correctness_t1.rs::v1_minimal_rollback_leak`: BEGIN; fifo_apply_batch_maximal with a receipt; ROLLBACK; assert `fifo_arena_recon` reports drift OR the ring contains the rolled-back layer.
- **A2-equivalent (~1-2 days).** Implement (a). Likely shares PENDING_STACK with the existing WAC arena infrastructure via a tagged enum (BalanceDelta vs RingDelta). May need a separate FIFO_PENDING_STACK if intermingling complicates the WAC code path.
- **B4-prep-equivalent.** Seqlock for FIFO concurrent reads — recon snapshots vs apply mutators. Lower priority than WAC's seqlock since FIFO uses LWLock not lock-free atomics; cell EXCLUSIVE during mutation gives natural exclusion. May not be needed.

## Out of scope

- WAL crash safety for FIFO arena (multi-week, separate epic).
- GUC-driven FIFO_N_BUCKETS / MAX_LAYERS sizing (acct-ibib calibration epic).
- Same-batch RYW limitation for durable_only path (acct-cpe8 documented limitation; not a rollback issue).

## Acceptance criteria

1. Gate test confirms the bug exists pre-fix (mirrors acct-2733 polarity).
2. Same gate test flips polarity post-fix to assert drift=0 after ROLLBACK.
3. Extended test coverage: SAVEPOINT + ROLLBACK TO; nested savepoint; commit after savepoint rollback; backend crash mid-apply (process kill).
4. All 45 prior FIFO tests still green (40 pre-cpe8 + 5 cpe8).
5. Bench delta on M9 fan-in/fan-out — hypothesis: 5-15% throughput drop from commit-time apply; acceptable. >25% → investigate.

## Why P2 not P1

The PoC FIFO arena is not yet integrated into the production acct codebase. Production integration would gate on this work (M10 stipulates the WAC arena had A2 closed before any production wiring). For the PoC alone, the gap is documented behavior — useful for benchmarks, not yet for real workloads.

Once the FIFO arena is wired into the production schema (via a hypothetical post_batch_fifo_shmem analogous to post_batch_shmem from acct-sw4i M8), this becomes a P1 blocker for that wiring.

## Lineage / references

- acct-tpqw (closed 2026-05-13) — WAC arena M10 hardening epic.
- acct-2733 (closed) — WAC A1 gate test confirming the WAC rollback leak.
- acct-4e91 (closed) — WAC A2 XactCallback + SubXactCallback + PENDING_STACK + REGISTERED.
- acct-e9tf (closed 2026-05-14) — FIFO arena epic; all 8 subs shipped but rollback hardening was intentionally out of scope (the PoC was throwaway-prone).
- Memory `state-2026-05-13-tpqw-M10-COMPLETE-B4-shipped` for the WAC analogue's full design + commit chain.

## Open design questions

- Q1: extend WAC's PENDING_STACK with a tagged enum vs maintain a separate FIFO_PENDING_STACK?
- Q2: does Phase 8.5 spill walk's SPI side need any deferral? Today it SELECT FOR UPDATE on cost_layers + computes total_cost — the SELECT/FOR UPDATE rolls back cleanly. Likely no shmem-side deferral needed, but verify.
- Q3: how does Phase 8.6 durable_only interact? No cell, no ring mutation — only SPI work + pl_*/dp_*/accum_drain (all TX-bound). Likely zero rollback exposure on the durable_only path.
- Q4: same-batch RYW limitation documented in Phase 8.6 — does deferring to commit make this WORSE (envelopes can't see each other's writes at all) or BETTER (envelopes apply against a coherent shadow)? Lean (a) → better.

These resolve during A2 design. Surface to user before authoring.
close_reason: A2 shipped @ dff20bd. acct-majp epic complete: A1 gate at 0827461 + a859d3f; A2 deferred-apply at dff20bd. Phase 8 of fifo_apply_batch_maximal now stages ops in per-backend FIFO_PENDING_STACK, replayed at xact_commit, discarded at xact_abort. SubXactCallback handles SAVEPOINT/ROLLBACK TO. V1/V2 polarity flipped; V6-V10 added (10 rollback cases total). Full FIFO test surface 50 passing. Bench 17-19% drop vs baseline (above hypothesis but below 25% fail threshold); Alt D thread-local pre-alloc filed as acct-8axd P3 follow-up.

title: M10.D1 — document extension invariants + pin tests for the unpinned ones
description:
Coverage-completeness audit surfaced 2026-05-12. The M10 sub-issues (A1, A2, B1-B8, C1-C6) all probe scenarios. None catalog the invariants those scenarios are protecting. Without an explicit invariant list, it's impossible to know what the test plan DOESN'T cover.

## Scope

Two deliverables:

### Deliverable 1: poc/ledger-extension/INVARIANTS.md

Canonical list of every invariant the M9 PoC + M10 hardening must uphold. Format mirrors REVIEW.md / R1-R7 class-confusion checklist style. Each invariant gets:
- ID (I1 through I18+)
- Statement (one sentence)
- Why it matters (correctness consequence if violated)
- Where in lib.rs it's enforced (line reference or function name)
- Which test pins it (or "STRUCTURAL — no explicit test")

Starting catalog from 2026-05-12 walk:

| # | Invariant | Enforced by | Pinned by |
|---|---|---|---|
| I1 | APPLY_SEQ monotonic increasing; per-cell last_seq monotonic | APPLY_SEQ.fetch_add; cell.last_seq.store after fetch_add | NONE — add T1.I1 |
| I2 | drained_seq ≤ last_seq always | stamp_drained CAS-max loop | NONE — add T1.I2 |
| I3 | occupied=1 Release implies key_hi/key_lo visible to Acquire readers | Memory ordering on insert_new_seeded | Structural |
| I4 | OCCUPIED_COUNT.load() == count(buckets WHERE occupied=1) | OCCUPIED_COUNT.fetch_add on insert; reset zeroes both | NONE — add T1.I4 |
| I5 | Exactly one cell per (account_id, period_id, currency_id, ledger_kind) | EXCLUSIVE re-probe in cold path | M3 sanity (8-way same-key race) |
| I6 | Drain conservation: rollup row's (balance, qty, last_seq) == cell snapshot at gather time | Phase 1 of do_drain_tick + UPSERT with last_seq guard | M5 implicit |
| I7 | At quiescence: shmem_balance per cell == SUM(debits)-SUM(credits) per account in posting_lines | ledger_shmem_recon SPI math | M7/M8 (drift=0 assertion) |
| I8 | Rollback → shmem unchanged; commit → shmem applied | XactCallback (post-A.2) | acct-2733 / acct-4e91 |
| I9 | Idempotent replay: same idempotency_key returns sentinel without double-apply | post_batch_shmem CTE de-dup | M8 |
| I10 | Dimension isolation: cells at distinct (currency, period, kind) don't cross-contaminate | Packed u128 key; per-cell atomics | acct-jjqc / acct-nn31 / acct-713c |
| I11 | Reader sees consistent (balance, qty) pair (no torn reads) | Seqlock pattern (post-B.4-prep) | acct-zo4t |
| I12 | Open-addressing probe terminates at first occupied=0 | Structural in try_update_existing | Structural |
| I13 | Bgworker scoped to drain_database GUC; other DBs see no rollup writes | connect_worker_to_spi(Some(dbname), ...) | NONE — add T1.I13 |
| I14 | ledger_shmem_reset zeros all atomics; OCCUPIED_COUNT == 0; subsequent applies start fresh | reset function | Used as fixture in M3+; add explicit T1.I14 |
| I15 | Common-path apply is lock-free beyond SHARED concurrent acquire | SHARED + atomic fetch_add | M9 throughput (5.55x lift) is proxy |
| I16 | Apply path takes no locks on accounts table | Architectural — no SQL touches accounts in apply | acct-mii6 S4 |
| I17 | balance() reader: shmem if present, else rollup, else (0,0,0,'none'); source label correct | extension_sql balance() body | M4 |
| I18 | M6 lazy-load: new cell starts at (rollup_seed + delta); drained_seq = rollup.last_seq; next drain finds it dirty | insert_new_seeded with rollup_seed | M6 |

Walk the lib.rs and tests directories once more to surface any I19+ I missed. Hold the catalog to "invariants" strictly — not "things we want to be true" but "things the code currently guarantees, that a future refactor must preserve."

### Deliverable 2: poc/ledger-extension/tests/invariants_t1.rs

New test binary. One test per unpinned invariant:

**T1.I1 — seq monotonicity.** Read APPLY_SEQ via ledger_shmem_apply_seq() before/after a single apply; assert strict increment by 1. Run 10K applies in a loop; sample APPLY_SEQ at intervals; assert never decreases. Same for per-cell last_seq via ledger_balance_lookup.

**T1.I2 — drained ≤ last_seq.** After N applies followed by drain wait, walk all cells (via dirty_count + drained_count + occupied) and assert each cell's drained_seq ≤ last_seq. Test fails if the CAS-max loop in stamp_drained is broken.

**T1.I4 — OCCUPIED_COUNT consistency.** Apply against K distinct keys; assert ledger_shmem_occupied() == K. Then reset; assert == 0. Concurrency variant: 8 workers each inserting 100 distinct keys; total 800; assert occupied count == 800 post-join. Tests the fetch_add in insert_new_seeded matches reality.

**T1.I13 — bgworker per-database scope.** Create a second test database (acct_poc_test); CREATE EXTENSION there too. Verify drain_database GUC defaults to "acct_poc"; apply deltas in acct_poc; observe rollup row in acct_poc only — NOT in acct_poc_test. Then SET ledger.drain_database (postmaster restart needed); rerun.

**T1.I14 — reset completeness.** Apply N deltas across K cells, wait for drain; call ledger_shmem_reset(); assert: occupied=0, apply_seq=0, dirty_count=0, drained_count=0, ledger_balance_lookup on any prior key returns NULL. (Rollup rows DO survive reset — that's by design; document.)

## Acceptance

- INVARIANTS.md exists at poc/ledger-extension/INVARIANTS.md.
- Every invariant in the catalog has either a "Pinned by: <test>" or "Structural — see <code location>" reference.
- T1.I1, T1.I2, T1.I4, T1.I13, T1.I14 implemented and passing.
- Cross-reference added to README.md milestone block.
- Future M10 sub-issues (A2, B4, etc) update INVARIANTS.md when they pin previously-unpinned invariants.

## Files touched

- poc/ledger-extension/INVARIANTS.md (new)
- poc/ledger-extension/tests/invariants_t1.rs (new, 5 tests, ~250 LOC)
- poc/ledger-extension/README.md (cross-reference)

## Dependencies

Independent. Can ship before A1 — INVARIANTS.md just documents what's there; the unpinned tests test M9-as-is.

## Estimate

4 hours. INVARIANTS.md walk through lib.rs: 1h. T1.I1-I14 implementation: 3h.

## Out of scope

- Acct-integration invariants (I1-I7 from tests/common/mod.rs::assert_invariants_hold). When the extension eventually lands in acct, those must continue to hold under the shmem apply path. File as separate epic when acct integration starts.
- Formal proof or model-checking of the invariants. Documentation + tests is sufficient for PoC.

title: M10.B4 — post_batch_wac_shmem + WAC fan-in/fan-out bench (load-bearing acct integration target)
description:
The load-bearing perf target for the acct-togd custom-extension epic. WAC under shmem apply is the ERP-realistic case; M9 only benched simple transfer.

## Motivation

Per acct-togd bench memory: WAC fan-out projected 7-10× lift over mutable, WAC fan-in projected 3.4×. These were not measured in M9; PoC has no shmem-integrated WAC path. WAC FOR-UPDATE on pool accounts is the cost that shmem eliminates — confirming the projected lift validates the architectural premise for the realistic acct workload (not just simple-transfer microbench).

## Design

Build `post_batch_wac_shmem(p_envelopes JSONB)` in poc/batch-ledger/db/migrations/0014_post_batch_wac_shmem.up.sql. Drop-in replacement for `post_batch_wac`'s UPDATE accounts SET balance path:

1. Pre-pass: parse envelopes, collect distinct source pool keys.
2. For each source pool: read current `(pool_balance, pool_qty)` via `ledger_balance_lookup(...)`. Under seqlock (B.4-prep) this is consistent.
3. Compute per-envelope: `unit_cost = pool_balance / pool_qty`, depletion `amount = qty_out * unit_cost`. (For provisional pricing extensions: dispatch through cost_method_strategies if needed; not in MVP scope.)
4. INSERT posting_lines via same CTE chain as post_batch_append_only.
5. For each fresh leg: PERFORM `ledger_apply_balance_delta(debit_account, ..., +amount, +qty_delta_d)` + `ledger_apply_balance_delta(credit_account, ..., -amount, -qty_delta_c)`.

## Test method

### Correctness (T1)

Direct comparison test: same 1000-envelope WAC scenario through both `post_batch_wac` (mutable) and `post_batch_wac_shmem`. Assert:
- `accounts.balance` after `post_batch_wac` == `ledger_shmem_recon().shmem_balance` after `post_batch_wac_shmem` (post-drain).
- `posting_lines.amount` per envelope matches between the two paths.
- WAC unit_cost recomputed correctly across multi-receipt sequences (verifies B.4-prep seqlock is actually preventing torn-read regressions).

### Concurrency correctness (T2)

8 writers × 1000 envelopes each, all touching one shared pool (fan-in WAC). Assert at end:
- `shmem_balance / shmem_qty == 1` (or whatever the seeded unit cost was).
- Drift = 0 between shmem and posting_lines.
- No silent variance leak in `variance_wac_periodic` or equivalent.

### Bench validation (T3)

Re-use `tests/bench_wac_fan.rs` (the existing acct-togd WAC bench harness). Add `POC_BENCH_FUNCTION=post_batch_wac_shmem` route:
- Fan-in WAC: 50 receipt SKUs + 1 hot pool; 20 writers × batch=1000 × 3×60s. Compare against `post_batch_wac` baseline (22.9K tps from acct-togd memory).
- Fan-out WAC: 5000 pools; same workload shape; compare against `post_batch_wac` baseline (4K tps, p99 5.5s).
- RYW mix: 0% / 20% / 50% in-batch issue rate (verifies seqlock retries don't dominate under reads-during-writes).

Hypothesis from acct-togd:
- Fan-in WAC: 22.9K → ~75K tps (3.4× projection lower bound).
- Fan-out WAC: 4K → ~30-40K tps (7-10× projection).
- p99 latency drops at fan-out from 5.5s to <1s.

If measured lift is < 50% of projection (e.g., fan-out only 2×), file followup to investigate (likely: WAC dispatch overhead in plpgsql swamps the shmem savings, suggests `ledger_apply_batch(jsonb)` as next lever).

### Recon (T4)

`ledger_shmem_recon()` filtering on the WAC test's pool accounts. Assert drift=0 after drain settles. This is the critical signal that WAC math under shmem is producing the same ledger state as the mutable path.

## Acceptance

- T1-T4 all pass.
- Bench results documented in `poc/batch-ledger/bench/results-shmem-wac.md`:
  - Median tps + p50/p99 ms for fan-in and fan-out WAC.
  - Lift vs mutable post_batch_wac.
  - Comparison to projection.
  - Headline plot: 4 datapoints (mutable fan-in, mutable fan-out, shmem fan-in, shmem fan-out).
- README.md milestone M10.B4 marked complete.
- bd memory `state-2026-05-12-acct-togd-bench-complete-ready-for-sw4i` updated with measured WAC lift.

## Files touched

- poc/batch-ledger/db/migrations/0014_post_batch_wac_shmem.up.sql (new)
- poc/batch-ledger/tests/bench_wac_fan.rs (extend with shmem variant)
- poc/batch-ledger/tests/wac_shmem_correctness_t1.rs (new — T1, T2)
- poc/batch-ledger/bench/run-shmem-wac-sweep.sh (new)
- poc/batch-ledger/bench/results-shmem-wac.md (new)

## Dependencies

Blocks-on: acct-zo4t (B.4-prep seqlock — REQUIRED, not optional, because WAC computes unit_cost from torn-read-vulnerable pair).
Blocks-on: acct-4e91 (A.2 transactional apply — required to make WAC under shmem semantically equivalent to mutable WAC under rollback).

## Estimate

2-3 days. WAC logic itself is straightforward; bench setup + analysis + reconciling measured vs projected is the bulk.

## Out of scope

- Cost-method dispatch (FIFO, lot, retroactive). These are separate registry entries; only standard WAC perpetual in MVP B.4. FIFO would be acct-sw4i-m10.b4-fifo if needed (likely unnecessary at PoC scale).
- Period-close WAC (wac_periodic close hook). Not in PoC.
- Cross-currency WAC. Single-currency PoC scope.

title: M10.B4-prep — seqlock on Bucket reads to prevent torn balance/qty reads (WAC prerequisite)
description:
Prerequisite for B.4 (WAC integration). Eliminates a torn-read race on the (balance, qty) pair that's invisible to simple-transfer workloads but silently produces wrong unit cost for WAC.

## Hypothesis

In current M9 code, `Bucket.balance: AtomicI64` and `Bucket.qty: AtomicI64` are separate atomics. A writer doing:
```
b.balance.fetch_add(amount_delta, AcqRel);
b.qty.fetch_add(qty_delta, AcqRel);
```
is observable by a concurrent reader as `(balance_new, qty_old)` if the reader's `balance.load()` happens between the two fetch_adds.

For simple transfer (PoC `post_batch_shmem`): qty_delta is always 0 — no observable torn read.
For acct WAC (`post_batch_wac_shmem` in B.4): cost dispatch computes `unit_cost = pool_value / pool_qty`. A torn read of `(post_apply balance, pre-apply qty)` divides updated value by stale qty → silently wrong unit cost → wrong subsequent depletion amounts → silent variance leak.

## Options weighed

| Option | Mechanism | Pros | Cons |
|---|---|---|---|
| A | Per-bucket version counter (seqlock) | Standard pattern, ~20 LOC | Reader retries on contention |
| B | Pack balance+qty into single AtomicI128 | Truly atomic | i128 cmpxchg needs nightly OR cmpxchg16b intrinsic; alignment doubled to 16B |
| C | LWLock per bucket | Simple semantics | Defeats the lock-free hot path that gives the 5.55× lift |
| D | Document as eventual consistency | 0 LOC | Wrong for WAC; cannot ship B.4 |

**Decision: Option A (seqlock).** Standard lock-free pattern, well-understood semantics, no dependency on x86-64-specific intrinsics, no nightly.

## Design

Add to Bucket struct:
```rust
#[repr(C, align(64))]
pub struct Bucket {
    pub occupied: AtomicU8,
    pub _pad0: [u8; 7],
    pub key_hi: AtomicU64,
    pub key_lo: AtomicU64,
    pub seq: AtomicU64,        // NEW: even = stable, odd = writer in progress
    pub balance: AtomicI64,
    pub qty: AtomicI64,
    pub last_seq: AtomicU64,
    pub drained_seq: AtomicU64,
}
```

**Writer pattern** (in try_update_existing and insert_new_seeded):
```rust
// Acquire writer half of seqlock
let s0 = b.seq.fetch_add(1, Ordering::AcqRel);  // s0 even → s0+1 odd
debug_assert!(s0 % 2 == 0, \"concurrent writer detected — should be SHARED+atomic only\");
b.balance.fetch_add(amount_delta, Ordering::AcqRel);
b.qty.fetch_add(qty_delta, Ordering::AcqRel);
b.seq.fetch_add(1, Ordering::AcqRel);  // s0+2 even — stable
b.last_seq.store(new_seq, Ordering::Release);
```

NOTE: fetch_add(1, AcqRel) twice does NOT enforce "one writer at a time" — multiple SHARED-mode writers can interleave. The seqlock here is for READERS not WRITERS. Writers compose correctly via the existing atomic fetch_add semantics; the seqlock just lets readers detect mid-write torn reads.

**Reader pattern** (in ledger_balance_lookup and recon Phase 1):
```rust
loop {
    let s_pre = b.seq.load(Ordering::Acquire);
    if s_pre % 2 != 0 { std::hint::spin_loop(); continue; }
    let bal = b.balance.load(Ordering::Acquire);
    let qty_v = b.qty.load(Ordering::Acquire);
    let s_post = b.seq.load(Ordering::Acquire);
    if s_post == s_pre { return (bal, qty_v); }
    // s_pre != s_post means a writer fired between our loads — retry
    std::hint::spin_loop();
}
```

Bounded retry (give up after 16 iterations and return last-read pair with a tombstone flag) prevents pathological livelock under sustained heavy write contention; in practice writes are fast (atomic fetch_add) so retry rate should be < 1%.

## Test method

**T1 — single-writer correctness.** Apply (1000, 1) 1000 times sequentially; read after each; assert (balance, qty) is always exactly (n*1000, n*1).

**T2 — concurrent writer-reader torn-read probe.** 4 writers doing `apply(1000, 1)` in a loop for 10s; 4 readers calling `ledger_balance_lookup` in a loop. Reader asserts `balance % 1000 == 0 && qty == balance / 1000`. Without seqlock, this fails. With seqlock, it passes. Run with `--release` and `RUST_TEST_THREADS=1` against an isolated test DB to avoid CI noise.

**T3 — concurrent 8-writer write-amplification.** 8 writers each doing 10K applies to the SAME key. After all join, expect `balance = 80K * amount_delta`, `qty = 80K * qty_delta`. Pre-existing test (M3 sanity); rerun under seqlock to confirm no regression in concurrent fetch_add composition.

**T4 — bench delta.** Re-run M9 fan-in/fan-out sweep. Hypothesis: throughput unchanged within noise (~3%); the seqlock instructions add ~1ns per apply, negligible against the rest of the path. Document in `bench/results-shmem-apply-B4prep.md`. If unexpected regression > 10%, investigate.

**T5 — bounded retry under pathological load.** 16 writers hammering one cell while 16 readers loop on it. Read-loop measures retry count distribution; assert max < 1000 (writers should complete fast enough that no reader retries unboundedly).

## Acceptance

- Bucket struct gains `seq: AtomicU64`.
- All readers (ledger_balance_lookup, ledger_shmem_recon, do_drain_tick gather, dirty/drained counters) use the seqlock read pattern.
- All writers stamp seq via fetch_add(1) before and after the (balance, qty, last_seq) writes.
- T1-T5 pass.
- M9 bench rerun within ±5% (noise band).
- M9 `recon drift = 0` invariant still holds.

## Files touched

- poc/ledger-extension/src/lib.rs (Bucket struct + writer/reader patterns at ~6 sites)
- poc/ledger-extension/tests/seqlock_torn_read_t1.rs (new — T1-T5)
- poc/batch-ledger/bench/results-shmem-apply-B4prep.md (new — perf delta)

## Dependencies

Blocks-on: acct-4e91 (M10.A2). Seqlock semantics interact with deferred-apply; cleaner to ship after the commit-hook refactor settles.

Blocks: acct-sw4i-m10.b4 (WAC integration). B.4 cannot ship without B.4-prep — WAC computes unit_cost from torn-read pair.

## Estimate

0.5 day. Pattern is well-known; implementation is mechanical.

## Future considerations

If torn-read measurement shows the seqlock retry rate is high (>5% under typical load), reconsider Option B (i128 packed). Tracked as deferred decision in the acceptance review.

Falsification: pre-fix t2_torn_read_probe captured (balance=38022000, qty=38021) in 15s; post-fix 0 torn reads / >100K observations across T1+T2+T3+T5. title: M10.A2 — XactCallback + SubXactCallback for transactional apply (correctness fix)
description:
The fix for the rollback bug confirmed in M10.A1. Refactors ledger_apply_balance_delta from synchronous shmem mutation to deferred-apply-at-commit, with full subtransaction support.

## Design (refined against external architectural review 2026-05-12)

Replace immediate shmem fetch_add with stage-and-defer pattern:

1. **Per-backend thread-local PENDING_STACK**: `RefCell<Vec<Vec<(u128 key, i64 amount_delta, i64 qty_delta)>>>` initialized with one empty frame for the top-level transaction. Each savepoint START pushes a fresh frame; ABORT pops; COMMIT merges-into-parent.

2. **Per-backend REGISTERED flag**: `RefCell<bool>` — set once per backend on first apply. Guards against repeated callback registration (callbacks accumulate; PG does NOT auto-deregister).

3. **Three XactCallback hooks** (all `#[pg_guard] extern \"C-unwind\"`):
   - **PreCommit** (`PgXactCallbackEvent::PreCommit`): walk PENDING_STACK[0]; check projected occupied_count + new-keys ≤ N_BUCKETS; raise pgrx::error! on overflow so SQL txn aborts cleanly. Reads HASH_TABLE.share() briefly to count current occupied. NO SPI in callback.
   - **Commit** (`PgXactCallbackEvent::Commit`): apply staged deltas. EXCLUSIVE on HASH_TABLE if any new keys; SHARED otherwise. Must succeed — panic here = backend crash. No SPI (rollup load was already done in apply call, captured in pending entry).
   - **Abort** (`PgXactCallbackEvent::Abort`): clear PENDING_STACK. No-op on shmem.

4. **SubXactCallback** (`SUBXACT_EVENT_START_SUB` push / `_COMMIT_SUB` merge / `_ABORT_SUB` pop). Registered alongside XactCallback at first apply.

## Critical concerns the implementation must address

**(a) Lazy rollup load TIMING.** Currently M6 lazy-loads rollup state in the apply call (before EXCLUSIVE) so the cell starts with the right cumulative state. After A.2, the apply call only STAGES the delta — the actual shmem cell creation happens in Commit callback. Two options:
  - Eager: lookup_rollup_seed at apply time (preserves M6 behavior but performs SPI in user txn instead of bgworker). Stored alongside the pending delta.
  - Lazy: lookup_rollup_seed inside Commit callback. CAN'T — Commit callback runs during txn teardown, SPI is unsafe.
  Decision: eager rollup-seed-capture at apply time; pending entry becomes `(key, amount_delta, qty_delta, Option<rollup_seed>)`.

**(b) Read-Your-Writes within transaction.** Old behavior: apply → immediate shmem mutation → in-txn `ledger_balance_lookup` returns post-apply value. New behavior: apply stages, Commit applies → in-txn lookup returns PRE-apply value. Document this as an architectural limitation. For acct workloads, post_batch_shmem doesn't read shmem post-apply within the same txn, so this is non-load-bearing. If a future workload needs RYW, options C (provisional shmem deltas + commit-confirm) or D (TX-local sidecar cache).

**(c) Multiple apply calls to same cell within one txn.** PENDING_STACK[0] may carry multiple deltas for the same key. Either collapse on push (key+delta merge) or apply N times in Commit. Collapsing is cleaner and matches expected acct usage (BOM rollup sums into one cell). Implementation: HashMap<u128, (i64, i64)> per frame, merged on push.

**(d) FFI guards on EVERY callback.** PG passes function pointers to callbacks; panic across plain `extern \"C\"` is UB. Use `#[pg_guard] pub extern \"C-unwind\"` on all four registered functions.

## Test method

Layered test plan:

**Test 1: rollback no-op (extends M10.A1).** Same scenario as A.1 — apply inside txn, rollback, assert drift = 0. This is the primary correctness assertion; flips A.1's assertion polarity in-place.

**Test 2: savepoint nesting.**
```rust
BEGIN;
  apply(A, +100);
  SAVEPOINT s1;
    apply(A, +50);
    SAVEPOINT s2;
      apply(A, +20);
    ROLLBACK TO s2;       -- discards +20
  RELEASE s1;             -- preserves +50, merges into top frame
COMMIT;
-- expected: shmem(A) = 150, drift = 0 against posting_lines.
```

**Test 3: cross-backend isolation.** Two backends apply concurrently in their own txns; verify PENDING_STACK is per-backend (no leakage between connection pool members).

**Test 4: PreCommit capacity rejection.** Pre-fill hash to N_BUCKETS - 1 occupied. Open new txn applying 5 new keys. Expect: COMMIT raises ERROR; shmem occupied unchanged; posting_lines rolled back.

**Test 5: multi-cell collapse within single txn.** apply(A, +100); apply(B, +50); apply(A, +30); COMMIT. Expect 2 cells (A=130, B=50) with single Commit-time atomic mutation per key.

**Test 6: drain interaction.** Apply in long txn; verify bgworker drain skips uncommitted state (PENDING_STACK is per-backend memory, not in shmem until Commit fires). Apply COMMIT; verify next drain tick picks up the cell.

**Test 7: RYW documentation.** Apply within txn; immediate `ledger_balance_lookup` returns PRE-apply value; this test PINS the documented behavior so a future regression is caught.

**Bench re-run.** Re-run M9 sweep (`bench/run-shmem-apply-sweep.sh`). Hypothesis: throughput drops 5-15% due to PENDING_STACK overhead + commit-time apply burst. If drop exceeds 25%, investigate (likely the apply-burst at commit serializes too long under HASH_TABLE EXCLUSIVE).

## Acceptance

- All 7 tests pass.
- Re-run M9 fan-in/fan-out at 20w × batch=1000 × 3×60s; report median tps + p99 ms. Document delta vs M9 in `poc/batch-ledger/bench/results-shmem-apply-A2.md`.
- A.1 assertion in tests/rollback_correctness_t1.rs flipped to drift = 0.
- M9 bench's `recon drift = 0` assertion still holds.

## Files touched

- poc/ledger-extension/src/lib.rs (callback registration in _PG_init OR first-apply lazy registration; pending stack; deferred apply)
- poc/ledger-extension/tests/transactional_t1.rs (new — 7 tests above)
- poc/batch-ledger/bench/results-shmem-apply-A2.md (new — perf delta report)
- README.md milestone block (add M10.A2)

## Dependencies

Blocks-on: acct-2733 (M10.A1 must confirm the bug first; if A.1 falsifies hypothesis, this issue closes scope-collapsed).

## Estimate

1 day (was 0.5 day pre-architectural-review; +0.5 day for SubXact + REGISTERED flag + RYW handling).

XactCallback + SubXactCallback + PENDING_STACK + REGISTERED implemented; rollback_correctness_t1 V1/V2 polarity flipped to drift=0; transactional_t1 6 tests (T2 savepoint nesting / T3 cross-backend / T5 multi-cell collapse / T6 drain isolation / T7 RYW limitation + T4 #[ignore]'d capacity check); invariants_t1 I1 updated for new return semantics; bench delta: fan-in -14.9% (in predicted band), fan-out +32.6% (commit burst amortizes lock cycling); 0 deadlocks; recon drift=0 preserved.

title: EPIC: ledger-extension M10 hardening — transactional correctness + WAC integration + error handling
description:
Follow-up epic to acct-sw4i (M1-M9 PoC closed 2026-05-12). The M9 bench validated the architectural premise (5.55× lift fan-out, 13× p99) but the PoC has known correctness and scenario-coverage gaps that block any production use of the apply path.

## Three exploration tracks

**Track A — Transactional rollback semantics (CORRECTNESS BLOCKER).**
Current apply path mutates shmem immediately on `ledger_apply_balance_delta(...)` call. PG transactions can roll back AFTER the apply via constraint violation, ROLLBACK, savepoint rollback, or backend crash. Result: shmem retains the delta while posting_lines does not. Ledger diverges silently.

**Track B — Complex scenarios.**
M9 only benched simple-transfer fan-in/fan-out at (period_id=1, currency_id=1, ledger_kind=1). Multi-currency, multi-period, multi-ledger_kind, WAC integration, concurrent read consistency, and bgworker backpressure are all untested.

**Track C — Error handling.**
Hash table full currently raises `error!` aborting the calling transaction. SPI errors in bgworker are log-swallowed. GUC reload on SIGHUP, deliberate panic cleanup, recon under concurrent writes — all unverified.

## Critical findings from 2026-05-12 architectural review against external recommendations

(See conversation pre-this-issue + bd memory state-2026-05-12-acct-sw4i-M9-shipped-M10-plan.)

**F1.** Track A scope is larger than initially planned. The naive "register Commit callback to defer apply" approach misses:
  - PreCommit vs Commit split (capacity validation in PreCommit because Commit cannot abort the txn — already WAL-flushed).
  - SubXactCallback for SAVEPOINT/ROLLBACK TO support (BLOCKER for general-purpose use inside acct).
  - Per-backend `REGISTERED` flag (callbacks accumulate; register-once-per-backend).
  - Thread-local `PENDING_STACK` (Vec<Vec<...>>) for nested savepoint support.

**F2.** WAC integration (B.4) has a torn-read hazard. `balance` and `qty` are separate `AtomicI64` fields. Reader doing `pool_value / pool_qty` between a writer's two `fetch_add` calls reads a torn pair. For simple transfers invisible (consumers only need balance). For WAC, silently wrong unit cost. Requires seqlock or AtomicI128 before B.4 can ship correctly.

## Sub-issue priority

Implementation order (P2 = critical path, P3 = layered coverage):

P2 path:
  acct-sw4i-m10.a1 — confirm rollback bug exists (1h gate)
  acct-sw4i-m10.a2 — XactCallback + SubXactCallback + PENDING_STACK + REGISTERED (1 day)
  acct-sw4i-m10.b4prep — seqlock for torn-read prevention (0.5 day)
  acct-sw4i-m10.b4 — post_batch_wac_shmem + bench (2-3 days)

P3 layered coverage:
  B.1/B.2/B.3 — multi-dimension scenario tests (~1 day total)
  B.5 — concurrent read consistency under load (replaces by b4prep if seqlock chosen)
  B.6 — bgworker backpressure
  B.7 — high-load-factor probe distance
  C.1 — hash table full as recoverable Result<i64>
  C.2 — bgworker SPI error escalation
  C.3 — crash recovery via SIGKILL
  C.4 — GUC SIGHUP reload smoke test
  C.5 — recon under concurrent writes
  C.6 — deliberate panic cleanup path

## Estimated wall-time

~7-10 days total. Track A + B.4 are the load-bearing 4-5 days; the rest is layered hardening that can ship piecemeal.

## Files of record

- poc/ledger-extension/src/lib.rs (current M9 implementation)
- poc/ledger-extension/README.md
- poc/batch-ledger/bench/results-shmem-apply.md (M9 bench numbers)
- poc/batch-ledger/db/migrations/0013_post_batch_shmem.up.sql (M8 integration)

## Decision: separate epic vs extending acct-sw4i

Filed as separate epic (this issue) because M9 validated a self-contained scope (PoC viability proof). M10 is hardening for use, not bench-extension.

title: Audit acct dispatchers that depend on FOR-UPDATE-on-accounts — contract for sw4i to preserve
description:
Prerequisite to acct-sw4i. We need to know exactly which dispatchers depend on FOR UPDATE on the accounts row for correctness (not just for the balance UPDATE) so the shmem rollup design preserves their semantics.

## Why this exists

sw4i was originally framed as a perf optimization (recover the +98% append-only win). Empirical work 2026-05-12 (fan-in/fan-out benches) + correctness analysis revealed sw4i is actually a HARD CORRECTNESS REQUIREMENT for append-only on cost-dispatched workloads. The shmem hash bucket isn't just a cache — it's the serialization primitive that replaces FOR UPDATE.

Before implementing sw4i, we need to know exactly which dispatcher paths the shmem design must preserve serialization for, and what each one's read-modify-write contract looks like.

## Scope

Audit every code site in acct that does:
- SELECT ... FROM accounts WHERE ... FOR UPDATE
- UPDATE accounts SET balance / qty

For each, document:
1. The dispatcher / wrapper that invokes it
2. The cost method(s) it serves
3. What state it reads (pool_value, pool_qty, both)
4. What it computes from that state (amount, unit_cost snapshot, etc.)
5. Whether the read-then-compute-then-write is genuinely atomic (acct-du2 R4)
6. What concurrent writer would break correctness if FOR UPDATE were removed
7. Whether sw4i shmem bucket CAS preserves the semantics or needs additional primitives

## Expected findings (hypotheses to verify)

H1: wac_perpetual outbound (_compute_amount_wac_perpetual_outbound) is the canonical case — FOR UPDATE on the value account, read pool_value + pool_qty, compute amount = qty × pool_value/pool_qty. CAS-able cleanly.

H2: wac_periodic / wac_retroactive outbound — also reads pool but result is the same as wac_perpetual at dispatch time (provisional). The close-hook recompute is a separate concern.

H3: fifo / lot_fifo outbound — FOR UPDATE on cost_layers / inventory_lots, NOT on accounts. sw4i shmem rollup doesn't need to preserve serialization here (their own locking is intact).

H4: standard cost dispatch — no pool read, no FOR UPDATE on accounts needed.

H5: post_cost_adjustment (live-pool adjust, acct-fii lineage) — reads pool under FOR UPDATE for per-class qty divisor. CAS-able but per-class semantics need care (R1).

H6: post_standard_cost_roll (acct-quca lineage) — reads pool qty for raw + fg + WIP revaluation. FOR UPDATE required (R7 audit-field correctness). Multiple accounts touched per call; whether shmem's per-bucket lock composes correctly is open.

H7: post_inventory_adjustment on WAC SKUs — reads pool for cost basis on negative adjustments. CAS-able.

H8: WO close orchestration (post_wo_complete pre-balance + residual sweep, acct-69e) — reads stock_wip + inv_value_wip pool under FOR UPDATE for solo-at-pool gating. Multi-row read-then-write; shmem CAS per-bucket may not compose. Open question.

## Deliverables

1. Audit table in research/sw4i-foreupdate-audit.md mapping every FOR-UPDATE-on-accounts site to its (dispatcher, cost method, contract, sw4i strategy) row.
2. Per-site: is shmem CAS sufficient, or does the site need a multi-bucket transaction primitive?
3. List of any dispatchers that CAN'T be supported by sw4i v1 (would need follow-up work).
4. Updated sw4i design doc reflecting the audit findings.

## Estimated wall-time

1-2 days. Pattern-grep + read each dispatcher body + walk the read-then-compute-then-write.

## Why P2

This is the missing piece before sw4i can be designed concretely. Without it, the shmem design risks missing a dispatcher's semantics and silently corrupting ledger under contention.
notes:
2026-05-12: previously framed as a HARD blocker for sw4i (acct-sw4i). On reflection that was over-cautious. Re-classified as 'related' parallel work.

sw4i PoC lives in poc/batch-ledger/ — a separate crate against acct_poc DB. The PoC can be built + benched without needing acct's full dispatcher contract; the PoC's questions are 'does pgrx ship a working shmem extension' and 'does CAS on shmem buckets correctly serialize WAC-style RMW' — both answerable against PoC functions.

The audit's findings actually apply when sw4i is BACKPORTED into acct's production path (acct-qb0q P8 territory). That's when dispatcher-by-dispatcher we need to confirm shmem CAS is sufficient or identify which dispatchers need additional primitives.

The three can run in parallel:
  - acct-sw4i: PoC implementation + bench
  - acct-tk3w: dispatcher audit (this issue) — informs backport
  - acct-qb0q (P8): backport synthesis — consumes both

title: Reservation system architectural exploration — separate from status, soft/hard, detailed/generic
description:
Architectural doubt flagged 2026-05-12. **This is an exploration, not a defined refactor.** User direct quote: 'I have doubts about our current reservation system (architecturally frail), and would probably want to rework how statuses, active vs inactive work, and treat allocations for work orders or sales orders separately from status.'

Clarification 2026-05-12: 'I am not arguing that reservations would be derived, only that they are separate from status. They can be soft or hard, be detailed (lot/inv #) or generic. Shipped vs not shipped is very relevant — you are decreasing inventory (any active vs non-active status has cost implications like a quantity change).'

Reservations are first-class rows (not derived). The doubt is about what 'status' is doing today and whether the dimensions reservations actually have are being represented well.

## Areas to explore (open)

### Reservations as separate from status

Today inventory_reservations.status (active/allocated/expired/shipped/cancelled) is doing several jobs:
- Marking whether the reservation is in-effect
- Encoding which document drove the latest transition
- Distinguishing 'committed pre-ship' (allocated) from 'tentative' (active)
- Marking the terminal state where inventory actually moved (shipped)

These may not be the same kind of thing. What if 'status' meant only one of these and the other concerns lived elsewhere?

### Soft vs hard reservations

Soft reservation = intent / tentative hold; can be displaced by higher-priority allocations or expire.
Hard reservation = commitment; cannot be touched until released by the owning document.

Current 'active' vs 'allocated' loosely reflects this distinction but the soft/hard semantics aren't first-class. What would change if soft/hard were an explicit dimension on the reservation row, and the transition rules (when can soft become hard? can hard go back to soft?) were enforced explicitly?

### Detailed vs generic reservations

Generic reservation = qty at (sku, location). 'I need 20 units somewhere in this warehouse'.
Detailed reservation = specific lot_id, unit_ids[], serial, etc. 'I need THESE 20 specific serial numbers'.

inventory_reservations has lot_id (acct-uze) and unit_ids[] (acct-sxl2) bolted on, but the schema isn't deliberately structured for the generic/detailed split. What would change if detailed-ness were explicit (e.g., a discriminator + nullable specificity columns)?

### Shipped vs not shipped is a real inventory change

When a reservation flips active→shipped, that is NOT a label change — inventory was actually consumed; cost flow happened. Lumping 'shipped' into the same enum as 'active'/'allocated'/'cancelled' obscures that some transitions are cost events and some are pure state-machine moves.

What would change if 'shipped' were tracked elsewhere (e.g., on the document that drove the shipment) and the reservation row simply ended its active life? Or if there were an explicit 'reservation_consumed' marker tied to the qty change?

### Allocations for WO vs SO

WO allocations and SO allocations both end up as 'allocated' status today but mean different things:
- WO: raw inventory committed to be consumed at WO start / op_arrival
- SO: FG inventory committed to be shipped out

What would change if allocation-target (WO vs SO vs other) were explicit, and the lifecycle rules diverged where their semantics actually diverge?

## Process

This issue is **research/design first, not implementation**. Deliverables of the exploration phase:

1. Audit every wrapper that touches inventory_reservations and catalog the implicit transitions and their meanings.
2. Audit every read site and classify by what dimension the read actually cares about.
3. Sketch 2-3 alternative shapes (NOT a single recommended shape) and walk each one against the existing flows.
4. Surface trade-offs honestly: what does each alternative break / what does it gain?

Then decide together what (if any) refactor to commit to.

## Relationship to acct-ujhn

acct-ujhn proposes Pattern A (derived) or Pattern B (document-state hooks). User has ruled out Pattern A here. acct-ujhn becomes a sub-case once the exploration converges.

## Out of immediate scope (PoC perf work)

User noted reservation interleave is not worth benching in PoC if the system may be overhauled. Dropped from the complicated-scenario PoC bench plan.

## Why P2

Architectural shape decisions get more expensive over time. Worth surfacing and exploring even without immediate implementation.

The exploration axes (status decomposition; soft/hard; detailed/generic; shipped-as-cost-relevant transitions) are folded into the acct-476a.2 design-note scope, which resolves reservation semantics under the alt-C no-gate posture — the two questions must be answered together at the seam. Original user quotes and full axis detail remain in this issue body as the record. See poc/design_research/convergence-decisions-2026-08-07.md.

title: Direction 3: PAC-style period-fixed dispatch for wac_periodic
description: acct-8hv2 audit direction 3. WAC dispatch's FOR UPDATE on accounts is the system's primary contention surface (audit measured 97% of wait_events on accounts). Decouple via period-fixed dispatch cost (Oracle PAC / SAP Material Ledger pattern). Same close-hook variance model; lock-free runtime dispatch. See --design for full scope + open Qs. Stability gain: throughput stops being capped by accounts-row serialization. Certainty gain: industry-validated pattern with known variance properties.
design:
acct-8hv2 audit direction 3 — decouple cost-method dispatch from accounts FOR UPDATE via period-fixed dispatch cost.

WHY: Today's WAC dispatch (wac_perpetual, wac_periodic, wac_retroactive) reads the running pool average under FOR UPDATE on the accounts row. THAT is the FOR UPDATE that serializes all writers to the same (sku, location, currency) pool. The audit (acct-8hv2) measured 100% of granted=false pg_locks samples on accounts.tuple AccessExclusiveLock; 97% of all wait_events are row-lock-related on accounts. Removing the FOR UPDATE at dispatch removes the single largest contention surface in the system.

DESIGN: PAC-STYLE PERIOD-FIXED DISPATCH (Oracle Process Cost, SAP Material Ledger pattern):
- During an open period P, all depletions on (sku, location, currency, cost_method='wac_periodic_v2') post at a fixed unit_cost = AVG(receipts value / qty) from the prior closed period.
- Receipts in period P post at their actual asserted cost (unchanged).
- At period close, wac_periodic_close_hook recomputes the period's actual average from in-period receipts and posts variance through variance_wac_periodic on each non-zero-delta depletion (already implemented).
- The DEPLETION dispatch path no longer reads under FOR UPDATE; it reads the period-start avg from a non-contended config table OR from materialized period-summary rows.
- Initial implementation: introduce 'wac_periodic_v2' as a new cost_method enum value. Migrate selected SKUs. Compare contention via acct-8hv2's sampler harness.

ALTERNATIVES CONSIDERED:
- wac_perpetual stays as the high-correctness option (depletions post at the live running avg, FOR UPDATE'd; needed for SKUs where intra-period variance is unacceptable).
- wac_periodic_v2 becomes the high-throughput option (depletions post at period-fixed; variance reconciled at close).
- wac_retroactive remains as-is (already does chronological replay; the FOR UPDATE there is unavoidable).

OPEN DESIGN QUESTIONS (raise BEFORE claiming):
- Q1: Where does the period-fixed avg live? Options: (a) new column on accounts (period_avg_cost), (b) materialized view per (sku, location, currency, period), (c) compute on-demand from posting_lines (slow). Lean: (b).
- Q2: First period for a SKU has no prior — what's the dispatch cost? Lean: standard_cost fallback.
- Q3: Does wac_periodic_close_hook still run? Yes — variance is still posted at close. The change is at runtime, not at close.
- Q4: What about mixed-cost-method parents (wac_periodic_v2 parent + standard component or vice versa)? Same routing as today's variance_material_mixed handling (acct-7eo).

DELIVERABLE SCOPE: a new mig (e.g., 0071) adding wac_periodic_v2 to the cost_method enum, the new period_avg materialization, the dispatcher's strategy registry row + _compute_amount_wac_periodic_v2_outbound function, T1 + T2 tests. NOT a wholesale conversion of existing SKUs.

DEPS: blocks-on nothing structural. Could ship in parallel with direction 1 (acct-xr5j) and direction 5 once they unblock the contention picture.
notes: Re-pointed 2026-08-07 (convergence Q9b): parent epic acct-qdp5 closed UNVERDICTED; this issue stands independently. PAC-style period-fixed dispatch for wac_periodic is an acct-main costing-layer direction — its fate rides the Q2 document-layer decision (acct-476a.2/.4), not the batch-ledger PoC.

title: Direction 5: contention observability + bound + alert
description: acct-8hv2 audit direction 5. The 1s6r workload's row-lock contention on accounts is fundamental (97% of wait_events). Don't fight it; instrument it; bound it; alert on it. See --design for deliverable scope. Stability gain: throughput ceiling becomes a real, monitored property, not an unknown. Certainty gain: SLOs have evidence.
design:
acct-8hv2 audit direction 5 — accept the contention; bound it; make the bound observable.

WHY: 97% of all wait_event samples in 1s6r are row-lock-related on accounts. Contention is fundamental to this ledger's correctness (FOR UPDATE on accounts is what guarantees WAC dispatch reads a stable running average). The architectural response is not to eliminate contention but to TREAT IT AS A FIRST-CLASS PROPERTY — instrument it, bound it, alert on it.

DELIVERABLES:
1. Observable bounds:
   - run_daily_reconciliation check that flags pg_stat_database deadlock-rate exceeding a configured threshold per period.
   - run_daily_reconciliation check that flags pg_stat_statements top-N by total_exec_time for FOR UPDATE-heavy queries exceeding a threshold.
   - Optional: a new lightweight cron-driven sampler that captures pg_stat_activity wait_event_type='Lock' counts at fixed intervals and aggregates into a table (e.g., wait_event_observations) — like inventory_movements but for contention.
2. Throughput SLO declaration:
   - Document the measured throughput floor (~211 ops/s with psync, ~234 ops/s sync) in perf_baseline_v2.md as the WORKLOAD-CEILING, not as a tunable.
   - Add T4 perf-baseline-history regression detector (similar to acct-ltza but scoped to the 1s6r workload shape).
3. Backpressure documentation:
   - Document the pgBouncer transaction-pooling pattern as the recommended frontend if writer count needs caps.
   - Document max-writer-concurrency knobs for the application tier (when one exists; currently Phase 0).

NON-GOALS:
- No raising the throughput ceiling.
- No new lock-elimination architecture (that's direction 3).
- No new sampler v2 (filed as acct-brqb).

DEPS: blocks-on nothing. Can ship in parallel with acct-xr5j (direction 1). Independent of acct-bdq6.
notes: Re-pointed 2026-08-07 (convergence Q9b): acct-qdp5 closed UNVERDICTED; this issue stands independently. Contention observability / bound / alert targets the acct main tree — deferred with the document layer under Q2.

title: Cross-wrapper contention matrix — measured tiered (Tier 1 singleton / Tier 2 pairwise / Tier 3 scale)
description: acct-8hv2 audit revealed the most consequential bottleneck in 1s6r is the cross-wrapper FOR UPDATE race between post_so_ship and post_customer_invoice on sales_order_lines rows (psync mode dropped post_customer_invoice setup p99 by 99.6%). There are likely other cross-wrapper races visible by static code review: post_op_move ↔ post_wo_complete on stock_wip + wo_events; post_po_receipt ↔ post_ap_bill on po_receipt_lines; post_customer_return ↔ post_customer_credit_memo on customer_return_lines. Build a wrapper × document-table FOR UPDATE incidence matrix; each cell with concurrent writers is a candidate for acct-bdq6's psync decision tree.
design:
acct-8hv2 audit direction 1 — cross-wrapper contention matrix BUILT BY MEASUREMENT, not static review.

WHY MEASUREMENT NOT STATIC REVIEW:
Static code grep tells us which cells COULD race; doesn't tell us if/how badly they DO. The deliverable is numbers per cell of the (wrapper × wrapper) matrix, with scale sensitivity for the cells that matter. Without numbers, this is theory and the prior audit's credibility lesson applies: predictions without measurement is exactly the pattern we are correcting.

CANDIDATE WRAPPERS (~18 — exclude obvious non-candidates):
  post_po_receipt, post_ap_bill, post_po_return,
  post_inventory_adjustment, post_cost_adjustment,
  post_so_allocate, post_so_ship, post_customer_invoice,
  post_customer_return, post_ar_payment,
  post_wo_start, post_op_move, post_wo_complete, post_scrap,
  post_wo_close_unproduced, post_osp_ship, post_osp_receive,
  post_lot_transfer.
EXCLUDED (one-shot or non-contention-bound): post_eco_approve,
  post_standard_cost_roll, post_journal_entry,
  post_service_bill, post_expense_report,
  post_cost_adjustment_retroactive,
  post_ap_payment, post_customer_credit_memo, post_vendor_debit_memo,
  post_so_ship_psync (variant of so_ship; measured separately).

TIERED MEASUREMENT METHODOLOGY:

TIER 1 — Per-wrapper singleton characterization (~90 min).
  For each candidate W:
    5×60s run with T4_OP_WEIGHTS=W:1.0 (all 32 writers do only W); sampler ON.
    Captures per-W: hot-zone signature (top relations by Lock.tuple sample
    count + transactionid wait count), throughput solo, p99 solo,
    section decomposition solo, deadlocks delta.
  Output: 18-row singleton fingerprint table.

TIER 2 — Pairwise interference (filtered subset, ~2-3 hr).
  Filter: only run pairs (W1, W2) where TIER 1 fingerprints' hot zones
  overlap (e.g., both lock sales_order_lines OR both lock the same
  accounts pool kind). Likely 10-25 pairs survive of C(18,2)=153.
  For each surviving pair:
    5×60s run with T4_OP_WEIGHTS=W1:0.5,W2:0.5; sampler ON;
    T4_OVERLAP_POOL=4 (writers pick from 4 SKUs/customers instead of 50)
    to induce worst-case race intensity. Without forced overlap, statistical
    dilution can hide real races.
  Per-cell deliverable (NUMBERS):
    columns: W1, W2, T_mix/avg(T_solo), W1_p99_mix/W1_p99_solo,
             W2_p99_mix/W2_p99_solo, Lock.tuple_mix/sum(solo), classification
    classification rules:
      INDEPENDENT      — T_mix ≈ avg(T_solo), p99 unchanged, lock counts additive
      SHIELD           — T_mix ≈ min(T_solo), no p99 amplification either side
      RACE-CONFIRMED   — T_mix < both T_solo AND one p99 amplifies >2× AND
                         Lock.tuple counts super-additive
      RACE-PLAUSIBLE-BUT-NOISE — directionally a race but inside rig IQR

TIER 3 — Scale sensitivity (5 confirmed races × 4 scales × 5 reps = ~3 hr).
  For each RACE-CONFIRMED pair from Tier 2:
    Sweep T4_WRITERS ∈ {8, 16, 32, 64}; 5×60s each.
  Captures: amplification curve. Does the race scale linearly with writers,
  superlinearly, or cliff at some N? This is the architectural-stability
  question — does the system get WORSE at scale, or does it stabilize?

TIER 4 — Synthesis.
  Deliverable: research/cross-wrapper-contention-matrix.md with:
    1. Tier 1 singleton fingerprint table (18 rows × ~6 metrics)
    2. Tier 2 pairwise matrix (one row per measured pair) with
       classification + numbers
    3. Tier 3 scale-amplification curves for confirmed races
    4. Recommended interventions per race (direction 2/3 candidate, direction 5
       alerting candidate, or below-noise/ignore)

HARNESS EXTENSIONS REQUIRED (NOT YET BUILT):
  1. T4_OP_WEIGHTS env var — string parser like "so_ship:0.5,customer_invoice:0.5".
     Replaces hardcoded OP_WEIGHTS array. Default unset = current 9-op mix.
     ~50 lines Rust in tests/load_phase1_mixed_workload.rs.
  2. T4_OVERLAP_POOL env var — sizes the (SKU, customer, vendor) pools writers
     pick from. Currently controlled by T4_BENCH_SKUS=50 etc.; this exposes a
     forced-overlap mode where all writers pick from a small subset. ~10 lines.
  3. scripts/run-audit-tiered.sh — driver that loops Tier 1 / 2 / 3 scenarios
     with the right env vars, captures logs, produces a CSV of per-scenario
     metrics. ~120 lines bash. Models on scripts/run-audit-replicate.sh.
  Sampler v1 (tests/common/pg_locks_sampler.rs) is already in place; no
  changes at this tier. Sampler v2 (ctid → row-key, acct-brqb) only matters
  if Tier 4 surfaces a need to disambiguate hot rows within same relation.

TIME ESTIMATE:
  Harness extensions:              3-4 hr
  Tier 1 measurement:              1.5 hr
  Tier 1 analysis + filter pairs:  1 hr
  Tier 2 measurement:              2-3 hr
  Tier 2 analysis + select Tier 3: 1 hr
  Tier 3 measurement:              3 hr
  Tier 4 writeup:                  2 hr
  TOTAL:                           ~13-15 hours

STOP POINTS (will stop at each):
  1. After harness extensions land + compile clean + smoke-tested with one
     Tier 1 run. Surface to user.
  2. After Tier 1 — singleton fingerprint table. User decides pair filter
     (or accepts auto-filter).
  3. After Tier 2 — pairwise matrix. User decides which races scale-sweep
     (or accepts auto-filter).
  4. After Tier 3 — scale curves.
  5. After Tier 4 — final matrix doc.

OPEN QUESTIONS (raise BEFORE claiming):
  Q1. Forced-overlap (T4_OVERLAP_POOL=4) is worst-case probe. Do we ALSO
      want natural-overlap measured per pair (doubles Tier 2 time), or is
      worst-case sufficient for the matrix?
  Q2. Tier 3 scales — 8/16/32/64 reasonable, or also include 128/256
      (rig may saturate before then)?
  Q3. 3-way+ combinations — C(18,3)=816 triples too many. The realistic
      9-op mix from existing load_phase1_mixed_workload is the de-facto
      integration test. Skip 3-way unless user wants it explicit.

EXPLICITLY NOT IN SCOPE:
  - 3-way+ combinations (deferred per Q3).
  - Production-tier instrumentation.
  - Sampler v2 (acct-brqb).
  - CHANGING wrappers based on findings — the matrix is the deliverable, not
    the fix. Direction 2 (acct-nczy) consumes this matrix; this issue only
    produces it.

DEPS UPDATE:
  acct-nczy (direction 2) blocked-by THIS issue — confirmed.
  This issue blocks-on nothing structural; ready to claim after user
  buy-in on methodology + answers to Q1/Q2/Q3.

title: E2.5-followup: post_so_allocate + post_so_ship pinned-reservation handling
description:
Complete the lot-pinned reservation lifecycle. E2.5 (acct-knuu) added p_lot_id + p_lot_specific to reserve_inventory; mig 0044 schema columns inventory_reservations.lot_id + lot_specific in place. But post_so_allocate (mig 0018) and post_so_ship (mig 0050) are pin-blind: pinned reservations flow through allocate without residual validation, and so_ship's lot_fifo branch reads p_lines.lot_id without consulting reservation pins.

W1 — post_so_allocate validates pinned lot residual: for each pinned reservation in (so_id, status='active'), look up _inventory_lot_remaining_qty(lot_id, receipt_date) under FOR UPDATE on stock_available; raise P0053 'pinned_lot_underfulfilled' if residual < qty.

W2 — post_so_ship consults reservation pins in lot_fifo branch: lookup pinned reservations matching so_line_id; resolve cases (0/1/N pins × NULL/match/mismatch caller lot_id). Raise P0054 'ship_lot_pin_conflict' on caller-vs-pin mismatch; P0055 'ambiguous_pinned_reservation' on >1 pins with no caller lot_id.

W3 — t1 tests: lot_so_allocate_pinned_t1 + lot_so_ship_pinned_t1.

Single mig 0053. Per saved memory feedback-favor-migration-granularity, scope is one logical lifecycle completion.
acceptance_criteria: W1 post_so_allocate validates pinned lot residual; raises P0053 when short. W2 post_so_ship consults reservation pins; routes 0/1/N pins × NULL/match/mismatch correctly. P0054 + P0055 raised on conflict/ambiguous. All existing tests pass; t1 covers both wrappers. ci-check clean.

title: W4: FG-FIFO end-to-end (post_so_ship + apply_event FG + WO parent gates)
description:
Phase E1 follow-up W4. Extends FIFO from raw materials to finished goods. Three coordinated changes:

(1) apply_event E1 block: widen gate from inv_value_raw to (inv_value_raw, inv_value_fg) on both DR (receipt-side layer creation) and CR (issue-side depletion writeback) sides. Layer creation triggers when post_wo_complete drains WIP to FG (debit=inv_value_fg, FIFO parent). Depletion triggers when post_so_ship sells FG (credit=inv_value_fg, FIFO SKU).

(2) post_so_ship (mig 0018 line 476): drop FIFO from IN ('fifo','lot') gate. Add FIFO branch that walks _fifo_walk_layers for v_unit_cost audit field on so_shipment_lines (mirroring the WAC pattern's v_value_balance/v_qty_balance after FOR UPDATE). The dispatcher then walks again for the actual ledger amount via _compute_amount_fifo_outbound (already registered).

(3) Parent SKU gates at post_wo_start (line 1189), post_op_move (line 1497), post_wo_complete (line 1757): widen NOT IN list from ('standard','wac_*') to include 'fifo'. For value-leg dispatch, FIFO parent is treated as WAC parent (running avg from WIP pool) since WIP-FIFO is out of scope. The drain at wo_complete debits inv_value_fg → apply_event's E1 block creates the FG layer.

End-to-end scenario: SKU-FG-FIF cost_method='fifo'. Manufacture via post_wo_start → post_op_move → post_wo_complete creates FG layer at WIP-pool-avg. Sell via post_so_ship walks FG layers FIFO.

title: E1.2: _compute_amount_fifo_outbound dispatcher + apply_event layer writes (mig 0032)
description:
Phase E1 sub-issue. Ships db/migrations/0032_fifo_dispatcher.{up,down}.sql with the FIFO compute and apply paths.

DISPATCHER:
CREATE OR REPLACE FUNCTION _compute_amount_fifo_outbound(p_event JSONB, p_d_acct accounts, p_c_acct accounts, p_idx INT) RETURNS BIGINT
- Resolves credit-side SKU + location (R2 credit-first per acct-7py).
- Walks layers ORDER BY receipt_date ASC, layer_id ASC FOR UPDATE.
- For each layer: residual = original_quantity - SUM(depletions.depleted_quantity); allocate min(residual, qty_remaining).
- Accumulates total_amount += allocation × layer.unit_cost.
- Returns total_amount. P0006 if layers exhaust before qty fulfilled (cost_method_layer_exhausted).
- Registers in cost_method_strategies INSERT.

DEPLETIONS WRITEBACK (open design call — choose at implementation time):
Option A: separate _fifo_write_depletions(p_posting_line_id) helper called from apply_event AFTER posting_line INSERT. Re-walks under FOR UPDATE (deterministic given same state since dispatcher held lock through to apply_event).
Option B: change dispatcher signature to RETURNS JSONB carrying allocation plan; apply_event reads plan and writes depletions.

Recommendation per saved memory plan-phase-e1-fifo: Option A (cleaner registry pattern, idempotent re-walk under same FOR UPDATE).

APPLY_EVENT D-BLOCK EXTENSION:
- For receipt reasons (po_receipt, etc.) on FIFO SKUs: after the inventory_movements row writes, INSERT a cost_layers row with original_quantity = receipt qty, unit_cost = receipt unit_cost, receipt_movement_id = movement.movement_id, receipt_date = business_date.
- For issue reasons on FIFO SKUs: call _fifo_write_depletions to write per-layer depletions rows.
- Populate posting_line_inventory.cost_layer_id with FIRST consumed layer's layer_id (per §4.E.E1 plan note).

FIFO COMPONENTS in WO consumption: rm_issue_to_wo on a fifo SKU triggers dispatcher per acct-7py credit-first SKU resolution. Verify component_sku is picked correctly.

TESTS: tests/fifo_dispatcher_t1.rs covering — receipt creates layer, single-layer issue, multi-layer-spanning issue, layer exhaustion P0006, layer immutability via UPDATE attempt rejection, dispatcher math correctness across multiple cost levels.

FIXTURE IMPACT: SKU-FIF in tests/common/mod.rs currently has no inv_value_raw account (D2 test fifo_sku_does_not_write_movement and D3 test fifo_sku_still_blocks_at_dispatcher tests rely on this). After E1.2: those D2/D3 boundary tests need rewriting to assert FIFO succeeds and writes movements + layer rows; SKU-FIF/MAIN/USD inv_value_raw + stock_available accounts likely need adding to fixture.
close_reason: Shipped in 63a9bdd. _compute_amount_fifo_outbound + _fifo_walk_layers + _fifo_write_depletions registered + apply_event D-block extended for FIFO receipts (cost_layers INSERT) and issues (cost_layer_depletions INSERT). post_posting_lines qty-leg gates widened. 12 T1 cases + 5 obsolete conformance cases removed. Suite 770/0/9. Wrapper integration (post_po_receipt etc.) remains follow-up.

title: E1.1: cost_layers + cost_layer_depletions schema (mig 0031)
description:
Phase E1 sub-issue. Ships db/migrations/0031_cost_layers_schema.{up,down}.sql with the FIFO foundation tables.

Schema (per cost-methods-subledger-design.md §7.2-§7.3):

CREATE TABLE cost_layers (
  layer_id BIGSERIAL,
  product_id UUID NOT NULL REFERENCES skus(id),
  legal_entity_id SMALLINT NOT NULL REFERENCES legal_entities(id) DEFAULT 1,
  cost_book_id SMALLINT NOT NULL REFERENCES cost_books(id) DEFAULT 1,
  location_id UUID NOT NULL REFERENCES locations(id),
  receipt_movement_id BIGINT,  -- FK inventory_movements (movement_id, movement_date) composite
  receipt_date DATE NOT NULL,
  original_quantity NUMERIC(19,6) NOT NULL CHECK (original_quantity > 0),
  unit_cost NUMERIC(19,4) NOT NULL CHECK (unit_cost >= 0),
  cost_currency CHAR(3) NOT NULL,
  created_at TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL DEFAULT clock_timestamp(),
  PRIMARY KEY (layer_id, receipt_date)
) PARTITION BY RANGE (receipt_date);

CREATE TABLE cost_layer_depletions (
  depletion_id BIGSERIAL,
  layer_id BIGINT NOT NULL,    -- references cost_layers via fk to (layer_id, receipt_date)
  layer_receipt_date DATE NOT NULL,
  issue_movement_id BIGINT,    -- FK inventory_movements composite
  issue_date DATE NOT NULL,
  depleted_quantity NUMERIC(19,6) NOT NULL CHECK (depleted_quantity > 0),
  unit_cost NUMERIC(19,4) NOT NULL,
  cost_amount BIGINT NOT NULL,  -- INTEGER cents to match posting_lines.amount BIGINT
  posting_line_id BIGINT REFERENCES posting_lines(id),
  created_at TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL DEFAULT clock_timestamp(),
  PRIMARY KEY (depletion_id, issue_date),
  FOREIGN KEY (layer_id, layer_receipt_date) REFERENCES cost_layers(layer_id, receipt_date)
) PARTITION BY RANGE (issue_date);

- 24-month partition window pre-baked 2026-01..2027-12 (mirrors mig 0025 pattern).
- pg_cron rollover for both tables on 25th-of-month creating next-month + month-after.
- Indexes: (product_id, location_id, receipt_date) WHERE remaining_qty > 0 (computed); (layer_id) on cost_layer_depletions.
- Helper function _cost_layer_remaining_qty(p_layer_id, p_receipt_date) RETURNS NUMERIC for residual computation.
- Activate cost_layer_id BIGINT on posting_line_inventory: NO FK enforced (composite PK on cost_layers means simple FK won't work; document as soft pointer audited via recon).

DESIGN INVARIANTS (per cost-methods doc §7.2):
- Layers immutable after creation. Enforce via append-only trigger on cost_layers (mirror posting_lines pattern).
- One layer per receipt; no consolidation.
- No current_quantity column on cost_layers; residual computed.

TESTS: tests/cost_layers_t1.rs schema invariants — partitions exist, FK constraints, append-only blocks UPDATE/DELETE, partition rollover idempotent, _cost_layer_remaining_qty helper math.

Note: cost_amount uses BIGINT cents (matches posting_lines.amount/posting_lines.qty integer convention; whole project uses BIGINT for monetary amounts per CLAUDE.md). receipt/depleted quantities use NUMERIC(19,6) because skus may have fractional units and FIFO walks are exact.
close_reason: Shipped in 037d1e0. Schema + 24 T1 cases passing. cost_layers + cost_layer_depletions partitioned tables (24-mo window each), composite FK enforced, append-only triggers, _cost_layer_remaining_qty helper. cost_layer_id on posting_line_inventory documented as soft pointer per E1.3 recon plan.

title: Phase E1: FIFO/LIFO via cost_layers + cost_layer_depletions
description:
Phase E1 of the acct-wb75 convergence plan. Adds FIFO cost method (and LIFO follow-up) on top of the inventory_movements foundation shipped in Phase D.

Per research/posting-lines-convergence-plan.md §4.E.E1 and research/cost-methods-subledger-design.md §7.2-§7.4, FIFO uses an immutable cost_layers table (one row per receipt) + cost_layer_depletions (one row per layer drawn at issue). Greedy walk under FOR UPDATE ORDER BY receipt_date ASC. posting_line_inventory.cost_layer_id (currently nullable BIGINT no FK) gets activated to point at first consumed layer.

Schema invariants (cost-methods doc §7.2):
- Layer rows are immutable after creation.
- One cost_layers row per receipt (no consolidation).
- No 'current_quantity' column on cost_layers — residual computed via SUM(cost_layer_depletions.depleted_quantity).

Sub-issues follow Phase D's D1-D6 cadence per feedback-favor-migration-granularity:
- E1.1: schema (cost_layers + cost_layer_depletions partitioned tables, 24-mo window, pg_cron rollover, FK activation)
- E1.2: dispatcher (_compute_amount_fifo_outbound + receipt-side layer creation in apply_event D-block + multi-layer depletions writeback)
- E1.3: recon check #8 (per-product-location residual = on-hand qty)

Property test: tests/property_fifo_consistency.rs covering 7 invariants per saved memory plan-phase-e1-fifo.

Out of scope for this epic: LIFO (would need ALTER TYPE ADD VALUE; LIFO follow-up issue if needed), Lot (Phase E2), Serial (Phase E3).

title: C1: posting_line_inventory schema + backfill + dispatcher
description:
Phase C main work: posting_line_inventory extension table + backfill from existing posting_lines + _post_posting_lines_apply_event dispatcher hook. Per research/posting-lines-convergence-plan.md §4.C.

Schema (1:1 join with posting_lines.id):
- posting_line_id BIGINT PRIMARY KEY REFERENCES posting_lines(id)
- product_id UUID NOT NULL REFERENCES skus(id)
- quantity NUMERIC(19,6) NOT NULL  (mirrors current posting_lines.qty for inventory rows; will eventually replace it)
- qty_uom VARCHAR(10) NOT NULL DEFAULT 'EA'
- unit_cost NUMERIC(19,4)  (NULL for non-cost-bearing rows)
- cost_layer_id BIGINT  (FK to cost_layers; NULL until Phase E1)
- lot_id BIGINT  (FK to inventory_lots; NULL until Phase E2)
- unit_id BIGINT  (FK to inventory_units; NULL until Phase E3)
- cost_method_at_event cost_method NOT NULL  (snapshot for audit)
- created_at TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL DEFAULT clock_timestamp()

Backfill: for every existing posting_line with qty IS NOT NULL, insert a row with product_id from credit-first account.sku_id. Preflight audit (acct-wb75.2.1) ensures clean derivation.

Dispatcher: _post_posting_lines_apply_event writes the extension row atomically alongside posting_lines INSERT for inventory-touching events.

Recon: SUM(posting_line_inventory.quantity signed) == SUM(posting_lines.qty signed) per (sku, location) — added to run_daily_reconciliation.

title: DECISION: lift acct-2thf (account_kind enum → row table) from threshold-gated to immediate?
description:
The synthesis recommends lifting acct-2thf from its current 'threshold-gated, do it when we hit ~80 enum values' posture (we're at 46) to 'do it now' P2 posture. The threshold was always a soft signal; the structural drift (industry uses chart-of-accounts row tables; we use a PG enum) is real regardless of value count. Lifting before multi-entity (acct-3gzh) prevents sequence pain — multi-entity migrations either inherit the enum constraint or have to redo per-entity account setup post-lift.

This issue is a decision request, not implementation. The implementation lives in acct-2thf itself; this issue closes once you say 'yes, lift it' or 'no, keep threshold-gated' and notes are updated on acct-2thf accordingly.

References:
- research/architecture-synthesis.md §5.3 (Account taxonomy comparison)
- research/architecture-synthesis.md §6.2 (gap-action: acct-2thf gated on a soft threshold)
- research/architecture-synthesis.md §10.1 (issue catalog: lift recommendation)
- research/architecture-synthesis.md §10.4 (cross-walk: blocks acct-3gzh / acct-w1v3 / acct-v9sq / acct-3uh)
- Existing issue: acct-2thf

Synthesis recommendation: yes, lift to P2 immediate. Cost is moderate (M effort: new account_kinds row table + enum→FK lookup replacement in plpgsql + sweep across _post_transfers_* and post_* functions); unblock-effect on multi-entity / chart-of-accounts work is real.

title: acct-1cer.payment_workflows: property test for post_ar_payment + post_ap_payment
description:
Property test binary covering post_ar_payment and post_ap_payment in one file (single-event drains share the same shape).

## Scope

- post_ar_payment: cash DR / ar CR per (customer, currency)
- post_ap_payment: ap DR / cash CR per (vendor, currency)

Both are caller-supplied amount, no cost dispatch — the simple-workflow shape.

## Random ops

For each of N customer/vendor counterparties, generate a sequence of payment ops with random amounts. Assert:

1. Per (counterparty, currency): SUM(payment.amount) == ar.balance_delta (or ap.balance_delta with sign reversed).
2. Cash account net delta == sum of ar inflows minus sum of ap outflows for the same currency.
3. Idempotency: replay returns same id, no duplicate transfers.
4. Negative or zero amount → P0039 / P0042.
5. Standard I1-I7 invariants.

Partial payment sequences should drain ar (or ap) to 0 then potentially overdraw — overdraw should NOT trip accounts_check because both ar and ap are flexible-direction (debit-normal / credit-normal stay non-negative; opposite direction allowed).

## Pattern

PROPTEST_CASES default 100, --test-threads=1, mod common, assert_invariants_hold per op. ~400-500 lines.

## Acceptance

- tests/property_payment_workflows.rs lands, 100 cases pass.
- Asserts per-(counterparty,currency) balance reconciliation against payment.amount.
- Asserts idempotency dual-check shape on both fns.
close_reason: Closed

- Per (counterparty, currency): cleared-account delta == sum of lines.
- Staging accounts (ar_unsettled / ap_unsettled) UNTOUCHED.
- Idempotency.
- I1-I7.

## Pattern

title: acct-1cer.so_ship: property test for post_so_ship full surface
description:
## Why

property_ap9_audit_ledger_consistency.rs (acct-ct0p) pins post_so_ship's AP9/R7 invariant (transfer.amount == qty × audit_unit_cost) but is intentionally narrow — single happy path with snapshot-vs-ledger consistency. The fuller surface is uncovered:

- Multi-line ships (interleaved so_lines, mixed cost methods on different SKUs in the same batch)
- Reservation lifecycle transitions (active → shipped, allocated → shipped)
- Cost dispatch behaviors:
  - standard SKU: cogs at resolve_standard_cost_at
  - wac_perpetual SKU: cogs at FG running avg, R1 per-class qty divisor
- Cumulative qty constraints (P0038 over-ship)
- Validation gates (P0037 invalid so / line, empty p_lines, missing required fields)
- Multi-currency (line.currency drives ar_unsettled / revenue / cogs partition)
- Tax leg routing when tax_amount > 0
- Idempotency dual-check (R6) under repeated calls

This is the Slice C ship-side mirror of property_po_receipt_invariants on the AP receive-side.

## Scope

New tests/property_so_ship.rs. Generate fixtures with N customers + N so_lines (1-3 lines per case, mix of standard + wac_perpetual SKUs at different ship locations). Pre-seed FG pools at  per SKU.

Random op sequence:
- Ship(so_line_idx, qty) bounded by cumulative qty_ordered
- (Optional: Reserve(so_line_idx, qty) before Ship to test allocated→shipped transition)

Per-ship assertions:
- I1-I7 (assert_invariants_hold)
- For each so_line: cumulative qty_shipped ≤ qty_ordered (P0038 invariant from caller side)
- For each event posted: transfer.amount == qty × so_shipment_lines.unit_cost (R7/AP9 pin)
- Cost dispatch correct per SKU's cost_method:
  - standard: ledger amount = qty × resolve_standard_cost_at
  - wac_perpetual: ledger amount = qty × (pre-ship inv_value_fg.balance / per-class signed qty)
- ar_unsettled receives qty × unit_price (revenue) + tax_amount (if tax > 0)
- inv_value_fg drains by qty × unit_cost
- COGS receives qty × unit_cost (P&L recognition)
- so_shipment_lines.cost_method_at_ship snapshot matches sku.cost_method at ship time (mig 0087)
- Reservation status flips: active → shipped (when Reserve was called pre-Ship)

## Catches

- AP9/R7 drift on the broader ship surface (multi-line interactions)
- Cost-method dispatch bugs surfaced by future FIFO/lot work (acct-8gg)
- Reservation lifecycle drift (acct-ujhn risk)
- Multi-currency partition leak (revenue/cogs/ar_unsettled by currency)
- Idempotency replay races

## Acceptance

- New tests/property_so_ship.rs ≥100 cases under PROPTEST_CASES
- Uses assert_invariants_hold from tests/common/mod.rs

## Effort

~½-1 day (multi-line scaffold needs more setup than po_return; ~600-700 lines)

## Surfaced from

acct-1cer follow-up triage 2026-05-06 — 4th of 4 high-risk picks. Closes the umbrella's 'cost-event reason side' coverage.

Reservation lifecycle deferred (covered by acct-ujhn). Multi-currency deferred (orthogonal scaffolding lift).
