## Why

post_standard_cost_roll is rare-ops, high-blast-radius: walks all open inv_value_raw + inv_value_fg pools and revalues against (Δstd × per-class qty); with p_revalue_wip=TRUE also walks inv_value_wip pools. Touches every SKU's pool at once. Has a known unfixed AP3 finding under acct-quca (WIP-reval reads paired stock_wip qty without FOR UPDATE; concurrent op_move skews the variance amount).

Integration test (tests/standard_cost.rs) covers the happy path + a few error cases. Random-scenario property coverage missing.

## Scope

New tests/property_standard_cost_roll.rs. Generate fixtures with N SKUs at varying pool states (some empty, some non-empty raw, some non-empty fg, some open WIP at multiple routing ops with mixed parent_sku × routing_op pools). Random sequences of:
- post_standard_cost_roll without WIP (gates on no-WIP-present)
- post_standard_cost_roll with p_revalue_wip=TRUE
- Interleave with adjust IN / adjust OUT to grow / shrink pools mid-roll
- Multiple consecutive rolls (Δstd compounding correctly)

Assert I1-I7 invariants hold post-each-roll, plus:
- raw + fg pool revaluation correct: pool.balance_after - pool.balance_before == Δstd × per-class qty (within ±1 BIGINT truncation)
- variance_std_cost_roll posted exactly Δstd × qty per pool
- variance_wip_revaluation posted exactly Δstd × stock_wip.qty per (sku, routing_op) WIP pool
- no orphan transfers_provisional rows from a roll (rolls don't flag)

## Catches

- AP3 lock-gap on stock_wip read (acct-quca finding) — concurrent ops between roll's qty read and value mutation should surface
- Off-by-one between balance update and per-class qty divisor
- Idempotency drift on retry
- Standard-cost cache invalidation if any (skus.standard_cost is gone post-mig-0027 but resolve_standard_cost_at could surface skew)

## Acceptance

- New tests/property_standard_cost_roll.rs ≥100 cases under PROPTEST_CASES
- Uses assert_invariants_hold from tests/common/mod.rs
- Documents what gets caught (AP3 surface + ledger consistency)
- Ships independently of acct-quca fix; if acct-quca's bug surfaces in a case, file as P2 regression

## Effort

~½ day (matches other property_*.rs binaries: 400-600 lines)

## Surfaced from

acct-1cer follow-up triage 2026-05-06.
close_reason: Shipped tests/property_standard_cost_roll.rs (100 cases, ~17s, 84th test binary). RawFg (60%) + WipPresent (40%) modes. Asserts balance delta == Δstd × pool_qty per-class for raw/fg pools and Δstd × stock_wip.qty for WIP pools, plus I1-I7 invariants and P0006 gate firing. acct-quca's concurrency lock-gap remains out of scope (concurrent-writer test needed).

title: acct-7t4.6: yield variance at wo_complete (variance_yield_byproduct)
description:
Sub of acct-7t4 (umbrella). Depends on acct-7t4.3 (the by-product pre-pass exists) — strictly speaking can ship before 7t4.4/.5 since it only operates on the qty side.

Adds the planned-vs-actual yield variance at wo_complete. Industry-standard ERPs (SAP / Oracle / D365) all surface this as a discrete variance line; without it, the by-product feature is half-baked per the project owner.

## Schema additions

ALTER TYPE account_kind ADD VALUE IF NOT EXISTS 'variance_yield_byproduct';

Seed: variance_yield_byproduct USD + EUR, normal_side='unrestricted' (favorable = credit, unfavorable = debit).

## Function changes

post_wo_complete: at the same pre-pass walking wo_by_products, AFTER the per-treatment qty + value emissions, compute yield variance per row:

variance_qty = actual_qty - planned_qty
- variance_qty > 0 (we produced MORE than planned): favorable; the by-product fg gets unit_value × |variance_qty| more value than the snapshot would have predicted. For nrv_credit, the parent WIP got drained by unit_value × actual_qty, so the favorable variance is implicitly captured in the larger drain. For yield variance reporting, we want a SEPARATE line that surfaces this for analytics.
- variance_qty < 0 (we produced LESS than planned): unfavorable.

Variance leg (only for nrv_credit and disposal_cost rows; negligible has unit_value=0 so variance is always zero):
- (actual_qty - planned_qty) × unit_value posted as:
  - For nrv_credit: variance_yield_byproduct DR/CR / inv_value_fg(by_product) DR/CR (signed by direction). This separates the yield-variance contribution from the snapshotted NRV value.
  - For disposal_cost: variance_yield_byproduct DR/CR / accrued_disposal_liability(vendor) DR/CR. Adjusts the accrual to reflect actual qty.

Alternative (simpler): the value-leg in the pre-pass uses actual_qty (not planned_qty). The variance is then INHERENT in the actual_qty × unit_value drain — no separate variance line needed.

DESIGN CHOICE TO RESOLVE: which approach is correct per industry standard? SAP's Assembly Variance is typically a discrete line for analytics; Oracle does it similarly. We'll go with discrete variance line (option A) for analytic clarity. Document in migration comment.

## Tests

- planned_eq_actual_no_variance: actual_qty == planned_qty → variance_yield_byproduct unaffected
- planned_lt_actual_favorable: actual > planned → variance_yield_byproduct credit (favorable)
- planned_gt_actual_unfavorable: actual < planned → variance_yield_byproduct debit (unfavorable)
- variance_with_nrv_credit_balances: by_product fg + variance line + parent WIP drain all balance per (ledger_kind, currency)
- variance_with_disposal_cost_inventoriable: variance against accrued_disposal_liability adjusts accrual to actual

## Acceptance

- Migration up + down for account_kind + seeds
- post_wo_complete updated to compute + post variance per by-product row
- All existing tests pass; new variance tests pass
- ci-check clean
- bd close acct-7t4 only after all 6 sub-issues + this one are closed
close_reason: Closed

title: acct-7t4.5: post_ap_bill kind='disposal_match' + tolerance handling
description:
Sub of acct-7t4 (umbrella). Depends on acct-7t4.4 (accrued_disposal_liability + disposal_cost flow must exist).

Closes the AP-side reconciliation loop. Disposal vendor sends a bill for actual waste pickup; we match it against the WO-time accrual.

## Schema additions

vendor_bill_lines.kind currently CHECK (kind IN ('po_match', 'service')). Extend to include 'disposal_match'.

vendor_bill_lines new optional columns for disposal_match:
- disposal_wo_event_id UUID — nullable; references wo_events(id) for the originating WO completion. Optional but recommended for audit trail.
- by_product_no INT — nullable; references the wo_by_products row by composite key (disposal_wo_event_id wo_id, by_product_no).
- Existing po_line_id remains NULL for disposal_match (only po_match uses it).

## Function changes

post_ap_bill: handle kind='disposal_match' branch.

Per disposal_match line:
1. Validate vendor_id of bill matches the wo_by_products.disposal_vendor_id
2. Resolve accrued_disposal_liability(vendor, currency) account
3. Three-way match: line.qty ≤ accrued by-product qty for this vendor (cumulative across prior disposal_match lines on this and other bills); line.unit_cost vs the snapshotted unit_value (within vendor's unit_cost_tolerance_pct from mig 0090)
4. Drain accrued_disposal_liability(vendor) by line.qty × accrued_unit_value (the original asserted price)
5. Credit ap(vendor) by line.qty × line.unit_cost (the actual bill price)
6. Tolerance Δ = line.qty × (bill_unit_cost - accrued_unit_value) absorbs to variance_match_tolerance(currency) per mig 0090 pattern (sign-aware DR/CR)
7. Out-of-tolerance: P0024 (reuse the existing three-way mismatch error code)

## Tests

- disposal_match_exact_price_drains_accrual: bill = accrual; accrued_disposal_liability(vendor) goes to zero, ap(vendor) credited; no variance
- disposal_match_within_tolerance_absorbs: vendor.tolerance_pct=5, bill 1% over → variance_match_tolerance gets the Δ
- disposal_match_out_of_tolerance_rejects: bill 10% over with tolerance=5 → P0024
- partial_disposal_match: bill covers half the accrued qty; remainder stays accrued for next bill
- disposal_match_multi_wo: bill covers two separate WO events from same vendor; cumulative qty ≤ accrued
- mixed_bill: po_match + service + disposal_match in one bill
- assert_invariants_hold I1-I7

## Acceptance

- vendor_bill_lines.kind extended; CHECK updated
- post_ap_bill DROP+CREATE (parameter signatures unchanged but body grows; CREATE OR REPLACE works since no parameter rename)
- All existing post_ap_bill tests pass; disposal_match tests pass
- ci-check clean
close_reason: Closed

title: acct-7t4.4: disposal_cost (inventoriable + period bases) + accrued_disposal_liability
description:
Sub of acct-7t4 (umbrella). Depends on acct-7t4.3 (foundational pre-pass exists).

Adds the disposal_cost treatment in both bases (inventoriable / period) and the bridging accrual liability that mirrors Slice A's GRNI pattern.

## Schema additions

ALTER TYPE account_kind ADD VALUE IF NOT EXISTS 'accrued_disposal_liability';
ALTER TYPE account_kind ADD VALUE IF NOT EXISTS 'disposal_expense';

Seed:
- accrued_disposal_liability USD + EUR (currency-only un-partitioned for fixture; per-vendor created inline by tests). normal_side='credit'.
- disposal_expense USD + EUR. normal_side='debit'.

Per-vendor accrued_disposal_liability is keyed (kind, counterparty_id=vendor_id, currency). Same partitioning as ap_unsettled.

## Function changes

post_wo_complete pre-pass (extending acct-7t4.3): handle disposal_cost rows in wo_by_products.

Per row, by disposal_basis:

- inventoriable:
  - Qty leg: stock_available(by_product, fg_loc) DR / creation_void(qty) CR
  - Value leg per co-product (split by allocation_pct):
    inv_value_fg(co_product, co_product_fg_loc) DR / accrued_disposal_liability(disposal_vendor) CR
    amount = (|unit_value| × actual_qty) × allocation_pct / 100
    Note: this is INDEPENDENT of v_total_drain reduction. inv_value_wip(parent, last_op) is NOT touched. Co-products absorb full v_total_drain (from std × p_qty), AND co-product fg gets a SECOND debit from disposal_cost adder.
- period:
  - Qty leg: stock_available(by_product, fg_loc) DR / creation_void(qty) CR
  - Value leg: disposal_expense_account_kind (or 'disposal_expense' default if NULL) DR / accrued_disposal_liability(disposal_vendor) CR
    amount = |unit_value| × actual_qty
    inv_value_wip(parent) untouched.

Note: disposal_basis='period' allows disposal_expense_account_kind=NULL → defaults to 'disposal_expense'. Caller can override with any value-side account_kind for finer GL classification.

## Tests

- disposal_cost_inventoriable_inflates_co_product_basis: 1 parent + 1 disposal_cost (inventoriable); verify co-product fg = (std × qty) + (|unit_value| × disposal_qty); accrued_disposal_liability(vendor) credit balance matches
- disposal_cost_period_recognizes_separately: disposal_expense debited, co-products absorb full v_total_drain, accrued_disposal_liability credited
- disposal_cost_inventoriable_with_two_coproducts: allocation_pct splits the disposal cost adder correctly
- disposal_cost_period_with_custom_expense_kind: caller sets disposal_expense_account_kind='maintenance_expense'; events route there
- mixed_treatments_in_one_wo: 1 nrv + 1 negligible + 1 disposal_inventoriable + 1 disposal_period; all balance per (ledger_kind, currency)
- assert_invariants_hold I1-I7

## Acceptance

- Migration up + down (account_kind + seeds)
- post_wo_complete updated; all existing tests pass; disposal_cost cases covered
- ci-check clean
close_reason: Closed

title: acct-7t4.3: post_wo_complete pre-pass for nrv_credit + negligible treatments
description:
Sub of acct-7t4 (umbrella). Depends on acct-7t4.2 (wo_by_products must exist + be populated at wo_start).

Implements the foundational by-product accounting logic at WO completion for the two simpler treatments (nrv_credit, negligible). disposal_cost is deferred to acct-7t4.4 because it requires the accrual liability schema.

## Function changes

post_wo_complete: insert pre-pass between pre-balance step and co-product distribution loop.

Pre-pass walks wo_by_products WHERE wo_id = p_wo_id ORDER BY by_product_no. For each row:

- nrv_credit:
  - Qty leg: stock_available(by_product, fg_loc) DR / creation_void(qty) CR, amount = actual_qty, qty = actual_qty, reason='wo_complete'
  - Value leg: inv_value_fg(by_product, fg_loc) DR / inv_value_wip(parent, last_op) CR, amount = unit_value × actual_qty, qty = actual_qty, reason='wo_complete_v'
  - Accumulate v_byproduct_drain += unit_value × actual_qty
- negligible:
  - Qty leg only (same shape as nrv_credit qty leg)
  - No value leg
  - v_byproduct_drain unchanged

After pre-pass: v_total_drain := v_total_drain - v_byproduct_drain. Co-product loop distributes v_total_drain (now reduced).

disposal_cost rows in wo_by_products are SKIPPED in this sub-issue (no-op; they'll be handled in acct-7t4.4). Existing wo_by_products rows that would skip don't break anything — they just don't fire.

## Tests

- happy_path_nrv_credit_reduces_co_product_drain: 1 parent + 1 nrv_credit by-product; verify co-product fg gets std×qty − unit_value×qty; by-product fg gets unit_value×qty; per-(ledger_kind, currency) DE invariant holds
- happy_path_negligible_only_qty_leg: by-product appears in stock_available at zero cost; co-product absorbs full drain
- co_products_plus_nrv: 2 co-products + 1 nrv by-product; verify allocation_pct math after by-product drain
- multiple_by_products_mixed: 2 nrv + 1 negligible on same WO; cumulative drain correct
- assert_invariants_hold (I1-I7) after every test

## Acceptance

- post_wo_complete updated; all existing tests pass; new tests cover nrv_credit + negligible
- ci-check clean
close_reason: Closed

title: acct-7t4.2: wo_by_products + snapshot at wo_start
description:
Sub of acct-7t4 (umbrella). Depends on acct-7t4.1 (bom_by_products must exist).

Adds the per-WO snapshot table and wires post_wo_start to populate it from the resolved BOM.

## Schema

CREATE TABLE wo_by_products (wo_id, by_product_no, output_sku_id, fg_location_id, planned_qty BIGINT > 0, actual_qty BIGINT >= 0, unit_value, treatment, disposal_basis, disposal_vendor_id, disposal_expense_account_kind, PK (wo_id, by_product_no), CHECK constraints mirror bom_by_products).

planned_qty: snapshot at wo_start as ROUND(bom_by_products.qty_per_parent × wo.qty_target). Immutable thereafter (no UPDATE allowed; trigger-enforced).
actual_qty: defaults to planned_qty at INSERT. Caller can UPDATE before wo_complete to assert actual yield.

## Function changes

post_wo_start: after auto-init of wo_outputs, also iterate bom_by_products for the resolved BOM and INSERT wo_by_products rows with planned_qty = ROUND(qty_per_parent × wo.qty_target) and actual_qty = planned_qty (default). All other fields copied from bom row.

If wo_by_products rows already exist for the WO (caller pre-populated for ad-hoc by-products without BOM declaration), post_wo_start does NOT overwrite — caller intent wins. Same pattern as wo_outputs auto-init.

## Tests

- BOM-driven snapshot: WO with BOM that has 2 by-products → wo_by_products has 2 rows with correct planned_qty
- Ad-hoc INSERT: caller pre-populates wo_by_products before wo_start; post_wo_start preserves rows
- Mixed: caller pre-populates 1 row, BOM declares 2 — caller's wins, BOM rows still added with line numbers that don't conflict
- planned_qty immutability trigger: UPDATE planned_qty raises P00xx
- actual_qty mutability: UPDATE actual_qty before wo_complete succeeds; UPDATE after wo_complete may also succeed (trigger doesn't gate; out-of-order UPDATE's effect on already-posted ledger is the caller's problem)

## Acceptance

- Migration up + down
- post_wo_start updated; existing tests pass; new tests for snapshot pass
- T2 probe tests/wo_by_products_snapshot.rs covers the cases above
close_reason: Closed

title: acct-7t4.1: bom_by_products schema + ECO/revision wiring
description:
Sub of acct-7t4 (umbrella). Adds the BOM-side declaration table for by-products. Standalone schema-only sub-issue; no function changes.

## Schema

CREATE TABLE bom_by_products (bom_id, by_product_no, output_sku_id, fg_location_id, qty_per_parent NUMERIC(18,6) > 0, unit_value, treatment ∈ {nrv_credit, negligible, disposal_cost}, disposal_basis ∈ {inventoriable, period}, disposal_vendor_id, disposal_expense_account_kind, PK (bom_id, by_product_no), per-treatment CHECK constraints).

Treatment-specific CHECKs:
- nrv_credit: unit_value > 0; disposal_* fields NULL
- negligible: unit_value = 0; disposal_* fields NULL

Indexes: (bom_id, output_sku_id) for lookup; (disposal_vendor_id) for vendor-side audits.

ECO/revision lifecycle: inherits via bom_id FK to bom_headers. When a BOM revision is approved (status='active'), its bom_by_products rows become effective for new WOs that resolve that BOM. Existing WOs already snapshotted via wo_by_products are NOT re-resolved — same lifecycle as bom_lines.

title: property test for post_inventory_adjustment per-class qty divisor (R1 pin)
description:
Sub of acct-1cer. Property test for post_inventory_adjustment on wac_perpetual SKUs covering R1 (per-class qty divisor): raw and fg classes share stock_available but maintain INDEPENDENT running averages computed from per-class signed qty SUM on the value account's transfers.qty (mig 0030 acct-1vr fix).

Invariants:
1. wac_perpetual +qty with p_unit_cost: pool_value Δ = qty_delta × p_unit_cost; effective_uc = p_unit_cost.
2. wac_perpetual +qty without p_unit_cost (non-empty pool): effective_uc = pool_value / pool_qty (per-class).
3. wac_perpetual -qty: effective_uc = pool_value / pool_qty (per-class); pool_value Δ = qty_delta × effective_uc; depletes at running avg.
4. R1 cross-class isolation: raw adjustments do NOT affect fg avg; fg adjustments do NOT affect raw avg, despite sharing stock_available pool qty.
5. inventory_adjustments.unit_cost = effective_uc (audit field matches dispatched value).
6. I1-I7 invariants throughout.

Random sequences of (class, qty_delta, optional p_unit_cost) for both raw and fg classes on the same wac_perpetual SKU + location. Test mirrors the in-memory expected state vs db ledger.

Mirrors tests/property_ap9_audit_ledger_consistency.rs as the template. ~½ day, ~400-500 lines.

On completion: close THIS sub-issue, leave acct-1cer umbrella OPEN.
close_reason: Shipped tests/property_inventory_adjustment_per_class.rs. 100-case property test asserts: (1) per-class effective_uc matches mirror running avg; (2) inv_value_<class> Δ = signum × |qty| × effective_uc; (3) inventory_adjustments.unit_cost = effective_uc (R7 audit); (4) R1 cross-class isolation — raw adj does not change inv_value_fg, fg adj does not change inv_value_raw, despite shared stock_available pool; (5) I1-I7 invariants throughout. Random alternating raw/fg adjustments on same wac_perpetual SKU with bias toward IN ops to keep pools non-empty for depletion paths. Umbrella acct-1cer stays OPEN.

title: property test for post_customer_invoice three-way match + tolerance window
description:
Sub of acct-1cer. Mirror of acct-x8so on the AR side. Property test for post_customer_invoice covering:

1. Base leg: ar DR Δ = qty × so_line.unit_price (preserves accrual integrity at original asserted price); ar_unsettled CR Δ = qty × so_line.unit_price.
2. Tolerance absorption leg (if invoice_unit_price ≠ so_line.unit_price): variance_match_tolerance Δ = qty × (invoice_price - so_price), sign-correct for over/under.
3. Cumulative qty invoiced per so_line stays ≤ qty_shipped (P0040 cumulative remainder).
4. Net ar DR per line = qty × invoice_unit_price (base + tolerance composes to invoice price).
5. I1-I7 invariants throughout.

Random sequences: pre-ship qty, then bills with varying invoice_unit_price within tolerance window. tolerance_pct ∈ {0, 5, 10}.

Mirrors tests/property_ap_bill_invariants.rs as the template. ~½ day, ~500 lines.

On completion: close THIS sub-issue, leave acct-1cer umbrella OPEN.

Random tolerance_pct ∈ {0, 5, 10} with within-window invoice prices. Umbrella acct-1cer stays OPEN.

title: property test for post_ap_bill three-way match + tolerance window
description:
Sub of acct-1cer. Property test for post_ap_bill covering:

1. Three-way match: bill qty ≤ received-not-yet-billed remainder per po_line (P0024 enforcement on cumulative).
2. Within-tolerance unit_cost delta absorbs into variance_match_tolerance; out-of-tolerance raises P0024.
3. ap_unsettled debit-side drain per line = qty × po_unit_cost (original po_line price; preserves accrual integrity).
4. ap credit-side increase per line = qty × po_unit_cost + (tolerance absorption Δ when within window).
5. variance_match_tolerance Δ = qty × (bill_unit_cost - po_unit_cost) sign-matches over/under direction.
6. I1-I7 invariants hold throughout.

Random sequences of (po_receipt, ap_bill_at_po_unit_cost, ap_bill_within_tol, ap_bill_out_of_tol) on a 2-line PO with mixed cost-method SKUs. Test exercises strict (tolerance=0) and non-zero tolerance pcts.

On completion: close THIS sub-issue, leave acct-1cer umbrella OPEN.

Random tolerance_pct ∈ {0, 5, 10} and bill_unit_cost drawn from within-window range. Umbrella acct-1cer stays OPEN.

title: property test for post_po_receipt cumulative-qty + value-pool conservation
description:
Sub of acct-1cer. Property test for post_po_receipt covering invariants:

1. Σ po_receipt_lines.qty_received per po_line ≤ po_line.qty_ordered (P0023 enforcement).
2. Standard SKU: PPV transfer amount = qty × (po_unit_cost - std_at_BD); favorable/unfavorable direction matches sign.
3. WAC SKU: pool value increase = qty × po_unit_cost (no PPV).
4. AP_unsettled credit-side increase = qty × po_unit_cost (always).
5. Stock_available debit-side increase = total qty (always).
6. I1-I7 invariants hold throughout.

Random sequences of multi-line + multi-receipt against one PO with mixed-cost-method SKUs (standard + wac_perpetual). Single-threaded; pins the invariants so future refactors can't silently break them.

Mirrors tests/property_ap9_audit_ledger_consistency.rs as the template. ~½ day, ~300-400 lines, PROPTEST_CASES default 100.

title: Return functions: state-aware routing for pre-invoice / partial / post-invoice cases
description:
## Problem

post_po_return (acct-quk, mig 0085) and post_customer_return (acct-ari, mig 0084) hard-code the post-clearance routing path:
- post_po_return: value leg always debits **ap**
- post_customer_return: revenue leg always credits **ar**

This works only when the bill / invoice has fully cleared the staging account. For receipts/shipments that are not yet invoiced (or only partially invoiced), the function trips accounts_check on a credit-/debit-normal account because the staging balance is on the wrong account.

## Concrete failure scenarios

### AP side (post_po_return)
- Receipt of 10 units. Goods received, value sits in ap_unsettled (qty * po_unit_cost).
- No bill yet → ap balance is 0.
- Return 5 units → tries to debit ap by 5*po_unit_cost.
- Trip: ap is credit-normal; debits > credits violates the CHECK constraint (mig 0006).

### AR side (post_customer_return)
- Ship 10 units. Revenue posted to ar_unsettled.
- No invoice yet → ar balance is 0.
- Return 5 units → tries to credit ar by 5*unit_price.
- Trip: ar is debit-normal; credits > debits violates the CHECK constraint.

### Mixed (partially invoiced)
- Receipt 10 units, billed for 6, returning 4.
- 4 of the receipt's value still sits in ap_unsettled; 6 has cleared to ap.
- Returning 4 units → if we route to ap, ap drains by 4*po (correct partial drain) but ap_unsettled still has its balance. Net result: ap_unsettled holds an orphan balance forever.
- Returning 6 instead → routing to ap drains the 6 that was billed; correct.
- Returning 7 → 6 should drain ap, 1 should drain ap_unsettled. Splitting needed.

## Correct routing logic (mainstream ERP convention)

For each return line, query the cumulative billed/invoiced amount per receipt-line / ship-line, compute the unbilled-not-yet-returned remainder, and split:

```
unbilled_remaining = qty_received - SUM(vendor_bill_lines.qty WHERE po_line_id matches)
                   - SUM(po_return_lines.qty_returned WHERE recv_line same and prior to this)

if qty_returned <= unbilled_remaining:
    route entire amount to ap_unsettled  (cancel before bill)
elif unbilled_remaining == 0:
    route entire amount to ap            (credit memo against billed)
else:
    split: first unbilled_remaining units → ap_unsettled
           rest                          → ap
```

Symmetric for AR side using customer_invoice_lines.

## Design choices

1. **Caller-supplied vs function-dispatched**: Function-dispatched is preferred — the function already has the data; caller shouldn't have to track invoice/bill state separately.

2. **Split events vs combined**: Each disposition / route should emit its own value-leg event. PPV reversal also needs to follow the same split (PPV against ap_unsettled if pre-bill, against ap if post-bill).

3. **Tax leg routing on AR side** — currently customer_return routes tax to ar_unsettled. After this fix, tax routing should also be state-aware: pre-invoice tax stays in ar_unsettled (already correct); post-invoice tax... well, the current customer_invoice doesn't migrate tax for so_match lines anyway, so this stays in ar_unsettled regardless. Sanity-check that this is still correct after the routing change.

## Acceptance criteria

- post_po_return computes per-line unbilled remainder; splits the value leg + PPV leg between ap_unsettled and ap as needed.
- post_customer_return computes per-line uninvoiced remainder; splits revenue leg + tax leg between ar_unsettled and ar as needed.
- Tests covering: pre-invoice/bill return, partially-invoiced/billed return (split case), fully-invoiced/billed return.
- Tests covering: returns that span multiple invoices/bills (cumulative across all prior bills/invoices).
- No regression to existing tests in tests/po_return.rs and tests/customer_return.rs.

## Priority justification

P2: latent failure mode for pre-invoice / pre-bill returns. Real-world inflow workflows commonly inspect goods AT receipt and return defectives BEFORE the bill arrives. Our current implementation will refuse those returns with a constraint trip (cryptic error from caller perspective). Same shape on AR side though slightly less common.

## Dependencies

- acct-ari (closed): post_customer_return
- acct-quk (closed): post_po_return

## Out of scope

- Returns crossing the bill boundary in unusual ways (e.g., returning units that were billed on a different vendor_bill than received-on receipt). Cumulative-by-po_line is sufficient for MVP.
close_reason: Closed

title: acct-du2 Phase 3 follow-up: tests/property_post_cost_adjustment.rs

title: AP1: post_standard_cost_roll uses stock_available cross-class qty for per-class revaluation
description:
Surfaced by Phase 2 of acct-du2 audit. mig 0028 post_standard_cost_roll line 281 reads v_pool_qty from stock_available(sku, location) — CROSS-CLASS qty. Then iterates separately over inv_value_raw and inv_value_fg pools (line 265-280, joined to stock_available via location), applying v_delta := v_pool_qty * (p_new_cost - v_prior) to each pool.

When a SKU has BOTH raw and fg pools at the same location, both pools are revalued using the SAME (cross-class) qty. The aggregate delta is doubled relative to the actual on-hand. v_total_delta accumulator and the variance_std_cost_roll posting are both inflated.

Fix: replace stock_available qty read with per-class qty for each inv_value_<class> pool. Either (a) per-class signed SUM on transfers.qty filtered to the class-specific value account (mirrors mig 0069 fix), or (b) maintain a per-class qty companion account.

Note: similarly suspect for the 'common case' single-class — works correctly because v_pool_qty == per-class qty when only one class exists. The bug surfaces only with multi-class same-location.

Test: SKU with raw + fg at same location; post_standard_cost_roll; assert per-pool delta uses per-class qty, not stock_available cross qty.
close_reason: Closed

title: AP5: post_wo_close_unproduced residual sweep missing solo-at-pool gate (acct-69e shape)
description:
Surfaced by Phase 2 of acct-du2 audit. mig 0056 post_wo_close_unproduced walks all inv_value_wip(parent_sku, op_*, ccy) pools this WO's routing touches and absorbs each non-zero residual into wo_close_v variance (line 108-159). Missing the solo-at-pool gate that acct-69e applied to post_wo_complete (mig 0068).

If another WO shares (parent_sku, routing_op) and has unfinished WIP balance, this function's residual sweep absorbs that other WO's WIP into THIS WO's variance_wo_close. Same bug shape as the original acct-69e.

P2 because: less commonly hit than post_wo_complete (close_unproduced is for fully-scrapped WOs), but operators with shared parent_sku × op pools across WOs would silently mis-attribute close variance.

Fix: gate the residual posting on stock_wip(parent, op) qty == 0 — the same solo check applied in mig 0068 lines 350-356. If not solo, skip absorption (variance lands at the last sharing WO's close).

Test: two WOs sharing parent_sku × routing_op pools; one fully scrapped and closed via post_wo_close_unproduced while the other still has WIP balance; assert closing the unproduced WO does NOT absorb the open WO's WIP.
close_reason: Closed

title: AP8: post_osp_ship / post_osp_receive idempotency replay race (acct-69p shape)
description: Surfaced by Phase 1 of acct-du2 audit. mig 0057 lines 55-57 (post_osp_ship) and 157-159 (post_osp_receive) pre-check transfers.idempotency_key, then take FOR UPDATE on work_orders. A concurrent T1 with the same key can commit a transfer between T2's pre-check and T2's PERFORM post_transfers (line 118 / 221). T2's post_transfers INSERT trips the UNIQUE constraint on transfers.idempotency_key, raising an error rather than returning idempotently — the same shape as the acct-69p bug fixed for post_wo_start in mig 0039. Fix: re-check transfers.idempotency_key immediately after the FOR UPDATE on work_orders (line 68 / 170), bail out if found. Test: two concurrent post_osp_ship calls with identical idempotency_key; assert both return successfully and exactly one transfer is posted.
close_reason: Closed

title: AP3: post_wo_complete residual-sweep gate reads stock_wip without FOR UPDATE
description: Surfaced by Phase 1 of acct-du2 audit. mig 0068 line 350 reads v_op_qty on stock_wip(parent, op) in the per-routing-op residual sweep loop WITHOUT a preceding FOR UPDATE on that account. The lock at line 358 covers the inv_value_wip row only. Same race as acct-du2-A. Lower severity because residual-sweep absorption is already an approximation per acct-69e and the eventual last-WO close picks up unabsorbed residue. Fix: PERFORM 1 FROM accounts WHERE id = (stock_wip account id) FOR UPDATE before line 350. Test: two WOs sharing an intermediate op with overlapping close-times that hit the gate under the race; assert residue lands at last sharing WO's close.
close_reason: Closed

title: AP3: post_wo_complete solo-at-last gate reads stock_wip without FOR UPDATE
description: Surfaced by Phase 1 of acct-du2 audit. mig 0068 line 164 reads v_pool_qty_pre on stock_wip(parent, last_op) WITHOUT a preceding FOR UPDATE on that account. The read drives v_solo_at_last (the gate that decides whether pre-balance variance applies). Concurrent post_op_move on the same op pool can change qty between this read and the drain at line 327, mis-classifying solo and absorbing other WOs' WIP into THIS WO's variance_wo_close — same shape as the original acct-69e bug. Fix: PERFORM 1 FROM accounts WHERE id = v_qty_from FOR UPDATE before line 164 (and v_val_from too for consistency). Test: extend tests/wo_complete_interleaved_pool.rs with the race scenario.
close_reason: Closed

title: Tier 2: wac_periodic components issue at running avg + close-hook recompute
description:
Sub-issue of acct-rgb. Extends tier 1 (acct-24b) to wac_periodic / wac_retroactive components.

**Change.** _wo_emit_bom_lines uses running pool avg under FOR UPDATE for wac_periodic components (same math as tier 1). The resulting rm_issue_to_wo value-leg flags into transfers_provisional with the component's cost_method.

**Close-hook integration (the harder half).** wac_periodic_close_hook's topological pool walk (acct-smn) currently builds the DAG from in-period op_move_v transfers. Tier 2 extends the edge set: rm_issue_to_wo from a wac_periodic raw pool feeds the destination inv_value_wip pool. Edge: raw_pool → wip_pool. Same Kahn topological sort handles raw + WIP combined chain. Same LEFT-JOIN-on-variance_amount cache propagates the cost shift downstream.

**Internal vs leaf classification.** rm_issue_to_wo on a wac_periodic component is an internal-chain depletion (its destination is another tracked WIP pool). Use the tier 2 (acct-smn) pattern: record variance, do NOT post a transfer; cost shift propagates through the cache.

**Composes with parent cost methods.**
- Standard parent: WIP fills at component-running-avg (tier 2 here) but drains to FG at parent_std (deterministic). WIP residual at WO close gets absorbed into wo_close_v as material variance.
- wac_perpetual parent: WIP fills at component-running-avg, WIP drains at WIP-pool running avg (acct-wig). Now the WIP avg reflects actual material cost rather than mirroring parent_std.
- wac_periodic parent: WIP fills flagged AND drains flagged. The close hook handles both ends via topological walk through raw → WIP → WIP → FG chain.

**Acceptance.**
- 2-WO same-period through wac_periodic raw component with drift in raw cost: close hook re-amounts WIP fills at raw final_avg, downstream WIP final_avg picks up the shift, leaf wo_complete_v variance lands on FG / variance_wac_period.
- Mixed components: one standard, one wac_periodic in same BOM. Standard component's rm_issue is unflagged; wac_periodic component flags into transfers_provisional. Close hook only walks the wac side.
- 3-tier chain: raw (wac_periodic) → WIP@op10 → WIP@op20 → FG. Topological walk handles all 4 pools.

**Files.** db/migrations/0067_rm_issue_actual_cost_tier2.{up,down}.sql + tests/wac_periodic_component_issue.rs.

**Depends on:** acct-24b (tier 1).
close_reason: Tier 2 of acct-rgb: lifted wac_periodic gate in _wo_emit_bom_lines (parent must be wac_periodic — mixed cases defer to acct-7eo); switched _post_transfers_apply_event to credit-first SKU resolution and added rm_issue_to_wo to the cost-event reasons list; extended wac_periodic_close_hook topological pool walk to include rm_issue_to_wo edges (raw → WIP) and treat rm_issue as internal-chain. Fixed latent cache double-count by filtering LEFT JOIN cache to internal-chain rows only (variance_transfer_id IS NULL). 8 new tests in tests/wac_periodic_component_issue.rs cover single-WO drift, two-WO sharing pool, mixed std+wac BOM, 3-tier chain, mixed-parent gates (P0026 + acct-7eo defer), no-drift no-op, and rework cycle (P0036). 346/0/9 tests passing; ci-check round-trip clean (digest 40b97ed3...). Migration 0067.

title: Tier 1: single-routing-op WAC parents (wac_periodic + wac_retroactive)
description: First tier of acct-8in. Single-routing-op WO has no upstream WIP — all inv_value_wip(parent, op) receipts come from leaf sources (rm_issue_to_wo, labor_apply, oh_apply, burden_apply, lot_charge_apply). The existing wac_periodic_close_hook + wac_retroactive_close_hook per-pool walks work as-is once: (1) post_wo_start accepts wac_periodic/wac_retroactive WHEN wo_routings has exactly 1 op, (2) post_wo_complete dispatch on cost_method extends to wac_periodic/wac_retroactive (read source-pool running avg, mirrors wac_perpetual branch from acct-wig 0063), (3) transfers_provisional flagging condition picks up the BOM2 *_v reasons (op_move_v / wo_complete_v / scrap_v) so the close hook can find depletions, (4) cost-event detection scan in post_transfers similarly extends so cost_method is resolved for *_v events. Multi-op routing on wac_periodic/wac_retroactive raises P0026 with hint to acct-8in-tier2.
acceptance_criteria: Single-op WO lifecycle on wac_periodic + wac_retroactive parents posts depletions flagged in transfers_provisional; close hook recomputes pool avg from in-period receipts; variance posts via variance_wac_period (periodic) or wac_retroactive's variance routing. Multi-op routing on these methods raises P0026 directing to tier 2. Tests in tests/wac_periodic_wip.rs / tests/wac_retroactive_wip.rs.
close_reason: Migration 0064 + tests/wac_periodic_wip.rs (7 tests covering clean lifecycle, drift, scrap, partial complete, fully-scrapped close_unproduced, multi-op gate, wac_retroactive gate). 320 tests passing. ci-check digest ed5c4f9274a2830f7c6c82eaaaec9a92e2ff6bf5f90ba2441c567c5691c47467. Scope reduced during edge-case audit: wac_retroactive moved entirely to tier 3 (acct-rso) — its per-event chronological replay needs merging qty-side events for WIP pools.

title: WAC perpetual on WIP parent: lift cost_method gate + dispatch in post_op_move/post_wo_complete
description: Sub-issue of acct-p7v. Smallest unit that enables WAC parents on WO. Scope: post_wo_start drops the parent.cost_method='standard' gate (P0026) for wac_perpetual; post_op_move and post_wo_complete pre-balance step dispatch on parent_sku.cost_method, mirroring post_scrap's pool-avg pattern (accumulated_unit_cost = inv_value_wip(op) / stock_wip(op)). post_wo_start emission is unchanged because all per_unit/per_lot bom_lines fire via canonical reasons through the dispatcher, which already handles wac_perpetual on inv_value_wip. Acceptance: WO with wac_perpetual parent runs rm_issue → op_move → wo_complete; amounts equal qty × pool_avg at each step; tests cover (1) clean wac_perpetual lifecycle, (2) variance at wo_complete absorbs truncation residue, (3) scrap mid-flight, (4) parent.cost_method='standard' path still works unchanged. Defers wac_periodic/wac_retroactive to acct-p7v-B (recursive cost-chain across WIP pools).
acceptance_criteria: Migration 0063 (or similar) applied; post_op_move + post_wo_complete dispatch on parent_sku.cost_method; P0026 gate in post_wo_start lifted to allow wac_perpetual (still rejects wac_periodic/wac_retroactive); tests/wac_perpetual_wip.rs passes; existing 310 tests still green.
close_reason: Migration 0063 + 3 tests in wac_perpetual_wip.rs. 313 tests passing. ci-check digest c6b8ec882e98573f5b9c4983fe6231be08ea165d1674e3297aa00022cad9729c. wac_periodic/wac_retroactive on WIP unblocks acct-8in (topological per-pool close-hook recompute, the recursive cost-chain problem).

title: BOM2 yield-mode dual-mode: drop gross-up at emission/per-op flow + add skus.yield_mode flag
description:
Why: the original C5b implementation grossed up rm_issue qty + value at WO_start emission (CEIL math in _wo_emit_bom_lines) AND grossed up per_unit_cum in post_op_move. User correction: build cost must come from ACTUAL usage, not planned-grossed-up — the per-op pool flow has to be literal, otherwise op_move_v over-drains pool@from_op into negative territory and hits the inv_value_wip CHECK constraint.

The dual-mode (Approach A 'absorbed' vs Approach B 'plan_only') differs in whether scrap_pct factors into the *parent's standard cost rollup*, not in pool flow. Today standard_costs.cost is caller-set (no auto-rollup function); the yield_mode flag captures intent so the future rollup tool can do the right thing per parent.

Deliverable:
- Migration 0061:
  1. ALTER TABLE skus ADD COLUMN yield_mode TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT 'plan_only' CHECK IN ('plan_only','absorbed')
  2. CREATE OR REPLACE _wo_emit_bom_lines: drop CEIL gross-up; emit p_qty × qty_per_parent literal
  3. CREATE OR REPLACE post_op_move: drop / (1 - scrap_pct/100) divisor in per_unit_cum
- Rewrite the 2 C5b tests:
  1. yield_plan_only: default mode, BOM with scrap_pct=5%, verify literal emission (200 not 211) + clean op_move with no yield-driven over-drain
  2. yield_absorbed_via_scrap_aware_parent_std: yield_mode='absorbed', BOM with scrap_pct=5%, caller pre-sets parent_std to scrap-aware rolled-up value, verify variance_wo_close at close captures the planned-vs-actual yield gap

Future: a post_standard_cost_roll_from_bom helper that walks bom_lines and produces a yield_mode-aware standard_costs entry. Tracked separately.
close_reason: Yield-mode dual-mode shipped (migration 0061). Pool flow always literal in both modes. plan_only (default) = scrap_pct as planning metadata only. absorbed = caller pre-sets scrap-aware parent_std, post_wo_complete pre-balances pool@last_op via wo_close_v before per-output drain (avoids debit-normal CHECK violation). Both modes verified by 2 rewritten C5b tests. Future rollup tool tracked as acct-YIELD.

title: Tests C5d: wo_lifecycle_advanced.rs scrap-aware safety + partial-scrap (4 cases)
description:
WHY: User-specific question — what happens with partial scrap of a lot that has whole-lot charges? And: what if a WO is scrapped before reaching an op that would have fired a per_lot charge? DELIVERABLE: 4 tests in tests/wo_lifecycle_advanced.rs:

2. Partial scrap with per-lot charge already fired: scrap 5 of 100 at op30 after osp_freight (00) fired on first arrival. Verify ~0 of 00 goes to variance_scrap (5/100 share at accumulated unit cost), 90 carries forward with 95 survivors. (Sub-case (a).)

Verify variance_scrap from op20 scrap contains accumulated cost including op10 burdens and op20 burdens, but NOT op30 freight.
4. Full scrap then post_wo_close_unproduced: scrap all 100 at op10; call post_wo_close_unproduced. Verify status='closed', qty_completed=0, qty_scrapped=100, variance_wo_close absorbs any pre-fire residual.

ACCEPTANCE:
- All 4 tests pass with the canonical partial-share math
- variance_scrap and variance_wo_close balances reflect the right per-share and residual amounts
- Per-lot charges never fire if their op is unreached

DEPS: B9 (post_scrap), B10 (post_wo_close_unproduced).

title: Functions B7: post_op_move rewrite
description:
WHY: post_op_move drains stock_wip(parent, from_op) into stock_wip(parent, to_op) and posts the value-leg op_move_v at the accumulated standard cost up through from_op. With per-line BOMs and fire_at='op_arrival', the function must also detect 'first arrival at to_op' and fire those op-arrival lines. First-arrival detection: query wo_events history for any prior op_move with routing_op_to = p_to_op (Q-impl-1).

DELIVERABLE: In db/migrations/0041_unified_bom_functions.up.sql, rewrite CREATE OR REPLACE FUNCTION post_op_move(p_wo_id, p_from_op, p_to_op, p_qty, p_business_date, p_posted_by, p_idempotency_key):
1. Idempotency + status checks (status='released', re-entrant safe per 0039 pattern)
2. Validate p_from_op and p_to_op present in wo_routings; p_to_op > p_from_op
3. Resolve BOM via _wo_resolve_bom_for
4. Compute std_cum_at_from_op:
   - Σ per_unit lines (items + services) at applies_at_op ≤ from_op (each item line: qty_per_parent × resolve_standard_cost_at(comp, business_date) / (1 - scrap_pct/100))
   - + Σ per_lot charges at applies_at_op ≤ from_op (only those that already fired) / parent_sku.default_lot_size
5. Emit op_move qty leg: stock_wip(parent, to_op) DR, stock_wip(parent, from_op) CR, qty=p_qty
6. Emit op_move_v value leg: inv_value_wip(parent, to_op) DR, inv_value_wip(parent, from_op) CR, amount=p_qty × std_cum_at_from_op
7. First-arrival detection at p_to_op: EXISTS query against wo_events for prior op_move events landing at p_to_op
8. If first arrival: emit per_unit + per_lot lines at p_to_op with fire_at='op_arrival' via _wo_emit_bom_lines
9. Else: emit only per_unit lines at p_to_op (per_lot already fired on first arrival)

title: Schema A5: create bom_lines + self-reference trigger
description:
WHY: bom_lines is the body of the BOM — items, services, charges with per-line fire_at, scrap_pct, applies_at_op. Discriminator CHECKs ensure 'item' rows have component_sku/loc/qty (not absorption_class/std_amount), and 'service'/'charge' rows have absorption_class_id+std_amount (not component fields). The basis × kind invariant ensures item lines are always per_unit, charge lines are always per_lot, services are flexible. Self-reference must be prevented (a SKU's BOM line cannot consume itself) but cross-table CHECK isn't valid SQL — implemented via row-level trigger raising P0034 bom_line_self_reference.

DELIVERABLE: In db/migrations/0040_unified_bom_schema.up.sql:
CREATE TABLE bom_lines (
  bom_id              BIGINT NOT NULL REFERENCES bom_headers(id) ON DELETE CASCADE,
  line_no             INT  NOT NULL,
  kind                TEXT NOT NULL CHECK (kind IN ('item','service','charge')),
  basis               TEXT NOT NULL CHECK (basis IN ('per_unit','per_lot')),
  applies_at_op       INT  NOT NULL CHECK (applies_at_op > 0),
  fire_at             TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT 'op_arrival'
                      CHECK (fire_at IN ('wo_start','op_arrival')),
  scrap_pct           NUMERIC(5,2) NOT NULL DEFAULT 0
                      CHECK (scrap_pct >= 0 AND scrap_pct < 100),
  component_sku_id    UUID REFERENCES skus(id),
  component_loc_id    UUID REFERENCES locations(id),
  qty_per_parent      BIGINT,
  absorption_class_id BIGINT REFERENCES absorption_classes(id),
  std_amount          BIGINT,
  PRIMARY KEY (bom_id, line_no),
  CHECK (
    (kind = 'item'
     AND component_sku_id IS NOT NULL AND component_loc_id IS NOT NULL
     AND qty_per_parent IS NOT NULL AND qty_per_parent > 0
     AND absorption_class_id IS NULL AND std_amount IS NULL)
    OR
    (kind IN ('service','charge')
     AND component_sku_id IS NULL AND component_loc_id IS NULL AND qty_per_parent IS NULL
     AND absorption_class_id IS NOT NULL
     AND std_amount IS NOT NULL AND std_amount >= 0)
  ),
  CHECK (
    (kind = 'item'    AND basis = 'per_unit')
 OR (kind = 'charge'  AND basis = 'per_lot')
 OR (kind = 'service')
  ),
  CHECK (basis = 'per_lot' OR fire_at = 'op_arrival')
);

Plus a BEFORE INSERT/UPDATE trigger function bom_line_self_reference_check() that raises P0034 if NEW.component_sku_id = (SELECT parent_sku_id FROM bom_headers WHERE id = NEW.bom_id).

ACCEPTANCE:
- Table created with composite PK (bom_id, line_no)
- All three CHECK constraints enforced
- Self-reference trigger raises SQLSTATE P0034 when component = parent
- ON DELETE CASCADE wired so dropping a bom_header cascades to its lines
- T1 probes (C4) validate the discriminator, basis × kind, fire_at × basis, and self-reference trigger

DEPS: A3 (absorption_classes for the FK), A4 (bom_headers for the FK).

See plan §14 acct-A5.

title: EPIC: Unified BOM model — header/lines, alternates, revisions, runtime burden taxonomy, manufacturing-types coverage
description:
Umbrella epic for the BOM/routing schema rewire that addresses two structural issues from Slice B (acct-h7j):

1. The burden taxonomy lived in the account_kind PG enum, requiring ALTER TYPE migrations to add new burden types. Should be runtime-configurable data, not schema.
2. The BOM was a flat per-SKU table with no header/lines split, no alternates, no revisions. Real ERPs separate the BOM-as-a-thing (header) from the BOM contents (lines), and a SKU can have multiple alternate BOMs (substitute material, alternate vendor) plus revisions over time (engineering changes).

This refactor unifies both concerns. User locked the maximum scope (D1): phantoms, yield-per-line, co-products/by-products, alternates, revisions/ECO, OSP custody, backflush policy column, scrap-aware fire timing. Smaller items (lot/serial, catch-weight, disassembly, multi-tier traceability, capacity-based costing, payroll, alt-routings, process PI sheets) stay deferred with concrete schema sketches in Phase D.

User-locked decisions (D1-D8):
- D1. Maximum scope. Bundle phantoms, yield-per-line, co-products, BOM alternates+revisions, ECO foundation, OSP physical custody, fire_at scrap-aware timing, per-WO BOM selection.
- D2. Per-line fire_at in {wo_start, op_arrival} with scrap awareness.
- D3. Strict P0028 — post_wo_start raises if any active BOM line's applies_at_op doesn't appear in the WO's wo_routings.
- D4. Hard cutover. No backwards-compat shim. Phase 0/1 has no production data.
- D5. Time-phased revisions via effective_at/obsolete_at on bom_headers + per-WO selection via work_orders.bom_id.
- D6. default_lot_size on skus (default 1) for amortizing per-lot charges.
- D7. op_move_v reason stays. (Lifting the dispatcher's standard branch on inv_value_wip is acct-p7v Phase 2.)
- D8. Use BOM terminology consistently. No recipe anywhere.

Decomposes into 31 sub-issues across three phases:

- Phase B (acct-B1..B12): function rewrites in migration 0041, one commit per function

Plus 14 Phase D Phase-2 follow-up epics (acct-VARIANT, acct-LOTSERIAL, acct-CATCHWEIGHT, acct-DISASSEMBLY, acct-MULTITIER-TRACE, acct-TIMEPHASED-RATES, acct-CAPACITY, acct-BURDENCLOSE, acct-PAYROLL, acct-ALT-ROUTING, acct-PROCESS-PI, acct-BACKFLUSH, acct-YIELD, acct-ECO-WORKFLOW).

title: Slice B.1 — schema + functions: work_orders, routings/boms (decision), post_wo_start + post_op_move + post_wo_complete
description:
First sub-issue of Slice B. Schema additions + WO lifecycle functions.

KICKOFF QUESTIONS for user:
Q1. Routings: formal routings table (template reused across WOs) vs per-WO inline operations? Lean: per-WO inline for MVP; formal templates can be added later as a reference table that wo_routings reads from.
Q2. BOMs: formal boms table (parent_sku → component_sku × qty_per_parent) vs caller-supplied component qty per RM-issue event? Lean: formal boms for MVP since multi-component WOs are common; rm_issue_to_wo derives qty from BOM expansion.
Q3. Variance grain: surface MUV/LV/OHV at op_move time, or only at wo_close as a residual plug? Lean: residual at wo_close for MVP; per-op variance is a Phase 2 reporting refinement.
Q4. WIP cleanup at close: add a fourth close hook (e.g. orphan_wip_close_hook) for WOs that didn't reach wo_complete, or treat that as caller responsibility?

SCHEMA (proposed; lock at kickoff):
- work_orders (id UUID, wo_no TEXT UNIQUE, parent_sku_id UUID FK, qty_target BIGINT, status TEXT, posted_by, posted_at, idempotency_key UUID UNIQUE)
- wo_routings (per-WO; or routing template + wo_routings link). Columns: wo_id, routing_op, op_name, std_hours, std_oh_hours, work_center
- boms (parent_sku_id, component_sku_id, qty_per_parent BIGINT, currency for component value; PK = (parent, component))

FUNCTIONS (per consolidated doc §3.4 event recipes):
- post_wo_start(p_wo_id, p_business_date, ...) — emits the §3.4 'WO start at Op 10' batch: rm_issue_to_wo (qty + value legs per BOM component), wo_start (qty leg), labor_apply (op std labor), oh_apply (op std oh)
- post_op_move(p_wo_id, p_from_op, p_to_op, p_qty, ...) — read-then-write under FOR UPDATE lock for unit cost; emits qty leg + value leg moving (sku, op_N) → (sku, op_N+1)
- post_wo_complete(p_wo_id, p_qty, p_business_date, ...) — emits qty leg (stock_wip last_op → stock_available, fg_loc), value leg (inv_value_wip → inv_value_fg at std_cost), residual variance leg (variance_wo_close, sign by favorable/unfavorable)
- post_scrap(p_wo_id, p_op, p_qty, ...) — §3.5 recipe; emits scrap-out leg + variance_scrap leg
- post_labor_apply / post_oh_apply — may be subsumed by post_wo_start or split out

- P0028 routing_op_invalid (op not in WO's routing template)
- P0029 bom_missing (parent_sku has no BOM rows; only relevant if Q2=formal boms)

title: Slice A inflow workload load test (post_po_receipt + post_ap_bill cycles)
description:
Add a perf-shape-N load test that drives high-volume post_po_receipt + post_ap_bill cycles, comparable to the existing shapes A-M (perf_baseline_v0.md). Slice A's matrix tests assert correctness; this test characterizes throughput and contention shape under realistic concurrent inflow load.

WHY: foundation audit (acct-ok2) re-benched the post_transfers shape after Phase 1 cost-method work landed. Slice A added two new doc-layer functions (post_po_receipt, post_ap_bill) that fan out to multiple post_transfers calls, plus three-way-match SELECTs and document-table INSERTs. None of the existing load tests exercise this. Without it we'd be guessing at Slice A's perf cost when Slice B starts adding more dispatcher branches.

WORKLOAD SHAPE (proposed shape N):
- Setup: N vendors (default 100); 1 BENCH SKU per vendor (BENCH-001..N); 1 MAIN location; 1 PO per vendor with one PO line (qty_ordered=10_000_000, unit_cost=1=std_cost so no PPV); per-vendor accounts (vendor_pool qty, ap_unsettled USD, ap USD); per-SKU accounts (stock_available MAIN qty, inv_value_raw MAIN USD).
- Writers (default 32, configurable T4_WRITERS): each writer in a loop until T4_DURATION_SECS:
  1. Pick a random vendor's PO line.
  2. Call post_po_receipt for qty=5 (configurable T4_QTY_PER_CYCLE).
  3. Call post_ap_bill po_match for qty=5 against the same po_line.
  4. Record cycle latency (receipt+bill end-to-end).
- Per cycle: 2 doc-function calls → 3 post_transfers events (qty leg + value leg + ap_bill clearance leg). No PPV (std==po). No service lines.

OUTPUT: same instrumentation as load_realistic_workload.rs — pg_stat_database / pg_stat_io snapshots, WAL bytes, p50/p95/p99 of cycle latency, ok+err counts, deadlock guard. Headline metric is cycles/sec (= receipts/sec = bills/sec).

ACCEPTANCE: tests/load_inflow_workload.rs compiles, runs under #[ignore], assertions: zero deadlocks, ok_count > 0. T4_DURATION_SECS=30 default for sanity check; full benchmarking uses run-perf-baseline.sh-style invocation. Optional: add a row to perf_baseline_v1.md when the shape gets benched.

NOT IN SCOPE:

- Mixed po_match + service bills.
- Three-way match contention (single-line POs avoid the over-receipt SELECT race).
- Re-running perf_baseline_v1.md with shape N included.

- post_ap_bill(p_supplier_id UUID, p_lines JSONB [{kind, po_line_id|expense_account_id, qty, unit_cost, amount}], p_business_date DATE, ...) RETURNS UUID. Two line modes:

title: Slice A — inflow cycle: PO receipt + AP bill + three-way match
description:
Phase 1 first feature slice (per memory erp-slice-framing-by-transactional-cycle: inflow). Builds the PO receipt + vendor-bill workflow with GRNI semantics and strict three-way match. Inventory adjustment (Epic A) and the cost-method matrix are already shipped; this slice adds the supplier-counterparty side and the receipt-to-bill clearance flow.

DESIGN DECISIONS (locked 2026-05-01 in planning conversation):
D1 — GRNI semantics. PO receipt posts qty + value AGAINST ap_unsettled (goods received not invoiced), NOT directly to ap. ap_bill clears ap_unsettled → ap. Revises design doc §3.1 (which was written speculatively as direct-to-ap; Slice A is its first real implementation, so this is the right time to revise).
D2 — Service bills: caller passes expense_account_id per line (no fixed taxonomy at this slice). Q2 follow-up issue files the taxonomy-vs-flexibility exploration for later.
D3 — Three-way match strict. PO line ↔ receipt ↔ bill must match exactly on (sku, location, qty, unit_cost). Mismatches are caller-resolved via post_cost_adjustment or reversal+rebook; tolerance/over-receipt is Phase 2.

SUB-ISSUES (three, following established .1/.2/.3 pattern):
.1 schema + functions: suppliers table, purchase_order_lines, vendor_bills/_lines, post_po_receipt, post_ap_bill. Includes folded acct-q43 (post_transfers consolidation pass) as preparatory work BEFORE adding new dispatcher branches.

.3 docs: design doc §3.x ap_bill recipe (currently absent), db/README.md updates (new error codes, GRNI section), CLAUDE.md status, fixture expansion (suppliers, supplier_pool/ap_unsettled accounts).

WHY: completes the inflow side of the transactional cycle (inventory comes in via po_receipt; service costs come in via standalone ap_bill); foundation for Slice B (conversion: WO/routings/scrap) and Slice C (outflow: SO/AR).

NOT IN SCOPE: ap_payment workflow (separate slice — that's outflow-of-cash), commodity provisional pricing (§3.13/§10 already covered by reservation flow), over/under-receipt tolerance (Phase 2), expense-taxonomy reporting buckets (filed as follow-up).

title: og1.1 — Schema + post_cost_adjustment_retroactive + close hook real body
description:
First sub-issue under acct-og1. Tightly coupled changes shipped in one migration.

Migration scope (next available, likely 0032):

1. CREATE TABLE inventory_cost_adjustments_retroactive (
     id UUID NOT NULL PRIMARY KEY DEFAULT uuidv7(),
     sku_id UUID NOT NULL REFERENCES skus(id),
     location_id UUID NOT NULL REFERENCES locations(id),
     currency TEXT NOT NULL,
     inventory_class TEXT NOT NULL CHECK (inventory_class IN ('raw', 'fg')),
     target_period_id BIGINT NOT NULL REFERENCES periods(id),
     target_avg BIGINT NOT NULL CHECK (target_avg >= 0),
     business_date DATE NOT NULL,
     posted_by UUID NOT NULL,
     posted_at TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL DEFAULT clock_timestamp(),
     finalized_at TIMESTAMPTZ,
     finalized_count BIGINT,
     total_variance BIGINT,
     idempotency_key UUID NOT NULL UNIQUE,
     notes TEXT
   );
   Indexes: (target_period_id) WHERE finalized_at IS NULL, (sku_id, target_period_id), (posted_at).

2. post_cost_adjustment_retroactive function:
   Signature: post_cost_adjustment_retroactive(p_target_period_id BIGINT, p_sku_id UUID, p_location_id UUID, p_currency TEXT, p_inventory_class TEXT, p_target_avg BIGINT, p_business_date DATE, p_posted_by UUID, p_idempotency_key UUID, p_notes TEXT DEFAULT NULL) RETURNS UUID

   Body:
   - Replay check via idempotency_key.
   - Validate p_target_avg >= 0.
   - Validate p_inventory_class IN (raw, fg) — wip → P0006 referencing acct-p7v.
   - Validate target period exists and is OPEN (closed_at IS NULL). Else raise P0021 (target_period_closed) with message referencing acct-7h4 (reopen workflow).
   - Validate p_business_date is within target period bounds (between opens_at and closes_at).
   - Validate SKU exists.
   - Resolve pool: inv_value_<class>(sku, location, currency, NOT is_closed). Error P0010 if missing.
   - INSERT row. Return id.

3. DROP FUNCTION cost_adjust_retroactive_hook(BIGINT) and CREATE 2-arg with real body:
   cost_adjust_retroactive_hook(p_period_id BIGINT, p_force_provisional BOOLEAN DEFAULT FALSE) RETURNS BIGINT

   Body:
   - For each un-finalized queue row WHERE target_period_id = p_period_id:
     a. Look up pool inv_value_<class>(sku, location, currency).
     b. Get period bounds.
     c. Walk depletions: SELECT id, amount, qty FROM transfers WHERE credit_account_id = pool AND business_date BETWEEN opens AND closes AND qty IS NOT NULL AND qty > 0.
     d. For each depletion: provisional_unit_cost = amount / qty (truncating). variance = qty × (target_avg - provisional_unit_cost). Skip if 0.
     e. Resolve variance_cost_adjust_retro(currency). Build 2-transfer batch routing through it (same pattern as wac_periodic/retroactive). PERFORM post_transfers(batch, FALSE).
     f. Accumulate total_variance and depletion count.
     g. UPDATE queue row SET finalized_at, finalized_count, total_variance.
   - Return count of finalized queue rows.

4. close_period: thread p_force_provisional to cost_adjust_retroactive_hook (currently 1-arg).

DOWN MIGRATION:
- Restore close_period to 1-arg call to cost_adjust_retroactive_hook.
- DROP cost_adjust_retroactive_hook(BIGINT, BOOLEAN); CREATE 1-arg stub returning 0.
- DROP TABLE inventory_cost_adjustments_retroactive.
- DROP FUNCTION post_cost_adjustment_retroactive.

NEW ERROR CODE:
- P0021 — target_period_closed. Documented in db/README error codes by og1.3.

ACCEPTANCE:
- ci-check round-trips clean.
- Smoke test: queue a retroactive adjustment for current period; close; verify variance posted and queue finalized.
- Smoke test: target_period closed → P0021 with reference to acct-7h4.

description:

3. post_inventory_adjustment: add wac_retroactive branch. Same shape as wac_periodic (IN at pool avg, OUT at pool avg + provisional flag). WIP class early guard.

4. wac_retroactive_close_hook: REAL body replacing the s6n stub. Algorithm per Epic 9tw description D6.
   Signature: wac_retroactive_close_hook(p_period_id BIGINT, p_force_provisional BOOLEAN DEFAULT FALSE) RETURNS BIGINT.
   Drop the old 1-arg stub first (PG signature change requires DROP).
   Update close_period to pass p_force_provisional through to wac_retroactive_close_hook (currently only threaded to wac_periodic).
   
   Body steps:
   a. Load periods.opens_at and closes_at.
   b. Find distinct (sku, location, currency, kind) pools that have un-finalized wac_retroactive provisional rows in this period.
   c. For each such pool:
      - Compute pre-period running state: pool_value = SUM(amount signed) WHERE pool affected AND business_date < period_opens; pool_qty = SUM(qty signed) WHERE pool affected AND business_date < period_opens AND qty IS NOT NULL.
      - Walk all in-period events affecting this pool, ordered by (business_date ASC, posted_at ASC, id ASC).
      - For each event:
        * Receipt (debit to pool): pool_value += amount; pool_qty += qty.
        * Depletion (credit from pool): recomputed_avg = pool_value / pool_qty (truncating); recomputed_amount = qty × recomputed_avg; pool_value -= recomputed_amount; pool_qty -= qty.
        * If depletion has a transfers_provisional row with cost_method=wac_retroactive AND finalized_at IS NULL: variance = recomputed_amount - original.amount; if variance != 0, post 2-transfer batch routing through variance_wac_retroactive(currency); UPDATE transfers_provisional SET finalized_at, variance_amount, variance_transfer_id.
   d. Return count of finalized rows.

5. Pool-emptiness during replay: if at any depletion point pool_qty <= 0 (would be a P0006 at posting time too), raise an internal error — the chain has a real inconsistency. Should not happen in normal flow. Document.

title: Phase 1 Epic: per-class qty tracking on transfers (fixes WAC multi-class coupling)
description:
Fix the structural coupling between qty-side and value-side accounts that breaks per-class WAC math when a single SKU has multi-state inventory simultaneously (raw + fg open).

ROOT CAUSE. _post_transfers_lookup_qty_account (migration 0021) maps both inv_value_raw and inv_value_fg to the SAME stock_available(sku, location) qty account. Correct accounting (raw and fg are both 'available' by qty), but breaks per-class cost division when a SKU has multiple value pools active.

MANIFESTATIONS:
1. wac_periodic_close_hook: final period avg = numerator-per-class / denominator-pooled-across-classes → wrong per-class avg.
2. wac_perpetual compute_amount: unit cost = inv_value_<pool>.balance / stock_available.balance → divisor inflates if multi-class.

NOT YET CATASTROPHIC because real workflows assign one inventory class per SKU (raw-material SKUs have no fg pool; fg SKUs have no raw). The matrix test raw_class_and_fg_class_close_independently_via_separate_skus deliberately uses two SKUs to sidestep the bug. User explicitly rejected 'document the constraint' and asked for a proper fix.

RECOMMENDED FIX (Option A). Add qty BIGINT NULL column to transfers, populated at INSERT time from event JSONB. Per-class qty computed from history (SUM over transfers tagged with debit/credit on the value pool), not from pooled stock_available balance.

Other options weighed and rejected:
- Option B (split stock_available into stock_raw/stock_fg): too invasive; churns every receipt/issue path
- Option C (document_id join at close time): partial fix; doesn't cover single-leg cost-relevant events (op_move/scrap/wo_complete/so_ship)
- Option D (pool_class tag column without qty): leaves wac_perpetual divisor problem unfixed

LOCKED-IN DECISIONS (user confirmed 2026-05-01):
1. Fix BOTH wac_periodic + wac_perpetual in this work (close latent bug before it manifests).
2. Epic + 3 sub-issues structure (matches s6n/hlr/qfj pattern).
3. Forward-only, no backfill machinery (dev DB wipes; test DB recreates; no production data).

SUB-ISSUES:
- .1: Schema + dispatcher refactor (migration 0030 + smoke test verifying single-class behavior unchanged)
- .2: Multi-class test matrix (wac_perpetual_multi_class.rs + wac_periodic_matrix.rs::raw_class_and_fg_class_close_independently_via_one_sku + conformance A14)
- .3: Doc updates (design doc §6.2 + §6, db/README, CLAUDE.md, retire 'single-class assumption' caveat)

ACCEPTANCE:
- New multi-class wac_perpetual test passes (would fail on 0029).
- New multi-class wac_periodic test passes (would fail on 0029).
- Existing 136-test suite remains green (no regression on single-class).

- Doc no longer carries the 'single-class assumption' caveat.

title: s6n.2 — close_period() orchestration function + close-hook stubs
description:
Second sub-issue under acct-s6n. Builds the orchestration layer on top of s6n.1's schema.

Depends on: acct-4mt (s6n.1).

Function signature:
  close_period(
    p_period_id         BIGINT,
    p_force_provisional BOOLEAN DEFAULT FALSE,  -- bypass un-finalized rows check
    p_force_recon       BOOLEAN DEFAULT FALSE,  -- bypass reconciliation alerts check
    p_actor             UUID
  ) RETURNS JSONB

Behavior:
1. Look up period; raise P0014 if not found OR already closed.
2. Call each registered close-hook in order:
     - wac_periodic_close_hook(period_id) — stub, returns 0
     - wac_retroactive_close_hook(period_id) — stub, returns 0
     - cost_adjust_retroactive_hook(period_id) — stub, returns 0

   finalized_at IS NULL AND NOT p_force_provisional.
4. Run run_daily_reconciliation(); refuse close (P0016) if alerts > 0
   AND NOT p_force_recon.
5. UPDATE periods SET closed_at = clock_timestamp(), closed_by = p_actor.
6. Return summary: { closed_at, finalized_count, hook_results, alerts, forced }.

Lock-order note: close_period writes variance transfers BEFORE setting
closed_at (so post_transfers' P0005 gate doesn't fire on the variance
postings themselves). The variance transfers are posted INTO the
period being closed.

  P0014 — period_close_invalid (period missing OR already closed)

title: s6n.1 — Schema: transfers_provisional + variance account_kinds
description:
First sub-issue under acct-s6n. Adds the foundational schema.

Migration scope:
1. CREATE TABLE transfers_provisional (
     transfer_id          BIGINT PRIMARY KEY REFERENCES transfers(id),
     period_id            BIGINT NOT NULL REFERENCES periods(id),
     cost_method          cost_method NOT NULL,    -- which dispatch produced this row
     finalized_at         TIMESTAMPTZ,             -- NULL = un-finalized
     variance_amount      BIGINT,                  -- signed; NULL until finalized
     variance_transfer_id BIGINT REFERENCES transfers(id)  -- variance posting at close

title: Phase 1 foundational slice: period-close machinery + provisional cost flag
description:
The foundational infrastructure that wac_periodic, wac_retroactive, and retroactive cost adjustment all depend on. Period-close in Phase 0 already exists at the schema level (periods.closed_at) and post_transfers gates on it (P0005). What's missing is the cost-finalization batch: the ability to mark transactions as provisional during a period and reconcile them at close.

Scope:
1. transfers.cost_provisional flag (BOOLEAN DEFAULT FALSE) — or a parallel side table like transfers_provisional(transfer_id, ...). Records depletions whose final cost depends on period-end recomputation.
2. New variance account kind for these reconciliations:
   - variance_wac_period (Epic B)
   - variance_wac_retroactive (Epic C, may share with wac_period)
   - variance_cost_adjustment_retro (Epic E, may share with the above — open design question)
3. Per-(cost_method) close hook function pattern. Skeleton:
     post_period_close_finalize(p_period_id) RETURNS JSONB
   Walks all SKUs with cost_method ∈ {wac_periodic, wac_retroactive} that have un-finalized transfers in p_period_id; dispatches to the appropriate batch:
     - wac_perpetual: nothing to do (already finalized)
     - wac_periodic: call wac_period_close(period_id) — Epic B's body
     - wac_retroactive: call wac_retroactive_close(period_id) — Epic C's body
     - cost adjustments retroactive: re-cost depletions per Epic E
4. period_close gate: extend the period-close trigger or function to refuse close until post_period_close_finalize returns success (zero un-finalized rows).
5. Tests covering: provisional flag set on relevant transfers; post_period_close_finalize runs idempotent; period-close blocks until finalization complete.

Out of scope:
- The actual wac_periodic/wac_retroactive math (Epics B and C consume this infrastructure).
- The retroactive cost adjustment workflow (Epic E).

DEPENDS ON: nothing — this IS the foundation.

BLOCKS: acct-qfj (Epic B), acct-9tw (Epic C), acct-og1 (Epic E). Add dependency edges when filed.

Notes:
- Slice D in phase1_planning_v0.md described "period close + reconciliation hardening" as a cross-cutting slice. This epic is its concrete sub-piece. Other Slice D concerns (period_snapshots usage, RBAC for period-close authorization) are separate future issues.

title: Phase 1 Epic D: cost_adjustment workflow (current avg, immediate-effect)
description:
Document-layer workflow for adjusting the current per-unit average cost of inventory without moving qty. Distinct from inventory_adjustment (which moves qty + value together) — this is a value-only revaluation.

User direction (2026-04-30): 'we likely need the idea of an "average cost adjustment" to adjust the current average cost'.

Use cases:
- Accountant determines pool's avg should be different (e.g., quality issue revealed, late vendor credit)
- Lower-of-cost-or-market write-down on existing inventory
- Manual revaluation following an audit

NEW transfer_reason: 'cost_adjustment' — distinct from cost_restate (which is for §10 commodity provisional-to-actual settlement reversal — different conceptual workflow). Filed because cost_restate was found to have a specific narrated meaning (commodity §10) and isn't a general cost-adjustment primitive.

NEW account_kind: 'variance_cost_adjustment' — bidirectional P&L (normal_side='unrestricted'). Distinct from inv_adj_expense (qty-driven adjustments) so the income statement can separately report revaluation events from cycle-count gain/loss.

Scope:
1. Migration adds:
   - ALTER TYPE transfer_reason ADD VALUE 'cost_adjustment'
   - ALTER TYPE account_kind ADD VALUE 'variance_cost_adjustment'
   - inventory_cost_adjustments table (id, sku_id, location_id, currency, target_unit_cost, posted_by, posted_at, idempotency_key, notes)
   - post_cost_adjustment(p_sku_id, p_location_id, p_currency, p_target_unit_cost, p_posted_by, p_idempotency_key, p_notes) function
2. Function behavior by cost_method:
   - 'wac_perpetual': read pool current_value/current_qty under FOR UPDATE; compute delta = (target_unit_cost - current_avg) * current_qty; post value-only transfer to inv_value_* (the appropriate class) with counterpart variance_cost_adjustment.
   - 'standard': P0011 — to change a standard SKU's cost, update skus.standard_cost via a separate workflow (see future issue).
   - 'wac_periodic'/'wac_retroactive': record as provisional; finalize at period close.
   - 'lot'/'fifo': P0006 (filed under acct-8gg).
3. Seed.sql adds variance_cost_adjustment(USD) and variance_cost_adjustment(EUR) accounts.
4. Tests:
   - Adjust pool from $6 avg to $7 avg; verify pool value moved to 200 * 7 = 1400; verify variance_cost_adjustment receives 200 credit (revaluation gain)
   - Adjust pool from $6 to $5; variance_cost_adjustment receives 200 debit (revaluation loss)
   - Reject on standard SKU (P0011)
   - Reject on lot/fifo (P0006)
   - Idempotency
   - Pool with qty=0 → P0011 (no avg to adjust)
5. Doc updates: §3.12 narrative for the new workflow; db/README docs.

Out of scope:
- Retroactive cost adjustment (Epic E)
- standard_cost roll-update workflow (separate future issue if needed; Phase 2+)

Could be the next implementation slice after Epic A — independent of period-close machinery.

title: Migration 0022: inventory_adjustments table + post_inventory_adjustment function
description:
Implementation issue for acct-sb6 epic.

Migration 0022 (reversible):
- Up: CREATE TABLE inventory_adjustments + CREATE FUNCTION post_inventory_adjustment.
- Down: DROP FUNCTION + DROP TABLE.

Table:
  id UUID PK uuidv7()
  sku_id UUID NOT NULL FK skus(id)
  location_id UUID NOT NULL FK locations(id)
  qty_delta BIGINT NOT NULL CHECK (qty_delta != 0)
  unit_cost BIGINT NOT NULL CHECK (unit_cost >= 0)
  currency TEXT NOT NULL
  inventory_class TEXT NOT NULL CHECK (inventory_class IN ('raw','fg'))
  business_date DATE NOT NULL
  posted_by UUID NOT NULL
  posted_at TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL DEFAULT clock_timestamp()
  idempotency_key UUID NOT NULL UNIQUE
  notes TEXT

Function signature:
  post_inventory_adjustment(
    p_sku_id UUID, p_location_id UUID,
    p_qty_delta BIGINT, p_unit_cost BIGINT,
    p_currency TEXT, p_inventory_class TEXT,
    p_business_date DATE, p_posted_by UUID,
    p_idempotency_key UUID,
    p_notes TEXT DEFAULT NULL
  ) RETURNS UUID

Behavior:
1. INSERT into inventory_adjustments. ON CONFLICT (idempotency_key) DO NOTHING; if conflict, look up existing id and return it (idempotent replay).
2. Resolve accounts:
   - qty: stock_available(sku, location), creation_void(qty)
   - value: inv_value_{class}(sku, location, currency), creation_void(value, currency)
3. Build 2-event batch using cycle_count_adj reason; sign-flip on qty_delta < 0.
4. Call post_transfers with override_closed_period=FALSE.
5. RETURN the inventory_adjustments.id.

- adjust_out_reduces_balances_and_audit_row

- adjust_negative_unit_cost_rejects (CHECK constraint)
- adjust_in_against_wac_sku_re_averages_pool (proves WAC compatibility)
- adjust_with_currency_eur_works
- adjust_with_class_raw_uses_inv_value_raw
- adjust_with_class_fg_uses_inv_value_fg

- ./scripts/ci-check.sh round-trip clean

title: Production: tighten container seccomp profile (whitelist io_uring syscalls only)
description:
Phase 0 dev environment uses 'seccomp:unconfined' on the postgres container because Docker's default seccomp profile denies the io_uring_setup / io_uring_enter / io_uring_register syscalls — without that override, postgres 18 with io_method=io_uring fails to start with 'could not setup io_uring queue: Operation not permitted'.

Acceptable for local dev. Not acceptable for production.

Action: write a custom seccomp profile (JSON) that takes Docker's default profile and adds an allow-list for the three io_uring syscalls only. Wire it into the production deploy (or a docker-compose.prod.yml) via 'security_opt: seccomp:./db/seccomp/postgres-iouring.json'.

References:
- https://docs.docker.com/engine/security/seccomp/
- The default profile is at https://github.com/moby/moby/blob/master/profiles/seccomp/default.json — clone, add io_uring_* to the syscalls allow array.

Out of scope for Phase 0 since there is no production deploy yet. File once a deploy target exists.
close_reason: Production seccomp profile landed at db/seccomp/postgres-iouring.json (Docker v28.0.0 default + io_uring trio, +3 lines vs upstream). Verified: dev container boots with the custom profile, io_method=io_uring works, extensions load, smoke test passes. db/seccomp/README.md documents provenance and re-derivation. title: Backport design: close-hook orchestration mapping, error-identity convention, reopen sequencing
description:
Why (three integration cliffs, one note): (a) ledger_close_period is a monolithic pgrx function with one boolean force; acct's close_period is a registry-driven hook iterator (close_hooks at ordering 10/20/30) with independently bypassable gates — the drain-gate/sweep/fence must be re-expressed as close_hooks or acct's orchestrator taught to call engine SPIs. (b) pgrx's SPI boundary remaps non-enum SQLSTATEs to XX000, so v3.2 standardized on 55000 + 'PeriodClosed:' message prefix and 53400 for backpressure, while the parent's contract is P00xx codes; four distinct config errors also share class 22000 in ledger_error_map.rs — a backport needs one deliberate error-identity mechanism (native plpgsql RAISE with P00xx, or a structured DETAIL code contract), never message-prefix matching or XX000. (c) Reopen (D14, charter-excluded) is the named resolution for two shipped failure surfaces (post-close straggler alarm, sticky throttle) and the parent tracks it as Phase 2 Epic K (acct-7h4, referenced by P0021) — at backport, sequence reopen ahead of or with alt-C adoption, wire it to the 0017 reject site, and note it invalidates any closed-boundary replay checkpoint.

What: one backport-plan note covering the hook mapping, the error-identity decision, and the reopen sequencing against acct-7h4. Reference, don't duplicate: acct-7h4 remains the reopen tracker.

PROVENANCE: hot-path, archaeology, parity, design-core, recalc-close (0017 header, ledger_error_map.rs, parent close_hooks/acct-w0lo, D14 → acct-7h4)

title: Establish and commit the perf baseline: calibrated SLO, depth axis, worker/staging sweeps, long-run readiness
description:
Why: (a) slo-sweep.sh exists to produce throughput-at-SLO but soak-results §7 records no verdicts; the 10ms default fails even the 200/s direct rung (p99 11,100us) so the script would report best_rate=0 — never calibrated; per-rung JSON goes to gitignored bench/out, so no machine-readable baseline is committed (parent posture: baseline before complexity). (b) The depth axis was never swept: v3.2 moved the ceiling into the engine (Pareto-hot pool = close-drain floor; R-2 replay scales with tail length) but no run varies seeded depth — no recalc-pass-latency-vs-depth or close-drain-time-vs-depth curve exists, and the recalc-c §4 close-drain-floor formula still rests on the v3.1-era offline strict curve. (c) recalc-c §10/§11: no periodic-cadence run, no D10 worker-count sweep (only 4 workers ever ran); staging saturates ~450/s with committer count/batch named-but-never-swept as the scale knob. (d) The harness is structurally not multi-day-ready: single accounting period ending current_date (midnight breaks it), verify loads every trx_line into memory, no host-noise capture in reports (memory: this host swings 2x+ under Chrome; single-shot 12-20s rungs are the exact short-run-noise failure mode acct-ezm exposed).

What: calibrate a host-realistic SLO (or declare the p99-vs-rate curve the baseline) and commit a per-rung JSON snapshot next to soak-results.md; add a depth axis to ledger-bench (deep-seed layers per pool) measuring incremental step, full replay after a floor drop, and forced-close drain at depths 10/100/1000/10000; sweep SOAK_WORKERS {1,2,4,8} and a periodic-cadence variant; sweep drainers x drain_batch at the 800/1600 rungs; seed a rolling multi-period calendar, make verify windowed, capture /proc/loadavg + process snapshot into every LoadOutcome, add SWEEP_REPEATS taking the median. Then a bounded multi-hour soak recording growth-rate and gauge trends (n_dead_tup + pg_relation_size sampling on hot tables; evaluate pool_state fillfactor if bloat shows).

PROVENANCE: bench-ops (6 items merged), parity (depth axis); soak-results §7, recalc-c §10/§11, memory: noisy bench host
