title: Property-net extensions: specific/std methods, standard basis, multi-line shapes, seed replay, unit-test gaps
description:
Why: (a) 'specific' appears in zero property nets and std is absent from the recalc/close nets — two of the hot-path audit's findings live exactly in specific's unprobed region; method-isolation invariants (R7/C7) check only that WAC pools gain no settlement state, so a method-scoping regression (strict fold running on std) would go uncaught. (b) Every random FL pool uses provisional_basis='running_avg'; the acct-qm7o.10 defect lived in precisely one basis×arm×sign cell no harness reached. (c) All random nets submit single-line transactions only; the Phase-2 'deadlock-free by construction' two-tier lock-order claim has never been exercised against overlapping pool sets, and no concurrent multi-line submit test exists. (d) TestRunner::default() is unseeded with no persisted corpus — a known-failing case is not retained and greenness is probabilistic at known flake horizons. (e) run-tests.sh never executes ledger-feed's pgoutput unit tests or ledger-spi-common's lib tests (the --test flag skips lib tests), and decode_trx_line has zero units (missing/NULL/non-int column, unknown relation). (f) The WAC negative-derived-average edge (acct-qm7o.2 close reason) needs a zero-cost-receipt seed to become reachable, then a deliberate clamp-vs-reject decision.

What: extend METHODS with specific+std in recalc/close/backpressure nets asserting non-strict pools are no-ops (no settlement row, never swept, never counted); randomize provisional_basis per FL pool (seed standard_cost when drawn); add a multi-line op (2-4 lines, random pools, shared posted_at) plus a concurrent multi-line submit stress asserting zero deadlocks; honor PROPTEST_SEED env (log the seed every run); add the lib-test blocks to run-tests.sh and the decode units; add the zero-cost WAC seed. Also add a small randomized concurrent property binary (2 worker tasks + 1 feed + 1 submitter over 1-2 shared fifo pools per case, then quiesce and run R1-R8 reference-anchor checks) — the tier that found acct-qm7o.8 only exists as hand-built choreographies today.

PROVENANCE: tests (6 items merged), archaeology (WAC edge, qm7o.10 lesson); property_*.rs METHODS lines, run-tests.sh:39-75

title: Privilege surface: revoke PUBLIC execute on the extension API
description:
FOUND BY the audit completeness critic. Zero GRANT/REVOKE across all 19 migrations and the crate SQL; PG grants EXECUTE to PUBLIC on new functions by default, so every entry point (ledger_submit_trx, ledger_recalc_step, ledger_staging_drain, ledger_close_period, ledger_settle_pool) plus the raw tables are callable/writable by any connecting role. Fine for a single-user dev PoC; wrong posture for graduation. WORK: a migration that REVOKEs PUBLIC and GRANTs to a ledger_rw role; document the role model in the README; note the backport implication (parent repo RBAC = consolidated doc Q6, still open).

title: Failed-inbox requeue SPI + SQLSTATE capture
description:
Why: failed ledger_inbox rows are terminal — after fixing the underlying config (e.g. the missing posting_account_map row that failed every envelope of a pool), each failed envelope must be re-enqueued by hand; no requeue SPI or script exists. The error column stores message text only (drain.rs:195-204), so failure classes cannot be queried by SQLSTATE.

What: a requeue function (failed → pending with an attempt counter), an errcode column populated from the caught error report, and a test covering fix-config-then-requeue-succeeds. (Inbox tail pruning is covered by the retention issue in the write-amplification epic.) Also align the two InsufficientInventory message shapes: the WAC CTE gate-fail raise (submit.rs:275-281) omits the available count that ledger-core's variant includes.

title: OPERATIONS.md: symptom → diagnosis → remediation runbook with alert thresholds
description:
Why: no operations document exists anywhere in the stream, but Phase 6 already generated the exact incident catalog one must cover: ENOSPC recovery with feed/workers wedged in retry loops (soak §4), wedged-pool diagnosis via identical repeating claim errors (§5), throttled pools surfacing SQLSTATE 53400 and what auto-releases them (§8), the close gate-fail persisted state='closing' and how it converges (README Phase 5), and slot loss/recovery. It all lives scattered across bench narrative, bd close reasons, and code comments. Gauges have no thresholds — what G2b gross or g2c_oldest_mark_ms is alarming is undefined — and no sampler exists outside a bench run (bench/out is gitignored).

What: write OPERATIONS.md keyed on the recalc-c §7 gauge table: per symptom (gauge reading / SQLSTATE) give the diagnosis query and remediation axis, covering ENOSPC, wedged pool, stuck throttle, gate-fail close, slot loss. title: Operational gauge surface: G3 conservation view, negative_pools, drift bound, method-scoped recalc_pool_lag
description:
Why: (a) recalc-c §7 lists G3 (conservation sweep) as a first-class detection signal alongside G1/G2, but it shipped only inside ledger-bench verify — requires the harness and quiesce; nothing runs conservation on a cadence in a production posture. (b) The §16 'flagged, not rejected' negative-inventory posture has NO flag surface: no view lists pools with aggregate qty < 0, no negatives count in the close report — yet uncovered depletions swing the drift tail hardest (soak §3). (c) recalc-c §7's drift bound (G2b gross × the oracle's per-depletion rel%, measured 22-36%) is computed nowhere — the operator must do the arithmetic by hand. (d) recalc_pool_lag (0015) is not method-scoped: wac/std/specific pools have no pool_settlement row and read as forever-unsettled; the fix was applied in the bench sampler and the close gate but never in the raw operator view (acct-qm7o.6 lesson).

What: one migration + small function set — V1 per-pool qty conservation as a view, V2's fold as a callable function, a negative_pools view (pool, qty, since-when), a drift_bound column (unsettled_gross × configured rel%) on recalc_pool_lag, and a method filter (or exposed pool.method column) on recalc_pool_lag. Schedule the conservation check via pg_cron as the G3 recon job or document the operator cadence.

PROVENANCE: design-core, recalc-notes, bench-ops, parity, archaeology (recalc-c §7, 0014/0015, verify.rs, soak §3)

title: Feed hardening: singleton enforcement, floor line_type filter, env footguns
description:
Why: (a) consumer.rs:36-39 commits to exactly-one-consumer but nothing enforces it — two run-feed.sh instances interleave successfully; marks/floors are idempotent but the backpressure bump double-counts persistently between settles (~2x pending_events → spurious 53400 engages well below the real bound). (b) The feed's guarded-min recost-floor UPDATE has no line_type filter, so a cost_adjustment_line delivery can participate in floor lowering on day-granularity timestamp collisions (acct-qm7o.8 close reason deferred this as latent test fragility). (c) FEED_SLOT/FEED_PUBLICATION env overrides let an operator rename the slot while the 0014 feed_lag view hardcodes slot_name='ledger_feed' — a renamed slot works functionally but blinds G1 and the close report (NULL, same as no slot).

What: pg_try_advisory_lock keyed on the slot name at consumer startup, refuse to run second (one-line guard); add line_type <> 'cost_adjustment_line' to the floor UPDATE; drop the env overrides (single-slot posture makes them footguns) or make the gauge enumerate slots on the publication. If the close-gate slot-check issue lands first, align naming there.

PROVENANCE: feed, recalc-notes, archaeology, parity (consumer.rs:36-39/278-305, 0014:18, acct-qm7o.8 deferred item)

title: Close-transaction scalability: pre-drain, sweep scoping, settle_pool budget, D12 disposition
description:
Why (four coupled findings on one code path): (a) recalc-e §5 scopes the sweep to pools with in-period activity, but gate_pools scopes on EXISTS activity at-or-before end-of-period (close.rs:386-390) — monotonically accumulating, so close cost/lock footprint grows with total pool population (headline soak already sweeps 200 pools) and each swept pool's hot-path appends freeze from aggregate-lock acquisition until close commit. (b) D12 (forced-close drain granularity) was never ratified: the drain is single-caller serial inside one close transaction (close.rs:171-203), paying Σ(per-pool folds) serially exactly where the 25-events/s deep-pool fold floor binds, with workers locked OUT. (c) The feed applies each batch in one transaction, so a batch touching ANY swept pool stalls the ENTIRE feed for the close duration (documented, not redesigned, in the acct-qm7o.7 close reason). (d) ledger_settle_pool drains with NO aggregate lock (close.rs:251-267) — sustained appends outpacing the fold hit MAX_DRAIN_PASSES=10000 and abort the whole transaction, re-paying the entire fold on retry.

What: pre-drain gate-scoped pools via parallel ledger_settle_pool calls BEFORE taking the closer mutex (shrinks the in-mutex drain to stragglers); scope the sweep to in-period activity or a lock-free nonzero-drift pre-screen; give ledger_settle_pool an optional aggregate-lock mode (convergent) or a pass-budget parameter returning partial progress; record the D12 disposition and the append-freeze window in the spec/close report.

PROVENANCE: recalc-notes (2 items), recalc-close (2 items), archaeology (close.rs:167-203/251-267/464-513, recalc-e §5/§6/§10)

title: Bound full replay: closed-boundary checkpoint + streaming scan
description:
Why: any recost floor replays from opening (opening = Vec::new(), scan from None — recalc.rs:166-173). D11 resolved 'no historical checkpoints in v3.2' on the rationale that they only pay off for backdates into closed periods — but 0017 makes the closed prefix immutable and rejects backdated inserts into it, so on a healthy system floors can never point below the last closed period's end: a single layer-state checkpoint persisted at each close would bound every future full replay to O(open-period events) with no reopen machinery. As periods accumulate, per-backdate replay cost otherwise grows with total pool history (recalc-b §2: ~25 events/s at depth 50k). Compounding: the pass is O(stream) in worker memory — scan_events collects the whole stream into a Vec, and decide_queue/load_priors ship all scanned ids as one ANY(bigint[]) array (recalc.rs:463-528, 908-931).

What: persist a per-pool opening checkpoint (layer snapshot + frontier) at ledger_close_period and start full replays there; stream the event scan cursor-wise; replace the scanned-ids ANY-array missed-probe with a range/anti-join formulation. Note: a future reopen workflow invalidates the checkpoint — sequence with the reopen design issue.

Acceptance: full-replay-after-floor cost measured flat vs closed-history depth; property_recalc_engine R1-R8 unchanged.

PROVENANCE: recalc-close (P2/backport), archaeology (D11 rows); recalc.rs:166-173/463-528, design-v3.2-recalc-b §2

title: Wire-contract guard sweep: negative unit_cost at decode, trx_type allowlist, zero-line reject, CTE method predicate
description:
Why (four small, related holes): (1) trx_line CHECK unit_cost >= 0 rejects negative asserted cost for wac/fifo/lifo/specific receipts, but STD records c_std not the actual — a caller sign typo silently lands as a large favorable PPV variance on the fifth method (standard.rs:114-139). (2) insert_trx casts caller text straight to the trx_type enum, so a caller can burn the engine-reserved 'cost_adjustment' label + sequence key (bulk_write.rs:96-98 vs 0008); line_type IS allowlisted — the trx_type asymmetry is the gap. (3) An empty lines[] / all-zero-qty submission inserts a line-less trx row and permanently consumes its idempotency key. (4) None of the four hot-path CTEs predicate on pool.method — a stray UPDATE pool SET method lets a WAC statement post a cost leg against a re-labeled fifo pool silently; recalc.rs:979-988 already models the in-statement re-check pattern.

What: one decode-time unit_cost >= 0 check in apply_submission (covers direct + staging); allowlist caller trx_types (reject 'cost_adjustment'); reject zero-effective-line submissions; add a pool.method predicate (join/EXISTS) to WAC_RECEIPT/WAC_DEPLETE/FL_RECEIPT/FL_DEPLETE so a routing disagreement writes nothing and surfaces as the expect_row internal error. Tests for each rejection.

PROVENANCE: hot-path (4 merged items: standard.rs, bulk_write.rs:84-108, submit.rs:114-146, cte.rs); memory: defensive guards are load-bearing

title: v3.2 hot path: FL_DEPLETE missing-row arm decrements value_sum by unclamped standard cost while recording the clamped 0
description:
FOUND BY the acct-qm7o.9 pre-commit verification workflow (wf_bb04a8c0-536, refute:formula agent) as the one (method x arm x sign) cell where the recorded line cost diverges from the value_sum decrement. Currently unreachable in every harness (all seeds use non-negative costs) but latent: standard_cost.unit_cost is BIGINT NOT NULL with NO >= 0 CHECK (migration 0003), and submit.rs passes the raw stored value as FL_DEPLETE $3 for standard-basis fifo/lifo depletions.

DEFECT (ledger-direct/src/cte.rs FL_DEPLETE): the ON CONFLICT UPDATE arm clamps the value_sum decrement (GREATEST(COALESCE($3, pool_state.unit_cost), 0)) and the RETURNING applied_uc clamps in both arms (GREATEST(COALESCE($3, old.unit_cost, 0), 0)) — but the missing-row VALUES arm writes value_sum = (($2 * COALESCE($3, 0)) * -1) UNCLAMPED. Cell: standard-basis FL pool + negative stored standard cost + first-ever physical event on the pool is a depletion => value_sum INCREASES by |qty x cost| while the trx_line records unit_cost 0 (passing the trx_line unit_cost >= 0 CHECK). Breaks the CTE doc contract "the clamped cost also drives the value_sum decrement, keeping value_sum == Σ signed qty×recorded-cost reconcilable to the lines"; R3 (apply-order fold) and verify V2 would diverge silently.

REMEDY ALTERNATIVES (decide before implementing): (a) clamp the VALUES arm (one-expression cte.rs fix; engine rebuild + reinstall + full suite tier); (b) migration 0019 CHECK (unit_cost >= 0) on standard_cost making negative standards unrepresentable (no rebuild; aligns storage with the trx_line CHECK and the clamping convention); (c) both — formula self-consistency AND domain validity (defensive-guards posture: the clamp stays load-bearing for future edit surfaces even once the CHECK makes it unreachable).
close_reason: DECISION RECORD: user ratified remedy (c) BOTH via AskUserQuestion. (1) cte.rs FL_DEPLETE missing-row VALUES arm now decrements value_sum by GREATEST(COALESCE($3,0),0) — every arm of the statement uses the same clamped cost as the RETURNING applied_uc, restoring the documented contract value_sum == sum(signed qty x recorded-cost) on all arms. (2) Migration 0019 adds CHECK (unit_cost >= 0) to standard_cost — negative standards rejected at the source, aligned with trx_line unit_cost CHECK. Clamp kept despite CHECK-unreachability per the defensive-guards posture (load-bearing for future edit surfaces). Regression tests in acceptance_direct_methods: standard-basis first-event depletion pins the missing-row arm math (recorded == decrement basis, aggregate (-qty, 0, -qty x standard)); negative INSERT raises 23514. Engine-touch tier honored: release rebuild + reinstall + docker restart + orphan sweep + full suite green (13 binaries / 0 red). NO soak (user constraint: high machine usage; none needed — one-expression formula fix + CHECK). Found by acct-qm7o.9 verification wf_bb04a8c0-536 refute:formula agent. Shipped as e9690f1.

title: v3.2: lazy per-pool backpressure (recalc-c §5) — global flag + throttled set + hot-path consult
description: Deferred from acct-qm7o.4 by explicit decision (dkk, 2026-07-11): the recalc engine phase shipped without the recalc-c §5 backpressure lever. Scope: the deliberate, lazily-engaged re-coupling — a cheap global "backpressure active" flag gating a per-pool throttled-set consult on the hot path (alt-C read-free property preserved in the common case); bound tied to the G2 gauges (per-pool settled_through lag ceiling and/or dirty-set depth), engage at the bound, release at a low-water mark. Touches the shipped phase-2 hot path (admission control on ledger_submit_trx / ledger_staging_drain), which is why it is its own reviewable slice. recalc-c §5 is the design; §10 lists the soak assertions (engages exactly at the bound, releases at low-water, stays off otherwise). Not correctness-affecting: nothing makes a hot pool fold faster (recalc-b §3 ceiling); this only stops the qty plane running arbitrarily far ahead of authoritative cost.
design:
DECIDED (dkk via AskUserQuestion, 2026-07-11) — all five STEP 0 choices:
(a) Bound metric: per-pool UNSETTLED-EVENT COUNT (G2a-shape), maintained as a cheap counter — feed increments at mark time (FL pools only, excluding cost_adjustment_line), engine RESETS to the exact indexed count above its new frontier at settle (transient feed-lag skew is wiped every settle, so residue never accumulates). No trx_line scans on the hot path.
(b) Throttle semantics: REJECT AT ADMISSION on both paths with SQLSTATE 53400 (configuration_limit_exceeded) — ledger_submit_trx checks touched pools pre-write; a BEFORE INSERT trigger on ledger_inbox gates enqueue (raw-INSERT surface). ledger_staging_drain untouched: envelopes admitted before engagement still apply, never retroactively failed. apply_submission gains an enforce flag (submit=true, drain=false).
(c) Storage: plain logged tables. recalc_backlog(pool_id PK, pending_events) = the counter/gauge; recalc_backpressure(pool_id PK, engaged_at, engage_events) = the throttled set (EXISTS probe on its PK IS the cheap global flag — empty-index probe on the common path); recalc_backpressure_config single row (bound_events, low_water). No shmem, no posture change.
(d) Ownership: SPLIT — feed ENGAGES (after counter upsert, INSERT into throttled set where pending_events >= bound, FL-scoped), engine RELEASES (at settle, after exact-count reset, DELETE where pending_events <= low_water). No sweeper; transitions fire exactly at the events that change the metric. Row-lock order everywhere: pool_settlement -> recalc_backlog -> recalc_backpressure (matches existing feed floor-then-mark order; engine counter write happens at settle tail so feed blocks at most for the settle-commit window).
(e) Defaults: bound_events=200, low_water=20 (config-table tunables per D10; ~3x observed healthy global max; paused-worker rig crosses it in tens of seconds).
Scope guards: close/settle_pool on a throttled pool auto-releases via its settles (close must always be able to drain); engine/close internal writes are NOT gated (admission-only); WAC/STD/specific pools never engage (FL scoping at both counter and engage).
notes:
RESUME PLAN (written pre-compaction 2026-07-11; acct-qm7o.8 SHIPPED as 1cbf114 and CLOSED — phases 1-6 + the .8 P1 all closed with decision records; HEAD 1cbf114 on branch ledger-v3.2, worktree /home/kaalin/dev/acct/.claude/worktrees/ledger-v3.2, paths under poc/ledger-v3.2/).

READ ORDER before anything: (1) bd show acct-qm7o (epic onboarding) + THIS issue in full; (2) poc/design_research/design-v3.2-recalc-c.md sections 5 (the lever: lazy engagement — cheap global "backpressure active" flag gating a per-pool throttled-set consult; common case stays read-free preserving alt-C; bound = per-pool settled_through lag ceiling AND/OR dirty-set-depth ceiling; engage at bound, release at low-water), 10 (the soak assertions this must pass: engages EXACTLY at the bound, releases at the low-water mark, stays OFF otherwise), 11 (interfaces), plus design-v3.2.md section 16 (why alt C severed the hot-path->recalc coupling — backpressure deliberately re-couples, last resort not steady state); (3) bench/soak-results.md section 4 — the adjustment-storm write-amplification + ENOSPC finding is the natural input (bullet: "cadence alone does not bound the storm; the write-amplification rate is the natural backpressure input, and slot-lag/ENOSPC is what quiet backlog escalates to"); (4) the code to touch/consult: ledger-direct/src/submit.rs + cte.rs (direct hot path), drain.rs (staging path), close.rs gate (per-pool G2 lag precedent + gauge queries), db/migrations/0015 gauge views, ledger-bench/src/gauges.rs (G2 sampler joins method IN (fifo,lifo)) and soak.rs (--pause-workers drives G2 up = the natural engage/release test rig).

STEP 0 — MANDATORY AskUserQuestion BEFORE writing code (the issue + recalc-c section 5 enumerate alternatives; per the surface-design-choices rule, claiming is NOT authorization to pick): (a) bound metric — per-pool unsettled-event count (G2a-style), per-pool unsettled gross value (G2b-style), settled_through wall-clock age, and/or global dirty-set depth; (b) throttle semantics per path — direct ledger_submit_trx: reject with a distinct SQLSTATE vs wait; staging: reject at enqueue vs ledger_staging_drain skipping/deferring throttled pools' envelopes in the inbox (defer keeps intent, changes drain fairness); (c) flag/set storage — the extension is SHMEM-FREE today (run-tests.sh relies on it; no preload per the no-preload-for-inactive-streams rule) so shared memory would change install/test posture: plain single-row table + throttled-pools table vs unlogged table vs other; (d) engage/release ownership — engine pass (sees its pool's post-fold lag), feed apply (sees marks/floors), or both; (e) default bound values + low-water (D10 posture says soak-output tunable, ship as GUC-like table config).

SCOPE after answers: one migration (0018+, content-addressed — never edit applied ones) for throttle state/config; hot-path gate wiring (flag check cheap; throttled-set consult only when flag on); engage/release transitions with low-water hysteresis; tests per the property-per-entry-point convention (acceptance binary for engage-at-bound/release-at-low-water/off-otherwise + property invariant: gate never fires when all pools under bound); a bounded soak demonstration using --pause-workers to drive G2 over the bound (engage) then resume workers (drain -> release) — recalc-c section 10 assertions; docs: README phase paragraph + bench/soak-results.md addendum if a soak run produces numbers worth recording.

Ultracode is on for this session: use Workflow orchestration for substantive design-space exploration / adversarial verification (the .8 pre-commit verify workflow pattern paid for itself — caught a comment misattribution, a test strengthening, and found acct-qm7o.9).

SHIPPED as e3cc835. All five STEP 0 design choices user-ratified via AskUserQuestion (recorded in --design): (a) per-pool unsettled-event count, feed-incremented / engine-exact-reset; (b) reject-at-admission both paths, SQLSTATE 53400, drain exempt; (c) plain logged tables, shmem-free preserved; (d) feed engages / engine releases (engine also applies the bound to its own reset — completion, not deviation; deterministically tested); (e) defaults 200/20 in a deletion-guarded config table.

Pre-commit adversarial verification (6-skeptic ultracode workflow, wf_c80a6fd2-385, ~708k tokens) refuted 4 of 6 claims and drove real fixes before commit:
- WEDGE (fixed + red-green): feed marks ran before counter bumps; a pass settling events whose delivery was in flight could consume the queue row while the mark was swallowed by ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING against the claim-locked row, leaving the late bump as permanent residue (engaged, empty tail, no queue row, admission rejecting the re-marking appends). Fix: apply order floors -> bumps -> MARKS; the trailing mark re-creates the deleted queue row, guaranteeing the healing pass. Pinned by late_delivery_of_settled_events_heals_via_trailing_mark (three-party lock-queue choreography; RED in 0.34s under marks-first, GREEN fixed).
- Cross-pool deadlock class on recalc_backlog (feed one-statement bump, arbitrary GROUP BY lock order, vs close sweep sequential): fixed by ascending pool-id lock order in the bump (close sweeps ascending via gate_pools ORDER BY p.id); standalone feed loop now retries errored ticks instead of panicking (deadlock-victim resilience).
- Trigger hardened fail-open on malformed payloads (error surface no longer depends on throttle state; psql-verified); config singleton deletion-guarded; engine engage gained a local fifo/lifo method guard.
- Surviving-mutant test gaps closed: engine at-bound engage (engine_engages_when_reset_lands_at_bound, feed-lag window), <=-boundary release + exact-tail-reset-vs-decrement discrimination (test-4 second parked leg with pre-staged drain-exempt envelopes), 53400-before-23505 gate precedence on duplicate sources.

Deliberately NOT taken (scope guards): below-frontier/backdate-flood throttling — the ratified metric is the un-costed tail; backdate storms are the write-amplification axis (soak-results §4/§8 scope note), bounded by cadence + close gate, future input if ever needed. Close-duration feed stall on swept pools' counter rows — same pre-existing exposure class as the sweep's pool_settlement holds, documented not redesigned. Bump non-idempotence under at-least-once redelivery — conservative direction, wiped at next settle, documented in consumer.rs header. Pass-abort -> sticky throttle — pre-existing wedged-engine alarm surface (G2a/G2c + worker errors), correct to throttle a stuck pool, resolution is D14 reopen workflow.

Validation: full suite 13 DB binaries / 63 tests green (incl. 7-case acceptance + 100-case property_backpressure + R9 in property_recalc_engine); soak demonstrations on shipped code — stays-off (max per-pool backlog 6 vs bound 200, drift identical to §3 baseline) and engage/release (40 pools engaged, hot-pool backlog frozen at 203 = bound + batch overshoot, 1511+1518 classified rejects, clean release through an unforced close; the post-close 55000 probe doubles as a no-stuck-throttle assertion). bench/soak-results.md §8 + README backpressure paragraph document the shipped story.

title: ledger-v3.1: optional stateright/TLA+ model of the SKIP LOCKED staging drain
description:
Optional formal-methods complement, scoped OUT of acct-0at4.6 (which shipped the two mandatory layers: the ledger-core model-equivalence proptest and the kill-9 staging-recovery loop). The gate re-scope (acct-0at4.11.5, design-v3.1 §18) listed "a light stateright model of the SKIP LOCKED drain" as optional; this issue captures it as a deliberate future exploration rather than dropping it.

WHAT TO MODEL
A stateright (Rust model checker) or TLA+ model of the SPIKE-A staging-drain protocol (ledger-direct-c/src/drain.rs, driven from ledger_inbox):
  caller enqueue (own tx) -> committer claim (FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED, ORDER BY id, LIMIT) -> apply via ledger-core -> mark rows done -> (optional crash between any steps) -> restart -> reclaim.
Abstract the ledger apply to a boolean "applied" effect; the interesting state is the row lifecycle (pending / claimed-by-K / applied-not-committed / done) across K concurrent committers plus crash/restart transitions.

PROPERTIES TO CHECK
  - Safety: no submission is ever double-terminal (applied+committed twice) — the trx UNIQUE (trx_type, source_id) key and the atomic claim+apply+mark-done tx must make this unreachable; no submission is orphaned forever (claimed then lost).
  - Liveness: every enqueued row eventually reaches a terminal state (done, whether committed or dropped) under fair committer scheduling.

WHY OPTIONAL / DEFERRED
  - The crash-safety this would formalize is already covered EMPIRICALLY by scripts/kill9-staging-recovery.sh (acct-0at4.6 Part 2): 3/3 iterations conservation-clean with ~50k in-flight rows hard-killed and WAL-recovered per crash.
  - No-double-claim under FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED is a Postgres lock-manager guarantee, not a property of our code — a model would be re-deriving Postgres semantics.
  - stateright is a heavy new dev-dependency (not in the workspace today) for marginal added assurance over the empirical loop.
The value is a machine-checked liveness/safety argument as a complement to the crash loop — worth it if the drain protocol grows (per-pool committer partitioning, a real 23505 re-drive path, backpressure), not before.

BUILDING BLOCKS ALREADY PRESENT
  ledger-direct-c/src/drain.rs (the drain), bench/spike-a-inbox.sql (ledger_inbox), scripts/kill9-staging-recovery.sh (empirical crash loop), ledger-verify (conservation sweep).
acceptance_criteria: A stateright or TLA+ model of the staging-drain protocol exists and its safety (no double-terminal, none orphaned) + liveness (every row eventually terminal) properties are machine-checked green; OR a written decision that the empirical kill-9 loop is sufficient and this stays closed. Either outcome resolves the issue.
notes: Sibling of the closed acct-0at4.6. Do NOT auto-start — exploratory, P3, no downstream blocker. If picked up, confirm whether stateright vs TLA+ before adding the dep (surface the choice).

title: ledger-v3.1 ARCH-ALT-CATALOG: document deferred alternatives E (app-tier partitioned consumer) + F (TB split) with rationale
description:
Source: FEEDBACK-ARCH.md alternatives E + F. Documentation-completeness — the decision record must state what was considered and rejected, with rationale. Downstream of the gate (written as part of dispositioning the decision).

## E — Application-tier partitioned consumer
Same single-writer-per-pool idea as routed, but as an **ordinary service**: pools sharded across worker processes (consistent hash or Kafka-partition-style assignment), each worker batching its pools' events into ordinary PG transactions. Identical batching math to the routed committer; ordinary deployment / upgrade / debugging; horizontal scale-out; PG returns to being storage. The shmem design is precisely this pattern implanted into the postmaster — the implantation bought enqueue latency and paid for it in lifecycle (flag-day upgrades, gdb-against-postgres, replica-invisibility). Document why in-postmaster was chosen over app-tier, or flip.

## F — Revisit the TigerBeetle split already designed
The earlier ledger design had TB as the hot quantity/value plane with PG for catalog + projections. TB's native batching (8k transfers/commit, single-writer core) **is** the routed committer — built by people who did nothing else for years, with the debit/credit invariants enforced in the engine. Path C inside pgrx is, from one angle, a reimplementation of TB's write path with weaker guarantees to avoid operating a second database. That tradeoff might still be right — but given the prior art is the project's own, it should be an **explicit comparison** in the doc, not an unstated assumption. (Note: the parent acct repo has committed hard to Postgres-native / no-TB-parity; this item is to record the comparison for the v3.1 PoC decision, not to reopen the parent's direction.)

## Acceptance
design-v3.1 gains an "alternatives considered" subsection covering E (app-tier partitioned consumer) and F (TB split) with an explicit keep/reject rationale for each, consistent with whatever posture + spike verdict the gate produces.
acceptance_criteria: design-v3.1 'alternatives considered' subsection covering E + F with keep/reject rationale, consistent with the gate's posture + spike verdict.

F (TB split) is a sharper comparison under alt C (insert-only hot path == TB write path) but recorded as comparison only; the parent acct repo has committed to Postgres-native / no-TB-parity and this does not reopen it.

title: ledger-v3.1: review-surfaced smaller architecture/schema items (roll-up)
description:
Source: FEEDBACK.md (poc/ledger-v3.1) findings #6, #7, #10, #16, #17, #18, #19. Each is minor individually; grouped so none is lost. Split any that grow teeth into its own issue.

- **#17 `trx_line (pool_id, id)` composite index** — *most actionable of this set.* §14.1 tells queries to "replay trx_line directly" and recalc/close walks per-pool streams in id order; `trx_line_pool(pool_id)` alone forces a sort. Cheap now, painful against a large table later. Also unblocks efficient offline replay (the variance-magnitude issue). Land the index or record why not.

- **#6 Routed durability asymmetry / outbox framing** — trx ⟹ caller committed, but caller committed ⇏ trx (postmaster crash, poison, spurious drop). Recovery = "caller observes absence and resubmits" ⇒ a production caller needs a durable pending-submission record + reconciliation poller = a transactional outbox. Once the caller has an outbox, the shmem queue is a latency/batching optimization, not a reliability primitive. §6.1 should state this; it also weighs on the §11.4 crossover (direct-batched carries none of this caller-side machinery cost).

- **#7 `pool_lock` row `FOR UPDATE` vs `pg_advisory_xact_lock(pool_id)`** — the row lock writes xmax (XLOG_HEAP_LOCK, page dirty) per acquisition: WAL + checkpoint churn on one hot page, in a PoC whose headline metric is lock-hold time. Advisory lock gives identical blocking/release-at-commit with zero WAL and removes the §5.1-step-2 lazy-create dance and the table. Costs (advisory keyspace collision, less introspectable) are real but minor. Record why the row-lock design won — or ablate it (covered by the baselines/ablations issue).

- **#10 Idempotency key granularity** — `UNIQUE(trx_type, source_id)` = one ledger event per business doc per type, ever. Corrected/reopened receipts, a second adjustment vs the same doc, or two upstream systems sharing an id space all collide. Dedup is also first-write-wins with no payload comparison → a retry with *mutated* lines is silently skipped, not conflict-flagged. A payload hash in the dedup would catch it cheaply. (Defensible for a PoC; flag for production.)

- **#16 `posting_line` pair-dimension** — paired debit/credit-per-row means `posting_line_dimension` attaches to the *pair*, so the debit leg can't be dimensioned differently from the credit leg (cost_center on the expense side only). One-row-per-leg with signed amount is the conventional fix; trial-balance queries also then need a UNION over both account columns.

- **#18 Poison evidence lives only in shmem** — postmaster restart erases the submissions AND the evidence they were poisoned. Production dead-lettering must be a table, or §6.8's "operator review" posture is vapor. Fine as a PoC metric; note the production requirement.

- **#19 Input CHECKs under-specified at schema level** — no CHECK against `qty=0` trx_lines (makes the §3.7 sign-based direction rule undefined) or negative unit_cost receipts. ledger-core presumably guards; state where the authority lives (schema vs core).

## Acceptance
Each item is either implemented, or gets a one-line disposition in the design doc (accept / defer / reject, with reason). The #17 index is landed or explicitly deferred with rationale.

title: Routed: reclaim CAS valid 2->1 is not identity-gated — ABA yanks a re-claimed live entry
description: Found while fixing acct-mvq4.32 (Q11), distinct from it. try_reclaim_dead_committer_entry (router.rs ~937-964) reads (valid==2, generation=G_dead, slot=S_dead), confirms is_committer_alive(S_dead,G_dead)==false, then CAS valid 2->1 — gating on valid ONLY, never re-checking identity. Interleaving: reclaimer R1 reads the dead entry; before R1 CASes, a second reclaimer R2 (another committer boot running reclaim_dead_committers, or the router sweep) fully reclaims it (valid 2->1) AND a live committer C re-claims it (claim_next_committer_entry: valid 1->2, generation=G_c). R1 stale CAS 2->1 still sees valid==2 and succeeds, yanking C live claim back to valid==1 while C is actively processing the group. Consequences: (a) a new claimer C2 elects on the now valid==1/gen==0 entry and double-processes the SAME commit_group as C -> duplicate writes (only partially masked by dedup_against_trx, and only if C already committed) plus cleanup double-free; (b) C finalize (CAS 2->3 in finalize_committer_queue_slot) fails against the yanked valid==1, leaving the entry at valid==1 AFTER C frees the CQ arena via free_committer_queue_arena -> a subsequent claim reads freed arena offsets (use-after-free) or emit reuses them (cross-corruption). Reachable when multiple committers boot concurrently (each calls reclaim_dead_committers) racing the same dead entry with an interleaved re-claim; rare, recovery-path only. PRE-EXISTING (present before acct-mvq4.32): the yank is the identity-unvalidated CAS, unchanged by the .32 reclaim reorder — that reorder only widens the R1 read->CAS window by four relaxed stores, negligible next to the is_alive kill() syscall already in that window. Distinct from Q11 (which was the slot=MAX memory-ordering clobber); this is an identity-unvalidated CAS.
design: Anchor the reclaim to the specific dead generation instead of a bare valid CAS. Preferred shape: use CAS committer_bgw_generation from G_dead->0 (AcqRel) as the arbiter, and only on its success flip valid 2->1 (Release). A concurrent re-claim advances generation to G_c, so the generation CAS fails and the reclaimer aborts WITHOUT yanking the live claim. Must preserve the identity-clear-before-valid-Release ordering acct-mvq4.32 established (the generation store is now the arbiter, so the slot=MAX clear and the valid flip order need re-checking against both Q11 and this fix together). Alternative: re-read generation==G_dead immediately after the valid CAS and roll back the 2->1 if it changed — messier; the generation-CAS-arbiter is cleaner. A deterministic test likely needs a test hook to hold R1 between its identity read and its CAS while another thread runs the R2-reclaim + C-reclaim.
notes: X-ref acct-mvq4.32 (Q11 sibling, commit 103c489), AUDIT-PASS3 section B-ii.6, is_committer_alive semantics in identity.rs. Do NOT conflate with Q11: Q11 was memory-ordering (fixed); this is CAS-atomicity/ABA (open). Surfaced to the user 2026-07-07 during .32 close; user approved filing.
close_reason: Identity-gated the dead-committer reclaim: arbiter is now the generation CAS G_dead->0 (AcqRel), symmetric to claim_next_committer_entry, replacing the identity-unvalidated `valid 2->1` CAS that allowed an ABA yank of a re-claimed live entry. Extracted commit_dead_committer_reclaim() pure helper + 3 unit tests (incl. core ABA regression). Verified: 76/76 lib + 7/7 live orphan-recovery green. Commit pending in HEAD.

title: Pass-3 Q13: u32 xid staged where xid8 epoch semantics are required — post-epoch triage misclassifies to keep
description: Found by acct-mvq4.4 (AUDIT-PASS3.md section B-ii.6 Q13, P3, production-later). ledger_enqueue_trx_c stages GetCurrentTransactionId() (u32 TransactionId) widened to u64 (enqueue.rs:97/:243); classify_and_eject feeds it to pg_xact_status(x::xid8), which expects an epoch-qualified FullTransactionId. Below 2^32 transactions the epoch is 0 and everything agrees; after xid-epoch advance, staged values reference epoch-0 xids -> pg_xact_status returns NULL (too old) -> CallerTxStatus::Unknown -> KEPT - in-progress caller work would be committed. Unreachable in any PoC run (epoch 0 throughout); a correctness time-bomb for a long-lived production deployment. Fix: GetCurrentFullTransactionId().
close_reason: Fixed (commit, see log). ledger_enqueue_trx_c / _batch_c now stage GetCurrentFullTransactionId().value (64-bit epoch-qualified) instead of GetCurrentTransactionId() widened to u64 (epoch 0). classify_and_eject feeds this to pg_xact_status(x::xid8) which needs a FullTransactionId; the old bare 32-bit xid would, after an xid-epoch advance, resolve to a too-old xid -> NULL -> CallerTxStatus::Unknown -> wrongly KEPT (committing in-progress caller work). Same assign-if-none semantics preserved; consumer pipeline was already u64 so this is the only change; epoch-0 (all PoC runs) numerically identical so reachable path unaffected. Schema regen touched only generated source-line provenance comments. Full routed acceptance suite green (5 binaries / 27 tests incl. enqueue path + ledger_enqueue_trx_c property test).

title: Pass-3 Q12: COMMITTER_QUEUE share guard held across the entire SPI write phase — router exclusive-claim starvation
description: Found by acct-mvq4.4 (AUDIT-PASS3.md section B-ii.6 Q12, P3, structural lock hygiene). attempt_commit_phase takes COMMITTER_QUEUE.share() at committer.rs:645 and keeps it alive across pool_lock FOR UPDATE waits (up to deadlock_timeout), hydrate, and the full batched write - solely so three span-counter fetch_adds can use the guard. The router CQ claim needs the exclusive lock (router.rs:272) and PG LWLocks admit new sharers past a waiting exclusive, so with cc=4 under load router emission can starve until a gap with zero in-flight write phases - coupling committer write latency into router formation cadence (an unmeasured interaction; formation-cadence attribution in the hh7b/ozln work rests on the tick + scan). No deadlock cycle (cleanup/claim take share; callers never touch CQ; row-lock holders do not need this lock to commit) and longjmp-skipped guards are reclaimed by AbortSubTransaction LWLockReleaseAll - stall-only, never a wedge. Fix shape: drop the guard before acquire_pool_locks and use statement-scoped guards per fetch_add, matching the surrounding code. X-ref sibling LWLock-scan sites (not re-filed): acct-ozln (staging O(ring) head-scan), acct-m4g5.2 (claim-loop O(ring) scan).
close_reason: Fixed (commit, see log). attempt_commit_phase no longer holds COMMITTER_QUEUE.share() across acquire_pool_locks / hydrate / plan_and_write — each of the three span counters (pool_lock/hydrate/apply) now takes a statement-scoped COMMITTER_QUEUE.share() for just its fetch_add, matching process_commit_group_inner pipeline-span idiom. Removes the head-of-line stall where a long-lived sharer parks in front of the routers exclusive CQ claim (PG LWLocks admit sharers past a waiting exclusive) and couples committer write latency into router formation cadence at cc>=4. Behavior identical (same counters/values); stall-only fix, no deadlock cycle existed. Full routed acceptance suite green (5 binaries / 27 tests incl. acceptance_routed_committer write phase). x-ref sibling LWLock-scan sites acct-ozln / acct-m4g5.2 (not re-filed).

title: Pass-3 Q11: sweep Phase-2 / claim-rollback clear CQ identity after the valid CAS — weak-memory double-claim hazard (x86-immune)
description: Found by acct-mvq4.4 (AUDIT-PASS3.md section B-ii.6 Q11, P3, weak-memory defect). router.rs:897-901 (Phase-2 revert) CASes CQ valid 2->1 Release THEN stores committer_bgw_slot=u32::MAX / generation=0 with Relaxed; committer.rs:294-295 mirrors the shape on claim rollback. This inverts the data-before-flag discipline the codebase follows everywhere else. A racing claimer elects on generation==0 (AcqRel CAS) and stores its own slot ordinal - on non-TSO hardware nothing orders the sweep earlier slot=MAX store before the claimer store, so MAX can clobber the new owner slot field: an in-flight entry whose owner reads as slot=u32::MAX -> is_committer_alive false -> a second committer claims the SAME group concurrently -> both run cleanup -> free_committer_queue_arena double-free -> duplicate freelist entries -> two future allocs can return the same offset (payload cross-corruption; the arena cycle guard does not catch duplicates). Impossible on x86-TSO (stores retire in program order) so the shipped platform is safe; real on ARM. Contrast finalize_committer_queue_slot whose identical-looking trailing clears ARE safe (share guard held vs the router exclusive-only claim of empty slots). Fix shape: clear identity BEFORE the valid CAS - a three-line reorder at each site.
close_reason: Fixed (commit 103c489). Restored emit_commit_group data-before-flag order at the three claim/reclaim sites that inverted it: (1) try_reclaim_dead_committer_entry clears the dead owners identity BEFORE the valid 2->1 Release CAS (was after), so the Release publishes slot=MAX/gen=0 ahead of the valid==1 flag and a re-electing claimers own slot store lands strictly after ours; (2) claim_next_committer_entry success publish widened valid 1->2 CAS Acquire->AcqRel so valid==2 implies the identity is visible to a sweep; (3) claim rollback (defensive) Releases the gen=0 store so slot=MAX is published before re-election. Closes the weak-memory window where a sweep reads valid==claimed + stale slot=MAX -> is_committer_alive false -> double-claim -> free_committer_queue_arena double-free. x86-TSO-immune (shipped platform safe), real on ARM; no runtime repro on x86 so correctness is by memory-model review. finalize_committer_queue_slot untouched (share vs emits exclusive on valid==0 never overlap). Full routed acceptance suite green (5 binaries / 27 tests) incl. claim (acceptance_routed_committer) + reclaim (acceptance_routed_orphan_recovery) paths — no functional regression.

description: Found by acct-mvq4.3 (B-i.7 Q4, P3, measurement honesty). driver_direct.rs caller_loop batched arm (:232): each in-batch success records its ack latency into the histogram immediately; a later mid-batch failure rolls the whole user-tx back but the recorded entries stay, so throughput_trx_per_sec counts rolled-back submissions. title: Pass-3 Q3: sampler.rs committer_wait_summary bucketing-rules comment stale vs code
description: Found by acct-mvq4.3 (B-i.7 Q3, P3, stale comment - same class as A4). sampler.rs:169-175 doc comment for committer_wait_summary says IO | WALSync | LWLock -> io_wait; the code at :183-185 gives LWLock its own lwlock_wait bucket (the CommitterWaitSummary struct docs agree with the code) and adds IPC to io_wait. notes:

GOAL: update the stale bucketing-rules doc comment for committer_wait_summary in ledger-harness/src/sampler.rs (comment at lines 168-175) to match the shipped code at :180-186.

SHIPPED CODE (:180-186) match arms:
  ("Extension","Extension") -> idle
  ("Running","Running")     -> running
  ("Lock", _)               -> lock_wait
  ("LWLock", _)             -> lwlock_wait      [its OWN bucket]
  ("IO",_)|("WALSync",_)|("IPC",_) -> io_wait   [IPC is here; LWLock is NOT]

STALE COMMENT (:169-175) currently says: wait_event_type 'IO' | 'WALSync' | 'LWLock' -> io_wait (WRONG: LWLock has its own bucket now; IPC missing). AND the tail (:174-175) "the four sub-buckets need not sum to total; busy - lock - running - io is other" is ALSO stale post-split.

FIX -- replace the doc comment (lines 168-175) with (use the real arrow char and the real minus char matching existing style; keep the /// prefix and 3-space alignment of the existing rule lines):
  Bucket committer_wait_observations into the acct-0usf STEP 1b summary.
  Bucketing rules (by wait_event_type, then wait_event):
    ('Extension','Extension') -> idle (parked on the latch between drains)
    wait_event_type 'Lock'    -> lock_wait (row-lock / transactionid handoff)
    ('Running','Running')      -> running (on-CPU, NULL wait_event)
    wait_event_type 'LWLock'   -> lwlock_wait (shmem-region LWLock contention)
    wait_event_type 'IO' | 'WALSync' | 'IPC' -> io_wait
  Everything else still counts toward total but no sub-bucket (so the five sub-buckets need not sum to total; busy - lock - running - lwlock - io is "other").

DO NOT touch the CommitterWaitSummary struct docs at :59-73 -- they already agree with the code.

title: Pass-3 Q2: scenarios.rs:158 unreachable unwrap_or arm + hardcoded s6 caller-count literal
description: Found by acct-mvq4.3 (B-i.7 Q2, P3, misleading code). s6 stripe sizing uses pool_ids.len().checked_div(1000).unwrap_or(1).max(1) - checked_div returns None only on a zero divisor and the divisor is the literal 1000, so the unwrap_or(1) arm is unreachable and reads as load-bearing when the real floor is .max(1). The 1000 is also a hardcoded copy of s6 callers=1000 rather than derived from it - changing the caller count would silently leave stripe sizing stale. Contrast workload.rs:138 which documents its unreachable fallback honestly.
acceptance_criteria: Replace with plain division derived from the caller-count value plus .max(1); or document why the literal is intentional.
close_reason: Fixed scenarios.rs s6 stripe sizing. Was `u.pool_ids.len().checked_div(1000).unwrap_or(1).max(1)` — checked_div only returns None on a zero divisor and the divisor was the literal 1000, so the unwrap_or(1) arm was unreachable dead code masquerading as load-bearing (the real floor is .max(1)); and the 1000 was a hardcoded copy of s6 callers=1000 that could drift from it. Now binds `let callers: usize = 1000` once and uses it for BOTH the stripe divisor and the spec caller argument: `stripe_size = (u.pool_ids.len() / callers).max(1)`. Matches the existing doc-comment (universe / callers, floored at 1) verbatim; behavior-preserving for all inputs. title: Committer commit-group sizing: batch_size_max default + cc=1 ingress ceiling (fsync amortization)
description:
Follow-up from acct-e95d item 2 (fsync characterization; commit c7f3c16; results/committer_fsync_vs_batch_size.md). fsync is one COMMIT per commit_group, so fsync/trx = per-group-fsync / commit_group_size — a clean 1/cg amortization. Measured at cc=1: cap 50 -> cg 48 -> fsync 41% / ~11.2k trx/s; cap 200 -> cg 182 -> 18% / ~16.7k; cap 400 -> cg 323 -> 12% / ~18.9k; cap 800 -> cg 480 -> 9% / ~20k. Two deferred levers:

1. batch_size_max default. Production default is 50 — the worst point (fsync 41%, ~11.2k trx/s). Raising to ~200-400 cuts fsync to 12-18% and lifts throughput ~1.5-1.7x at the same host load, purely by amortizing the commit. Tradeoff: larger groups raise per-submission ack latency (bounded by batch_window_us), NOT measured in the characterization. Picking a value needs a latency SLO -> gated on the Structured-testing phase (Part IV section 14, not yet started). No committer code change — it is a GUC default.

2. cc=1 ingress ceiling. At cc=1 single-push a lone flooding caller caps achieved cg at ~480 even with batch_size_max=800 (cannot fill 800-trx groups within the 20ms window). Pushing cg (hence fsync) lower needs more ingress: caller-side batching (ledger_enqueue_trx_batch_c, run-1sku-batched.sh CBATCH=8192, acct-ruex) or more callers/committers.

apply us/trx is flat across the sweep (~44) — per-trx irreducible floor; the whole throughput gain is fsync amortization.
notes: Gated on a latency SLO (Structured-testing phase). Characterization method + data: results/committer_fsync_vs_batch_size.md and results/apply_spans_fsync_rb*.csv. acct-e95d covered the prep code fixes + prep/fsync characterization; this is the residual tuning/ingress lever.
close_reason: Both deferred levers resolved by work that landed after filing; reconciliation committed (578de32). Lever 1 (batch_size_max default): the e95d fsync sweep premise ("default 50, raise to ~400") is doubly stale — acct-p1al set the default to 200, and acct-czz4/§C.1 (N=5 two-regime) showed "~400" is single-pool-fsync-regime-specific and collapses the many-pool regime -57%/-74% at 800; the cross-regime optimum is 200. §C.1 also supplied the ack-latency read finding 4 flagged as missing (hot-pool p50 497->287ms), closing the "latency not measured" gate. Lever 2 (cc=1 ingress ceiling): the caller-side batch lift (`ledger_enqueue_trx_batch_c`, CBATCH=8192) is shipped + characterized cc=1/2/4 in acct-ruex (CLOSED), which also named `LWLock/ledger_v31_staging_queue` as the ingress ceiling. No new bench to run. Residual = a formal latency-SLO-gated re-tune, which belongs to the not-yet-started Structured-testing phase (Part IV §14), not a standalone P3. Fsync char doc updated with a cross-regime resolution note pointing to §C.1 / acct-ruex.

title: ledger-harness: scale routed drain_deadline with run length (end-of-drain tail)
description: Bench-only follow-up from acct-0516 (long-duration routed sweep). The routed driver (ledger-harness/src/driver_routed.rs) uses a fixed 30s drain_deadline. On longer / higher-throughput runs a fixed-size in-flight tail can still be un-materialized when the deadline elapses, recorded as submitted_but_unseen>0 (seen on s3/s8/s9/s10/s11/s12 in the §(g) sweep). This is NOT data loss (dropped=0 everywhere; submissions remain in the cluster-lifetime staging queue and the committer keeps draining after the harness stops observing) and NOT a Path C defect — it is a harness observer-window artifact: the s8 tail is LARGER at 1m (~8%) than 10m (~0.3%), so the fraction shrinks with duration. Options: (a) scale drain_deadline with run duration, (b) poll staging+commit queue counts to drain-to-empty rather than a fixed wall-clock deadline, (c) report the residual end-of-drain tail explicitly in the JSON so it stops registering as a discovery. Bench-only; touches no production code. See POC-REPORT.md §(g) and run-routed-longdur.sh.
notes: Pass-3 .3 audit annotation (acct-mvq4.3, AUDIT-PASS3.md B-i.4, 2026-06-06): two adjacent observations beyond the fixed-30s-tail this issue names. (1) Throughput convention: routed reports count submitted-in-window work that drains AFTER callers stop against the caller-window denominator - ambiguity vs instantaneous drain rate bounded by ring/total (up to ~25 pct on 20-30s cells, <2 pct at the 120-300s durations the headline docs use). (2) wait_for_committer_quiet declares drained after 3 stable 200ms reads (~600ms) - a 1s deadlock-backoff stall (retry cap) can outlast the window and fire it early; effect surfaces visibly as submitted_but_unseen > 0 and errs conservative (undercounts throughput). equivalence.rs is the model: quiescence heuristic backed by an explicit completeness assert. Neither changes shipped conclusions; both belong to whatever fix this issue lands.
close_reason: Routed driver now drains to completeness, not committer quiescence (commit c0755c0). User-selected option a+b+c: adopt the equivalence.rs::apply_routed completeness model on the perf path. wait_for_drain_complete polls the run-range trx count until every enqueued submission (submission_log.len(), oversell-free + unique source_ids) materializes — a mid-drain committer stall (deadlock-backoff) can no longer end the wait early (audit #2). Cap is duration-scaled: max(drain_deadline, run_duration), floored at 30s (issue primary: fixed 30s too short for long/high-tput runs). Explicit reporting: new `drain_complete` bool in JSON (submitted_but_unseen kept for backward compat) — nonzero residual now means a genuine cap-hit (drain_complete=false), not the cosmetic tail. Module-doc states the "offered work fully materialized / window" throughput convention explicitly (audit #1); analyze-routed-longdur.py finding (e) distinguishes genuine cap-hit from pre-x9bg residual; POC-REPORT §(g) records the hardening. Replaces the now-unused wait_for_committer_quiet. Validated: cargo check + clippy clean, driver_routed unit tests 2/2, live sparse routed smoke drained to completeness (drain_complete=true, submitted_but_unseen=0, dropped=0). Bench-only; no production-path change.

title: Long-duration routed-only bench (1m + 10m per scenario, clean DB per run)
description:
Smoke runs (5s / 30s) have not surfaced any long-duration-only failure modes on the routed path — every cell in the current matrix lands clean (drops/poison/deadlock_retries all 0). Whether that holds at production-realistic run lengths is unverified. Time-dependent failure surfaces are routed-specific: poison threshold (P3.4 retry-then-poison), takeover after committer death, deadlock-retry accumulation, shmem arena spillover, staging-queue back-pressure, in-flight router-orphan recovery, and drain-deadline behavior under sustained pressure.

Goal: run every scenario (S1-S21) through routed mode at TWO durations, with a clean DB between every timed run, and capture any cell where the 10-minute verdict differs from the 1-minute verdict.

This deliberately drops the direct-per-call and direct-batched columns from the matrix — they are CPU/IO measurements that do not develop new failure modes with duration the way routed does (their committer/shmem path is absent). Direct verdicts are already characterized in artifact (b).
design:
Design forks to surface via AskUserQuestion at claim time:

(a) Clean-DB semantics — three options (clean happens ONCE per scenario, before the 1m run; the 10m extends the same universe):
    (a1) `docker restart acct-postgres` + `reset_ledger_tables` + reseed (RECOMMENDED, matches the existing bench convention; preserves schema migrations).
    (a2) `DROP DATABASE poc_v3_1; CREATE DATABASE poc_v3_1` + reapply migrations + reseed (more aggressive; surfaces migration / extension-init bugs at the cost of ~30s/run setup overhead).
    (a3) Wipe pg_data volume + container recreate (most aggressive; clears shmem ledger arena state too).

(b) Run ordering is FIXED by user direction: per scenario, clean -> 1m run -> (no clean) -> 10m run -> next scenario. The 10m inherits the 1m terminal state. This is the long-duration-discovery shape — resetting between 1m and 10m would hide accumulated-state issues (drift, pool exhaustion sequencing, identity-registry drift, shmem arena fragmentation).

(c) Seed depth for deplete scenarios (S5-S9, S14-S21 — all deplete > 0):
    The 1m + 10m cumulative depletion volume per pool must fit the seeded universe, or the 10m hits P0006 InsufficientInventory and the cleanliness signal is conflated with exhaustion. At ~2000-3000 routed trx/s on hot scenarios, 11 min runs against the s5 hot-pool (single pool absorbs everything) would drain a depth-10 universe in seconds. Options:
    (c1) Scale `seed_depth` proportional to cumulative deplete volume — e.g. s5 depth=100000, s7/s8/s9 depth=10000, s14-s21 deplete-50 scenarios depth=1000. RECOMMENDED — preserves architectural intent (shallow vs deep stays meaningful relative to cumulative throughput). Implementation: extend `depth_for` in the new longdur script with a separate multiplier.
    (c2) Cap caller_count or throughput to a level the existing depths can sustain for 11 min (changes the measured concurrency).
    (c3) Accept exhaustion as the 10m terminal state for depletion-heavy scenarios and explicitly mark those cells (the scenario IS clean from a routed-correctness standpoint even when pools run dry — the depletions just fail with P0006). Per criterion 3 this is calibration noise not a structural difference, so this is the cheapest option but produces lower-information 10m cells for several scenarios.

(d) pgbouncer requirement — S5-S9 (1000 callers) currently route through pgbouncer:6432 per `dsn_for_scenario`. At 10m that still holds (no new constraint). Verify pgbouncer container `poc-v3-1-pgbouncer` is up before the run.

Time budget: 21 scenarios x (1m + 10m + 1 x reseed + 1 x docker-restart) ~= 4-5 hours wall. Background single watcher pattern; sequential not parallel.

Implementation lives in a new `ledger-harness/bench/run-routed-longdur.sh` that builds on `common.sh` (re-uses restart_db, dsn_for_scenario, build_harness) but adds a per-scenario long-duration depth override.

Cross-refs: acct-2ttr.9 (P5 characterization), acct-34ce (multi-touch generator), acct-s90k (Pareto family), POC-REPORT.md artifact (b) (the current crossover map this extends).
acceptance_criteria:
1. Every S1-S21 scenario driven through routed at BOTH durations (1m, then 10m), with a `clean DB` (`docker restart acct-postgres` + reset_ledger_tables + reseed at the scenarios depth_hint) ONCE PER SCENARIO before the 1m run. The 10m run extends the same universe (NO reset between 1m and 10m). Total cells = 21 x 2 = 42; clean-db operations = 21.

2. Per-cell capture of: throughput_trx_per_sec, errors_total, attempts_total, trx_materialized, submitted_but_unseen, drains_total, commit_group_size_avg, pool_lock_acquisitions_total, aggregate_upserts_total, dropped_submissions_total, poisoned_total, deadlock_retries_total, takeover_count, ack_latency_us p50/p95/p99, committed_latency_us p50/p95/p99, top_wait_events.

3. Identify and surface any (scenario) where the 10m verdict differs structurally from the 1m verdict — defined as any of (a) new non-zero counter that was zero at 1m, (b) order-of-magnitude shift in commit_group_size_avg or pool_lock_acquisitions/trx_materialized ratio, (c) ack_latency p99 grows superlinearly with duration, (d) drains_total/duration_s ratio shifts > 50%, (e) submitted_but_unseen > 0 at end-of-drain. Pool exhaustion (P0006 InsufficientInventory from depletions running the universe dry partway through the 10m run) is an EXPECTED surface — record it in the per-cell capture but do NOT flag it as a structural difference under (a). It is a calibration signal that the seed depth must be sized for the cumulative 1m + 10m depletion volume.

4. POC-REPORT.md section (g): `Long-duration routed cleanliness sweep` — combined table (one row per scenario, two columns per metric: 1m | 10m) plus a separate `Long-duration discoveries` callout listing any cell from criterion 3.

5. If a 10m cell uncovers a defect, file a fresh bd issue per defect (blocked-by this issue). DO NOT fix in this bench-only delivery.
notes:
Filed 2026-05-28 after the acct-s90k Pareto family delivery. User-directed: i want to see clean bench of only routed, as well as any errors/inconsistencies that might come out of a longer duration run. i want clean db on each, with a 1 min run followed by a 10 minute run FOR EACH BENCH.

Run ordering clarified 2026-05-28: NO reset between the 1m and 10m. Clean-DB happens ONCE per scenario before the 1m; the 10m extends the same universe (so accumulated state — drift, arena pressure, queue back-pressure — has a chance to surface).

Bench-only (no production code touched). The harness `_longdur` script + any POC-REPORT.md section are the only files this issue ships. If criterion 5 triggers (a 10m run uncovers a defect), the FIX is a separate issue and NOT in scope here.

Total cells (21 scenarios x routed-only x 2 durations) = 42, clean-db operations = 21. Skipping direct-per-call and direct-batched is deliberate — see description rationale.
close_reason: Routed-only long-duration sweep complete: 21 scenarios (S1-S21) x 2 durations (60s + 600s) = 42 cells, clean DB (a2 DROP/CREATE + restart) once per scenario before the 60s, 600s extends the same universe (decision b). Crossover seed depths (c1 premise shown false: each layer = 1e9 units, routed never walks layers, so pools cannot exhaust in 11min at any depth). VERDICT: CLEAN — every cell at both durations recorded 0 dropped / 0 poisoned / 0 deadlock_retries / 0 takeover. No 10m verdict differs structurally from 1m in a way that indicts the Path C committer. Discoveries are all measurement artifacts, none a Path C defect: (1) submitted_but_unseen at end-of-drain is a harness observer-window artifact (dropped=0; s8 tail shrinks 8%@1m to 0.3%@10m) -> bench follow-up acct-x9bg; (2) 200-caller enqueue errors = expected staging back-pressure (dropped=0); (3) throughput sag 1m->10m = host warming. Bench methodology FINDING documented in POC-REPORT.md (g): a bare DROP DATABASE wedges the routed committer (cluster-lifetime shmem arena not cleared) — a postmaster restart is required; not a production defect. Ships: ledger-harness/bench/run-routed-longdur.sh, analyze-routed-longdur.py, POC-REPORT.md section (g). No AC5 Path C defect filed.

title: Harness: Pareto 80/20 overlap mode + receipts / builds / mixed scenario families
description:
Bench S1-S9 brackets the contention envelope at extremes (s6 disjoint = 0%; s5 single-pool = 100%) and approximates the realistic middle via Zipf(1.2). It does NOT provide a discrete hot/cold MIXTURE (e.g., 80% of submissions land on 20% of pools — textbook Pareto 80/20). Mid-market ERP loads are typically 10-200 simultaneous posting sessions against a heavy-tail catalog where a few SKUs handle disproportionate volume; the current matrix only meets that region by interpolation across extremes.

Add a new OverlapMode::Pareto { hot_pool_fraction, hot_traffic_fraction } in ledger-harness/src/workload.rs that emits a discrete two-population mixture: each submission rolls hot/cold by hot_traffic_fraction, then samples uniformly from the first hot_pool_fraction * N pools (hot) or from the rest (cold). Composes orthogonally with the existing Complexity, deplete_pct, and multi-touch knobs.

Layer THREE workload FAMILIES on top of it, each parameterized via the new OverlapMode and the existing axes:

  1. RECEIPTS family — deplete_pct=0, multi_touch_pct=0. Models PO receipt and transfer-in flows. Fills the receipt-side gap that today only S1-S4 cover, none under a Pareto mixture.

  2. BUILDS family — deplete_pct ~ 50, multi-touch enabled (dist 1:60,2:30,3:10). Models WO completion shape (backflush + scrap + output on one SKU/location). S9 already exercises this at 1000 callers / depth 1000; the new family fills in lower-caller and shallower-depth rows.

  3. MIXED family — deplete_pct=50, multi_touch_pct=0. Models generic transfer / sale flows without multi-touch repetition. The "no special shape, just balanced" baseline.

Suggested initial canned scenarios per family (4 variants each = 12 total), along Pareto + concurrency + depth axes:

  variant     | callers | overlap        | depth | description
  ------------|---------|----------------|-------|--------------------------------------
  mid-typ     | 50      | Pareto 80/20   | 0     | day-to-day mid-market posting load
  high-vol    | 200     | Pareto 80/20   | 100   | larger shop, moderate depth
  long-tail   | 50      | Pareto 90/10   | 0     | catalog with few hot SKUs
  balanced    | 50      | Pareto 50/50   | 0     | uniform-ish baseline at typical scale

Final scenario count, naming, parameter ranges, and the surface (CLI overlay flag(s) vs. canned-scenario presets vs. both) get worked out via AskUserQuestion at claim time — same shape as acct-34ce, where the user picked "both CLI flags + s9 preset" + a weighted distribution model after surfacing the design forks.

Harness-only addition. NO migration, NO SQL, NO ledger-core / spi-common / flavor production code. Pattern matches acct-34ce verbatim.
design:
Implementation pattern mirrors acct-34ce (the multi-touch addition that just shipped):

  Step 1: workload.rs — add OverlapMode::Pareto variant, pick_pareto free fn, unit tests. Default-path RNG unchanged (Pareto only consulted when the scenario selects it).
  Step 2: scenarios.rs — add 3-12 canned scenarios across the families. The spec() helper stays as-is; family scenarios override Pareto/deplete/multi-touch fields post-construction.
  Step 3: cli.rs / driver_common.rs / driver_*.rs / main.rs — thread CLI overlays through Run subcommand, apply via apply_pareto helper (parallel to apply_multi_touch).
  Step 4: bench/run-crossover.sh — add new scenarios to the default list and to depth_for / dsn_for_scenario as needed.
  Step 5: results/POC-REPORT.md — add rows / section.

Cross-refs: acct-34ce (multi-touch harness addition, closed 2026-05-28, commit 07fcb02), acct-2ttr.8 (P4 harness epic), acct-2ttr.9 (P5 characterization report).

Three forks to surface via AskUserQuestion at claim time:
  (a) CLI overlay flags vs. canned scenarios vs. both — recommended both (matches 34ce).
  (b) Discrete two-population mixture vs. piecewise Pareto distribution — recommended discrete (simpler, matches textbook 80/20, easier to reason about).
  (c) Final scenario count and names — start with one variant per family to validate the pattern, then ratchet.
acceptance_criteria:
1. OverlapMode::Pareto variant exists in workload.rs with unit tests covering the mixture: hot fraction sees hot_traffic_fraction of picks, cold the complement; degenerate values (0/0, 1/1, 0/1, 1/0) handled.

2. At least one canned scenario per family registered in scenarios.rs and resolvable via run --scenario sX (3 scenarios minimum; final count surfaced at claim time, recommended 12 = 4 variants x 3 families).

3. CLI overlay flags (e.g., --pareto-hot-pool-pct, --pareto-hot-traffic-pct) compose with the existing --multi-touch-pct / --touch-dist overlays; flags override the scenario default the same way acct-34ce wired its overlays.

4. A bench run with each new family scenario x {direct-per-call, routed} emits clean results: errors=0 on direct-per-call, drops=0 + poison=0 + deadlock_retries=0 on routed.

5. results/POC-REPORT.md updated with at least a refreshed crossover table covering the new family rows; a new artifact section (g) added if the Pareto data exposes a structural finding not previously characterized (e.g., a region of the crossover map currently bracketed by extremes).

6. Existing SPI suite still passes (both-path tests stay green); harness changes do not touch production .so.
notes: Filed 2026-05-28 during interpretation of the 2026-05-28 S1-S9 full bench + s9 equivalence run (commits f2a1b05, aadd470). Pattern explicitly mirrors acct-34ce. The gap surfaced from a user question: "do we have a bench that measures 80/20 uncontended vs contended? I am trying to think of scenarios that would be typical." The existing matrix tests ARCHITECTURAL premises (depth-invariance, contention-collapse, multi-touch coalesce) but does not characterize the typical-mid-market region cleanly — Zipf(1.2) over 10000 pools is ~87/20 (more concentrated than Pareto 80/20), not exactly the textbook split.
close_reason: Harness Pareto 80/20 overlap + receipts/builds/mixed family block delivered. OverlapMode::Pareto + 12 canned scenarios (s10-s21) + CLI overlays. All 24 (direct-per-call, routed) cells satisfy acceptance criterion 4 (errors=0 / drops=0 / poison=0 / dlk_retries=0). 39/39 harness unit tests pass. Commit a8579d7.

title: Harness: opt-in multi-touch (same-pool-twice) load scenario to exercise coalesce under load
description:
Post-build review concern 3. PlanResult coalesce_aggregates correctness IS covered by 3 tests (ledger-core plan_apply_provisional, direct acceptance_direct_methods, routed acceptance_routed_committer). But the harness workload generator enforces DISTINCT pool_ids per submission (workload.rs pick loop) for clean lock-hold measurement, so the same-pool-twice (multi-touch) path is never exercised under LOAD. Production submissions will touch the same pool twice in one trx (e.g. WO backflush + scrap on the same SKU/location).

Scope: add an OPT-IN workload mode that emits same-pool-twice submissions (a multi_touch flag / scenario), keeping the default distinct-pool generation. Lets a bench run characterize the coalesce path under load without confounding the standard lock-hold scenarios.

Pushed back on reverting the distinct-pool default (user decision): distinct pools keep per-submission pool-count unconfounded for lock-hold measurement; multi-touch is an additive scenario, not a default change.
acceptance_criteria: An opt-in multi-touch workload mode exists; default workload still distinct-pool; a bench run can drive same-pool-twice submissions through both flavors.
notes: Scope refinement (design-team review, round 2): the multi-touch load scenario must use a REALISTIC distribution, not a single synthetic worst-case. Production workloads mix submissions that touch one pool, several pools, and the same pool more than once (WO completions especially). Parameterize the fraction of submissions that are multi-touch and the per-submission touch-count distribution so the bench result is actionable — a 100%-worst-case run tells us little about real behavior. Default workload stays distinct-pool.
close_reason: Opt-in multi-touch workload mode shipped (multi_touch_pct + weighted TouchDistribution); CLI overlay --multi-touch-pct / --touch-dist + canned s9 preset; default stays distinct-pool. Verified via 33 unit tests + direct/routed smoke (errors=0, clean coalesce on both flavors). Harness-only.

title: Routed property test: mixed-sequence replay determinism
description:
Post-build review concern 7. design-v3.1 14.2 claims the WAC running average produces a deterministic final state given the multiset of receipts. property_ledger_enqueue_trx_c.rs asserts E1 (final aggregate QTY == order-independent net signed sum) but only reads qty — it never asserts the running-average UNIT_COST, which is the reviewers actual worry (read-modify-write on the running average).

No RMW race exists by construction (routing affinity routes same-pool submissions to one committer; running avg computed in-memory in submission_id order; pool_lock FOR UPDATE serializes across split chunks) and receipts-only final avg = sum(qty*cost)/sum(qty) is order-independent. But the unit_cost determinism is asserted, not verified.

Scope: extend property_ledger_enqueue_trx_c.rs with a receipts-only property: for each pool, final pool_state.unit_cost (layer_id=0) == banker-rounded sum(qty*cost)/sum(qty) over that pools receipts. Reuse the existing interleaved-submission generator; restrict the assertion to receipts-only pools (depletions make unit_cost order-sensitive).
acceptance_criteria: property_ledger_enqueue_trx_c.rs asserts receipts-only final unit_cost equals the value-weighted average per pool; passes under PROPTEST_CASES default.
notes: Scope refinement (design-team review, round 2): extend beyond the receipts-only unit_cost assertion. The receipts-only final average is order-independent algebraically; the MIXED receipt+depletion case is the more interesting property — it is order-dependent and deterministic ONLY because the committer processes submissions in submission_id (enqueue) order. That is where a regression could hide: e.g. if the committer ever switched to pool-ascending order to optimize lock acquisition, it would silently change recorded provisional costs without failing the qty check. Add a replay-determinism property: given a fixed mixed receipt+depletion submission sequence replayed N times, assert final pool_state AND trx_line content (per-line provisional unit_cost) match across all replays. May split into a sibling ticket if receipts-only and mixed want separate test bodies.
close_reason: Shipped routed_mixed_sequence_replay_deterministic (commit 23e1a88): a fixed mixed receipt+depletion enqueue sequence replayed 3x from a clean DB lands byte-identical pool_state (qty+unit_cost) AND trx_line content (per-line provisional unit_cost). 100 cases x 3 replays green (54s). This catches a committer that reorders a pool away from submission_id order (preserves qty, silently changes running-average provisional costs) — the case E1 is blind to. The other requested assertion (receipts-only unit_cost == Sum(qty*cost)/Sum(qty)) is NOT a valid invariant against the current incremental-rounding implementation (order-sensitive per §11.1); it is gated behind the value_sum refactor and lives in acct-0qps acceptance.

title: ledger-routed-c committer.rs: stale comments list UNIQUE-survivor as direct poison cause (contradicts acct-yojk.9 re-drive)
description:
Found during acct-gd3g docs↔code coherence reconciliation. Two comments in ledger-routed-c/src/committer.rs still list "UNIQUE survived dedup" as a *direct* non-retryable→poison cause, but acct-yojk.9 (commit 6fe3979) changed that path: a 23505 that survives pre-flight dedup is classified as PhaseOutcome::DuplicateRace and the group is re-driven minus the offender; it poisons ONLY if the re-dedup resolves no offender (irresolvable). The function-body comments (lines ~380-454, ~525-530, ~663-665) already describe the re-drive correctly; only these two doc-comments are stale:

1. Module header (lines ~39-42): "A non-retryable SQLSTATE (UNIQUE survived dedup, check / not-null, …) … POISONs the commit_group."
2. PhaseOutcome::Poisoned variant doc (lines ~252-253): "Terminal: a non-retryable SQL error (UNIQUE survived dedup, NOT-NULL, check, disk-full, …)".

Fix: drop "UNIQUE survived dedup" from the poison enumerations in both comments (it is a re-drive path, not a direct poison path); optionally note that an *irresolvable* UNIQUE re-drive degrades to poison. No behavior change — comment-only edit. Greenfield rule: describe current behavior only.

Filed (not fixed inline) because acct-gd3g is constrained to docs-only; any production-code edit (incl. source-file comments) is filed separately.
acceptance_criteria: Both committer.rs comments no longer list a bare UNIQUE-survivor as a direct poison cause; consistent with the acct-yojk.9 re-drive behavior and the function-body comments. cargo build clean (comment-only).
close_reason: Fixed both stale comments (module header §6.8 block + PhaseOutcome::Poisoned variant doc) to describe the acct-yojk.9 re-drive: a UNIQUE that survives dedup is DuplicateRace (re-drive minus offender), poisoning only when irresolvable. Comment-only, no behavior change. Commit follows.

title: Flaky: enqueue_stages_to_shmem_without_db_write races the router tick
description: acceptance_routed_enqueue.rs:47 (enqueue_stages_to_shmem_without_db_write) asserts staging_pending==2 immediately after two enqueues WITHOUT pausing the BGWorkers. The router ticks every 50ms (wait_latch) and moves slots pending→routed, so on an unlucky docker-restart timing the read sees 0 pending (line 44 trx_count==0 still passes — routed-but-not-committed). Observed failing once during acct-yojk.10 regression run, passing on immediate re-run. Fix: wrap the enqueue+assert in the existing paused() helper (pause router+committer, stage, assert pending, then resume) like acceptance_routed_committer does — deterministic observation of the staged-but-unprocessed state. Pre-existing; unrelated to the classify_and_eject change that surfaced it.
acceptance_criteria: Test pauses the BGWorkers before asserting pending/arena counts (or otherwise made deterministic); no longer races the router tick.
close_reason: Fixed by pausing router+committer around the enqueue+read (capture-while-paused, resume-before-assert) so the assertions no longer race the ~50ms router tick. acceptance_routed_enqueue 5/5 pass on the test_hooks build. Test-only change.

description: equivalence.rs (:209-231): the routed drain-wait is a quiescence heuristic; on timeout/early-quiet it returns Ok and diffs a partially-drained state, surfacing as a confusing qty-mismatch FAIL. Decide implement vs won't-fix-for-PoC.

Baseline-delta (not absolute count==subs.len()) because universe seeding/deepen writes its own trx rows — caught while testing: 420 trx for 400 submissions + 20 seed rows. A shortfall now reports "routed drain incomplete: C/E submissions ... (trx B→N)" instead of a misleading equivalence-qty FAIL against a partially-drained state. Per-submission committer cost is SPI-dominated: single-row trx INSERT (w/ UNIQUE index, in-backend) ~6.4us; ~3 such INSERTs/submission (insert_trx/trx_lines/posting_lines) ~19us before lock+hydrate. clone is ~0.5-1% of per-submission cost (<3% even vs a single INSERT) — SPI dominates by ~100x. apply-then-rollback/pools-only-clone would trade simple-correct clone-per-trial for mutation-reversal complexity on a concurrency-critical path for <1% saving.
