title: P2.2: parse_caller_status couples to PG literal 'in progress' string
description: committer.rs (:812): parse_caller_status matches the literal pg_xact_status text "in progress"; a wording change across PG versions would silently reclassify callers as Unknown-keep, committing work for a still-open caller tx. Mirrors sibling D5.2. Decide harden (match on a more stable signal) vs won't-fix-for-PoC.
acceptance_criteria: Status parse hardened against string drift, OR closed won't-fix-for-PoC with reason.
close_reason: Hardened: parse_caller_status now splits None (NULL pg_xact_status = frozen/committed xid → Unknown → keep) from Some(unrecognized) (a status-wording drift → new CallerTxStatus::Unrecognized). Unrecognized emits a WARNING naming the value and rides the not-yet-committed eject path (never kept), so a future PG rename of "in progress" fails loud (WARNING + caller timeouts) instead of silently committing work for a still-open caller tx. Behavior identical for all real PG-18 statuses. Unit tests pin None→Unknown vs Some(garbage)→Unrecognized. Routed suite 5 green/0 red. Commit e9eb7eb. title: ledger-v3.1 harness: seed standard_cost for std-method pools (unconfound mixed-method S3/S4)
description: The ledger-v3.1 harness seeder (pool_universe.rs) creates every pool with provisional_basis=running_avg and does NOT establish any standard_cost rows. In the mixed method-mix (50/30/20 fifo/wac/std), the 20pct std-method pools therefore have no standard cost in effect, so any submission touching one aborts with MissingStandardCost. For the Complex scenario shape (10-20 distinct pools per submission) that is nearly every submission, which is why P5 scenarios S3/S4 showed ~95pct error rates and depressed throughput (see results/POC-REPORT.md methodology + crossover map footnote). This confounds the mixed-method throughput numbers; it does NOT affect the clean all-fifo (S5-S8) / all-wac (S1/S2) measurements the Path C conclusions rest on. Fix: have the seeder bulk-insert standard_cost rows for std-method pools (one row per std pool, e.g. a fixed unit_cost) during seed/reseed so mixed-method scenarios can run without spurious aborts.
acceptance_criteria: Seeder inserts a standard_cost row for every std-method pool during seed-pools and the --method-mix reseed path; re-running the P5 crossover with method-mix=mixed yields S3/S4 with errors=0 on the direct-per-call and routed paths (no MissingStandardCost aborts); all-fifo/all-wac scenarios unchanged.
close_reason: Fixed (commit 9b6e6b5): seeder now bulk-inserts standard_cost (STD_UNIT_COST=500) for every std-method pool (sku,location) + seeds variance account 3000, and the workload emits variance_account on every line. Two compounding aborts removed: MissingStandardCost (no std cost) and MissingVarianceAccount (std receipt at actual!=standard with no variance target). Validated mixed 1000-pool reseed (200 std w/ standard_cost): S3 direct errors 17594->0, S4 direct 415->0, S4 routed committer dropped 3193->0. All-fifo/all-wac unchanged (0 std rows, errors 0). Harness-only change; 26 harness unit tests green.

title: Integration test for pg_xact_status return literal strings
description:
committer.rs::parse_caller_status (line 805-812) matches against literal PG strings: 'committed', 'aborted', 'in progress' (with space). Unknown strings map to CallerTxStatus::Unknown which is treated as Committed (kept).

If PG ever changes the pg_xact_status output format, callers stuck in_progress would be silently classified Unknown → kept → processed against a still-open caller tx → UNIQUE-violate on next attempt. The defensive default masks a regression.

Audit acct-o00c D5.2.

title: committer Step 5: drop posting_lines RETURNING when no downstream join needs it
description:
## Context

acct-pl3b stage-timing: bulk_insert is 45.5% of pipeline. Step 5a posting_lines uses INSERT ... RETURNING posting_line_id because Step 5d (posting_line_inventory) needs the IDs to write inventory snapshot rows tied to the posting_line they correspond to.

## Problem

RETURNING materializes results back to the caller per row. The bulk INSERT ... RETURNING has higher cost than a no-RETURNING INSERT — PG must flow rows back through SPI in addition to writing them. The cost is non-trivial at scale.

For SBs where posting_line_inventory is empty (e.g., no inventory side, just GL postings — though all v2.1 events currently touch inventory), the RETURNING is wasted.

For SBs where the downstream join can be done by (correlation_id, ordinal) instead of the BIGSERIAL id, RETURNING can be dropped if a unique identity is already in the rows (correlation_id + sub_priority forms a candidate key for the apply step).

## Proposed Change

Option A — Drop RETURNING entirely for std/avg if downstream join can use (correlation_id, sub_priority, ordinal) as the link key. Requires posting_line_inventory to take those columns in UNNEST too and SELECT the posting_line by composite key.

Option B — Conditional RETURNING: keep RETURNING only when posting_line_inventory_inserts is non-empty. Cheap win when GL-only SBs exist.

Option C — Replace RETURNING with a side-array of caller-allocated ordinals (Rust pre-assigns then PG just writes back).

## Expected Impact

Hard to estimate without bench. Probably ~5% bulk_insert reduction. ~2-3% e2e lift on its own.

## Acceptance

- Code change in committer.rs Step 5a + 5d
- Acceptance tests pass
- Bench at optimal config — expect e2e >= 4350 evps
- Stage-timing reports bulk_insert reduced ~5%

## Risks

- Option A requires schema work: posting_lines doesn't currently have an obvious composite key for the apply-step ordinal. Adding a (correlation_id, sub_priority) UNIQUE constraint would index those columns — that costs at INSERT time too. Net win might be negative.
- Option B is cheap and low-risk but small impact.

## Cross-refs

- Likely subsumed by heap_multi_insert FFI (separate issue) which has its own ID-return mechanism
- Lower priority than skip-cost-layers (acct-xwu3) — that drops a whole INSERT

title: Add startup calibration warning per spec §1.7: theoretical_max_ejects vs max_eject_count
description:
Spec §1.7 line 563 mandates a startup calibration check:

  'theoretical_max_ejects = caller_tx_timeout_ms × 1000 / batch_window_us
   (the upper bound on how many ejects a single envelope could accumulate
   if every router tick cycled it). If theoretical_max_ejects > max_eject_count / 2,
   log a WARNING: max_eject_count may not be the primary bound under tight cycling;
   verify the wall-clock timeout is the intended bound, or raise max_eject_count
   to >= 2 × theoretical_max_ejects.'

Current code: no such check in lib.rs _PG_init or postmaster-start path.

WHY: catches operator misconfiguration where batch_window_us is lowered or caller_tx_timeout_ms is raised without proportionally adjusting max_eject_count, causing eject counter to terminate envelopes before the wall-clock bound — the inverse of the spec's intent.

IMPLEMENTATION SHAPE: add a fn called from _PG_init (or first BGWorker tick) that reads the three GUCs via the now_*() accessors and compares them. Use pgrx::warning! or ereport at WARNING severity. Idempotent: only logs at startup, not per-tick.

REFERENCES:
- Spec §1.7 line 563 (full warning template + threshold)
- Related: max_eject_count GUC default fix (separate issue) — once GUC default is 10000, the warning won't fire under default config.
acceptance_criteria: On extension load (or first BGWorker tick), if theoretical_max_ejects = caller_tx_timeout_ms × 1000 / batch_window_us > max_eject_count / 2, a WARNING is logged with the spec'd message. Test: SET poc_v21.batch_window_us = 50 + reload → WARNING in log under default max_eject_count.
close_reason: Closed

title: Widen StagingEntry.eject_count from AtomicU16 to AtomicU32 per spec §1.6
description:
Spec re-revision (poc-v2.1.md 2026-05-18 14:42 lines 485-488) explicitly widens eject_count from u16 to u32:

  pub eject_count: AtomicU32,  // Incremented each time committer ejects (caller-tx in_progress).
                               // Widened to u32 so max_eject_count can sit comfortably above the
                               // wall-clock bound (~1500-6000 ejects at 30s/5-20ms-per-cycle).

GUC max_eject_count default 10000, range 100-1000000 (§1.7 line 552). The u16 ceiling of 65535 is below the GUC range maximum, so values above 65535 would not be representable under the current AtomicU16.

CURRENT CODE: StagingEntry.eject_count is AtomicU16 (per session handoff and src/lib.rs definition).
SPEC: AtomicU32 with the padding adjusted (line 488: _pad2: [u8; 4]).

LOW RISK CHANGE — purely a struct field widening + padding adjustment. CAS sites that use it need their type updates; everything else flows.

AFFECTED: src/lib.rs StagingEntry struct definition. Any site in src/router.rs / src/committer.rs / src/recovery.rs that loads or fetch_adds eject_count needs the type adjusted (u16 → u32 throughput). Pre-flight grep: 'eject_count' usage sites.
acceptance_criteria: StagingEntry.eject_count is AtomicU32. Padding rebalanced to match §1.6 layout (line 488: _pad2: [u8; 4]). All call sites compile against u32. v21 acceptance + property tests green.

title: committer-checkpoint-cow: CoW SkuPoolState clone to cut snapshot allocation (Q7, DEFERRED)
description:
poc/queue-extension-v21/src/committer.rs:1000-1003 clones SkuPoolState per touched pool: snapshot.sku_pools.get(key).cloned(). SkuPoolState at cost_method.rs:78-99 contains layers: Vec<LayerView> — dynamically allocated, can be large for FIFO with many layers.

Clone is required for the rollback contract (snapshot mutation must be reversible per-envelope). Reviewer suggests CoW via Arc<SkuPoolState> + .clone() (cheap) until mutation forces a deep clone.

Defer until snapshot-clone profile data shows this is a measurable cost (likely surfaces under FIFO with deep layer chains or contended shared-pool workloads).
acceptance_criteria: (1) Profile data shows snapshot.sku_pools.cloned() as measurable cost. (2) SkuPoolState converted to Arc<SkuPoolState> with CoW via Arc::make_mut. (3) Rollback contract preserved (per-envelope mutation isolation). (4) Full v21 regression green.
notes:
M8.2 (acct-6h3o, 2026-05-19) shipped S2 N-sweep data — partially feeds this issue's decision math but does NOT close it.

What M8.2 captured (bench/results-m82-s2-n-sweep.md):
- At N=32 peak throughput: 23074 drains/60s × ~7 pool keys/SB = ~2700 SkuPoolState clones/sec
- Pipeline_ns/drain at peak = 6.82 ms

What's NOT in M8.2: allocator pressure fraction. Pure counter-based capture can't isolate clone cost from total pipeline cost; needs heaptrack / jemalloc stats / perf-record flamegraph.

To decide this issue (threshold ≥10% allocator-pressure fraction → ship; <5% → close):
Run heaptrack against the test backend during a 60s S2 N=32 cell; look for `<SkuPoolState as Clone>::clone` in the flamegraph + measure peak resident-set delta against a no-clone variant. Distinct measurement from M8.2 cell-counters; filing as a follow-up.

This issue stays IN-PROGRESS pending the heaptrack measurement.

Stale in_progress claim from 2026-05-18 released by this close.

title: committer-error-codes: replace format! errors with static codes in hot paths (Q6, DEFERRED)
description:
poc/queue-extension-v21/src/committer.rs has 30+ format!("...{e}") allocations in error returns. Each format! allocates on the heap. In hot paths (per-superbatch error returns), these add up.

Reviewer recommends replacing with static &'static str error codes (e.g., 'pipeline_dispatch_failed') plus an optional context field for the variable bits. Trade-off: loses inline context, but cuts allocation.

Defer until hot-path allocation profile shows this matters. Most format! sites are in error paths that fire rarely; only a few fire on the happy path.
acceptance_criteria: (1) Allocation profile data shows format! in error paths as measurable cost. (2) Static error code enum + optional context payload added. (3) Hot-path error sites converted.
close_reason: L4 + Q6 shipped together: CommitterError enum with &'static str discriminants in Spi variant subsumes both 'typed errors at call sites' (L4) and 'static codes on hot path' (Q6). 14/14 smoke tests green.

title: committer-spi-prepared: use prepared statements for hot-path SPI calls (Q4, DEFERRED)
description:
poc/queue-extension-v21/src/committer.rs has 16 Spi::run_with_args sites using raw SQL strings without prepared statements. pgrx's SPI plan-cache behavior depends on version; needs profile data to confirm this is a measurable hot-path cost.

Blocked on M8.2 SPI-time measurement (acct-6h3o). If §5.6 B2 classifier shows significant per-SuperBatch SPI parse/plan cost, claim this issue and switch the 7 bulk-insert sites + 6 lookup sites to prepared statements via SPI_prepare + SPI_execute_plan.
acceptance_criteria: (1) M8.2 measurement data exists showing SPI parse/plan cost > 5% of pipeline ns_total per SuperBatch. (2) Prepared statement infrastructure implemented. (3) Hot-path SPI calls switched to prepared statements. (4) Re-measured M8.2 shows reduced SPI overhead.
notes:
M8.2 (acct-6h3o, 2026-05-19) shipped S2 N-sweep data — partially feeds this issue's decision math but does NOT close it.

What M8.2 captured (bench/results-m82-s2-n-sweep.md):
- avg_pipeline_ns_per_drain @ N=32 peak throughput = 6.82 ms (IQR/median = 6.9%, clean)
- Growth across the sweep: 1.99ms (N=1) → 6.82ms (N=32) → 10.09ms (N=64) → 15.11ms (N=128)
- Cross-SB FOR UPDATE waits = 0 across all cells (intra-SB lock acquisition is the contention site, not inter-SB)

What's NOT in M8.2: plan-vs-execute split. The pipeline_ns counter sums Steps 2..12; SPI plan time is a fraction of that we can't recover from aggregate counters alone.

To decide this issue (threshold ≥10% plan-time fraction → ship; <5% → close):
Either (a) controlled A/B: build the prepared-statement variant on a feature flag, re-run M8.2 S2 N=32 cell, compare avg_pipeline_ns_per_drain medians; or (b) wire pg_stat_statements.plan_time_ms / total_time_ms aggregation into the M8.2 cell tear-down — captures it without a code variant.

Option (b) is cheaper. Filing as a follow-up; this issue stays OPEN pending the plan-time fraction measurement.

title: FU2: Fairness backstop re-validation under grouped packing rule
description:
Deferred follow-up. The current fairness backstop force-packs starved head entries as size-1 SuperBatches when starvation_tick_count >= router_starvation_threshold_ticks (default 10). Under acct-shpc's inverted packing rule, this still works semantically — a starved head entry that has no cluster siblings in the router window goes through as size-1.

But: the threshold value was calibrated under the disjoint rule, where 'starvation' meant 'kept getting bypassed by newer disjoint entries.' Under the grouped rule, a head entry may legitimately wait several ticks for cluster siblings to arrive (the cluster-coalescing benefit is what we're optimizing for). The 10-tick threshold may be either too aggressive (force-packs singletons that would have benefited from grouping a tick later) or too lenient (lets head entries wait longer than the I-router-progress invariant allows).

Re-validate under M8.2:
- Measure head-entry wait distribution per shape (S3, S4 contended; S2 disjoint).
- Compare against the I-router-progress acceptance bound (threshold × batch_window_us × 2 per §4.1 C2).
- If the threshold needs adjustment, file as router_starvation_threshold_ticks GUC tuning under M8.3 GUC sweep.

Likely no-op — the existing threshold is generous (10 ticks × 100us = 1ms). But worth a measurement pass under acct-shpc.
design: Pure measurement pass; no code changes expected. If measurement reveals a real fairness issue, file follow-up under M8.3.
acceptance_criteria: M8.2 / M8.3 measurements show I-router-progress invariant holds under contended shapes (S3 / S4 / S5 hot_pool). Either: existing threshold is fine (close as no-op) OR threshold tuning recommendation lands in M8.3 GUC sweep results.
notes: REOPENED 2026-05-18 (acct-pdgo audit retraction): close-as-superseded subsumed this under acct-y6ts on the premise that FIFO makes the backstop defensive-only. If grouped packing is the correct rule, the threshold-calibration question still has its own teeth (head entry may legitimately wait for cluster siblings). Hold until spec direction resolved.
close_reason: Spec re-revision (2026-05-18 14:42) keeps fairness backstop defensive (§3.9): 'Under affinity grouping in single-router PoC, this should NEVER happen — the oldest-first sort by min(request_seq) on connected components guarantees the group containing the head envelope is dispatched first in each tick.' Threshold tuning sweep is at §5.5 (router_starvation_threshold_ticks ∈ {1, 5, 10, 20, 50} on shape S5) — owned by acct-y6ts (M8.3 GUC sweep). The 'subsumed by acct-y6ts' verdict from the prior close stands under the new spec because the spec keeps the backstop defensive AND the threshold sweep is in scope of acct-y6ts.

title: Possible optimization: cluster overflow + committer affinity (hash-mod queue topology)
description:
Deferred follow-up. When a shared-cluster's envelope count exceeds batch_size_max (default 50), the cluster must split across multiple SuperBatches. Those split-SBs MUST serialize through one committer — else the cross-committer race that acct-0frn / acct-shpc fixed returns at the overflow boundary.

Implementation:
1. Hash the cluster's canonical pool-key signature (e.g. min sku_pool_key) to a committer shard via hash(cluster_signature) % committer_count.
2. Replace the single global committer queue with N per-committer queues (one ring per committer; CAS-claim within own queue only).
3. Router pushes the split-SBs in cluster-order to the deterministic committer's queue.

Requires:
- per-committer queue topology change in src/lib.rs (CommitterQueue → CommitterQueue[N]).
- router push function in src/router.rs picks the right queue by hash.
- M5a orphan recovery sweeps need to scan all N queues.

Defer until M8.2 statistical runner (acct-6h3o) measurements show single-cluster overflow as a practical concern. For typical S3 (g=50 K=5) and S4 (g=1 K=5), cluster sizes stay well below batch_size_max=50 by construction. S7 (very_large_wo K=50) could overflow if many backends submit overlapping K=50 envelopes simultaneously; that's where measurement is needed.
design: Acceptance path depends on M8.2 evidence. File the measurement requirement under M8.2 itself; this issue stays deferred until that data arrives.
acceptance_criteria: (a) FU not needed: M8.2 cell at batch_size_max=50 + S7-style workload shows no single-cluster overflow; close as won't-fix with measurement evidence. OR (b) FU needed: implementation lands; per-committer queue topology + hash-mod routing; M8.2 cell measurements show split-cluster serialization via single committer.
notes:
HOLD LIFTED 2026-05-18 14:42 (spec re-revision): Spec now affirms grouped packing AND spec'd the cluster-overflow case in §1.5 ('Splitting oversized components'): components > batch_size_max split into ⌈N/batch_size_max⌉ chunks; chunks become separate SuperBatches that serialize via cross-SuperBatch FOR UPDATE on pool_locks rows as the fallback. So the original FU1 'cluster overflow needs sticky-committer routing to avoid the cross-SB race' framing is partially answered — cross-SB FOR UPDATE IS the spec'd correctness fallback (not a bug). The optimization question remains: 'if measurement shows cross-SB FOR UPDATE serialization is too slow under hot-pool workloads (shape S4/S5), is hash-mod committer-queue topology a better fallback than PG row locks?' Reframe FU1 to that measurement-gated optimization. §2.1 B5 has the analytical ceiling for the cross-SB case.
2026-05-19: Reparented standalone (was acct-shpc child). Reframed as a possible optimization rather than a correctness gate — §1.5 cross-SuperBatch FOR UPDATE on pool_locks is the spec'd correctness fallback for cluster overflow, so this hash-mod topology is purely a perf optimization if measurement shows cross-SB FOR UPDATE serialization is too slow on hot-pool workloads (S4/S5). Stays deferred until M8.2 (acct-6h3o) produces the measurement evidence.

title: v2.1 PoC follow-up: bgworker_paused GUC for deterministic sync-tick testing
description:
M5c.2's acceptance suite trades per-cycle assertion specificity (was: 'eject_count grows 1,2,3 across sync ticks; staging.valid transitions 3→1→3→1→0') for BGWorker-timing robustness (now: 'arena_outstanding returns to baseline; envelope dropped'). The current test set retains the property assertions (terminal-fail eventually fires) via arena observable + invariant checks, and adds a synchronous-cycle probe (acceptance_v21_caller_tx_eject_counter_grows) that exercises eject_count monotonicity using the BGWorker (still in the SAFE direction — counter can only grow, never shrink).

Lost specificity (vs. the pre-rewrite tests):
1. Per-cycle eject_count == 1, then == 2, then == 3 (monotone with specific values).
2. staging.valid transitions through the 3→1→3→1→...→0 state machine observable.

The lost specificity is the kind of regression a bug like "eject_count increments by 2 instead of 1" would slip through. The current tests catch wrong-direction bugs and missing-increment bugs but not exact-counter bugs.

# Proposed fix: poc_v21.bgworker_paused runtime GUC

Add a Sighup-context Bool GUC (default FALSE). Both poc_v21_router_main and poc_v21_committer_main check it at the top of their tick loop; if TRUE, sleep and skip without claiming work.

Test usage:
  ALTER SYSTEM SET poc_v21.bgworker_paused = on;
  SELECT pg_reload_conf();
  -- BGWorkers now idle; sync ticks via poc_v21_test_router_drain + poc_v21_test_committer_tick are the only progress.
  -- Test asserts per-cycle eject_count value EXACTLY.
  ALTER SYSTEM RESET poc_v21.bgworker_paused;
  SELECT pg_reload_conf();

This recovers full deterministic coverage of the eject_count growth and staging.valid state machine that the original (pre-rewrite) tests had.

# Production-relevant side benefit

The bgworker_paused primitive is useful operationally beyond testing:
- Graceful maintenance windows: pause new processing while draining.
- Postmaster-attached debugging: pause to inspect shmem state without race interference.
- Hot-path performance experiments: A/B compare BGWorker-on vs sync-driven tick rates without recompiling.

# Implementation surface

- Add poc_v21.bgworker_paused GucSetting<bool> in lib.rs.
- Add bgworker_paused_now() accessor.
- Edit poc_v21_router_main: check bgworker_paused_now() at start of each wait_latch wake; if true, continue (skip the inner work).
- Edit poc_v21_committer_main: same shape.
- Test additions: replace OR augment the timing-robust scenarios C, D, F in acceptance_v21_caller_tx_coupling with sync-tick variants that exercise the BGWorker-paused path and assert per-cycle counter values exactly.

# Scope and dependencies

Blocked-by: nothing — additive primitive, doesn't change existing semantics.
Cross-ref: acct-1hyx (M5c.2), which documented the coverage gap this follow-up closes.

# Priority rationale

P3: the current M5c.2 test set already covers the core correctness via end-state observables. This follow-up upgrades the specificity from "system eventually reaches terminal" to "system progresses through the exact state machine per cycle". Not gating PoC correctness; raises the bar for regression detection on future eject-path edits.
acceptance_criteria:
- poc_v21.bgworker_paused GUC registered in _PG_init; Sighup context; default FALSE.
- router_main and committer_main respect the GUC: when TRUE, tick loops skip (no claim, no processing, just sleep).
- Sync tick helpers (poc_v21_test_router_drain, poc_v21_test_committer_tick) still work while BGWorkers are paused — they run in the caller backend.
- Test additions:
  - Per-cycle eject_count assertion test that pauses BGWorkers, drives sync ticks, asserts exact counter values per cycle.
  - Same for staging.valid 3→1→3→1 state machine observable per cycle.
- Existing M5c.2 tests still pass (BGWorker-paused mode is opt-in via test ALTER SYSTEM).
- Document the GUC in the spec or README as a test-only primitive (not a production tuning knob).
notes: Superseded by acct-gx1z.2 (commit 65acbd3). The proposed bgworker_paused primitive landed as test-only shmem AtomicU8 + poc_v21_test_set_bgworker_paused SQL fn (rather than as a runtime GUC). Production hook 'sighup-context GUC' could still ship later if operators need it; meantime the existing primitive is sufficient for the deterministic-sync-tick testing acct-iypm originally asked for.

title: v2.1 PoC follow-up: committer_terminal_decisions for observable in_progress terminal-fail
description:
M5c.2 (acct-1hyx) implements the caller-tx coupling check per spec §3.11 with the load-bearing rule "committer NEVER sleeps for callers". The committer's pg_xact_status switch has three branches:

- committed → process envelope normally
- aborted   → lazy INSERT poc_v21_submission_status state='failed' with error_code='caller_tx_aborted'. SAFE because the caller's prior 'queued' row is a dead tuple post-abort; PG's unique-index conflict check sees the dead tuple and INSERT proceeds without XactLockTableWait.
- in_progress + exhausted eject/timeout budget → terminal-fail by SILENTLY DROPPING the envelope (Step 14 cleanup CAS 3→0 frees the staging arena). NO lazy INSERT — the path would XactLockTableWait on the caller's in_progress xid, violating I-committer-non-blocking.

The drop behavior leaves an observability gap: if the in_progress caller eventually commits, their 'queued' row materializes from enqueue-side INSERT and stays 'queued' indefinitely — an orphan. If the caller eventually aborts, no row exists. Either way the caller has no committer-side signal that their envelope was terminal-failed.

This follow-up adds the missing observability without violating the spec invariant.

# Why the original approach broke

Discovered 2026-05-17 via property test hang. pg_locks evidence:

  pid 833 (committer)  waiting on  transactionid 189537571  ShareLock  granted=f
  pid 835 (caller)     holding     transactionid 189537571  ExclusiveLock  granted=t

The committer's `INSERT INTO poc_v21_submission_status ... ON CONFLICT (correlation_id) DO UPDATE` triggered _bt_check_unique, which found the caller's still-uncommitted 'queued' row's index entry and called XactLockTableWait on the caller's xid. Direct spec violation.

# Proposed implementation

Add a new append-only table:

  CREATE TABLE poc_v21_committer_terminal_decisions (
      decision_id   BIGSERIAL PRIMARY KEY,
      correlation_id UUID NOT NULL,
      error_code    TEXT NOT NULL,
      decided_at    TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL DEFAULT now(),
      committer_tx_id BIGINT NOT NULL,
      superbatch_id BIGINT NOT NULL,
      merged_at     TIMESTAMPTZ NULL,
      error_detail  JSONB NOT NULL DEFAULT '{}'::jsonb
  );
  CREATE INDEX ON poc_v21_committer_terminal_decisions (correlation_id) WHERE merged_at IS NULL;
  CREATE INDEX ON poc_v21_committer_terminal_decisions (decided_at);

No unique constraint on correlation_id — the committer can INSERT freely without conflicting against any caller's in_progress row in submission_status (different table; no shared unique key path).

Committer Step 2.45 in_progress terminal-fail branch INSERTs a row here instead of dropping silently. The staging slot still goes through Step 14 cleanup as today.

Reconciliation runs in two complementary places:

1. Trigger on poc_v21_submission_status INSERT: when a caller's tx commits and the 'queued' row materializes, an AFTER INSERT trigger checks poc_v21_committer_terminal_decisions for unmerged rows on the same correlation_id. If found, UPDATEs submission_status to state='failed' with the recorded error_code + error_detail, and sets merged_at on the decision row.

2. Periodic sweep (piggybacked on the router BGWorker's 60s slot leak audit per M5d.2 — file as cross-ref): finds unmerged decisions older than a threshold and either (a) merges them if a submission_status row materialized post-trigger-install, or (b) marks them 'caller_never_committed' if the caller's xid is confirmed aborted/unknown.

This keeps the committer's hot path simple (single INSERT, no conflict) and pushes the reconciliation work to a path that already exists.

# Spec implications

§3.11 should be amended to note:

- Lazy submission_status INSERT is safe for aborted callers but NOT for in_progress callers (XactLockTableWait).
- The in_progress terminal-fail path writes to a separate committer_terminal_decisions table whose schema avoids the unique-index conflict with the caller's still-open 'queued' row.
- Reconciliation transitions submission_status post-caller-commit OR after a confirmed caller-abort.

# Scope and non-goals

In scope:
- New table schema migration.
- Committer Step 2.45 in_progress terminal-fail path writes to the new table.
- Trigger on submission_status INSERT to merge unmerged decisions.
- Periodic sweep for orphans (piggybacked on M5d.2 router audit).
- Test coverage: terminal-fail row appears in committer_terminal_decisions; on caller commit, submission_status transitions to 'failed' with the right error_code.

Out of scope:
- Application-layer poll-for-stale-queued reconciler (caller-side concern).
- Real-time notification to callers (NOTIFY) — deferred unless measured to matter.

# Dependencies

Blocked-by: acct-1hyx (M5c.2 — must land the foundational eject + drop path first).
Cross-ref: acct-y0bp (M5d.1 startup recovery — may extend that worker's sweep).
Cross-ref: acct-q4d6 (or wherever M5d.2 lands — sweep integration).

# Priority rationale

P3: doesn't gate PoC correctness (the silent-drop satisfies I-committer-non-blocking). Adds observability for production use. The PoC scope explicitly accepts the orphan-queued limitation per user direction 2026-05-17 ("we are not so worried about the application at this point").
acceptance_criteria:
- poc_v21_committer_terminal_decisions table migration added; indexes per the design block.
- Committer Step 2.45 in_progress terminal-fail INSERTs into poc_v21_committer_terminal_decisions (no submission_status touch).
- AFTER INSERT trigger on poc_v21_submission_status merges unmerged decisions for the inserted correlation_id; submission_status transitions to 'failed' + error_code='caller_tx_eject_exhausted' or 'caller_tx_timeout' as appropriate.
- Periodic sweep (M5d.2 piggyback) catches orphan decisions where caller never committed; marks them resolved.
- Property test extended: in_progress callers with eject/timeout exhaustion produce a committer_terminal_decisions row immediately; after the caller commits, the test asserts submission_status visible to other backends transitions to 'failed' with the right code.
- I-committer-non-blocking still holds (no XactLockTableWait under any path).

title: v2.1 PoC follow-up: persistent router starvation_tick_count (Q-B)
description:
Spec §7 Q-B notes the router's per-entry starvation_tick_count is ephemeral (lost on router death). PoC accepts this; production hardening would persist the counts.

Scope: option to persist starvation_tick_count in shmem (per-StagingEntry field) or in a side table polled on startup. Measure overhead. Decide whether the production version should adopt.

Mainly a question of whether router-death + restart starves head-of-queue entries that were close to forced-as-size-1. PoC's M5b restart tests measure this; if observed starvation under router-restart is bounded (< 2x normal), ephemeral is fine. If observed > 2x: persistence needed.

title: v2.1 PoC follow-up: router sliding-window cursor alternative (Q-E)
description:
Spec §7 Q-E flags sliding-cursor router as alternative to head-scan: sliding gives better throughput at cost of fairness.

Scope: implement the sliding-cursor variant behind a GUC poc_v21.router_window_mode ∈ {head_scan (default), sliding}. Sweep on shape S2 + S3 to measure throughput delta. Document fairness tradeoff (longer tail for head-of-queue entries under sliding).

If sliding shows > 10% throughput improvement under disjoint workload AND tail-latency degradation is acceptable: recommend as production option (with documented tradeoff).

Spec: §7 Q-E.
acceptance_criteria:
- Sliding-cursor variant implemented behind GUC.
- Sweep on S2 + S3 produces head_scan vs sliding throughput comparison.
- Document fairness tradeoff.
- Recommendation logged.

title: Queue PoC: caller-side batch RPC (b=1000) — measure gap to shmem rollup PoC
description:
M10.1 verdict (acct-4d4n.23, 2026-05-16) surfaced that the queue PoC's poc_ledger_apply RPC takes one event at a time (per spec §5.2: 'b=1 for the PoC; multi-item batches deferred'). The shmem rollup PoC (acct-sw4i, poc/ledger-extension) reached 43K-67K events/sec at b=1000 on the same shapes the queue PoC measured at 6K-12K events/sec at b=1. The gap is almost entirely caller-side per-event RPC overhead (sqlx + libpq + context switches), not server-side committer batching — which the queue PoC's M9.3 sweep already validated. Adding caller-side batching is structurally trivial: new pg_extern poc_ledger_apply_batch(events JSONB[]) that unpacks the array and pushes N slots before parking; committer drain path unchanged.

Scope (deliberately narrow):
- Implement poc_ledger_apply_batch(events JSONB[]) entrypoint that takes an array of (sku_id, location_id, qty, issue_id, method) tuples
- Single batch size b=1000 (matches shmem rollup baseline; no need for full sweep)
- Three shapes: fan_in, fan_out, small_batch — at N=32 and N=128 only
- Default GUCs (bw=500 bs=1024 sc=on), 5×60s + 30s settle methodology
- Report events/sec, p99 per-batch-call, classifier, deadlocks

NOT in scope (avoid bench-matrix expansion):
- Full N sweep (N=32, N=128 only — these are the two contention regimes that matter)
- Multi-batch-size sweep (b=1000 only — establishes the comparable-to-shmem-rollup data point)
- GUC sweep (already covered by M9.3 for server-side batching)
- All 6 shapes (3 shapes — the same fan_in/fan_out/small_batch surface the verdict used)

Output: bench/results-m10-batch-rpc.md with three small comparison tables (queue PoC b=1 vs queue PoC b=1000 vs shmem rollup b=1000 reference numbers) + headline ratio. Append §M10 update to poc-validation-spec.md if the result shifts the verdict (it shouldn't — this is characterization, not correctness).
acceptance_criteria: poc_ledger_apply_batch shipped + benched at b=1000 across fan_in/fan_out/small_batch × N={32, 128} × 5×60s. results-m10-batch-rpc.md committed with the three-way comparison table. No regression to existing single-event behaviour.
close_reason: Closed

description: M10.1 verdict (acct-4d4n.23, 2026-05-16) marked C2 CONDITIONAL because per-milestone evidence chain stands but a single proptest binary exercising all seven invariants under random kill/cancel/abort sequences does not exist. title: M6.1 follow-up: SubXactCallback for ROLLBACK TO SAVEPOINT compensation
description:
M6.1 (acct-4d4n.16) ships ABORT-only compensation per spec §1.7 MVP scope. SubXact rollback (SAVEPOINT / ROLLBACK TO SAVEPOINT) does NOT trigger the regular XactCallback — it fires SubXactCallback with SUBXACT_EVENT_ABORT_SUB.

This follow-up covers: register a SubXactCallback alongside the M6.1 XactCallback; on SUBXACT_EVENT_ABORT_SUB, identify cost rows produced inside that subxact (requires tracking subxact-nesting-level alongside user_tx_xid on cost rows, OR scanning by subtxid which is more involved); emit compensation rows for those.

Adds requirements: subtransaction_id (xid) column on cost rows, OR an in-memory mapping of (rows-produced-this-subxact) cleared on subxact commit/abort.

Driver: any workload that uses savepoints for retry logic (rare in our PoC scope but realistic in ERP integrations).

Scope is structurally larger than ABORT-only (touches schema if column added; touches apply path to track subxact nesting). Filed at P3.

See acct-4d4n.16 description for the parent M6.1 architecture.

title: M5c.2 follow-up: spillover arena allocator + slot-recycle coupling
description: Filed during M5c.1/M5c.2 work 2026-05-15. M5c.2 (acct-4d4n.15) shipped narrow — slot leak audit only. The spillover arena (PocResultSlot.spillover_offset reserved field) has no allocator backing it today; PocResultSlot.depletion_ids_inline[32] is the only depletion-output surface. Spec §3.9 wants spillover-arena blocks tied atomically to slot recycle. Driver for this work is M9 fan_out depletion workloads where >32-deplet-per-slot becomes real; until then the inline cap is sufficient. Acceptance per the original M5c.2 issue: test_spillover_arena_exhaustion — undersized arena + large fan_in → clean exhaustion error; caller retries with smaller batch. Implementation surface: new shmem region + free-list + arena_block_id linkage on the slot + atomic free-on-recycle.

title: M2.1 follow-up: same-issue-id-within-batch dedup gap
description: Surfaced 2026-05-15 while writing M5a.2 (acct-4d4n.11) acceptance tests. When multiple backends push the same issue_id concurrently from independent sessions, all of those events land in a single committer's batch. M2.1's dedup_lookup runs ONCE per batch against the durable cost tables (poc_cost_consumptions / poc_cost_depletions) — it does not dedup *within* a batch. plan_apply then produces N PocApplyResult rows all keyed on the same (issue_id, method_used), and the bulk INSERT trips the UNIQUE constraint on the 2nd row. The 1st INSERT row lands cleanly; the rest abort, the batch's slot fills surface partial-success in confusing ways (one backend gets the result, others see ERROR or SLOT_FILLED-CAS-failed). Reproducer: bench/run-m5a2-cancel-retry.sh's original Test 3 design — 4 concurrent psql sessions each calling poc_ledger_apply with the same issue_id. The current M5a.2 script tests the sequential cancel-then-retry path instead, which exercises the inter-batch dedup successfully. Same-batch dedup needs to land in process_group: after the dedup_lookup categorization, collapse to_plan events by issue_id (keeping the first; subsequent same-issue events become replayed-with-pending pointers to that first event's slot). Both the cost-table INSERT and the slot fill loop need to honor the in-batch grouping. Touches src/committer.rs::process_group only — no schema change. Acceptance: bench/run-m5a2-cancel-retry.sh Test 3 storm variant (4 concurrent same-issue-id) passes: all 4 backends return the same result; exactly one durable cost row; no UNIQUE violation; quiescent at end. P3 (correctness gap, but workaround exists: callers should not push the same issue_id from N sessions concurrently — that's typically a retry-after-cancel pattern which M5a.2 handles sequentially).

description:
Implement workload generators per spec §5.2: (1) fan_in g=1 (all N backends one SKU; worst-case contention), (2) fan_out g=5000 (N backends disjoint; linear scaling), (3) balanced g=50 (moderate shared partial), (4) zipfian g=1000 alpha=1.0 (realistic hot-pool; one pool 10× traffic), (5) small-batch b=100 g=50 (coalescing efficiency), (6) mixed-method 33/33/33 FIFO/AVG/STD on balanced g=50. Backend orchestrator spawns N psql connections, coordinates start via barrier, collects per-backend latency histograms.

Spec cross-refs: §5.2 (workload shape definitions).

title: M8.3: Bottleneck classifier metrics (B1 LWLock / B2 WAL / B3 plan_apply / B5 wake)
description:
Per spec §5.7. Per-cell metric capture during bake-off: B1 LWLock wait time via pg_locks sampler (reuse pattern from acct repo tests/common/pg_locks_sampler.rs reference; vendor or reimplement narrowly per R5 risk note in plan); B2 WAL fsync time via pg_stat_wal deltas before/after cell; B3 method plan_apply CPU via cumulative Instant::now() deltas inside committer; B5 wake latency (SetLatch → ProcWaitForSignal round-trip timestamp). Per-cell classifier emits one label per measured workload × N × GUC cell.

Spec cross-refs: §5.7 (bottleneck classification taxonomy).
acceptance_criteria: Classifier produces a label per cell under M9 bake-off. Labels match intuition under spot-checks: fan_in at N=32 → B1 or B3; fan_out at N=128 → B2 (WAL) or B5 (wake). Mixed cells documented as such. Output format usable by M9.3.

Tip a8e21e2.

SQL-callable observability functions. poc_ledger_shard_stats() TableIterator returns (shard_id, depth, committer_pid, committer_lease_remaining_ms, last_committer_tx_id, error_count). poc_ledger_method_stats() TableIterator returns (method_id, dispatch_count, error_rate, plan_apply_p50, plan_apply_p99). title: M6.1: Compensation semantics — XactCallback(ABORT) + tagged-union PocRequestKind
description:
Per-user-backend XactCallback registered on first apply call. On XACT_EVENT_ABORT: scan cost rows stamped with current user_tx_xid; for each, enqueue PocPendingRequest with kind.tag = Compensate, body.compensate filled with PocCompensatePayload (tagged union per spec §1.4 — FullTransactionId typed wrapper note honored). Committer drain dispatches by kind: Apply triggers M2.x plan_apply path; Compensate writes reversal rows. FIFO 1:1 compensation cardinality: 32-layer original apply → 32 compensation rows (one per depletion_id).

Spec cross-refs: §1.7 (compensation flow), §1.4 (PocRequestKind tagged union with Apply/Compensate variants).
acceptance_criteria: End-to-end abort test: user-tx applies 1 FIFO event consuming 5 layers (5 depletion rows written) → user-tx aborts → 5 compensation rows appear stamped with that user_tx_xid. FIFO cardinality test passes. C2 invariant I-compensation-coverage (proptest under chaos): every aborted user-tx has compensations for ALL cost rows it produced.
close_reason: Closed

title: M5c.2: Slot leak audit + spillover arena lifecycle coupling
description:
Failure modes §3.7 + §3.9. (1) Periodic 10s scan flags slots in 'allocated' state >60s with dead backend (pg_pid_alive false) → force-free with telemetry counter increment. (2) Spillover arena blocks are tied atomically to slot transition → free: the slot's CAS-free path also returns arena block to freelist. Decoupling these two operations → leak risk if the slot frees but arena block doesn't. Under undersized arena + large fan_in workload, exhaustion error propagates cleanly to caller, caller retries with smaller batch.

Spec cross-refs: §3.7 (slot exhaustion / leak), §3.9 (spillover arena exhaustion), §7 Q-C (allocation policy freelist vs slab — PoC uses freelist; measure fragmentation in soak).
acceptance_criteria: test_slot_leak_recovered: kill backend mid-allocation; 70s later periodic audit reclaims the slot + its arena block; counter increments. test_spillover_arena_exhaustion: undersized arena + large fan_in → caller receives clean exhaustion error; caller retries with smaller batch and succeeds. Slot-free + arena-free are observably atomic (no intermediate state visible).
close_reason: Closed

title: M5c.1: Backpressure (push blocks on cv with queue_full_timeout_ms)
description:
Failure mode §3.4. When ring at capacity-1, push blocks on condition variable. Committer drain signals after advancing head. CHECK_FOR_INTERRUPTS every 100ms for cancel. Bounded queue_full_timeout_ms (default 5s) returns clean queue_full error to caller — NOT a panic, NOT silent drop.

Spec cross-refs: §3.4 (backpressure), §7 Q-G (sustained overload behavior — measure under stress; PoC defaults to 5s timeout).
acceptance_criteria: test_backpressure_blocks_then_unblocks: fill ring to capacity, push blocks; drain one event; push unblocks. test_backpressure_timeout: fill ring, sleep past queue_full_timeout_ms; push returns queue_full error cleanly. CHECK_FOR_INTERRUPTS fires on cancel mid-wait → caller gets cancel error rather than queue_full.
close_reason: Closed

title: M5b.2: Lease false-positive protection + slow-committer mitigation
description:
Failure mode §3.6. Before any lease takeover CAS, candidate MUST pg_pid_alive(stored_committer_pid) verify dead. Alive → back off, sleep committer_lease_ms, retry. This blocks a known false-positive class where a legitimately slow committer (e.g., long-running batch) gets stolen by a contender during a lease-expiry window. Slow-committer mitigation: caller-side batch_size_max shrink so per-batch SPI time stays under committer_lease_ms in expected workload.

Spec cross-refs: §3.6 (lease timeout false positives), §1.6 step 10 (lease + pid mechanism).
acceptance_criteria: test_slow_committer_not_stolen: committer batch takes 3 × committer_lease_ms with live pid; contender's pg_pid_alive returns alive; no takeover; committer completes normally. test_dead_committer_stolen: lease expired AND pg_pid_alive false → takeover succeeds. Documents recommended batch_size_max relative to lease_ms in operator guide.
close_reason: Closed

title: M5b.1: Startup recovery worker (postmaster restart + xid8 scan)
description:
Failure mode §3.5. Recovery worker registered at _PG_init runs on postmaster startup: (1) Scan max(committer_tx_id) per shard from cost tables to seed per-shard counters past any pre-restart values. (2) Scan cost tables by denormalized user_tx_xid xid8 column; for each distinct xid query pg_xact status; if aborted, emit compensation request via the same enqueue path M6.1 uses for live aborts.

Spec cross-refs: §3.5 (crash recovery), §1.2 (user_tx_xid xid8 denormalized on every cost row), §7 Q-F (production watermark deferred — PoC scans bounded test tables; production needs incremental tracking, deferred to design-v2).
acceptance_criteria: test_postmaster_restart_recovers_in_flight: load 100 in-flight transactions, kill -9 postmaster, restart — recovery completes within 30s (O2 precursor); no data loss in committed cost rows. test_postmaster_restart_no_data_loss: every committed user-tx has its expected cost rows; every aborted user-tx has compensations emitted. Per-shard committer_tx_seq counter seeded past pre-restart max.

Phase A counter seeding via fetch_max'd queue::seed_committer_tx_at_least across three cost sources (consumptions / layers / depletions JOIN layers). Phase B xid abort scan stub (TransactionIdDidAbort + log!) wired for M6.1 enqueue wire-up. Pre-check via to_regclass guards against fresh-DB. UNION ALL outer-aliasing applied. Tests: Test 1 counter seeding across docker restart (10 applies, 8 shards seeded, no committer_tx_id collisions on new applies). Test 2 fresh-DB no-op (0-scan, no FATAL, all 16 shards at seq=0). M5a.1 + M5a.2 regression suites still pass.

title: M5a.2: Waiter cancel + dedup-replay (CAS abandoned + idempotent retry)
description:
Failure mode §3.3. CHECK_FOR_INTERRUPTS in waiter's wait loop (per Postgres query cancel convention). On cancel: CAS slot allocated → abandoned atomically; committer still INSERTs durable row (the work is idempotent at the cost-table level via M2.1's dedup-lookup). On caller retry with same issue_id, dedup-lookup at §1.6 step 17d returns cached result without re-applying.

Spec cross-refs: §3.3 (waiter cancel), §4.2 C2 invariant I-eventual-resolution (every slot reaches {filled, filled_with_error, abandoned} within 10 × committer_lease_ms), §1.6 step 17d (dedup-lookup).
acceptance_criteria: test_waiter_cancel_mid_wait_processes: cancel waiter mid-wait; committer still INSERTs durable row; row visible in cost tables. test_waiter_cancel_after_commit_compensates: cancel after commit but before result-read; result discarded but durable row remains. test_replay_returns_same_result: caller retries same issue_id → dedup-lookup returns cached result; no duplicate rows. C2 I-eventual-resolution: every slot reaches terminal state within 10 × committer_lease_ms (proptest invariant under chaos: random kills + cancels + retries).
close_reason: Shipped @ 3178d02. Waiter cancel cleanup wired into poc_ledger_apply (mark slot ABANDONED + release_committer if held, BEFORE ProcessInterrupts unwinds). drain_and_commit treats SLOT_ABANDONED CAS failure as benign (durable INSERT preserved). All three acceptance tests pass (cancel mid-wait → slot abandoned + no durable row; sequential retry returns cached; cancel-then-manual-drain-then-retry hits dedup-lookup). M5a.1 regression suite still clean. Same-issue-id-within-batch dedup gap surfaced and filed as acct-psye.

title: M5a.1: Orphan recovery — committer death pre/post commit + lease takeover
description:
Failure mode §3.2. Lease mechanism: CAS committer_pid + separate-store committer_lease_ts. pg_pid_alive FFI via unsafe { libc::kill(pid, 0) } — returns ESRCH if dead. On lease expiry candidate must verify pg_pid_alive==dead before takeover (false-positive guard from M5b.2 is a sibling fix). Exponential-backoff pg_xact status poll: 10ms → 20ms → 40ms → 80ms → ... clamped at committer_lease_ms * 10. Per-slot backfill from poc_cost_depletions/consumptions if user-tx committed; mark abandoned if aborted; on neither (still in flight) keep waiting.

Spec cross-refs: §3.2 (committer death scenarios pre-/post-commit), §3.6 (lease timeout) — works with M5b.2.
acceptance_criteria: test_committer_sigkill_pre_commit: kill committer between batch build and INSERT — orphan recovery scans pg_xact, all slots in batch marked abandoned; cost tables empty. test_committer_sigkill_post_commit: kill committer between INSERT and slot-fill — orphan recovery backfills slots from cost tables via committer_tx_id JOIN; results correct. Lease takeover completes within 2 × committer_lease_ms p99.
close_reason: Closed

title: M4.1: Multi-shard hash routing + parallel committers
description:
Hash-route (sku_id, location_id) to N shards via shard_idx = hash & (shard_count - 1) per spec §1.6 steps 3-4. Per-shard independent committer + drain loop; cross-shard parallelism with no inter-shard lock contention except where pools collide (which Q-A's pool-lock layer handles). Aggregate metrics across shards (depth, election count, drain count).

Spec cross-refs: §1.1 (components), §1.6 steps 3-4 (hash dispatch).
acceptance_criteria: g=N*4 SKUs hashed across N=4 shards; cross-shard parallelism observable (concurrent committers across shards under load). Aggregate throughput scales sub-linearly per active-shard count (P1 precursor — full P1 measurement deferred to M10). Q-H (per-shard fairness) noted for monitoring; not enforced in PoC.
close_reason: Closed

title: M3.2: Pool-lock granularity decision (Q-A: poc_pool_locks table vs row-lock anchor)
description:
Spec §7 Q-A: PoC sketches a poc_pool_locks table for committer-to-committer serialization on the same pool (one extra SPI per batch). Alternative: row-lock anchor — FOR UPDATE on a designated row in a poc_pool_lock_anchors table populated once per pool. Implement both behind a GUC switch; bench under fan_in shape (single pool, N=8 concurrent committers across shards routing to same pool); pick winner by measured throughput + p99.

Spec cross-refs: §7 Q-A (the decision text), §1.6 steps 16c-d (FOR UPDATE on pool lock precedes snapshot construction).
acceptance_criteria: Both implementations exist behind GUC. Bench cell run under fan_in produces signal (one wins outside the other's IQR). Winner wired into committer drain path as default. Q-A resolution + measurement noted in spec §7. Loser implementation either deleted or retained behind GUC for future re-measurement.
close_reason: M3.2 Q-A pool-lock granularity RESOLVED 2026-05-15 @ a2958f7. Three modes wired behind poc_ledger.pool_lock_mode GUC: 'none' (default winner), 'pool_locks', 'pool_lock_anchors'. Single-shard fan_in bench (8w x 15s x 3 runs): medians 747/743/731 tps — within ~2%, IQRs overlap. No signal. Structural reason: M3.1's committer-PID CAS already serializes within-shard, and current hash routes one pool to one shard so cross-shard collisions are unreachable at M3 scope. Two non-default modes retained behind GUC for re-measurement at M4.1.

title: M3.1: Multi-backend coordination on single shard (election + wait/wake)
description:
Multiple backends push concurrently to one shard. Per spec §1.6 steps 6-14: losers of the committer-election CAS wait on per-slot wakeup primitive (ProcWaitForSignal on Latch); committer signals waiters via SetLatch immediately after writing each slot's result. Per-shard correctness verified at N=8 concurrent backends.

Spec cross-refs: §1.6 steps 6-14 (election + wait/wake), §3.3 lays groundwork for cancel handling (deferred to M5a.2).
acceptance_criteria: 8 backends push 10 events each (80 events total) concurrently to one shard; one wins election; others wait on slot; all 80 results returned with correct attribution. No spurious wakeups (latch only fires when slot actually filled). C2 invariant I-row-attribution holds: every cost row has valid committer_tx_id + user_tx_xid stamping.
close_reason: M3.1 shipped @ e3c5c5f. PocResultSlot.waiter_pid field + signal_waiter helper + wait/wake loop in poc_ledger_apply. 8 backends x 10 calls on one shard: 80 rows / 30 distinct committers / 118ms / zero errors. FIFO/AVG/STD + replay regression smoke clean.

title: M2.3: AVG + STD method impls + SPI snapshot helpers
description:
Implement two trait impls behind PocCostMethod: AVG reads poc_cost_avg running aggregate (qty + value) for the pool, computes unit_cost, produces 1:1 poc_cost_consumptions rows with UNIQUE (issue_id, method_used). STD reads poc_standard_costs by sku_id, produces 1:1 consumption rows. Both share SPI snapshot helpers (FOR UPDATE on pool lock from M3.2 once available; M2.3 reads without lock since single-backend in scope).

Spec cross-refs: §1.2 (poc_cost_consumptions schema), §1.3 (trait). Pool-lock granularity decided in M3.2.
acceptance_criteria: T1 AVG: 3 sequential receipts (qty 100 @ $10, 100 @ $20, 100 @ $15) → next consumption applies at running avg $15. T1 STD: standard cost lookup returns asserted value; consumption row stamped with unit_cost from std table. UNIQUE catches duplicate within same batch.
close_reason: Closed

title: M2.2: FIFO method impl (plan_apply + per-layer depletion writeback)
description:
Implement FIFO behind PocCostMethod. plan_apply walks poc_cost_layers ordered by layer_seq under FOR UPDATE (R4 enforcement at committer per spec §1.6 R4 note). Sums per-layer depletions into a Vec<DepletionRecord>. Committer's INSERT phase writes 1:N rows to poc_cost_depletions with composite UNIQUE (issue_id, method_used, layer_id). Empty-pool / partial-fill raises per-event InsufficientInventory (carried via PocApplyResult, NOT a batch-abort).

Spec cross-refs: §1.2 (poc_cost_layers + poc_cost_depletions schema with xid8 user_tx_xid + committer_tx_id columns), §1.3 (trait), §1.6 R4 semantic note.
acceptance_criteria: T1 FIFO single-layer case: 1 event consuming 1 layer → 1 depletion row. T1 FIFO multi-layer case: 1 event consuming 5 layers → 5 depletion rows (cardinality test). T1 partial-fill: empty pool → per-event InsufficientInventory; siblings in batch unaffected. UNIQUE constraint never triggers under non-replay; replay path returns cached result via M2.1 dedup-lookup.
close_reason: Closed

title: M2.1: PocCostMethod trait + per-event partial-success flow + batched dedup-lookup
description:
Define the trait surface per spec §1.3: method_id() → &'static str, plan_apply(batch: &PocApplyBatch, snapshot: &PocSnapshot) → PocApplyResult. PocApplyResult carries per-event success/error variants. Implement three-category partitioning at §1.6 step 17d: (a) replayed via batched dedup SPI lookup, (b) plan_apply success, (c) plan_apply error. Dedup-lookup is ONE SPI per (method, batch) via WHERE issue_id = ANY($1::bigint[]) AND method_used = $2 — NOT per-event.

Spec cross-refs: §1.3 (trait surface), §1.6 step 17d (batched dedup-lookup + 3-category partition), §3.10 (per-event error propagation).
acceptance_criteria: Trait surface compiles. Test test_per_event_error_partial_success: a batch where one event errors but others succeed — error propagates only for the erroring event, others commit. Test test_mixed_replay_and_fresh_in_one_batch: caller retries 5 events (3 replayed from prior commit, 2 fresh); 3 return cached, 2 apply fresh. Dedup-lookup verified as ONE SPI call regardless of batch size.
close_reason: Closed

title: M1.2: Committer election + batch drain (synchronous, fake INSERT)
description:
CAS-based committer election with separate-store lease timestamp per spec §1.6 step 10 (committer_pid CAS first, lease_ts store second; readers check pid then lease). Single-shard drain loop: committer reads ring [head, tail), builds batch up to batch_size_max OR drain on batch_window_us elapse, performs fake 'INSERT INTO poc_test_rows' via SPI inside BeginInternalSubTransaction, on commit writes result to each slot, releases committer role atomically (CAS committer_pid → 0).

Spec cross-refs: §1.6 steps 10-21 (committer election through release), §1.2 (placeholder poc_test_rows schema). Decides Q-E (per-shard vs global committer_tx_seq) by using per-shard counter (already determined in saved decisions).
acceptance_criteria: One backend calls poc_ledger_apply(payload), becomes committer, drains its own one-event batch, INSERTs one poc_test_rows row, returns result. Single-shard ordering test pins C2 invariant I4: committer_tx_seq strictly increases. No crashes under sequential calls.
close_reason: Closed

title: M1.1: PocQueueShard + slot pool + ring buffer (single-shard primitive)
description:
Shmem data structures per spec §1.4: PocQueueShard struct (head/tail/committer_pid/committer_lease_ts atomics, PendingRequest array sized requests_per_shard, ResultSlot pool sized slots_per_shard, spillover arena, per-shard LWLock). Implement slot allocation OUTSIDE the LWLock per §1.6 step 5: atomic fetch_add for index reservation, CAS state transition free→allocated, linear probe ≤16 slots before signaling exhaustion. Slot state machine: free → allocated → in_flight → {filled, filled_with_error, abandoned} → free. No committer election yet (M1.2). No real INSERT yet (M1.2).

Spec cross-refs: §1.4 (PocQueueShard layout, ResultSlot fields, spillover arena), §1.6 steps 4-8 (slot acquisition + ring push).
acceptance_criteria: T1 single-thread allocation cycles: acquire slot → mark in_flight → mark filled → recycle to free; states transition atomically. Ring buffer head/tail invariants hold under bounded sequential push/drain. Slot pool exhaustion returns clean error (not panic). Linear-probe ≤16 enforced.
close_reason: Shipped @ 8912ba4. PocQueueShard / PocPendingRequest / PocResultSlot per spec §1.4 with single global PgLwLock; slot allocation OUTSIDE LWLock with POC_MAX_SLOT_PROBE=16 enforcement per §1.6 step 5; ring push/drain per §1.6 steps 6-9 / 12-14. Sizing compile-time const (16x512x512 = ~3.6 MB shmem); spec-default 256x4096x4096 deferred until M9 demands. All four acceptance gates pass against acct_poc_queue: T1 slot state machine (acquire→filled→recycle, acquire→abandoned→recycle, reject invalid transitions), T2 ring head/tail invariants under push/drain, T3 slot pool exhaustion returns NULL, T4 linear-probe-16 enforced via next_slot_seq advance math (100 attempts on fully-allocated pool consume exactly 1600 seq numbers).

title: M0.1: Extension scaffolding (poc_ledger crate, GUCs, shmem reservation)
description:
Bootstrap the poc/queue-extension/ pgrx crate. _PG_init registers 9 GUCs per spec §1.5: poc_ledger.shard_count (default 256, postmaster), requests_per_shard (4096, postmaster), slots_per_shard (4096, postmaster), spillover_arena_mb (64, postmaster), batch_window_us (500, sighup), batch_size_max (1024, sighup), committer_lease_ms (100, sighup), queue_full_timeout_ms (5000, sighup), semantics (compensation|reservation, sighup). Shmem reservation via RequestAddinShmemSpace sized from GUCs. Dummy #[pg_extern] poc_ledger_hello() returns a greeting. Docker-compose adds 'poc_ledger' to shared_preload_libraries (already has pg_stat_statements,pg_cron,ledger_extension). Creates new DB acct_poc_queue on existing localhost:5111 cluster.

Spec cross-refs: §1.4 (shmem layout sketch), §1.5 (GUC table).
acceptance_criteria: CREATE EXTENSION poc_ledger succeeds in acct_poc_queue DB. pg_settings shows all 9 poc_ledger.* GUCs at documented defaults. SELECT poc_ledger_hello() returns. PG starts with shared_preload_libraries entry without OOM or crash.

Extension scaffolding live in container; acct_poc_queue DB exists; CREATE EXTENSION poc_ledger works; all 9 GUCs visible at spec-correct defaults + reload contexts; poc_ledger_hello() returns build identifier; PG starts cleanly with extended shared_preload_libraries.

title: zm69.h11 followup: production layer-lifecycle GC for h_layer_arena
description:
Path 4 (acct-xeee) bumped HL_N_BUCKETS from 2^16 to 2^22 (256 MiB shmem) to cover 60s benches. At measured fan_out throughput (~24K new layer cells per second at 30% receipts), even 256 MiB only buys ~3 minutes before hash-table load exceeds 50%. h_layer_arena has no cell reclamation — cells live until next h_layer_arena_reset() call. Production cannot rely on this.

Three options to evaluate (file sub-issues per chosen option):

OPTION 1 — Tombstone-on-drained-and-quiescent reclamation.
  When a cell hits residual=0 AND no concurrent backend has it staged in H_LAYER_PRE_APPLIED:
    - Mark bucket.occupied = 2 (tombstone). probe chain treats tombstones as 'skip but continue probing', not 'terminate'.
    - Insertion can reuse tombstoned buckets after re-probe under EXCLUSIVE.
  Pros: generic, no schema knowledge required, works for any workload shape.
  Cons: needs last_touched_xid tracking + xid-quiescence test on each candidate; tombstone-aware probe chain is invasive; latent risk of probe-chain corruption if tombstone logic has edge cases.
  Effort: medium-high (~3-4 days). Needs property test on the tombstone-aware probe.

OPTION 2 — Per-period or per-lot partition with explicit reset.
  h_layer_arena cells carry a partition key (e.g., period_id or lot_root_id).
  Reset operates per-partition (walk buckets, clear ones whose partition_key matches the reset target).
  Caller (post_posting_lines close-hook, lot retention sweep) triggers explicit per-period reset at period close.
  Pros: natural retention boundary; no XID tracking; clean operational story.
  Cons: assumes a partition concept (period, lot, fiscal year) that maps to the application's lifecycle; PoC has no such concept.
  Effort: medium (~1-2 days). Likely the production answer for acct.

OPTION 3 — GUC-driven sizing tied to receipt retention window.
  HL_N_BUCKETS becomes runtime-configurable via shmem_request_hook + ShmemInitStruct. Operator sizes to cover their target retention window.
  Pros: simplest code change; matches existing PG idioms (work_mem, shared_buffers).
  Cons: stopgap, not a solution. Eventually cells must be reclaimed.
  Effort: small (~half day).

Likely (2) is the production answer for acct; (1) is the generic alternative for non-period-bounded workloads; (3) is a stopgap.

Acceptance:
- A decision document selecting one option with rationale.
- Implementation of the chosen option in poc/ledger-extension/.
- New T1: long-run bench (10 minutes at fan_out shape) maintains stable shmem load — no hash-table-full errors.
- bench/results-h-ext-path4-gc-2026-05-XX.md documents the throughput delta (expect within 5% of pre-GC numbers; GC overhead should be amortized).

Blocks: any non-PoC adoption of path 4 architecture.
design: Sub-options should be filed only AFTER the design choice is made (option 1/2/3 each generates different concrete sub-issues). The 'decision document' acceptance is a research output — surface in research/ before any implementation code.
notes: Surfaced 2026-05-14 from path 4 bench notes (acct-xeee). The acct codebase has a natural partition surface: lot_id (acct-uze + sxl2 work). For production backport, Option 2 with lot_id as partition key likely wins.

title: zm69.h11 followup: native intrusive layer list in h_layer_arena
description:
Path 4 (acct-xeee) closed the FIFO cost-attribution gap, matching A2 baseline at fan_out (35,635 vs 37,400 transfers/s). At fan_in g=1, path 4 lands at 15,753 transfers/s — significantly above paths 1/2/3 (40x/12x wins) but ~2.3x below fan_out on the same hardware.

Root cause: path 4 issues one SPI 'SELECT layer_id, unit_cost FROM cost_layers_h_ext WHERE layer_group_id = ANY($1) ORDER BY born_at, layer_id' per batch. The query is correctly indexed but rows-per-group grow monotonically. At fan_in g=1 over 60s, ~290K layers accumulate in one group; the per-batch SPI fetch dominates.

Proposal: move layer ordering out of the durable table into a native intrusive linked list in h_layer_arena.
- HLBucket gains 'next_in_group: AtomicI64' (8 bytes; absorbed by existing _pad1).
- New HLGroupHead shmem region (one cell per active group, sized to expected concurrent-group count). Each cell holds head_layer_id + tail_layer_id under per-group spinlock.
- h_layer_create appends to its group's tail under the group spinlock (acquire-release).
- Path 4 phase 3 replaces the SPI SELECT with: lookup HLGroupHead per touched group, walk next_in_group pointers natively. Layer unit_cost can be cached on HLBucket directly so even unit_cost lookup stays in shmem.

Acceptance:
- bench_h_batched fan_in g=1 at 20w x 60s x b=1000 reaches >50K transfers/s (3x improvement over current 15,753).
- bench_h_batched fan_out g=5000 unchanged within noise band.
- h_ext_fifo_correctness_t1 passes with POC_TEST_FUNCTION=h_apply_batch_fifo.
- New T1 invariant: durable cost_layers_h_ext (born_at, layer_id) ordering matches intrusive list walk order per group.

Scope: native-only change in poc/ledger-extension/. No new migration; durable table unchanged. Path 4 wrapper updated to use intrusive walk. Bench harness unchanged.
design: Per-group head/tail pointers under per-group LWLock or atomic CAS. Cells append-only within a group's chain. The chain is never compacted in PoC; production GC (separate followup) handles tombstoning. The existing acct-xeee bench results doc has the design sketch under 'Mitigation path' in Limitations section 1.
notes: Blocked-by nothing; depends on path 4 (acct-xeee, closed). Surfaced 2026-05-14 from path 4 bench results-h-ext-path4-2026-05-14.md.

title: zm69.h11: H+ext path 4 — native batch FIFO wrapper (single FFI per batch)
description:
Single Rust extension function that takes the whole batch JSONB, walks shmem per-layer state natively, accumulates depletion + consumption records in Vec, bulk-INSERTs via 1-2 SPI calls at the end. Eliminates the plpgsql/SPI roundtrip overhead that bottlenecked paths 1/2/3 at 3-10K transfers/s vs A2's 37K.

## Architecture

Function: h_apply_batch_fifo(envelopes JSONB) -> VOID (or SETOF status).
- Native JSONB parse into Rust envelope structs.
- For each issue: enumerate layers of the group in receipt order (option A: one SPI per touched group to SELECT layer_id, unit_cost FROM cost_layers_h_ext WHERE group=X ORDER BY born_at, layer_id; option B: native intrusive linked list per group in shmem). Walk in order; per layer call h_layer_decrement-equivalent inline (no SPI — direct shmem CAS in the same function); accumulate depletion record on take.
- Bulk-INSERT depletions + consumptions via 1-2 SPI calls at end.
- XactCallback eager-apply + ABORT-reverse pattern already provided by h_layer_arena module (acct-1grr).

## Why this should match or beat A2

A2 (fifo.rs post_batch_fifo_maximal_F) is already 'single FFI + native batch walk + bulk SPI'. Path 4 substitutes A2's shadow ring + deferred replay with shmem per-layer CAS (correct by construction; no R-MB6 over-consume gap). No structural reason throughput should drop; one less ring walk (no shadow + replay second pass) suggests it could be faster.

## Correctness guarantee strictly stronger than A2

- A2 has the R-MB6 over-consume window (consume_from_head discards ConsumeResult at fifo.rs:1175-1179; two backends both write depletions against shadow-time slice state).
- Path 4 eager-applies via CAS atomically; the invariant cannot be violated by construction. fifo_overconsume_check_h_ext returns 0 rows under any concurrency.

## Trade-offs vs A2

- Eliminates the over-consume gap (the original zm69 driver).
- Loses A2's deferred-commit-apply model in favor of eager-apply + XactCallback reversal (matches sw4i M10.A2 pattern).
- Native code surface: probably half of fifo.rs (3,026 lines) because no shadow + replay machinery. Still substantial work.

## Acceptance

- Native fn h_apply_batch_fifo in ledger_extension (likely new module h_batch_fifo or extension of h_layer_arena).
- Same correctness probe (tests/h_ext_fifo_correctness_t1.rs with POC_TEST_FUNCTION=post_batch_h_ext_native) — 80/80 commits, 0 overshoot, 0 drift.
- Bench at b=1000 g=5000, b=1000 g=1, b=100 g=50, b=10000 g=50 at 20 workers / 60s. Target: ≥ A2's 37K transfers/s at b=1000 g=5000.
- File correctness probe at the R-MB6 thin-layer shape that A2 fails (per fifo_rollback_correctness_t6.rs); path 4 should pass.

## Open design questions (decide during build, not before)

- Q1: layer enumeration — SPI-per-group vs native intrusive linked list. Lean SPI for first cut (simpler); switch to native list if benches show enumeration dominating.
- Q2: bulk INSERT shape — single multi-row INSERT vs prepared-statement loop. Likely multi-row INSERT via SPI with array-typed params.
- Q3: receipt-side shmem cell creation timing — eager at apply (matches issue-side) vs deferred to PRE_COMMIT (cheaper but breaks same-txn receipt→issue). Eager wins; same as h_layer_arena.
- Q4: error semantics on partial batch — single bad envelope aborts the whole batch (consistent with paths 1/2/3) vs per-envelope status row (matches A2). Lean single-batch-abort for simplicity.
- Q5: per-currency / per-cost-book partitioning of the shmem hash — out of scope at PoC; flag for production.

## bench/results-h-ext-paths-2026-05-14.md context

This is path 4 of the original three-path evaluation (paths 1/2/3 closed at acct-oh6l, acct-1grr, acct-xida). Findings doc explains why paths 1/2/3 failed perf bar despite passing correctness. Path 4 is the architecturally interesting answer — 'do what A2 does but with correctness fix from path 2'.
close_reason: Path 4 native batch FIFO shipped 2026-05-14 @ cac7916. Matches A2 baseline (35,635 vs 37,400 transfers/s at b=1000 g=5000 fan_out — within rig noise). Dominates paths 1/2/3 at every measured shape: 40x path 1 / 12x path 2 / 12x path 3 e2e at fan_in. Closes R-MB6 driver: correct-by-construction + append-only durable. Shmem residual is truth (path 2 pattern). 80/80 commits in concurrent correctness probe. See poc/batch-ledger/bench/results-h-ext-path4-2026-05-14.md for full numbers, design, and follow-ups.

title: zm69.h10: H+ext path 3 — deferred per-layer attribution (FIFO cost attribution)
description:
Hot path writes flat consumption rows with caller-supplied unit_cost (from h_arena_lookup-based WAC or constant). A bgworker (or SQL projector) later walks consumption rows in receipt order and computes per-layer depletion against cost_layers_h_ext. Hot path stays clean; FIFO attribution is eventually-consistent.

Acceptance:
- New mig with post_batch_h_ext_deferred wrapper (flat insert; no FIFO walk in hot path).
- New ledger_extension bgworker (or pure-SQL projector function) that drains pending consumption rows into cost_layer_depletions_h_ext per-layer in FIFO order.
- Bench at fan_in g=1 + fan_out g=5000 + thin-layer concurrent-issue shape; measure both hot-path throughput AND drain throughput.
- Correctness probe: after drain quiesces, SUM(depletions per layer_id) ≤ layer.qty_received.
- Lag metric: how stale can the projected per-layer state be under sustained load.

Trade-off this path makes: FIFO unit_cost is determined POST-COMMIT, not at issue time. Consumption row's unit_cost is the wrong-for-FIFO value (WAC or constant). True FIFO unit_cost lives only on cost_layer_depletions_h_ext rows. Audit semantics shift; whether this is acceptable depends on whether consumers (cost ledger postings, COGS reports) can wait for the projected view.

Why under acct-zm69: evaluating whether H+ext can replace A2 for full FIFO cost-flow. Path 3 of 3. May be the throughput winner but with the largest correctness-semantics change.
close_reason: All three paths implemented + tested + benched. Correctness clean across all paths under thin-layer concurrent-issue probe. Throughput gaps surfaced: path 1 4× under A2, path 2 ~30× under A2 (plpgsql LOOP overhead), path 3 end-to-end ~13× under A2 (drain bottleneck). Details in bench/results-h-ext-paths-2026-05-14.md and commit (next msg). Path 4 (native batch FIFO wrapper) is the architecturally interesting next step; will file as zm69.h11.

title: zm69.h9: H+ext path 2 — per-layer shmem residual (FIFO cost attribution)
description:
Extend h_arena (or sibling module in ledger_extension) with per-(group_id, layer_id) residual qty under shmem CAS. FIFO walk picks the oldest non-empty layer; CAS-decrements its residual; writes depletion row. Lock-free; closest A2 functional equivalent but without row-level Postgres lock contention.

Acceptance:
- New native module h_layer_arena (or extension of h_arena) — per-layer residual shmem hash, CAS-checked decrement, layer-ordering by receipt timestamp.
- New mig with post_batch_h_ext_layer_shmem wrapper.
- Bench at fan_in g=1 + fan_out g=5000 + thin-layer concurrent-issue shape.
- Correctness probe: SUM(cost_layer_depletions_h_ext.qty_consumed per layer_id) ≤ layer.qty_received under all concurrent shapes.
- Compare throughput to path 1 (FOR UPDATE walk) and path 3 (deferred).

Open question: how does FIFO ordering work in shmem? Receipt timestamp ordering requires sorted access; either maintain a per-group ordered list or scan all layers of a group at apply time. Initial implementation can scan; optimize if perf demands.

Why under acct-zm69: evaluating whether H+ext can replace A2 for full FIFO cost-flow. Path 2 of 3.
close_reason: All three paths implemented + tested + benched. Correctness clean across all paths under thin-layer concurrent-issue probe. Throughput gaps surfaced: path 1 4× under A2, path 2 ~30× under A2 (plpgsql LOOP overhead), path 3 end-to-end ~13× under A2 (drain bottleneck). Details in bench/results-h-ext-paths-2026-05-14.md and commit (next msg). Path 4 (native batch FIFO wrapper) is the architecturally interesting next step; will file as zm69.h11.

title: zm69.h8: H+ext path 1 — FOR UPDATE layer walk (FIFO cost attribution)
description:
Add per-layer FIFO cost attribution to H+ext via SELECT ... FOR UPDATE on cost_layers_h_ext rows in the wrapper. Locks each source layer row before computing depletion + cost. Closest analog to A2's existing shape; brings back A2-style row-level lock contention but only on the cost-walk path. Qty invariant still in shmem.

Acceptance:
- New mig with post_batch_h_ext_fifo_walk wrapper that walks layers FOR UPDATE per issue, writes cost_layer_depletions_h_ext rows with per-layer cost.
- Bench at fan_in g=1 + fan_out g=5000 + thin-layer concurrent-issue shape.
- Correctness probe: SUM(cost_layer_depletions_h_ext.qty_consumed per layer_id) ≤ layer.qty_received under all concurrent shapes. Use fifo_overconsume_check_h_ext().
- Compare throughput to plain H+ext (qty-only) and A2.

Why under acct-zm69: evaluating whether H+ext can replace A2 for full FIFO cost-flow, not just group qty invariant. Path 1 of 3 evaluated in parallel; pick winner based on perf + correctness.
close_reason: All three paths implemented + tested + benched. Correctness clean across all paths under thin-layer concurrent-issue probe. Throughput gaps surfaced: path 1 4× under A2, path 2 ~30× under A2 (plpgsql LOOP overhead), path 3 end-to-end ~13× under A2 (drain bottleneck). Details in bench/results-h-ext-paths-2026-05-14.md and commit (next msg). Path 4 (native batch FIFO wrapper) is the architecturally interesting next step; will file as zm69.h11.

title: zm69.h7: history-growth probe at ERP scale — verify trigger SUM stays sub-ms
description:
Per audit zm69.h0 caveat #2. PoC scale doesn't surface trigger SUM cost growth. ERP scale (months/years of consumption history per layer_group) would.

Bench:
- Pre-seed cost_consumptions with N rows per layer_group across 50 groups: N ∈ {100, 1K, 10K, 100K}.
- Run Regime 3 realistic at each N.
- Measure: trigger fire latency (p99) and overall committed/s.

title: zm69.h4: disambiguate trigger-raised 40001 from SSI 40001 (business vs concurrency)
description:
Per audit critical finding. H's check_no_overconsume trigger raises 40001 on TWO distinct conditions:
- Concurrency conflict (SSI's classic write-skew detection): retryable; the client should retry.
- Retroactive over-adjustment (business error: user tried to reverse a receipt that has already been consumed below the reversal qty): NOT retryable; client retry will keep failing.

The audit doc §Candidate H §Risks calls this out. Both currently surface as SQLSTATE 40001 which is wrong.

DESIGN:
- Add per-row check: if the violation is purely due to NEW row's qty + existing committed consumptions > existing layers qty (snapshot-isolated math without concurrent contributions), it's a business error. Raise SQLSTATE 'AC001' (custom) with a distinct message 'business: reversal exceeds available qty'.
- If the violation appears only when concurrent commits are merged into the snapshot (i.e., snapshot-effective qty >= 0, post-commit effective < 0), it's an SSI conflict. Raise SQLSTATE 40001 'serialization_failure'.
- The trigger can distinguish by re-running the SUM with explicit hint or by computing two separate views. Implementation TBD; could also be a separate AFTER trigger paired with the deferred one.

CLIENT:
- Retry loop catches 40001 → retry.
- AC001 → surface to application as business error, no retry.
