title: acct-e9tf sub 8: FIFO_N_BUCKETS graceful overflow — route to durable-only when no free cell
description:
When all FIFO_N_BUCKETS=16384 buckets are occupied with other keys and a new pool arrives, `insert_fifo_cell` returns None and `fifo_apply_batch_maximal` currently raises:

  pgrx::error!("FIFO arena full inserting pool_account_id={}", pool_account_id)

That aborts the whole batch with SQLSTATE XX000. This issue makes the surface graceful by routing that pool's apply through a durable-only path — same philosophy as acct-b8ub (sub 3) spill-to-durable for MAX_LAYERS.

## Design — runtime fallback

When `insert_fifo_cell` returns None for a pool:

1. The pool gets NO shmem cell. It is durable-only for the lifetime of the batch (and beyond, until arena occupancy drops and a future apply can claim a cell).
2. Receipts for that pool: INSERT cost_layers directly. No shmem push_layer / pending_drain.
3. Issues for that pool: SPI walks cost_layers WHERE pool_account_id = P AND qty_remaining > 0 ORDER BY receipt_date ASC, id ASC under FOR UPDATE; consume via existing `_fifo_walk_layers` helper; emit cost_layer_depletions; UPDATE qty_remaining inline.

This is the inline mutable `post_batch_fifo` path applied selectively to the unhosted pool, while other pools in the same batch stay on the fast shmem path.

## Implementation shape

Pre-scan extension in fifo_apply_batch_maximal Phase 4 (the EXCLUSIVE-insert phase): instead of `unwrap_or_else(|| pgrx::error!(...))`, on None mark the pool as `durable_only` in pool_to_cell mapping (use a sentinel like `usize::MAX` or a separate set). All later phases consult that mapping:

- Phase 7 (push receipt to ring): skip if durable_only.
- Phase 9c (INSERT cost_layers): always runs — unchanged.
- Phase 9d (consume_from_head): if durable_only, use a SPI consume helper instead.
- Phase 9e (drain): durable_only pools have no shmem state, so nothing to drain.

The Rust function gains a small inline-consume helper that walks cost_layers via SPI in FIFO order under FOR UPDATE — mirrors the body of the existing pure-SQL `post_batch_fifo` for the consume path.

## Cell-reclaim story (future polish, not in this issue)

A pool that hit no-cell at apply time may later get a cell when arena occupancy drops (other pools' cells get reclaimed). Two options:
- Manual: an operator-callable `fifo_reclaim_cells()` pg_extern walks pools-with-durable-state and tries to seed shmem cells.
- Automatic: extend the bgworker drain tick to opportunistically promote durable-only pools when free buckets exist.

Neither is in this issue's scope — `durable_only` is sticky per-batch (and across batches until the arena has room AND the pool's next apply triggers lazy-seed).

## Test plan

- T1: synthesize 16385 distinct pools in successive applies; verify the 16385th hits durable-only path; verify cost_layers state correct; recon clean.
- T2: mixed batch (one durable-only pool + N healthy pools) — verify segregated path; healthy pools at maximal_F tps.
- T3: bench: durable_only pool runs at inline-shape (~14K tps); arena-resident pools unaffected.

## Out of scope

- **Structural sizing fix**: GUC-tunable N_BUCKETS via `RequestAddinShmemSpace` + `ShmemInitStruct` refactor. Same hardening item also blocks acct-sw4i's HASH_TABLE. File as separate issue covering both arenas at once.
- **Cell reclaim**: post-MVP polish (see above).
- **MAX_LAYERS overflow**: that's acct-b8ub (sub 3).

## Status

Parked until a workload driver pushes active pool count past 16384. PoC bench shapes top out at 5000 pools.

## Sizing/calibration relationship

This issue handles the OVERFLOW behavior. Sizing the cap correctly so overflow doesn't happen in the first place is acct-ibib (FIFO arena sizing calibration). Both are needed; they don't substitute for each other.
close_reason: Shipped @ 59a6876. Phase 8.6 durable-only path + test helpers (fifo_force_arena_full / fifo_release_sentinels). 5/0/0 new tests + 40 prior FIFO tests still green. Mirrors sub 3 spill-to-durable philosophy at the bucket dimension.

title: FIFO arena sizing calibration — measure MAX_LAYERS / N_BUCKETS / PENDING_DRAIN_CAP from real workload trace
description:
The current FIFO arena defaults (poc/ledger-extension/src/fifo.rs) are PoC values fit to the 5000-pool fan-out synthetic bench:

  FIFO_N_BUCKETS    = 16384        # power-of-2; sized for ~30% load factor at 5K active pools
  MAX_LAYERS        = 256          # ~1.7x the 70/30 bench peak (~150 layers/pool)
  PENDING_DRAIN_CAP = 64           # vastly over-provisioned at PoC issue rates

Arena cost: ~117 MB at PG startup (shmem-resident, allocated once).

Before backporting the FIFO extension to a production acct deployment, calibrate the three knobs against a realistic workload trace.

## Procedure

Each knob targets a different workload statistic:

| Knob | Statistic | Formula |
|---|---|---|
| MAX_LAYERS | p99 across pools of max concurrent live layers | next_round_up(2 × p99) |
| PENDING_DRAIN_CAP | p95 of (issues/pool/tick × avg layers/issue) | next_round_up(4 × p95) |
| FIFO_N_BUCKETS | peak active pool count | next_pow2(peak_pools / α_target), α ∈ [0.25, 0.50] |

Live layer = qty_remaining > 0. Active pool = (sku, location, cost_book) with non-zero inventory.

## Measurement inputs

1. Run acct-1s6r mixed-workload load test (or successor) for a representative period (weekly cycle).
2. Snapshot hourly:
   - count(distinct pool_account_id) FROM cost_layers WHERE qty_remaining > 0   → peak_pools
   - per pool: max concurrent live-layer count (timeline from receipt insert + first-drain-to-0)  → p99_live_layers
   - per pool: issue rate × avg layers walked per issue (from cost_layer_depletions per-cell aggregation)  → p95_pending_per_tick
3. Fit the three formulas. Sanity-check arena_bytes = N_BUCKETS × (128 + 24×MAX_LAYERS + 16×PENDING_DRAIN_CAP) against memory budget (target <2% of shared_buffers).

## Sizing asymmetry to respect

MAX_LAYERS overflow is FATAL (pgrx::error! aborts batch) until spill-to-durable (acct-b8ub, parked) ships. PENDING_DRAIN_CAP overflow is GRACEFUL (falls back to inline UPDATE via accum_drain). Bias: be generous on MAX_LAYERS, be tight on PENDING_DRAIN_CAP.

If arena_bytes exceeds the budget after Step 3, prefer raising α_target (0.30 → 0.50) over trimming MAX_LAYERS. Long probe chains are slow but recoverable; hard cap breaches are not.

## When this matters

Only when the FIFO extension is on the path to production deployment. PoC defaults are fine for further bench / hardening work.

## Out of scope

- Variable-size layer storage (free-list pool) — alternative architecture, much more complex; file separately if structural memory becomes a problem at deployment scale.
- Tiered cells (small vs large by pool class) — same.
- GUC-tunable N_BUCKETS — requires refactor from pg_shmem_init! macro to raw RequestAddinShmemSpace + ShmemInitStruct; sw4i hardening territory (also useful for acct-sw4i HASH_TABLE which is similarly compile-time-sized).

title: acct-e9tf sub 3: MAX_LAYERS spill-to-durable on overflow
description:
When n_layers == MAX_LAYERS at receipt time, route the overflowing receipt directly to durable cost_layers, skipping shmem residency. The pool's ring keeps its current 256 in-shmem layers untouched; the new receipt lands in cost_layers only.

Issues consume in-shmem layers first (FIFO head-outward as today). After the in-shmem range is exhausted, fall through to SPI walking cost_layers in (receipt_date ASC, id ASC) order for the spilled tail.

Strict FIFO costing preserved at per-unit grain. No averaging, no precision loss.

Slow-path is paid only by the overflowing pool. Other pools stay on the fast shmem path.

## Design

### Receipt path on overflow

Phase 9c of fifo_apply_batch_maximal INSERTs all cost_layers rows regardless. The shmem push step (push_layer) is what fails today; on overflow, skip push_layer + skip pending_drain staging for that receipt but still INSERT the cost_layers row. The layer is durable-only.

### Issue path

Phase 9d consume_from_head walks the in-shmem ring. If shortage > 0 after the ring drains to n_layers=0, enter spill-fallback: SPI walks cost_layers WHERE pool_account_id = P AND qty_remaining > 0 ORDER BY receipt_date, id under FOR UPDATE; consume layers in order via _fifo_walk_layers (existing helper from the pre-shmem inline path); emit cost_layer_depletions rows; cap the issue when shortage reaches 0.

### Cell state machine

Add a per-cell flag `overflow_active: AtomicBool`. Set when first overflow receipt lands. While set:
- Future receipts ALWAYS go straight to cost_layers (don't try push_layer).
- Issues consume in-shmem first, then spill.

Cleared when in-shmem ring drains to n_layers=0 AND durable cost_layers count for the pool is also 0 (caught by the drain or recon path).

### Test plan

- T1: force receipt burst past 256 live layers; verify shmem cells stay capped at 256 + cost_layers grows beyond.
- T2: issue against spilled pool; verify in-shmem range consumed first, then spill range in FIFO order.
- T3: recon drift=0 across spill boundary (recon equation extends to count spill-tail).
- T4: bench: overflowing pool runs at inline-shape (~14K tps); healthy pools unaffected.

## Status

Parked. Gates on a workload driver pushing a real pool past 256 live layers. Current bench shapes (70/30 fan-out at 5000 pools) peak ~150 layers/pool.

## Out of scope

FIFO_N_BUCKETS overflow (no free cells for a new pool arriving when all 16384 buckets are occupied with other keys) is a separate hardening item; this issue covers MAX_LAYERS only.
close_reason: Shipped spill-to-durable per design: overflow_active flag + watermark on FifoBucket; Phase 8 receipt + lazy-seed cap at MAX_LAYERS and route durable-only; Phase 8.5 SPI walks cost_layers with id>=watermark FOR UPDATE for spill consume; recon adds shmem_spilled_qty + adjusted drift formula. Tests fifo_spill_to_durable_t1 (S1-S4, 4/0/0 in 47s). All prior FIFO + rollback tests pass on rebuilt .so. Commit d47f2cc.

title: FIFO maximal F (revised): per-cell LWLock tranche + synchronous apply
description:
Supersedes acct-nosj (closed). Architectural shift: move FIFO per-pool layer state into shmem. The revised design corrects three structural errors in the acct-nosj draft (incorrect locking primitive, incorrect apply timing, missing abort-handling strategy) and aligns with the existing acct-sw4i shmem philosophy.

## Why the rewrite vs acct-nosj

Per architectural review 2026-05-13 (in conversation):

| Aspect | acct-nosj (wrong) | This issue (correct) |
|---|---|---|
| Locking primitive | per-pool AtomicU8 spinlock | LWLock tranche w/ per-cell locks |
| Apply timing | A2-deferred via XactCallback / PENDING_STACK | Synchronous during batch function |
| Abort handling | Implicit (assumed A2 gives clean rollback) | Three explicit options; (a) shmem-as-cache + recon backstop, recommended |
| Layer storage | Slab + free-list, unbounded | Ring buffer per cell, MAX_LAYERS bounded; spill-to-durable on overflow |
| Posting_lines INSERT | External (SQL wrapper) | Internal to fifo_apply_batch (atomicity) |
| Deadlock prevention | (not addressed) | Sort cell-indices ascending before multi-cell acquisition |
| SPI under cell lock | (not addressed) | Pre-scan / pre-seed pattern; SPI happens outside cell locks |

The structural difference from acct-sw4i (balances) is:
- Balances: lock-free CAS on AtomicU128, deferred apply at commit (acceptable to return 0 mid-batch; the new last_seq is the deferred value).
- FIFO: per-cell exclusive LWLock (multi-step critical section: walk -> cost -> consume), synchronous apply during batch function (applied cost is the value going into posting_lines.amount — can't be deferred).

Everything else carries over: shmem-as-cache, durable-table-as-truth, bgworker drain to rollup, lazy seed from rollup on first touch, recon as drift backstop.

## Architectural design

### 1. Per-cell LWLock tranche

Setup in _PG_init: allocate a tranche ID via `LWLockNewTrancheId`, register tranche name `c"fifo_cell"`, allocate a fixed array `FifoLockArray { locks: [LWLockPadded; N_BUCKETS] }` in shmem. PG-integrated query-cancel, backend-death cleanup, deadlock detector all work.

Per-cell acquisition: wrapper `acquire_fifo_cell(idx, mode)` returns a Drop-guard that releases. Modes are `LW_SHARED` (read-only walk) and `LW_EXCLUSIVE` (apply path + drain layer-snapshot).

### 2. Cell layout — ring buffer per cell with MAX_LAYERS cap

```rust
const MAX_LAYERS: usize = 256;  // GUC-tunable; tune by workload
```

### 3. fifo_apply_batch internal flow

`fifo_apply_batch` is the SQL entry point. ONE pg_extern function. Internal flow:

1. Parse envelopes.
2. Group ops by item; compute cell index per item; sort indices ascending.
3. Pre-scan for lazy seeds: identify cells with `occupied == 0`; SPI-fetch from cost_layers rollup table (NO LOCKS HELD).
4. Phase 3 apply: in cell-index order, acquire each cell's LWLock EXCLUSIVE, apply ops (push_layer / consume_layers), release. Append applied (cost, qty) to results.
5. Bulk SPI: multi-row INSERT posting_lines (UNNEST), multi-row INSERT cost_layers (receipt drain), multi-row INSERT cost_layer_depletions. ALL POST-CELL-LOCK.
6. Return per-envelope results.

Step 4 + 5 separation is load-bearing: the lazy seed pattern (SPI before cell locks) plus the bulk-INSERT after cell locks keeps SPI work strictly outside cell locks.

### 4. Sorted cell-index acquisition prevents deadlock

Two concurrent batches touching the same set of cells will sort by cell index identically, acquire in identical order. Disjoint-cell batches don't contend. Same-cell batches serialize at cell granularity (acceptable — pool contention is the workload's intrinsic bottleneck).

### 5. Abort handling — option (a) shmem-as-cache + recon backstop (default)

The batch function mutates shmem synchronously and INSERTs posting_lines internally. If the user transaction aborts (e.g., constraint violation upstream), posting_lines rolls back (WAL) but shmem is wrong. Next access reconciles via recon path against posting_lines truth.

Add a background recon job that auto-corrects drift in cells not touched recently.

If abort-induced drift turns out common in production, escalate to option (b): per-backend undo log with OCC validation at restore time. Skip option (c) unless workloads have very short batches + acceptable per-item blocking.

### 6. Overflow handling — spill-to-durable

When n_layers == MAX_LAYERS at receipt time, the overflowing receipt goes directly to durable cost_layers, skipping shmem. The pool's in-shmem ring keeps its current 256 layers; the new layer is durable-only. Issues consume in-shmem layers first (FIFO head-outward as today); after the in-shmem range exhausts, fall through to SPI walking cost_layers in (receipt_date ASC, id ASC) order for the spilled tail. Strict FIFO at per-unit grain preserved. Slow-path paid only by the overflowing pool. Detail in acct-b8ub (sub 3).

### 7. Bgworker drain — extends existing ledger_drain

Each tick:
1. Walk cells under HASH_TABLE.share(); identify dirty cells via atomic `last_seq > drained_seq` (no cell-lock acquisition).
2. For each dirty cell: acquire cell LWLock EXCLUSIVE briefly, snapshot layers, release.
3. Bulk SPI UPSERT to durable cost_layers (set-based per tick via UNNEST).

### 8. Crash recovery — lazy seed from cost_layers

On PG restart, shmem is empty. First per-cell access triggers the pre-scan SPI seed (step 3 of batch flow). Mirrors acct-sw4i's M6 pattern.

### 9. Recon extension

ledger_shmem_recon extended with per-cell layer check:
- SUM(layers[].qty) per cell vs SUM(cost_layers.qty_remaining) per pool from durable rows.
- Drift = 0 at drain quiescence.

## Sub-issue breakdown

1. **LWLock tranche + cell layout** (~2-3 days, acct-0agz, CLOSED): _PG_init setup, FifoLockArray, acquire_fifo_cell helper, FifoBucket layout. Tests for lock acquisition / release / multi-cell sorted acquisition / deadlock detector integration.

2. **fifo_apply_batch (no SPI inside cell locks)** (~2-3 days, acct-uy4p, CLOSED): parse, group, sort, pre-scan SPI seed, apply under cell locks, bulk-INSERT outside. Returns per-envelope (cost, qty). Tests for FIFO correctness + atomic apply.

3. **MAX_LAYERS spill-to-durable** (acct-b8ub, OPEN — parked): receipt overflow routes to durable cost_layers; issues spill-fallback walks cost_layers in receipt order via SPI. Strict per-unit FIFO preserved.

4. **bgworker drain extension** (~1-2 days, acct-0450, CLOSED): dirty-cell scan via last_seq > drained_seq, briefly take cell LWLock for snapshot, bulk SPI UPSERT to cost_layers. Test for I4 (drain quiescence drift=0).

5. **Crash recovery (lazy seed)** (~1 day, acct-u324, CLOSED): first-access SPI seed from cost_layers. Test for I5 (kill bgworker + restart container).

6. **Recon extension** (~0.5-1 day, acct-6g2u, CLOSED): per-cell layer check in fifo_arena_recon. Property test.

7. **Bench sweep** (~0.5 day, acct-ylmo, CLOSED): 3-replicate sweep vs mutable + L-accounts + (probably) inline-no-shmem (acct-vh5y) as upper-bound reference.

## Correctness invariants

- **I1**: Receipt at txn T's commit appends EXACTLY ONE Layer to its cell's ring (or to durable cost_layers if spilled). Rollback: layers state unchanged, but shmem may drift (recon catches).
- **I2**: Issue at txn T's commit decrements layers in strict FIFO order (head outward), spilling to durable cost_layers walk in receipt order after in-shmem range exhausts.
- **I3**: Two concurrent issues on the same cell serialize via cell LWLock.
- **I4**: After drain quiescence, SUM(Layer.qty in shmem) + SUM(pending_drain qty_consumed) per cell matches SUM(cost_layers.qty_remaining) per pool. With spill active: per-pool invariant extends to include spilled-durable-only layers.
- **I5**: After PG restart, first per-cell access lazy-seeds matching durable state.
- **I6**: Multi-cell batches with disjoint items run in parallel; same-item batches serialize.
- **I7**: Per-unit FIFO costing is preserved across the spill boundary — issues consume in-shmem head before any durable spill-tail row.

## Bench expectations

Per acct-t59i regression analysis and acct-ylmo sweep:
- Headline (acct-ylmo, MAX_LAYERS=256, 70/30 fan-out): 40,824 tps median (3.44x inline, 52x mutable).
- Zero deadlocks across 15 replicate runs.
- Spill path (when active for a pool): expected to degrade that pool to ~inline-shape (~14K tps); healthy pools unaffected.

## Risks

- LWLock tranche initialization timing (pg_shmem_init vs LWLockNewTrancheId) requires shmem_startup_hook in some PG versions. Test on PG18 specifically.
- SPI under cell lock is a foot-gun. Pre-scan pattern enforced in code review.
- Crash recovery race: first-access from multiple backends could double-seed. CAS on `occupied` flag gates seed.

## Scope

10-14 days wall, comparable to acct-sw4i M1-M9.

## Files

Crate: poc/ledger-extension (extends existing).
New types: FifoLockArray, FifoBucket.
New pg_externs: fifo_apply_batch.
Extension to bgworker: ledger_drain.
Mig in poc/batch-ledger/db/migrations for SQL entry-point exposure.

## Status of open questions

- N_BUCKETS for FIFO arena: 16384, same as acct-sw4i (locked in at sub 1).
- MAX_LAYERS default: 256 (bumped from 64 in acct-ylmo follow-up at 6dfc4e6).
- FIFO_N_BUCKETS overflow (no free cells for new pool): separate hardening item, not yet filed.
close_reason: All 8 sub-issues shipped. PoC FIFO arena complete: per-cell LWLock tranche (sub 1), pgrx apply path (sub 2), MAX_LAYERS spill-to-durable (sub 3), bgworker drain half-α (sub 4), crash-recovery lazy-seed (sub 5), per-cell recon (sub 6), bench sweep (sub 7), FIFO_N_BUCKETS graceful overflow durable-only (sub 8). Both layer-dimension and bucket-dimension overflow paths in place; arena saturation no longer aborts batches.

title: FIFO pre-F probe: inline-no-shmem fifo_apply_batch
description:
Cheap measurement (~1 day) to isolate the dispatcher+CTE-wrapper cost from the durable-WAL cost in FIFO maximal designs. Informs whether `acct-nosj-v2` (shmem-LayerArena F revised) is worth the ~10-14 day investment.

## Motivation

acct-t59i's L-accounts bench (committed at a0fec3c) showed mig 0022 was 8-17× slower than mig 0020 mutable, with FOR UPDATE cardinality matched. The dominant cost was per-batch CPU in `ledger_dispatch_fifo_batch` (Rust pg_extern with TableIterator) + 7-CTE plpgsql wrapper marshaling ~7K rows out and chaining them through CTE-based INSERTs.

This raises the load-bearing question for F: does removing the dispatcher+CTE wrapper alone recover the win, or is per-batch durable-write cost (posting_lines + cost_layers + cost_layer_depletions ~2900 row writes/batch) the actual ceiling? F-shmem helps if the answer is the former; F-shmem won't help much if the answer is the latter.

## Design

Write `fifo_apply_batch_inline` as the SQL entry point. ONE Rust pg_extern function (no plpgsql wrapper, no CTE chain). Internally:

1. Parse envelopes (JSONB → Vec<Op>).
2. Pre-scan: SPI fetch active cost_layers for all touched issue-pools (one query). Build pool→Vec<LayerRec> map in plain Rust (no shmem, no LWLocks — just an in-function HashMap).
3. Walk envelopes: per receipt, append to map; per issue, walk FIFO + decrement.
4. SPI multi-row INSERT for posting_lines (single statement, UNNEST(ARRAY[...])).
5. SPI multi-row INSERT for new cost_layers (receipt rows) RETURNING ids.
6. SPI multi-row INSERT for cost_layer_depletions.
7. SPI multi-row UPDATE for pre-existing cost_layers qty_remaining (UPDATE FROM unnest).
8. Return per-envelope results.

Same FOR UPDATE accounts.id pattern at the top (mirrors mig 0020 / mig 0022).

## Acceptance

1. Mig 0023 ships `fifo_apply_batch_inline` (separate name, sibling to fifo_apply_batch_maximal — keeps mig 0022 around for comparison).
2. T1-T5 from tests/fifo_shmem_correctness_maximal_t1.rs adapted to route through new function — all 5 cases green.
3. Bench sweep (3 reps × 60s × 4 cells: fan-in mutable / fan-in inline / fan-out mutable / fan-out inline).
4. Update bench/results-shmem-fifo-maximal.md with inline numbers.

## Decision branches

| Inline fan-out tps | Read |
|---|---|
| < 200 (i.e., still much slower than mutable's 793) | Bottleneck is somewhere weirder than expected; investigate before F. |
| 500-1500 (mutable parity ± 2×) | Dispatcher+CTE wrapper WAS the L-accounts regression. Per-batch durable writes are the ceiling. F's shmem-native lift over inline would be modest (2× at best). F's 10-14 days probably not worth it. |
| 1500-5000 (3-6× mutable) | Inline is the architectural win; shmem on top brings extra lift but the bulk of the win is from eliminating the wrapper. F's projection holds; go. |
| > 5000 (lift saturated) | Surprising result; reproduce + investigate. |

The 500-1500 band is the most likely outcome IMO — eliminates the marshaling overhead but durable WAL is still per-row.

## Scope

~1 day wall. Single migration + dispatcher edit (or new fn) + adapt T1-T5 + 12-run bench sweep.

## Risk

Low. Reuses existing test harness, bench script, FIFO algorithm. The Rust function is structurally simpler than mig 0022's dispatcher (no TableIterator, no plpgsql plumbing — just SPI INSERTs).

## Files

- New: poc/batch-ledger/db/migrations/0023_fifo_apply_batch_inline.up.sql
- New: poc/ledger-extension/src/lib.rs::fifo_apply_batch_inline pg_extern
- New: poc/batch-ledger/tests/fifo_apply_batch_inline_t1.rs (T1-T5 adapted)
- Modified: poc/batch-ledger/bench/run-fifo-maximal-sweep.sh (add inline cells)
- Modified: poc/batch-ledger/bench/results-shmem-fifo-maximal.md (probe addendum)

title: FIFO maximal F — shmem-cached LayerArena (FIFO-native shmem path)
description:
Architectural shift: move FIFO per-pool layer state into shmem (mirroring acct-sw4i's WAC approach). Durable `cost_layers` becomes the bgworker drain target rather than the live read/write source. Brings FIFO into the same shmem-native model as WAC maximal; eliminates row-level FOR UPDATE on `cost_layers` as a serialization point.

## Motivation

acct-oqje surfaced a structural regression in the row-locked maximal design (`acct-lhgh`):

| Shape   | Mutable (mig 0020) | Maximal-FOR-UPDATE (mig 0021) |
|---------|--------------------|-------------------------------|
| fan-in  | 313 tps            | **36 tps**                    |
| fan-out | 631 tps            | **34 tps**                    |

FIFO's per-pool state is structurally different from WAC's:
- **WAC**: scalar per-pool state (running avg value + qty). Fits one shmem cell. Per-cell AtomicU128 CAS gives lock-free updates. acct-2g9w achieved 1.28×/5.24× lift.
- **FIFO**: ordered list of layers per pool. Does NOT fit a single fixed-size shmem cell.

L-accounts (`acct-t59i`) is the smaller-scope alternative — keep durable cost_layers but move serialization to account-level FOR UPDATE. It's correct but caps throughput at the account-lock-serialization ceiling.

F is the architectural answer: per-pool layer queue lives in shmem. Lock-free reads via per-bucket spinlock. Drain to durable cost_layers via bgworker. Crash recovery via lazy-load on PG restart.

## Architectural design

### 1. LayerArena — variable-length per-pool layer queues in shmem

New shmem region, parallel to the existing cell hash table:

```rust
struct LayerArenaHeader {
    free_head: AtomicU32,           // free-list of available LayerRec slots
    capacity: u32,                  // total slots
    occupied: AtomicU32,             // current allocated count
}

struct LayerRec {
    // 64 bytes — 1 cache line
    pool_id: AtomicI64,             // back-pointer for drain (sanity check)
    layer_id: AtomicI64,            // durable cost_layers.id, or NEGATIVE sentinel
    qty_remaining: AtomicI64,
    unit_cost: AtomicI64,
    receipt_date_epoch: AtomicU32,  // days since epoch, for FIFO ordering
    next_slot: AtomicU32,            // next-in-queue index, or U32_MAX for tail
    flags: AtomicU8,                 // bit 0: durable (drained to cost_layers)
    _pad: [u8; 19],
}
```

Per-pool head/tail pointers stored in an extension to the existing cell hash table (one new column in `Bucket`, or a parallel hash):

```rust
struct PoolLayerQueue {
    head_slot: AtomicU32,            // first LayerRec, or U32_MAX if empty
    tail_slot: AtomicU32,            // last LayerRec
    queue_lock: AtomicU8,            // 0 = unlocked, 1 = locked (queue-level spinlock)
}
```

Slot allocator: open-addressed free-list. `free_head` points to first free slot; each free slot's `next_slot` points to next free slot. Allocation: atomic CAS pop from free_head. Deallocation: atomic CAS push to free_head.

### 2. A2-compliant staging path (PENDING_STACK extension)

Receipts append to per-pool queue at commit (deferred via XactCallback like acct-17vr).
Issues pop from per-pool queue at commit, decrementing qty_remaining via CAS.
Both go through PENDING_STACK so SAVEPOINT rollback discards the change.

Extension to PendingEntry — add:
```rust
enum PendingOp {
    BalanceDelta { account_id, period_id, currency_id, ledger_kind, amount_delta, qty_delta },
    LayerAppend  { pool_id, layer_id_or_sentinel, qty, unit_cost, receipt_date },
    LayerDeplete { pool_id, layer_slot, qty_consumed },
}
```

Commit callback walks the pending ops in order, applying each to shmem. Same atomicity guarantees as acct-4e91.

### 3. Receipt path

```rust
fn ledger_layer_append(pool_id, layer_id, qty, unit_cost, receipt_date_epoch) {
    PENDING_STACK[top].push(LayerAppend { ... });
}
```

At commit:
1. Allocate slot from free-list (CAS pop free_head).
2. Initialize LayerRec atomic stores.
3. Acquire queue_lock for the pool.
4. Append slot to tail; update tail_slot CAS.
5. Release queue_lock.

### 4. Issue path

```rust
fn ledger_layer_drain(pool_id, qty_needed) -> Vec<(layer_slot, take, cost)> {
    // Read-only walk (no PENDING yet); returns plan.
    // At commit, PENDING_STACK[top].push(LayerDeplete { ... }) per consumed layer.
}
```

At commit:
1. Acquire queue_lock for the pool.
2. Walk queue from head; for each layer: CAS-decrement qty_remaining by `take`.
3. If qty_remaining reaches 0, mark `flags.bit_drained = 1` (signals bgworker to free the slot).
4. Release queue_lock.

Note: the queue_lock is per-pool, not global. Concurrent writers on different pools don't contend.

### 5. Bgworker drain

Extension of `ledger_drain` (the existing bgworker):

Every tick:
1. Walk LayerArena. For each LayerRec with `flags.dirty = 1`:
   - If layer_id is NEGATIVE (in-batch sentinel): INSERT INTO cost_layers RETURNING id; update LayerRec.layer_id with real id; clear sentinel.
   - If layer_id is POSITIVE: UPDATE cost_layers SET qty_remaining = LayerRec.qty_remaining WHERE id = layer_id.
2. For each LayerRec with `flags.drained = 1` (issue fully consumed) AND drained_to_durable = 1: free the slot back to free_head.

INSERTs and UPDATEs done set-based per tick via UNNEST(ARRAY[...]).

### 6. Crash recovery

On PG restart:
1. LayerArena is reset (shmem doesn't persist).
2. First `ledger_layer_drain` or `ledger_layer_append` for a pool triggers lazy-load:
   - SPI: `SELECT id, qty_remaining, unit_cost, receipt_date FROM cost_layers WHERE pool_account_id = $1 AND qty_remaining > 0 ORDER BY receipt_date, id`
   - Allocate slots, populate LayerRecs, build per-pool queue.
3. Subsequent ops proceed against shmem.

Mirrors M6's WAC lazy-load pattern.

### 7. Recon extension

`ledger_shmem_recon` extended with a layer-pool check:

For each pool with active layers in shmem:
- SUM(LayerRec.qty_remaining) per pool, vs:
- SUM(cost_layers.qty_remaining) per pool from durable rows, adjusted for in-flight (un-drained) layers.
- Drift = 0 at quiescence (after drain ticks settle).

## Correctness invariants (to pin in tests)

- **I1**: A receipt at txn T's commit appends EXACTLY ONE LayerRec to its pool's queue. Rollback: no LayerRec appended.
- **I2**: An issue at txn T's commit decrements LayerRecs in strict FIFO order (head-to-tail). Rollback: all decrements undone.
- **I3**: Two concurrent txns issuing from the same pool serialize via the per-pool queue_lock. Each sees a consistent FIFO snapshot at lock acquire time.
- **I4**: After drain quiescence, SUM(LayerRec.qty_remaining) per pool == SUM(cost_layers.qty_remaining WHERE qty_remaining > 0) per pool.
- **I5**: Crash recovery: on PG restart followed by a same-pool access, LayerArena state matches the durable cost_layers state for that pool.
- **I6**: Slot allocation never returns an in-use slot (free_head CAS correctness).
- **I7**: Per-pool queue ordering: head → tail traversal yields LayerRecs in receipt_date order (FIFO).

## Sub-issues (file at claim time, not now)

Sub 1: shmem LayerArena scaffold — header, slab, free-list, per-pool queue pointers, allocation/dealloc CAS primitives. Tests for I6.

Sub 2: A2 staging extension — PendingOp::LayerAppend / LayerDeplete in PENDING_STACK; XactCallback commit-time application. Tests for I1, I2 (receipt + rollback, issue + rollback).

Sub 3: receipt path — `ledger_layer_append` pg_extern; commit-time queue append. Tests for I7.

Sub 4: issue path — `ledger_layer_drain` pg_extern; commit-time queue decrement under queue_lock. Tests for I3 (concurrent issues; FIFO consistency).

Sub 5: bgworker drain — extend `ledger_drain` to flush LayerArena to cost_layers. Tests for I4 at quiescence.

Sub 6: crash recovery — lazy-load from cost_layers on first per-pool access. Tests for I5 (kill bgworker / restart container scenarios).

Sub 7: dispatcher integration — `ledger_dispatch_fifo_batch` v2 emits LayerAppend / LayerDeplete instead of cost_layers writes; SQL wrapper drops layer INSERTs (bgworker handles them). Re-run full correctness tests (T1-T5 from acct-m6q3).

Sub 8: 3-replicate bench sweep — same harness as acct-oqje; expected lift in WAC-shape band.

Sub 9: recon extension — add layer-pool check to `ledger_shmem_recon`. Property test.

## Test strategy

- **Correctness pinning per sub**: each sub closes with property tests pinning its I-invariants.
- **End-to-end (Sub 7)**: T1-T5 from `tests/fifo_shmem_correctness_maximal_t1.rs` route through the new path. Drift=0 after drain quiescence in T5 (8-writer fan-in).
- **Crash recovery (Sub 6)**: container-restart test similar to acct-e5gl's pattern.
- **Workload property tests**: random sequences of receipts + issues + rollbacks, verifying I1-I7 hold.

## Bench expectations

If the WAC shape transfers (which is the design hypothesis):

| Shape | Mutable | Maximal-L target | F target |
|---|---|---|---|
| fan-in  |   313 tps |  500-1500 |  20-50K (WAC: 71K) |
| fan-out |   631 tps | 3000-8000 |  50-100K (WAC: 59K) |

F's fan-in target is LOWER than WAC because per-pool queue_lock is exclusive (one writer per pool at a time), whereas WAC's CAS is fully lock-free at the cell level. Fan-out should approach WAC throughput because writers spread across distinct pools.

## Scope estimate

10-14 days wall, comparable to acct-sw4i (~3 weeks at half-time pace for WAC's M1-M9 milestones).

Phase breakdown:
- Sub 1-2: 3-4 days (shmem layout + A2 integration; highest design risk)
- Sub 3-4: 2 days (path implementations; medium risk)
- Sub 5: 1-2 days (bgworker drain; low risk, pattern exists)
- Sub 6: 1 day (lazy-load; pattern exists)
- Sub 7: 2 days (dispatcher rewrite + correctness re-test)
- Sub 8: 0.5 day (bench)
- Sub 9: 0.5 day (recon)

## Risks

- **Variable-size per-pool list in fixed-size shmem region** drives the slab allocator design. If a few pools have many layers (>100) and most have few, slab fragmentation could be costly. Mitigation: cap LayerArena at e.g. 1M slots; raise P0099-style error if exhausted; bgworker drains aggressively.
- **A2 atomicity** — receipt+issue rollback must perfectly undo. Edge case: a receipt's LayerAppend is staged, then an issue in the same txn consumes from it via LayerDeplete. Rollback must undo BOTH consistently.
- **Per-pool queue_lock contention** — fan-in (1 pool, 20 writers) still serializes. Better than mutable's account-lock serialization only by the avoided heap-row-locking + faster spin-lock acquisition. Final lift in fan-in is uncertain; may be 2-5×, not 10-50×.
- **Crash recovery durability gap** — between a commit and the next bgworker drain tick (default 100ms), shmem holds state not yet in durable cost_layers. A crash in this window LOSES the layer state. Same durability gap as acct-sw4i's M10.A2 design; acceptable for PoC, NOT for production. Production requires WAL custom record (M10 future work, currently OUT of M10 scope per acct-tpqw).

## Decision relationship to L-accounts (`acct-t59i`)

- If L-accounts ships and matches mutable's correctness while exceeding its perf: F becomes optional. Pursue only if FIFO needs full shmem-native parity with WAC.
- If L-accounts ships and reveals account-level serialization is the ceiling (no meaningful lift): F is the only path forward.
- L-accounts is a half-day spike; F is a 2-week epic. Cost-rational to ship L-accounts first.

## Out of scope

- Production-grade WAL crash safety (acct-tpqw deferred).
- LayerArena memory-bound contracts under adversarial inputs (acct-16kr — though F's design provides natural caps via the slab capacity).
- Multi-database LayerArena (single drain_database GUC inherited from acct-sw4i).
- Lot / serial integration (E2/E3 territory; separate epics).
notes: Deferred to acct-e9tf (FIFO maximal F revised). acct-nosj design had three structural errors surfaced in review 2026-05-13: (1) AtomicU8 spinlock is wrong primitive — LWLock tranche is correct (cancel/deadlock integration); (2) A2-deferred apply is wrong for FIFO — applied cost goes into posting_lines.amount, must be synchronous; (3) abort-handling not addressed — shmem-as-cache + recon backstop is right philosophy. acct-e9tf supersedes with corrections + sorted cell-index acquisition, lazy-seed pre-pass, ring buffer + coalescing. acct-e9tf is blocked-on acct-vh5y (inline-no-shmem probe ~1 day) which gates whether F's 10-14 day investment is justified.

title: L-accounts — wrapper FOR UPDATE accounts.id; drop FOR UPDATE on cost_layers
description:
Alternative to acct-lhgh's maximal design: keep the Rust dispatcher (`ledger_dispatch_fifo_batch`) + single-CTE wrapper architecture from acct-m6q3, but move serialization from row-level FOR UPDATE on `cost_layers` to wrapper-level FOR UPDATE on `accounts.id`. Mirrors mig 0020 mutable's serialization model exactly — no new correctness contract introduced.

## Motivation

acct-oqje bench surfaced an 8-18× regression vs mutable when the maximal dispatcher pre-locks all active layers under FOR UPDATE on cost_layers:

| Shape   | Mutable | Maximal (current) |
|---------|---------|-------------------|
| fan-in  | 313 tps | **36 tps**        |
| fan-out | 631 tps | **34 tps**        |

Root cause: mutable's FOR UPDATE on `accounts.id` locks ~3 rows per batch (pool + AP + COGS). Maximal's FOR UPDATE on `cost_layers` locks ~5 × N pools = thousands of rows per batch in fan-out. Per-batch lock acquisition cost overwhelms the Rust HashMap walk + set-based INSERT win.

## Correctness model

**Identical to mig 0020 mutable** — no new contract:

- Any FIFO write necessarily touches the pool account (pool is the credit account on `fifo_issue`, debit on `fifo_receipt`).
- `FOR UPDATE accounts.id` on the pool row, taken at the start of the wrapper, serializes all concurrent FIFO writes against that pool.
- Within the serialized region, the dispatcher reads `cost_layers` via a plain SELECT — snapshot is internally consistent for the duration of the wrapper's txn.
- Receipts append new layers via INSERT; issues UPDATE qty_remaining via the CTE chain. All under the same accounts lock.

Anybody else writing to cost_layers MUST also acquire FOR UPDATE on the pool account first (the existing mutable function does; no new code paths exist). The serialization point is the account, enforced by Postgres' row-level lock, NOT a contract that "writers must go through this function."

## Design changes vs current acct-m6q3 (mig 0021)

### 1. Wrapper takes FOR UPDATE on touched pool accounts

At the top of `post_batch_fifo_maximal`, add a CTE (or PERFORM in plpgsql; sticking with SQL preferred):

```sql
WITH touched_pools AS (
    SELECT DISTINCT pool_id FROM (
        SELECT (e->>'debit_account_id')::BIGINT  AS pool_id
          FROM jsonb_array_elements(p_envelopes) e
         WHERE e->>'kind' = 'fifo_receipt'
        UNION
        SELECT (e->>'credit_account_id')::BIGINT AS pool_id
          FROM jsonb_array_elements(p_envelopes) e
         WHERE e->>'kind' = 'fifo_issue'
    ) p
),
pool_locks AS (
    SELECT a.id FROM accounts a
    JOIN touched_pools t ON a.id = t.pool_id
    ORDER BY a.id
    FOR UPDATE
),
input AS (...),
...
```

The `pool_locks` CTE acquires FOR UPDATE on every pool account before the dispatcher runs. The ORDER BY a.id is critical for deadlock-freedom (consistent locking order across writers).

LANGUAGE sql wrappers cannot use `FOR UPDATE` in CTEs directly inside an SQL function. May need to switch wrapper to LANGUAGE plpgsql (one PERFORM ... FOR UPDATE at the top, then run the existing CTE chain). Acceptable trade-off; per-batch plpgsql overhead is negligible vs the lock acquisition savings.

### 2. Drop FOR UPDATE from the Rust dispatcher's SPI

`ledger_dispatch_fifo_batch` changes its SPI query from:

```sql
SELECT ... FROM cost_layers cl
WHERE cl.pool_account_id = ANY($1::bigint[]) AND cl.qty_remaining > 0
ORDER BY cl.pool_account_id, cl.receipt_date, cl.id
FOR UPDATE
```

to:

```sql
SELECT ... FROM cost_layers cl
WHERE cl.pool_account_id = ANY($1::bigint[]) AND cl.qty_remaining > 0
ORDER BY cl.pool_account_id, cl.receipt_date, cl.id
```

(drop the `FOR UPDATE` and switch back to `client.select` from `client.update` — `Spi::connect` instead of `Spi::connect_mut` works again since FOR UPDATE is gone).

### 3. Everything else stays

- Two-output-stream design (`row_kind ∈ {leg, depl}`)
- Sentinel→real_layer_id resolution in the wrapper
- `in_batch_drain` / `pre_existing_drain` split
- All 5 correctness tests (T1-T5)

## Acceptance

1. Mig 0022 (new file; mig 0021 stays installed) — `post_batch_fifo_maximal_v2` (or rename via DROP+CREATE; tbd at claim time) with pool-account FOR UPDATE at the top.
2. `ledger_dispatch_fifo_batch` SPI swap: drop FOR UPDATE.
3. Re-run `tests/fifo_shmem_correctness_maximal_t1.rs` — all 5 cases green.
4. Re-run acct-oqje's bench sweep (4 cells, 3 replicates × 60s).
5. Update `bench/results-shmem-fifo-maximal.md` with new numbers.

## Expected bench outcome

If correct, maximal should now MATCH or BEAT mutable at both shapes (Rust HashMap + set-based CTE wins without the row-lock overhead):

| Shape | Mutable | Maximal-L target |
|---|---|---|
| fan-in  |   313 tps |   500-1500 tps  (1.5-5×) |
| fan-out |   631 tps | 3000-8000 tps  (5-13×, WAC-shape lift) |

If maximal-L is NOT meaningfully faster than mutable, the bottleneck was never the dispatcher's per-envelope cost — it was always the account-level serialization itself. That finding would be load-bearing for the F-shmem path's value proposition.

## Scope estimate

Half a day. Single migration file + dispatcher SPI swap + re-test + re-bench.

## Risks

- **LANGUAGE sql → plpgsql wrapper**: probably needs the switch to use FOR UPDATE inside the function body. Adds ~minor per-batch plpgsql overhead but should be negligible vs the lock acquisition savings.
- **Deadlock risk if ORDER BY missing**: the `ORDER BY a.id` is load-bearing. Writers locking pool accounts in different orders would deadlock. Test in T5 (multi-writer fan-in already covers this).

## Relationship to acct-FIFO-SHMEM (F)

L-accounts is a smaller, durable-row-model fix that keeps `cost_layers` as the canonical truth. F is the architectural shift to shmem-native FIFO (LayerArena in shmem, drain to cost_layers).

If L-accounts succeeds (matches or beats mutable), F becomes optional — pursued only if FIFO needs the same lock-free hot-path characteristics as WAC.

If L-accounts fails (no lift), F is the only path forward.

title: PoC Rust dispatcher memory-bound contracts + adversarial testing
description:
Both shipped + planned PoC Rust dispatchers (acct-2g9w ledger_dispatch_wac_batch; FIFO maximal ledger_dispatch_fifo_batch) allocate transient state through Rust's system allocator. PG's memory accounting (work_mem, temp_buffers, MemoryContext) does NOT see these allocations. The only ceiling is RSS + OS OOM-killer.

For PoC bench shapes this is fine. For production-realistic workloads with adversarial inputs (pathologically long active-layer lists per pool, deep subxact nesting, very large batch sizes, unique-key explosion) it's a real concern.

## Scope

1. Derive a soft cap per-dispatcher from PG config knobs:
     dispatcher_cap = min(
       work_mem × budget_fraction,
       total_ram × global_fraction / max_connections
     )
   Read once at first call per backend; cache.

2. Pre-flight aggregate check before SPI fetch: count active-layer rows (FIFO) or distinct keys (WAC) the batch would touch; project bytes; raise P0099 (or similar) if exceeds cap. Error message names the exact byte estimate + which knob to raise to admit the batch.

3. Cover all current dispatchers:
   - ledger_dispatch_wac_batch (acct-2g9w) — HashMap<i64, (i64, i64)>, trivial at PoC scale but uniform discipline.
   - ledger_dispatch_fifo_batch (FIFO maximal, when shipped) — HashMap<i64, Vec<LayerRec>>, the load-bearing case.
   - PENDING_STACK growth on unique-key-explosion txns (bulk backfill scenarios).

4. Document the formula + reasoning in poc/ledger-extension/MEMORY_BUDGET.md (or extend INVARIANTS.md).

## Adversarial testing scenarios

- Pathological active-layer counts (10K+ per pool) — verify cap fires before OOM.
- Deep subxact nesting (50+ frames).
- Large batches (batch=100,000+).
- Unique-key explosion across one txn (single backend touching 100K distinct cells).
- Hash table near saturation (N_BUCKETS at >70% load factor — this is the existing acct-togd N_BUCKETS GUC followup territory).

## Dependencies / sequencing

- FIFO maximal (acct-lhgh) should ship first so the load-bearing case has a concrete shape to test against.
- This epic's sub-issues filed at claim time, not now (per user direction).

## Out of scope (file as follow-ups if needed)

- Custom Rust allocator backing HashMap with palloc/pfree (would put allocations under PG MemoryContext accounting). Requires unstable allocator_api or manual unsafe wrappers; substantial pgrx work.
- N_BUCKETS GUC-sizing for the shmem hash table — already tracked separately under acct-togd-followup.
- True memory pressure response (eviction, spill-to-disk). Out of scope for PoC.

title: FIFO Sub 2 — ledger_dispatch_fifo_batch + post_batch_fifo_maximal + correctness tests
description:
Core epic work. Push FIFO layer walk + depletion dispatch into Rust via a new #[pg_extern], wrapped by a single-CTE SQL function that handles posting_lines INSERT + cost_layers INSERT + cost_layer_depletions INSERT + cost_layers.qty_remaining UPDATE all set-based.

## Rust dispatcher: ledger_dispatch_fifo_batch

Signature:
  ledger_dispatch_fifo_batch(envelopes: pgrx::JsonB)
    -> TableIterator<'static, (
         envelope_idx INT,
         row_kind TEXT,          -- 'leg' or 'depl'
         kind Option<TEXT>,      -- 'fifo_receipt' / 'fifo_issue' (legs only)
         debit_account_id Option<i64>,
         credit_account_id Option<i64>,
         amount Option<i64>,
         qty Option<i64>,
         unit_cost Option<i64>,  -- for fifo_receipt legs
         layer_sentinel Option<i32>,  -- depl rows: NEGATIVE for in-batch new layers
         layer_id Option<i64>,        -- depl rows: real cost_layers.id for pre-existing
         depl_qty Option<i64>,
         depl_cost Option<i64>,
       )>

Logic:
1. Parse + validate envelopes (two-pass for atomicity).
2. SPI fetch active layers for all touched issue-pools under FOR UPDATE in ONE query (WHERE pool_account_id = ANY(...)). Build HashMap<i64, Vec<LayerRec>>.
3. Walk envelopes in envelope_idx order:
   - fifo_receipt: assign negative sentinel id, append LayerRec to pool's Vec, emit 1 'leg' row.
   - fifo_issue: greedy walk pool's Vec, build depletion plan, mutate qty_remaining in-place, emit 1 'leg' row + N 'depl' rows.
4. stage_apply each balance leg (debit/credit per envelope).

## SQL wrapper: post_batch_fifo_maximal (new migration)

Single SQL statement with WITH CTEs:
- input: parse JSONB array once
- existing: replay anti-JOIN against posting_lines.idempotency_key
- non_replay: filtered input
- dispatched: dispatcher call on non_replay envelopes (JSONB-aggregated)
- legs / depls: split dispatched by row_kind
- inserted_pl: INSERT INTO posting_lines from legs JOIN non_replay (currency from accounts), RETURNING (id, idempotency_key)
- inserted_layers: INSERT INTO cost_layers from legs WHERE kind='fifo_receipt' (uses receipt_posting_line_id from inserted_pl), RETURNING (id, receipt_posting_line_id) -> mapping back to envelope_idx
- sentinel_resolved: depls JOIN inserted_layers on (envelope_idx → posting_line_id → layer_id) for sentinel<0 rows; layer_id direct for sentinel IS NULL rows
- inserted_dep: INSERT INTO cost_layer_depletions from sentinel_resolved
- updates: UPDATE cost_layers.qty_remaining via aggregated UPDATE FROM agg
- Final SELECT: per-envelope status row.

## Correctness tests (tests/fifo_shmem_correctness_maximal_t1.rs)

T1 — receipt then issue lands correctly; cost_layer_depletions match per-layer truth.
T2 — in-batch sentinel resolution: receipt at idx=0 + issue at idx=1 consuming from it. Verify INSERTed cost_layers.id is wired into the cost_layer_depletions.layer_id.
T3 — cross-batch layer state: 3 receipts in batch A, 1 issue in batch B consuming from layer 1 first.
T4 — idempotent replay: single-envelope replay returns idempotent_replay status; cost_layers + depletions unchanged.
T5 — multi-writer fan-in: 8 writers × 50 mixed receipts/issues on shared pool; layer math holds after settle.

## Acceptance

- Tests 5/5 green sequentially.
- Recon equivalent: SUM(cost_layer_depletions.cost_amount per issue_posting_line) = posting_lines.amount for that issue.
- Closed-form pool balance check: SUM(receipts.amount) - SUM(depletions.cost_amount) = pool account balance.
- Compiles + installs cleanly via existing build/install/refresh cycle.

## Out of scope (covered separately)

- Memory-bound contract for HashMap<i64, Vec<LayerRec>>. Active-layer count per pool currently uncapped; bench-seeded pools have 5 layers each so this isn't a PoC-blocking issue, but production-shape work needs a derived cap. Tracked in separate memory-bound epic.
- 3-replicate sweep + headline lift table — that's Sub 3.
close_reason: Sub 2 shipped @ c44620d. ledger_dispatch_fifo_batch (~340 lines) + post_batch_fifo_maximal CTE wrapper (mig 0021) + tests/fifo_shmem_correctness_maximal_t1.rs (5 cases T1-T5 all green). Two design twists surfaced + locked in: (a) Spi::connect_mut + client.update needed for FOR UPDATE in C function context, not volatility marker; (b) UPDATE in WITH cannot see rows inserted by sibling CTE — split layer bookkeeping: in-batch new layers pre-deduct qty_remaining at INSERT via in_batch_drain CTE, pre-existing layers UPDATE via pre_existing_drain CTE. WAC suites re-run green; no regression on cohabitating dispatcher.

title: FIFO maximal r8xv — push layer walk + depletion dispatch into Rust
description:
FIFO insert-time throughput is ~80-100× slower than WAC at the same shape (fan-in 305 tps p99 107s; fan-out 620 tps p99 36s; vs WAC mutable 25K and 4.3K respectively at fan-in/fan-out). Root cause: plpgsql jsonb_set on per-pool layer lists runs per-envelope per-layer (O(n²) in batch size × active-layer count).

Pattern mirrors acct-2g9w (WAC maximal): Rust dispatcher consuming envelope JSONB + emitting priced legs through TableIterator + set-based SQL wrapper. Adds one wrinkle vs WAC: TWO output streams (priced legs + depletion records) and sentinel→real_layer_id resolution for in-batch new layers.

Goal: comparable lift to WAC maximal — target band 20-50K tps fan-out, p99 sub-second.

Out of scope: memory-bound contract for the Rust HashMap of layers. The active-layer count per pool can theoretically grow unbounded; needs a soft cap derived from work_mem × budget_fraction. Tracked in a separate epic covering WAC, FIFO, and adversarial testing scenarios.

## Decomposition

Sub 1: post_batch_fifo named baseline — install mig 0020 + bench harness + baseline probe results.
Sub 2: ledger_dispatch_fifo_batch + post_batch_fifo_maximal SQL wrapper + correctness tests.
Sub 3: 3-replicate sweep + results doc.

## Acceptance

- Three sub-issues closed.
- Final results doc lands at bench/results-shmem-fifo-maximal.md with mutable baseline + maximal numbers + lift table.
- 5/5 correctness tests green sequentially.
- Recon drift=0 on all bench cells.

title: Polish pass: extension hardening (review #5/#6/#7/#8/#9)
description:

title: Per-cell last_seq race probe test
description:
External review surfaced the last_seq monotonicity bug (acct-sw4i fix shipped edd6ced) that the existing i1_seq_monotonicity test didn't catch. i1 samples APPLY_SEQ — the global counter — across many applies and asserts increasing. The bug was in per-cell last_seq under multi-writer SHARED. Different probe needed.

Test design: N writers concurrently apply to the SAME cell. After each apply, sample b.last_seq (or via ledger_balance_lookup's last_seq column). Track max-observed. Assert per-cell last_seq is monotonically non-decreasing across all observations.

Pre-fix (store): occasional regression of last_seq below max-observed.
Post-fix (fetch_max): never regresses.

Add to invariants_t1.rs as i1b_per_cell_last_seq_monotonic.

I1 in INVARIANTS.md updated to list both i1 (single-threaded) and i1b (multi-writer stress) as pinning tests.

title: Register XactCallback / SubXactCallback in _PG_init (eliminate mid-subxact registration edge case)
description:
External review #3. Today ensure_callbacks_registered is lazy — runs on first stage_apply per backend. If that first apply happens inside an active subxact (BEGIN; SAVEPOINT s; SELECT my_fn() — where my_fn calls ledger_apply_balance_delta), we miss the SUBXACT_EVENT_START_SUB event for the open subxact. PENDING_STACK then has one frame representing the subxact's deltas conceptually attached to the top-level. On ROLLBACK TO s, that frame is correctly discarded. On RELEASE s, the merge-to-parent logic conflates subxact and top-level deltas.

Reachable but uncommon. transactional_t1.rs doesn't pin this — all its savepoint tests do an initial top-level apply first.

Fix: register both callbacks unconditionally in _PG_init. Cost: one no-op callback dispatch per transaction in the entire backend even when ledger is untouched (PG callbacks are cheap). Eliminates the lazy-registration edge case entirely. Drop REGISTERED RefCell; ensure_top_frame still needed for the first frame.

Alternative: backfill frames at lazy registration time via GetCurrentTransactionNestLevel — more code, same effect, retains the lazy-registration micro-optimization that buys us this exact problem.

Recommend: _PG_init registration. Add a transactional_t1 test case for first-apply-mid-subxact to pin.
close_reason: Shipped at 508fee9. _PG_init now registers both callbacks unconditionally; REGISTERED RefCell and ensure_callbacks_registered helper removed. New t8 test exercises rollback + release after first-apply-mid-subxact across two fresh-backend pools. INVARIANTS.md I8 updated.

title: do_drain_tick: SPI errors leave aborted txn state for rest of tick
description:
External review #2. PgTryBuilder.catch_others catches the longjmp, but the surrounding BackgroundWorker::transaction is now ABORTED. Subsequent SPI calls in the same tick get 'current transaction is aborted, commands ignored' — also caught, also counted.

In theory: a single missing-table error generates N failures in LEDGER_DRAIN_TOTAL_FAILURES (one per dirty cell), and LEDGER_DRAIN_CONSECUTIVE_FAILS hits the warning threshold on the first tick instead of the fifth.

In practice: bgworker_error_escalation_t1.rs T1 measured consecutive=12 / total=12 over a 1.2s outage at 10Hz cadence — exactly 1 failure per tick, no cascade. Either BackgroundWorker::transaction resets txn state between ticks (likely) or the workload had ≤1 dirty cell per tick.

Two fixes available:
  (a) Pre-flight check at tick start: SELECT 1 FROM account_balances_rollup LIMIT 0. Failed pre-check → skip the dirty-cell loop, log + bump counter once. Simpler, narrowly targets the known failure mode.
  (b) Subxact per SPI call: BeginInternalSubTransaction / catch_others rolls back the subxact / ReleaseCurrentSubTransaction on success. More robust against ANY mid-tick SPI failure.

Write a multi-dirty-cell outage test first to verify cascade actually occurs in our setup; if it does not (the current T1 evidence suggests it doesn't), document and close. If it does, ship (a) at minimum.
close_reason: Negative result. Shipped at f5eb033 — t3_multi_cell_cascade_probe is the falsification record. PG log inspection during 50-cell outage shows every per-cell SPI failure carries ERRCODE_UNDEFINED_TABLE (root error), NOT ERRCODE_IN_FAILED_SQL_TRANSACTION (cascade marker). pgrx's Spi::run_with_args isolates each call from the txn-poisoning cascade — likely via internal subxact wrapping. Confirmed cascade IS a real PG behaviour generally via vanilla psql probe; pgrx is shielding the bgworker tick. total_failures inflates N× per outage tick but accurately (each cell is its own independent failure with its own root error). consecutive_fails escalation pacing is correct (1/tick). Recovery path works (t1 pins). Pre-flight short-circuit would be a noise reducer, not a correctness fix; deferred indefinitely. t3 stays in tree as regression net for the per-cell-independent-failure behaviour; if someone ever revisits and ships the noise reducer, t3 assertion flips from ratio≈N to ratio≈1.

title: ledger_apply_batch maximal — push WAC running-avg dispatch into Rust
description: Minimal r8xv (acct-r8xv) falsified the call-overhead hypothesis: collapsing per-leg PERFORMs into one ledger_apply_batch call produced -9.4%/+6.9% deltas (both within rig noise). The real ceiling is plpgsql per-envelope work (FOR LOOP, jsonb_set on running-avg map, per-envelope staging INSERT) — none of which minimal r8xv addressed. Maximal variant: post_batch_wac_shmem becomes a thin wrapper over a Rust entry point that maintains the running-avg map as a HashMap<u128,(i64,i64)>, walks envelopes in Rust, computes amounts via direct shmem reads (no SQL round-trip via ledger_balance_lookup), and stages into PENDING_STACK. Effort 3-5d. Target: 6-8× fan-out lift, matching the acct-togd 7-10× projection.

Fan-out 59K tps (5.24x B4, 13.67x mutable), p99 collapse 2,626ms → 453ms (-83%). Mig 0018 plpgsql wrapper + mig 0019 single-CTE refinement (+9.5%). 5/5 correctness tests green. title: M10.B8 — concurrent accounts table activity during ledger apply (onboarding + locks + DDL)
description:
Coverage gap surfaced 2026-05-12 architectural review. M9 and the filed M10 plan all run with a static accounts table — pre-seeded N rows, TRUNCATE between runs, no INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE on accounts during workload. ERP-realistic operation has the accounts table mutating concurrently with ledger activity even on a greenfield deployment.

## Scope note

Originally this issue included an S1 "mixed-mode operation during cutover" scenario probing interleaved post_batch (mutable) + post_batch_shmem (extension) traffic. **Removed 2026-05-12** — acct is greenfield; there is no legacy UPDATE-accounts-SET-balance path in production to coexist with. The extension is either used everywhere or not at all. PoC retains both functions for bench comparison only.

Also originally included an S3 "accounts.kind/currency change mid-run" scenario. **Removed 2026-05-12** — greenfield design call: accounts.currency and accounts.kind are immutable once posted-against. Enforce via constraint or trigger (separate small task; file as acct-mii6-immutability-followup if needed). Once enforced, the scenario can't arise.

Remaining scope is three runtime-behavior probes that hold regardless of deployment model.

## Three scenarios

### S2 — Account creation mid-run

Vendor/customer/SKU onboarding INSERTs an accounts row at the same time as ledger applies. FK protects posting_lines against orphan account_ids, but ledger_apply_balance_delta doesn't check accounts existence — it accepts any i64 key.

Probe: apply against a fabricated account_id NOT in accounts → cell created in shmem → recon shows ledger_balance = NULL (no accounts row). Document this as "shmem extension is accounts-existence-agnostic; FK at posting_lines is the gate."

Why this matters even on greenfield: defends against caller bugs where a code path manages to compute the wrong account_id (typo, off-by-one in a join, dropped FK). The extension wouldn't fail loudly — it'd silently create a shmem cell that doesn't map to any real account. Recon's ledger_balance=NULL signal is the catch-net; verify it's actually surfaced and visible.

### S4 — Concurrent accounts row locks

Backend B1: BEGIN; SELECT * FROM accounts WHERE id = 42 FOR UPDATE; -- (holds lock for 60s). Backend B2: SELECT ledger_apply_balance_delta(42, ...).

The architectural premise of sw4i is that B2 does NOT block — apply path takes no accounts row locks, only the shmem LWLock. Verify this empirically. If B2 blocks, there's a hidden lock-acquire somewhere (an FK validation, a trigger, something), and the premise that drives the 5.55× fan-out lift is wrong.

Test: time B2's apply latency with and without B1's long-held FOR UPDATE. Expect: <1ms in both cases.

### S5 — DDL on accounts during run

ALTER TABLE accounts ADD COLUMN custom_attribute TEXT takes AccessExclusiveLock on accounts. Apply path doesn't touch accounts → unaffected. But ledger_shmem_recon() does SPI against accounts → blocks until ALTER releases.

Test: run sustained apply load; trigger ALTER; verify apply throughput unaffected (no apply-side block); verify recon SPI returns "table lock timeout" or blocks-then-completes after ALTER finishes. Document the recon behavior.

## Test method

poc/ledger-extension/tests/concurrent_accounts_mutation_t1.rs:

- S2 — orphan cell. Apply against fabricated id=99999 (no accounts row); assert cell created in shmem; assert recon row shows shmem_balance non-null, ledger_balance NULL, drift NULL.
- S4 — concurrent FOR UPDATE. tx1 holds FOR UPDATE on account 42 for 5s in a background tokio task; tx2 in main test runs 100 apply calls against id=42; assert tx2 total wall time < 50ms. Cleanup: tx1 rollback.
- S5 — DDL during apply. Background: 1 worker sustained apply for 30s; 5s in trigger ALTER TABLE accounts ADD COLUMN test_attribute TEXT; measure throughput before/during/after ALTER from 100ms windows; assert all three are within noise of each other. Concurrent ledger_shmem_recon() call during ALTER window: assert either lock-timeout error or completion-after-ALTER, document which. Cleanup: ALTER TABLE accounts DROP COLUMN test_attribute.

## Acceptance

- S2/S4/S5 all probed.
- S2 documents apply-path is accounts-existence-agnostic; FK is the gate; recon NULL ledger_balance is the surfaced signal.
- S4 confirms the architectural premise (no accounts row lock dependency).
- S5 documents the recon-blocks-on-DDL behavior.

## Files touched

- poc/ledger-extension/tests/concurrent_accounts_mutation_t1.rs (new, ~200 LOC across 3 scenarios)
- poc/ledger-extension/README.md (architectural notes section on accounts-table independence)

## Dependencies

Independent. None of these scenarios need A.2 or B.4-prep.

## Estimate

4 hours. Test orchestration of background lock-holder + ALTER timing is the main cost.

## Why this matters

S4 is load-bearing: the entire 5.55× fan-out lift premise rests on "apply path takes no accounts row locks." Currently this is asserted by reading the source. An empirical test pins it so a future refactor (e.g., adding a trigger to accounts, or a recon-aware FK constraint) that violates the premise gets caught at test time.

title: M10.C4 — GUC SIGHUP reload smoke test (drain_interval_ms hot-change)
description:
`DRAIN_INTERVAL_MS` is registered with `GucContext::Sighup` (lib.rs:145). Verify the bgworker actually picks up the new value mid-run.

## Test method

`poc/ledger-extension/tests/guc_reload_t1.rs`:

```rust
// Pre: drain_interval_ms = 100ms (default). Verify drain rate.
// Sample: count drained_at timestamps from rollup over 1s → expect ~10 rows.

// Mid-run: ALTER SYSTEM SET ledger.drain_interval_ms = 1000; SELECT pg_reload_conf();
// Or: SET ledger.drain_interval_ms = 1000 in session (but that's session-scope, not bgworker — verify the right mechanism).

// Post: sample drained_at over next 1s → expect ~1 row.
```

Subtle: bgworker reads GUC on each tick (lib.rs:190 `DRAIN_INTERVAL_MS.get().max(10)`), so reload effect is immediate after SIGHUP. But the FIRST tick after reload still uses the old interval (since wait_latch was called with the old interval).

`DRAIN_DATABASE` is `GucContext::Postmaster` — only changes at postmaster restart. Test that ALTER SYSTEM SET succeeds but doesn't take effect until restart.

## Acceptance

- T1: drain_interval_ms reload changes drain frequency within 1-2 ticks.
- T2: drain_database ALTER takes restart to apply.
- Documented in README.md.

Independent.

title: M10.C2 — bgworker SPI error escalation (currently log-and-swallowed forever)
description:
Current bgworker drain (lib.rs:280-287) swallows SPI errors with a `log!` and retries next tick. If the rollup table is missing or has schema drift, the worker fails silently every 100ms forever — no visible signal except log spam.

## Design

Track consecutive failure count. After N consecutive ticks fail with SPI error:
- Emit `pg_log_warning!` (visible in pg_stat_activity, observable from outside).
- Optionally raise `error!` to trigger the bgworker restart cycle (set_restart_time=1s) — but only after a higher threshold (M failures over T seconds).

Reset counter on first successful tick.

## Test method

`poc/ledger-extension/tests/bgworker_error_escalation_t1.rs`:

1. Drop `account_balances_rollup` table.
2. Apply a delta (triggers dirty cell).
3. Wait 30s; sample PG logs (via `pg_read_server_files()` or test fixture exposing log path).
4. Assert: after ~3-5 ticks (300-500ms), warning surfaces. Worker not crashed — keeps trying.
5. Restore rollup table; apply another delta; wait 1s; verify counter reset and worker drained the cell.

Secondary scenario: temporary error (force pg_locks contention on the rollup table from another backend with a long-held SHARE ROW EXCLUSIVE lock; verify counter increments but doesn't reach the panic threshold before the test backend releases).

## Acceptance

- Failure counter implemented; warning threshold = 5 ticks; documented.
- Test verifies escalation + recovery.
- log! messages include rich context (table name, error code if available, last 3 cell keys attempted).

## Files touched

- poc/ledger-extension/src/lib.rs (do_drain_tick error path)
- poc/ledger-extension/tests/bgworker_error_escalation_t1.rs (new)

## Dependencies

Independent.

## Estimate

3 hours.

title: M10.C1 — hash table full as recoverable Result<i64> (currently aborts txn)
description:
Currently `insert_new_seeded` raises `error!()` on hash table full (lib.rs:441-444). This aborts the entire SQL transaction and propagates a SQLSTATE up to the caller. Better contract: return a sentinel and let the caller decide whether to abort, retry, or fall back to direct posting_lines insert.

## Options

**Option A (recommended)**: Change `ledger_apply_balance_delta` return type from `i64` (sequence number) to `i64` with sentinel `-1` meaning "deferred to durable path." Caller (post_batch_shmem) checks the return; if -1, falls back to UPDATE accounts SET balance directly. This preserves the optimization on the common path and degrades gracefully when capacity is exceeded.

**Option B**: Raise a dedicated SQLSTATE (`P0006` or new `LEDGER_SHMEM_FULL`) that callers can CATCH. Cleaner semantically but every caller must know to handle it.

**Option C**: Hash table full triggers an emergency drain — block the current backend until bgworker frees N cells, then retry. Couples apply path latency to drain path; would create hard-to-debug tail latency.

**Decision**: Option A for the apply path; PreCommit validation (in A.2) ALSO checks projected capacity and prefers to abort the txn cleanly. Defense in depth.

## Test method

`poc/ledger-extension/tests/hash_full_recoverable_t1.rs`:

1. Pre-seed `N_BUCKETS - 1` cells.
2. Call `ledger_apply_balance_delta` with a new (16385th distinct) key.
3. Assert: returns -1; shmem occupied count unchanged; transaction NOT aborted (caller can continue).
4. Caller fallback: post-detect -1 → manually UPDATE accounts SET balance += delta. Verify ledger consistency after.

Stress test: 16 writers all racing to insert at 99% load factor. Some succeed (find a vacated slot from another writer's seeded prior state), some hit -1. Aggregate: 16 attempts → some Some-N, some -1; total accounts.balance correct after fallback.

## Acceptance

- `ledger_apply_balance_delta` signature unchanged (i64); return -1 instead of error!().
- Test verifies graceful degradation.
- Documentation in lib.rs notes the contract.
- Existing M8 `post_batch_shmem` migration extended to handle -1 fallback.

## Files touched

- poc/ledger-extension/src/lib.rs (insert_new_seeded return path)
- poc/batch-ledger/db/migrations/0015_post_batch_shmem_fallback.up.sql (caller fallback)
- poc/ledger-extension/tests/hash_full_recoverable_t1.rs (new)

## Dependencies

Independent of A/B tracks.

## Estimate

3 hours.

New SQL: ledger_shmem_insert_failure_count(). tests/hash_full_recoverable_t1.rs (4 cases): T1 fill-to-capacity, T2 overflow rejected at pre_commit with SQLSTATE message, T3 existing-key applies at full capacity, T4 counter starts clean. title: M10.B7 — high-load-factor probe distance regression test
description:
Open-addressing probe distance grows as load factor approaches 1. M9 at 5K cells on 16K buckets = 30% load factor — clean. Need data at higher load factors to characterize the degradation curve.

## Test method

`poc/ledger-extension/tests/load_factor_t1.rs`:

Pre-seed N cells into shmem; measure single-apply latency at:
- N = 1K (6% load)
- N = 4K (24%)
- N = 8K (49%)
- N = 12K (73%)
- N = 14K (85%)
- N = 15.5K (95%)

For each load level:
- 1M apply calls against random pre-seeded keys (UPDATE path, no inserts).
- Record p50, p99, p99.9 latency.
- Also measure INSERT-only path: pre-seed N cells, then apply to N+1 distinct new keys, time each insert (cold path EXCLUSIVE lock + probe to find empty slot).

Hypothesis:
- Update latency flat (~50ns) up to ~70% load.
- Insert latency degrades exponentially past 70% (open addressing's known cliff).
- At 95% load: insert may probe 100+ slots before finding empty.

title: M10.B6 — bgworker backpressure under sustained load (dirty_count bound check)
description:
Validate that `ledger_drain` bgworker keeps up under sustained apply load. If apply rate exceeds drain throughput, dirty_count grows. Question: does it bound?

## Hypothesis

- At default `drain_interval_ms=100`, drain processes O(N_BUCKETS) dirty cells per tick via N SPI UPSERTs.
- M9 measured 43.5K tps fan-out at 60s. Each apply marks 2 cells dirty (debit + credit). 87K dirty-updates/sec.
- Each cell is touched many times — only the LATEST `last_seq` matters for drain. Re-dirty rate per CELL is bounded by N_distinct_cells.
- At 5000 cells, drain cycle = ~5000 UPSERTs / 100ms = ~50K UPSERTs/sec.
- Net: dirty_count should bound at O(N_distinct_cells), not grow unboundedly.

## Test method

`poc/ledger-extension/tests/bgworker_backpressure_t1.rs`:

```rust
// Sustained 5-minute apply at 30 writer threads × 1000 apply/batch.
// Sample dirty_count every 5s via SELECT ledger_shmem_dirty_count().
// Plot. Expected: dirty_count rises in first 100ms then oscillates between
// 0 and ~N_distinct_cells * fraction-touched-per-tick.

// Fail condition: dirty_count grows monotonically with time (drain falling behind).
```

Secondary measurement: drain tick latency. Sample wall-time of one tick under load via querying `drained_at` distribution in `account_balances_rollup`. Hypothesis: drain ticks complete within 50ms even under contention (PG's per-row UPSERT is ~10µs; 5000 rows = 50ms).

Tertiary: starve the drain — set `drain_interval_ms=10000` (10s). Verify dirty_count rises during a 30s apply burst, then catches up after drains resume.

## Acceptance

- 5-min sustained load shows bounded dirty_count.
- Documented oscillation range.
- Starvation test confirms drain catches up (no permanent backlog).

## Files touched

- poc/ledger-extension/tests/bgworker_backpressure_t1.rs (new)
- README.md milestone block

## Dependencies

Independent. Could parallel with C track.

## Estimate

4 hours including the 5-min sustained run.

title: M10.B3 — multi-ledger_kind (qty + value) coexistence test
description:
Verify a single (account, period, currency) can have multiple ledger_kind cells (qty=1 vs value=2). This is the WAC pattern in acct — pool value AND pool qty are tracked in separate accounts, both flowing through shmem.

## Test method

`poc/ledger-extension/tests/multi_ledger_kind_t1.rs`:

```rust
// Pool: account 100 carries value (ledger_kind=2 'value'); account 101 carries qty (ledger_kind=1 'qty').
ledger_apply_balance_delta(100, 1, 1, 2, 5000, 0);  // +5000 value
ledger_apply_balance_delta(101, 1, 1, 1, 0, 10);    // +10 qty
```

2 hours.

title: M10.B2 — multi-period apply + period close semantics

Verify shmem behavior across period_id boundaries. ERP period close shifts new applies to a new period_id; existing cells should be 'frozen' (drained but never re-touched) while new cells accept further deltas.

## Scenarios

1. **Distinct cells per period.** apply(A, period=1, +100); apply(A, period=2, +200). Result: 2 cells, distinct balances.

3. **Quiescence detection.** After period close, no new applies on period 1 expected. Verify `dirty_count` for period 1 cells stays 0 indefinitely.

- 3 scenarios pass.
- Documents that the EXTENSION does NOT enforce period-close immutability — that's the acct schema's `periods.closed_at` + `post_posting_lines` gate. Extension is period-naive.

title: M10.B1 — multi-currency apply test (shmem cells across currency dimension)
PG18 configuration audit + tuning for ledger workload
description:
Sub-issue of acct-togd. Operational, immediate. PoC and extension benchmarks need to be measured against a properly-tuned config, not PG18 defaults.

## Motivation

Live setting audit on dev box (60GB RAM, 8 cores, SSD, PG18 in Docker) shows the project running on near-defaults targeted at a 1GB server. The acct-qdp5 PoC's 80K/155K append-only ceilings were measured against this conf. Extension PoCs would inherit the same disadvantage.

## Gap table (current → target)

| Setting | Current | Target | Why |
|---|---|---|---|
| shared_buffers | 128 MB | 8-15 GB | 25% of RAM rule; current ~100x undersized |
| effective_cache_size | 4 GB | 30-45 GB | planner hint for SSD-cached working set |
| work_mem | 4 MB | 64-256 MB | per-sort/hash; matters for property tests + close hooks |
| maintenance_work_mem | 64 MB | 1-2 GB | VACUUM, CREATE INDEX |
| wal_buffers | 4 MB | 16-64 MB or -1 | reduce WAL contention under burst |
| max_wal_size | 1 GB | 4-16 GB | reduce checkpoint frequency for write-heavy |
| min_wal_size | 80 MB | 1-2 GB | avoid WAL recycling churn |
| checkpoint_timeout | 5 min | 15-30 min | smooth I/O; spread checkpoint work |
| commit_delay | 0 | 10-100µs | group commit (relevant for batch API) |
| wal_compression | off | lz4 | PG18 native; ~50% WAL volume reduction on ledger rows |
| random_page_cost | 4 | 1.1 | SSD storage |
| track_io_timing | off | on | EXPLAIN ANALYZE I/O stats |
| effective_io_concurrency | 16 | 200-300 | NVMe parallelism |

## Scope

1. Add tuned settings to docker-compose.yml command list (or switch to a postgresql.conf file mounted into the container).
2. Re-baseline acct-qdp5 PoC benchmarks (P3 simple, append-only, WAC, FIFO, specific) on the tuned conf. Expected: 2-4x lift on metrics bottlenecked by WAL or buffer cache.
3. Verify io_uring + huge_pages still work after tuning.
4. Document each setting's rationale in db/README.md.

## Acceptance

- docker-compose.yml updated with tuned settings (or postgresql.conf mounted)
- 5x60s sweep on append-only batch=1000 post-tune; compare to PoC headline numbers
- Per-setting rationale comment / doc
- No regression on existing test suite (1073/0/9 should still pass)

## Risk

- shared_buffers too aggressive can cause double-buffering with kernel page cache; target 25% not 50% on 60GB.
- max_wal_size large means longer recovery time on crash — for a dev box this is fine.
- commit_delay > 0 adds latency to single-tx writes; only beneficial for batch workload. Test impact on the acct suite which is many small txns.

## Estimated wall-time

~0.5 day for conf changes; +1 day to re-baseline and document.

## Composability with extension work

This work is independent and immediately beneficial. Should land BEFORE acct-sw4i (shmem rollup) bench measurements so the extension's win isn't conflated with conf gains.

## Production deployment note

Numbers tuned here are for dev. Production deployment will need separate tuning based on real hardware (RAM, NVMe vs HDD, network topology, replicas). File acct-togd-followup for production tuning guide when production target is concrete.
