A/B vs PoC default produced +3.8% median (83,592 vs 80,514 tps) — inside the rig's 8.6% IQR noise band. commit_delay A/B: cd=20µs wins on median + variance vs cd=0. Conf NOT the bottleneck for append-only workload; the working set fits any reasonable buffer pool. Bottleneck is WAL serialization + B-tree latches + plpgsql call overhead — extension territory. Conf retained for analytics workloads + longer-run WAL sustainability + observability + professional baseline. Tip 93b20c4.

title: FK validation cache — shmem bloom for accounts dimension
description:
Fourth component of acct-togd. Small, contained win.

## Motivation

acct-qdp5 measurement: 2 FK validations per posting_lines INSERT = +3µs at 20w. accounts is small (~few thousand rows) and slowly-changing. Validating by hitting accounts heap + B-tree is overkill per row.

## Scope

- Shmem hash set populated by bgworker on accounts INSERT (catalog trigger or logical decoding)
- Extension function is_valid_account(id BIGINT) RETURNS BOOLEAN consults shmem in O(1)
- Constraint trigger on posting_lines INSERT (or extension-provided check function) calls is_valid_account instead of FK lookup
- bgworker syncs shmem from accounts on PG start + on every accounts INSERT

## Acceptance

- pgrx extension contributes is_valid_account function
- posting_lines INSERT path uses shmem check instead of FK constraint
- Microbenchmark: FK overhead drops from 3µs to <0.5µs per row
- Correctness: invalid account_id INSERT raises P0001-equivalent (mirroring current FK violation behavior)
- shmem state matches accounts table contents at quiescence

## Risks

- FK constraint replacement loses some PG-native error semantics (FK violation DETAIL string). Extension check raises a custom error code.
- Catalog sync correctness: bgworker must not miss accounts INSERT events. AFTER INSERT trigger on accounts is simplest; logical decoding is more robust but adds infra.
- Order: if shmem hasn't yet absorbed a new account INSERT and a posting_line referencing it arrives same-tx-window, the check fails. Tx-local FOR UPDATE on accounts + tx-end shmem update would block; simpler: bgworker poll interval bounded < typical tx duration.

## Estimated wall-time

~1 week.

## Dependency

Standalone.

title: Native FIFO + wac_retroactive replay in C/Rust hot path
description:
Third component of acct-togd. Unblocks FIFO's structural ceiling and wac_retroactive close-hook wall-time.

## Motivation

acct-qdp5 P5 measurement: plpgsql FIFO at batch=1000 reaches 762 tps. Per-envelope state held in jsonb that grows as in-batch receipts accumulate; O(n) per envelope × n envelopes = O(n^2). Filed acct-fw2w with three resolution paths; this is path 1 (pgrx native extension).

wac_retroactive_close_hook has a similar plpgsql + cursor-walk shape; reaches 17-65s on property tests via chronological replay. Same native-code lever applies.

## Scope

- Implement _fifo_walk_layers as LANGUAGE C (pgrx). Layer state in per-backend buffer (not jsonb), held across envelopes in a single batch via hash from (sku, location) → buffer pointer
- Same pattern for wac_retroactive_close_hook chronological replay — per-pool buffer holds running pool_value / pool_qty, walked in C without jsonb_set churn
- Register both in cost_method_strategies registry alongside existing plpgsql strategies; dispatcher EXECUTE-formats by name as today (extension functions callable from plpgsql)

## Acceptance

- pgrx extension builds clean against PG 18 + Rust 1.85+
- FIFO batch (PoC migration 0008 shape) reaches 30K+ tps at 20w / batch=1000 (vs 762 today)
- wac_retroactive close hook on property-test corpus drops 5x or better in wall-time
- Correctness: SUM(cost_layer_depletions.cost_amount) = posting_line.amount across 100 property workloads
- pg_stat_statements shows native function calls (not plpgsql line counts)

## Risks

- pgrx framework maturity: confirm pgrx 0.13+ supports needed PG18 APIs (BufferAccess, FOR UPDATE within C functions, MemoryContext lifecycle for batch buffers)
- Operator class for cost_layers (id, receipt_date) composite primary key — confirm pgrx exposes catalog-aware composite type handling
- For wac_retroactive: the chronological-replay ordering by (business_date, doc_chrono, document_id, sub_priority, id) must be preserved exactly; off-by-one regression here silently corrupts variance attribution

## Estimated wall-time

2 weeks for FIFO; +1 week for wac_retroactive (similar shape, shared infra).

## Dependency

Standalone. Composes with shmem rollup (acct-sw4i) — native FIFO can call into shmem balance updates without round-tripping through plpgsql.

title: Shmem rollup + bgworker drain — eliminate UPDATE accounts via in-memory balance
description:
Second component of acct-togd. The biggest perf lever.

## Motivation

Per acct-qdp5: UPDATE accounts SET balance + FOR UPDATE pre-lock is +12µs/row at 20w — half of P3 simple's per-row cost. Removing it doubles throughput (40.6K → 80.5K tps). Append-only does this by deleting accounts.balance entirely; the cost is forcing every app-side read to re-aggregate from posting_lines OR read a projection table.

This component eliminates that trade-off: app reads accounts.balance and gets the live in-memory value, not a stale projection. App writes don't pay UPDATE serialization.

## Design

- Shared-memory hash table keyed by (account_id, period_id, currency, ledger_kind) → running_balance BIGINT + qty BIGINT
- _post_posting_lines_apply_event calls extension function ledger_apply_balance_delta(...) instead of UPDATE accounts. shmem hash bucket increment is lock-free (or per-bucket spinlock)
- bgworker drains shmem buckets to durable account_balances_rollup table every N ms (configurable)
- App reads balance(account_id) SQL function that consults shmem (fast path) or falls back to durable rollup (after restart, before bgworker catches up)
- Crash-safety: emit a balance-delta WAL record at apply_event time (~30 bytes/posting_line). On recovery, replay WAL to rebuild shmem state

## Acceptance

- pgrx extension with shmem hash + bgworker
- WAL replay rebuilds shmem on PG restart; balance(X) returns correct value pre- and post-recovery
- Microbenchmark: live-period append at 20w / batch=1000 reaches 150K+ tps (recover the +98% append-only win)
- Recon: shmem state matches SUM(posting_lines.amount signed by side) across all (account, period) cells at quiescence
- Crash-injection test: kill PG mid-batch; recovery produces correct balances

## Open design questions

1. Shadow accounts.balance (double-write for safety; built-in invariant check) vs replace (cleaner; bigger schema change). Lean: shadow during PoC, indefinitely as recon signal. Double-write cost negligible vs eliminated UPDATE.
2. Bucket count / hash strategy — start with 2^16 buckets; size based on workload distribution.
3. Period rollover — when period closes, shmem cells flush + freeze in durable rollup. No more deltas after closed_at.
4. Multi-currency / multi-ledger_kind cells share account_id key prefix; cache-friendly access.

## Risks

- Crash recovery semantics are the hardest part of the whole epic. WAL replay correctness must be bulletproof.
- shmem allocation in PG is sized at startup; need to budget for max active (account × period × currency × ledger_kind) cells.
- bgworker drain lag means recon comparing shmem to durable rollup will show transient drift; recon must compare against posting_lines truth, not durable rollup.

## Estimated wall-time

3-4 weeks.

## Dependency note

Depends on rational_t (acct-es0k) only if we want shmem rollup to store balance as rational_t for exact running averages. Lean: store BIGINT; if drift surfaces, retrofit to rational_t.
notes:
2026-05-12 reframing: sw4i is a CORRECTNESS REQUIREMENT for append-only on cost-dispatched workloads, not just a perf optimization.

Two distinct things UPDATE accounts is doing today:
(1) Maintain queryable balance for app reads
(2) Serialize concurrent computation of amounts that depend on pool state

Skipping (1) is fine (read via projection). Skipping (2) BREAKS WAC perpetual dispatch — two concurrent writers can both read stale pool_value/pool_qty, both compute drain at the same stale avg, both insert. Race; non-deterministic cost; variance leaks. The PoC's post_batch_wac benches masked this because within-batch was single-writer; across concurrent batches with no FOR UPDATE, WAC is silently broken.

Workload class impact:
- Caller-supplied amount (transfers, AP bills, journal entries, AR payments): append-only alone is correct.
- WAC perpetual cost dispatch: append-only alone is BROKEN (race) or slow (FOR UPDATE returns). sw4i restores serialization via per-bucket spinlock = nanosecond-scale.
- FIFO: NOT affected (own FOR UPDATE on cost_layers).
- Specific (lot_and_serial): NOT affected (UNIQUE active-partial idx on inventory_units).
- Live balance read: slow without rollup (SUM aggregate) → fast with shmem.

Reframing for design:
- shmem hash bucket is the serialization primitive, not just the cache.
- compare_and_swap on bucket = atomic read-modify-write of (value, qty) = equivalent semantics to FOR UPDATE + UPDATE on accounts row, but at memory-bus speed.
- Read-your-writes within txn: option A (update shmem at apply-event-time + txn-local journal for rollback) vs option B (commit-time WAL replay + per-txn cache). Decide during PoC.

Implication for priority: sw4i isn't a perf-win-to-layer-on. Without sw4i (or equivalent fast-serialized-balance mechanism), append-only can't run WAC workloads at all. Materially raises priority + reduces conditionality.
close_reason: M1-M9 PoC scope complete. Shipped @ 2d86c35 (poc/ledger-extension/, 11 commits). Bench validates architectural premise: fan-in 2.16× (31K→67K tps, 96% of append-only ceiling), fan-out 5.55× (7.8K→43.5K tps, 52% of ceiling, 13× p99 improvement to 708ms). Zero deadlocks across 18 runs. Hardening (transactional rollback semantics, WAC integration, error handling) tracked as acct-sw4i-m10 epic. See bd memory state-2026-05-12-acct-sw4i-M9-shipped-M10-plan for full M10 plan and architectural-review pickup.

title: rational_t type — precision-preserving fraction arithmetic for ledger math
description:
First component of acct-togd. Smallest, most self-contained piece; PoC-grade.

## Motivation

WAC running averages, co-product allocation_pct splits, and wac_retroactive chronological replay all involve chains of BIGINT multiply-then-divide where integer truncation accumulates. Today we mitigate via:
- Residual sweeps in post_wo_complete (acct-69e — solo-at-pool gate)
- Pre-balance step before per-output drain
- Two-pass accumulation in some variance calcs

With (num, den) exact arithmetic, division happens once at boundary writes (posting_line.amount, *_lines.unit_cost). Intermediate state stays exact.

The perf angle isn't 'frac_t is faster' — it's 'frac_t lets us delete precision-preserving workarounds' (residual sweeps, gates on solo-at-pool that exist partly because residue accumulates). Cost: GCD reduction to keep num/den from overflowing across long chains.

## Scope

- Define rational_t as a fixed-width type (16 bytes: num BIGINT + den BIGINT) via pgrx
- Implement +, -, *, /, ==, < operators with auto-GCD reduction
- Implement cast functions rational_t <-> BIGINT (BIGINT cast does ROUND or TRUNC at boundary)
- Implement aggregate rational_sum(rational_t) -> rational_t (parallel-safe)
- Implement rational_avg constructor for 'sum/count' pattern
- Test: build a parallel wac_perpetual strategy using rational_t for pool running avg; compare ledger amounts vs current BIGINT-truncated impl on a property-test corpus

## Acceptance

- pgrx extension builds clean against PG 18 + Rust 1.85+
- 10-case correctness test demonstrating exact arithmetic for chains where BIGINT would truncate
- Microbenchmark: cost of rational_t add/mul/div vs BIGINT within 5x (correctness extension; not a perf win)
- Property test confirming rational_t WAC pool produces ledger amounts within 1 cent of BIGINT pool across 100 workloads — surfaces *whether* truncation drift is detectable today

## Estimated wall-time

~1 week.

## Open question

Whether to ship as standalone extension first OR as part of larger ledger-extension crate. Lean: standalone — minimum lock-in, surfaces pgrx ergonomics before bigger components.

title: Custom Postgres extension for ledger hot-path optimization (research + PoC)
description:
**TYPE-CONVERTED FROM `epic` → `task` ON 2026-05-20 to enable PAUSE-blocking.**

This issue was originally type=epic (organizing 8 sub-issues). bd disallows task-typed issues (like the ledger-extension-PAUSE gate) from blocking epic-typed issues, so the type was downgraded to `task` here to allow the PAUSE dependency.

**On unblock (when ledger-extension-PAUSE closes): reclassify this issue back to type=epic via `bd update acct-togd --type=epic`** to restore its umbrella role and the `bd show` CHILDREN rollup view. The children themselves carry parent references independently — converting back is a pure type flip.

---

Research-and-PoC epic exploring a pgrx-based Postgres extension targeting the live-period write hot path identified by the acct-qdp5 PoC.

## Motivation

Per acct-qdp5 measurements:
- Append-only batch ceiling: 80K tps @ 20w / batch=1000 (vs 40.6K for mutable accounts.balance)
- FIFO batch ceiling in plpgsql: 762 tps (O(n^2) jsonb cost; structural)
- Per-row decomposition at 20w contention: 6µs bare INSERT + 6µs idx + 3µs FK + 12µs UPDATE accounts = 27µs

The extension recovers the append-only +98% without forcing the app onto a read-from-projection model, plus eliminates FK + index overhead and unblocks FIFO/wac_retroactive structural ceilings.

## v1 components (sub-issues to be wired)

1. rational_t type — precision-preserving (num, den) arithmetic. Deletes residual sweeps + truncation workarounds.
2. Shmem rollup + bgworker drain — eliminates +12µs UPDATE accounts. App still reads accounts.balance and gets live shmem value.
3. Native FIFO + wac_retroactive replay — 30-50x on FIFO writes; 5-10x on wac_retro close hook.
4. FK validation cache — shmem bloom for accounts dim. Eliminates +3µs/row.

## Stacked ceiling estimate

~4-7µs/row vs 27µs today → 150-250K tps for live-period appends. Composable with sharded-balances (acct-slhp) to push hot-account ceiling further.

## Explicitly OUT of v1 scope (per user direction 2026-05-12)

- money_t custom type — universal practice is BIGINT.
- Custom TAM for closed periods — analytics workload, not critical path.

## Relationship to acct-qdp5 backport (acct-qb0q P8)

Parallel track. The backport (batch API + append-only) is the cheap+fast path. The extension targets the next ceiling once the backport reveals where remaining bottlenecks live.

## Future / research catalog

Filed as separate sub-issue capturing R1-R8 directions that surfaced during v1 design but are out of v1 scope.
notes:
Multi-step transactional perf measured 2026-05-12 (tip 30a1aee, WAC fan-in/fan-out bench). Key findings updating v1 ceiling estimates:

WAC fan-in (1 hot pool, BOM destination shape):  22K tps, 45us/row
WAC fan-out (5K pools, BOM component-source shape): 4K tps, 233us/row

The 200us/row cost in fan-out is dominated by FOR UPDATE pre-lock acquisition on ~1000 distinct cold accounts per batch — the SAME pattern observed in simple-transfer fan-out vs fan-in (acct-sw4i framing). Sw4i shmem rollup specifically eliminates this cost: per-bucket spinlock is microsecond-scale regardless of how many distinct buckets are touched.

Multi-step finding (the question that prompted this): there is NO inherent 'many-step is expensive' effect. A 50-step txn = sum of 50 per-step costs. Postgres txn machinery is well-amortized. Internal RYW dependencies (issues reading state set by prior receipts in same batch) cost <5% — essentially free.

The dragons in multi-step txns are:
1. Cold-lock acquisition when steps touch many distinct accounts → sw4i fixes
2. Per-step plpgsql dispatch overhead → fngj (native cost dispatch) fixes
3. NOT internal state dependencies — those are cheap

Updated lift projections for sw4i (across workload classes):
  Simple fan-in:  3.8x  Simple fan-out:  9.6x
  WAC fan-in: 3.4x      WAC fan-out: 7-10x

Realistic-shape ERP workloads match fan-out (per-vendor-per-currency, per-sku-per-location pools). sw4i value materially higher than the original simple-PoC 2x projection.

title: PoC: worker affinity / sharded balances (eliminate accounts.tuple contention)
description: Diagnostic showed 90% Lock:tuple wait at 20w × 50 accounts; workers serialize on hot rows. Two designs to measure: (a) worker affinity — each worker uses a disjoint subset of accounts; (b) sharded balances — each account = N sub-accounts, transfer picks random shard, balance reads SUM shards. Expected 5-10× scaling vs current 2× sub-linear scaling. Different from acct-7ull (which measures observability); this measures the structural fix.
notes:
2026-05-12 fan-in/fan-out bench (tip 67babbf) surfaced that fan-out mutable balance (5K accounts, no hot row) is actually SLOWER than fan-in mutable balance (1 hot credit, 50 accounts) — 7K tps vs 20K tps. The cold-lock-acquisition cost on many distinct accounts via post_batch's FOR UPDATE pre-lock exceeds the hot-row contention cost. Append-only sidesteps both shapes (68K vs 77K).

Implication: most of what slhp was targeting (hot-account FOR UPDATE serialization) is already captured by acct-sw4i (shmem rollup eliminates the UPDATE entirely). Sharded balances' remaining benefit is only the logical 'this account must agree across writers' relaxation in scenarios where readers depend on strict monotonic balance, not contention relief.

Recommend: re-evaluate slhp scope after sw4i lands. May converge to a much narrower scope or be obviated entirely depending on what shmem rollup leaves on the table.

title: Direction 2: claim-and-finalize wrapper architecture (Phase A/B)
description: acct-8hv2 audit direction 2. System-wide generalization of the c4p pseudo-sync pattern: split candidate wrappers into Phase A (validate + claim, commit) and Phase B (re-verify preconditions, finalize via post_posting_lines, commit). Optimistic concurrency with explicit preconditions; ledger writes remain serializable. Caller-visible failure becomes a NAMED claim state (committed/aborted-precondition-X/failed/dead). See --design for full failure-mode catalog + candidate list. Stability gain: caller latency stops depending on other callers' transaction duration. Certainty gain: failure modes become enumerable, not emergent.
design:
acct-8hv2 audit direction 2 — claim-and-finalize wrapper architecture (Phase A/B).

WHY: Today every wrapper holds FOR UPDATE on document tables (purchase_order_lines, sales_order_lines, work_orders, etc.) for its full duration (~2s at p99 on transport-bound wrappers). This blocks any other wrapper that needs to read those rows. The audit identified the post_so_ship ↔ post_customer_invoice race on sales_order_lines as the most consequential case (psync removal of so_ship's so_line lock dropped customer_invoice setup p99 by 99.6%). Direction 2 generalizes this pattern: split EVERY candidate wrapper into Phase A (validate, claim, commit) and Phase B (re-verify preconditions, finalize via post_posting_lines, commit). Caller-visible consistency becomes "committed | aborted-precondition-X | failed | dead" — a NAMED state machine instead of "exception or success."

CONSISTENCY MODEL: optimistic concurrency with explicit preconditions, hoisted from MVCC to the application layer. Ledger writes remain strictly serializable (FOR UPDATE on accounts inside Phase B is unchanged). Caller-visible semantics shift: the call returns "claim durable; outcome will be notified" instead of "everything happened atomically."

FAILURE-MODE CATALOG (full reasoning from 2026-05-11 session):

A. Database/server crash. Phase A and Phase B are each their own ACID tx; WAL persists both; recovery same as existing ledger_outbox. NO NEW failure surface.

B. Network failure caller↔DB during Phase A. Caller retries with idempotency_key; UNIQUE catches duplicate claim; caller waits at rendezvous OR polls outbox.status. NO NEW failure surface.

C. Network failure between Phase A commit and rendezvous notification. Caller times out; falls back to polling. Same as today's c4p path. NO NEW failure surface.

D. Drainer crash mid-finalize. Phase B's tx rolls back; claim returns to pending; next iteration retries. NO NEW failure surface vs existing outbox.

E. THE REAL NEW HAZARD: precondition violation between Phase A and Phase B. Phase A observed state S at time T; concurrent writer mutated to S'; Phase B re-checks and sees S'. Mitigation: Phase A captures explicit preconditions (row versions via xmin or explicit version column) in the claim payload. Phase B re-verifies under FOR UPDATE BEFORE finalizing. On failure: mark claim 'aborted' with named precondition; notify caller. Two policy options per-wrapper: STRICT (abort) or LENIENT (re-evaluate against current state). The policy is explicit per-wrapper, not hidden.

F. Dead-letter / poison-pill claims. Add max_attempts to ledger_outbox (already has attempt_count); on exceed, status='dead'; reconciliation check #16 surfaces; operator escalation.

G. Drainer permanently down. Caller rendezvous times out; outbox depth grows; reconciliation alert fires. Operational, not consistency.

H. Reservation lifecycle coherence. Today's reservation flip is atomic with ship. In direction 2: introduce 'shipping' intermediate state. Phase A flips active→shipping. Phase B flips shipping→shipped atomic with ledger write. Compensator on Phase B failure: shipping→active. Adds one state to reservation_status enum.

I. Multi-drainer ordering. perf_baseline_v0 shape K shows multi-drainer regresses. Stay single-drainer (FIFO on outbox by id); per-(sku, location) causality preserved by Phase B's FOR UPDATE.

J. Idempotency_key alignment. Single claim_idempotency_key UUID; drainer reuses for the posting_line. UNIQUE on both tables. Either retry path lands on the same idempotent result.

NOT-CANDIDATES (explicit):
- post_eco_approve — needs unique-active-ECO invariant; serializability of approval is the point; keep sync.
- post_standard_cost_roll — touches every account; nothing to gain from Phase A/B split.
- post_journal_entry — small, fast, not contention-bound.
- post_service_bill / post_expense_report — same.
- Period close — already orchestrated.
- post_cost_adjustment_retroactive — already queue-then-flush-at-close.

CANDIDATES (initial cut, driven by acct-xr5j direction 1's incidence matrix):
- post_so_ship (already piloted via post_so_ship_psync; c4p infrastructure proven).
- post_customer_invoice (the cross-wrapper relief target).
- post_po_receipt / post_ap_bill (PO/AP cycle has similar cross-wrapper race shape).
- post_so_allocate / post_so_ship (allocate→ship pair).

DELIVERABLE: per-candidate, a new wrapper_psync entry-point + reservation lifecycle extension if needed. SUB-ISSUES per candidate; this issue is the umbrella spec + failure-mode catalog.

DEPS: BLOCKED-BY acct-xr5j (direction 1 — need the matrix before knowing which wrappers are candidates) AND acct-bdq6 (decision tree for shape-L applicability — same input).

PRIORITY: lowest of the four directions. Single-wrapper psync (c4p / post_so_ship_psync) is shipped and provides the proof-of-concept; system-wide direction 2 is a significantly larger commitment and should wait for directions 1, 5, 3 to land their stability gains first.

title: Shape-L applicability decision tree — when is c4p the right tool?
description:
## Why this exists

acct-c4p shipped shape-L pseudo-sync infrastructure (mig 0070 + tests/common/psync_runtime.rs + load_phase1_mixed_workload T4_USE_PSYNC=1 opt-in). The actual measurement vs h73o prediction:

| Predicted | Measured |
|---|---|
| post_so_ship p99 ~25 ms (110× drop) | post_so_ship p99 2043 ms (1.4× drop) |
| Combined-wrapper p99 ~3100 ms ceiling | Combined-wrapper p99 went UP 2902 → 3931 ms |
| Throughput ~unchanged | Throughput -28% (253 → 183 ops/s) |

Root cause of the gap: the h73o prediction extrapolated from perf_baseline_v0 shape-L (100-writer single-account contention, 15× p99 drop) to the spread workload of 1s6r. Spread workloads run parallel sync post_posting_lines across 32 writers; shape L's single drainer funnels them serially, becoming the new bottleneck.

The takeaway: **shape L is for shared-write contention, not transport contention generally**. Migrating a wrapper to shape L can WORSEN combined-workload metrics when the workload is spread.

## What this issue ships

A small, reusable decision aid that callable BEFORE migrating any new wrapper to psync. Could be:

(a) A Rust-side bench harness that takes a wrapper name + workload mix + writer count, runs both sync and psync variants for ~60s each, reports caller p99 / combined p99 / throughput delta, and outputs a clear "migrate? yes/no" verdict.

(b) A documented checklist in perf_baseline_v2.md or research/c4p-decision.md with measurable criteria:
   - "Are >50% of writer p99 attempts hitting the same row at any time?"
   - "Does the wrapper have a Q-shape lock-contention profile (perf_baseline_v0 shape D/E) or an F-shape (spread)?"
   - "Will migrating create cross-wrapper drainer contention with still-sync wrappers?"

Lean (b) first: cheap to write, immediately useful, and informs the design of (a) later.

## Acceptance

- Decision-tree document or harness shipped.
- Applied retroactively to the four hot wrappers (so_ship, wo_start, op_move, customer_invoice): does each pass the criteria?
- For each: ship/skip recommendation backed by measurement.

## Out of scope

- Re-measuring c4p itself with a different workload mix (could be a separate followup).
- Building the multi-drainer alternative (K-shape; per perf_baseline_v0, multi-drainer regresses).
- Adapting psync_runtime to support per-wrapper drainers (architectural; would need its own design).
notes:
UNBLOCKED 2026-05-11 by acct-8hv2 audit (research/architectural-review-2026-05-11.md). Decision tree shape from audit Phase F1: USE shape-L when wrapper pair A↔B shares FOR UPDATE on a *document* table (so_lines, po_lines, wo_events, etc.) AND A fits psync shape (no caller reads of posted ledger). DO NOT USE when contention is intra-wrapper or on accounts table. Measured cost on 1s6r: -20% throughput, +18% deadlocks. Acceptable when latency relief on the targeted wrapper pair exceeds throughput cost. See audit Tables C2 and D2 for evidence. Implementation: ship a markdown decision-tree doc citing the audit findings; no code changes.
Re-pointed 2026-08-07 (convergence Q9b): acct-qdp5 closed UNVERDICTED; this issue stands independently. The shape-L applicability decision tree concerns acct-main outbox/psync wrappers — deferred with the document layer under Q2. The acct-8hv2 audit evidence base is unchanged.

title: post_customer_invoice setup contention — option (c): materialized per-so_line running totals
description:
## Why this exists

acct-3aak shipped option (a) — aggregate-batching outside the per-line FOR LOOP — and measured the result against the h73o baseline. (a) was a noise term: setup p99 3127ms → 3333ms (within rig variance, deadlocks 513 → 548). p50 / p95 both flat. See perf_baseline_v2.md "acct-3aak measurement (option (a) shipped — mig 0069)" addendum for full numbers.

This confirms the plan-3aak "stays 500-3000ms" decisional branch: the per-line aggregate SUMs were NOT the dominant cost; the remaining setup-side contention lives in the per-line FOR UPDATE OF sl serialization chain against contemporaneous post_so_ship + per-line indexed account lookups (v_cust_unsettled, v_match_tol_acct).

## Option (c)

Materialize per-so_line running totals via trigger-maintained columns or a sibling projection table:
  - sales_order_lines.qty_shipped_running (or so_line_totals.qty_shipped)
  - sales_order_lines.qty_invoiced_running
  - sales_order_lines.qty_returned_to_ar_unsettled_running

Maintained inside _post_posting_lines_apply_event (so the projection is in-transaction with the underlying ledger writes; no async catch-up race).

The per-line cumulative check in post_customer_invoice then reads three indexed columns from the FOR UPDATE'd so_line row — already locked, already in cache. The aggregate scans go away entirely.

Sibling work: per-line account-id lookups (v_cust_unsettled inside the LOOP, v_match_tol_acct inside the diff_total branch) could memoize once per invoice. Cheap to ship in the same migration as (c).

## Acceptance

- Schema migration adds maintained running totals (columns or projection table).
- Triggers / apply_event extensions update totals atomically with the underlying ledger event.
- Backfill from existing posting_lines on migration apply (Phase 0/1 has no production data so this is just a one-shot computed UPDATE).
- post_customer_invoice CREATE OR REPLACE replaces per-invoice JSONB-aggregate (the mig 0069 surface) with per-line so_line projection read.
- Account-id memoization in same mig: hoist v_cust_unsettled lookup outside the LOOP (per-currency-customer, same in every iteration).
- Full suite stays green.
- Re-run T4_DURATION_SECS=600 T4_WRITERS=32 T4_REPORT_TIMINGS=1 perf measurement; target setup p99 < 200ms (matching post_so_ship / post_op_move / post_wo_start's setup p99s — they were 23131µs / 11126µs / 10145µs in h73o).

## Risks

R1 — Trigger-maintained totals fan out to all callers that INSERT into so_shipment_lines / customer_invoice_lines / customer_return_lines. Need to verify which paths exist (so_ship; customer_invoice; customer_return; the standalone memo wrappers) and update the schema appropriately.

R2 — Backfill consistency at migration time: the computed UPDATE must hold a moment-of-truth lock against any concurrent writer. Doable but needs a brief blocking pass.

R3 — Memoization correctness: v_cust_unsettled, v_match_tol_acct are tied to (kind, counterparty_id, currency) — all stable across an invoice. Safe to hoist. Verify there is no per-line currency override (there isn't — the wrapper rejects line-level currency mismatch up front).

## Out of scope

- Reservation lifecycle changes (those go through other wrappers).
- Multi-currency posting normalization.
- Customer credit memo + vendor debit memo running totals (different conventions; surface separately if a sibling contention pattern emerges in their workloads).
notes: Filed 2026-05-11 after acct-3aak option (a) measurement. Decisional branch was 'setup p99 stays 500-3000ms' per plan-3aak-2026-05-11. Pre-condition: build on mig 0069 baseline. h73o instrumentation remains shipped, so pre/post measurement is one perf-run away.

title: post_customer_invoice setup-side contention: SO-line FOR UPDATE + aggregate SELECTs
description:
## Why this issue exists

acct-h73o decomposed the 1s6r combined-wrapper p99 tail. Three of four hot wrappers are >99% transport-dominated (acct-c4p addresses those). The outlier is **post_customer_invoice**: >99.8% of its p99 (3127ms of 3132ms total) lives in the SETUP section, NOT in post_posting_lines (only 5ms p99).

acct-c4p cannot help post_customer_invoice. This is a separate fix.

## Root cause

Inside the per-line FOR LOOP in post_customer_invoice (mig 0018 line 744 onward), each `so_match` line does:

  1. `SELECT sl.so_id, sl.unit_price, sl.currency, so.customer_id INTO v_sl
       FROM sales_order_lines sl
       JOIN sales_orders so ON so.id = sl.so_id
      WHERE sl.id = v_so_line_id
        FOR UPDATE OF sl;`  -- row lock on sales_order_lines.id
  2. `SELECT COALESCE(SUM(qty_shipped), 0) INTO v_total_shipped
       FROM so_shipment_lines WHERE so_line_id = v_so_line_id;` -- aggregate scan
  3. `SELECT COALESCE(SUM(qty), 0) INTO v_total_invoiced
       FROM customer_invoice_lines
      WHERE so_line_id = v_so_line_id AND kind = 'so_match';` -- aggregate scan
  4. `SELECT COALESCE(SUM(crl.qty_to_ar_unsettled), 0) INTO v_returns_to_us
       FROM customer_return_lines crl
       JOIN so_shipment_lines ssl ON ssl.id = crl.ship_line_id
      WHERE ssl.so_line_id = v_so_line_id;` -- aggregate scan with JOIN

Under 32-writer concurrency: a contemporaneous post_so_ship (which also touches the same so_shipment_lines side) lengthens the wait on the aggregate SUMs, AND the FOR UPDATE OF sl on the SAME so_line that an SO-allocation/cancel might also touch creates a per-so_line serialization chain.

The three aggregates also re-scan the same partitioned tables that the ongoing workload is writing. Under contention they accrue lock waits behind WAL flushes / index inserts.

Why this exists: the FOR UPDATE was defensive against concurrent SO modifications. The 3 aggregate SUMs implement the strict cumulative-cumulative three-way match (qty <= shipped - already_invoiced - prior_returns_to_us, mig 0018 line 818).

## Candidate fixes

**(a) Batch the aggregates OUTSIDE the FOR LOOP / OUTSIDE the FOR UPDATE.** All N invoice lines share the same so_id; the three aggregates can be a single GROUP BY scan per invoice, computed BEFORE acquiring per-line locks. Reduces 3 aggregate scans per line to 3 per invoice. Trade-off: cumulative remainder calc is per-so-line, not per-invoice; still has to dispatch per-line at the application layer, but the scans are batched at the SQL layer.

**(b) Replace FOR UPDATE OF sl with optimistic check.** At so_line grain the row is conceptually immutable post-creation (unit_price, qty_ordered, customer_id, currency don't change after the SO is locked-in). The FOR UPDATE is defensive against a non-existent threat model. Drop it; the cumulative three-way match still catches over-invoice via the aggregate check. Trade-off: if SO cancellation ever flips a so_line state mid-invoice, that race becomes possible — file SO-cancel design as joint concern.

**(c) Hoist cumulative shipped/invoiced/returned aggregates into a materialized per-so_line projection refreshed in apply_event.** Trigger-maintained per-so_line running totals (qty_shipped, qty_invoiced, qty_returned_to_us) updated as post_so_ship / post_customer_invoice / post_customer_return commit. SO-line read becomes a single index hit. Trade-off: write-amplification (3 extra UPDATEs per ship/invoice/return), schema growth, but ELIMINATES the scan cost.

**LEAN: (a) + (b).** Cheapest combination. The aggregates batch-precompute outside the loop (single index range scan per source table per invoice, not per-line). Drop FOR UPDATE OF sl — defer SO-cancellation race to a future SO-state-machine issue if/when SO cancel ever ships.

## Acceptance

- post_customer_invoice CREATE OR REPLACE with restructured setup
- Aggregates run once per invoice over the union of involved so_line_ids, not per-line
- FOR UPDATE OF sl removed (no concurrent threat model justifies it at so_line grain)
- Per-line remainder check unchanged in correctness (still strict cumulative)
- Re-run T4_REPORT_TIMINGS=1 600s x 32w; verify post_customer_invoice setup p99 drops materially (target: under 50ms)
- Full test suite still 1073/0/9 (or current oracle)
- ci-check clean
- perf_baseline_v2 addendum extended with the new measurement

## Decisional outcome

If post_customer_invoice setup p99 drops below post_posting_lines p99 (~5ms): victory; combined-wrapper p99 then bottoms on the remaining tails (which c4p will address).

If setup p99 stays above 100ms despite batching: file additional issue for option (c) materialized per-so_line projection.

## Estimate

1-2 hours: read post_customer_invoice body verbatim from mig 0018, write the surgical mig (likely 0069), re-run smoke + 30s + 600s with timings, verify oracle.

## References

- perf_baseline_v2.md addendum (acct-h73o verdict)
- acct-c4p (transport-side companion; c4p alone doesn't fix this wrapper)
- mig 0068_wrapper_instrumentation (instrumentation tool stays; flip T4_REPORT_TIMINGS=1)
notes:
REVISION 2026-05-11 — option (b) DROPPED per user correction.

Original draft proposed dropping FOR UPDATE OF sl on the basis that "so_line is conceptually immutable post-creation." That reasoning is wrong for an ERP. Real-world SO-line mutations that are absolutely in-scope for any production system:
  - Price renegotiation (unit_price changes after SO lock-in, before invoicing)
  - Quantity adjustments (qty_ordered up or down)
  - Discount application (unit_price drops)
  - Line cancellation (status flip)
  - Sales-rep typo corrections

The FOR UPDATE OF sl protects the tolerance check at the post_customer_invoice line 779 path (IF v_unit_price <> v_sl.unit_price -> IF v_diff_pct > v_tolerance_pct). Under READ COMMITTED, an SO-line edit committing between the SELECT and the diff compute would let an out-of-tolerance invoice slip through without the row lock. That is a correctness hole, not a perf nit. The lock stays.

REVISED PATH:
  (a) FIRST — batch the three aggregates outside the per-line FOR LOOP (one scan per invoice, not per line). Surgical; ~1 hour; no schema change. Independently correct regardless of locking.
  (c) MEASURE-THEN-DECIDE — re-run h73o instrumentation after (a) ships. If post_customer_invoice setup p99 drops materially (say <200ms), stop and pivot to c4p. If setup p99 stays high after (a), the FOR UPDATE OF sl contention with post_so_ship is the dominator and (c) (materialized per-so_line running totals) is the right next move.

The (a)-then-measure ordering also tells us WHICH cost matters: (a) helps if aggregate-scan cost dominates; (a) doesn't help much if cross-wrapper lock chain dominates. We don't know today.

When (c) eventually ships, any future change to the cumulative-remainder logic MUST continue to protect against a contemporaneous SO-line edit (not just the running-totals UPDATE).
close_reason: Option (a) shipped via mig 0069 (commit 39d0fe5). Aggregate-batching is independently correct (T1 19/0, property test clean) but was a noise term under contention: setup p99 3127ms → 3333ms, within rig variance. Per plan-3aak-2026-05-11 'stays 500-3000ms' branch: FOR UPDATE OF sl serialization chain + per-line account lookups dominate. Filed acct-3zfj for option (c) (materialized per-so_line running totals + account-id memoization). Perf addendum updated.

title: Profile 1s6r wrappers to decompose p99 tail (gates acct-c4p ROI)
description:
## Why this issue exists

acct-1s6r (shipped 2026-05-11, perf_baseline_v2.md) measured the end-to-end Slice A+B+C mixed-workload baseline: 32 writers × 600s, p50=19ms, p99=2353ms, 513 deadlocks. acct-c4p (pseudo-sync pivot trigger) is now FIRED — combined wrapper p99 4.7× the 500ms threshold.

But acct-c4p shipping shape L (pseudo-sync transport) is 1-3 days of real work (production wrapper migration + supervision + error-contract + per-call-site test rewrites). Before paying that cost, we need to know: **is the p99 tail dominated by the transport (post_posting_lines + FOR UPDATE serialization), or by wrapper-side work that shape L cannot help?**

This issue measures that decomposition. Output is a decisional gate, not a code change.

## The hypothesis to test

Each wrapper call decomposes as:
  total = wrapper_setup + post_posting_lines + wrapper_followup

  - wrapper_setup: account lookups (7+ SELECTs in post_so_ship), idempotency probe, validation
  - post_posting_lines: the lock-contended core (FOR UPDATE on shared inventory pools)
  - wrapper_followup: line-table audit writes (so_shipment_lines.unit_cost, etc.) + state-machine updates

acct-c4p's shape L compresses ONLY post_posting_lines. If the p99 tail is dominated by post_posting_lines (predicted), c4p is the right lever. If wrapper_setup or wrapper_followup dominates, c4p won't help and the bottleneck is elsewhere (e.g., excessive SELECTs in wrapper bodies — separate issue).

## Scope

1. Add per-section timing instrumentation to the four hottest wrappers (by 1s6r mean_ms): post_so_ship, post_customer_invoice, post_wo_start, post_op_move. Each section records its elapsed-µs in a local table or via RAISE NOTICE collected by the test.

2. Re-run load_phase1_mixed_workload at 32 writers × 600s with instrumentation active.

3. Decompose p50 / p95 / p99 / max per wrapper into the three sections.

4. Report findings in a short addendum to perf_baseline_v2.md (or perf_baseline_v2b.md if cleaner).

5. Update acct-c4p notes with the decomposition: either confirming the transport-dominated hypothesis (c4p ROI real) or surfacing wrapper-side issues (file new issues for those, downgrade c4p).

## Approach options

**Option A: PL/pgSQL inline timing via temp table.**
Add `INSERT INTO _wrapper_section_timings (wrapper_name, section, started_at, elapsed_us)` calls at section boundaries inside the wrappers. Test reads the table at the end.
Pros: precise, no app-layer changes. Cons: writes contend with the workload (may bias measurements).

**Option B: clock_timestamp() RAISE NOTICE.**
RAISE NOTICE 'TIMING wrapper=X section=Y elapsed_us=Z' at each boundary. Test harness parses notices via the connection's notice handler.
Pros: no extra table I/O. Cons: notice volume could be heavy; harness wiring nontrivial.

**Option C: SET LOCAL track_planning + pg_stat_statements at FUNCTION level.**
Wrappers internally already CALL post_posting_lines as a SELECT. pg_stat_statements at function-call granularity gives us mean_ms per inner statement.
Pros: zero code changes. Cons: doesn't decompose within a single wrapper invocation; aggregate only.

**Option D: app-layer split.**
Replace wrapper calls in the harness with their decomposed shape: writer issues raw SQL for the lookups, then calls a wrapper variant that takes pre-resolved account IDs and skips lookup, then a separate call for the followup writes.
Pros: clean separation. Cons: forks the wrapper API for measurement purposes.

**LEAN: Option A.** Smallest behavior delta. The instrumentation table can use UNLOGGED to avoid WAL cost. Truncate before each run. Read aggregates post-run.

## Acceptance

- New mig (or instrumentation-only patch) adds _wrapper_section_timings temp/unlogged table + RAISE-or-INSERT timing at section boundaries in 4 wrappers
- Re-run of 1s6r at default settings captures timings into the table
- Aggregate query reports per-wrapper per-section p50/p95/p99 in microseconds
- perf_baseline_v2 addendum doc captures the headline decomposition
- acct-c4p notes updated with the verdict (either "transport dominates, c4p ROI confirmed" or "wrapper overhead dominates, c4p deferred, file <new issues>")

## Decisional outcome

If post_posting_lines section is >60% of p99 across the 4 wrappers: claim acct-c4p next; the ROI is concrete.

If post_posting_lines is <40%: file new issues for wrapper-side bottlenecks (likely account-lookup batching). Defer c4p until those are addressed and re-baseline reveals contention again.

If post_posting_lines is 40-60%: c4p remains worth doing but expectation-set: gain will be partial (maybe 2-3× p99 improvement rather than 10-15×).

## Out of scope

- Profiling at the SQL-statement level inside post_posting_lines (separate issue if needed).
- Profiling the apply_event vs lock-pre-scan split inside post_posting_lines.
- Cross-currency / lot+serial / period-close workload variants.
- Production wrapper code changes (instrumentation is for measurement only and reverts after).

## Estimate

30 minutes to 1 hour of work:
  - 15 min: write instrumentation migration (UNLOGGED table + RAISE/INSERT in 4 wrappers)
  - 15 min: re-run 1s6r workload
  - 10 min: aggregate query + addendum doc
  - 10 min: bd notes updates on acct-c4p

## Reference data

- perf_baseline_v2.md (1s6r baseline, this is what we're decomposing)
- acct-c4p (gated on this issue's verdict)
- acct-zroo (SERIALIZABLE investigation — sibling concern; same data informs that decision)
- CLAUDE.md "Sync post_posting_lines for now" load-bearing decision (this work is what informs the pivot)

## Priority

P3 — small, fast, decision-gating. Should ship before claiming acct-c4p.
close_reason: Instrumentation shipped via mig 0068. Decomposition verdict in perf_baseline_v2.md addendum: 3 of 4 hot wrappers >99% transport-dominated (gates on acct-c4p), 1 wrapper >99.8% setup-dominated (handled by acct-3aak). Suite verification deferred per user direction; commit 5ed8944.

title: Lot+Serial — serial as traceability metadata over lot_fifo costing
description:
WHY: Industry-standard pattern (SAP "Batch-with-Serial-Profile", Oracle "Lot+Serial", D365 lot+serial tracking dimensions) — pharma / med-devices / packaged-goods need per-unit traceability (warranty, recall, FDA UDI) but cost at LOT grain. Each serial inherits cost from its parent lot; serial is metadata only.

Distinct from acct-0kz (full E3 cost-at-serial) — that's the aerospace / heavy-equipment / engineered-to-order model where each unit carries its own unit_cost. This issue is the much smaller increment that leverages all existing lot_fifo infrastructure.

SCOPE:
1. Schema:
   - skus.tracked_by ENUM extension: add 'lot_and_serial' value.
   - New table inventory_units(unit_id BIGSERIAL, product_id UUID, lot_id BIGINT NOT NULL, lot_receipt_date DATE NOT NULL, serial_no VARCHAR(128), status TEXT, current_location_id UUID, work_order_id UUID NULL, customer_id UUID NULL, mfg_date DATE NULL, expiry_date DATE NULL, attributes JSONB, received_at TIMESTAMPTZ, receipt_posting_line_id BIGINT REFERENCES posting_lines, FK to inventory_lots on composite (lot_id, lot_receipt_date), UNIQUE (product_id, serial_no), PARTITION BY RANGE (received_at)).
   - New table inventory_unit_events(event_id BIGSERIAL, unit_id BIGINT, event_type SMALLINT, posting_line_id BIGINT REFERENCES posting_lines, business_date DATE, from_location_id UUID NULL, to_location_id UUID NULL, notes TEXT, created_at TIMESTAMPTZ, PARTITION BY RANGE (business_date)). event_type taxonomy: 1=receipt 2=issue 3=transfer 4=hold 5=release 6=warranty_register 7=warranty_expire 8=scrap 9=lost.
   - Append-only trigger via shared block_inventory_lot_modifications fn.
   - inventory_reservations.unit_ids BIGINT[] NULL for unit-pinned reservations.

2. NO cost_method change. lot_fifo continues to dispatch at the lot grain; serial is metadata only. inventory_units.unit_cost is REMOVED from the schema (vs the catch-weight-derived plan in acct-0kz) — for lot_and_serial SKUs the unit inherits its parent lot's unit_cost via JOIN.

3. Wrapper integration:
   - post_po_receipt accepts unit_serials TEXT[] for tracked_by='lot_and_serial' SKUs alongside the existing lot_code. Creates inventory_units rows per serial under the new lot.
   - post_so_ship accepts unit_ids BIGINT[] (or unit_serials TEXT[] resolved to ids). Marks units status='sold', emits inventory_unit_events type=2.
   - post_wo_complete accepts unit_serials TEXT[] for the FG outputs. Creates units under the new FG lot.
   - post_inventory_adjustment accepts unit_ids (or unit_serials) for tracked_by='lot_and_serial' SKUs.
   - post_lot_transfer creates new units at destination tied to the new dest lot, drains source units, emits inventory_unit_events type=3.
   - rm_issue_to_wo similar — consumed units linked to wo_lot_consumption.

4. Recon check #14 (next slot): per (lot_id, lot_receipt_date), COUNT(units WHERE status='available') = lot_residual_qty (already computed by check #9). Catches drift where units exist but their parent lot's qty was depleted without unit_event, or vice versa.

5. Optional T1+P1 coverage: receipt with units, ship with unit_ids, warranty event lifecycle, unit count vs lot residual recon, multi-WO unit-genealogy via lot_genealogy already-shipped infrastructure.

EFFORT: ~1-2 weeks (1 mig schema + 1 mig dispatcher hooks + 4-6 wrapper extensions + ~12 T1 cases + property test). Much smaller than acct-0kz's multi-month effort because cost stays at lot grain.

NOT IN SCOPE:
- Per-unit unit_cost (that's acct-0kz / full E3 cost-at-serial).
- Unit lifecycle automation (warranty expiry cron, status-based archival to cold partition — separate operational sub-issue).
- post_journal_entry on serial-specific accounts.

REFERENCES:
- Saved memory state-2026-05-09-phase-f-complete-e2e3-planned §E3 schema sketch (the inventory_units / inventory_unit_events tables; this issue drops the unit_cost / cost_currency columns since lot drives costing).
- research/cost-methods-subledger-design.md §9.5 ('lot_and_serial' dimension toggle).
- ERPs surveyed: SAP S/4HANA "Batch with Serial Profile", Oracle Cloud "Lot and Serial Numbers", D365 F&O "Tracking dimension group" (cost dim toggle), NetSuite "Inventory Serial/Lot Tracking".
close_reason: All 6 sub-issues (.1–.6) shipped 2026-05-10 → 2026-05-11. Final commit 717efbe on main. Migrations 0061–0066 ship inventory_units + inventory_unit_events schema, apply_event E2.5 dispatcher, wrappers A/B/C (po_receipt + inventory_adjustment + so_ship + wo_complete + lot_transfer + rm_issue_to_wo), wo_unit_consumption mirror table, and recon check #14. Full suite 1065/0/9; ci-check clean.

title: Lot-epic follow-up: lot genealogy (parent-child lineage)
description:
When a WO produces an FG-lot from raw-component lots, the produced lot inherits cost from the consumed lots but the LINEAGE (this FG-lot was made from these specific raw lots) is currently unrecoverable except by reconstructing from posting_lines + inventory_lot_events JOIN at WO-document grain.

SCOPE:
1. New table lot_genealogy (parent_lot_id BIGINT, parent_receipt_date DATE, child_lot_id BIGINT, child_receipt_date DATE, qty_consumed NUMERIC, wo_id UUID NULL, posting_line_id BIGINT REFERENCES posting_lines, recorded_at TIMESTAMPTZ). Composite FK to inventory_lots on both sides.
2. _wo_emit_bom_lines (consume) and post_wo_complete (produce) cooperate: when wo_complete creates an FG inventory_lots row (lot_fifo parent path from mig 0050), it INSERTs lot_genealogy rows tying each consumed component lot to the new FG lot. qty_consumed is split proportionally if multiple FG lots emerge from one WO (rare; primary case is 1 FG lot per WO_complete).
3. Lineage query: recursive CTE 'walk genealogy backwards from FG-lot=X' returns full upstream chain.
4. Forward-chaining: 'what FG-lots used component lot=Y' inverts the join.
5. Compliance use case: pharma recall of vendor lot V → identify all FG lots that consumed it via lot_genealogy → cascade through downstream sales.
6. Optional: store yield_loss qty per genealogy row when FG-output qty differs from consumed (covers scrap/yield variance attribution).
7. Recon: SUM(lot_genealogy.qty_consumed) per (parent_lot_id) ≤ SUM(inventory_lot_events.quantity_change) for issue events on that lot. Add as recon check #12 (loose bound, not equality, since some lots may consume to scrap without an FG-side genealogy).

EFFORT: 2-3 days (schema + post_wo_complete extension + recursive CTE views + T1 + property test for recall scenarios).

REFERENCES:
- Saved memory state-2026-05-10-e2-7-shipped lists this as remaining lot follow-up.
- Mainstream-ERP convention: SAP Batch Where-Used / Oracle WMS Genealogy / NetSuite Lot Tracking all maintain explicit parent-child lot graphs.
- Out-of-scope at MVP per saved memory; file when traceability/recall scenarios become real.

title: Lot-epic follow-up: lot transfers between locations (post_lot_transfer)
description:
post_lot_transfer wrapper for moving a specific lot (or unpinned FIFO/FEFO walk) between locations. Currently post_inventory_adjustment with location-change is the only path and it explicitly blocks lot SKUs at any cross-location semantics. Need a first-class transfer document.

SCOPE:
1. New table lot_transfers (id UUID PK, from_location_id, to_location_id, posted_at, posted_by, idempotency_key UUID UNIQUE) + lot_transfer_lines (transfer_id FK, sku_id, qty, lot_id NULLABLE for unpinned).
2. New posting_line_reason 'lot_transfer'. Apply_event handles dual-leg posting:
   - qty leg: debit stock_available@to_loc, credit stock_available@from_loc
   - value leg: debit inv_value_*@to_loc, credit inv_value_*@from_loc; same currency same value
3. Lot subledger: writes inventory_lot_events 'transfer' (event_type=4 per acct-uze design) decrementing residual at from_loc, AND a NEW inventory_lots row at to_loc carrying same lot_code (or an override) with same expiration_date / unit_cost / supplier_lot_number.
4. Strategy: by default, lot row at to_loc inherits ALL metadata from source lot (audit-preserving). lot_code uniqueness per (product, entity, lot_code, receipt_date) — receipt_date for the destination is the transfer date (so naturally distinct).
5. Three-walk pattern: wrapper specifies lot_id pin OR unpinned (FIFO/FEFO walk via skus.allocation_strategy); apply_event re-walks under FOR UPDATE.
6. Recon invariant: net qty conservation across (sku, *, period) — sum of from-leg negatives + to-leg positives = 0 per transfer.
7. T1 cases: pin transfer / unpinned walk / strategy=fefo / partial qty / cross-currency rejection (P0006) / idempotent replay / recon clean.

EFFORT: 1.5-2 days (schema mig + apply_event extension + wrapper + ~10 t1 cases).

REFERENCES:
- Saved memory state-2026-05-10-e2-7-shipped (lot transfers listed as remaining lot follow-up).
- Cost-methods doc §9.x for lot transfer model (status='transferred' on source, fresh row at dest).

title: Lot-epic follow-up: lot_fifo parent + by-products at post_wo_complete
description:
Currently when a lot_fifo parent SKU has by-products configured (bom_by_products), post_wo_complete's by-products pre-pass at mig 0050 raises P0006 because the apply_event by-product credit path is gated on parent cost_method='standard' or WAC family. lot_fifo parents should also be supported. title: Lot-epic follow-up: op_arrival lot pinning persistence in WO routing
description:
Currently when a WO with lot_fifo components reaches op_move, _wo_emit_bom_lines walks _lot_walk_layers without persisting which lot was selected. If the op-arrival event is replayed (or downstream traceability is queried), the lot lineage is lost beyond inventory_lot_events. Worse: per-routing-op cost-flow analysis can't tie a specific lot consumption to a specific routing_op without joining transfer-time data.

SCOPE:
1. New table wo_lot_consumption (wo_id FK, routing_op INT, sku_id, lot_id, lot_receipt_date, qty NUMERIC, posted_at, posting_line_id REFERENCES posting_lines).
2. _wo_emit_bom_lines extended: after the dispatcher computes value via _lot_walk_layers walk, the helper also INSERTs one row per consumed lot into wo_lot_consumption stamping the routing_op + the posting_line_id.
3. p_component_lot_pins JSONB extension at post_wo_start/op_move continues to work — pinned consumption fills wo_lot_consumption with the pinned lot_id; unpinned fills with the walked lot_ids.
4. Audit query support: 'show me every lot that fed into WO=X' joins wo_lot_consumption for the answer.
5. Recon: wo_lot_consumption.qty SUM per (wo_id, sku_id, lot_id) = inventory_lot_events SUM where document_id matches wo_event document. Add as recon check #11.
6. T1: lot_fifo component end-to-end via WO; op_move arrival on next op picks up SAME lot_id when pinned; multi-component multi-op coverage.

EFFORT: 1-1.5 days (schema mig + _wo_emit_bom_lines extension + recon + ~6-8 t1 cases).

REFERENCES:
- Mig 0049 (acct-7jkk) ships _wo_emit_bom_lines lot branch with p_component_lot_pins JSONB but doesn't persist beyond inventory_lot_events.posting_line_id.
- Saved memory state-2026-05-10-e2-7-shipped lists this as remaining lot follow-up.
- Mainstream-ERP convention: SAP MM-IM stores per-WO lot consumption explicitly for traceability.
close_reason: Closed

title: Lot-epic follow-up: per-lot value-level subledger↔GL recon (check #11)
description:
Recon check #9 (lot_residual_mismatch, mig 0051) compares lot side residual (SUM original_quantity + SUM event qty_delta) vs on_hand stock_available net qty. This is QTY-level only. The keystone D5 invariant has subledger ↔ GL value-level check at (product, location, period) grain (recon check #7). Need a deeper variant for lot-tracked SKUs at (product, location, period, lot_id) grain.

SCOPE:
1. New recon check (#11 or whatever the next slot is — currently 10 in mig 0051): per (product, location, period, lot_id), SUM(inventory_movements.quantity * actual_unit_cost) where lot_id IS NOT NULL = SUM(posting_lines.amount) where document touches that lot via posting_line_inventory.lot_id, both filtered to that period's business_dates.
2. Tolerance: 1¢ as in check #7.
3. Why deeper: catches drift at the LOT level — e.g., if FIFO/FEFO walk wrote one lot's depletion but the apply_event D-block stamped a DIFFERENT lot_id on inventory_movements (would be a bug). Check #9 only catches qty-level drift, not value attribution mismatch.
4. T1: clean workload (no alerts) / phantom inventory_movements row with wrong lot_id (alert) / phantom posting_line_inventory.lot_id mismatch (alert).
5. Optional: also add value-level negative residual check — for lot_fifo SKU, inv_value_raw partition per lot_id should never go negative. Per saved memory, accounts.lot_id was considered but DEFERRED — confirm it's NOT in the schema today (only stock_available has lot_id-aware partitioning if at all). If accounts is NOT lot-partitioned at value side, this check reduces to the partition-by-product-location level which is what check #7 already covers — meaning #11 is meaningful only if value-side is lot-partitioned. May be a no-op until accounts.lot_id is shipped.

EFFORT: 0.5-1 day if schema is sufficient; gates on accounts.lot_id at value side if not.

REFERENCES:
- Saved memory state-2026-05-10-e2-7-shipped lists this as remaining lot follow-up.
- Cross-reference acct-uze design discussion (Q5 in saved plan) about whether accounts.lot_id partitions value-side.

title: Multi-cost-book implementation (parallel postings under different cost methods)
description:
Phase D of the convergence plan (acct-wb75) prelays cost_book_id columns in inventory_movements + the cost_books lookup table seeded with id=1 ('primary'). All Phase D dispatchers write cost_book_id=1.

This issue covers implementing actual multi-book functionality: parallel postings of the same physical inventory event under different cost methods, supporting use cases like:

- IFRS book (e.g., FIFO) alongside US-GAAP book (e.g., WAC) for entities filing under both standards
- Tax book valued under a different method than financial-reporting book
- Separate book for transfer-pricing or local statutory reporting

When this lands, post_* dispatchers iterate over enabled books per legal entity and write N inventory_movements rows per physical event (one per book), each with its own cost_method_at_event and unit_cost. Cost-method dispatch becomes (book × method) tuple, not just method.

Schema scaffold already in place from Phase D — this issue is about lifting the dispatcher and reconciliation to multi-book.

Acceptance: when one book is configured, behavior is unchanged from convergence baseline. When >1 book is configured per LE, parallel postings exist with consistent qty (qty conserved across books) and method-specific unit_cost (different cost_method_at_event per book row).

title: Document transfers row-per-pair vs row-per-leg deliberate divergence
description:
The transfers table uses TigerBeetle-style row-per-debit-credit-pair shape, while industry ERPs and the alternate ledger-architecture proposal use ACDOCA/Oracle-XLA-style row-per-leg. Our shape works (preserves double-entry; supports 3+ leg entries via shared document_id and multiple rows) but diverges from research-prescribed and industry-standard architecture. Without an explicit load-bearing-decision note, future contributors reading the proposal may 'fix' the shape and break every test and every dispatcher branch.

Per research/architecture-synthesis.md §5.1 (Single line-item store), §6.4 (drift-action acknowledged), §9.A3 (free-and-clear additive phase), §10.1.

(2) Cross-reference from CLAUDE.md 'Load-bearing design decisions' section. (3) No code or schema change.

title: WAC parents with nrv_credit by-products: by-product value leg gets re-dispatched at period close
description:
## Bug

post_wo_complete by-products pre-pass (acct-u1n9, mig 0098) is gated to STANDARD parents only. WAC parents with bom_by_products rows of treatment='nrv_credit' have their pre-pass silently skipped at wo_complete.

Root cause: the by-product value leg is 'inv_value_fg(by_product) DR / inv_value_wip(parent, last_op) CR' with reason='wo_complete_v'. Mig 0064 (acct-bol) flags wo_complete_v events into transfers_provisional when the credit-side SKU's cost_method is wac_periodic / wac_retroactive. The period-close hook then recomputes the value at the parent's final running avg.

But by-product NRV is FIXED at WO-time per the BOM declaration (treating it as a cost-method-dispatched depletion is semantically wrong — by-products represent caller-supplied salvage value, not cost flow from the parent pool).

## Scope

When lifting the gate:
1. Pick a way to NOT flag the by-product value leg at apply time. Options:
   (a) Add a new transfer_reason ('wo_byproduct_credit') NOT in the wo_complete_v flag list — lets the dispatcher / close hook ignore it, but requires schema change.
   (b) Detect by-product context in apply step (e.g. inspect document_kind or output_sku_id presence in wo_by_products) — fragile.
   (c) Bypass by setting an explicit 'no_flag' flag on the event — schema-clean and explicit.
2. Update wac_periodic_close_hook + wac_retroactive_close_hook (or the apply-time flagging gate) to skip by-product credit events.
3. Add tests for WAC parent + nrv_credit by-product across period close.

## Workaround

Until lifted: WAC parents with nrv_credit by-products silently get NO by-product recognition at wo_complete. Negligible by-products (qty leg only) would also be skipped under the current blanket gate, even though they have no flagging concern. Negligible could be unconditionally allowed, but for simplicity the current gate is blanket-on-cost-method.

## Acceptance

- WAC parent + nrv_credit by-product fires correctly at wo_complete
- Period close on a WAC parent with by-products doesn't re-dispatch the by-product credit
- assert_invariants_hold passes across the close
- Same-shape lift for wac_perpetual / wac_periodic / wac_retroactive

## Surfaced from

acct-u1n9 implementation 2026-05-06. Filed at gate-time rather than blocking u1n9 closure since the standard-parent foundational case is the larger value.
close_reason: Lifted at 9f6f66b. WAC parents (perpetual/periodic/retroactive) now run by-products pre-pass; new wo_byproduct_credit reason bypasses apply_event flagging; wac_periodic_close_hook subtracts byproduct credits from period-avg numerator; wac_retroactive's chronological replay handles the case natively. Tests cover wac_perpetual fires + wac_periodic/retroactive close-no-redispatch. Suite 807/0/9 ci-check clean. FIFO parent + by-products remains deferred.

title: acct-1cer.state_transitions: property test for post_so_allocate + post_eco_approve

Property test binary covering post_so_allocate and post_eco_approve. Both are pure state transitions (no ledger events) — assert state machine + idempotency only.

## Scope

title: Per-op by-product backflush (mid-routing emission)
description:
Filed as Phase 2+ follow-up to acct-7t4. Not blocking; core ships with by-product emission at wo_complete only.

## Why

In SAP and Oracle, by-products can be configured to backflush at any routing operation (not just at the final completion). E.g., 'kerosene fraction comes off at op30, before final blend at op40'. This affects when the by-product fg appears (partway through production, available for early downstream consumption) and how the WIP pool's value flows.

acct-7t4 ships emission at wo_complete only. That's adequate for many real workloads but not for process industries with mid-routing extraction.

## Proposed shape

bom_by_products gets a new column: emit_at_op INT (nullable; NULL = at wo_complete). When emit_at_op = N, post_op_move(N+1, ...) drains qty + value per the by-product treatment (mirroring how bom_lines fire at applies_at_op).

## Acceptance

- Schema column added; CHECK that emit_at_op exists in wo's resolved routing
- post_op_move handles by-product emission at the destination op
- Idempotency: backflush fires once per op transition, not on rework moves
- Tests: by-product fires at op30, parent continues to op40, wo_complete handles only remaining by-products

title: By-product NRV LCM revaluation at period close (ASC 330 / IAS 2)
description:
Filed as Phase 2+ follow-up to acct-7t4. Not blocking; core by-product feature ships without this.

## Why

ASC 330 and IAS 2 require by-product fg pools booked at NRV (nrv_credit treatment from acct-7t4.3) to be revalued at period close if NRV has dropped. ASC 330: write-downs are PERMANENT (no reversal allowed). IAS 2: write-downs CAN reverse if NRV recovers, capped at original cost.

Without LCM revaluation, by-product fg pool can carry stale value that overstates inventory on the balance sheet.

## Proposed shape

New close hook: lcm_revaluation_close_hook(p_period_id, p_force) RETURNS BIGINT.

- Walks all open inv_value_fg pools that originated from by-product nrv_credit (filter via transfers history with reason='wo_complete_v' and credit_account_id='inv_value_wip(parent)').
- Caller-provided current_nrv per (output_sku_id, fg_location_id) — separate fact table or lookup function.
- If current_nrv < booked_unit_value: post variance_lcm_writedown DR / inv_value_fg(by_product) CR for the difference × pool_qty.
- ASC mode (default): writedowns are permanent.
- IAS mode (skus.lcm_mode flag): writedowns can be reversed up to original_value via inv_value_fg(by_product) DR / variance_lcm_writedown CR.

## Acceptance

- Schema for current_nrv source (table or function signature)
- Close hook implementation
- Tests covering both ASC and IAS modes
- Composes with existing close hooks (wac_periodic, wac_retroactive, cost_adjust_retroactive)

title: post_standard_cost_roll WIP-reval AP3 lock-gap on stock_wip qty read
description:
## Finding

`post_standard_cost_roll` WIP-revaluation path (mig 0078, lines 328–331) reads paired `stock_wip` qty WITHOUT FOR UPDATE on that account. The lock-set at lines 207–224 covers `inv_value_wip` (the value pool) but not `stock_wip` (the qty pool). A concurrent `post_op_move` / `post_wo_complete` / `post_scrap` on the same `(sku, routing_op)` can change qty between the read and post_transfers commit, skewing the `pool_qty × Δstd` revaluation delta.

Same shape as acct-du2.6 / .7 / .12 which were closed via migration 0073.

## Discovery

Audit refresh on migrations 0071–0090 (REVIEW.md addendum, 2026-05-05). Phase 2 walk against AP1–AP8.

## Concrete location

```
db/migrations/0078_wip_material_revaluation.up.sql

Lines 318–322 (resolve paired stock_wip account):
   SELECT s.id INTO v_qty_acct
   FROM   accounts s
   WHERE  s.kind = 'stock_wip' AND s.sku_id = v.sku_id
                              AND s.routing_op = v.routing_op
                              AND NOT s.is_closed;

Lines 328–331 (read qty without FOR UPDATE):
   SELECT debits_total - credits_total INTO v_pool_qty
   FROM   accounts
   WHERE  id = v_qty_acct;

Lock acquisition at lines 222–224 (covers v_lock_ids which is built at 207–219):
   PERFORM 1 FROM accounts WHERE id = ANY(v_lock_ids) ORDER BY id FOR UPDATE;
```

`v_lock_ids` is built from `inv_value_wip` accounts only when `p_revalue_wip = TRUE`; the paired `stock_wip` accounts are NOT included.

## Severity

P3 — race window narrow but real, magnitude `Δqty × Δstd` per pool.

The mig 0078 design rests on the "every roll revalues WIP atomically" invariant; the same-transaction `post_transfers` commit at line 408 handles ledger atomicity, but a concurrent `post_op_move` arriving units to `stock_wip(parent, op)` between the read at line 328 and the post_transfers commit at line 408 makes `v_pool_qty` stale, skewing the variance amount that lands in `variance_wip_revaluation`.

The standard-cost roll itself is rare (per Phase 2 design, infrequent); the race window is correspondingly small. But under `p_revalue_wip = TRUE` the function holds locks on potentially many `inv_value_wip` accounts during the loop, increasing the chance a concurrent op_move arrives during the held-lock window.

## Fix shape

Mirror acct-du2.6/.7/.12 closure (mig 0073 pattern). Two options:

**Option A (smallest change)**: Inside the WIP-loop (lines 308–382), immediately after resolving `v_qty_acct` at line 318–322, add:

```sql
PERFORM 1 FROM accounts WHERE id = v_qty_acct FOR UPDATE;
```

Acquires the qty-pool lock for the duration of the loop iteration; released when the function commits.

**Option B (structural)**: Extend the lock-set build at lines 207–219 to UNION-in the paired `stock_wip` accounts when `p_revalue_wip = TRUE`. Single FOR UPDATE call at 222–224 covers both kinds.

Recommend Option B for cleaner ordering (single bulk FOR UPDATE in id-sorted order avoids deadlock risk between concurrent rolls).

## Test scenario for regression

```rust
// tests/wip_material_revaluation.rs
// scenario: start a post_standard_cost_roll with p_revalue_wip=TRUE on a SKU
// with active WIP at op 10. Concurrently, post_op_move 10→20 arriving qty.
// Assert: variance_wip_revaluation absorbs (pool_qty × Δstd) where pool_qty
// is consistent with whichever serialization order won (block until post-roll
// or block until post-move).
```

## Dependencies

- INTERSECTS with acct-bru (closed) — this is a follow-up correctness fix on the shipped feature.

title: post_so_ship AP3 lock-gap on wac_* unit_cost dispatch (audit-trail drift)
description:
## Finding

`post_so_ship` (mig 0087, lines 470–486) reads pool qty + value to compute wac_* unit_cost BEFORE the post_transfers lock-pre-scan acquires FOR UPDATE on the value account. Same shape as acct-du2.6 (post_wo_complete) and acct-du2.7 (post_op_move) which the original audit flagged as P3 drift and were closed via mig 0073.

## Discovery

Audit refresh on migrations 0071–0090 (REVIEW.md addendum, 2026-05-05). Phase 2 walk against AP1–AP8.

## Concrete location

```
db/migrations/0087_snapshot_cost_method_at_receipt_ship.up.sql

Lines 470–474 (per-class qty divisor read):
   SELECT COALESCE(SUM(CASE WHEN t.debit_account_id = v_val_acct THEN t.qty
                            WHEN t.credit_account_id = v_val_acct THEN -t.qty END), 0)
   INTO   v_qty_balance
   FROM   transfers t
   WHERE  v_val_acct IN (t.debit_account_id, t.credit_account_id) AND t.qty IS NOT NULL;

Lines 483–484 (pool value read):
   SELECT debits_total - credits_total INTO v_value_balance
   FROM   accounts WHERE id = v_val_acct;

Line 503 (persisted on audit-trail column):
   INSERT INTO so_shipment_lines (..., unit_cost, ...)
   VALUES (..., v_unit_cost, ...);
```

The post_transfers lock-pre-scan at line 574 eventually FOR UPDATEs `v_val_acct`, but by then `v_unit_cost` has already been computed from the pre-lock read.

## Severity

P3 — **audit-trail drift, NOT a ledger bug.**

The actual transfer.amount is correct because `_post_transfers_compute_amount` re-reads the pool under lock during the WAC two-pass dispatcher and overwrites the batch's amount. So `accounts.balance` updates use the post-lock value.

What drifts is `so_shipment_lines.unit_cost` — the persisted document-level audit field. Becomes the source of truth for `post_customer_return`'s cogs reversal. A concurrent po_receipt landing inventory between the read at 470 and post_transfers's lock-pre-scan can make the document say "shipped at $X" while the ledger says "shipped at $Y."

For wac_perpetual SKUs the divergence is `Δqty × Δunit_cost` per concurrent receipt; for standard SKUs the path uses `resolve_standard_cost_at` which is canonical (no drift).

## Fix shape

Mirror acct-du2.6/.7 closure (mig 0073 pattern). Add a `PERFORM 1 FROM accounts WHERE id = v_val_acct FOR UPDATE;` immediately before the read at line 470. The post_transfers lock-pre-scan would then re-encounter an already-locked row (no-op).

Alternative: lift the dispatch entirely into post_transfers — let `_post_transfers_compute_amount` produce the unit_cost and persist it via a return-amount channel that flows back to the document layer. Bigger change; reserve for the dispatcher refactor (acct-w0lo).

Recommend the minimal fix (FOR UPDATE prefix) for this issue; defer the structural change to acct-w0lo.

## Test scenario for regression

```rust
// tests/property_so_ship.rs (gates on acct-1cer property-test coverage)
// scenario: while one writer runs post_so_ship for a wac_perpetual SKU,
// another writer concurrently post_po_receipt's into the same inv_value_fg
// pool. Assert: so_shipment_lines.unit_cost matches the resulting transfer's
// effective unit cost (transfer.amount / transfer.qty), within rounding.
```

## Dependencies

- INTERSECTS with acct-w0lo (dispatcher refactor) — long-term fix is to lift dispatch into post_transfers, but minimal FOR UPDATE prefix is correct independently.
- INTERSECTS with acct-1cer (property-test coverage) — sibling property test for post_so_ship would catch this.

## Acceptance

- Migration 0091+ adds `PERFORM 1 FROM accounts WHERE id = v_val_acct FOR UPDATE;` before pool reads in post_so_ship.
- Audit-trail unit_cost matches post-lock dispatched amount.
- Test in `tests/so_ship.rs` (or new `property_so_ship.rs`) demonstrating the race scenario passes.
- REVIEW.md addendum entry updated to remove "fix-needed" verdict.

## Surfaced from

REVIEW.md addendum 2026-05-05 (audit refresh on migrations 0071–0090).
notes: Codified as AP9 / R7 in REVIEW.md + CLAUDE.md (2026-05-05). AP9 = document-level audit field snapshot drift while ledger silently corrects via _post_transfers_compute_amount post-lock recompute. R7 = the canonical rule. This issue is the motivating case alongside acct-quca.

Regression tests added; ci-check clean; 546/0/9 tests pass; REVIEW.md addendum verdict flipped.

title: Property-test coverage requirement for all entry-point functions (umbrella)
description:
## Why this issue exists

acct-du2 Phase 3 shipped 4 property-test binaries (`property_post_transfers.rs`, `property_wo_lifecycle.rs`, `property_post_cost_adjustment.rs`, `property_period_close.rs`) covering ~5 of the ~25 entry-point functions. The other 20 entry-point functions have integration tests but NOT property-driven random-scenario coverage against the I1-I7 invariants in `tests/common/mod.rs::assert_invariants_hold`.

This is the gap that allows AP1-AP8 violations to slip into new entry-points: integration tests probe specific scenarios; property tests probe random scenarios that catch the class-confusion bugs the AP catalog exists to prevent.

ERP_RESEARCH.md follow-up review (2026-05-05) called this out: comprehensive property-test coverage is the single highest correctness-leverage investment we can make.

## Standing requirement

Every entry-point function (current and future) MUST have a property-test binary alongside its integration tests. Sub-issues to file as the work happens; this is the umbrella.

## Existing coverage (4 binaries)

- `property_post_transfers.rs` — random valid post_transfers batches; cycle_count_adj seedings; cost_adjustment value events
- `property_wo_lifecycle.rs` — interleaved multi-WO scenarios sharing parent_sku × routing_op pools; random parent cost_method
- `property_post_cost_adjustment.rs` — random cost-adjust scenarios on existing pools
- `property_period_close.rs` — close orchestration sequences

## Missing coverage (~20 entry-points)

Slice A inflow:
- post_po_receipt (cumulative-qty race per acct-du2.9 — covered by integration but not property test)
- post_ap_bill (similar)
- post_po_return (state-aware split per mig 0086)

Slice B conversion (already partially covered by wo_lifecycle):
- post_op_move (delta from wo_lifecycle's coverage)
- post_scrap (similar)
- post_eco_approve

Slice C outflow:
- post_so_ship (cost-event reason; AP2 / R2 risk)
- post_customer_invoice (three-way match shape)
- post_so_allocate
- post_customer_return (state-aware split mirror)

Standalone:
- post_customer_credit_memo
- post_vendor_debit_memo
- post_ar_payment
- post_ap_payment
- post_inventory_adjustment (delta from existing coverage)
- post_standard_cost_roll (with p_revalue_wip per mig 0078)

## Approach

1. **Phase 1 — extend `assert_invariants_hold`** to cover new invariants surfaced by Slice C / return semantics (per-counterparty per-currency partition consistency; transfers_provisional state consistency; reservation lifecycle consistency).

2. **Phase 2 — new property-test binaries**, one per uncovered entry-point. Each binary follows the existing `property_*.rs` pattern: random scenario generator, post the random batch, call `assert_invariants_hold` after each step, repeat.

3. **Phase 3 — standing PR-time requirement**: any new entry-point function added to the codebase must include a sibling `property_<fn>.rs` test binary in the same PR.

## Estimated effort

Per binary: ~½ day (scenario generator + invariant assertions + smoke). 20 binaries × ½ day = ~10 days total spread across Phase 2 work.

Probably best landed incrementally — file sub-issue per binary; close as each property test binary lands. Don't try to ship all 20 at once.

## Acceptance

- Phase 1: `assert_invariants_hold` extended; new invariants documented in `tests/common/mod.rs`.
- Phase 2: at least 8 of the 20 uncovered binaries shipped (the riskiest ones first — the ones touching cost dispatch / return routing / state-aware split).
- Phase 3: convention documented in CLAUDE.md / contributing notes.
- Sibling sub-issues filed per uncovered entry-point.

## Why this is consequential

The R1-R6 / AP1-AP8 catalog is articulated discipline; property tests are AUTOMATED enforcement. Without them, every new function is a discipline-dependent risk. acct-du2 found 12 SQL bugs in the existing codebase via the structural audit + property tests; the same effort applied prophylactically to new code prevents the bug class from accreting.

## Priority

P3 — safety-net investment. Highest correctness-leverage / effort ratio per the ERP_RESEARCH.md follow-up review.

## Surfaced from

ERP_RESEARCH.md follow-up review 2026-05-05 (R1-R6 enforcement gap analysis).
notes: Property tests must include AP9 / R7 coverage: assert document-level audit fields (e.g., so_shipment_lines.unit_cost, po_receipt_lines.cost_method_at_receipt) match the ledger truth (transfer.amount / transfer.qty for that line) under random concurrent traffic. Standard pattern: spawn N concurrent operations on the same pool, then assert per-line audit fields are consistent with the resulting accounts.balance updates.
