title: Periodic load-test execution + perf-history regression detection
description:
## Why this issue exists

Nine load-test binaries exist (`load_realistic_workload.rs`, `load_inflow_workload.rs`, `load_outbox_*.rs`, `load_deadlock_freedom.rs`, `load_value_workload.rs`, `load_reservation_interleave.rs`). All `#[ignore]`'d so default `cargo test` skips them; manual invocation via `./scripts/run-perf-baseline.sh` only.

Result: regressions go unnoticed for arbitrary time. perf_baseline_v0.md / v1.md were captured at specific points (acct-1ia in 2026-04-29; v1 at post-Slice-A). Between baselines, we can ship code that regresses contention behavior without realizing it. The acct-ezm investigation in 2026-04-30 caught this kind of drift only because someone ran it manually.

## Scope

CI integration for periodic load-test execution.

### Option A: GitHub Actions nightly job (if we adopt CI)
- Schedule: nightly at 02:00 UTC, dedicated runner
- Run: each `#[ignore]`'d load test for `T4_DURATION_SECS=120` (light run)
- Output: append to `perf_history/<date>_<test>_<branch>.json` with metrics
- Alert: if median throughput drops > 15% vs trailing 7-day median

### Option B: Local `./scripts/ci-check-load.sh` (no remote CI)
- Manual but consolidated runner
- Single command runs all 9 load tests with light config
- Outputs to `perf_history/`
- Compares against last-known baseline; warns on regression
- Documented as part of the close-of-iteration checklist

### Option C: PR-time perf-impact check
- For PRs touching `_post_transfers_*` or `db/migrations/`, require running a focused subset (e.g., load_realistic_workload + load_inflow_workload) and pasting results in the PR description
- Lightest effort but human-discipline-dependent

Recommend Option B for now (no remote CI configured per current policy); Option A when CI is adopted.

## Trade-off

- Compute cost: 9 tests × 2 min × nightly = 18 min runner time / day. Tractable.
- Maintenance cost: when load-tests fail to compile after a schema change, the nightly run breaks; need a "skip on compile error" handler.
- Signal-to-noise: load tests have native variance; the 15% threshold balances false-positive rate vs catching real regression. acct-ezm research showed real regressions are visible above ~15% noise floor.

## What this catches

- post_transfers latency regressions (the kind acct-ezm originally feared from acct-uxu)
- Deadlock introduction (load_deadlock_freedom)
- Pseudo-sync degradation (load_outbox_*)
- accounts-table partial-index plan drift on growing partition counts

## Out of scope

- Production-scale longitudinal data (no production deployment exists)
- Cross-version migration timing (covered by ci-check.sh round-trip)
- UI / API tier load (no UI / API tier)

## Acceptance

- `scripts/ci-check-load.sh` runs all 9 load tests in light config
- Outputs JSON metrics to `perf_history/`
- Compares against baseline (perf_baseline_v1.md or trailing run)
- Warns / errors on > 15% regression
- Documented in `db/README.md` close-of-iteration section

## Priority

P3 — drift mitigation. Currently low-risk (one developer, careful manual baseline capture), but compounding over time.

## Surfaced from

ERP_RESEARCH.md follow-up testing-gap review 2026-05-05.

title: Cost-method hybridization property test (interleaved standard + WAC trio)
description:
## Why this issue exists

Property tests + matrix tests cover each cost method in isolation:
- standard via `post_inventory_adjustment.rs`, `wo_lifecycle.rs`, etc.
- wac_perpetual via `wac_perpetual_*.rs`
- wac_periodic via `wac_periodic_*.rs`
- wac_retroactive via `wac_retroactive_*.rs`

What's missing: a test that exercises **interleaved cost methods within a single period close**. Real workloads have a mix of SKUs each on a different method — say, 50% standard, 30% wac_perpetual, 15% wac_periodic, 5% wac_retroactive — with concurrent activity across all of them, and a period close that finalizes all four classes' provisional state in one orchestrator run.

acct-7eo (mig 0077) lifted some of the mixed parent/component cost-method gates with `variance_material_mixed`, but full hybrid stress isn't tested.

## Scope

New `tests/property_costmethod_hybrid.rs` (proptest, `--test-threads=1`):

- Generate a fixture with N SKUs randomly assigned cost methods per the mix above.
- Generate M random transactions over a simulated period (po_receipt, rm_issue_to_wo, op_move, wo_complete, scrap, so_ship, inventory_adjustment).
- Random op_moves within multi-op routings.
- Mixed parent/component cost methods on WOs (e.g., wac_periodic parent with standard component, wac_retroactive parent with wac_perpetual component).
- close_period at end.
- Assert: invariants_hold across period boundary; transfers_provisional fully finalized; per-pool variance_* postings reconcile to their drained pools; no negative balances.

Property test: 50-200 generated cases, each asserting the same invariants across random transaction sequences.

## What this catches

- Hook-ordering bugs in close_period when multiple classes have provisional state
- variance_material_mixed routing edge cases (acct-7eo / acct-7eo-mig0077)
- Cross-class interaction in `_post_transfers_compute_amount` (R2 credit-side resolution drift)
- transfers_provisional CHECK constraint violations under interleaved finalization

## What this complements

- `property_post_transfers.rs` (unit-level random sequence)
- `property_wo_lifecycle.rs` (WO-focused random scenarios)
- `property_post_cost_adjustment.rs` (cost-adjust focused)
- `property_period_close.rs` (close_period focused on single class)

## Trigger / consequence

Could plausibly find P0006 / accounts_check / transfers_provisional CHECK trips that single-class tests miss. Especially valuable BEFORE acct-w0lo (dispatcher refactor) ships — gives baseline behavior to compare refactored output against.

## Out of scope

- Performance / latency assertions (covered by load tests)
- FIFO / lot interleaving (gates on acct-8gg)

## Acceptance

- New test binary at `tests/property_costmethod_hybrid.rs`
- Uses proptest crate (already a dependency, see existing `property_*` binaries)
- PROPTEST_CASES env var controls case count (default 100)
- Runs with `--test-threads=1` (per existing property test convention)
- All generated cases pass invariants_hold

## Priority

P3 — correctness safety net. Most valuable before acct-w0lo (dispatcher refactor) and acct-8gg (FIFO/lot) — provides a regression baseline for both.

title: Kitchen-sink lifecycle integration test (full document chain in one binary)
description:
## Why this issue exists

Each test binary covers one workflow in isolation. Cross-binary regressions are statistically possible: a change to (e.g.) `_post_transfers_apply_event`'s flagging logic might pass `wo_complete.rs` and `customer_invoice.rs` tests independently but break the interaction (e.g., a WO completion's variance posting against a parent_sku later sold via SO ship + invoice).

No test today walks a full document-lifecycle scenario end-to-end in a single binary.

## Scope

New `tests/kitchen_sink_lifecycle.rs` — single integration test that exercises the full document chain:

```
1. Set up: 1 vendor, 1 customer, 1 standard SKU, 1 wac_perpetual SKU, 1 BOM, 1 routing
2. post_po_receipt (10 units of standard SKU, 5 of wac_perpetual)
3. post_ap_bill clearing the receipt
4. post_wo_start (assemble 5 of finished SKU using 2 of each component)
5. post_op_move (route through op 10 → 20)
6. post_wo_complete (5 finished SKU into FG)
7. post_so_allocate (reserve 3 finished for SO)
8. post_so_ship (3 finished to customer)
9. post_customer_invoice clearing the ship
10. post_ar_payment (full)
11. post_inventory_adjustment (write off 1 stale unit)
12. post_cost_adjustment (revalue 1 unit of wac_perpetual SKU)
13. close_period
14. reopen_period (acct-7h4 — gate on its impl)
15. post_cost_adjustment_retroactive against the closed period
16. close_period again
17. Assertions: invariants_hold, balance_per_ledger_kind == 0, no orphan reservations, no orphan transfers_provisional, accounts_check_holds for every account
```

Each step asserts incremental balances and invariants.

Test runs in default `cargo test` (not `#[ignore]`'d). ~30-60s wall time acceptable.

## What this catches

- Cross-workflow interactions that single-workflow tests miss
- Reservation-lifecycle drift across multiple reservation-touching workflows
- transfers_provisional state inconsistency across multi-period spans
- accounts_check trips that surface only at specific intermediate row states
- Period-close hook ordering bugs

## What this complements

- Property tests probe random-input invariants
- Conformance tests probe acceptance-criteria correctness
- This test probes scenario completeness — does the full happy path actually work?

## Out of scope

- Negative test paths (per-step error cases stay in per-workflow tests)
- Multi-currency variant (extension once base scenario is green)
- Multi-entity variant (gates on acct-3gzh)

## Acceptance

- New test binary at `tests/kitchen_sink_lifecycle.rs`
- Runs in default `cargo test` (NOT ignored)
- All 17 steps + assertions pass
- Run time < 60s
- Step ordering documented as comment at top of file

## Priority

P3 — safety net. ~½ day effort. Catches a class of bug we currently have no detection for.

title: End-to-end Slice A+B+C mixed workload load test
description:
## Why this issue exists

Existing load-test binaries each cover one workload shape:
- `load_realistic_workload.rs` (shape F) — bin_move only, cross-SKU spread
- `load_inflow_workload.rs` (shape N) — Slice A PO+AP cycle only
- `load_outbox_*` — outbox transport variants
- `load_deadlock_freedom.rs` / `load_value_workload.rs` / `load_reservation_interleave.rs` — focused single-aspect stress

What's missing: a load-test binary that simulates a **realistic mix of inflow (Slice A) + conversion (Slice B) + outflow (Slice C) traffic concurrently**, over a multi-period span, with realistic ratios.

Without it, the triggers for acct-c4p (pseudo-sync pivot), acct-e8g (transfers partitioning), and the un-quantified accounts-table-explosion question are speculative. Existing benchmarks tell us about specific shapes, not realistic operator workload contention.

## Scope

New `tests/load_phase1_mixed_workload.rs` (`#[ignore]`'d, env-driven). Per cycle simulates:

- 1 PO receipt against random vendor (qty 5-50)
- 0.8 AP bills clearing prior receipt
- 0.5 WO starts (random parent, BOM exploded)
- 1.5 op_moves on in-flight WOs
- 0.4 WO completes
- 1.0 SO ships against random customer (qty 1-20)
- 0.7 customer invoices
- 0.3 AR payments
- 0.05 customer returns / PO returns

Run for `T4_DURATION_SECS` (default 600 = 10 min) with `T4_WRITERS=32`.

Pre-create fixture:
- 50 SKUs (mix: 25 standard, 15 wac_perpetual, 8 wac_periodic, 2 wac_retroactive)
- 10 vendors, 10 customers
- 5 BOMs (mix of single-op and multi-op routings)
- 3 absorption classes
- Per-vendor / per-customer / per-currency partition accounts

Assertions:
- Zero deadlocks across run
- post_transfers p50 / p95 / p99 latency reported
- Per-doc-type latency reported
- pg_stat_statements top-20 queries reported
- accounts-table size growth measured
- transfers-table size growth measured

## What this unblocks

- **acct-c4p evidence**: are caller p99s exceeding 500ms under realistic 32-writer load?
- **acct-e8g evidence**: how fast does transfers grow per period? Does query plan degrade at 10M / 50M / 100M rows?
- **accounts-explosion question**: how many accounts rows after 10 simulated periods of 50-SKU traffic? Linear or super-linear?
- **acct-mqi8 (RBAC) overhead measurement**: once RBAC ships, re-run to measure permission-check cost.

## Out of scope

- UI-driven workload (we have no UI).
- Multi-tenant simulation (gates on Q12 architectural decision).
- Slice C-only or Slice B-only variants (cover by existing single-shape binaries).

## Acceptance

- New test binary compiles and runs end-to-end without panic.
- Documented in `perf_baseline_v2.md` (or extension of v1) with measured contention numbers.
- Evidence-based update on acct-c4p / acct-e8g trigger status.
- 10-min run produces baseline; 30-min run available for stress.

## Priority

P3 — investment in safety net. Recommend before deeper Phase 2 features ship to validate triggers for the deferred infrastructure pivots.

title: Investigate SERIALIZABLE isolation for hot paths to reduce R4 discipline burden
description:
## Architectural concern

Postgres default isolation is READ COMMITTED; we run all entry-point functions at default. Class-confusion rule R4 (CLAUDE.md) says: pool reads happen under FOR UPDATE on the SAME account before subsequent writes; FOR UPDATE on the value account does NOT cover the qty account.

The Phase 3 audit (acct-du2, REVIEW.md) flagged ~6 sibling lock-gap findings (acct-du2.1, .2, .6, .7, .9, .12) — places where the function locked the wrong account or the right account too late. All fixed via migrations 0071-0076, but the discipline is required for every new function.

## Smell

Correctness depends on developer discipline + audit cycles. As more entry-point functions land (Phase 2 features will add ~10-15 more), R4 violations are statistically likely; each requires either pre-merge audit or post-incident fix.

## Refactor proposal

Investigate moving hot paths to SERIALIZABLE isolation. PG's SERIALIZABLE catches the kinds of races R4 manually guards against — at the cost of serialization-failure retries on conflict.

### Investigation scope

1. Identify "hot paths" — functions where R4 violations would have correctness impact AND contention is realistic (e.g., post_po_receipt under inflow burst, post_so_ship under outflow burst, post_op_move under WO burst).

2. Benchmark sync inline at SERIALIZABLE vs READ COMMITTED + FOR UPDATE. SAP enqueue server's 1-5ms target is the reference; SERIALIZABLE retry storms past that threshold are a no-go.

3. Decide: per-function isolation level (some at SERIALIZABLE, some at READ COMMITTED) vs global. Per-function lets us migrate incrementally; global is simpler.

4. Application-side: callers must handle 40001 (serialization_failure) by retrying. sqlx has retry helpers; integration tests need to account for retries in their concurrency tests.

### Where SERIALIZABLE wins

The R4 audit in REVIEW.md found bugs of the form: "function reads pool A under FOR UPDATE, then reads pool B without lock, then writes both." Under SERIALIZABLE, two concurrent callers with overlapping reads + writes would conflict and one would retry. Eliminates this bug class entirely.

### Where SERIALIZABLE loses

Hot single-account contention (e.g., a global cogs account taking 1000+ posts/sec). SERIALIZABLE would force serialization-failure retries; per-row FOR UPDATE just blocks. The L-shape pseudo-sync architecture (acct-c4p) is the right answer for that contention pattern, not SERIALIZABLE.

## Out of scope

- Property-test-driven race finding (acct-du2.14/.15/.16 already filed).
- Replacing FOR UPDATE entirely — the manual lock pattern is correct, just discipline-dependent.

## Trigger / inflection point

Phase 1+ contention measurement (gates on acct-c4p triggers). If Phase 1 shows R4-violation incidents in production, SERIALIZABLE for affected paths becomes a force multiplier. Until then, R4 audit remains the mitigation.

## Dependencies

- INTERSECTS with acct-c4p (pseudo-sync pivot) — both address contention but different bug classes.

## Priority

P3 — investigation, not refactor. Filing as a watch item; promote to P2 if Phase 1 reveals real R4 incidents.

## Surfaced from

ERP_RESEARCH.md follow-up architectural review 2026-05-05.

title: Couple reservation lifecycle to document state machine (drift risk)
description:
## Architectural concern

`inventory_reservations.status` (mig 0014, extended in mig 0079 for 'shipped' and mig 0083 for 'allocated') has its own state machine: active → allocated → shipped, with cron-driven expired and operator-driven cancelled.

Sales-order shipment lifecycle (sales_orders.status, so_shipments existence) is implicitly coupled — when an SO line ships, `post_so_ship` flips matching reservations from 'active'/'allocated' to 'shipped'. When `post_so_allocate` runs, it flips 'active' to 'allocated' (mig 0083).

These are two state machines that should be one.

## Smell

Drift risk grows as more workflows touch reservations:
- `post_customer_return` currently doesn't touch reservations — should it? (If the customer returns shipped goods, should the reservation flip back to something?)
- acct-fv1 disassembly returns FG to raw inventory — does that release any reservation?
- `post_inventory_adjustment` can drain stock_available out from under an active reservation — should it warn / refuse / silently allow?

Each of these is an ad-hoc decision today because reservation state isn't consistently coupled to the document state machine. As more touchpoints appear, the inconsistency surfaces as bugs.

## Refactor proposal

Choice of two patterns:

### Pattern A: Reservation as document-derived view
Drop the explicit `inventory_reservations.status` column; treat reservation as a *derived* state computed from (so_line state, qty_shipped, qty_returned, etc.). Reservation is then a query, not a row.
- Pro: cannot drift from document state.
- Con: reservation is no longer first-class; can't reserve speculative inventory before SO exists; loses pre-SO reservation use cases (commodity provisional, planning reservations).

### Pattern B: Document-state hooks update reservation
Keep reservation as a row but make every document-state-change function explicitly call `_update_reservation_state(reservation_id, new_status, reason)`. Add a trigger or wrapper that disallows direct UPDATE of reservation status outside this helper. Each new workflow that affects reservations is explicit about which transitions it triggers.
- Pro: first-class reservations preserved.
- Con: requires audit + retrofit of all 5+ existing reservation-touching workflows.

Recommend Pattern B for Phase 2; Pattern A is a bigger semantic shift.

## Trigger / inflection point

Surface before the next reservation-touching workflow lands. Candidates:
- acct-fv1 (disassembly): does completing a disassembly release reservations on input parent?
- acct-uze (lot/serial): lot-specific reservations need state coupling to lot-level stock.
- A speculative pre-SO reservation flow (commodity hedging, etc.) — would force Pattern A vs B choice.

## Out of scope

- The `expired` cron transition (acct-93b background job) is independent and stays.
- Reservation overshoot / no-stock detection at reserve time stays in `reserve_inventory` function.

## Surfaced from

ERP_RESEARCH.md follow-up architectural review 2026-05-05.
notes: Subsumed by acct-cz1v (broader reservation structural overhaul, 2026-05-12). Pattern B from this issue is closer to the orthogonalized model proposed there. Re-evaluate as a sub-case once cz1v design lands.

title: Convert account_kind / bom_lines.kind enums to reference tables
description:
## Architectural concern

Multiple enum-typed columns are growing past the threshold where enum-vs-row-table trade-off flips:

1. `account_kind` enum — currently ~50 values. Phase 2 work will add ~15-20 more (lot/serial dimensions, by-product disposal cost, customer credit balance, vendor advance, etc.). At ~80+ values the migration cost per-add becomes notable: each new value requires `ALTER TYPE ADD VALUE`, a seed update, and a review of every dispatch site that walks kinds.

2. `bom_lines.kind` enum — currently `{item, service, charge}`. Phase 2 wants `co_product`, `by_product`, `catalyst`, `energy`, `configurable_item`, possibly more. Same pattern as account_kind.

3. `transfer_reason` enum — currently ~25 values. Each new internal-chain reason adds a value plus dispatcher branch.

4. `account_kind` partial-unique-index proliferation: each partitioned kind has its own `WHERE kind='X' AND NOT is_closed UNIQUE (...)` partial index. Currently ~10 such indexes; growing.

## Smell

Postgres enums optimize for tiny stable sets. Once an enum exceeds ~80 values and changes monthly, a row table is the cleaner shape — versionable, query-able, per-row metadata extensible (normal_side, partition strategy, allowed reasons, etc.).

SAP / Oracle / D365 / NetSuite all use row tables for their analogues (SAP G/L account master `SKB1`; Oracle natural account segment values; D365 main accounts; NetSuite chart of accounts). None use database enums.

## Refactor proposal

Convert `account_kind` and `bom_lines.kind` to reference tables:

```sql
account_kinds(
  code TEXT PRIMARY KEY,        -- 'ap', 'ar_unsettled', 'inv_value_raw', etc
  name TEXT,
  ledger_kind TEXT,             -- 'value', 'qty', 'reservation' etc
  normal_side TEXT,
  partition_keys TEXT[],        -- ['counterparty_id', 'currency'] etc
  is_value_pool BOOLEAN,
  active_at TIMESTAMPTZ,
  obsolete_at TIMESTAMPTZ,
  notes TEXT
)
```

Existing `accounts.kind` becomes FK to `account_kinds.code`. Migration converts enum to text + FK; existing rows retain their values.

Same for `bom_lines.kind` and possibly `transfer_reason`.

Per-kind partition strategy moves from hand-coded partial indexes to a generic partial-index template that reads `partition_keys` array at table-creation time (PG dynamic SQL in a migration helper).

## Trade-off

Loss of compile-time enum check (sqlx compile-time queries lose that guarantee). Mitigated by domain CHECK on the FK + tests.

Migration is non-trivial: enum to text-FK conversion across all dependent columns + dispatch sites + tests. Best done in a single migration.

## Trigger / inflection point

Cross threshold:
- account_kind exceeds ~80 values, OR
- A migration to add a single account_kind starts touching >5 dispatch sites.

Either trigger argues for the refactor. Currently at ~50 values; not yet triggered.

## Out of scope

- `cost_method` enum (4 values, stable shape) — leave as enum.
- `period_status` enum (3 values, stable) — leave as enum.
- `reservation_status` enum (5 values, occasional add) — borderline; defer.

## Surfaced from

ERP_RESEARCH.md follow-up architectural review 2026-05-05.
notes: 2026-05-07: Re-scoped to Phase G1 of acct-wb75 convergence. Per research/posting-lines-convergence-plan.md §4.G.G1. Lifted from threshold-gated per acct-58h9 resolution (closed). account_kinds row table + backfill from enum + plpgsql sweep.

title: Replace transfers_provisional CHECK with policy-trigger function
description:
## Architectural concern

`transfers_provisional` has accumulated CHECK constraint relaxations as new internal-chain reason patterns landed:

- mig 0029 original: `(finalized_at IS NULL) OR (variance_amount IS NOT NULL AND variance_transfer_id IS NOT NULL)` — rejected mismatched finalize states
- mig 0065 relaxed: also permits `(finalized_at IS NOT NULL AND variance_amount != 0 AND variance_transfer_id IS NULL)` — internal-chain op_move_v case where variance is recorded but no transfer is posted
- mig 0067/0070 may have implicit further relaxations for rm_issue_to_wo + wac_retroactive

Each new internal-chain reason (rm_issue_to_wo, op_move_v, future osp_*, future disassembly_*) potentially requires another CHECK relaxation. The CHECK is encoding state-machine policy that the application logic also encodes — duplication that drifts.

## Smell

The CHECK is becoming a partial DSL for "valid transfers_provisional row states." It enforces correctness, but every new flag-able reason requires editing it. Migration cost compounds.

## Refactor proposal

Replace the body CHECK with a BEFORE INSERT/UPDATE trigger that calls a policy function:

```sql
CREATE FUNCTION _validate_transfers_provisional_state(
  p_cost_method TEXT,
  p_reason TEXT,
  p_finalized_at TIMESTAMPTZ,
  p_variance_amount BIGINT,
  p_variance_transfer_id BIGINT
) RETURNS VOID
LANGUAGE plpgsql AS $$
BEGIN
  -- explicit per-(cost_method, reason) state-validity rules
  -- raises with a P-code if invalid
  -- new internal-chain reasons add a branch here, not a CHECK relaxation
END $$;
```

Trigger calls the function. Adding a new reason adds a branch in the function — single edit point, version-controllable, testable in isolation, no CHECK constraint surgery.

## Trade-off

Triggers have function-call overhead vs static CHECK. Measured impact likely negligible (transfers_provisional INSERT count is small relative to transfers); benchmark before committing.

## Out of scope

- Migrating existing CHECK semantics to the trigger is the work; the validity rules don't change.
- Other CHECK-encoded policies elsewhere (accounts.normal_side, periods.closed_at) are appropriately CHECK-encoded — they're stable invariants, not extensible policy.

## Trigger / inflection point

Pick before the next internal-chain reason lands (likely acct-fv1 disassembly or acct-3uh OSP — both could introduce new internal-chain semantics).

## Surfaced from

ERP_RESEARCH.md follow-up architectural review 2026-05-05.

title: Declarative period-close hook dependency table + topological orchestrator
description:
## Architectural concern

`close_period` (mig 0026) sequences three close hooks in implicit order encoded in the function body:
1. wac_periodic_close_hook
2. wac_retroactive_close_hook
3. cost_adjust_retroactive_hook

Order is correct today (each hook's variance posts must finalize before the next looks at pool state) but the dependency is encoded in code, not declared as data. As the hook list grows the ordering will matter more:

- acct-oef (burden close hook) must run BEFORE wac hooks (burden absorbed-vs-actual netting affects pool values that WAC reads)
- acct-3dz2 (FX revaluation) must run AFTER all material/cost hooks (final pool values determined first; FX reval revalues the resulting balances)
- Future: variance prorate-to-COGS+FG+WIP would run after wac hooks but before fx reval

Hand-encoding this in `close_period` body each time we add a hook is fragile.

## Refactor proposal

Declarative dependency table:

```sql
close_period_hooks(
  hook_name TEXT PRIMARY KEY,
  hook_fn_name TEXT NOT NULL,
  depends_on TEXT[] NOT NULL DEFAULT '{}',
  description TEXT,
  active_at TIMESTAMPTZ
)
```

Seed with current hooks + their dependencies:
- wac_periodic_close_hook depends_on '{}'
- wac_retroactive_close_hook depends_on '{wac_periodic_close_hook}' (or independent — verify)
- cost_adjust_retroactive_hook depends_on '{wac_periodic_close_hook, wac_retroactive_close_hook}'

`close_period` orchestrator runs `topological_sort(close_period_hooks)` then walks the sorted list, invoking `EXECUTE format('SELECT %I($1, $2)', hook_fn_name) USING period_id, force_provisional`.

Cycle detection raises P0050+ at orchestration time.

## Trigger / inflection point

Refactor BEFORE acct-oef + acct-3dz2 land. Same cost-now / cost-later inflection — wiring acct-oef into the hand-encoded order means choosing where to splice it; getting it wrong is an audit issue.

## Out of scope

- Hook parallelism (concurrent execution of independent hooks) — keep serial for MVP.
- Hook retry / failure semantics beyond what `close_period` already does (gated bypass via `p_force_provisional`).

## Dependencies

- BLOCKS: acct-oef (burden close hook), acct-3dz2 (fx revaluation hook).

## Surfaced from

ERP_RESEARCH.md follow-up architectural review 2026-05-05.

title: Refactor _post_transfers_compute_amount to strategy registration
description:
## Architectural concern

`_post_transfers_compute_amount` (the cost dispatcher) is currently a switch on `cost_method × event_type` — standard / wac_perpetual / wac_periodic / wac_retroactive × po_receipt / so_ship / op_move / wo_complete / scrap / rm_issue_to_wo. Each cell can have its own logic.

Branch count today: 4 cost methods × ~6 cost-event reasons = 24 paths plus internal-chain dispatch for the WAC trio. Function is approaching unwieldy size.

Adding the deferred work compounds it:
- acct-8gg (FIFO + lot) — adds 2 new cost methods × 6 reasons = 12 more paths
- acct-tt1 (cross-currency BOMs) — adds translation branch on every existing path
- acct-cms (provisional cost sources) — adds 6-way branch on the WAC paths

Without refactor, a 7+ × 6+ × N matrix in one function will be the most complex code in the repo and the bottleneck where future cost-method work concentrates.

## Refactor proposal

Strategy-registration pattern. Each cost_method registers a callback:

```sql
cost_method_strategies(
  cost_method TEXT,
  event_kind TEXT,                  -- 'inbound', 'outbound', 'internal_chain'
  compute_fn_name TEXT,             -- name of plpgsql function to dispatch to
  flag_provisional BOOLEAN,
  registered_at TIMESTAMPTZ
)
```

Per (cost_method, event_kind), one row points at a per-strategy implementation:
- `_compute_amount_standard_outbound`
- `_compute_amount_wac_perpetual_outbound`
- `_compute_amount_wac_periodic_outbound`
- `_compute_amount_fifo_outbound`
- ...etc

`_post_transfers_compute_amount` becomes a one-line lookup + dynamic dispatch. Adding FIFO is a new function + INSERT into the registry, not a 200-line edit to the existing dispatcher.

Same shape for close-hook recompute logic — `cost_method_close_hooks(cost_method, hook_fn_name)`.

## Trigger / inflection point

Refactor BEFORE acct-8gg (FIFO/lot) lands. Refactoring after means doubling the work — touching 30+ branches in the existing dispatcher, then immediately fragmenting them. The cost-now / cost-later inflection is real.

## Out of scope

- Migration of existing strategies to the registry can be incremental — register existing 4 first, then refactor each cell to use the registry, then ship FIFO via the new pattern.
- The class-confusion R1-R6 audit checklist still applies per-strategy.

## Why P3 not P2

P3 because no current functionality is broken. The refactor pays for itself only when the next cost method lands. If acct-8gg is deprioritized indefinitely, this stays paper-only.

## Dependencies

- BLOCKS: acct-8gg (FIFO + lot) should depend on this.

## Surfaced from

ERP_RESEARCH.md follow-up architectural review 2026-05-05.
close_reason: Strategy-registration refactor shipped end-to-end across migrations 0094 (cost dispatcher) + 0095 (close hooks). Per launch notes' 2-step plan: acct-d5t8 (cost-method-hybridization property test) shipped first as regression baseline, then refactored both _post_transfers_compute_amount and close_period to iterate registry tables. Adding FIFO/lot (acct-8gg) is now INSERT into the registry + write per-strategy fn — no orchestrator edits.

title: Drop-ship workflow (vendor direct to customer, no warehouse touch)
description:
## Why this issue exists

Drop-ship workflow: vendor ships goods directly to customer, bypassing our warehouse. The PO and SO are linked; goods never touch our inventory; revenue + COGS post simultaneously at vendor-to-customer ship; no inventory pool involvement.

This is a common pattern (e-commerce, distributors, made-to-order) that our current model doesn't support — post_so_ship requires draining stock_available, post_po_receipt credits stock_available.

## Scope

1. Schema additions:
   - `sales_orders.drop_ship BOOLEAN DEFAULT FALSE`.
   - `sales_order_lines.drop_ship_po_line_id UUID NULL` — FK to a paired purchase_order_lines row.
   - `purchase_order_lines.drop_ship_so_line_id UUID NULL` — symmetric pair.
   - When both flags are set, the SO and PO lines are linked; cost-flow rules change.

2. Functions:
   - `post_drop_ship(p_so_line_id, p_qty, p_business_date, ...)`: single-event workflow that combines:
     - Vendor → Customer ship (no warehouse touch).
     - AP accrual: ap_unsettled(vendor, currency) CR / cogs(currency) DR for vendor's cost.
     - AR ship: ar_unsettled(customer, currency) DR / revenue(currency) CR for selling price.
     - No stock_available change.
   - Subsequent post_ap_bill (against the linked po_line) clears ap_unsettled → ap.
   - Subsequent post_customer_invoice (against the linked so_line) clears ar_unsettled → ar.
   - No inv_value_raw / inv_value_fg involvement — the goods passed through but were never on our books.

3. Three-way match still applies:
   - Vendor invoice qty × unit_cost vs drop-ship-shipped qty × po_line.unit_cost.
   - Customer invoice qty × unit_price vs drop-ship-shipped qty × so_line.unit_price.

4. Margin reporting: drop-ship gross margin = revenue − vendor cost (per line). Make this a first-class drilldown.

5. New error codes (P0050+): drop_ship_invalid (paired but lines mismatched), drop_ship_unpaired (drop_ship=TRUE without PO link), etc.

## Industry mapping

- SAP: Third-party order processing — Sales order item category TAS triggers a purchase requisition → PO → vendor ships direct → MIRO clears AP and the goods receipt is statistical (not inventory-affecting).
- Oracle Cloud: Drop ship sales order with linked PO; deferred COGS until vendor invoice.
- D365: Direct delivery (sales-order → linked purchase order → vendor ships); intercompany variant uses chained workflows.
- NetSuite: Drop Ship PO type linked to SO; itemfulfillment by vendor triggers the GL postings.

## Compliance anchors

- ASC 606 revenue recognition: principal vs agent assessment determines if drop-ship revenue is gross (us) or net (commission only). Our model assumes gross.
- Sales tax nexus: drop-ship can trigger vendor-state nexus separately from our nexus.

## Acceptance

- drop_ship flags on sales_orders + sales_order_lines + purchase_order_lines.
- post_drop_ship function.
- Three-way match on both sides.
- Tests: full drop-ship cycle (SO + PO + drop-ship-event + vendor-bill + customer-invoice); margin reporting; mismatch handling.

## Out of scope

- Drop-ship returns (post-MVP — caller can issue a credit memo + debit memo, but a unified drop-ship-return workflow is a Phase-2 follow-up).
- Vendor commission accounting (principal-agent ASC 606 alternative).

## Priority

P3 — operational. Common in distributors / e-commerce; deferred until a real workload demands it.

## Surfaced from

ERP_RESEARCH.md cross-cutting (universal pattern across all 4 ERPs; not on backlog).

title: AR aging + dunning + AP aging workflows
description:
## Why this issue exists

We have ar / ap accounts per counterparty per currency, and per-counterparty balances are computable, but there's no aging analysis (30/60/90/120 days) or dunning workflow. This is a basic AR/AP capability shipped by every mainstream ERP.

## Scope

### AR aging + dunning

1. New views:
   - `v_ar_aging(customer_id, currency, current_amt, days_31_60, days_61_90, days_91_120, over_120)` — buckets per customer per currency based on customer_invoices.business_date vs current date.
   - `v_ar_aging_summary(currency, total_current, total_31_60, total_61_90, total_91_120, total_over_120)` — global rollup.

2. New tables:
   - `dunning_levels(id, level_no, days_overdue, message_template, fee_amount, escalation_action ENUM('email','letter','call','collections'))`.
   - `dunning_runs(id, run_date, status, posted_by)`.
   - `dunning_notices(run_id, customer_id, invoice_id, level_no, sent_at, fee_posted_transfer_id NULL)`.

3. Functions:
   - `generate_dunning_run(p_business_date)`: walks open customer_invoices, classifies by age, picks dunning level, creates dunning_notices.
   - `post_dunning_fee(p_notice_id)`: emits AR fee assessment via new transfer reason `dunning_fee` + new account_kind `dunning_fee_revenue`.

### AP aging

1. New views:
   - `v_ap_aging(vendor_id, currency, current_amt, days_31_60, days_61_90, days_91_120, over_120)` — buckets per vendor.
   - `v_ap_aging_summary(currency, ...)`.

2. Use case: cash forecasting — "what AP is coming due in next 30/60 days at what rate per currency".

3. Payment proposal worklist (gates on payment-run RBAC):
   - `payment_proposals(id, proposal_date, vendor_filter, max_amount, due_date_cutoff)`.
   - `payment_proposal_lines(proposal_id, vendor_id, currency, amount, due_date, selected_for_payment)`.

## Industry mapping

- SAP: F.30 (AR aging) + F150 (Dunning); FBL5N customer line items; Automatic Payment Program (F110) for AP.
- Oracle Cloud: AR Aging Report + Reminders / Late Charges; Auto-Pay program for AP.
- D365: Customer aging snapshot + Collections module + Dunning letter functionality; Vendor aging + payment proposal.
- NetSuite: Aged Receivables / Aged Payables saved searches + Statement Frequency + Payment Run.

## Industry extensions

- Customer credit limits + automatic SO holds when aging exceeds threshold.
- Late-payment fees per dunning level.
- Promise-to-pay tracking.
- Collections workflow with task management.

## Compliance anchors

- ASC 326 CECL (current expected credit losses) — aging informs allowance calculation.
- SOX 404 collections controls.

## Acceptance

- v_ar_aging + v_ap_aging views with bucketed aging.
- dunning_levels + dunning_runs + dunning_notices schema.
- generate_dunning_run + post_dunning_fee functions.
- Payment proposal worklist tables.
- Tests: aging-bucket boundary cases; partial-payment age reduction; multi-currency aging.

## Out of scope

- Email/letter generation (application-tier).
- Collections agency integration (application-tier).
- Automatic SO hold on credit-limit trip — file separately if needed.

## Dependencies

- SOFT: RBAC for payment-run authorization, dunning-fee waiver authorization.

## Priority

P3 — operational gap-fill. Higher value once a real customer/vendor base exists.

## Surfaced from

ERP_RESEARCH.md cross-cutting (universal AR/AP module across all 4 ERPs; not on backlog).

title: Chart-of-accounts reporting hierarchy (FSV / account categories)
description:
## Why this issue exists

We have flat `account_kind` enum (~50 values) and `accounts` rows partitioned per (kind, sku/location/counterparty/currency). There's no reporting hierarchy — the income statement and balance sheet can't be rolled up because there's no concept of "operating expenses → utilities + rent + software" or "current assets → cash + ar + inventory."

acct-063 (expense taxonomy) touches one slice of this; the bigger absent piece is hierarchical reporting structure for financial statement preparation.

ERP_RESEARCH.md showed all four mainstream ERPs have first-class hierarchical reporting:
- SAP: Financial Statement Versions (FSV) — hierarchical tree of GL accounts (Assets / Liabilities / Equity / Revenue / Expenses) for B/S and P&L.
- Oracle: Account Hierarchy on Natural Account segment with Asset / Liability / Owner's Equity / Revenue / Expense qualifiers; date-effective reporting trees.
- D365: Main account category (~70 standard, extensible) ties accounts to default reports.
- NetSuite: Account Type fixed enum + Subaccount-of for hierarchy within type.

## Scope

1. New tables:
   - `account_categories(id, code, name, statement ENUM('balance_sheet','income_statement','cash_flow'), category_type ENUM('asset','liability','equity','revenue','cogs','operating_expense','other_income','other_expense'), normal_side, parent_category_id NULL, sort_order, active_at, obsolete_at)`.
   - `account_kind_categories(account_kind TEXT, category_id BIGINT)`: maps each existing `account_kind` enum value to its reporting category.

2. Helper:
   - `account_category_path(p_account_kind)` returns full ancestor chain — for drilldown reports.
   - `v_balance_sheet_at(p_business_date, p_entity_id?)` view: aggregates per category.
   - `v_income_statement_for_period(p_period_id, p_entity_id?)` view: aggregates per category.

3. Backward compat:
   - All existing `account_kind` values get pre-populated category mappings via mig that ships the schema.
   - Adding a new account_kind requires also picking its category — guarded by FK or trigger.

## Why this matters

- Without it: the operator must hand-build SQL to roll up "all variance accounts" or "all P&L lines" — error-prone and not auditable.
- With it: standard B/S + P&L queries are a SELECT against the views.

## Industry mapping

- SAP FSV (transaction OB58); FAGLA = Account Group; multiple FSVs per COA for different reports.
- Oracle Account Hierarchy (Manage Account Hierarchies app); Natural Account segment qualifiers.
- D365 Main account categories (~70 shipped); Financial reports use them; custom categories supported.
- NetSuite fixed Account Types (Asset/Liability/COGS/Income/Expense/etc.) + Subaccount-of tree.

## Compliance anchors

- GAAP / IFRS financial statement structure requirements.
- SEC filing schemas (XBRL US GAAP taxonomy mapping).
- SOX 404 reporting structure controls.

## Acceptance

- account_categories + account_kind_categories schema with all current 50+ enum values mapped.
- Trigger/FK preventing orphan account_kinds.
- v_balance_sheet_at + v_income_statement_for_period views.
- Tests: standard B/S + P&L queries return expected aggregates against fixture data.

## Out of scope

- Multiple-FSV variants (different reports for different audiences) — single tree at MVP.
- Date-effective hierarchies (Oracle pattern) — single static tree at MVP.

## Dependencies

- INTERSECTS with acct-063 (expense taxonomy) — both expand `account_kind` for reporting; this issue handles the categorization layer, acct-063 the specific expense kinds.

## Priority

P3 — reporting capability gap-fill.

## Surfaced from

ERP_RESEARCH.md Group 4 acct-063 research + cross-cutting reporting structure observation.
notes: 2026-05-07: Re-scoped to Phase G2 of acct-wb75 convergence. Per research/posting-lines-convergence-plan.md §4.G.G2. Chart-of-accounts hierarchy via account_kinds.parent_kind_id forming a tree. Sequence after Phase G1 (acct-2thf row-table).

title: Generic accruals + auto-reverse-next-period primitive
description:
## Why this issue exists

We have specific accrual mechanisms baked into specific functions:
- GRNI accrual (ap_unsettled, mig 0034)
- Sold-not-yet-invoiced (ar_unsettled, mig 0079)
- Future: unrealized FX (acct-3dz2)

Each of these manually implements the auto-reverse-next-period pattern. Generic month-end accruals (operating expense accruals, prepaid expense amortization, deferred revenue recognition) need a reusable primitive.

ERP_RESEARCH.md surfaced this implicitly — SAP's standard close process makes auto-reverse-next-period a universal primitive. Currently we'd hand-roll it for each new accrual type.

## Scope

1. New tables:
   - `accruals(id, code, name, accrual_type ENUM('expense', 'revenue', 'prepaid', 'deferred', 'fx_unrealized'), debit_account_kind, credit_account_kind, active_at, obsolete_at)`.
   - `accrual_postings(id, accrual_id, period_id, amount, currency, business_date, reverse_at_period_id, status ENUM('posted','reversed','cancelled'), original_transfer_id, reversal_transfer_id, posted_by, posted_at)`.

2. Functions:
   - `post_accrual(p_accrual_code, p_amount, p_currency, p_business_date, p_reverse_at_period_id, p_actor, p_idempotency_key)`: posts the accrual + records reversal scheduling.
   - `process_period_reversals(p_period_id)`: at period start (or via close_period orchestrator), walks accrual_postings WHERE reverse_at_period_id = p_period_id AND status = 'posted'; emits reversal transfers; flips status to 'reversed'.
   - Hook into close_period: scheduled reversals fire automatically.

3. Audit-friendly:
   - Original + reversal transfer IDs both recorded.
   - Cancellation path for accruals that should NOT reverse (e.g., true-up adjustments).

## Use cases the primitive unlocks

- FX unrealized revaluation auto-reverse (acct-3dz2 — currently designed bespoke).
- Operating expense accruals (utilities billed in arrears).
- Deferred revenue recognition (subscription revenue spread over period).
- Prepaid expense amortization (annual insurance amortized monthly).
- Lease accruals under ASC 842 / IFRS 16.
- Bonus accruals (HR-driven, accrued monthly, paid quarterly).
- Warranty accruals.

## Industry mapping

- SAP: Posting with auto-reversal indicator (FBS1 / Manual Accrual Engine + CO-PA accrual postings); FB60 with reverse-on date.
- Oracle Cloud: Manual journals with auto-reversal flag + Period-end accrual program.
- D365: General journals with reversing entry option; accrual schemes.
- NetSuite: Reversing journal entries (auto-reverse on first day of next period).

## Compliance anchors

- ASC 606 deferred revenue / ASC 842 leases / ASC 250 accounting changes.
- SOX 404 accrual controls.
- IFRS 16 lease accruals.

## Acceptance

- accruals + accrual_postings schema.
- post_accrual + process_period_reversals functions.
- Hook integrated into close_period orchestrator (or period-open trigger).
- Tests: post → close period → verify reversal; cancel before reversal; idempotency on replay.
- Migrate acct-3dz2 unrealized-FX implementation to use this primitive (proves the abstraction).

## Priority

P3 — quality-of-life primitive. Highest-value if multiple accrual types are anticipated; less urgent if FX reval is the only use case in the near term.

## Surfaced from

ERP_RESEARCH.md acct-3dz2 research (auto-reverse-next-period as universal pattern across all 4 ERPs).

title: Bank reconciliation workflow
description:
## Why this issue exists

Bank reconciliation is a universal ERP module — every operating entity reconciles their bank statement against the cash account in the GL monthly (or weekly). We have a `cash` account_kind and post_ar_payment / post_ap_payment touch it, but there's no:
- Bank statement import
- Statement-line-to-transaction matching
- Outstanding-items tracking (deposits in transit, outstanding checks)
- Reconciliation report

## Scope

1. New tables:
   - `bank_accounts(id, code, name, currency CHAR(3), gl_cash_account_id, bank_name, account_number_masked, active_at, inactive_at)`.
   - `bank_statements(id, bank_account_id, statement_date, opening_balance, closing_balance, status ENUM('imported','reconciling','reconciled'), imported_at, reconciled_at, reconciled_by)`.
   - `bank_statement_lines(id, statement_id, line_no, transaction_date, description, amount, direction ENUM('debit','credit'), reference, matched_transfer_id NULL, match_status ENUM('unmatched','matched','accepted_with_difference','disputed'))`.
   - `bank_recon_outstanding_items(id, bank_account_id, transfer_id, item_type ENUM('deposit_in_transit','outstanding_check','adjustment'), amount, recorded_at, cleared_at)`.

2. Functions:
   - `import_bank_statement(p_bank_account_id, p_statement_lines JSONB)`: bulk import.
   - `auto_match_statement_lines(p_statement_id)`: heuristic matching on (date, amount, reference) against transfers in the cash account.
   - `accept_match(p_statement_line_id, p_transfer_id, p_actor)`: confirms a match.
   - `record_recon_adjustment(p_bank_account_id, p_amount, p_reason, p_account_id)`: handles bank fees, interest, errors via post_transfers.
   - `complete_reconciliation(p_statement_id, p_actor)`: validates GL cash balance + outstanding items = bank closing balance; raises P0050+ on mismatch.

3. Reporting:
   - Outstanding deposits + checks list.
   - Reconciliation summary (book balance + adjustments + outstanding = bank balance).

## Industry mapping

- SAP: Bank Statement Import (FF.5 / FF67 / FF_5) + Electronic Bank Statement (EBS) processing + BAI/MT940 formats.
- Oracle Cloud: Cash Management + Bank Statement Import + auto-reconciliation rules.
- D365: Bank statement reconciliation + Advanced bank reconciliation; MT940/BAI2/CSV import.
- NetSuite: Bank Reconciliation + bank feeds + Match Bank Data.

## Industry extensions

- Real-time bank feeds via Plaid / Yodlee / Tink.
- Lockbox processing for AR remittance auto-application.
- Positive pay / fraud prevention integration.

## Compliance anchors

- SOX 404 cash controls.
- AICPA Trust Services Criteria (system audit).

## Acceptance

- bank_accounts + bank_statements + lines + outstanding_items schema.
- Statement import + auto-match + accept-match functions.
- Reconciliation completion validates balance.
- Tests: full import → match → adjust → complete cycle; mismatch detection.

## Out of scope

- Bank format parsers (BAI2, MT940, CSV) — application-tier (Rust crate).
- Real-time feed integration — application-tier.

## Priority

P3 — operational gap-fill. Common in any real shop.

## Surfaced from

ERP_RESEARCH.md cross-cutting (mentioned as universal AR/AP module across all 4 ERPs; not on our backlog).

title: Cycle counting / physical inventory workflow
description:
## Why this issue exists

We have a `cycle_count_adj` reason in the transfer_reason enum (mig 0002) and `post_inventory_adjustment` (mig 0022) can be used for ad-hoc adjustments, but there's no actual cycle-count workflow — no count plan, no count entry, no variance approval, no per-SKU / per-location count cadence tracking.

This is a basic operational capability that every mainstream ERP ships:
- SAP: MI01/MI04/MI07 — Create count document → Enter counts → Post differences. ABC analysis drives count cadence.
- Oracle Cloud: Cycle count generates schedule, approval threshold for variances, count entry UI.
- D365: Counting journals (manual + cycle); ABC code + count threshold per item.
- NetSuite: Cycle Count Plans + Count Entries + variance approval workflow.

## Scope

1. New tables:
   - `cycle_count_plans(id, name, location_filter JSONB, cadence ENUM('daily','weekly','monthly','quarterly','annual'), abc_filter, active_at)`.
   - `cycle_count_runs(id, plan_id, run_date, status ENUM('draft','in_progress','completed','cancelled'), posted_by)`.
   - `cycle_count_lines(id, run_id, sku_id, location_id, expected_qty, counted_qty, variance_qty, variance_amount, status ENUM('pending','approved','rejected'), approved_by, approved_at)`.

2. Functions:
   - `generate_cycle_count_run(p_plan_id, p_business_date)`: snapshots expected qty per (sku, location) per the plan's filter.
   - `record_cycle_count_line(p_run_id, p_sku, p_location, p_counted_qty)`: records the count.
   - `approve_cycle_count_variance(p_line_id, p_actor, p_approval_reason)`: gated on variance threshold; over threshold needs approval (RBAC).
   - `post_cycle_count_run(p_run_id)`: emits transfers via post_inventory_adjustment for each approved variance line, reason=cycle_count_adj.

3. ABC classification: skus.abc_class TEXT NULL (A/B/C/D); cadence drives by ABC class.

4. Variance threshold: skus.cycle_count_variance_threshold_pct NUMERIC(5,2) — over-threshold variances require approval.

5. Reporting: open variances by location, count completion % per plan run, audit trail of approvals.

## Why this matters

- High-velocity warehouses: weekly A-class counts catch shrinkage early.
- Audit / compliance: SOX requires periodic physical inventory verification.
- Cost accuracy: WAC pools drift if shrinkage/overage isn't periodically reconciled.
- Negative-inventory remediation (acct-9ij): catch-up workflow needs count data.

## Industry mapping

- SAP: MI01/MI04/MI07 + count documents + ABC analysis + posting differences.
- Oracle Cloud: Cycle count execution + approval + variance posting; ABC classification per item-org.
- D365: Counting journal + count groups + min/max thresholds + warehouse mobile count.
- NetSuite: Cycle Count Plans + Auto-generation + approval routing.

## Compliance anchors

- SOX 404 inventory controls.
- ASC 330 inventory measurement (periodic verification).
- ISO 9001 §8.5.4 preservation.

## Acceptance

- cycle_count_plans + runs + lines schema.
- generate_cycle_count_run, record_cycle_count_line, approve_cycle_count_variance, post_cycle_count_run functions.
- ABC classification on skus.
- Threshold-driven approval gating.
- Tests: full plan → run → count → approve → post round-trip; over-threshold rejection; bulk approval.

## Out of scope

- RFID / barcode integration (application-tier).
- Mobile count UI (application-tier).

## Dependencies

- SOFT: RBAC for approval roles.

## Priority

P3 — operational gap-fill.

## Surfaced from

ERP_RESEARCH.md cross-cutting (acct-9ij research surfaced count workflow as part of negative-inventory catch-up; broader gap is independent).

title: RBAC / authorization framework (consolidated doc Q6)
description:
## Why this issue exists

Consolidated doc Part VII Q6 (RBAC / authorization model) has been open since project start. ERP_RESEARCH.md surfaces it as a precondition for multiple high-value features:

- acct-ir7 multi-stage ECO approval (approver roles)
- acct-7h4 period reopen (separate role from poster)
- acct-9ij negative-inventory authorization
- New approval-workflow framework (approver_role)
- Payroll runs (post_payroll_run authorization)
- Period close (close_period authorization)
- Refund / advance / deposit handling (cash-out authorization)

Today every entry-point function takes a `p_actor UUID` parameter that is unvalidated — no permission check, no role concept, no audit beyond who-posted.

## Scope

1. New tables:
   - `roles(id, code, name, description, active_at, inactive_at)`.
   - `permissions(id, code, description)`.
   - `role_permissions(role_id, permission_id)`.
   - `users(id, code, name, email, active_at, inactive_at)`.
   - `user_roles(user_id, role_id, granted_at, granted_by, revoked_at)`.

2. Permission model:
   - Permission codes: namespace.action — e.g., `ledger.post`, `period.close`, `period.reopen`, `eco.approve`, `payment.authorize`, `inventory.permit_negative`, etc.
   - Built-in roles: `accountant`, `controller`, `inventory_clerk`, `engineer`, `approver`, `admin`.

3. Helper:
   - `_check_permission(p_actor UUID, p_permission_code TEXT) RETURNS BOOLEAN` — gates entry-point functions.
   - Entry-point functions raise P0050+ on permission denial.

4. Audit:
   - `user_action_log(user_id, action_code, target_table, target_id, actor_at)` — append-only, distinct from `transfers` audit.

5. Backward compat:
   - Bootstrap a single 'system' user + 'admin' role with all permissions; existing tests pass through unchanged.
   - Gradual rollout: each entry-point function adds a permission check guarded by a config flag (rbac_enforced BOOLEAN per role) so legacy callers still work.

## Industry mapping

- SAP: Authorization objects (S_TCODE, F_BKPF_BUK, etc.) + roles + profiles via PFCG; SU01 user master.
- Oracle Cloud: Function Security + Data Security via roles in Identity Cloud Service.
- D365: Security roles + duties + privileges + permissions; per-legal-entity grants.
- NetSuite: Role + permissions + restrictions (record-level); SuiteCloud Identity.

## Compliance anchors

- SOX 404 segregation of duties.
- ISO 27001 access control.
- HIPAA / PCI-DSS for verticals.

## Out of scope (later)

- Federated identity (SAML / OIDC integration) — application-tier.
- Per-record row-level access (SAP's data-security model) — heavy.
- Time-bounded grants — post-MVP.

## Acceptance

- roles + permissions + users + user_roles schema.
- _check_permission helper.
- At least 5 entry-point functions gated (e.g., close_period, post_eco_approve, post_payroll_run, post_ap_payment authorization, reopen_period when it lands).
- Audit log table.
- Bootstrap 'admin' role with all permissions.
- Tests: permission-denied raises P0050+; admin passes through; role-grant lifecycle.

## Dependencies

- BLOCKS: acct-ir7 multi-stage approval, acct-7h4 reopen role, approval-workflow framework, post_payroll_run authorization, post_ap_payment authorization.

## Priority

P3 — long-open Part VII Q6. Recommend prioritizing as foundation for multi-stage approval features.

## Surfaced from

ERP_RESEARCH.md cross-cutting + Part VII Q6.

title: Generic approval-workflow framework
description:
## Why this issue exists

Multiple workflows need multi-stage approval — ECO approval (acct-ir7), vendor invoice approval, journal entry approval, payment runs, period-close approval, customer credit/refund authorization, large purchase orders. Today we have one-off approval logic in post_eco_approve (single-stage). A generic framework factors out the shared machinery.

ERP_RESEARCH.md showed that all four mainstream ERPs have generic workflow engines:
- SAP: Workflow Engine (WS / SWE / SWO) — drives approvals across FI, MM, PP, etc.
- Oracle Cloud: BPM / Workflow Manager — approval rules, escalations, parallel approvers.
- D365: Workflow infrastructure — approval, completion, automatic and manual.
- NetSuite: SuiteFlow + SuiteApprovals — declarative + scriptable approval flows.

## Scope

1. New tables:
   - `approval_workflows(id, code, name, target_table, target_filter JSONB, active_at, obsolete_at)`.
   - `approval_workflow_steps(workflow_id, step_no, approver_role, approver_user_id NULL, condition JSONB, parallel_with_step NULL, escalation_after INTERVAL)`.
   - `approval_requests(id, workflow_id, target_table, target_id, status ENUM('pending', 'approved', 'rejected', 'cancelled'), submitted_by, submitted_at)`.
   - `approval_step_results(request_id, step_no, approver_id, status, comments, acted_at)`.

2. Functions:
   - `submit_for_approval(p_workflow_code, p_target_table, p_target_id, p_actor)`: creates approval_request + initial step.
   - `approve_step(p_request_id, p_step_no, p_actor, p_comments)`: advances; if final step, sets request to 'approved' and triggers a callback.
   - `reject_step(p_request_id, p_step_no, p_actor, p_reason)`: terminates request.
   - Callback contract: each approval_workflow declares an `on_approve` and `on_reject` SQL function name; final transition invokes them with target_id.

3. RBAC integration: approver_role gates on RBAC framework (separate new issue).

4. Migration of existing single-stage approvals:
   - post_eco_approve becomes a callback registered against the eco_approval workflow.
   - Existing post_eco_approve stays as backward-compat alias.

## Industry mapping

- SAP Workflow Engine — generic; ~20 yrs of evolution; LO-ECH ECO uses it.
- Oracle BPM Cloud — declarative + JavaScript; embedded across SCM/Financials.
- D365 Workflow infrastructure — declarative state machine; per-form workflow.
- NetSuite SuiteFlow — UI-based + SuiteApprovals + email-based approvals.

## Use cases (factor-out targets)

- ECO multi-stage approval (acct-ir7)
- Vendor invoice approval (over threshold)
- Customer credit memo authorization (acct-tae shipped, but no approval gate yet)
- Vendor debit memo authorization (acct-b6e shipped, ditto)
- Standard cost roll approval (mig 0028 has none)
- Period close approval
- Payment run authorization (post_ap_payment, post_ar_refund)

## Compliance anchors

- SOX 404 segregation of duties.
- Internal-control documentation (ICFR).
- Spend-management policies.

## Acceptance

- approval_workflows + approval_workflow_steps + approval_requests + approval_step_results schema.
- Generic submit/approve/reject functions.
- At least one workflow migrated to the framework (recommend ECO as the showcase).
- RBAC integration (gates on RBAC framework issue).

## Priority

P3 — factors out duplicated logic; quality-of-life. Recommend AFTER RBAC framework.

## Dependencies

- SOFT: RBAC framework.

## Surfaced from

ERP_RESEARCH.md Group 2 acct-ir7 research + cross-cutting recurrence.

title: Transfer orders for intra/inter-warehouse stock movement
description:
## Why this issue exists

We have NO transfer-order document — moves between locations / warehouses are not modeled at the document layer. The closest primitive is a manual cycle_count_adj or post_inventory_adjustment, which is not the right semantics: transfer orders are bidirectional documents (ship from A, receive at B) with in-transit tracking and cost preservation, not adjustments.

ERP_RESEARCH.md surfaced this as gating acct-3uh (OSP physical custody): SAP's Special Stock O pattern relies on transfer-order-like 541/542/543 movements, NetSuite's outsourcing-location-per-vendor needs transfer documents, D365's vendor-managed-warehouse pattern uses Transfer Journals.

## Scope

1. New tables:
   - `transfer_orders(id, from_location_id, to_location_id, business_date, status ENUM('draft', 'shipped', 'in_transit', 'received', 'closed'), posted_by, idempotency_key, notes, created_at)`.
   - `transfer_order_lines(id, transfer_id, line_no, sku_id, qty_requested, qty_shipped, qty_received, unit_cost_at_ship)`.

2. Functions:
   - `post_transfer_ship(p_transfer_id, p_lines, p_business_date, ...)`: drains stock_available(from_location), credits stock_in_transit (NEW account_kind, qty-only). Persists unit_cost snapshot per line for in-transit valuation.
   - `post_transfer_receive(p_transfer_id, p_lines, p_business_date, ...)`: drains stock_in_transit, credits stock_available(to_location).
   - In-transit value pool: inv_value_in_transit (NEW account_kind, value-side companion to stock_in_transit, partitioned by (sku, currency)).

3. Cost preservation: same-cost-basis transfer is identity; cross-cost-method-flip (e.g., from_location uses standard, to_location uses wac_perpetual) snapshots cost_method_at_ship per line (mirror of mig 0087 pattern) and routes any reconciliation through variance_transfer.

4. New transfer_reasons: transfer_ship (qty + value out of from-location), transfer_receive (qty + value into to-location).

5. New error codes (P0050+): transfer_invalid, transfer_overshipped, transfer_already_received, etc.

## Why this matters

- acct-3uh (OSP custody) — Special Stock O pattern needs transfer document.
- Multi-warehouse operations (any non-trivial real shop) — basic capability gap.
- Drop-ship workflow (separate new issue) — requires transfer-like semantics.

## Industry mapping

- SAP: Stock Transport Order (STO) — type UB/NB/UD; movement types 351/641/643/645 for plant-to-plant, 311 for storage-location-to-storage-location.
- Oracle: Internal Sales Order or Inter-Org Transfer; in-transit account on the source-org side.
- D365: Transfer Order (Inventory management → Transfer orders); Transit warehouse type for in-transit valuation.
- NetSuite: Transfer Order; In-Transit account for inter-location.

## Compliance anchors

- Sarbanes-Oxley: in-transit inventory must be auditably accounted on the books of one entity at all times.
- Tax: in-transit goods crossing borders may have customs/duty implications (gates on tax integration).

## Acceptance

- transfer_orders + transfer_order_lines schema.
- post_transfer_ship + post_transfer_receive functions.
- inv_value_in_transit + stock_in_transit account_kinds.
- Cost-method snapshot at ship time (like mig 0087 receipts).
- Tests: same-location reject; same-cost-method round-trip; cross-cost-method round-trip with variance.

## Out of scope

- In-transit insurance accruals (separate concern).
- Transfer pricing across legal entities (gates on intercompany work).

## Priority

P3 — gap-fill. Recommend before acct-3uh's special-stock layer (which can build on this primitive).

## Surfaced from

ERP_RESEARCH.md Group 4 acct-3uh research.

title: Intercompany transactions + matching + consolidation eliminations
description:
## Why this issue exists

Once a multi-entity model exists (separate issue), cross-entity transactions need intercompany matching — entity A sells to entity B, both legs post in their respective functional currencies, the consolidated report eliminates the intercompany revenue and COGS so they don't double-count.

All four mainstream ERPs handle this:
- SAP: AGIS (Advanced Global Intercompany System) + cross-company-code postings + group reporting eliminations.
- Oracle Cloud: Intercompany Module + AGIS + consolidation rules.
- D365: Intercompany sales/purchase + consolidation companies.
- NetSuite OneWorld: Intercompany journal entries + intercompany sales/purchases + automatic eliminations.

## Scope

1. New tables:
   - `intercompany_relationships(from_entity_id, to_entity_id, intercompany_ar_account, intercompany_ap_account, transfer_pricing_method)`.
   - `intercompany_transactions(id, from_entity_id, to_entity_id, currency, amount, business_date, document_type, document_id, status, matched_at)`.

2. Workflow:
   - When entity A ships to entity B (via post_so_ship from A's books to B's customer record): entity A posts ar(B as customer) DR / revenue CR; entity B simultaneously posts inv_value DR / ap(A as vendor) CR.
   - Intercompany matching: nightly job pairs A's ar with B's ap; raises mismatches.
   - At consolidation: eliminate matched ar↔ap and revenue↔expense legs.

3. Currency: each side posts in its own functional currency; settlement uses fx_rates at posting date (gates on realized-FX issue).

4. Transfer pricing:
   - Cost-plus (markup over standard cost)
   - Resale-price-minus (markup-down from sales price)
   - Comparable uncontrolled price (third-party benchmark)

5. New error codes for unmatched intercompany at period close.

## Compliance anchors

- ASC 810 (consolidation) elimination rules.
- IFRS 10 consolidated financial statements.
- Transfer pricing documentation per OECD BEPS Pillar 1/2.

## Industry mapping

- SAP AGIS + cross-company-code postings (transaction OBYA mapping) + ECCS/SEM-BCS for eliminations.
- Oracle Cloud: Intercompany Module with manual + automatic invoicing.
- D365: Intercompany sales/purchase + consolidation companies + global ledger.
- NetSuite: Automated Intercompany Management (AIM) + Intercompany Sales/Purchases + automatic eliminations at consolidation.

## Out of scope

- Transfer-pricing tax compliance reporting (separate compliance project).
- Multi-currency hedging on intercompany flows (gates on hedge-accounting work).

## Dependencies

- HARD: multi-entity / legal-entity model (separate new issue).
- HARD: realized FX on cross-currency settlement (separate new issue).
- SOFT: COA reporting hierarchy (for elimination rule engine).

## Priority

P3 — only matters once multi-entity is real.

## Surfaced from

ERP_RESEARCH.md Group 4 (acct-tt1 cross-currency BOMs research repeatedly cites intercompany flows as the universal cross-entity pattern).

title: Multi-entity / legal-entity / subsidiary model (foundation)
description:
## Why this issue exists

Foundation gap surfaced by ERP_RESEARCH.md (Group 4 across multiple issues). The codebase is single-ledger — there's no concept of legal entity / subsidiary / company code. Every cross-currency BOM (acct-tt1), FX revaluation (acct-3dz2), OSP custody (acct-3uh special-stock pattern), intercompany flow, and consolidation question implicitly assumes one entity boundary.

All four mainstream ERPs have first-class entity models:
- SAP: Company codes (BUKRS) within client; controlling areas span codes; up to 3 currencies per posting (local / group / profit-center) via Material Ledger.
- Oracle: Ledgers (with primary/secondary/reporting currencies) within data access set; legal entities for jurisdictional reporting.
- D365: Legal entities (per-entity COA, currency, period); cross-entity flows always intercompany.
- NetSuite: OneWorld subsidiaries with base currency per (immutable post first-save); cross-subsidiary via intercompany journal entries.

## Scope

1. Decide entity granularity model: single multi-entity ledger vs per-entity ledgers (NetSuite vs SAP shape). Recommend per-entity COA with shared transaction infrastructure (mirrors NetSuite OneWorld and D365 LE).

2. Schema:
   - `entities(id, code, name, functional_currency CHAR(3), country_code, parent_entity_id, active_at, inactive_at)`.
   - All transactional tables (transfers, accounts, periods, work_orders, customers, vendors, sales_orders, purchase_orders, etc.) gain `entity_id UUID NOT NULL` (with default = single bootstrap entity for backward compat).
   - Account partitioning extends from (counterparty_id, currency) to (entity_id, counterparty_id, currency).
   - Periods become per-entity (or shared with per-entity status — design decision).

3. Functional/home currency per entity (replaces the "single home currency" pre-req of acct-3dz2).

4. Cross-entity flows route through intercompany — gates separate issue (Intercompany transactions + matching + consolidation eliminations).

5. Migration strategy: introduce `entities` table + bootstrap row for existing data; backfill `entity_id` columns from the bootstrap row; add NOT NULL constraints. Plan for ~3-5 migrations.

## Why this is foundational

Without entities, the following stay incomplete or hacky:
- acct-3dz2 (FX reval) — home_currency conflated with single-ledger config
- acct-tt1 (cross-currency BOMs) — every example is fundamentally cross-entity in the real world
- acct-3uh (OSP custody) — vendor-managed warehouses are typically distinct entities
- acct-rp2 (sales tax) — nexus is per-entity
- acct-9e2 (payroll) — payroll is per-entity (legal employer)
- acct-7h4 (period reopen) — periods are per-entity in every mainstream ERP

## Risk

This is large — touches every transactional table. Best landed BEFORE the larger Phase 2 features above to avoid retrofitting. But for current single-entity workloads, the bootstrap-row approach keeps the migration-complexity tractable.

## Compliance anchors

- IFRS / GAAP consolidated reporting requires legal-entity boundary.
- ASC 830 functional-currency designation per entity.
- Tax jurisdiction nexus per entity.

## Industry mapping

- SAP: Company code + Controlling area + Operating concern (CO-PA) + Profit center.
- Oracle Cloud: Ledger + Legal entity (with subledger separation).
- D365: Legal entity + cross-company workflow.
- NetSuite: OneWorld subsidiary tree + consolidated reporting + intercompany rules.

## Acceptance

- entities table + entity_id partitioning across all transactional tables.
- Bootstrap migration preserves existing single-entity data.
- per-entity functional_currency replaces single-ledger home_currency.
- Cross-entity flows raise "use intercompany" error (intercompany work is separate issue).

## Priority

P3 — large foundation. Recommend prioritizing if multi-entity scenarios are anticipated; otherwise can stay deferred as long as we document the implicit single-entity assumption.

## Surfaced from

ERP_RESEARCH.md Group 4 cross-cutting (acct-3dz2, acct-tt1, acct-3uh) + cross-cutting themes section.
notes: 2026-05-07: Sequence after Phase D (acct-wb75.3) ships for cleanest legal_entity_id promotion. Phase A2 (acct-ewhs) laid the column with DEFAULT 1; Phase D establishes the inventory_movements foundation that becomes entity-scoped at acct-3gzh. Per research/posting-lines-convergence-plan.md §10.

title: Realized FX gain/loss on cross-currency cash settlement
description:
## Why this issue exists

post_ar_payment (mig 0081) and post_ap_payment (mig 0082) both reject cash-currency ≠ ar/ap-currency. When a customer pays a EUR invoice with USD cash, or we pay a USD bill with EUR cash, the realized FX gain/loss leg can't post because both functions assume single-currency settlement.

This is the foundational pre-req for acct-3dz2 (unrealized FX revaluation) — research in ERP_RESEARCH.md identified that period-end revaluation of unrealized FX is incomplete without realized-FX-on-settlement first; SAP / Oracle / D365 / NetSuite all separate the two and the realized leg is the simpler primitive.

## Problem walked through

Invoice posts:
  ar(customer, EUR) DR 1000 / revenue(EUR) CR 1000   @ rate 1.10 USD/EUR ($1100 home)

Customer pays (later, rate now 1.20):
  Naive 2-leg: cash(USD) DR 1200 / ar(customer, EUR) CR 1000 → currency mismatch, P0010
  Single-currency (today): cash(EUR) DR 1000 / ar(customer, EUR) CR 1000 → forces operator to convert externally; loses FX gain in the ledger

What we want:
  cash(USD) DR 1200 / ar(customer, EUR) CR 1000 / realized_fx_gain(USD) CR 200
  (or symmetric loss leg if rate moved adversely)

## Scope

1. Add 2 new account_kind values: `realized_fx_gain`, `realized_fx_loss` (currency-only, un-partitioned, P&L). Mirror variance_* pattern.
2. Extend post_ar_payment + post_ap_payment to accept p_cash_currency CHAR(3) optional parameter; when ≠ counterparty currency, look up fx_rates at p_business_date, compute realized FX delta, emit 3-leg posting (cash DR / ar(or ap) CR / realized_fx_* DR-or-CR per direction).
3. Configuration: home_currency (or per-entity once acct-multi-entity lands).
4. Test scenarios: rate-up gain on ar settlement; rate-down loss on ar; mirror on ap; same-currency pass-through unchanged; multi-payment partial settlements at different rates.
5. New error code P0050+ for missing fx_rate at business_date.

## Why pre-req for acct-3dz2

Unrealized FX reval values open balances at period-end rate; realized FX surfaces at cash settlement. If realized never posts, then over time the open ar/ap balances drift away from "what we'll actually receive in cash" and the period-end reval has nothing to reconcile against — the ledger is incoherent.

## Compliance anchors

- ASC 830 / IAS 21: realized FX gain/loss is a separate P&L line from unrealized; both required under GAAP/IFRS.
- SOX 404 audit trail.

## Industry mapping

- SAP: realized FX posts at clearing (F-32 / F-44) using a separate G/L for exchange differences.
- Oracle Cloud: SLA generates the realized FX leg automatically when receipt currency differs from invoice currency.
- D365: posting profiles configure realized + unrealized FX accounts separately; settlement triggers realized.
- NetSuite: Realized Gain/Loss vs Unrealized Gain/Loss accounts in the OneWorld FX setup.

## Acceptance

- Both post_ar_payment and post_ap_payment accept cross-currency settlement.
- Realized FX leg posts correctly per direction (gain vs loss).

title: FX revaluation: home-currency reporting model + period-end revaluation of open ar/ap balances
description:
## Problem

The codebase tracks balances per-currency-partition (`inv_value_raw EUR` distinct from `inv_value_raw USD`; `ap EUR` distinct from `ap USD`). There's no home-currency translation point in any current workflow.

For multi-currency operators that report consolidated financials in a single home currency (typical), this is incomplete:

- Open EUR ap balance from Q1 receipt at rate 1.10 USD/EUR sits at unchanged EUR throughout Q2.
- Q2 close: home-currency view of that balance has shifted (1.20 USD/EUR by Q2 end).
- Without revaluation, the consolidated income statement understates / overstates depending on direction.

GAAP / IFRS requires period-end revaluation of monetary assets / liabilities denominated in foreign currency. The unrealized FX gain/loss flows to a P&L line (typically `fx_revaluation`).

## Scope

1. Decide on home-currency policy: a single reporting currency per ledger (e.g., USD). Configurable via a `reporting_currency` setting.
2. Define what monetary balances revalue: open ar / ap (and ar_unsettled / ap_unsettled) in non-home currency. Inventory value (raw / fg / wip) does NOT revalue under standard convention — it's measured at historical cost.
3. Implement `run_fx_revaluation(p_period_id, p_business_date)` workflow: walk each non-home-currency monetary account, look up home-currency-equivalent at `fx_rates` for `p_business_date`, compare to the snapshot at last revaluation (or original posting), post the delta to `fx_revaluation`.
4. Snapshot column on accounts (or a side table) for last-revaluation home-currency basis.
5. Test scenarios: rate-up gain, rate-down loss, multiple revaluation runs, no-drift no-op.

## Why this issue exists

acct-vli (FX revaluation on returns) was deferred until this foundation lands. Once this ships, the return-specific drift handling becomes a tiny additive feature reusing the same fx_revaluation account + rate-lookup pattern.

## Acceptance criteria

- Reporting-currency policy decision documented in CLAUDE.md.
- run_fx_revaluation function implemented and tested.
- Test coverage for rate-up / rate-down / no-drift scenarios.
- fx_revaluation account_kind seeded as currency-only un-partitioned.
- Period-close hook (or operator-triggered call) invokes run_fx_revaluation.

## Priority justification

P3: required for credible multi-currency reporting. Domestic-only operators don't need it. acct-vli (P4) is gated on this.

## Dependencies

- None hard. Builds on existing fx_rates table (mig 0004) + fx_revaluation enum value (mig 0002).

## Out of scope

- Hedging / forward contracts / derivative accounting.
- Cross-currency settlements (e.g., paying EUR ap from USD cash).
- Functional currency vs reporting currency distinction (single-level translation only).
design:
DESIGN COMMITMENT (2026-05-05, from ERP_RESEARCH.md):

Split scope: realized-FX (cross-currency settlement leg) is a foundational pre-req that must ship BEFORE unrealized-FX revaluation. The original issue scope conflated both; the dependency makes pure unrealized-only an incomplete delivery.

PRE-REQ (separate new issue — see "Realized FX gain/loss on cross-currency cash settlement"):
- post_ar_payment / post_ap_payment foundational pre-req.
- Both functions today reject cash-currency ≠ ar/ap-currency. The realized FX leg posts when an invoice in EUR is paid with USD cash — delta between invoice rate and payment rate routes through realized_fx_gain / realized_fx_loss.

THIS ISSUE'S REMAINING SCOPE (unrealized period-end revaluation):
- 2 new account_kind: unrealized_fx_gain, unrealized_fx_loss (currency-only, un-partitioned, P&L). Mirror variance_* pattern.
- post_fx_revaluation(p_period_id, p_revalue_at_rate_date, p_actor, p_idempotency_key): walks open per-counterparty per-currency ap / ap_unsettled / ar / ar_unsettled / cash balances; emits paired unrealized_fx_* events. Auto-reverse on period+1 day-1 (canonical SAP/Oracle/D365/NetSuite pattern).
- Treat WIP / inventory as non-monetary per ASC 830 / IAS 21 — exclude from reval (matches all 4 ERPs).

Configuration:
- home_currency / functional_currency at ledger level (single-ledger today; per-entity once entity model lands — gates on multi-entity issue).

Compliance anchors: SOX 404 auditor-traceable trail; IAS 21 monetary-vs-non-monetary distinction; ASC 830 functional-currency designation per legal entity; CTA (Cumulative Translation Adjustment) for consolidation deferred to multi-entity work.

Industry mapping: SAP FAGL_FCV (S/4HANA) / FAGL_FC_VAL (legacy) auto-reverse; Oracle Cloud Revaluation program + SFAS 52 / IAS 21 anchors; D365 per-sub-ledger reval (GL/AR/AP/Bank split to avoid double-counting); NetSuite OneWorld Revalue Open Currency Balances + Foreign Currency Variance Mapping.
notes: 2026-05-07: Sequence after Phase B2 (acct-wb75.1.2) ships for cleanest functional-currency model. B2 introduces legal_entities.functional_currency + transfer_line_currencies extension; FX revaluation builds on that foundation. Per research/posting-lines-convergence-plan.md §10 + R20.

ALTER TABLE po_return_lines

title: post_po_return / post_customer_return: multi-line return doc spanning split states

Per-line routing is the design, but no test exercises a SINGLE return document with multiple lines where each line resolves to a different state.

- Line B: recv_line / ship_line that is uncleared (pre-bill / pre-invoice) → routes to ap_unsettled / ar_unsettled
