title: post_vendor_debit_memo: standalone AP debit memo without PO/receipt reference
description:
## Problem

post_po_return (acct-quk, mig 0085) requires every return line to reference a po_receipt_lines row via NOT NULL FK `recv_line_id`. This precludes legitimate standalone-debit scenarios:

- **Disputed invoice** — vendor billed us for goods we never received, or charged the wrong price; we want a debit memo without sending anything back.
- **Damage-in-transit settlement** — goods arrived damaged but we kept and used them; vendor agrees to a 20% credit. We never returned the goods.
- **Vendor allowance** — quality / volume / promotional discount applied AFTER bill, no goods movement.
- **Stale-PO return** — we return a unit purchased long ago; original PO is archived / pre-system. Goods leave but there's no receipt line to reference.
- **Vendor invoice double-billed** — vendor mistakenly billed twice; we issue a debit memo to clear the duplicate.

Mainstream ERPs distinguish purchase return (inventory-driven, references original receipt) from debit memo (financially-driven, optional goods movement).

## Proposed shape

Mirror of post_customer_credit_memo (parallel issue):

```sql
CREATE TABLE vendor_debit_memos (
  id              UUID PK,
  vendor_id       UUID FK vendors,
  currency        CHAR(3),
  business_date   DATE,
  posted_by       UUID,
  idempotency_key UUID UNIQUE,
  notes           TEXT
);

CREATE TABLE vendor_debit_memo_lines (
  id                 UUID PK,
  memo_id            UUID FK vendor_debit_memos,
  line_no            INT,
  kind               TEXT CHECK (kind IN ('financial', 'goods_return')),
  expense_account_id BIGINT REFERENCES accounts(id),  -- for 'financial' (caller-supplied credit account)
  sku_id             UUID,                            -- for 'goods_return'
  location_id        UUID,                            -- for 'goods_return'
  qty                BIGINT,                          -- for 'goods_return'
  unit_cost          BIGINT,                          -- for 'goods_return' (caller-supplied)
  amount             BIGINT NOT NULL,
  CHECK (
    (kind = 'financial' AND expense_account_id IS NOT NULL AND sku_id IS NULL)
    OR
    (kind = 'goods_return' AND sku_id IS NOT NULL AND location_id IS NOT NULL
       AND qty IS NOT NULL AND qty > 0 AND unit_cost IS NOT NULL)
  )
);
```

post_vendor_debit_memo(p_vendor_id, p_currency, p_lines, ...) per line:
- 'financial': ap (or ap_unsettled, per acct-tk7) DR / caller-supplied expense account CR amount. The credit side is whatever the original cost was originally booked to (e.g., a specific expense GL line for a service charge, or inv_value_raw if reducing inventory cost without physical return).
- 'goods_return': mirror po_return's logic (vendor_pool DR / stock_available CR; ap DR / inv_value_raw CR), with caller-supplied unit_cost. PPV math gets tricky without a po_line reference — caller may need to either accept zero PPV or specify a 'reference unit_cost' separately.

## Why no disposition on AP side

Goods leaving us go in one direction (out the door to vendor); there's no equivalent of restock/scrap/repair on the inflow path. The customer-return disposition exists because customer-returned goods can land in different stock pools depending on condition. AP returns just reduce stock_available.

## PPV handling for goods_return without recv reference

Without po_line.unit_cost to compare against, we can't compute PPV the same way. Two options:
- Caller-supplied 'original_unit_cost' on the line — if differs from current unit_cost, compute PPV reversal.
- Skip PPV reversal entirely on standalone goods returns; leave PPV at receipt-time levels and accept the inconsistency.

The simpler (skip PPV) is fine for MVP. Document the limitation.

## Acceptance criteria

- New tables + post_vendor_debit_memo function.
- Tests: pure financial memo (e.g., disputed invoice for $200); standalone goods return (sku without recv reference); damaged-in-transit allowance scenario.
- Routing follows acct-tk7 (ap vs ap_unsettled depending on bill state).
- No regression to po_return semantics.

## Priority justification

P3: real-world business need, more common in AP than AR (vendor disputes are routine). Not strictly blocking but high-value.

## Dependencies

- acct-quk (closed): po_return reference shape.
- acct-tk7 (open, P2): state-aware routing.

## Related

- acct-customer-credit-memo (parallel AR-side issue, filed alongside this one)

## Out of scope

- Apply-debit-memo-against-bill workflow (settlement of which specific bills are reduced)
- Vendor-side cost-method-snapshot semantics (intersects with acct-6d8 — handled there if FK is added later)
close_reason: Closed

title: post_customer_credit_memo: standalone AR credit memo without SO/shipment reference
description:
## Problem

post_customer_return (acct-ari, mig 0084) requires every return line to reference a so_shipment_lines row via NOT NULL FK `ship_line_id`. This precludes legitimate standalone-credit scenarios:

- **Goodwill credit** — "sorry about the delay, here's $50 off your next order." Pure financial adjustment, no goods returning.
- **Dispute settlement** — customer claims the invoice was wrong; we agree to credit $200. No goods flow.
- **Volume rebate / promotional credit** — period-end rebate on cumulative purchases. Pure ar credit.
- **Stale-SO return** — customer returns a unit purchased years ago; original SO is archived / lost / pre-system. Goods come back but there's no ship line to reference.

Mainstream ERPs (SAP, Oracle Cloud, NetSuite) distinguish:
- **Sales return**: inventory-driven, references original shipment, drives qty back to stock per disposition. (This is what we have.)
- **Credit memo**: financially-driven; goods movement is OPTIONAL; references the customer / currency / amount but not necessarily a shipment.

## Proposed shape

New tables + function for credit memos, separate from customer_returns:

```sql
CREATE TABLE customer_credit_memos (
  id              UUID PK,
  customer_id     UUID FK customers,
  currency        CHAR(3),
  business_date   DATE,
  posted_by       UUID,
  idempotency_key UUID UNIQUE,
  notes           TEXT
);

CREATE TABLE customer_credit_memo_lines (
  id                 UUID PK,
  memo_id            UUID FK customer_credit_memos,
  line_no            INT,
  kind               TEXT CHECK (kind IN ('financial', 'goods_return')),
  -- financial: revenue_account_id + amount drive caller-supplied debit
  -- goods_return: sku_id + location_id + qty + unit_cost + disposition like customer_return
  revenue_account_id BIGINT REFERENCES accounts(id),  -- for 'financial'
  sku_id             UUID,                            -- for 'goods_return'
  location_id        UUID,                            -- for 'goods_return'
  qty                BIGINT,                          -- for 'goods_return'
  unit_cost          BIGINT,                          -- for 'goods_return' (caller-supplied)
  disposition        return_disposition,              -- for 'goods_return'
  amount             BIGINT NOT NULL,
  tax_amount         BIGINT NOT NULL DEFAULT 0,
  CHECK (
    (kind = 'financial' AND revenue_account_id IS NOT NULL AND sku_id IS NULL)
    OR
    (kind = 'goods_return' AND sku_id IS NOT NULL AND location_id IS NOT NULL
       AND qty IS NOT NULL AND qty > 0 AND unit_cost IS NOT NULL
       AND disposition IS NOT NULL)
  )
);
```

post_customer_credit_memo(p_customer_id, p_currency, p_lines, ...) per line:
- 'financial': caller-supplied account DR / ar (or ar_unsettled, per acct-tk7) CR amount.
- 'goods_return': mirror customer_return's per-disposition logic (qty back per disposition, value back per disposition), with caller-supplied unit_cost.

## Tax handling
Like customer_return, route tax to ar_unsettled if pre-invoice context, ar otherwise (gated by acct-tk7). For pure financial credit memos, tax routing is caller-decided (passed as separate line).

## Why a separate function vs extending customer_return

- customer_return's NOT NULL FK is a load-bearing invariant: it guarantees three-way auditability (every reverse is tied to a forward). Relaxing it would lose that.
- The two flows have different business semantics — customers / accountants distinguish 'return' (you got our goods back) from 'credit memo' (here's a credit).
- Separate doc types make audit reports cleaner.

## Acceptance criteria

- New tables + post_customer_credit_memo function.
- Tests: pure financial memo (e.g., $50 goodwill); standalone goods return (sku without ship reference); mixed memo (one financial line + one goods line on same memo).
- Tax handling consistent with customer_return (likely depending on acct-tk7).
- No regression to customer_return semantics.

## Priority justification

P3: real business need but not blocking. Most installations have at least the goodwill / settlement use case. Companies without those flows can ship without it.

## Dependencies

- acct-ari (closed): customer_return reference shape.
- acct-tk7 (open, P2): state-aware routing — credit memo also needs to choose ar vs ar_unsettled.

## Related

- acct-vendor-debit-memo (parallel AP-side issue, filed alongside this one)

## Out of scope

- Backfilling old archived SOs (orthogonal data-recovery problem).
- Allocating credit memos against specific invoices for settlement (that's an apply-credit workflow; defer).
close_reason: Closed

title: Cross-period PPV reversal: prior-period adjustment account vs current-period variance
description:
## Problem

When a return crosses a period boundary, PPV reversal currently posts to `variance_ppv` in the CURRENT period. This is acceptable for a Phase 1/2 system but doesn't satisfy SOX-style financial reporting that requires explicit prior-period adjustments.

### Concrete

- Q1: Receipt 10 @ po=120, std=100. variance_ppv DR 200 in Q1's P&L.
- Q1 closes. Books frozen.
- Q2: Return all 10 units. post_po_return posts variance_ppv CR 200 in Q2's P&L.

Net effect across Q1+Q2: PPV is 0 (correctly — the receipt that caused it was reversed). But Q1 reported a $200 PPV expense that's being undone in Q2 with no audit trail explaining the relationship.

## Mainstream ERP convention

Two acceptable patterns:

### Pattern A: Current-period offset (what we do)
PPV reversal hits variance_ppv in the return period. Simpler. Accepted by GAAP for non-material amounts.

### Pattern B: Prior-period adjustment account
Introduce `variance_ppv_prior_period_adj` (or similar name). Cross-period PPV reversals route there instead of variance_ppv. The new account is itself a P&L line but explicitly distinguished — financial statements call it out as a prior-period correction.

The dispatch is: 'is the original receipt's business_date in a closed period?' — if yes, route to variance_ppv_prior_period_adj. If no, current-period variance_ppv (existing path).

## Schema change for Pattern B

- ALTER TYPE account_kind ADD VALUE 'variance_ppv_prior_period_adj'
- Seed currency-only un-partitioned accounts in db/fixtures/small/seed.sql
- post_po_return: lookup the receipt's business_date via po_receipt_lines.receipt_id → po_receipts.business_date. If that period is closed (consult periods table), route PPV to the adj account.

Mirror reasoning applies on AR side (customer_return doesn't have direct PPV but it has revenue / tax reversal that crosses periods — SAME pattern with `revenue_prior_period_adj` could be argued, though revenue corrections are usually material enough to warrant restatement rather than P&L adjustment).

## Decision needed

- Is the SOX-grade prior-period adjustment account warranted? Or is current-period offset sufficient for our target audience?
- If warranted: just for PPV (AP side), or also revenue corrections (AR side)?

## Acceptance criteria

- Decision documented.
- If Pattern B chosen: new account_kind + seed + post_po_return dispatch + test coverage.
- Tests: cross-period return routes PPV to the right account; same-period return uses existing path.

## Priority justification

P3: pure-correctness work motivated by formal audit/disclosure. Most operators won't notice; auditors might.

## Dependencies

- acct-quk (closed)
- acct-ari (closed) — only relevant if we extend pattern to revenue corrections.

## Out of scope

- Restating prior-period financial statements (that's a process question, not code).
- Material vs non-material thresholds (caller policy; caller can manually route at the period boundary if needed).
close_reason: Closed

title: Returns: expose p_override_closed_period parameter on post_po_return / post_customer_return
description:
## Problem

post_transfers takes `p_override_closed_period BOOLEAN DEFAULT FALSE`. When TRUE, it bypasses the period.closed_at gate (P0005). post_po_return and post_customer_return don't accept this param — they always pass FALSE to post_transfers.

This is fine 90% of the time. But occasionally a closed period needs to be reopened (acct-7h4 future workflow) AND have a return posted to it. Without exposing the override, callers can't backdate returns to closed periods even when the period has been formally reopened.

## Fix

Add p_override_closed_period BOOLEAN DEFAULT FALSE to:
- post_po_return(p_vendor_id, p_lines, p_business_date, p_posted_by, p_idempotency_key, p_notes, **p_override_closed_period DEFAULT FALSE**)
- post_customer_return(p_customer_id, p_lines, p_business_date, p_posted_by, p_idempotency_key, p_notes, **p_override_closed_period DEFAULT FALSE**)

Pass the param through to post_transfers's second argument.

DROP+CREATE required (PG forbids parameter signature changes via CREATE OR REPLACE — bd memory `pg-forbids-renaming-function-parameters-via-create-or`).

## Acceptance criteria

- Both functions gain the optional parameter.
- Default FALSE preserves existing call-site semantics.
- Tests: closed-period return is rejected (P0005) when FALSE; succeeds when TRUE.

## Priority justification

title: Returns: snapshot cost_method at original receipt/ship time
description:
## Problem

post_po_return and post_customer_return dispatch on the SKU's CURRENT cost_method (`SELECT cost_method FROM skus`). If the cost_method changed between original receipt/ship and return, the math is wrong.

### Concrete scenario

- Day 1: SKU-A is 'standard' (std_cost = 100). Receipt 10 @ po=100 → inv_value_raw +1000 (at std), no PPV.
- Day 30: ops decides SKU-A should be 'wac_perpetual'. UPDATE skus SET cost_method='wac_perpetual'. Pool reads as today's running avg.
- Day 35: Customer returns 10 units of original receipt.
- post_po_return now dispatches on cost_method='wac_perpetual', uses po_unit_cost=100 for v_inv_amount.
- v_ap_amount = 10*100 = 1000. v_inv_amount = 10*100 = 1000. v_ppv = 0.
- This happens to be correct here because po=std on Day 1. If po had been 120 with std=100, the original receipt posted PPV of 200; now the return doesn't reverse PPV (because wac branch sets v_ppv=0). Net: PPV remains on the books even though the receipt was reversed.

### Worse mirror: WAC → standard
- Day 1: SKU-A is 'wac_perpetual'. Receipt 10 @ po=100. Pool +10 units, +1000 value at po (no PPV).
- Day 30: SKU goes to 'standard' with new std_cost=120.
- Day 35: Return 10. post_po_return dispatches on standard, computes v_inv_amount = 10*120 = 1200. ap_amount = 10*100 = 1000. PPV = -200 (favorable). Posts variance_ppv DR 200 / ap CR 200.
- The PPV is fictional — there was no PPV on the original receipt because it was WAC. We're inventing variance.

## Solution: snapshot at the time of original event

The fix is to record the cost_method-at-the-time on po_receipt_lines / so_shipment_lines when posting the original document, then read THAT field in the return function.

### Schema change
- ALTER TABLE po_receipt_lines ADD COLUMN cost_method_at_receipt cost_method NOT NULL DEFAULT 'standard';
- ALTER TABLE so_shipment_lines ADD COLUMN cost_method_at_ship cost_method NOT NULL DEFAULT 'standard';
- Migration backfills existing rows from skus.cost_method (best effort — may be wrong for SKUs whose method already changed pre-snapshot).
- post_po_receipt populates cost_method_at_receipt at INSERT time.
- post_so_ship populates cost_method_at_ship at INSERT time.
- post_po_return reads cost_method_at_receipt (not skus.cost_method) for dispatch.
- post_customer_return reads cost_method_at_ship.

### Alternative: snapshot on the return line itself
Less correct — caller would have to specify the original method. The receipt/ship line knows definitively.

### Even-deeper alternative: snapshot the resolved unit_cost as well
`unit_cost` IS already snapshotted (so_shipment_lines.unit_cost, customer_return_lines.unit_cost). The PPV math, though, also needs the std-at-receipt-time. resolve_standard_cost_at(business_date) handles that correctly because std_cost is append-only in standard_costs — but only if the SKU was standard at original time. For SKUs that started as standard and went to WAC, resolve_standard_cost_at still returns a value (the most recent standard_costs entry), but we shouldn't use it.

## Acceptance criteria

- po_receipt_lines and so_shipment_lines gain cost_method_at_* columns.
- post_po_receipt / post_so_ship populate at INSERT.
- post_po_return / post_customer_return dispatch on the snapshotted method, NOT skus.cost_method.
- Tests: SKU changes cost_method between receipt/ship and return; return uses original method's math.
- Backfill migration for existing rows handles the audit-log gap reasonably.

## Priority justification

P3: Real concern but cost_method changes are rare in practice. Most companies pick a method per SKU at SKU-creation and keep it. The bug surfaces when cost-method conversion projects happen — those are typically planned events with caller-side discipline. Still worth fixing for correctness.

## Dependencies

- acct-ari (closed)
- acct-quk (closed)

## Out of scope

- Cost-method-conversion workflow itself (that's a separate feature — auto-recompute pool values when a SKU switches methods).
close_reason: Closed

title: Customer credit / vendor advance: handle returns after full payment without trip
description:
## Problem

Returns post a credit memo against ap (vendor side) or ar (customer side). Both ap and ar are NORMAL-direction balanced (ap credit-normal; ar debit-normal). When the vendor has been paid in full or the customer has paid in full, the relevant account is at 0 — and crediting/debiting it for the return pushes it across the constraint boundary.

### AP failure
- Receipt 10 @ $100 → ap_unsettled CR 1000
- Bill → ap CR 1000 (ap balance: -1000 stored as debits=0 credits=1000)
- Pay → cash CR 1000 / ap DR 1000 (ap balance: 0)
- Return 10 @ $100 → tries to ap DR 1000. Result: debits=2000, credits=1000 → debits > credits on credit-normal account → CHECK trip.

### AR failure mirror
- Ship 10 @ $100 + tax 15 → ar_unsettled DR 1015
- Invoice → ar DR 1000, ar_unsettled keeps tax 15
- Customer pays → cash DR 1000 / ar CR 1000 (ar balance: 0)
- Return 10 → tries to ar CR 1000. Result: debits=1000, credits=2000 → credits > debits on debit-normal → CHECK trip.

## Why mainstream ERPs solve this differently

Three patterns exist; pick one for our model:

### Pattern A: Allow ap / ar to go negative
Relax the CHECK constraint so debit-normal can have credits > debits and vice versa. Negative ap = vendor owes US (refund pending). Negative ar = we owe customer money. Simplest implementation.

**Cost**: loses balance integrity. A negative ap from the constraint's standpoint can hide a legitimate booking error elsewhere. SOX-style audit raises eyebrows.

### Pattern B: Separate credit-balance accounts
Introduce `vendor_credit_balance` (debit-normal — represents vendor owing us) and `customer_credit_balance` (credit-normal — represents us owing customer). When a return would push ap negative, route the overflow to vendor_credit_balance. Same on AR side.

**Cost**: more accounts, more bookkeeping. Subsequent invoices/bills/payments need to consult both balances.

### Pattern C: Refund as a distinct event
Returns post normally up to the point ap/ar would go negative; the residual posts to a `refund_payable` (AR side) or `refund_receivable` (AP side). The refund workflow then settles via a real cash transfer.

**Cost**: most accounting-standard but most code. Adds post_ap_refund / post_ar_refund symmetric to post_ap_payment / post_ar_payment but going the other direction (cash CR / ap DR... but that has the same problem if we get a refund check from a vendor with 0 balance — circular).

## Recommendation when this is taken up

Pattern B (separate credit-balance accounts) gets the cleanest balance-sheet representation. Pattern A is the simplest if balance integrity is acceptably degraded. Pattern C is academically purest but ships the most code.

## Acceptance criteria

- Decision: Pattern A vs B vs C, documented in CLAUDE.md.
- Implementation: post_po_return and post_customer_return route correctly when prior payment has drained ap/ar.
- Tests: 'return after full payment' on both sides, with the chosen pattern's invariants asserted.
- Refund workflow if Pattern C is chosen.

## Priority justification

P3: real-world important but rare in our current test surface. Customers/vendors who get refunds vs. credit-on-account is more of a business-policy choice; both are legitimate.

## Dependencies

- acct-XXX (state-aware routing) — that issue handles the pre-/post-clearance split. This issue handles the *fully-paid* case, which is downstream of that.

## Out of scope

- Refund actually clearing through a bank (that's just reuse of post_ap_payment / post_ar_payment in reverse direction).
design:
DESIGN COMMITMENT (2026-05-05, from ERP_RESEARCH.md):

Adopt Pattern B+C hybrid (separate credit-balance accounts + refund-as-distinct-event). Pattern A (allow ar/ap to go negative) is universally rejected by SAP S/4HANA, Oracle Cloud, D365 F&O, and NetSuite — all four use dedicated credit-balance accounts. Treating A as an open option contradicts industry consensus.

Schema:
- 4 new account_kind values: customer_credit_balance (credit-normal, partitioned by (counterparty_id, currency)), vendor_debit_balance (debit-normal, ditto), customer_deposit (advance receipts, credit-normal), vendor_advance (prepayments, debit-normal). Mirror existing per-counterparty per-currency partitioning.
- Extend mig 0086's split-routing to mig 0084 / 0085 / 0088: when a return / credit-memo would push ar below zero (or ap above), route the over-clearing portion to *_credit_balance / *_debit_balance. Add 4th destination column to *_return_lines.
- post_customer_refund(p_credit_balance_acct, p_amount, p_cash_acct, ...) posts cash CR / customer_credit_balance DR. Symmetric post_vendor_advance_refund.
- Customer deposits ride new post_customer_deposit analogous to post_ar_payment, debiting cash and crediting customer_deposit. Later invoice clears via new customer_invoice_lines.kind = 'deposit_apply'.

Industry mapping: SAP F-29/F-48 special G/L indicator A; D365 prepayment main-account-type; NetSuite Customer Deposit + Customer Refund; Oracle on-account credit memo + unapplied receipts.

Compliance anchors: ASC 606 (deposits aren't revenue until performance obligations met); IFRS 15 same; US state escheat for unapplied credits aging beyond threshold.

title: post_po_return / vendor return workflow (AP-side mirror of acct-ari)
description:
Inverse of post_po_receipt + post_ap_bill. Vendor return — we send goods back to a vendor, reversing the inflow chain. Mirrors customer_return (acct-ari, mig 0084) on the AP side.

The transfer reason 'po_return_to_vendor' is already in the enum since mig 0002, and there's a single conformance fixture (A1_po_return_to_vendor) covering the raw qty leg. What's missing:
- post_po_return document wrapper function
- po_returns + po_return_lines header tables (mirror customer_returns shape)
- Disposition handling — what condition is the goods in when returned to vendor? Two main flows:
  - 'damaged' / 'defective' — usually credited fully (vendor takes back)
  - 'overage' / 'shipping_error' — credited at original cost
  - 'rejected_quality' — vendor may dispute; needs an in-transit middle state
- Three-way credit-memo match: validate qty_returned <= cumulative_received - cumulative_returned per po_line (mirrors P0045 pattern).
- AP-side reversal: revenue/ar reversal isn't symmetric here. The original chain was:
  - post_po_receipt: inv_value_raw DR / ap_unsettled CR (qty + value)
  - post_ap_bill: ap_unsettled DR / ap CR
- Return reverses to: stock back to vendor, value out of inv_value_raw, and credit memo back from vendor against ap (or ap_unsettled if not yet billed).

CONSIDERATIONS for the implementer:
- Symmetric to acct-ari's tax routing nuance: where ship-side tax sits depends on ap_bill state. Mig 0035's post_ap_bill comment notes the equivalent for AP — confirm before shipping.
- 'in-transit' middle state (goods left our dock, not yet received by vendor) is a real physical reality. May warrant a stock_in_transit flow. Out of scope for MVP.
- Stock disposition on AP side is simpler than AR side — only 'returned' destination (we're shipping out, not receiving back). The 'restock / scrap / repair' choices on AR don't have an AP analog.

ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA:
- post_po_return function (vendor_id, lines, business_date, posted_by, idempotency_key, notes)
- po_returns + po_return_lines tables
- Cumulative-not-yet-returned check (P-code mirror of P0045)
- Tests for: full + partial returns, idempotency, three-way mismatch, validation gates
- Decide: credit memo against ap or ap_unsettled (parallel to acct-ari's revenue→ar / tax→ar_unsettled split)
close_reason: Mig 0085 + tests/po_return.rs (11 tests). AP-side mirror of acct-ari. Standard SKUs reverse PPV; WAC clean. Event order discovery: PPV-first then value to keep ap credit-normal accounts_check satisfied. New error codes P0046/P0047. 475/0/9 tests pass. Committed as afc1a30.

title: Three-way match tolerance windows
description: Slice A's strict match (P0024) and Slice C's strict match (P0040) both require exact equality on (qty, unit_cost / unit_price). Phase 2: add tolerance windows for small deltas (e.g., ±2% on unit_cost; ±1 unit on qty). Tolerance is configurable per-vendor / per-customer.

title: Sales tax computation integration
description:
## Problem

Slice C accepts caller-supplied `tax_amount` per line on `sales_order_lines` and `customer_invoice_lines`. `post_so_ship` posts the tax leg as `ar_unsettled DR / sales_tax_payable CR`; `post_customer_invoice` does the equivalent for service-line tax (so_match lines: tax stays parked in ar_unsettled per mig 0081 design — "ship-side tax is the source of truth"). Tax computation (jurisdictions, exemptions, nexus, ship-from / ship-to nexus rules, product-category taxability, exempt customer certificates) is left entirely to the caller.

Phase 2 work: design how an integration point — external tax engine, internal rules table, or hybrid — would slot in WITHOUT breaking the caller-supplied path.

## Three integration patterns to evaluate

### Pattern A: Pure external engine (Avalara / TaxJar / Vertex / Sovos)

- Add a hook `_compute_sales_tax(p_customer_id, p_ship_from_loc, p_ship_to_loc, p_lines)` that calls out to an HTTP API.
- Return a tax_amount per line (and possibly a jurisdiction breakdown for compliance reporting).
- post_so_ship / post_customer_invoice consult the hook when caller passes `tax_amount = NULL` or `'auto'` sentinel; explicit numeric still wins.

Pros: best-in-class accuracy, regulatory updates handled externally.
Cons: external dependency, latency, vendor lock-in, requires committing to one vendor.

### Pattern B: Internal rules table

- New tables: `tax_jurisdictions(id, code, name, parent_id)`, `tax_rates(id, jurisdiction_id, rate_pct, effective_at, obsolete_at)`, `tax_taxability(sku_id?, sku_category?, jurisdiction_id, taxable BOOLEAN)`.
- A function `_compute_sales_tax(...)` walks the rule table.
- Caller policy: ship-to determines jurisdiction; sku × jurisdiction determines taxability.

Pros: no external dependency, deterministic, auditable.
Cons: regulatory upkeep is on us (rates change quarterly in many jurisdictions), no real-world coverage of nexus / exemption certificates / situs rules.

### Pattern C: Hybrid (rules table + external override)

- Internal rules table for common cases (single-jurisdiction operators, simple SKU taxability).
- Optional plug-in for external engine when configured (`tax_engine_url`, `tax_engine_api_key` on tenant config).
- Fallback chain: external if configured → internal rules → caller-supplied → 0.

Pros: flexible, good migration story (start internal, upgrade to external).
Cons: more surface area; two code paths to test.

## Acceptance criteria

- Pattern decision documented (the design conversation gates this issue).
- Integration point implemented; caller-supplied path unchanged (regression-locked by existing tests).
- Tests covering: caller-supplied path still works (no regression); integration path computes correctly for at least one example jurisdiction (e.g., a single US sales-tax rate); fallback semantics when integration unavailable / returns error.
- New error code(s) for tax-engine failures (e.g., P0050 tax_engine_unavailable, P0051 tax_engine_invalid_response).

## Open design questions

1. Where does jurisdiction live? `customers.default_ship_to_jurisdiction_id`, or computed per-shipment from `sales_order_lines.ship_location_id` → `locations.jurisdiction_id`?
2. Multi-jurisdiction tax (state + county + city + special district) — flatten to one tax_amount per line, or break out per jurisdiction for compliance reporting?
3. Tax-on-tax (some jurisdictions tax shipping which is itself taxed) — Phase 3 problem?
4. Exemption certificates (B2B sales to tax-exempt customers) — `customers.tax_exempt_at` + cert_id?
5. Use-tax accrual on AP side (own-state purchases from out-of-state vendors with no sales tax) — separate Phase 2 issue or fold here?

## Dependencies

- Slice C shipped (acct-th7, closed).
- acct-3dz2 (home-currency reporting) for cross-currency tax reporting — independent for now.
- The actual engine vendor selection is a business decision, not engineering.

## Out of scope

- VAT / GST mechanics (different model — input/output VAT netting); separate Phase 2 effort.
- Withholding tax on AP side (different again).
- 1099 reporting on AP service bills (US-specific compliance).

## Why this is P3

Real concern for any operator with multi-jurisdiction sales but not blocking core ledger work. Caller-supplied path is functional; this is about removing the "compute it yourself" burden from operators.

## Reference

Original deferral note: Slice C plan acct-th7 documented "tax integration is Phase 2 — caller passes tax_amount per line; ar_unsettled / sales_tax_payable accounts ship in seed".

## Recovery hints (for post-compaction context)

- Slice C ship-tax flow: see mig 0081 `post_so_ship` Event 4 (ar_unsettled DR / sales_tax_payable CR when tax_amount > 0).
- so_match invoice tax: see mig 0081 design note "tax stays parked in ar_unsettled" — invoice does NOT migrate tax for so_match lines; only service lines re-post tax.
- Customer return tax handling: mig 0084/0086 routes tax reversal to ar_unsettled.
- sales_tax_payable accounts: seed.sql line 94-95 (USD + EUR un-partitioned, credit-normal).
design:
DESIGN COMMITMENT (2026-05-05, from ERP_RESEARCH.md):

Adopt hybrid (internal rules table + external plug-in contract). Pure-internal and pure-external are both rejected by every mainstream ERP — SAP, Oracle, D365, and NetSuite all ship native engines AND certified Vertex/Avalara/ONESOURCE connectors. Hybrid wins on day-one + long-tail rate maintenance both.

MVP scope (internal rules):
- tax_jurisdictions(id, code, name, parent_id, country, state, local).
- tax_codes(jurisdiction_id, sku_taxability_class, rate, effective_at, obsolete_at).
- compute_tax(p_sku, p_ship_to, p_ship_from, p_amount, p_business_date) helper.
- Call from post_so_ship to validate caller-supplied tax against computed (strict equality first; tolerance window later via vendor_unit_cost_tolerance_pct pattern from mig 0090).
- Partition sales_tax_payable by (jurisdiction_id, currency) once jurisdictions exist (mirrors per-counterparty AP partitioning, mig 0086 split-routing precedent).

Plug-in scope (external engine):
- SQL contract: compute_tax_external(jsonb_request) RETURNS jsonb_response.
- Application layer routes to Avalara / Vertex / ONESOURCE via Rust crate.
- Postgres side stamps the returned amount as authoritative.
- skus.tax_engine_override TEXT NULL: 'auto' = use external when configured; numeric or NULL = caller-supplied wins.

Compliance follow-ups (file as separate issues if/when triggered):
- Post-Wayfair nexus determination
- EU VAT MOSS / IOSS
- E-invoicing mandates (Italy SDI, India IRP, Mexico CFDI, Brazil NFe)
- SAF-T compliance
- Withholding tax (NetSuite SuiteTax pattern)

Industry mapping: SAP TAXIN + Vertex/Avalara via SAP CPI + External Sales and Use Tax Calculation framework; Oracle EBT (E-Business Tax) / Cloud Tax + ONESOURCE/Avalara/Vertex; D365 Tax codes/groups + Tax Calculation Service hub; NetSuite SuiteTax + Avalara connector for complex US multi-state.
acceptance_criteria: Vendor / mechanism design decision (open). Integration point that does NOT break the caller-supplied path. Tests covering: caller-supplied path still works (no regression); integration path computes correctly for at least one example jurisdiction; fallback semantics when integration unavailable.

title: post_customer_return / credit memo workflow
description: Inverse of post_so_ship + post_customer_invoice. Customer returns goods; we issue credit memo (reverse ar). Reverses qty (back to stock_quarantine or stock_available depending on disposition), reverses revenue + cogs. Multiple disposition modes: restock, scrap, repair.

title: acct-du2 Phase 3 follow-up: tests/property_period_close.rs

title: DOCS: _post_transfers_lookup_qty_account should warn callers about per-class divisor hazard
description:
Surfaced by Phase 2 of acct-du2 audit. mig 0021 _post_transfers_lookup_qty_account returns stock_available for both inv_value_raw and inv_value_fg lookups (because they share the same qty pool). The helper itself is correct — it returns the matching qty account for a value account.

However, every per-class qty divisor bug (acct-fii / acct-du2.8 / acct-du2.11) traces back to callers using the returned account's debits_total - credits_total as their divisor. That balance is CROSS-CLASS for raw + fg same-location SKUs.

The COMMENT ON FUNCTION at line 82-83 is currently 'Maps a value-side account to its matching qty-side account. Returns NULL if no clean match.' — silent on the divisor hazard.

Fix: extend the helper's comment to explicitly warn 'Callers must use per-class signed SUM on transfers.qty filtered to the value account, NOT the returned qty account's balance, when computing per-class divisors. The returned stock_available pool is shared between inv_value_raw and inv_value_fg.'

No code change. Pure documentation.

title: AP3: post_standard_cost_roll reads stock_available qty without FOR UPDATE on it
description:
Surfaced by Phase 2 of acct-du2 audit. mig 0028 post_standard_cost_roll line 260 takes FOR UPDATE on inv_value_raw + inv_value_fg pools for the SKU, but stock_available is NOT in the lock set. Line 281 then reads stock_available qty as the revaluation divisor. Concurrent post_po_receipt / post_inventory_adjustment can mutate stock_available between the inv_value_* lock acquisition and the qty read, skewing v_delta.

Bundles with acct-du2.11 — fixing AP1 (per-class qty divisor) likely also moves the qty source off stock_available, sidestepping AP3. Filed separately for completeness.

Fix: extend the FOR UPDATE at line 260 to include the matching stock_available accounts.

title: AP3: post_po_receipt / post_ap_bill cumulative-qty check not under FOR UPDATE on po_line
description:
Surfaced by Phase 2 of acct-du2 audit. mig 0036 post_po_receipt line 163: 'SELECT COALESCE(SUM(qty_received), 0) FROM po_receipt_lines WHERE po_line_id = ...' reads cumulative-qty WITHOUT a preceding FOR UPDATE on the parent purchase_order_lines row. Concurrent receipts on the same po_line both pass the over-receipt gate (P0023) and both INSERT — qty_ordered breached.

Same shape in post_ap_bill (mig 0035) — cumulative read on vendor_bill_lines + po_receipt_lines for the strict three-way-match gate (P0024) is not under FOR UPDATE on po_line.

P3 because: (a) two concurrent receipts on the same po_line is uncommon in practice, (b) the actual transfers do go through post_transfers's lock-pre-scan so balances stay consistent — the breach is at the document-validation layer, not the ledger.

Fix: 'PERFORM 1 FROM purchase_order_lines WHERE id = v_po_line_id FOR UPDATE;' before the cumulative-qty read. Apply to both functions.

Test: two concurrent post_po_receipt with cumulative-qty crossing the qty_ordered boundary; assert exactly one succeeds.
close_reason: Closed

title: AP3: post_op_move wac_* branch reads stock_wip qty without FOR UPDATE
description: Surfaced by Phase 2 of acct-du2 audit. mig 0070 line 419 takes FOR UPDATE on v_val_from (inv_value_wip), line 420 reads v_pool_value, line 422 reads v_pool_qty from stock_wip(parent, from_op). Same shape as acct-du2.6 — value pool locked, qty pool unprotected. Concurrent post_osp_ship / post_osp_receive can mutate stock_wip between the two reads. Result: inconsistent value/qty pair, mis-priced unit cost. Fix: extend FOR UPDATE at line 419 to cover (v_val_from, v_qty_from) via 'WHERE id IN (...) ORDER BY id FOR UPDATE'. Same lock-extension is the right fix for acct-du2.6.
close_reason: Closed

title: AP3: post_wo_complete wac_* branch reads stock_wip qty without FOR UPDATE
description: Surfaced by Phase 2 of acct-du2 audit. mig 0068 line 178 takes FOR UPDATE on v_val_from (inv_value_wip), then line 179 reads v_pool_at_last (value), line 181 reads v_pool_qty from stock_wip(parent, last_op). The FOR UPDATE protects v_val_from only — v_qty_from is unprotected. Concurrent post_osp_ship / post_osp_receive (mig 0057) lock stock_wip without locking inv_value_wip, so they CAN commit stock_wip mutations between line 179 and line 181. Result: v_pool_at_last reflects pre-osp state, v_pool_qty reflects post-osp state — unit cost mis-priced. P3 because today only OSP touches stock_wip without inv_value_wip; op_move / scrap / wo_complete itself locks v_val_from. Fix: extend the FOR UPDATE at line 178 to cover (v_val_from, v_qty_from) IN-clause.
close_reason: Closed

title: AP8: post_op_move / post_scrap missing dual idempotency replay check (consistency)
description: Surfaced by Phase 1 of acct-du2 audit. post_op_move (mig 0070 lines 316-318) and post_scrap (mig 0038 lines 850-852) have only the pre-FOR UPDATE replay check on wo_events.idempotency_key. Race defense relies on the INSERT INTO wo_events ... ON CONFLICT (idempotency_key) DO NOTHING RETURNING id at the end of the function. SAFE — no side effects between pool read and INSERT, and NULL-RETURNING bails out correctly — but wasteful under contention (T2 does pool reads and amount computation that get discarded) and inconsistent with sister functions post_wo_start (mig 0070), post_wo_complete (mig 0068), post_wo_close_unproduced (mig 0056) which use the acct-69p dual-check pattern. Fix: add 'SELECT id INTO v_existing_id FROM wo_events WHERE idempotency_key = p_idempotency_key; IF v_existing_id IS NOT NULL THEN RETURN p_wo_id; END IF;' immediately after each function's SELECT * INTO v_wo FROM work_orders ... FOR UPDATE.
close_reason: Closed

title: AP2: _post_transfers_compute_amount uses debit-first COALESCE (consistency)
description: Surfaced by Phase 1 of acct-du2 audit. mig 0031 lines 85, 310, 389, 422 set v_cost_sku := COALESCE(p_d_acct.sku_id, p_c_acct.sku_id). Functionally equivalent today because every cost-event reason has at most one SKU-bearing leg, but drift risk: any future cost reason putting SKUs on both legs would silently pick the wrong side. The flagging path was migrated to credit-first by acct-7py (mig 0067, _post_transfers_apply_event line 528). Leaving the dispatcher debit-first is inconsistent. Fix: switch to COALESCE(p_c_acct.sku_id, p_d_acct.sku_id) and add a one-line comment citing acct-7py. Test: T5 conformance case A18_credit_first_sku_resolution (planned for Phase 4 of acct-du2).
close_reason: Closed

title: rm_issue_to_wo with mixed parent/component cost methods
description:
Follow-up to acct-7py. Tier 2 only handles wac_periodic component WHEN parent is also wac_periodic (homogeneous case). Mixed cases need additional variance routing because the destination WIP pool's residual handling depends on parent cost_method:

* standard parent + wac_periodic component: WIP drained to 0 by wo_close_v (deterministic). The wac_periodic close adjustment for rm_issue cannot 2-leg-wash through WIP (would leave residual). Need single-leg between variance_wac_period and raw_src, or 2-leg via variance_wo_close.

* wac_perpetual parent + wac_periodic component: WIP runs at WIP-pool running avg, drained by wo_complete_v. Similar issue — wac_perpetual is not flagged into transfers_provisional, so retroactive corrections cannot flow through cache.

Tier 2 raises P0026 with deferral marker on these. Follow-up should design variance routing for mixed cases. Likely needs distinct variance accounts (variance_material or similar) and per-parent-cost_method dispatch in close hook.
close_reason: Mig 0077 lifts the two P0026 gates in _wo_emit_bom_lines (wac_periodic and wac_retroactive components on non-matching parents). Close hooks detect mixed shape (destination SKU cost_method != hook method) and post single-leg variance through new variance_material_mixed P&L account against the component pool. Destination WIP untouched per R5. 5 P0026-asserting tests replaced with positive-path mixed-case regression tests. 382/0/9 tests pass, ci-check clean.

title: post_wo_complete pre-balance over-absorbs pool@last_op when other WOs share the pool
description:
post_wo_complete's pre-balance step (mig 0061, acct-6jq) computes v_prebalance = v_total_drain - pool@last_op_balance. For interleaved multi-WO scenarios where two or more WOs share parent_sku × routing_op (and thus inv_value_wip pool), the closing WO's pre-balance treats the OTHER WOs' WIP balance as if it were this WO's residual to sweep into variance_wo_close. This drains other-WO WIP prematurely. Affects standard / wac_perpetual / wac_periodic equally — pre-existing pre-balance design limitation, not introduced by tier 2.

Reproduction: 2 WOs same parent SKU, 2-op routing. wo_start both → pool@op10=$400 qty=20. op_move both → pool@op20=$400 qty=20. WO1 wo_complete (v_will_close TRUE): v_total_drain = 10 × $20 = $200; v_pool_at_last = $400; v_prebalance = -$200. Pre-balance posts dr variance_wo_close / cr op20 $200, draining WO2's portion. WO2 wo_complete then sees pool=0 → drains $0 to FG. WO1's FG gets $200, WO2's FG gets $0 — wrong.

Fix direction: gate pre-balance and residual sweep on "this WO holds all remaining WIP qty in the pool". Compare v_pool_qty (post-this-WO drain) against expected residual qty (qty_target - qty_completed - qty_scrapped from THIS WO across all routing_ops). Skip pre-balance + residual sweep when other WOs are using the same pool (stock_wip qty > this WO's contribution).

Test placeholder: prototyped interleaved multi-WO test in tests/wac_periodic_wip_multiop.rs and removed; left a comment block referencing this issue. Sequential multi-WO same-pool is covered by wac_periodic_two_op_drift_propagates_to_leaf and wac_periodic_three_op_drift_propagates.
acceptance_criteria: Interleaved multi-WO same-parent same-pool close produces correct per-WO FG drain; no premature absorption of other WOs' WIP into variance_wo_close. Tests in wac_periodic_wip_multiop.rs (interleaved variant) and wo_lifecycle.rs covering standard + wac_perpetual interleaved.
close_reason: Migration 0068 gates post_wo_complete's pre-balance and per-op residual sweep on solo-at-pool: stock_wip(parent, op) qty must equal p_qty before drain (== 0 after) to fire pre-balance / sweep. When multiple WOs share parent_sku × routing_op, the pool's qty exceeds this WO's contribution; gate skips, deferring truncation absorption to the LAST sharing WO's close. Per-WO close-variance attribution is approximate under shared pools (last WO carries cumulative residue) but pool-value integrity is preserved. 6 new tests in tests/wo_complete_interleaved_pool.rs cover standard / wac_perpetual / wac_periodic interleaved 2-WO, 3-WO interleaved, sequential same-pool baseline (gate non-restrictive), and explicit gate regression demonstration. 352/0/9 tests pass; ci-check digest cd46d624...

title: Tier 3: multi-op wac_retroactive across WIP pools (chronological replay + topological order)
description:
TIER 3 of acct-8in. wac_retroactive on WIP — single-op AND multi-op (the prior tier-1/tier-3 split moved single-op here too because wac_retroactive's per-event chronological replay reads transfers.qty from value-pool events; for inv_value_wip rm_issue_to_wo carries component qty, breaking final_avg).

DESIGN:
- Refactor wac_retroactive_close_hook's per-event replay to merge events from BOTH the value pool AND the matching qty-side account (stock_wip for inv_value_wip pools), sorted chronologically by (business_date, posted_at, id). For a value-pool event on inv_value_wip, the running pool_qty update should come from the paired stock_wip qty-leg, not from the value-leg's transfers.qty (which is component qty).
- Apply the same single-leg variance posting pattern from acct-bol (tier 1) when the source pool is inv_value_wip — the WIP pool is drained at WO close, so the wash-through-pool routing trips debit-normal CHECK on multi-WO drift.
- For multi-op routings on wac_retroactive: same topological dependency as tier 2 (acct-smn) but with per-event chronological replay; downstream pool's op_move debit needs upstream pool's already-replayed running avg.

Currently post_wo_start raises P0026 for ALL wac_retroactive parents (acct-bol mig 0064). This issue lifts that gate.

DEPENDS: acct-bol (tier 1 — establishes the BOM2 *_v flagging + single-leg WIP variance pattern), acct-smn (tier 2 — establishes the topological per-pool walk).
acceptance_criteria: Multi-op wac_retroactive WO lifecycle works; pools replayed chronologically respecting topological order; tests parallel tier 2's coverage.
close_reason: Tier 3 of acct-8in / acct-rgb shipped. Migration 0070: lifts wac_retroactive parent gate in post_wo_start, extends post_op_move's wac branch to include wac_retroactive, lifts wac_retroactive component gate in _wo_emit_bom_lines, refactors wac_retroactive_close_hook with topological per-pool walk + per-event chronological replay merging value-leg events on value pool with qty-leg events on paired stock_wip account into one stream sorted by (business_date, doc_chrono, document_id, sub_priority, id) where doc_chrono = MIN(posted_at) OVER (PARTITION BY document_id) anchors each wo_event chronologically and sub_priority orders qty-inflow BEFORE value BEFORE qty-outflow. Upstream variance via LEFT JOIN cache (variance_transfer_id IS NULL filter). Internal-chain reasons (op_move_v, rm_issue_to_wo) record variance only; leaf inv_value_wip depletions single-leg post; raw/fg 2-leg wash. Mixed cost methods raise P0026 (acct-7eo deferral). Rework P0036. tests/wac_retroactive_wip.rs: 9 tests (single-op clean, two-op clean, three-op clean, mixed standard/wac_perpetual parent + wac_retroactive component → P0026, rework cycle → P0036, wac_retroactive component clean, chronological-replay late-receipt drift, two-WO shared pool). 376/0/9 tests pass; ci-check digest 616e7414ec389f417fe18b14ed93266b3ef7bda222f8938c3769c19d9554a2e0. Closes acct-8in (umbrella), acct-rgb (umbrella). Unblocks acct-du2.

title: Tier 2: multi-op wac_periodic across WIP pools (recursive cost-chain via topological recompute)
description:
The recursive cost-chain piece. inv_value_wip(parent, op_N) gets debited by op_move(N-1→N) whose AMOUNT was set provisionally at upstream pool's running avg at time-of-move. After upstream's final avg is known at close, downstream receipts must be re-amounted; downstream final avg therefore depends on upstream final avg.

ALGORITHM (extension to wac_periodic_close_hook):
1. Collect pools: SELECT DISTINCT pool from transfers_provisional rows in this period.
2. Build the dependency DAG: for each inv_value_wip pool P, op_move debits to P in-period; the credit-side pool is P's predecessor. Edges: predecessor → P.
3. Topological sort.
4. Walk in order: for pool P, recompute receipts (op_move debits at predecessor.final_avg × t.qty); final_avg(P) = Σ(recomputed value) / Σ(qty). For each provisional depletion FROM P: variance = (final_avg − provisional_unit_cost) × qty. Post via variance_wac_period.

REWORK LOOPS: op_move(N→M) with M<N creates cycle. Detect via Tarjan SCC; raise explicit error (P0036?) and file acct-p7v-rework follow-up. Iterative-fixed-point (option 2) handling deferred.

DEPENDS: acct-bol (tier 1).
acceptance_criteria: Multi-op wac_periodic WO lifecycle: rm_issue → op_move → op_move → wo_complete; close hook walks pools in routing_op order; variances post correctly; rework loops raise explicit error. Tests cover 2-op + 3-op multi-pool chains, multi-WO interleaving same period.
close_reason: Closed

title: WAC periodic + retroactive close hooks across WIP pools: topological per-pool recompute
description:
Sub-issue of acct-p7v. Picks up where acct-wig leaves off: extend wac_periodic_close_hook + wac_retroactive_close_hook to handle inv_value_wip source pools.

DESIGN DECISION (per p7v option analysis): TOPOLOGICAL PER-POOL RECOMPUTE.
- Order pools by routing dependency: inv_value_wip(op_min) before inv_value_wip(op_min+1) ... before inv_value_fg.
- For each pool in order, recompute final avg = Σ(in-period receipts value at recomputed amounts) / Σ(in-period receipts qty). 'Receipts' = debits to the pool (op_move IN from upstream, rm_issue at op1, bom_lines fires).
- Once a pool's final avg is fixed, its outflow events (op_move credits) are re-amounted; downstream pool's receipts pick up the corrected amount.
- Variance at each pool routes through variance_wac_period (periodic) or the wac_retro variance account (retroactive).

Why topological over global event replay (option 3): the routing graph is a DAG in normal flow. Op_move(N→M) where M>N respects topology; rework (M<N within a WO) creates a cycle. For now, raise an explicit error (P0036?) if a wac_periodic/retroactive WO has rework events in-period — defer rework-period correctness as known limitation (acct-p7v-rework follow-up).

ACCEPTANCE:
- Migration extends both close hooks; lifts P0006-on-WIP guards in dispatcher (where applicable).
- Topological pool walk implemented (order by routing_op for stock_wip class; fg_loc for stock_available class).
- Tests: wac_periodic on WIP — single-WO lifecycle in one period, variance posts at close. Multi-WO interleaving same period. Receipts-only (no consumption) is no-op. Empty-pool guard preserved.
- Same coverage on wac_retroactive.
- Rework loops in-period: explicit error and follow-up filed.

DEPENDS ON: acct-wig (wac_perpetual on WIP — lifts gate + dispatch pattern that close hooks reuse).
design:
DESIGN — TOPOLOGICAL PER-POOL RECOMPUTE.

Decomposes into 3 tiers. Tier 1 ships the simplest case standalone; tier 2 adds the recursive cost-chain piece; tier 3 mirrors tier 2 for wac_retroactive.

== TIER 1 — single-routing-op WAC parents (wac_periodic + wac_retroactive)

WO with one routing op has no upstream WIP. All inv_value_wip(parent, op) receipts come from leaf sources: rm_issue_to_wo (component pool), labor_apply / oh_apply / burden_apply / lot_charge_apply (applied-account pools). No op_move debits to this pool. So the existing wac_periodic_close_hook per-pool walk works as-is once the surrounding plumbing is in place.

CHANGES:
  1. post_wo_start accepts wac_periodic + wac_retroactive (lift the P0026 gate from acct-wig/0063).
  2. post_op_move + post_wo_complete extend the cost_method dispatch added in 0063: wac_periodic and wac_retroactive read source-pool running avg same as wac_perpetual (mid-period running avg = provisional unit cost; close-hook variance posts later).
  3. transfers_provisional flagging condition (in _post_transfers_apply_event) extends to include op_move_v / wo_complete_v / scrap_v reasons. Currently checks only canonical ('op_move','scrap','wo_complete','so_ship'); BOM2 entry points use the *_v variants which bypass the dispatcher but still need flagging for the close hook to find them.
  4. Tests: WO with single routing op, parent=wac_periodic; rm_issue + wo_complete; pool depletion flagged; close hook recomputes avg, posts variance via variance_wac_period. Same for wac_retroactive (the wac_retroactive_close_hook already does chronological replay per pool — just needs to walk WIP pools too).

ACCEPTANCE: tier1 single-op WO lifecycle works on both wac_periodic and wac_retroactive parents. Multi-op WO still raises P0026 (multi-op = tier2).

== TIER 2 — multi-routing-op WAC parents (wac_periodic)

The recursive cost-chain piece. inv_value_wip(parent, op20) gets debited by op_move(10→20) whose AMOUNT was set provisionally at inv_value_wip(parent, op10)'s running avg at the time of the move. After op10's final avg is known at close, op20's receipts must be re-amounted, which changes op20's final avg, which changes wo_complete drain amount, etc.

ALGORITHM (close-hook extension):
  1. Collect pools: SELECT DISTINCT pool from transfers_provisional rows in this period.
  2. Build the dependency DAG: for each inv_value_wip pool P, find op_move debits to P in-period; the credit-side pool is P's predecessor. Edges: predecessor → P.
  3. Topological sort.
  4. Walk in order:
     - For pool P, recompute its receipts:
       - For non-op_move debits (leaf receipts: rm_issue_to_wo, labor_apply, etc.): use original transfer amount.
       - For op_move debits: use predecessor's already-finalized avg × t.qty as the recomputed amount. Post a 'cost_restate' event for the delta.
     - final_avg(P) = Σ(recomputed receipts value) / Σ(receipts qty).
     - For each provisional depletion FROM P (transfers_provisional rows where this pool is the source):
       - variance = (final_avg − provisional_unit_cost) × qty
       - Post 'cost_restate' event routing through variance_wac_period.
     - Mark P's provisional rows finalized.

REWORK LOOPS: an op_move(20→10) creates a cycle in the DAG. If detected (Tarjan's SCC), raise an explicit error (P0036?) suggesting acct-p7v-rework follow-up. Tractable algorithm with cycles = iterative fixed-point (option 2 from p7v's candidate list); deferred.

== TIER 3 — wac_retroactive multi-op

wac_retroactive_close_hook does chronological replay per (sku, location, currency) pool. For WIP pools, replay is per (sku, routing_op, currency), and the topological dependency between pools must be respected: when replaying op20's receipts, op_move(10→20) entries must use op10's already-replayed running avg as the in-cost. Same topological framework as tier 2; difference is that within a pool, wac_retroactive replays event-by-event (running avg evolves through the period) rather than wac_periodic's single-final-avg.

== EDGE CASES

- Multi-WO same period: each WO contributes events to the same pools (e.g. two WOs producing the same parent through different ops). Topological walk is per-pool, not per-WO; multi-WO is naturally handled.
- Negative receipts on a pool (e.g. inventory adjustment OUT before any IN): tier 1 inherits the existing P0020 wac_periodic_close_no_receipts guard.
- Empty pool at op_move time: post_op_move(0063) writes value_amount=0 in this case. Tier 2's recompute sees a 0-amount op_move; receipts_qty stays 0 if there's no other inflow; close hook should skip pools with qty_in=0 (or P0020 if depletions exist).
- Co-products via wo_outputs: each output debits its own inv_value_fg pool via wo_complete_v. The credit side is inv_value_wip(parent, last_op). All depletions are FROM that single WIP pool, with allocation already encoded in caller-supplied amounts. final_avg(last_op) recompute applies uniformly.

== COMPLEXITY ESTIMATE

  Tier 1: ~100 lines plpgsql + 4-6 tests. ~1-2 hours.
  Tier 2: ~200 lines plpgsql + 6-8 tests. Multiple hours.
  Tier 3: ~150 lines (mostly mirrors tier 2 in wac_retroactive_close_hook) + 4-6 tests.

Suggest filing tier 1 / tier 2 / tier 3 as sub-issues of acct-8in and shipping incrementally. Alternative: tier 1 alone closes the SIMPLEST case (single-op WAC parent) which may be enough for Slice C's WAC needs.
acceptance_criteria: Both close hooks extended; topological walk implemented; rework-in-period raises explicit error; tests cover wac_periodic + wac_retroactive WO lifecycles single + multi-WO; existing tests still green.
notes: Tier 1 (acct-bol, mig 0064) and Tier 2 (acct-smn, mig 0065) shipped. wac_periodic on WIP supported end-to-end (single-op + multi-op via topological per-pool recompute; rework cycles raise P0036). Remaining: Tier 3 (acct-rso) for wac_retroactive WIP — chronological replay refactor needed because rm_issue_to_wo's transfers.qty carries component qty (qty_per_parent × p_qty), not parent qty.
close_reason: All three tiers shipped: tier 1 wac_periodic single-op (acct-bol mig 0064); tier 2 wac_periodic multi-op (acct-smn mig 0065); tier 3 wac_retroactive (acct-rso mig 0070). Topological per-pool recompute via Kahn's algorithm + LEFT JOIN cache for upstream variance propagation works for both wac_periodic (final_avg per pool) and wac_retroactive (per-event chronological replay with merged value/qty stream). Rework cycles raise P0036.

title: By-products: NRV credit-back / negligible / disposal-cost treatments (Phase 2)
description:
# By-products: comprehensive industry-standard implementation

## Why this exists

The BOM2 refactor (acct-jg2) introduced `wo_outputs` for **co-products** — multiple SKUs that share joint production cost, allocated by `allocation_pct` summing to 100%. This is correct for co-products (joint production, equal-footing outputs) but does NOT model **by-products** — incidental side outputs of producing a parent. By-products have three distinct accounting treatments depending on their economics, and none of the current `wo_outputs` shape supports them cleanly.

Mainstream-ERP convention requires: BOM-side declaration with WO-snapshot at start, three accounting treatments, GRNI-style accrual liability bridge to AP, planned-vs-actual yield variance, and tolerance-windowed three-way match against the disposal-vendor bill. The 2026-05-06 design walk-through with the project owner confirmed: half-baked is not acceptable; match SAP / Oracle / D365 / NetSuite at minimum.

## Industry research (synthesis 2026-05-06)

- **SAP** (movement type 531): negative-qty BOM lines trigger auto-receipt of by-product to unrestricted stock at production confirmation. Linked to production order.
- **ASC 330 / IAS 2**: NRV = selling price minus costs of completion, **disposal**, and transportation. ASC permanent write-downs; IAS reversible.
- **Oracle / D365 / NetSuite**: by-product yield variance compares actual vs cost-formula-scaled planned, posted as Assembly Variance with recognized categories (including output mix).
- **ASC 450 / 410-30** (environmental obligations): disposal cost accrual required at obligation-incurrence (= production); bill-time adjustments recognized in the same P&L line.

## Treatment matrix

| Treatment | Trigger | wo_complete entry (value side) | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| `nrv_credit` | by-product has positive market value | `inv_value_fg(by_product) DR / inv_value_wip(parent, last_op) CR` | Drains parent WIP value by NRV; co-products absorb less |
| `negligible` | by-product worth ~zero | (qty leg only — qty from creation_void; no value leg) | Main carries full cost |
| `disposal_cost`, **inventoriable** | by-product has negative value, treat as part of product cost | `inv_value_fg(co_product) DR / accrued_disposal_liability(vendor) CR` per allocation_pct | Inflates co-product COGS basis; bridge liability to AP |
| `disposal_cost`, **period** | by-product has negative value, treat as period overhead | `disposal_expense DR / accrued_disposal_liability(vendor) CR` | Recognized at production; doesn't touch product cost |

Qty side in all four cases: `stock_available(by_product) DR / creation_void(qty) CR`, amount = qty (by-product qty appears from accounting void; not conserved against parent qty pool because of unit mismatch — by-product SKU has different physical units than parent).

## Schema additions

### `bom_by_products` (BOM-side recipe declaration)

```sql
CREATE TABLE bom_by_products (
  bom_id            BIGINT NOT NULL REFERENCES bom_headers(id) ON DELETE CASCADE,
  by_product_no     INT  NOT NULL,
  output_sku_id     UUID NOT NULL REFERENCES skus(id),
  fg_location_id    UUID NOT NULL REFERENCES locations(id),
  qty_per_parent    NUMERIC(18,6) NOT NULL CHECK (qty_per_parent > 0),
  unit_value        BIGINT NOT NULL,
  treatment         TEXT NOT NULL CHECK (treatment IN
    ('nrv_credit', 'negligible', 'disposal_cost')),
  disposal_basis    TEXT CHECK (disposal_basis IN ('inventoriable', 'period')),
  disposal_vendor_id UUID REFERENCES vendors(id),
  disposal_expense_account_kind account_kind,
  PRIMARY KEY (bom_id, by_product_no),
  CHECK (
    (treatment = 'nrv_credit'    AND unit_value > 0
     AND disposal_basis IS NULL AND disposal_vendor_id IS NULL
     AND disposal_expense_account_kind IS NULL) OR
    (treatment = 'negligible'    AND unit_value = 0
     AND disposal_basis IS NULL AND disposal_vendor_id IS NULL
     AND disposal_expense_account_kind IS NULL) OR
    (treatment = 'disposal_cost' AND unit_value < 0
     AND disposal_basis IS NOT NULL AND disposal_vendor_id IS NOT NULL
     AND (disposal_basis = 'period' OR disposal_expense_account_kind IS NULL))
  )
);
```

Inherits revision/ECO lifecycle from `bom_headers` via FK. Phantom expansion not relevant (by-products attach to the parent's primary BOM, not phantoms).

### `wo_by_products` (per-WO snapshot)

```sql
CREATE TABLE wo_by_products (
  wo_id              UUID NOT NULL REFERENCES work_orders(id) ON DELETE CASCADE,
  by_product_no      INT  NOT NULL,
  output_sku_id      UUID NOT NULL REFERENCES skus(id),
  fg_location_id     UUID NOT NULL REFERENCES locations(id),
  planned_qty        BIGINT NOT NULL CHECK (planned_qty > 0),
  actual_qty         BIGINT NOT NULL CHECK (actual_qty >= 0),
  unit_value         BIGINT NOT NULL,
  treatment          TEXT NOT NULL CHECK (...),
  disposal_basis     TEXT CHECK (disposal_basis IN ('inventoriable', 'period')),
  disposal_vendor_id UUID REFERENCES vendors(id),
  disposal_expense_account_kind account_kind,
  PRIMARY KEY (wo_id, by_product_no),
  CHECK (...)
);
```

`planned_qty` set at wo_start (snapshot from `bom_by_products.qty_per_parent × wo.qty_target`); `actual_qty` defaults to planned but caller can UPDATE before wo_complete to assert what was actually produced. Yield variance is computed at wo_complete from the difference.

### New account_kinds

- `accrued_disposal_liability` — credit-normal, vendor-partitioned (counterparty_id), currency-aware. Bridges wo_complete to AP bill (mirror of `ap_unsettled` for GRNI).
- `disposal_expense` — debit-normal, currency-aware. Generic disposal expense; callers can also route to other expense kinds.
- `variance_yield_byproduct` — unrestricted normal_side, currency-aware. Captures planned-vs-actual qty variance at wo_complete.

### Bill line kind extension

`vendor_bill_lines.kind` extended to include `disposal_match` (currently `po_match` / `service`). Drains `accrued_disposal_liability(vendor)` → `ap(vendor)` with three-way match against the WO's accrual rows. Tolerance window mirrors mig 0090's `unit_cost_tolerance_pct` (within: absorbs into `variance_match_tolerance`; out: P00xx).

## Function changes

- `post_wo_start`: snapshot `bom_by_products` rows for resolved BOM into `wo_by_products` (mirror of co-product wo_outputs auto-init). Caller can also INSERT directly for ad-hoc by-products on WOs without BOM-declared by-products.
- `post_wo_complete`: pre-pass after pre-balance, before co-product distribution loop. Walks `wo_by_products`, emits qty + value legs per treatment, adjusts `v_total_drain` for nrv_credit. Inventoriable disposal posts to co-product fg basis per allocation_pct. Period disposal posts to disposal_expense. Yield variance posts (actual - planned) × unit_value to `variance_yield_byproduct`.
- `post_ap_bill`: new `kind='disposal_match'` branch. Identifies accrual rows by (vendor, currency, qty + unit_value within tolerance); drains accrued_disposal_liability → ap; tolerance Δ absorbs to variance_match_tolerance.

## Sub-issue breakdown

This issue is the **umbrella**. Concrete work units are sub-issues to keep each ship-able and test-able:

- acct-7t4.1 — bom_by_products schema + ECO wiring
- acct-7t4.2 — wo_by_products + snapshot at wo_start
- acct-7t4.3 — post_wo_complete pre-pass: nrv_credit + negligible (foundational, no AP yet)
- acct-7t4.4 — disposal_cost both bases + accrued_disposal_liability + variance accounts
- acct-7t4.5 — post_ap_bill kind='disposal_match' + tolerance handling
- acct-7t4.6 — yield variance at wo_complete (variance_yield_byproduct)

## Follow-up (filed separately, not blocking core)

- NRV LCM revaluation at period close (per ASC 330 / IAS 2)
- Per-op by-product backflush (mid-routing emission, not just at wo_complete)
- wo_outputs.allocation_method='primary' rename to 'fixed_ratio' (cleanup)

## Acceptance criteria for closing this umbrella

All 6 sub-issues closed. Full lifecycle integration test (BOM declaration → WO snapshot → wo_complete with mixed treatments → AP bill → AP payment) passes. Industry-standard journal entries match.
