title: OSP physical custody — rebuild on standard ERP transactions when Slice C lands
description:
## Why this exists

acct-2yu (BOM2 B11, migration 0057) shipped dedicated OSP entry-points (post_osp_ship / post_osp_receive) plus an enum tax in migration 0040 (osp_ship / osp_receive transfer reasons, stock_consigned_at_vendor account_kind). Rolled back via migration 0059 (2026-05-03) after recognizing this was a premature special case ahead of Slice C (transfer orders / shipments / receipts).

This issue captures the trade-offs and standard-ERP modelling for the next implementer, so OSP can be picked up cleanly once Slice C exists.

## What dedicated OSP gave us (and what we lose by not having it)

The dedicated flow makes "these N units of parent_sku are physically at Vendor X right now" a database fact rather than an app-layer assumption. Concrete value:

- **Audit / SOX-style controls** — at any moment, how much of total inventory is offsite at vendors? A SUM query over stock_consigned_at_vendor balances answers it directly.
- **Customs / compliance** — when goods cross a border to/from vendor, attribution is auditable.
- **Insurance reconciliation** — claims coverage on offsite inventory needs a defensible offsite total.
- **Vendor-count reconciliation** — periodic vendor counts can match against the per-vendor balance in stock_consigned_at_vendor.

Without dedicated OSP, all of the above pushes to the application layer (or to a separate physical-custody log) and isn't enforceable at the ledger.

## How to model OSP using standard ERP transactions

Two reasonable approaches once Slice C lands:

### Approach 1: implicit custody via routing op (simplest)

- The OSP step is just a regular `wo_routings` row, e.g. `(wo_id, routing_op=30, op_name='osp_plating')`.
- Vendor's processing fee is a `bom_line` with `kind='service'` or `kind='charge'`, `applies_at_op=30`, and `absorption_class_id` pointing at an absorption_pool class scoped to OSP fees. Fires on first arrival at op30 via _wo_emit_bom_lines.
- Qty stays in `stock_wip(parent, op=30)` for the duration of vendor processing. The routing op IS "currently at OSP".
- No ship / receive transfers at the inventory level. Physical custody is implicit ("if WIP qty is sitting at the OSP op, it's at vendor; otherwise it's in our shop").

**Costs you give up**: per-vendor breakdown of offsite stock; cross-vendor analytics; auditable physical custody.

### Approach 2: vendor-location with transfer orders (Slice C composition)

When Slice C ships transfer orders, OSP can compose:

- `locations` table extended with `is_owned BOOLEAN` (or `vendor_id UUID` FK) to express "this location is a vendor's facility — we have title to inventory but not physical custody". This is a generic concern bigger than OSP — applies to any consignment relationship (consigned-out to customers, off-site warehouses, contract manufacturer plants, etc.).
- A "vendor warehouse" location row per OSP vendor, marked `is_owned=FALSE` with vendor_id set.
- **Ship to vendor** = standard transfer-order ship: drains `stock_wip(parent, OSP_op)` (qty stays at this op, but physical custody moves) using a custom transfer reason. Slice C will define this. The qty pool can either remain WIP-at-OSP-op (implicit custody) or move to `stock_consigned_at_vendor(parent, vendor, op)` if dedicated tracking is wanted (this is where the enum values from migration 0040 come back in).
- Vendor fee handled identically to Approach 1 (bom_line at OSP op).
- **Receive from vendor** = standard transfer-order receive at the production location. Yield variance for missing units handled by caller via `post_scrap` on the missing qty (per-unit accumulated cost from the WIP pool).

**Net**: the qty side becomes generic transfer orders; the cost side is unchanged from today (bom_line + applies_at_op already handle the fee). The "OSP" concept disappears as a special case — it's just another transfer with a vendor-location target.

## What's already in place that supports either approach

From the rolled-back acct-2yu work, the following remain in the schema (post-rollback) and are reusable:
- Migration 0040 enum values: `osp_ship`, `osp_receive`, `phantom_explode`, `lot_charge_apply`, `burden_apply` transfer_reasons; `absorption_pool`, `stock_consigned_at_vendor` account_kinds. These are unused but defined.
- absorption_classes (migration 0042) supports declaring an OSP-fee class at runtime (`INSERT INTO absorption_classes (code, applied_account_kind) VALUES ('osp_plating', 'absorption_pool')` — zero migration to add a new OSP fee type).
- bom_lines kind='service'/'charge' with absorption_class_id (migration 0044) carries the fee declaration cleanly.
- _wo_emit_bom_lines (migration 0051) fires the fee on first arrival at the OSP op via the `{fire_at='op_arrival', applies_at_op=N}` filter.

## When to revisit

- After Slice C produces transfer-order primitives (post_transfer_order_ship / post_transfer_order_receive).
- Decision at that point: does the value-add of dedicated OSP custody tracking (audit, vendor-recon) justify special functions, or does generic transfer-order machinery suffice with caller-side discipline?
- If dedicated: re-introduce post_osp_ship / post_osp_receive as thin wrappers that compose transfer orders + locations + the existing bom_line absorption path.
- If generic: keep OSP entirely app-layer, caller composes transfer orders + bom_line, and the locations.is_owned flag distinguishes offsite for analytics.

## Why rollback now (not later)

- Slice C doesn't exist; building OSP first means the API shape is provisional and will need re-aligning.
- Two unused entry-points in the function inventory (post_osp_ship / post_osp_receive) is more confusing than helpful while their composition target is missing.
- Rollback is cheap (drop two functions; enum values stay per project convention).
- The cost-accounting side (bom_line of kind=service/charge with absorption_pool class) already works without any OSP-specific code, via _wo_emit_bom_lines. Anyone needing to charge an OSP fee today can do so by:
  1. INSERT INTO absorption_classes (code, applied_account_kind) VALUES ('osp_<vendor>', 'absorption_pool')
  2. Add bom_line with kind='charge' or 'service', basis='per_lot' or 'per_unit', applies_at_op=<OSP_op>, absorption_class_id=<id>, std_amount=<fee>
  3. Optionally fire_at='op_arrival' so the fee only hits if the WO actually reaches the OSP op (scrap-aware safety from acct-jg2).

## Dependencies

- Blocks: [none currently]
- Blocked by: Slice C (outflow / transfer orders) — not yet filed as an epic.
- Related: acct-LOTSERIAL (lot/serial tracking, complementary for vendor-side recon).
- Related: any future "non-owned location" / consignment-out / consigned-from-vendor work — the locations.is_owned generalization would land there.

## Acceptance

When this issue is taken up:
- Decide approach (1 vs 2) and document.
- If approach 2, ensure locations gains is_owned and OSP composes from Slice C transfer-order primitives.
- Re-implement OSP entry points iff custody tracking is determined to be load-bearing (vs caller-driven).
- Migrate any existing OSP-fee bom_lines (caller's runtime data) without breakage.

title: Phase 2: full ECO approval workflow (acct-ECO-WORKFLOW)
description:
WHY: BOM2 ships engineering_change_orders (A2) and possibly post_eco_approve (B12, optional in 0041). If B12 ships, this issue is a placeholder for richer ECO workflow features. If B12 punts, this issue is the implementation home.

DELIVERABLE (sketch — depends on whether B12 ships):
If B12 punts:
- Implement post_eco_approve(p_eco_id, p_approved_by) as specified in plan §8
- Walk new bom_headers (eco_id = p_eco_id), set effective_at = ECO.effective_at, status='active'
- Walk predecessor revisions, set obsolete_at = ECO.effective_at, status='obsolete'
- P0031 'eco_invalid_state' on non-draft ECO

If B12 shipped:
- Multi-stage approval (engineering review → manufacturing review → finance review → final approval)
- ECO impact analysis: cost rollup delta, in-flight WO migration plan
- Bulk-update of in-flight WOs that should switch to the new revision
- ECO rejection workflow (status='rejected' with reason)
- ECO supersede workflow (newer ECO obsoletes older approved ECO)

INTERSECTS WITH: BOM2 (foundation), acct-VARIANT (config-resolved BOMs need ECO awareness), audit/compliance reporting.

Out of scope for BOM2 refactor unless B12 punts.

See plan §10 / §14 acct-ECO-WORKFLOW.
design:
DESIGN COMMITMENT (2026-05-05, from ERP_RESEARCH.md):

ECO effectivity-policy is FIRST-CLASS. Industry research surfaced "in-flight WO migration" (apply to WIP / new only / cutover date) as the single hardest planner choice in ECO management — currently invisible in our model.

Effectivity-policy additions:
- engineering_change_orders.wo_migration_policy TEXT CHECK (... IN ('apply_to_wip', 'new_wo_only', 'cutover_date')) NOT NULL DEFAULT 'new_wo_only'.
- engineering_change_orders.cutover_date DATE NULL (required when policy = cutover_date).
- post_wo_start consults the active ECO's policy + business_date when resolving BOM/routing.
- _wo_resolve_bom_for honors the policy.
- For 'apply_to_wip': bulk-update tool stamps in-flight WOs to use the new revision; variance settles through standard residual variance at wo_complete.

Multi-stage approval scope (existing):
- eco_approval_steps(eco_id, step_no, approver_role, approver_id, status, approved_at, comments).
- post_eco_approval_step advances one step; final-step transitions ECO to 'approved'.
- Roles drive RBAC (gates on RBAC framework — separate issue).
- eco_impact_report(p_eco_id) RETURNS TABLE: delta std cost rollup per affected sku, open-WO count by status, projected inv_value_wip revaluation amount.
- post_eco_supersede(p_old, p_new) stamps older as 'superseded', chains effective_at.

Compliance anchors (research-cited): aerospace/defense AS9100 ECN traceability; medical-device CAPA integration; automotive PPAP and tier-1 supplier change notifications.

Industry mapping: SAP ECM (LO-ECH) change records + impact analysis; Oracle PLM Cloud multi-stage workflow with rules-based / web-service approval; D365 ECM with product-lifecycle-state gating; NetSuite SuiteApprovals.

title: Phase 2: per-op planned yield + variance reporting (acct-YIELD)
description:
WHY: BOM2 ships per-line scrap_pct (planned material loss during assembly per component). What it doesn't ship: per-op planned yield (e.g., 'op30 plating expected to yield 95% — 5% loss is normal and amortizes'). And it doesn't ship the close-side variance reporter that compares planned vs actual yield.

SCHEMA SKETCH:
- bom_headers.yield_pct NUMERIC (overall planned yield) and/or per-op yield via new column on a routing-lines analog
- post_op_move math: when from_op declared yield_pct < 100, factor that into std_cum_at_from_op (caller pays for the planned loss)
- Period-close hook (or wo_close_v extension) that surfaces planned vs actual yield gap as a yield variance account (variance_yield)
- Reports: yield variance per WO, per SKU, per period

INTERSECTS WITH: BOM2 scrap_pct (per-line) is the input; yield_pct (per-bom or per-op) is the output check, acct-BURDENCLOSE (close-time variance distribution).

Out of scope for BOM2 refactor.

See plan §10 / §14 acct-YIELD.
close_reason: Superseded by mig 0061 (acct-6jq). Per-component yield already exists as bom_lines.scrap_pct with skus.yield_mode ∈ {plan_only, absorbed} controlling whether it amortizes into parent_std. Material variance flows through existing variance_wo_close. The 'per-op yield' framing in this issue's description was a separate routing-op-throughput concept, not typical BOM yield, and not load-bearing.

title: Phase 2: backflush consumption_policy dispatchers (acct-BACKFLUSH)
description:
WHY: BOM2 reserves the consumption_policy column on skus (forward / backflush_at_op / backflush_at_complete). Only 'forward' is dispatched in the BOM2 refactor; backflush variants raise P0035 'consumption_policy_not_implemented'. This issue implements the deferred dispatcher logic.

DELIVERABLE (sketch):
- post_wo_start path forks on parent_sku.consumption_policy:
  - 'forward' (today's behavior): drain components at fire_at
  - 'backflush_at_op': defer component drain until post_op_move(from_op = applies_at_op) completes
  - 'backflush_at_complete': defer component drain until post_wo_complete fires (drain proportional to qty_completed)
- post_op_move and post_wo_complete extended to walk the BOM and drain backflushed components retroactively
- New transfer_reason backflush_consume (or reuse rm_issue with a flag in metadata)
- Validation: backflushed BOM lines must have fire_at consistent with the policy (e.g., backflush_at_complete requires fire_at='wo_start' or equivalent)

INTERSECTS WITH: BOM2 (extends post_wo_start, post_op_move, post_wo_complete), acct-LOTSERIAL (backflush picks the lot at consume-time, not at fire-time).

Out of scope for BOM2 refactor.

See plan §10 / §14 acct-BACKFLUSH.

title: Phase 2: process-mfg PI sheets / master recipes (acct-PROCESS-PI)
description:
WHY: Process manufacturing (chemicals, food, pharma, beverages) uses 'master recipes' (PI sheets) that have semantics discrete-mfg BOMs don't capture: catalysts (don't deplete), recoverable solvents (return at end of run), energy as a cost component (kWh × rate), batch sizing with min/max yield, formula-based ingredient ratios. The BOM2 schema can extend to cover these without breaking discrete-mfg.

SCHEMA SKETCH:
- bom_lines.kind extended with 'catalyst' (consumed-then-returned at op_end), 'energy' (priced by kWh or BTU)
- New optional column bom_lines.recoverable_pct NUMERIC (catalyst lines: % returned to raw at op-complete)
- bom_lines.energy_uom TEXT for energy lines; energy_rate via absorption_classes
- bom_headers.batch_size_min/batch_size_max BIGINT (process-mfg has min/max economic batch)
- post_op_complete (new event?) reverses catalyst consumption: stock_raw(catalyst) ← stock_wip; net consumption only the unrecoverable portion
- Process-mfg uses 'recipe' as colloquial term but the model calls it bom_headers/bom_lines (D8)

INTERSECTS WITH: acct-CATCHWEIGHT (formulation by weight), acct-LOTSERIAL (batch tracking), acct-CAPACITY (kWh × rate is just hours × rate generalized).

Out of scope for BOM2 refactor.

See plan §10 / §14 acct-PROCESS-PI.

title: Phase 2: alternate routings (acct-ALT-ROUTING)
description:
WHY: BOM2 introduces alternate BOMs (substitute materials). The mirror concept on the routing side: alternate routings — same SKU, different production paths (different cells, different vendors, different op sequences). Today's wo_routings is single-valued per WO.

SCHEMA SKETCH:
- New table routing_alternates (id, sku_id, alternate_no, code, description, status, effective_at, obsolete_at, eco_id) — mirrors bom_headers
- routing_lines table (routing_id, op_no, work_center_id, std_hours, ...) — replaces today's wo_routings or composes with it
- work_orders.routing_id BIGINT REFERENCES routing_alternates(id) — pinned routing per WO; NULL falls back to primary at business_date
- Time-phased revisions like bom_headers
- post_wo_start consults work_orders.routing_id (or default-primary fallback) to populate wo_routings for the WO

INTERSECTS WITH: BOM2 (parallel-shaped concept), acct-CAPACITY (work centers + hours), acct-PROCESS-PI (process-mfg routings have different shapes).

Out of scope for BOM2 refactor.

See plan §10 / §14 acct-ALT-ROUTING.

title: Phase 2: payroll function for actual labor (acct-PAYROLL)
description:
WHY: Today's BOM model absorbs labor at standard via labor_apply / labor_applied. Actual labor — payroll runs, time-clock entries — needs a separate workflow that debits labor_expense and credits accrued payroll / cash. This is the companion to post_ap_bill (Slice A) but for labor instead of materials/services.

DELIVERABLE (sketch):
- New table payroll_runs (id, period_id, run_date, status, posted_by, posted_at)
- New table payroll_entries (run_id, employee_id, work_order_id?, routing_op?, hours, rate, gross, deductions JSONB)
- post_payroll_run(p_run_id, p_business_date, p_posted_by, p_idempotency_key): debits labor_expense, credits cash or wages_payable
- Optional: post_payroll_run can attribute hours to a specific WO/op for direct-labor capture (vs indirect/overhead)
- Per-op variance: planned_hours from BOM × accumulated qty vs actual_hours from payroll → variance_labor_efficiency (gates with acct-CAPACITY)

INTERSECTS WITH: acct-CAPACITY, acct-BURDENCLOSE, payroll provider integration (later).

Out of scope for BOM2 refactor.

See plan §10 / §14 acct-PAYROLL.

title: Phase 2: period-close burden netting (acct-BURDENCLOSE)
description:
WHY: Standard-cost burdens are absorbed into WIP/FG at standard rates throughout the period. At period close, actual expenses (labor payroll, overhead allocations) typically don't equal the absorbed amount. The net (overabsorbed / underabsorbed) needs to flow to a variance account or be re-distributed across COGS and inventory.

DELIVERABLE (sketch):
- New close hook burden_close_hook(p_period_id, p_force_provisional) RETURNING BIGINT
- For each absorption_classes row with expense_account_kind set: compute (Σ applied) vs (Σ expense) for the period
- Net the difference to variance_<class> (e.g., variance_labor_burden) at close
- Compose into close_period orchestrator (already supports plug-in hooks per Phase 1)
- Foundation already in place: absorption_classes.expense_account_kind column ships with BOM2 (A3)

INTERSECTS WITH: acct-PAYROLL (actual labor capture flows to expense), acct-TIMEPHASED-RATES, period-close orchestration.

Out of scope for BOM2 refactor.

See plan §10 / §14 acct-BURDENCLOSE.

title: Phase 2: capacity-based costing (acct-CAPACITY)
description:
WHY: True manufacturing costing decomposes per-unit cost into hours × rate, not pre-multiplied per-unit dollar amounts. This enables capacity planning, machine-utilization variance, labor-efficiency variance, and per-op time-and-attendance integration.

SCHEMA SKETCH:
- bom_lines.std_hours_per_unit NUMERIC (or BIGINT in scaled units, e.g., minutes)
- absorption_classes.std_hourly_rate BIGINT (or per-class rate sourced from acct-TIMEPHASED-RATES)
- post_wo_start: amount = qty × std_hours_per_unit × std_hourly_rate (separated from pre-multiplied std_amount)
- New event kind labor_actual or machine_actual capturing actual hours posted (from time-clock or MES)
- Variance accounts: variance_efficiency (planned vs actual hours), variance_rate (planned vs actual rate)

INTERSECTS WITH: acct-PAYROLL (actual labor capture), acct-TIMEPHASED-RATES, MES integration.

Out of scope for BOM2 refactor.

See plan §10 / §14 acct-CAPACITY.

title: Phase 2: time-phased absorption rates (acct-TIMEPHASED-RATES)
description:
WHY: Labor and overhead absorption rates change over time (annual rate updates, mid-year reforecasts). Today's bom_lines.std_amount is a single value per line; it doesn't separate the rate ($/hour) from the time-phasing of that rate.

SCHEMA SKETCH:
- New table absorption_classes_rate_history (class_id BIGINT, effective_at TIMESTAMPTZ, obsolete_at TIMESTAMPTZ, std_rate BIGINT, normal_side TEXT, ...)
- bom_lines.std_amount becomes a derived/cached value computed from rate history × std_hours (or similar) at WO_start
- resolve_std_rate_at(class_id, business_date) helper, like resolve_standard_cost_at
- post_wo_start consumes the rate at WO's business_date; revaluation hooks for in-flight WOs (decision: revalue or freeze at start? lean: freeze at start with rate reset on standard-cost roll)
- Period close hook (acct-BURDENCLOSE) honors time-phased rate boundaries

INTERSECTS WITH: acct-CAPACITY (rate × hours costing), acct-BURDENCLOSE (close hook netting), standard-cost roll workflow.

Out of scope for BOM2 refactor.

See plan §10 / §14 acct-TIMEPHASED-RATES.

title: Phase 2: multi-tier traceability (acct-MULTITIER-TRACE)
description:
WHY: FDA UDI / food traceability / aerospace requirements need full genealogy: 'this finished good was built from these specific lots of these components, on this date, by this operator, at this op step'. Today's wo_events is event-based but doesn't form a tree across multi-tier production (sub-assembly → assembly → finished good).

SCHEMA SKETCH:
- New table inventory_genealogy (parent_lot_id, parent_serial_id, child_lot_id, child_serial_id, work_order_id, event_id, recorded_at)
- post_wo_complete records genealogy: for each consumed component lot/serial, link to the produced lot/serial
- Recursive query function trace_upstream(p_lot_id) returns full ancestry
- Recursive query function trace_downstream(p_lot_id) returns all descendants (recall scope)
- Optional: genealogy is materialized at WO complete; recall queries hit the mat view

INTERSECTS WITH: acct-LOTSERIAL (foundation), acct-DISASSEMBLY (genealogy across reverse mfg).

Out of scope for BOM2 refactor.

See plan §10 / §14 acct-MULTITIER-TRACE.

title: Phase 2: disassembly / reverse manufacturing (acct-DISASSEMBLY)
description:
WHY: Reverse manufacturing — taking a finished good apart and yielding multiple component SKUs back into raw inventory (and possibly scrap). Common in returns, refurbishment, end-of-life recycling, salvage. Today's model only supports forward assembly (one parent → multiple children).

SCHEMA SKETCH:
- Either: work_orders.direction ∈ {assemble, disassemble} discriminator
- Or new disassembly_orders table with inverse semantics
- Inverse BOM: same bom_lines table but kind='item' lines represent OUTPUTS (qty_per_parent = qty_yielded_per_parent_torn_down)
- post_disassembly_start: drains stock_available(parent) → stock_wip(parent, op_disassembly)
- post_disassembly_complete: drains stock_wip → stock_available(component) per inverse BOM allocation
- Cost basis: parent's accumulated cost distributed to components per allocation_method (similar to co-product allocation)
- New transfer_reasons: disassembly_start, disassembly_complete, disassembly_yield_variance

INTERSECTS WITH: acct-LOTSERIAL (lot tracking through disassembly), acct-MULTITIER-TRACE (traceability across assembly/disassembly cycles).

Out of scope for BOM2 refactor.

See plan §10 / §14 acct-DISASSEMBLY.

title: Phase 2: catch-weight items (acct-CATCHWEIGHT)
description:
WHY: Catch-weight items are priced by weight but inventoried by count (e.g., meat, cheese, produce — '1 case of cheese, weighs 18.4 lb, priced $3.50/lb'). Today's model conflates qty and value. Catch-weight needs dual-uom: count (inventoried unit) plus weight (pricing unit).

SCHEMA SKETCH:
- skus.is_catch_weight BOOLEAN; skus.weight_uom TEXT; skus.count_uom TEXT
- inventory rows extend with weight_total BIGINT (in scaled units, e.g., milligrams) alongside qty (count)
- po_receipt_lines extend with weight_received BIGINT for catch-weight SKUs
- post_po_receipt: if catch-weight, value_leg amount = weight_received × po_unit_price (per weight); qty_leg balance gets count_received
- post_so_ship: catch-weight items pull weight from inventory pool proportional to count (FIFO/WAC-aware)
- BOM lines for catch-weight components: qty_per_parent in count or weight? (decision deferred — likely both, with explicit basis column)

INTERSECTS WITH: acct-LOTSERIAL (each lot has its own catch-weight), reservations, AP three-way match (qty + weight tolerance).

Out of scope for BOM2 refactor.

See plan §10 / §14 acct-CATCHWEIGHT.
notes: 2026-05-07: Re-scoped to Phase E3 of acct-wb75 convergence; blocked-by Phase D (acct-wb75.3). Per research/posting-lines-convergence-plan.md §4.E.E3 + cost-methods doc §10. 'Lot-based costing with lot size 1.' Volume strategies mandatory: time-based partitioning + status-based archival + columnar analytics.

title: Phase 2: lot/serial tracking (acct-LOTSERIAL)
description:
WHY: Lot/serial tracking is a deep change that intersects reservations, inventory pools, post_so_ship, post_po_receipt, post_wo_complete, and traceability. Needed for regulated industries (food, pharma, medical devices, aerospace) and for warranty/recall workflows.

SCHEMA SKETCH:
- New table inventory_lots (id, sku_id, location_id, lot_code, qty, expiry_at, attributes JSONB)
- New table inventory_serials (id, sku_id, lot_id?, serial_no, status TEXT, current_location_id, work_order_id?)
- skus.tracked_by ∈ {none, lot, serial, lot_and_serial}

design:
DESIGN COMMITMENT (2026-05-05, from ERP_RESEARCH.md):

Adopt D365's "tracking dimension toggles financial inventory" abstraction — costing dispatches on the same dimensions storage uses. Cleanest model surveyed across SAP/Oracle/D365/NetSuite.

Schema:
- New tables lots and serials. lots(id, sku_id, location_id, lot_code, qty, expiry_at, attributes JSONB), serials(id, sku_id, lot_id?, serial_no, status, current_location_id, work_order_id?).
- skus.tracked_by ENUM('none', 'lot', 'serial', 'lot_and_serial') controls which dimensions partition on the SKU.
- accounts gain lot_id UUID NULL / serial_id UUID NULL (CHECK: lot/serial only on stock_* kinds).
- Partition uniqueness: (kind, sku_id, location_id, currency, COALESCE(lot_id, NIL), COALESCE(serial_id, NIL)) UNIQUE WHERE NOT is_closed. Existing rows continue to work with lot=NULL — backward-compatible.
- inventory_reservations gain lot_id NULL + lot_specific BOOLEAN. NULL lot = any lot (fastest path); lot_specific = TRUE pins to exact lot.
- New table lot_genealogy(parent_lot_id, component_lot_id, qty, work_order_id) populated by _wo_emit_bom_lines and post_wo_complete. FSMA-compliant audit table.

Cost-method extensions:
- Add 'specific' and 'lot_fifo' to cost_method enum.
- Both compose with R1 per-class qty divisor (no special-casing required).

All inventory-touching functions (post_po_receipt, post_so_ship, post_wo_start, post_wo_complete, post_op_move, post_scrap, post_inventory_adjustment) extend with optional lot_id / serial_id parameters, NULL by default.

Compliance anchors (research-cited):
- FSMA 204 (effective 2026-01) — TLC + KDEs persisted 24 months, FDA delivery in 24h
- FDA UDI / EU MDR — DI + PI = lot + serial + mfg date
- AS9100 §8.5.2 — design-life pedigree (often 30+ years)
- GS1 Global Traceability Standard — GTIN + batch + serial as canonical identifier

Industry mapping: D365 tracking dimensions ('Active', 'Physical inventory', 'Financial inventory' flags); SAP LO-BM batch management + classification system (class type 022/023, chars LOBM_VFDAT/LOBM_HSDAT); Oracle Lot/Serial Genealogy + actual-cost orgs for specific costing; NetSuite Advanced Inventory Management + Lot Numbered/Serialized item types.

GATES: acct-90x (multi-tier traceability), acct-0kz (catch-weight per-lot weight), acct-lle Phase 3 (active-ingredient potency).

title: Phase 2: cross-currency BOMs (component in non-WO currency)
description:
Surfaced during acct-69p (Slice B.1 critical-analysis review).

Today's behavior: work_orders.currency is single-valued. post_wo_start looks up component inv_value_raw accounts in WO currency. If a component lives only in a different currency (e.g., EUR-priced raw consumed by USD-billed WO), the lookup raises P0010 'no open inv_value_raw account for sku=X loc=Y ccy=USD' — sane failure mode but not a real solution.

A real cross-currency BOM would need either:
  (a) FX conversion at consumption time using fx_rates, with the FX gain/loss leg routing through fx_revaluation; or
  (b) Multi-currency WIP pools per WO (more flexible, more complex).

Tracking as Phase 2 since Slice B MVP is single-currency by design and the failure mode is clearly diagnosable. Reopen when a real workload demands cross-currency BOMs.

Out of scope for Phase 1.

title: Slice B.1 critical-analysis review: BOM + per-op burden model
description:
Slice B.1 (acct-b82) shipped a generalized burden model: BOM components + per-op wo_routing_burdens rows that map to absorption account_kinds (labor_applied, oh_applied today; outside_processing_applied / setup_applied / tooling_applied later via ALTER TYPE). Functions: post_wo_start, post_op_move (with new op_move_v transfer_reason for the value-leg bypass), post_wo_complete, post_scrap.

This issue is a deliberate review pass — independent critical analysis of the design before Slice B.2 matrix tests cement it.

REVIEW SCOPE — gaps, edge cases, and surprises to surface:

1. Cost-rollup consistency: parent_sku.std_cost (resolved via resolve_standard_cost_at at WO start time) vs the WO's own implied roll-up (Σ BOM × comp_std + Σ wo_routing_burdens.std_amount). post_wo_complete's value-leg uses resolve_standard_cost_at(parent_sku); if WO data drifts from SKU-level std, residual hits variance_wo_close. Should we validate at WO creation or accept drift?

2. Burden timing edge cases:
   - Rework (op_move from a higher op to a lower op) re-applies destination op burdens. Is this the right semantic, or should rework events use a separate path that does NOT re-apply?
   - Partial wo_complete then later op_move into the partially-drained op: burdens re-apply for the moved qty even though the op was already begun for prior qty. Correct (per-unit semantics), but worth a test.
   - Scrap at first op AFTER WO_start applied first-op burdens: scrap reads pool unit cost (= std_cum_at_first_op), so variance_scrap captures both RM and first-op burdens. Standard ERP behavior.
   - Scrap at intermediate op before any units passed through: pool is empty (qty=0); function raises P0026.

3. Component cost methodology: BOM expansion calls resolve_standard_cost_at(component_sku) regardless of comp.cost_method. WAC/WAC-periodic components have no standard cost in effect → P0018. Should this be P0006 with a clearer message ('component must have standard cost in effect')?

4. Multi-currency: WO is single-currency (CHECK at column level). What if a component lives in a different currency? Function looks up inv_value_raw for v_wo.currency — won't find the comp's pool, raises P0010. Real-world WOs sometimes cross currencies; deferred to Phase 2 but worth confirming the failure mode is sane.

5. wo_close_v residual sign convention: code emits variance_wo_close DR / inv_value_wip CR for positive residual (unfavorable) and the reverse for negative. Verify the sign aligns with general accounting convention (variance = actual - standard; favorable = actual < standard = WIP under-absorbed).

6. Account-kind safety on applied_account_kind: schema doesn't constrain wo_routing_burdens.applied_account_kind to absorption-only kinds. Caller could pass 'cogs' or 'cash'. Function looks up by kind — succeeds — but the resulting transfer_reason mapping fails (P0026). Should the schema add a CHECK or trigger to gate at insert time?

7. No FK from wo_routing_burdens.applied_account_kind to a list of valid kinds — relies on the runtime _wo_apply_reason_for raise. Is this acceptable, or should a ledger-side enum (e.g., wo_burden_kind) sit between?

8. Transfer-reason discoverability: 'op_move' is in the dispatcher cost-event list (for future wac WIP work) but the standard MVP path uses 'op_move_v'. New readers may be confused. Doc'd in 0037 header but worth a Q: rename to 'op_move_qty' / 'op_move_v' pairing for symmetry?

9. Idempotency boundaries: post_wo_start uses wo_events.idempotency_key UNIQUE. ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING returns NULL → function returns p_wo_id without re-emitting events. Verify ALL replay paths are no-op-correct (T1 probe).

10. post_scrap calls PERFORM 1 ... FOR UPDATE on (val_from, qty_from) ordered by id. post_transfers internally also acquires FOR UPDATE on these same accounts during apply. Is the lock-order invariant honored, or is there a deadlock window?

11. Op-relative burdens applied multiple times: if the same op is destination of multiple op_moves (e.g., two batches arriving), burdens apply multiple times. Total burden absorbed = (Σ batch_qty) × std_amount = qty_target × std_amount eventually. Correct, but verify pool integrity holds across interleaved batches.

12. Empty wo_routing_burdens for an op: function emits 0 burden events (sum=0 short-circuit). WIP@op accumulates only RM + upstream burdens. Valid pattern for a no-burden op (e.g. queueing/inspection-only stations).

DELIVERABLE: a bullet-list memo (or new bd issues per item) before Slice B.2 (acct-wl1) matrix tests start writing assertions that bake in current behavior.

PRIORITY: P3 (review pass; not blocking). Should run in parallel with .2 / .3 sub-issues.
notes:
acct-69p REVIEW MEMO (2026-05-02) — Slice B.1 BOM + per-op burden model

REAL BUG FIXED IN MIGRATION 0039:

Item 9 — Idempotency replay race in post_wo_start and post_wo_complete.
  Reproduces when two callers issue the same idempotency_key while T1
  is mid-flight: T2's wo_events lookup finds nothing, T2 waits on FOR
  UPDATE, T1 commits + writes status, T2 acquires lock and sees the
  new status, status check raises P0026 instead of returning
  idempotently.
  Fix: re-check wo_events.idempotency_key AFTER the FOR UPDATE on
  work_orders, before the status check. post_op_move and post_scrap
  don't have this issue (status doesn't change during the call;
  ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING in the wo_events INSERT handles the actual
  race).

PHASE 2 FOLLOW-UP FILED:

Item 4 — Cross-currency BOMs. Filed as acct-tt1 (P3).

NOT BUGS — ANALYSIS NOTES:

Item 1 — Cost-rollup consistency (parent_sku.std vs Σ BOM × comp_std +
  Σ burdens). Not a bug; if the WO's implied roll-up diverges from
  parent_sku's standard cost (set via post_standard_cost_roll), the
  difference surfaces as wo_close_v residual at WO close. This is
  exactly what variance_wo_close exists for under standard cost
  accounting. Phase 2 could add a creation-time validation, but
  letting the variance catch drift is the principled answer.

Item 2 — Burden timing edge cases all behave correctly:
  - Rework (op_move from higher op to lower op) re-applies destination
    burdens. Realistic ERP semantics — labor is paid twice when work
    is redone.
  - Partial wo_complete then later op_move into partially-drained op:
    burdens re-apply per-batch. Correct.
  - Scrap at first op AFTER WO_start: pool unit cost = std_cum_at_op,
    so variance_scrap captures both RM and first-op burdens.
  - Scrap at intermediate op before any units arrived: P0026
    (qty_balance <= 0). Correct.

Item 3 — Component cost methodology. resolve_standard_cost_at(comp)
  unconditionally; non-standard components without a std cost row
  raise P0018. Failure mode is diagnosable. Pre-checking at WO start
  would improve UX but isn't load-bearing for correctness.

Item 5 — wo_close_v sign convention is correct. WIP balance > 0 after
  drain = "actual" (WO_total) > "standard" (parent_std) =
  unfavorable; DR variance / CR WIP increases variance balance
  (debit-normal). Reverse case for negative residual: DR WIP / CR
  variance, decreasing variance = favorable.

Items 6 + 7 — applied_account_kind safety. The runtime
  _wo_apply_reason_for(kind) raises P0026 for unmapped kinds. A
  schema-level CHECK or separate enum would tighten this but
  duplicates the runtime gate; deferred unless wo_routing_burdens
  insertion bypasses the function path (not currently a concern).

Item 8 — op_move / op_move_v naming asymmetry vs wo_complete (same
  reason for both legs). Asymmetry exists because op_move's value-leg
  cost cannot ride the dispatcher's standard branch (which returns
  parent's full std — wrong at intermediate ops). Documented in 0037
  header and §3.4. Could be fixed by extending the dispatcher's
  standard branch to read pool unit cost on inv_value_wip class
  (mirrors wac_perpetual logic), but that's a larger refactor —
  deferred to acct-p7v which lifts the WIP-side WAC restriction
  generally.

Item 10 — Lock ordering in post_scrap. Not a bug. post_scrap holds
  FOR UPDATE on (val_from, qty_from) in the same transaction as the
  subsequent post_transfers call; FOR UPDATE in the same backend tx
  is a no-op upgrade of an existing lock, never deadlocks against
  itself. Cross-transaction lock ordering is unaffected.

Item 11 — Op-relative burdens applied multiple times across op_moves
  arriving at the same op. Correct: total absorbed = (Σ batch_qty)
  × std_amount = qty_target × std_amount.

Item 12 — Empty wo_routing_burdens for an op. _wo_burden_events_for_op
  iterates zero rows; valid pattern for queueing/inspection-only ops
  that consume only upstream cost.

ASSERTIONS THE MATRIX TESTS (acct-wl1) SHOULD COVER:

- T2 idempotency replay across all four functions (post_wo_start,
  post_op_move, post_wo_complete, post_scrap), including the
  wo_start/wo_complete race scenario from Item 9 — ideally with
  concurrent connections to actually trigger the FOR UPDATE wait.
- Rework op_move (to_op < from_op) re-applying destination burdens.
- Multi-batch op_move into the same op (Item 11).
- Empty-burden op (Item 12).
- WO_total ≠ parent_std → wo_close_v residual lands on
  variance_wo_close with correct sign (Item 5).
- Component without std cost in effect → P0018 surfaces clearly
  (Item 3).
- WO with cross-currency component → P0010 (Item 4 — Phase 1
  failure-mode test, real fix is acct-tt1).
- applied_account_kind with unmapped kind (e.g., 'cogs') → P0026
  (Item 6/7).

title: Explore stable expense-account taxonomy for service bills
description:
Slice A (acct-XXX) chose D2 = caller-supplied expense_account_id per service-bill line. That keeps post_ap_bill flexible but means the income statement has no stable reporting buckets — the operator either uses ad-hoc account_kind values or invents per-deployment conventions.

This issue captures the Phase 2 question: should we add a small fixed taxonomy of operating-expense account_kind values (utilities, professional_services, rent, software, travel, etc.) so AP-side reporting is normalized?

ARGUMENTS FOR taxonomy:
- Income statement reporting can roll up by kind without operator-side conventions.
- Audit/lint can flag service bills posted to non-expense accounts.
- Matches how some mainstream ERPs constrain GL accounts at the document layer.

ARGUMENTS AGAINST:
- The set of expense kinds is jurisdiction-specific (US vs EU vs JP have different categorization conventions).
- Forces a one-size-fits-all that operators may have to subvert.
- post_transfers already accepts any account_id — the constraint would be doc-layer-only and could be added later non-additively (just an expanded enum).

WHEN TO REVISIT: when a real reporting requirement surfaces (Phase 2 financial-statement work, or first multi-jurisdiction tenant). Not blocking on it now.

title: Phase 2 Epic K: period reopen workflow
description:
Companion to acct-og1 (Epic E: cost_adjustment retroactive). cost_adjust_retroactive can only operate on the current open period — to retroactively adjust a closed period, the operator must first reopen it.

Currently no reopen mechanism exists. periods.closed_at is set by close_period() but never reset. acct-og1 surfaces this gap when it raises an error like 'target_period 2026-03 is closed; reopen the period before queueing retroactive adjustments.'

SCOPE (when claimed):

1. reopen_period(p_period_id BIGINT, p_actor UUID, p_reason TEXT) RETURNS JSONB function:
   - Validates period is currently closed.
   - UPDATE periods SET closed_at = NULL, closed_by = NULL.
   - Records audit (in periods table or new period_lifecycle table).
   - Lock-order: FOR UPDATE on the period row.

2. Audit trail: every reopen records who/why/when. period_lifecycle table or audit columns on periods.

3. Constraints to consider:
   - Can a period be reopened if a LATER period is already closed? In real ERPs this is usually disallowed (closed periods have to be in chronological order). Decision: defer to design phase.
   - Locking: should reopen require P-something to ensure no other operator is in the middle of a close?
   - What happens to the recon alerts that were dismissed when the period closed? Probably stay in recon_alerts table but flagged.

4. Tests:
   - Reopen a closed period.
   - Cannot reopen an already-open period (P-something).
   - Reopen + queue retroactive adjustment + re-close.

ACCEPTANCE: ability to reopen a closed period, audit the reopen, then re-close cleanly.

DEPENDS ON: nothing — close_period exists. Standalone workflow.

USE CASES:
- cost_adjust_retroactive (acct-og1) on closed periods.
- Any retroactive correction that needs to land in a closed period's books.
- Period close mistakes (force_provisional was wrong, etc.) where re-running with corrected data is needed.

OUT OF SCOPE:
- Cascading reopens (reopening period N while period N+1 is closed). Probably forbidden.
- Period merge/split.
- Recomputing period_snapshots after reopen+reclose.
design:
DESIGN COMMITMENT (2026-05-05, from ERP_RESEARCH.md):

Three-state period lattice + cascade-on-reopen is universal (SAP, Oracle, D365, NetSuite). Replace binary closed_at with full status enum.

Schema:
- period_status enum: 'open' / 'soft_closed' / 'permanently_closed'. Mirror F&O's three-state model.
- Replace periods.closed_at boolean semantics; keep timestamp column for audit.
- period_lifecycle audit table: (period_id, from_status, to_status, actor, reason, at).
- reopen_period(p_period_id, p_actor, p_reason TEXT): cascades to all later soft_closed periods; raises P0050+ if any are permanently_closed; writes audit rows. Separate role/capability from poster (gates on RBAC framework — separate issue).
- Permanently-closed transitions are terminal — no reopen path. Matches F&O's irreversible 'Permanently closed' state.

Once reopen_period lands, retire the per-call p_override_closed_period flags on post_po_return / post_customer_return (mig 0086) — they should call reopen_period then close_period again with audit, instead of bypassing silently.

Cross-module dependency (Oracle pattern: Receivables can't reopen if GL closed) is out of scope until a sub-ledger boundary exists in our model.

Industry mapping: SAP OB52 + FCLOCOC + FAGL_REOPEN; Oracle Open/Closed/Permanently Closed; F&O On hold/Permanently closed; NetSuite cascading reopen + Allow Non-G/L Changes.

title: Phase 2 Epic J: wac_periodic + wac_retroactive across WIP pools
description:
Companion epic to acct-qfj (Epic B, wac_periodic) and acct-9tw (Epic C, wac_retroactive). Both currently raise P0006 when the source pool is inv_value_wip — Phase 1 defers WIP support because periodic re-costing of WIP requires recursive cost-chain analysis: an op_move from a wac_periodic/retroactive WIP pool feeds another wac_periodic/retroactive WIP pool, and re-costing the source pool changes what the destination should have received.

WHY THIS IS HARD.
inv_value_wip pools are connected by op_move events:
  inv_value_wip(op10) -> op_move -> inv_value_wip(op20) -> op_move -> ... -> inv_value_fg
Each op_move is a cost-relevant value-leg event whose amount depends on the source pool's avg AT THE TIME of the move. For wac_periodic / wac_retroactive, that source pool's true avg only becomes known at period close. So:
  - The op_move's recomputed amount depends on the source pool's recomputed avg.
  - The destination pool's value (inv_value_wip(op20)) is built FROM op_move debits.
  - The destination's recomputed avg therefore depends on the source's recomputed avg.
  - And so on transitively through the routing chain.

This recursion is multi-pool and order-dependent. A naive per-pool replay (the approach used for raw + fg in Phase 1) doesn't compose because pools aren't independent.

OPTIONS TO RESEARCH (Phase 2 design choice):

1. TOPOLOGICAL REPLAY. Order pools by routing dependency (op10 before op20 before fg). Replay each pool in topological order; downstream pools see corrected upstream avgs. Works as long as the routing graph is a DAG (no rework loops within a period).

2. ITERATIVE FIXED-POINT. Replay all pools repeatedly until variances converge. Slow; may not converge in pathological cases.

3. GLOBAL EVENT REPLAY. Order ALL in-period events globally by (business_date, posted_at, id), maintain running state for ALL pools simultaneously, walk in chronological order. Each op_move debits one pool at the source's running avg, credits the other at same avg. Simplest mental model; biggest state machine.

4. PER-WO REPLAY. Group events by work order. Within a WO, pools are linearly ordered by op number. Cleanest for batch-shaped manufacturing but assumes WO-attribution on every event.

ACCEPTANCE (when claimed):
- Phase 2 design decision on the replay model.
- wac_periodic_close_hook + wac_retroactive_close_hook bodies extended to handle inv_value_wip source pools.
- Tests covering: rm_issue_to_wo + op_move + wo_complete sequence on a wac_periodic SKU; same on wac_retroactive; multi-WO interleaving in same period; rework loops (if scope allows).

DEPENDS ON:

- acct-9tw (Epic C, wac_retroactive) — when closed
- acct-1vr (per-class qty fix) ✓ closed — required for the running-state math to work per-pool

PRIORITY: P3, deferred until real Phase 1 workflows pressure it. Slice B (Conversion: WO + routings, not yet filed) is when this becomes load-bearing — until manufacturing flows are exercised, the deferral is acceptable.

title: qfj.1 — Implementation: wac_periodic dispatcher + close_hook body + transfers_provisional.qty
description:

Migration scope (next available, likely 0029):

1. ALTER TABLE transfers_provisional ADD COLUMN qty BIGINT.
   Nullable for backward-compat with s6n-era rows (which were stub-only and have no real cost data attached anyway).

2. CREATE OR REPLACE FUNCTION _post_transfers_compute_amount.
   wac_periodic branch changes from `RAISE P0006` to:
   - Same pool-read pattern as wac_perpetual (FOR UPDATE on the value account; v_unit = v_value_balance / v_qty_balance).
   - INSERT INTO transfers_provisional (transfer_id, period_id, cost_method, qty) VALUES (NEW transfer id, period at business_date, wac_periodic, v_qty).
   - Returns v_qty * v_unit (the provisional value-leg amount).
   Empty pool: P0006 with message "wac_periodic SKU has empty pool; first depletion must seed via inventory_adjustment IN with explicit cost".

3. CREATE OR REPLACE FUNCTION post_inventory_adjustment.
   wac_periodic branch: for OUT (p_qty_delta < 0), same treatment as wac_perpetual OUT (NULL p_unit_cost → pool avg; explicit → P0011 redirect to lot tracking) PLUS insert transfers_provisional row.
   For IN (p_qty_delta > 0), proceed as wac_perpetual IN. Receipts dont flag.

4. CREATE OR REPLACE FUNCTION wac_periodic_close_hook(p_period_id BIGINT) RETURNS BIGINT.
   Replaces s6n stub. Body:
   a. Look up periods.opens_at + closes_at for date-range query.
   b. SELECT * FROM transfers_provisional tp WHERE tp.period_id = $1 AND tp.cost_method = wac_periodic AND tp.finalized_at IS NULL FOR UPDATE.
   c. For each row, derive (sku_id, location_id, currency) by reading the original transfers debit account (which is inv_value_<class>(sku, loc, ccy)).
   d. Aggregate per (sku, location, currency): sum value_in and qty_in over the period from transfers WHERE business_date BETWEEN opens_at AND closes_at AND debit_account_id = inv_value_*(sku, loc, ccy). Result: final_avg = value_in / qty_in.
   e. If qty_in = 0 (no receipts): RAISE P0020 (wac_periodic_close_no_receipts) with message identifying the (sku, loc, ccy). Operator can either post receipts and re-try, or close with p_force_provisional=TRUE.
   f. For each provisional row: provisional_unit_cost = orig_transfer.amount / orig_transfer.qty (where orig_transfer.qty comes from tp.qty). variance = (final_avg - provisional_unit_cost) * tp.qty. Direction by sign — write-up: dr inv_value_*, cr variance_wac_period; write-down: reverse.
   g. Build a transfer batch and PERFORM post_transfers(batch, FALSE). Capture the variance transfer ids.
   h. UPDATE transfers_provisional SET finalized_at = clock_timestamp(), variance_amount, variance_transfer_id WHERE transfer_id = ...
   i. RETURN count of rows finalized.

LOCK ORDER: standard pattern. The hook holds transfers_provisional rows under FOR UPDATE; the variance posting goes through post_transfers which handles the per-event lock-order invariant.

NEW ERROR CODE:
- P0020 — wac_periodic_close_no_receipts. Documented in db/README error codes by qfj.3.

  * Period close lifecycle: receive twice + deplete once + close → variance posted, row finalized.
  * close_period on a wac_periodic period with no receipts but with provisional depletions: P0020 unless force.

title: Phase 2 Epic I: alternate provisional cost sources for wac_periodic / wac_retroactive
description:
Adds operator/SKU choice of provisional cost source for mid-period depletions on wac_periodic and wac_retroactive SKUs. Phase 1 ships running_avg only; this epic adds the alternatives that real ERPs offer.

CONTEXT. When a depletion fires mid-period on a wac_periodic SKU, the value-leg posts at a 'provisional' cost (running estimate), gets flagged in transfers_provisional, and is re-costed at period close from Σ(value_in)/Σ(qty_in). The provisional cost source is a real configuration choice in production ERPs:

| Source | Industry  | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| Running perpetual avg of period-to-date receipts | Oracle | Smallest close-time variance; reuses wac_perpetual code. Phase 1 default. |
| Last period's final close avg | SAP S/4 | Stable; lags by one period; needs a period_avgs snapshot |
| Configured/seeded value per SKU | Sage option | Operator picks at SKU setup |
| Last purchase price (most recent po_receipt) | NetSuite option | Simple lookup; misleading on rare receipts |
| Zero | Some shops | All variance hits at close; mid-period reporting useless |
| SKU's standard cost (if any in standard_costs stream) | SAP fallback | Mixes standard + WAC; uncommon |

PROPOSED DESIGN:

1. New SKU column: skus.provisional_cost_method TEXT or enum, with values matching the sources above. Default 'running_avg' for backward compatibility.

2. Internal helper _resolve_provisional_cost(sku, location, business_date, currency) RETURNS BIGINT that dispatches on the SKU's configured method.

3. _post_transfers_compute_amount's wac_periodic branch (and wac_retroactive) calls the helper instead of hard-coding running_avg.

4. New supporting infrastructure for some sources:
   - 'last_period_close': a period_avgs snapshot (sku, location, currency, period_id, final_avg) populated at period close
   - 'configured_value': new column skus.provisional_cost_value BIGINT
   - 'last_purchase_price': lookup in transfers WHERE reason='po_receipt' AND sku, location ORDER BY business_date DESC LIMIT 1 (already queryable, no new schema)
   - 'zero': trivial
   - 'standard': calls resolve_standard_cost_at; warns or rejects if SKU has no standard

5. Tests covering each source × edge cases (no prior period, no prior receipt, etc.).

ACCEPTANCE (when claimed):
- Migration adds the SKU column + helper + support infrastructure for chosen sources.
- _post_transfers_compute_amount updated.
- Test matrix for each source.
- Doc updates listing all sources and their semantics.

DEPENDS ON: Epic B (acct-qfj) — establishes the running_avg path and the dispatcher hook; this epic adds the alternatives.

OUT OF SCOPE:
- Per-period override of the SKU's default (e.g., one period uses standard, the rest use running_avg).
- Cross-SKU shared provisional cost (e.g., a category-level avg).
design:
DESIGN COMMITMENT (2026-05-05, from ERP_RESEARCH.md):

Add SAP's "release prior PUP as new standard" pattern as a source option — research identified this as the cleanest of the six sources surveyed. It makes the next period's mid-period valuation = prior period's actual close avg, so close-time variance shrinks period-over-period.

Updated source list:
- 'running_avg' (default) — Oracle/NetSuite mid-period default; Phase 1 baseline
- 'last_period_close_avg' — SAP S/4 PAC convention; lags by one period; needs period_avgs snapshot
- 'released_prior_pup' — SAP "release prior PUP as new standard" semantics; explicit "new period mid-period valuation = old period close" convention
- 'last_purchase_price' — NetSuite option; misleading on rare receipts
- 'standard' — falls back to standard_costs stream; warns/rejects if no standard
- 'configured' — operator-set per-SKU value
- 'zero' — defers all variance to close (engineer-to-order pattern from Epicor / Infor LN)

Schema:
- skus.provisional_cost_source TEXT CHECK (... IN above values) NOT NULL DEFAULT 'running_avg'.
- skus.provisional_cost_value BIGINT NULL (only used when source = 'configured').
- New table period_avgs(sku, location, currency, period_id, final_avg) populated at period close — supports 'last_period_close_avg' and 'released_prior_pup'.
- Helper _resolve_provisional_cost(sku, location, business_date, currency) RETURNS BIGINT dispatches on the SKU's source.
- _post_transfers_compute_amount's wac_periodic + wac_retroactive branches consult the helper instead of hard-coding running_avg.

R2 applies: SKU resolution from credit-side (depletion source). Test matrix per source covering edge cases (no prior period, no prior receipt, no standard, etc).

DEPENDS ON: stage AFTER acct-c4p (pseudo-sync pivot) to avoid double-rewriting the dispatcher; the hooks need rewrite either way.

Industry mapping: SAP Material Price Determination + release-prior-PUP-as-new-standard; Oracle Cost Profile provisional rules; D365 "Include physical value" flag (closest to our GRNI staging shape); NetSuite running-avg only.

title: Phase 2 Epic H: negative inventory support (oversold / catch-up)
description:
Investigation epic for supporting negative on-hand inventory — depletions that exceed current stock get posted at a best-guess cost; the next receipt 'catches up' the negative balance.

CONTEXT. Current schema enforces non-negative inventory via the accounts CHECK constraint:
  CASE normal_side
    WHEN 'debit'  THEN credits_total <= debits_total
    WHEN 'credit' THEN debits_total  <= credits_total
    ELSE TRUE
  END
A depletion past zero on a debit-normal account (stock_available) fails at the SQL level (23514). Real ERPs (NetSuite, Oracle option, Sage) allow this in 'permissive' mode for shops that ship before scanning receipts.

WHY IT MATTERS. High-velocity warehouses, made-to-order shops, retail with delayed receipt scanning — operators want to record the depletion when it physically happened, not wait for the receipt paperwork. The accounting catches up when receipts arrive.

INVESTIGATION SCOPE (research only; no code in this epic):

1. Schema-level options:
   (a) Relax CHECK on stock_available accounts (defeats the load-bearing invariant)
   (b) Add a separate 'stock_oversold' account_kind that carries the negative-balance debt; net qty = stock_available - stock_oversold
   (c) Per-SKU policy flag (skus.allow_negative_qty BOOLEAN); CHECK relaxes only for those SKUs
   (d) Per-location policy

2. Cost handling on the depletion that goes negative:
   (a) Use running perpetual avg of any prior receipts (might be zero or stale)
   (b) Use the SKU's configured provisional cost (Epic I)
   (c) Caller-asserted cost
   (d) Defer cost computation; mark transfer as 'cost-pending', resolve at next receipt

3. Catch-up at next receipt:
   (a) When a receipt arrives, if there's outstanding negative, the receipt's cost re-prices the prior depletion via a variance posting against a new variance_oversold_catchup account_kind
   (b) Or batch the catch-up at period close
   (c) Or refuse the receipt until a manual reconciliation runs

4. Edge cases:
   - Multi-receipt fill: what if the receipt qty doesn't fully cover the negative balance?
   - Mixed-cost receipts: receipts arrive at different costs; how is variance allocated across the negative-balance depletions?
   - Period boundaries: depletion in period N goes negative; receipt arrives in period N+1; variance posts in N or N+1?
   - Reservations: inventory_reservations explicitly checks promisable qty; do we let reservations exceed on-hand too?

ACCEPTANCE (when claimed):
- Phase 2 design decision on schema + cost handling + catch-up policy.
- Migration adding the chosen mechanism.
- post_inventory_adjustment + post_transfers + reserve_inventory updated to honor the new policy.
- Tests for the lifecycle: depletion past zero, receipt fills it, variance posted.

DEPENDS ON: nothing — could ship in parallel with other Phase 1 work, but probably waits until a real workflow needs it.

OUT OF SCOPE:
- Across-warehouse netting (negative at warehouse A, positive at warehouse B is its own concept).

- Backflushing automation (a related but distinct workflow).
design:
DESIGN COMMITMENT (2026-05-05, from ERP_RESEARCH.md):

Adopt Oracle ACV (Average Cost Variance) model. The 3-option investigation collapses: per-account allow_negative flag + variance_negative_inventory routing on under-issue. All 4 ERPs ship strict-by-default with explicit override and route the valuation discrepancy to a dedicated variance account.

title: Phase 2 Epic G: WIP material revaluation companion to standard cost roll
description:
Companion workflow for high-volume / never-zero-WIP environments where post_standard_cost_roll() (acct-8rv) is operationally blocked.

CONTEXT. acct-8rv blocks the roll with P0006 if any open inv_value_wip pool exists for the SKU. In long-lead-time or continuous-production shops, WIP may always be present, so the roll is unreachable in normal operations. Real ERPs handle this with a companion workflow that revalues WIP separately from the roll (SAP CON1 / WIP value adjustment, Oracle Cost Management WIP revaluation, NetSuite Recost flag).

WHY THIS IS HARD.
inv_value_wip carries three layers in one number:
  material_at_standard     — qty × prior_standard at issue time
  labor_applied            — actual_labor_rate × hours (from labor_apply events)
  overhead_applied         — overhead_rate × labor_hours (from oh_apply events)

Only the material layer is standard-cost-driven; labor and OH are based on actual rates and hours and shouldn't move when standard cost rolls. So revaluing 'qty × delta_standard' against the full WIP value is mathematically wrong — it implicitly multiplies the labor/OH portion by a factor that doesn't apply to it.

OPTIONS TO RESEARCH (Phase 2 design choice):

(1) MATERIAL-AT-STANDARD COLUMN. Add a separate 'material_value' column on WIP value accounts so material is tracked distinctly from labor/OH. Roll revaluation walks WIP pools and revalues the material portion only; labor/OH untouched. Cost: schema change to inv_value_wip accounts (or a parallel tracking table), reflow of every event that posts to WIP (rm_issue_to_wo, op_move, scrap, wo_complete, labor_apply, oh_apply) to maintain the material/labor/OH split. Most accurate; biggest schema change.

(2) RECOMPUTE FROM PRIOR STANDARD. At roll time, compute material = qty × prior_standard_at_business_date for each WIP pool. Assumes all units in WIP were issued under the prior standard — true for the very first roll, fragile after multiple rolls (a unit issued under standard A, in WIP through a roll to standard B, in WIP through another roll to standard C — what's its 'prior'?). Doable as an approximation but accumulates error.

(3) PER-EVENT MATERIAL/LABOR SPLIT. Don't change the schema; instead split the value into material/labor/OH at event time using metadata in the transfer (a 'cost_layer' field on the event). Rolls only touch transfers tagged 'material'. Cleanest semantically but requires reflowing the event JSONB shape — touches every cost-relevant reason and the conformance harness.

(4) SNAPSHOT-BASED REVALUATION. At roll time, capture each WIP pool's composition (material/labor/OH breakdown) via reverse-engineering from transfer history. Post variance against the captured material slice. Hybrid of (1) and (2); the snapshot is a one-time table populated from event replay, not maintained continuously.

ACCEPTANCE (when claimed):
1. Phase 2 design decision on the data shape (one of options 1-4 above, or a hybrid).
2. New function post_wip_material_revaluation(p_sku_id, p_at_business_date) — revalues WIP material against the active standard, posts variance against a TBD account_kind (likely a new 'variance_wip_revaluation').
3. Integration with post_standard_cost_roll — either as a follow-up step (run after roll), a pre-roll precondition (run before roll, then roll proceeds even with WIP), or a stand-alone workflow that the operator chooses to invoke.
4. Tests covering: WIP at single op, WIP at multiple ops with labor/OH layered in, sequence of rolls with WIP carrying across.

DEPENDS ON: acct-hlr (Epic F) — particularly acct-8rv for the block-on-WIP gate that this epic relieves.

OUT OF SCOPE:
- Retroactive WIP revaluation across past closed periods (separate concern).
- Reverse engineering of WIP composition from full transfer history (option 4) without explicit cost layering — may be too lossy.

NOTE: priority and timing depend on whether real Phase 1 use cases hit the always-on-WIP scenario. Until that pressure surfaces, the (a)-block behavior in acct-8rv is acceptable. This epic exists so the gap is tracked, not so it's necessarily worked next.

title: hlr.2 — Function: post_standard_cost_roll() (INSERT + revalue + audit)
description:
Second sub-issue under acct-hlr. Depends on hlr.1 (acct-x4t).

The roll workflow becomes INSERT-into-standard_costs (no UPDATE in skus) + revalue existing inventory if any + audit row. Distinct from the column-update workaround originally drafted.

Function signature:
  post_standard_cost_roll(
    p_sku_id            UUID,
    p_new_cost          BIGINT,
    p_effective_at      DATE,             -- date the new standard takes effect
    p_business_date     DATE,             -- date for variance transfers (revaluation)
    p_posted_by         UUID,
    p_idempotency_key   UUID,
    p_notes             TEXT   DEFAULT NULL,
    p_expected_old_cost BIGINT DEFAULT NULL  -- optimistic concurrency guard
  ) RETURNS UUID                          -- inventory_standard_cost_rolls.id

Body steps:
1. Replay: SELECT id FROM inventory_standard_cost_rolls WHERE idempotency_key = ; if found return.
2. Validate p_new_cost >= 0; else 23514.
3. SELECT cost_method INTO v_cm FROM skus WHERE id =  FOR UPDATE; NOT FOUND → P0010.
4. Cost-method dispatch:
     standard         → proceed
     wac_perpetual    → P0011 ('use post_cost_adjustment for WAC SKUs (Epic D)')
     wac_periodic     → P0011 (same)
     wac_retroactive  → P0011 (same)
     fifo / lot       → P0006 ('cost_method_not_implemented; acct-8gg')
5. Look up prior active standard:
     BEGIN
       v_prior := resolve_standard_cost_at(, p_business_date);
     EXCEPTION WHEN SQLSTATE 'P0018' THEN
       v_prior := NULL;  -- this is the first roll; no revaluation needed
     END;
6. Optimistic concurrency: if p_expected_old_cost IS NOT NULL: must equal v_prior; else P0017 with both values in message. (NULL must match NULL — first-roll case.)
7. INSERT new row into standard_costs (sku_id, cost=p_new_cost, effective_at=p_effective_at, posted_by, idempotency_key=p_idempotency_key, notes).
8. If v_prior IS NULL OR v_prior = p_new_cost: no revaluation pass. Skip to step 11 with delta=0, pool_qty=0.
9. WIP guard: count open inv_value_wip pools for this SKU. If > 0: P0006 ('WIP revaluation deferred to future epic').
10. Revaluation pass:
    - Walk all open inv_value_raw + inv_value_fg accounts for this SKU.
    - Order by account.id ASC; lock with FOR UPDATE.
    - For each value account, find paired stock_available(sku, location): read on_hand_qty (FOR SHARE for stable read).
    - Per pool: delta_value = on_hand_qty * (p_new_cost - v_prior). Skip if delta_value = 0.
    - Build a transfer event: reason='standard_cost_roll'; direction by sign (positive = dr inv_value_*, cr variance_std_cost_roll; negative = reverse); idempotency_key = gen_random_uuid().
    - Aggregate total_delta and total_pool_qty across all events.
11. INSERT audit row into inventory_standard_cost_rolls (sku_id, prior_standard_cost=COALESCE(v_prior,-1)? NO — schema needs prior_standard_cost NULLABLE for first roll; UPDATE F.1 schema accordingly OR use a sentinel column 'is_first_roll BOOLEAN'). RECOMMENDATION: make prior_standard_cost NULLABLE in F.1 schema; update during F.1's design review.
12. If batch non-empty: PERFORM post_transfers(batch, FALSE).
13. RETURN audit row id.

LOCK ORDER:
- skus row FOR UPDATE first (step 3).
- inv_value accounts in ascending id order (step 10).
- post_transfers internally locks debit/credit pairs in ascending id order. variance_std_cost_roll(currency) accounts have lower ids than per-SKU inv_value pools (seeded earlier in migration order), so the lock order is consistent.

EDGE CASES:
- First roll (v_prior IS NULL): no revaluation; audit row records prior=NULL, target, delta=0, pool_qty=0.
- p_new_cost = v_prior: no-op revaluation; audit only.
- No on-hand pools: audit only, no transfers.
- Pool with on_hand=0: skip (per-pool delta=0).

NEW ERROR CODE introduced or used:
- P0017 — optimistic_concurrency_violation (caller's expected old standard mismatched actual).
- P0018 — already exists from F.1; surfaces when caller backdates p_business_date before any standard exists. (Note: this is BEFORE the new INSERT, so even the first-roll case relies on the EXCEPTION-handling shape in step 5.)

UPDATE TO F.1 SCHEMA: prior_standard_cost in inventory_standard_cost_rolls must be NULLABLE (current draft has it NOT NULL). Address in F.1's design before coding F.2.

ACCEPTANCE: per F.3 test matrix.

OUT OF SCOPE: tests (F.3), docs (F.4).

title: hlr.1 — Schema refactor: standard_costs table + drop skus.standard_cost + P0018 gate
description:
First sub-issue under acct-hlr (Epic F refactor). The atomic schema change that makes everything else possible.

Migration scope (next available, likely 0027). All in one migration because dropping skus.standard_cost and updating its consumers must be atomic — leaving the column transitional adds confusion and we have no production data to preserve.

1. CREATE TABLE standard_costs (
     id              UUID NOT NULL PRIMARY KEY DEFAULT uuidv7(),
     sku_id          UUID NOT NULL REFERENCES skus(id),
     cost            BIGINT NOT NULL CHECK (cost >= 0),
     effective_at    DATE NOT NULL,
     posted_by       UUID NOT NULL,
     posted_at       TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL DEFAULT clock_timestamp(),
     idempotency_key UUID NOT NULL UNIQUE,
     notes           TEXT
   );
   CREATE INDEX std_cost_sku_eff
     ON standard_costs (sku_id, effective_at DESC);

2. CREATE OR REPLACE FUNCTION resolve_standard_cost_at(
     p_sku_id        UUID,
     p_business_date DATE
   ) RETURNS BIGINT
   LANGUAGE plpgsql STABLE AS $$
   DECLARE v_cost BIGINT;
   BEGIN
     SELECT cost INTO v_cost
       FROM standard_costs
      WHERE sku_id = p_sku_id
        AND effective_at <= p_business_date
      ORDER BY effective_at DESC
      LIMIT 1;
     IF NOT FOUND THEN
       RAISE EXCEPTION
         'standard_cost_not_established: sku=% has no standard cost in effect as of %',
         p_sku_id, p_business_date USING ERRCODE = 'P0018';
     END IF;
     RETURN v_cost;
   END;
   $$;

3. Data migration (run BEFORE dropping the column):
   INSERT INTO standard_costs (sku_id, cost, effective_at, posted_by, idempotency_key)
   SELECT id, standard_cost, '1970-01-01'::DATE,
          '00000000-0000-0000-0000-000000000000'::UUID, gen_random_uuid()
     FROM skus
    WHERE cost_method = 'standard' AND standard_cost IS NOT NULL;

4. ALTER TABLE skus DROP COLUMN standard_cost.

5. Refactor _post_transfers_compute_amount (migration 0019/0023 ancestor): standard branch reads via resolve_standard_cost_at(v_cost_sku, v_business_date) instead of skus.standard_cost. Use CREATE OR REPLACE FUNCTION (PG can replace plpgsql function bodies in-place).

6. Refactor post_inventory_adjustment (migration 0023 ancestor): standard NULL p_unit_cost path reads via resolve_standard_cost_at(p_sku_id, p_business_date). Same CREATE OR REPLACE pattern.

7. seed.sql changes:
   - skus INSERTs no longer include standard_cost (column dropped). All eight standard-method SKUs (SKU-A through SKU-H) get cost via the bulk INSERT below.
   - After SKU INSERTs, a single bulk INSERT into standard_costs:
       INSERT INTO standard_costs (sku_id, cost, effective_at, posted_by, idempotency_key)
       SELECT s.id, v.cost, '1970-01-01'::DATE,
              '00000000-0000-0000-0000-000000000000'::UUID, gen_random_uuid()
         FROM (VALUES
                 ('SKU-A', 100), ('SKU-B', 200), ('SKU-C', 50),
                 ('SKU-D', 150), ('SKU-E', 75),  ('SKU-F', 300),
                 ('SKU-G', 25),  ('SKU-H', 500)
              ) v(code, cost)
         JOIN skus s ON s.code = v.code;

8. tests/common/ helper: seed_standard_cost(pool, sku_code, cost, effective_at) that INSERTs directly into standard_costs. Used by tests that need to set up standard cost without going through post_standard_cost_roll() (which doesn't exist until F.2 lands). The seed.sql change above already covers fixture-loaded SKUs; this helper is for tests that create new SKUs mid-run.

DOWN MIGRATION:
- Re-add skus.standard_cost column.
- Backfill from standard_costs (latest by effective_at per SKU).
- DROP TABLE standard_costs.
- DROP FUNCTION resolve_standard_cost_at.
- Revert _post_transfers_compute_amount and post_inventory_adjustment bodies (use the prior up-migration text).

NEW ERROR CODE:
- P0018 — standard_cost_not_established. Documented in db/README error codes table by F.4.

ACCEPTANCE:
- ci-check round-trips clean (down + up + schema digest stable).
- Full existing test suite passes — this is a behavior-preserving refactor for SKUs that already had standard_cost set in the fixture (their data migrates to standard_costs at effective_at='1970-01-01', which is <= any test's business_date).
- Smoke test (tests/standard_costs_gate.rs or appended to transfers_provisional.rs):
  * Brand-new standard SKU (created mid-test, NO standard_costs row): post_inventory_adjustment with NULL p_unit_cost raises P0018.
  * Same SKU: a value-leg post_transfers event with cost-relevant reason raises P0018.
  * Backdated business_date BEFORE earliest effective_at: raises P0018.
  * After seed_standard_cost helper inserts a row: same operation succeeds.

OUT OF SCOPE (F.2): post_standard_cost_roll() function.

title: Phase 1 Epic F: standard cost as a separate transactional entity (refactor + gate)
description:
Refactor + gate. Standard cost is currently a column on skus (set at INSERT). This conflates two distinct concepts that real ERPs keep separate:
  (a) 'this item exists' (item master)
  (b) 'this item has a standard cost effective on/after some date' (cost estimate / cost update)

Today the column lets a SKU be created with a cost AND lets it be used immediately, regardless of whether anyone formally established the standard. There is no audit trail for who set the initial cost; no effective-date semantics; no append-only history; rolls would have to UPDATE in place. The gap surfaced when designing Epic F as originally scoped — fixing the column-update workaround forces the deeper refactor.

TARGET DESIGN:

1. New table 'standard_costs' (sku_id, cost, effective_at, posted_by, idempotency_key, notes) — append-only, time-ordered. Each row is a 'cost estimate' that becomes active on its effective_at date.

2. skus.standard_cost column DROPPED. All consumers go through one helper:

title: Phase 1 Epic E: cost_adjustment workflow (retroactive, period-close-applied)
description:
Operator-initiated retroactive cost adjustment: re-cost depletions in a target period using a corrected average. The accountant says 'we now know the avg in March was $7, not $6 — fix the books.'

LOCKED-IN DESIGN DECISIONS (acct-og1 memo, 2026-05-01, user confirmed):

D1 — TARGET PERIOD MUST BE OPEN. The retroactive adjustment can only target the period currently being closed (where close_period invokes the hook). To fix a closed period (e.g., March after April's close), the operator must first call reopen_period (acct-7h4 Phase 2 Epic K, separate workflow, not yet shipped) — standard ERP convention.

D2 — METHOD-AGNOSTIC. Works on any cost_method (standard, wac_perpetual, wac_periodic, wac_retroactive). It's an operator override of whatever cost was originally applied. wac_periodic/wac_retroactive double-correction is acceptable (their close hook already ran; this layers on top). For wac_perpetual it's the canonical operator-fix-the-perpetual-chain workflow.

D3 — VARIANCE BUSINESS_DATE in the target period. Per Q3: caller passes p_business_date which must fall within target_period_id''s opens_at/closes_at. Since target_period is open at queue time and at close-hook execution time, no override_closed_period is needed.

D4 — REAL HOOK BODY (acct-og1 fills the s6n stub). Workflow:
   1. Operator calls post_cost_adjustment_retroactive(target_period_id, sku, location, currency, inventory_class, target_avg, business_date, posted_by, idempotency_key, notes)
      - Validates target_period_id is OPEN (closed_at IS NULL). Else error referencing acct-7h4.
      - Validates target_avg >= 0.
      - INSERTs row into inventory_cost_adjustments_retroactive queue.
   2. close_period(target_period_id) invokes cost_adjust_retroactive_hook(p_period_id, p_force_provisional).
   3. Hook processes un-finalized queue rows for p_period_id:
      - For each row: find pool inv_value_<class>(sku, location, currency).
      - Walk depletions in target_period for this pool (credit_account_id = pool, business_date in period, qty IS NOT NULL).
      - For each depletion: variance = qty × (target_avg - amount/qty). Skip if variance = 0.
      - Post 2-transfer batch through variance_cost_adjust_retro (already seeded in s6n).
      - UPDATE queue row: finalized_at, finalized_count, total_variance.
   4. Hook returns count of finalized queue rows.

D5 — VARIANCE ROUTING through variance_cost_adjust_retro (already seeded in s6n in USD + EUR). Same 2-transfer pattern as wac_periodic / wac_retroactive: dr orig_debit, cr variance_cost_adjust_retro (T1); dr variance_cost_adjust_retro, cr orig_credit (T2). Net: variance_cost_adjust_retro accumulates audit-trail debit/credit pairs but balances to zero.

D6 — WIP CLASS DEFERRED. inventory_class='wip' raises P0006 referencing acct-p7v (Phase 2 Epic J: WAC + cost adjustments across WIP pools). Same restriction as wac_periodic / wac_retroactive — recursive cost-chain analysis required.

D7 — IDEMPOTENCY at queue-table level via UNIQUE(idempotency_key). Replay returns the existing queue id without re-queueing.

SUB-ISSUES:
- og1.1: Schema (inventory_cost_adjustments_retroactive table) + post_cost_adjustment_retroactive function + cost_adjust_retroactive_hook real body + close_period thread-through (1-arg → 2-arg signature change for the hook).
- og1.2: Test matrix (queue + close lifecycle, multi-depletion re-cost, multi-pool, force flag, target-period closed → error pointing to acct-7h4, replay idempotency, variance routing).
- og1.3: Doc updates retiring stub-hook bullets for cost_adjust_retroactive_hook; §3.13 (or similar) narrative; CLAUDE.md.

OPEN ITEMS FOR FUTURE EPICS:
- acct-7h4 (Phase 2 Epic K): reopen_period workflow. Required for adjusting periods that were already closed.
- acct-p7v (Phase 2 Epic J): WAC + cost_adjust across WIP pools. Required for inventory_class='wip' adjustments.

NEW ERROR CODES:
- P0021: target_period_closed (raised by post_cost_adjustment_retroactive when target_period_id has closed_at IS NOT NULL).

ACCEPTANCE:
- 100u in March at avg $6, deplete 50u (cogs = $300, inv_value_fg = $300 reduced).
- Operator queues post_cost_adjustment_retroactive(target_period=March, target_avg=$7).
- close_period(March) invokes the hook.
- Hook walks the 50u depletion: variance = 50 × ($7 - $6) = $50.
- Posts 2 transfers through variance_cost_adjust_retro: cogs +$50, inv_value_fg -$50.
- Queue row finalized.

OUT OF SCOPE:
- Closed-period adjustments without reopen (handled by acct-7h4).
- WIP class adjustments (acct-p7v).
- Auto-derived target_avg (operator must specify).
- Bulk operations across many SKUs (caller batches).
