title: post_ap_bill tolerance-pct divide-by-zero (cosmetic, raises 22012 instead of P0024)
description:
## Finding

`post_ap_bill` tolerance-pct computation at mig 0090 line 181 divides by `v_pl.unit_cost`. If `v_pl.unit_cost = 0` and `v_unit_cost <> 0`, this raises Postgres SQLSTATE 22012 (division-by-zero) instead of a clean P0024 three-way mismatch error.

Defensive: the surrounding IF at line 173 only enters this block when `v_unit_cost <> v_pl.unit_cost`, and a non-zero bill on a zero-cost po_line is a caller bug — but the error surfaced is `22012 ERROR: division by zero` rather than the application's documented `P0024 ap_bill_three_way_mismatch`.

## Discovery

Audit refresh on migrations 0071–0090 (REVIEW.md addendum, 2026-05-05). Cosmetic finding flagged during the AP3 walk on post_ap_bill.

## Concrete location

```
db/migrations/0090_three_way_match_tolerance.up.sql

Line 173:
   IF v_unit_cost <> v_pl.unit_cost THEN
Line 181:
     v_diff_pct := ABS(v_unit_cost - v_pl.unit_cost) * 100.0 / v_pl.unit_cost;
                                                              ^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^
                                                              divide-by-zero if v_pl.unit_cost = 0
```

Symmetric concern in `post_customer_invoice` (mig 0090) tolerance check; same fix shape applies if confirmed.

## Severity

P4 — cosmetic. Documented behavior has the same outcome (caller's bill is rejected) but with a different SQLSTATE. Operationally:
- 22012 stops the transaction with a generic message
- P0024 stops with the documented three-way-mismatch context

Both raise; both are correct in spirit. Cleanup improves error-handling clarity for consumers of the API.

## Fix shape

Add an explicit `v_pl.unit_cost = 0` arm before line 181:

```sql
IF v_unit_cost <> v_pl.unit_cost THEN
  IF v_tolerance_pct = 0 THEN
    RAISE 'P0024 ...';
  END IF;
  IF v_pl.unit_cost = 0 THEN
    -- Non-zero bill against zero-cost po_line: out of tolerance by definition.
    RAISE 'P0024 ap_bill_three_way_mismatch ...';
  END IF;
  v_diff_pct := ABS(v_unit_cost - v_pl.unit_cost) * 100.0 / v_pl.unit_cost;
  IF v_diff_pct > v_tolerance_pct THEN
    RAISE 'P0024 ...';
  END IF;
END IF;
```

Symmetric fix in `post_customer_invoice` if it has the same shape.

## Test scenario

```rust
// tests/ap_bill.rs
// scenario: po_line created with unit_cost=0; vendor bills with unit_cost=10.
// expect P0024 ap_bill_three_way_mismatch (NOT 22012).
```

## Severity / priority justification

P4 — defer until error-handling-clarity work surfaces; not load-bearing.

## Surfaced from

REVIEW.md addendum 2026-05-05 (audit refresh on migrations 0071–0090).
close_reason: Closed by mig 0091 audit-loop closure. Body-only fixes: post_so_ship FOR UPDATE on v_val_acct before WAC pool read; post_standard_cost_roll v_lock_ids extended to include paired stock_wip when p_revalue_wip=TRUE; post_ap_bill / post_customer_invoice zero-baseline arm before tolerance pct divide. Regression tests added; ci-check clean; 546/0/9 tests pass; REVIEW.md addendum verdict flipped.

title: FX revaluation on returns: handle currency rate drift between original event and return
description:
## Problem

When a return crosses a currency revaluation boundary, the snapshotted unit_cost / unit_price encodes the original-rate value, but the vendor / customer expects the credit at TODAY's rate (or some bilateral negotiation).

### Concrete

- Day 1: USD/EUR rate = 1.10. Receive goods from EU vendor, po_unit_cost = 100 EUR, booked into our USD-denominated books at 110 USD per unit.
- Day 30: Rate drifts to 1.20. Inventory still on books at 110 USD per unit.
- Day 35: Return all units. post_po_return uses snapshotted unit_cost=100 EUR.
- Vendor expects: a 100-EUR credit. At today's rate, that's 120 USD. We post: ap DR by amount derived from snapshotted unit_cost — at original rate, 110 USD per unit. Result: 10 units returned, ap reduced by 1100 USD, but we owe vendor 1200 USD. $100 unbalanced.

The gap goes to FX revaluation territory. Today our system has `fx_revaluation` account_kind in the enum but no fx-revaluation workflow — `acct-???` follow-up tracks revaluation of open ar / ap balances.

## Pattern

When post_po_return posts the AP debit, the value should be:
- Inventory leg: at the original-rate cost basis (snapshotted unit_cost) — preserves audit-trail integrity for inventory revaluation.
- AP leg: at the CURRENT FX rate to honor what we actually owe vendor today.
- Difference: routes to fx_revaluation as a P&L hit.

Mirror on AR side: customer expects credit at today's rate; our books drained ar at original rate; difference to fx_revaluation.

## Implementation sketch

- Look up current FX rate from fx_rates table for (currency, business_date).
- v_inv_amount = qty * snapshotted unit_cost (existing — original rate)
- v_ap_amount_today = qty * unit_cost * (fx_today / fx_at_receipt). Subtle: po_receipt_lines doesn't currently snapshot the FX rate at receipt; need a snapshot column.
- v_fx_diff = v_ap_amount_today - v_inv_amount (some sign math)
- Emit additional fx_leg or fx_revaluation event for the diff.

## Schema change

- ALTER TABLE po_receipt_lines ADD COLUMN fx_rate_at_receipt NUMERIC; -- and similar for so_shipment_lines
- post_po_receipt and post_so_ship populate at INSERT (looking up fx_rates for the line's currency at business_date).
- post_po_return / post_customer_return read the snapshot, compute drift vs current rate, post fx_revaluation legs.

Backfill: existing po_receipt_lines / so_shipment_lines without snapshots can default to today's rate (loses fidelity but avoids NULL handling).

## Acceptance criteria

- Schema additions for FX rate snapshotting on receipt / ship lines.
- post_po_receipt / post_so_ship populate the snapshots.
- post_po_return / post_customer_return read snapshots, compute drift vs business_date rate from fx_rates, post fx_revaluation legs.
- Tests: same-rate return (no fx_revaluation), drifted-rate return (fx_revaluation posts the diff), zero-drift on home-currency returns.

## Priority justification

P4: only matters for multi-currency operations crossing meaningful timeframes. Domestic-currency-only customers won't notice.

## Dependencies

- acct-quk (closed)
- acct-ari (closed)
- acct-XXX (cost_method snapshotting follow-up) — same shape, independent issue, same migration could carry both.

## Out of scope

- The broader FX-revaluation-on-open-balances workflow (separate large effort)
- Hedging / forward contracts (way out of scope)
- Negotiated bilateral rates (vendor/customer agreement on a fixed exchange rate) — caller policy, not engine policy
notes:
DEFERRED 2026-05-05 (autonomous review). Scope is contradictory.

Issue's scenario assumes the system translates EUR transactions to a
home-currency (USD) view at receipt time. The codebase doesn't do
that — it tracks per-currency partition (inv_value_raw EUR is
distinct from inv_value_raw USD; ap EUR distinct from ap USD).
There's no current point at which FX rates enter transactional math.

The "FX revaluation on returns" feature only makes sense as a corner
case of the broader period-end FX-revaluation-on-open-balances
workflow — which the issue itself marks "out of scope".

Snapshotting fx_rate_at_receipt / fx_rate_at_ship without a consumer
adds dead schema (an extra column on every receipt/ship line that
no function reads). Premature.

To unblock: file the broader FX-revaluation workflow first
(home-currency reporting model, period-end revaluation of open
EUR ar/ap balances). Once that lands, return-specific drift
treatment is a small additive change that can reuse the same FX
infrastructure.

For now: returns drain the same per-currency amount they originally
posted. If the customer/vendor expects a different rate, that's a
caller-side bilateral negotiation — out of engine scope per the
issue's own "Out of scope" section.

title: cost_adjust interleaved-with-other-doc-wrappers test coverage
description:
Cross-path coverage tests in tests/cost_adjust_interleaved.rs filling the gap noted post tier-2: prior tests exercised each doc-layer wrapper (post_inventory_adjustment, post_po_receipt, post_ap_bill, post_cost_adjustment, post_cost_adjustment_retroactive) in isolation. Eight tests walk realistic interleaved sequences:

  1. wac_perpetual_po_then_cost_adjust_then_po_pool_composes
  2. wac_perpetual_class_isolation_under_interleaved_adjust
  3. wac_perpetual_ap_unaffected_by_cost_adjust
  4. wac_perpetual_cost_adjust_is_forward_only
  5. wac_perpetual_cost_adjust_idempotent_under_interleaved_load

  7. wac_periodic_cost_adjust_retro_interleaved_with_depletions
  8. wac_periodic_retro_multi_class_independent_close

Verifies pool composition, class isolation (raw vs fg cost_adjust on different locations), AP non-interference, forward-only semantics (prior depletion variance unchanged by later cost_adjust), idempotency under interleaved replay, write-up + write-down netting, and the documented wac_periodic × cost_adjust_retroactive double-correction stacking at close.

Discovered behavior to document elsewhere:

- rm_issue_to_wo always uses component STANDARD cost (BOM2 plan_only), so cost_adjust on a wac_perpetual raw component does NOT affect a downstream WO's WIP pool — this is a deliberate BOM2 design (acct-6jq) and not a coverage gap.

title: acct-tyq sub (optional): 4-worker drainer variant characterization
description:
Optional follow-up to the single-worker shape G benchmark. Re-run the same shape G workload but with 4 concurrent drainers (each running the SKIP LOCKED loop). Characterize the fan-in/fan-out trade:
- Does throughput exceed single-worker (taking advantage of multi-core commit)?
- Does it reintroduce per-row contention via the 4 drainers competing for hot accounts (i.e., regress toward shape F's contention pattern)?
- What worker count is the sweet spot? (Likely informs an operational tuning knob.)

Backlog (P4) — only worth running if acct-tyq.4's single-worker result is promising AND we suspect we're CPU-bound on a single drainer. If we're commit-bound, 4 drainers won't help; spending time on this would be wasted.
acceptance_criteria: Either: results documented as a perf_outbox_v0 addendum, OR explicitly closed as 'not pursued because single-worker was [commit-bound|sufficient]'.
close_reason: Shape K added to perf_baseline_v0.md. 4-drainer super-batch HALVES throughput vs single-drainer (180 vs 365 evps) — smaller per-call super-batches plus 4-way FOR UPDATE contention on stock_available rows. Negative result documented as the answer: single-worker super-batch is the architectural sweet spot for this workload; T4_DRAINERS=1 is correct tuning. 0 deadlocks. Committed 52dff5c.

value: Audit/review work that calls itself 'comprehensive' or 'systematic' must actually walk every item — not condense to a matrix and skip the per-item analysis. **Why:** 2026-05-04, on acct-du2 Phase 2 (structural per-function audit), I proposed skipping the 7-question walk for ~38 functions because 'the matrix already has the verdicts'. User pushback was strong — the meta-epic exists *because* class-confusion bugs slip past pattern-grep; the per-function walk is the catch-net for novel shapes that don't pattern-match. Cutting it is half-assing the very thing being audited. **How to apply:** When a plan/epic says 'audit each function' or 'review every X', do the per-item analysis even if a higher-level summary seems sufficient. The summary is a deliverable, not a substitute. Suspect this rule whenever the next phase is more fun than the audit phase.

ALWAYS COMMIT completed work without asking, then git push AND bd dolt push after each wave/work item. User-level override of CLAUDE.md default. Why: pattern set 2026-05-01 (commits flow as part of the work cycle); extended 2026-08-07 — user directive "ensure you commit/push/dolt push after each wave" now that the remote exists (github.com/dkkloimwieder/acct, SSH; Dolt remote auto-configured from git origin). How to apply: when a logical unit of work completes (bd issue closed, tests green), commit immediately with the established style (subject line, HEREDOC body explaining why, Co-Authored-By trailer), git push, and bd dolt push if any bd state changed. At session close additionally refresh .beads/issues-export.jsonl via bd export --all, commit, push.

Cost-method dispatch (post-Phase-1, registry-driven via acct-w0lo): 'standard' / 'wac_perpetual' / 'wac_periodic' / 'wac_retroactive' all registered in cost_method_strategies (consolidated 0013); dispatcher EXECUTE-formats _compute_amount_<method>_outbound. 'fifo' / 'lot' values exist on the cost_method enum but raise P0006 ('cost_method_not_implemented') — tracked in acct-8gg / acct-uze / acct-0kz (all blocked-by acct-2c1m). post_posting_lines (renamed from post_transfers via acct-dhzc) does qty-NULL gate + R2 credit-first SKU resolution before EXECUTE-formatting the registered fn name. Adding FIFO/lot is INSERT into the registry + write the function — no edits to the dispatcher. Phase 0's 'standard only' rationale (smallest correctness surface; deterministic conformance) was lifted as the WAC family shipped.

Dev postgres: docker compose service 'postgres', host port 5111, container port 5432. Volume mount is /var/lib/postgresql (NOT /var/lib/postgresql/data — PG 18+ convention for pg_upgrade --link). Requires 'security_opt: seccomp:unconfined' because Docker default seccomp blocks io_uring syscalls (production-hardening tracked as acct-hbp). Connect string: postgres://acct:acct_dev@localhost:5111/acct.

Don't make silent design tradeoffs to avoid implementation friction. 2026-04-30: when adding inventory adjustment as Phase 1 first slice, I reused cycle_count_adj as the underlying reason and rationalized 'name is historical' to avoid the down-migration asymmetry of ALTER TYPE ADD VALUE. User pushed back: 'why is ledger name cycle count? that is not what i said. we want simple inventory adjustment.' The right call was to add the new enum value (PG 18 allows it inside a transaction; down-migration leaves the value in place per project convention — same pattern as migration 0020's down-comment 'Phase 0/1 has no production data; down is best-effort'). Lesson: when a user gives explicit naming/semantic guidance and the implementation friction is moderate not catastrophic, don't quietly rationalize a workaround — either do it right, or surface the tradeoff and ask. Especially for first-of-kind decisions that set precedent (this was the first new transfer_reason added since migration 0002).

ERP feature-slicing framing correction (2026-04-30): when proposing Phase 1 (or beyond) feature slices for an ERP/inventory system, ALWAYS frame them by transactional-cycle position — inflow (PO/vendor-bill/inventory-adjustment) → conversion (WO/routings/scrap) → outflow (SO/AR) → cross-cutting (period close, reconciliation). Inflow is the natural foundational starting point because inventory has to come in (or be adjusted in) before it can be transformed or shipped. Don't lead with SO or WO and bury PO/AP as a third option — that ignores domain logic. User correction prompted by my initial Slice A=SO, B=WO, C=PO ordering; corrected to A=Inbound, B=Conversion, C=Outbound, D=Cross-cutting. ALSO: 'paying for services' is a real flow distinct from PO receipt — ap_bill against an expense account (utilities, consulting) doesn't have an inventory side and shouldn't be conflated with PO matching. Include both inventory-tied and standalone AP paths when scoping inbound work. APPLIES TO: any future slice/feature proposal in this project, plus any other ERP/inventory work.

Always favor comprehensive testing over lightweight. Why: user directive 2026-05-08 — chose richer cost-flow property test over existence-and-shape probe for Phase D. 'Always be as comprehensive as possible'. How to apply: when scoping property tests, prefer random-workload signed-qty/cost-flow/invariant probing over minimal happy-path existence checks. T1 (schema invariants) + T2 (workflow matrices) + property tests should each go deep on their layer rather than skimming. PROPTEST_CASES default 100 with --test-threads=1 stays the convention; go higher when wall-time permits.

When polling a long-running background task (e.g., cargo test) across multiple ScheduleWakeup ticks, do NOT arm a fresh 'until ... sleep' watcher or Monitor each wakeup. Why: 2026-05-09 during E2.5-followup full-suite run, I armed 4 redundant watchers (b9kb97xo2, b4qiny3hd, b0izws0v5, Monitor bm079bsxd) over consecutive wakeups, all watching the same cargo test process; user asked 'why are there so many shells running?' Each wakeup added another sentinel. How to apply: ONE watcher per task, max — typically the original run_in_background:true Bash call's own task-notification on completion. On subsequent wakeups, just cat/wc -l the output file and pgrep the process. Companion to feedback-test-runs-background-sequential-no-timeout (which covers sequential not parallel runs).

Always split migrations to favor granularity. Why: user directive 2026-05-08 when answering Phase D open questions — chose 6 separate migs (one per sub-issue D1-D6) over one bundled mig per phase. Rationale: smaller migrations are easier to review, easier to isolate failures, and align with bd sub-issue structure. How to apply: when a phase has multiple sub-issues with distinct scope (schema vs dispatcher vs backfill vs recon vs close-hooks), ship each as its own migration file rather than bundling. Override the B2/B3/C single-mig pattern from this point on. Exception: trivial extensions (one column add, one CHECK relax) can still ride together if they share a single sub-issue.

Always background test runs (run_in_background: true) and run them sequentially — never in parallel. Why: parallel cargo test invocations against the same DB cause catastrophic interference (TRUNCATE collisions, account-row deadlocks, schema-state divergence). Background gating via task-notifications is the correct mechanism. Do NOT set timeout on backgrounded test commands — backgrounded jobs ignore timeout, and the user will notify if a run is taking excessively long or burning resources. Foreground is fine for narrowly-scoped runs (e.g., --test single_binary) where you genuinely need to block. How to apply: full ./scripts/run-tests.sh always backgrounded, no timeout. Single-binary runs may foreground if expected wall-time is small. Never have two test runs in flight at once.

Use tiered test runners; do NOT run full suite after every commit.

Three tiers measured 2026-05-10:
  scripts/run-tests-t1.sh     — 40 binaries, ~2m, 418 tests (T1 invariant probes)
  scripts/run-tests-fast.sh   — 99 binaries, ~4-5m, 940 tests (no property/conformance/outbox_drain/load)
  scripts/run-tests.sh        — full suite, ~13-15m, 978 tests

Why: full suite is slow; property tests dominate (~30-65s each, 24 binaries). Most commits don't need them.

How to apply:
  - Default for typical commits (new wrapper / new schema / new t1 cases): run fast.
  - For pure schema-add / pure helper-add (no ledger flow): t1 is enough.
  - Run FULL suite at session end OR before milestones OR when the change touches:
      * _post_posting_lines_apply_event (apply_event)
      * post_posting_lines (dispatcher)
      * cost_method_strategies (any new strategy)
      * run_daily_reconciliation
      * reserve_inventory
      * close_period or any close_hook
    These are the surfaces the property tests + conformance + outbox_drain regression-net protects.

Always commit-policy-always-commit-completed-work-2026-05-01 still applies — but use the right tier first.

Fresh git worktrees in this repo (.claude/worktrees/*) start with an EMPTY/uninitialized bd Dolt DB — bd create then fails with 'issue_prefix config is missing' and bd list shows 0 issues. Cause: the .beads/redirect file is missing. FIX: write .beads/redirect containing the relative path to the main repo's .beads, resolved relative to the WORKTREE ROOT (for .claude/worktrees/<name> that is '../../../.beads'); verify with 'bd worktree info' (should say 'redirects to /home/kaalin/dev/acct/.beads'). Do NOT run 'bd init' in a worktree — it creates a divergent local DB. New worktrees created via 'bd worktree create' get the redirect automatically; harness-created (plain git worktree add) ones do not.

ID strategy: internal document UUID PKs use PG 18 builtin uuidv7() (time-ordered, better B-tree locality). Random gen_random_uuid() reserved for client-supplied values that must be unpredictable — specifically transfers.idempotency_key per Part IV §1.2. Stub tables (skus/locations/sales_orders/purchase_orders) added in acct-93b.8 use uuidv7() as the column DEFAULT.

sqlx-cli treats migration files as CONTENT-ADDRESSED (checksum recorded in _sqlx_migrations table). Even editing a leading comment in a .up.sql file triggers 'migration N was previously applied but has been modified' on next sqlx migrate run. Lesson learned 2026-05-01 during foundation audit (acct-ok2): tried to add a HISTORICAL NOTE comment block to 0026_close_period.up.sql describing post-shipped state of close hooks. sqlx rejected the modified file. REVERTED. Post-shipped or current-state documentation belongs in db/README.md or ledger_design_consolidated_v0.md, NEVER in shipped migration files. Migration .up.sql / .down.sql are write-once after first apply on any database. Treat them as historical record. Even fixing a typo requires either (a) a new migration that supersedes, or (b) coordinated dev-DB reset across the team. ALSO: ci-check.sh schema digest is non-deterministic across runs in PG 18 because pg_dump emits a randomized '\restrict <key>' header. Don't rely on byte-stable digests across runs; only use it to detect drift after a single up-down-up cycle.

PG forbids renaming function parameters via CREATE OR REPLACE FUNCTION — error: 'cannot change name of input parameter X'. Renaming arguments requires DROP FUNCTION followed by CREATE. WHY: function signatures are identified by argument types, but parameter NAMES are part of the function descriptor and considered immutable across CREATE OR REPLACE. Hit during acct-397 (supplier → vendor rename, 2026-05-02) on post_ap_bill's first parameter. APPLY: any future migration that renames a function parameter must DROP+CREATE, not CREATE OR REPLACE. Internal variable names (v_*) are fine to change with CREATE OR REPLACE — only top-level parameters trigger the error.
Phase 0 fixture currencies: USD and EUR only (with one USD<->EUR fx_rate). The 5-currency list (USD/EUR/GBP/JPY/CAD) in the original plan was overscoped — explicitly trimmed by user.

Phase 0 calls post_posting_lines (renamed from post_transfers via acct-dhzc 2026-05-07) synchronously in-transaction with document writes. ledger_outbox table exists (consolidated 0021) but is opt-in for the load_outbox_* benches and outbox_drain test, not on the production path. Outbox vs sync is a perf question deferred until §14.1 baseline contention surfaces; tracked as acct-c4p (formerly acct-tyq, re-resolved 2026-04-30 as acct-0oy with shape L pseudo-sync as the documented escape hatch).

Plan files in ~/.claude/plans/ are a record of planning, NOT a claim of pending work. A plan can be (and often is) already executed. Before recommending work based on a plan file, verify by checking the codebase (git log, ls tests/, grep for filenames the plan mentions) — never recommend a 'next task' based on plan-file existence alone. Failure mode: I once told the user T5 (conformance fixture) was uncovered Phase 0 work because its plan file existed and it wasn't in bd. It had been completed and committed (0007453, Apr 29) with 100 cases and a 527-line harness. The user had to ask 'WHY did you think it needed done?' to surface my mistake. Always run a quick file-existence check before recommending tasks.

Postgres 18 with io_method=io_uring is the chosen DB. Extensions: pg_stat_statements, pg_cron. Dev runs in Docker. The official postgres:18 image may or may not be built with liburing — must verify during S1 setup; if missing, custom Dockerfile FROM postgres:18 + liburing-dev rebuild.

posting_lines table (renamed from transfers via acct-dhzc 2026-05-07) is NOT partitioned (decided in L3 / acct-93b.11). Doc §1.2 spec was internally inconsistent — PARTITION BY RANGE (posted_at) + UNIQUE (idempotency_key) cannot coexist (Postgres requires partition-key columns in unique constraints on partitioned tables). Consolidated 0009_posting_lines ships non-partitioned + idempotency_key UNIQUE directly. Conversion to partitioning + idempotency_keys side table is tracked as acct-e8g, gated on Part IV §14.1 exploratory baseline. Do NOT propose 'implement §1.2 verbatim' or add PARTITION BY without checking acct-e8g status.

Project deliberately avoids task runners (Make, just, etc.). Shell scripts in scripts/ are the canonical entry-points (dev-up.sh, dev-down.sh, run-migrations.sh, future ci-check.sh, run-tests.sh). Why: small project, two ways to do the same thing creates drift, scripts are self-documenting via filename. Revisit 'just' only when project complexity justifies a task runner — surface the case to the user, do not add unilaterally.

Project is written in Rust. Postgres driver: sqlx. Migrations: sqlx-cli (plain .sql under db/migrations/). Tests: cargo test (tokio + sqlx integration tests). Do NOT propose pgTAP, Python harnesses, golang-migrate, sqitch, or other non-Rust tooling — they were fabricated defaults in an earlier plan and have been removed.

RESOLVED 2026-08-07 (convergence Q10, commit 6ddbf47): shared_preload_libraries in the acct_acct-pgdata volume overlay is now just pg_stat_statements, pg_cron — recreating acct-postgres NO LONGER FATALs on missing custom .so, because no PoC extension is preloaded anymore. The surviving ledger-v3.2 architecture is shmem-free (ledger_direct needs no preload; ledger_feed is a logical-decoding output plugin, also no preload) — but runtime-installed .so (docker cp into the container writable layer) are still WIPED by recreation and must be reinstalled via the stream install scripts before their SQL functions resolve. Historical detail (pre-2026-08-07 the roster listed up to 5 custom preloads and recreation boot-blocked until all were rebuilt) matters only for reading old session logs. Real volume name: acct_acct-pgdata; an unprefixed empty acct-pgdata volume also exists (stale artifact).

restart-docker-before-full-testing-cycle: 'docker restart acct-postgres' before any full testing cycle (test suite, regression, bake-off) to ensure a clean slate — BGWorker state, shmem regions, in-flight committer ticks, and any leftover staging slots all reset. Especially important when prior session left work in flight, after .so install, or before measuring perf. Routine in dev; container has volume mount so data persists. Cheaper than chasing cross-test flakes.

The committed ledger-routed-c (and ledger-direct-c) generated schema sql/ledger_<x>--0.0.1.sql is the TEST_HOOKS-inclusive build (~47 test-hook extern mentions). install-*-c.sh regenerates it via cargo pgrx schema for WHATEVER feature set it just built, so a production install (WITH_TEST_HOOKS unset) rewrites the file WITHOUT the test-hook externs (big spurious diff: ~197 deletions). When committing a GUC-only or internal-only change that adds NO new pg_extern, git checkout -- <sql> to drop the churn — the extension schema genuinely does not change. Only commit a real sql delta when you added/changed a pg_extern. Ran into this on acct-0at4.16 (added ledger_routed_c.wake_committer_on_publish GUC + an internal wake fn; the sql regen from the test_hooks->prod .so restore looked like a 237-line rewrite but was pure feature-set noise).

When bounding an O(ring) scan over the routed shmem staging/committer ring with a worker-local low-water cursor, anchor the cursor on OCCUPIED (valid != 0), NOT on the target state you are collecting (valid == 1 pending). Why: staging entries can revert to an earlier state IN PLACE behind an advanced cursor — the committer ejects an in-flight slot back to pending via valid 3->1 / 2->1 (xact-probe-fail / rollback), at the slot's existing ring index. A cursor that advanced past it (because it was momentarily valid==2/3, not ==1) strands the ejected submission forever -> starvation, never committed. Caught on acct-ozln by acceptance_routed_orphan_recovery::xact_probe_failure_ejects_all_then_retries (timed out waiting for 1 trx). Fix: advance the cursor only past truly-free (valid==0) slots; treat any valid!=0 as band-occupied. The cursor is a pure hint (the valid 1->2 CAS stays the routing gate) so a stale value only widens a scan, never drops/reorders. Bootstrap (fresh worker / restart) does one full-ring min-request_seq pass over valid!=0 (wrap-safe). NOTE (2026-07-10): the committer-side application of this principle (acct-m4g5.2, the committer claim-loop shared-FIFO-head + O(ring)-scan-under-shared-LWLock fix) was CLOSED NOT-PURSUED — the whole committer->pool affinity lever was KILLED at the acct-m4g5.1 STEP A gate (B/A=1.26x on disjoint pools; limiter = shared staging-ring LWLock, not the row-lock affinity targets which are already ~0). Both committer defects are affinity-ON-only and inert at the shipped affinity_scheme=0 default. The cursor PRINCIPLE stands and still governs the router (acct-ozln, shipped); it would only re-apply to the committer if committer affinity is ever revived (do not anchor a revived CQ cursor on valid==1). Do not treat acct-m4g5.2 as pending work — it is closed.

Treat 'proceed' as scoped to the specific item under discussion, NOT a blanket green-light for the rest of an epic. **Why:** 2026-05-07, after user approved Q3/Q4/Q5 recommendations + B1 with 'i agree with your recommendations - proceed', I shipped B1 cleanly, then auto-claimed B2 and started surveying without asking. User correction was sharp ('WHO SAID TO START ANOTHER TASK!!!! I ASKED YOU A FUCKING QUESTION!!!') — their immediately preceding message was 'what is running background?', a purely informational query. I conflated it with continued go-ahead. Second incident of the same shape — the scope-correction reminder I had saved in state memory after the previous 'begin with item 1' episode failed to fire. **How to apply:** When a phase/epic boundary is reached (sub-issue closed, mig committed), STOP. Surface what shipped, surface the next available item, and wait for explicit direction. 'Auto mode' is about minimizing interruption WITHIN a sanctioned task, not crossing scope boundaries. An informational question ('what is X', 'show me Y') is NEVER a directive to continue work — answer it, then wait. Re-read the user's most-recent direct directive before claiming the next task.

v21-test-harness-isolation-via-cluster-per-binary-not-shmem-wipe: when v21 tests flake from cross-binary state, the fix is poc/queue-extension-v21/scripts/run-tests-v21.sh (docker-restart between binaries), NOT a poc_v21_test_force_recover_* shmem-wipe SQL fn. The latter races live BGWorkers (router/committer ticking every 50ms) and pins CPU at 100% when the wipe lands mid-Phase-6. Cluster-per-binary is the proper isolation boundary; within a binary, --test-threads=1 + the existing reset_state TRUNCATE keeps tests honest. acct-shpc.9 shipped the runner (ea0b68c) after a wrong-shaped force-recover attempt (rolled back).

When auditing a plpgsql function across migrations, ALWAYS verify the latest CREATE OR REPLACE version before reading the body. **Why:** acct-du2 Phase 2 walk (2026-05-04) read mig 0027 of post_inventory_adjustment as 'latest'; the actual latest is mig 0031, which already had the per-class signed SUM fix from acct-1vr (mig 0030). I filed acct-du2.8 as a P1 bug; closed as false alarm during fix attempt after re-reading. **How to apply:** Run 'grep -nE "CREATE OR REPLACE FUNCTION fname" db/migrations/*.up.sql | tail -1' or sort numerically before opening the body. The mig 0070-style high-numbered files often supersede the original definitions. Methodology error rate of this audit was 1/13 = 8% even with the rule unstated; with the rule explicit it should approach 0%.
